He looked for him; his tracks were many. He went quickly. He thought: 'I'll kill Panther.' Panther came to a river and climbed a tree. Skunk arrived; he drank. He saw Panther in the river; he shot him. He broke much wind; he had no more fluid. He took back his fluid; he did it and he broke wind again. He was tired; he lay down. Then he saw Panther in the tree: he shot him. Skunk killed Panther.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 40 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 牠一路走去時，又回到了有許多足跡的地方。臭鼬一路走去；牠心想美洲豹撒了謊，牠並沒有死。牠又動身了；牠回到了牠的桶那裡。牠的桶破了；牠沒看見美洲豹。牠知道牠並沒有死；牠看見了牠的足跡，便開始循著牠的足跡追去。足跡很多；牠看不出美洲豹在哪裡。牠尋找牠；牠的足跡很多。牠走得很快。牠心想：「我要殺了美洲豹。」美洲豹來到一條河邊，爬上了一棵樹。臭鼬到了；牠喝了水。牠在河裡看見了美洲豹；牠朝牠射去。牠放了許多屁；牠再沒有液體了。牠把牠的液體收了回來；牠這麼做了，卻又放了屁。牠累了；牠躺了下來。這時牠看見美洲豹在樹上：牠朝牠射去。臭鼬殺死了美洲豹。

title.en: The Deluge of Chicken Hawk and Yawo'nik!
title.zh: 雞鷹與洪水

region.en: Huckleberry camp of the Kutenai mountains (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 庫特內山地越橘營地（象徵定位）

period: Told by Michel to A. F. Chamberlain, 1891; published 1918 (Boas, BAE Bulletin 59)

source.work: Franz Boas, Kutenai Tales, Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 59 (1918) — No. 27, 'The Deluge'

summary.en: At a huckleberry camp, Chicken Hawk's wife is stolen by Yawo'nik!, who drinks all the water in the world when wounded — 'There was no more water' — until Chicken Hawk pulls out his arrow, and out comes the water: there is a flood. All the people go up the mountains, and the water reaches there; they all think they will die. Chicken Hawk takes off his tail, puts it up, and says, 'If there is no more tail, then we shall all be lost': the tail had four stripes, and the water is gauged by them — 'If there is no stripe on my tail, then we shall all die.' The water stops, then goes down, and the people go down.
summary.zh: 越橘營中，雞鷹之妻為 Yawo'nik! 所奪。雞鷹怒而射之；Yawo'nik! 中箭飲水——『水盡矣』——雞鷹拔箭，水自箭孔湧出，洪水滔天。眾人登山避難，水亦隨至，皆以為必死。雞鷹自斷其尾，舉之曰：『尾若失，吾等皆亡。』其尾原有四道斑紋，以之量水——『紋若盡沒，吾等皆斃。』水終止漲，退去，眾人下山。

sensitivity.note: Condensed paraphrase of a Kutenai flood narrative recorded by Chamberlain (Boas, 1918); not verbatim. Flood cluster parallel. Published folk-narrative only. Category 'myth'.

passages.text: There was a camp; there were many who picked huckleberries. Chicken Hawk had a wife. She picked huckleberries. Chicken Hawk went; he saw his wife. He did not know that Yawo'nik! had taken his wife — Yawo'nik! had taken her. He was angry. He shot him; he hit him. Yawo'nik! drank water: there was no more. He took it again; there was no more water. Yawo'nik! drank. Then Chicken Hawk took (pulled out) his arrow; out came the water. There was a flood.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 41 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 從前有一個營地；有許多人在採越橘。雞鷹（Chicken Hawk）有一個妻子。她採著越橘。雞鷹走去；他看見了他的妻子。他不知道是亞沃尼克（Yawo'nik!）帶走了他的妻子——是亞沃尼克帶走了她。他憤怒了。他朝牠射去；他射中了牠。亞沃尼克喝水：水沒有了。牠又去取水；水沒有了。亞沃尼克喝著。於是雞鷹拔出他的箭；水便湧了出來。於是發生了洪水。

passages.text: All the people went up the mountains; the water reached there. All the people thought they would die. Chicken Hawk took off his tail; he put it up. He said: 'If there is no more tail, then we shall all be lost.' The tail had four stripes. Then there was one left. He said: 'If there is no stripe on my tail, then we shall all die.' It reached there. The water stopped; then it went down. The people went down.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 41 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 所有的人都上了山；水也漲到了那裡。所有的人都以為自己要死了。雞鷹取下牠的尾巴；牠把尾巴舉起來。牠說：「如果尾巴上再沒有條紋了，那我們就都要完了。」那尾巴上有四道條紋。後來只剩下一道了。牠說：「如果我尾巴上再沒有條紋了，那我們就都要死了。」水漲到了那裡。水停了；然後退了下去。人們便下山了。

title.en: Chicken Hawk and Toad
title.zh: 雞鷹與蟾蜍

region.en: Deer-watching grounds of the Kutenai (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 庫特內故地觀鹿之所（象徵定位）

period: Told by Michel to A. F. Chamberlain, 1891; published 1918 (Boas, BAE Bulletin 59)

source.work: Franz Boas, Kutenai Tales, Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 59 (1918) — No. 28, 'Chicken Hawk and Toad'

summary.en: Toad goes with Golden Eagle to take Chicken Hawk for a husband because he is skillful and catches deer; watching the deer one morning, Chicken Hawk thinks 'I'll kill her' and kills Toad. Her parents see the body, take it home, and her angry mother says 'Let us go!' — the two lie in wait for Chicken Hawk on his passing trail, take him, carry him back to the tent, and make him perspire over the fire. Blue Hawk knows his younger brother is poor, goes, takes him, and restores him; on the following day he looked for all kinds of animals, and Chicken Hawk and Blue Hawk were no longer poor.
summary.zh: 蟾蜍隨金鵰往嫁雞鷹，因其技高能獵鹿。一日晨間觀鹿，雞鷹忽起殺心，誅蟾蜍。其雙親見屍而歸，母怒曰：『走！』母女埋伏於雞鷹必經之路，擒之，押回帳中，逼其於火上出汗受罰。藍鷹知弟落難，前往救出，使之復原。翌日遍尋群獸，雞鷹與藍鷹自此不再落魄。

sensitivity.note: Condensed paraphrase of a Kutenai tale recorded by Chamberlain (Boas, 1918); not verbatim. Published folk-narrative only. Category 'myth'.

passages.text: There was the Toad. With him was Golden Eagle. Toad said: 'Let us go! Chicken Hawk and Blue Hawk shall be our husbands.' Then he was her husband. He was skillful; he caught Deer. One morning he was watching the Deer. In the morning Toad said: 'I'll go with you.' Then he started; he watched the Deer and everything — mountain sheep, rams. Chicken Hawk and Toad went along. His stone was hard. Chicken Hawk thought: 'I'll kill her.' He killed Toad.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, pp. 41-42 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 從前有蟾蜍。金鵰與她同在。蟾蜍說：「我們走吧！雞鷹與藍鷹將作我們的丈夫。」於是他就成了她的丈夫。他技藝嫻熟；他獵得了鹿。一天早晨，他正守望著鹿。早晨，蟾蜍說：「我要與你同去。」於是他就出發了；他守望著鹿以及一切——山羊、公羊。雞鷹與蟾蜍一同前行。他的石頭堅硬。雞鷹心想：「我要殺了她。」他殺了蟾蜍。

passages.text: Chicken Hawk started back to his tent; Toad was seen by her parents. She was taken; they went to their tent. The mother of Toad was angry. The mother of Toad said: 'Let us go!' They started. She said: 'Chicken Hawk passes by here.' The two, Toad and her mother, stayed there; Chicken Hawk was watched for. They saw Chicken Hawk coming along; Toad and her mother were in hiding. Chicken Hawk arrived: he was taken, carried back to the tent. He was poor; he was made to perspire over the fire.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 42 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 雞鷹動身回他的帳篷；蟾蜍被她的父母看見了。她被帶走；他們回到他們的帳篷。蟾蜍的母親發怒了。蟾蜍的母親說：「我們走吧！」他們出發了。她說：「雞鷹從這裡經過。」蟾蜍與她的母親二人留在那裡；他們守候著雞鷹。他們看見雞鷹一路走來；蟾蜍與她的母親躲藏著。雞鷹到了：他被捉住，被帶回帳篷。他貧弱；他被逼在火上出汗。

passages.text: He was poor; Blue Hawk knew that his younger brother was poor. He went; he took his younger brother; he went to take him. Blue Hawk restored his younger brother. On the following day he looked for all kinds of animals. He was well. Chicken Hawk and Blue Hawk were no longer poor.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 42 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他貧弱；藍鷹知道他的弟弟貧弱。他去了；他帶走了他的弟弟；他去接他。藍鷹使他的弟弟復原。次日，他尋覓各種各樣的動物。他好了。雞鷹與藍鷹不再貧弱。

title.en: Race of Frog and Antelope
title.zh: 蛙與羚羊賽跑

region.en: Race-course of the Kutenai plains (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 庫特內平原賽道（象徵定位）

period: Told by Michel to A. F. Chamberlain, 1891; published 1918 (Boas, BAE Bulletin 59)

source.work: Franz Boas, Kutenai Tales, Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 59 (1918) — No. 29, 'Race of Frog and Antelope'

summary.en: Frog proposes to race Antelope, a fast runner never beaten; going to his tent, Frog tells all the Frogs 'Do this' — and all the Frogs lie down along the course. Frog puts down her clothes, Antelope puts down his, and they start; Antelope does not run fast, and Frog goes fast, gets ahead of Antelope, takes her clothes, and starts again — while all the Frogs lie there. Antelope was hungry and thirsty; in the evening all the Frogs started and got ahead of Antelope.
summary.zh: 蛙倡言與羚羊賽跑——羚羊善跑，從未落敗。至其帳，蛙呼眾蛙『照做』，群蛙沿道而臥。蛙與羚羊各自寬衣；起跑之後，羚羊未全力，蛙卻飛奔而前，先行脫衣換位——群蛙則沿途輪番臥伏。羚羊飢渴難耐；入夜，群蛙競發，又超羚羊而去。

sensitivity.note: Condensed paraphrase of a Kutenai tale recorded by Chamberlain (Boas, 1918); not verbatim. Relay-race trickster episode. Published folk-narrative only. Category 'myth'.

passages.text: There was Frog. He said: 'Let us go to Antelope's tent! We will race with him.' Antelope was a fast runner; he was never beaten in racing. Frog arrived there. He said to all the Frogs: 'Do this.' All the Frogs lay down. (Frog) put down all her clothes; Antelope put down his clothes. Then he ran fast: they two stood together. He started.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 42 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 從前有青蛙。他說：「我們到羚羊的帳篷去吧！我們要與他賽跑。」羚羊跑得很快；他在賽跑中從未被打敗。青蛙到了那裡。他對所有的青蛙說：「這樣做。」所有的青蛙都躺下了。（青蛙）放下了她所有的衣服；羚羊放下了他的衣服。於是他飛快地跑：他們兩個並立在一起。他出發了。

passages.text: Antelope did not run fast. Then Frog went fast, got ahead of Antelope, and took her clothes; she started again. All the Frogs were lying there. (Antelope) was hungry and thirsty. In the evening all the Frogs started; they got ahead of Antelope.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 42 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 羚羊沒有跑快。於是青蛙跑得快，趕到了羚羊前面，拿走了她的衣服；她又出發了。所有的青蛙都躺在那裡。（羚羊）又飢又渴。傍晚，所有的青蛙出發了；他們趕到了羚羊前面。

title.en: The Woman and the Giant
title.zh: 婦人與巨人

region.en: Giant's killing-ground on the Kutenai trail (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 庫特內小道上巨人殺戮之地（象徵定位）

period: Told by Michel to A. F. Chamberlain, 1891; published 1918 (Boas, BAE Bulletin 59)

source.work: Franz Boas, Kutenai Tales, Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 59 (1918) — No. 30, 'The Woman and the Giant'

summary.en: The Indians travelling along are killed by a Giant, and none return to their tents; one woman with a child starts and meets him. Asked 'What is it?', she says, 'This is your younger brother' — and to 'What did you do to make him so white?' she answers, 'I cooked him to make him white.' The Giant says, 'Cook me likewise,' and she does: when she puts her forked stick into the fire the Giant says, 'Tseika'tkeil' ('It is hot!') — and the woman thrusts him in and he dies.
summary.zh: 印第安人行旅為巨人所殺，無一生還。一婦携子出行，遇巨人。巨人問：『此為何物？』婦答：『此乃你弟弟。』又問：『何以使它如此白嫩？』答：『煮過才白。』巨人曰：『也把我煮了吧！』婦人燒火，將分叉木杖插入火中；巨人呼『燙！』——婦人將他推入火中，巨人遂死。

sensitivity.note: Condensed paraphrase of a Kutenai tale recorded by Chamberlain (Boas, 1918); not verbatim. Published folk-narrative only. Category 'myth'.

passages.text: There were the Indians. They started; they went along. They saw a Giant, who killed them; they did not return to their tents. One woman started; she had a child. She went along; she saw the Giant. She said to him: 'What is it?' The Giant said: 'What are you doing?' The woman said to him: 'This is your younger brother.' He said: 'What did you do to make him so white?' She said to him: 'I cooked him to make him white.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, pp. 42-43 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 從前有印第安人。他們出發了；他們一路前行。他們看見一個巨人，巨人殺了他們；他們沒有回到他們的帳篷。一個女人出發了；她帶著一個孩子。她一路前行；她看見了那巨人。她對他說：「這是什麼？」巨人說：「你在做什麼？」那女人對他說：「這是你的弟弟。」他說：「你做了什麼使他這樣白？」她對他說：「我煮了他，使他變白。」

passages.text: He said: 'Cook me likewise.' She cooked him likewise. Then he said: 'Push it in (with the forked stick).' She put her forked stick into the fire. The Giant said: 'Tseika'tkeil' — it is hot. Then the woman thrust him in, and he died. Enough.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 43 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他說：「你也照樣把我煮了。」她便照樣把他煮了。接著他說：「（用那根叉枝）把它推進去。」她把她的叉枝放進火裡。巨人說：「Tseika'tkeil」——好燙。於是那女人把他推了進去，他就死了。夠了。

title.en: The Sun: Chicken Hawk Proves the Better Sun
title.zh: 太陽：雞鷹稱職

region.en: Sun-making place far away (symbolic pin in Kutenai country)
region.zh: 遠方製日之所（象徵定位於庫特內故地）

period: Told by Angi McLaughlin (Lower Kutenai); collected by A. F. Chamberlain, 1891; published 1918 (Boas, BAE Bulletin 59)

source.work: Franz Boas, Kutenai Tales, Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 59 (1918) — No. 33, 'The Sun'

summary.en: Coyote travels with Chicken Hawk to the far place where the people are making the sun; Coyote claims 'I'll be the sun' first, Chicken Hawk claims 'I first', and Coyote refuses. On the way Chicken Hawk teaches the test: grease will be there, and when people pass they bite off a piece. Chicken Hawk bites off his piece and passes; Coyote takes it, the grease falls down, and Coyote goes rolling along. In the evening Coyote says 'I first', and sets out early — after a little while it is evening: Coyote is a bad sun. 'Now I, now I myself shall start,' says Chicken Hawk, and the sun rises: Chicken Hawk was a good sun. Coyote, angry, thinks to shoot Chicken Hawk — his arrow and his bow are all burned, the earth all burned; running with everything on fire, he comes to a trail and lies down there: the trail did not burn. 'I am glad that I am not dead.'
summary.zh: 郊狼與雞鷹同赴遠方製日之地。郊狼搶言『吾先為日』，雞鷹亦稱『我先』，郊狼不允。途中雞鷹授以試煉之法：彼處有油脂，行人經過皆咬取一片。雞鷹咬而過；郊狼咬之，油脂墜地，滾落塵埃。傍晚郊狼搶先昇日，未幾天又黑——郊狼乃劣日。雞鷹曰：『如今輪到我了！』遂昇日——雞鷹乃善日。郊狼怒欲射之；其箭其弓俱化為灰，大地盡焚。他奔逃於火海之中，得一道路，臥其上——道路未焚。郊狼曰：『幸而不死。』

sensitivity.note: Condensed paraphrase of a Kutenai sun-making narrative recorded by Chamberlain (Boas, 1918); not verbatim. Published folk-narrative only. Category 'myth'.

passages.text: Coyote went along with Chicken Hawk. Coyote said: 'Let us go there far away, where the people are making the sun.' Coyote said first: 'I'll be the sun.' (Chicken Hawk said:) 'I first.' Coyote said: 'No.' Then they started; they went along. Chicken Hawk said: 'You shall listen to me.' Coyote said: 'What is it?' Chicken Hawk said: 'It is where we are going.' Coyote said: 'What is it?' (Chicken Hawk said:) 'Then we'll stay over there. There will be grease. When people pass, they bite off a piece.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 48 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 郊狼與雞鷹同行。郊狼說：「我們到那邊遠方去吧，那裡的人們正在造太陽。」郊狼先說：「我來當太陽。」（雞鷹說：）「我先。」郊狼說：「不行。」於是他們出發了；他們一路前行。雞鷹說：「你要聽我的。」郊狼說：「什麼事？」雞鷹說：「就是我們要去的地方。」郊狼說：「什麼事？」（雞鷹說：）「那我們就待在那邊。那裡會有油脂。人們經過時，就咬下一塊。」

passages.text: They arrived there; Chicken Hawk bit off a piece. 'Now you,' said Chicken Hawk. Then Chicken Hawk passed; then Coyote took it. The grease fell down; Coyote went rolling along. Then Coyote started; he went quickly. Chicken Hawk overtook him: 'Listen to me, what I tell you' — then he did not speak. They arrived there; then in the evening Coyote said: 'I first.' Chicken Hawk said: 'No.' Then they started early. After a little while it was evening; Coyote arrived. The people said: 'Coyote is bad.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 48 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們到了那裡；雞鷹咬下一塊。「現在換你。」雞鷹說。於是雞鷹過去了；接著郊狼拿了它。油脂掉了下來；郊狼一路滾著走。於是郊狼出發了；他走得很快。雞鷹追上他：「聽我的，聽我告訴你的」——接著他就不說話了。他們到了那裡；到了傍晚，郊狼說：「我先。」雞鷹說：「不行。」於是他們一早就出發。過了一會兒，天就晚了；郊狼到了。人們說：「郊狼真糟糕。」

passages.text: After a little while Chicken Hawk said: 'Now I, now I myself shall start.' Thus spoke Chicken Hawk; then the sun rose. Chicken Hawk was a good sun. Coyote was angry; he thought he would shoot Chicken Hawk. Coyote's arrow burned; his arrow and his bow were all burned; he put it down. The earth was all burned. He started running, and everything was on fire; he did not know what to do. He came to a trail and lay down there; the trail did not burn. Then Coyote said: 'I am glad that I am not dead.' Enough.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 48 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 過了一會兒，雞鷹說：「現在我，現在我自己要出發了。」雞鷹這樣說道；於是太陽升起了。雞鷹是個好太陽。郊狼很生氣；他想射雞鷹。郊狼的箭燒了起來；他的箭和他的弓全都燒了；他把它放下。大地全燒了。他開始奔跑，一切都在燃燒；他不知道該怎麼辦。他來到一條小徑，便躺在那裡；那小徑沒有燒起來。於是郊狼說：「我很高興我沒死。」夠了。

title.en: Fox and Skunk: The Pot and the Whistle
title.zh: 狐與臭鼬：鍋與哨聲

region.en: River-drinking place of the Kutenai trail (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 庫特內小道河畔飲水處（象徵定位）

period: Told by Angi McLaughlin (Lower Kutenai); collected by A. F. Chamberlain, 1891; published 1918 (Boas, BAE Bulletin 59)

source.work: Franz Boas, Kutenai Tales, Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 59 (1918) — No. 34, 'Fox and Skunk'

summary.en: Skunk goes along carrying Fox in his pot, saying 'There is nothing I am afraid of — the only thing I am afraid of is whistling'; the sound of whistling comes, Skunk runs away, and Fox breaks the pot and starts. Skunk arrives and sees his pot broken, cries, and thinks he will kill Fox. Coming to a river to drink, he sees Fox inside the water, squirts his fluid at him, becomes tired, lies down and looks up — Fox is above; he turns around to squirt again, but Fox shot him. Enough.
summary.zh: 臭鼬負鍋而行，鍋中藏狐。臭鼬自誇無所畏懼——『唯懼哨聲』。哨聲忽起，臭鼬大驚而逃；狐趁機破鍋而去。臭鼬至，見鍋破，哭而思復仇。至河欲飲，見水中狐影，噴射臭液；力竭臥地仰視——狐竟在其上方。他翻身欲再噴，狐一箭將其射死。

sensitivity.note: Condensed paraphrase of a Kutenai tale recorded by Chamberlain (Boas, 1918); not verbatim. Published folk-narrative only. Category 'myth'.

passages.text: Skunk was going along. There was Fox; he carried a pot (that is, Fox was in the pot that Skunk was carrying). He wanted to sit down; he put down his pot. He went along. (Skunk) said: 'There is nothing I am afraid of.' He said: 'The only thing I am afraid of is whistling.' Then he sat down; Fox arose. There was the sound of whistling; Skunk ran away. Fox broke the pot; Fox started.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 48 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 臭鼬一路走著。有隻狐狸；他帶著一個鍋（也就是說，狐狸在臭鼬所帶的鍋裡）。他想坐下來；他放下了他的鍋。他一路走著。（臭鼬）說：「我什麼都不怕。」他說：「我唯一怕的就是吹口哨。」於是他坐了下來；狐狸起來了。傳來了吹口哨的聲音；臭鼬逃走了。狐狸打破了鍋；狐狸出發了。

passages.text: Skunk arrived; he saw that his pot was broken. He cried; he thought he would kill Fox. Then Skunk started. He saw a river; he was going to drink. He saw Fox inside the water; then he squirted his fluid at him. He became tired; he lay down and looked up. He saw Fox, being above. Then he turned around; he thought he would squirt his fluid at him, but Fox shot him. Enough.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, pp. 48-49 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 臭鼬到了；他看見他的鍋破了。他哭了；他想殺死狐狸。於是臭鼬出發了。他看見一條河；他要去喝水。他看見水裡有狐狸；於是朝他噴射他的液體。他累了；他躺下並向上看。他看見狐狸在上方。於是他轉過身；他想朝他噴射他的液體，但狐狸射了他。夠了。

title.en: Coyote and Caribou
title.zh: 郊狼與馴鹿

region.en: Young-grass meadows of the Kutenai (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 庫特內嫩草草甸（象徵定位）

period: Told by Angi McLaughlin (Lower Kutenai); collected by A. F. Chamberlain, 1891; published 1918 (Boas, BAE Bulletin 59)

source.work: Franz Boas, Kutenai Tales, Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 59 (1918) — No. 35, 'Coyote and Caribou'

summary.en: There were two — Coyote and Caribou. Caribou started; Coyote was angry and thought he would kill Caribou, asking, 'Why does it take you so long?' Caribou said, 'I eat small grass and I quickly get fat.' Coyote killed Caribou; Coyote came along, entered Caribou's tent — Caribou was dead. Coyote cried and said, 'I loved my friend.' Enough.
summary.zh: 郊狼與馴鹿同行。馴鹿先行；郊狼怒而欲殺之，問：『為何如此遲緩？』馴鹿答：『我食嫩草，易於長肥。』郊狼遂誅馴鹿，入其帳——鹿已死。郊狼哭曰：『吾深愛吾友。』

sensitivity.note: Condensed paraphrase of a Kutenai tale recorded by Chamberlain (Boas, 1918); not verbatim. Published folk-narrative only. Category 'myth'.

passages.text: There were two — (Coyote and) Caribou. Caribou started; Coyote was angry. He thought he would kill Caribou. Coyote said: 'Why does it take you so long?' Caribou said: 'I eat small grass and I quickly get fat.' Coyote killed Caribou; Coyote came along. He entered (Caribou's) tent; Caribou was dead. Coyote cried. He said: 'I loved my friend.' Enough.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 51 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 從前有兩個——（郊狼與）馴鹿。馴鹿先動身；郊狼發怒了。他想他要把馴鹿殺死。郊狼說：「你為什麼要這麼久？」馴鹿說：「我吃小草，很快就長肥了。」郊狼殺了馴鹿；郊狼一路走來。他走進（馴鹿的）帳篷；馴鹿已經死了。郊狼哭了。他說：「我愛我的朋友。」夠了。

title.en: Coyote and Owl: The Child-Stealer Danced to Death
title.zh: 郊狼與鴞：誘賊共舞

region.en: Evening camp where Owl steals children (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 鴞夜竊孩童之營地（象徵定位）

period: Told by Angi McLaughlin (Lower Kutenai); collected by A. F. Chamberlain, 1891; published 1918 (Boas, BAE Bulletin 59)

source.work: Franz Boas, Kutenai Tales, Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 59 (1918) — No. 36, 'Coyote and Owl'

summary.en: Owl stole children; Coyote said, 'I'll be a child,' and cried in the evening — 'You make a bad noise; Owl may almost take you away,' he was told, and Coyote was taken. He was thrown out of the doorway and Owl took him along; carrying him along, Coyote said, 'I am Coyote.' Owl was told, 'Let us dance!' — Coyote and Owl danced, and Coyote killed Owl, who had stolen the children. They started back, and he said, 'I killed Owl.' Enough.
summary.zh: 鴞專竊孩童。郊狼自言『吾扮孩童』，夜間啼哭——人告之：『哭聲太兇，鴞幾乎要來抓你了。』郊狼果被擄，拋出門外，為鴞所負。途中郊狼自報：『我是郊狼。』有人對鴞說：『我們跳舞吧！』郊狼與鴞共舞，郊狼趁機誅殺這個偷孩子的鴞。他返回後宣告：『我殺了鴞。』

sensitivity.note: Condensed paraphrase of a Kutenai tale recorded by Chamberlain (Boas, 1918); not verbatim. Published folk-narrative only. Category 'myth'.

passages.text: Owl stole children. Coyote said: 'I'll be a child.' Coyote cried in the evening. He was told: 'You make a bad noise; Owl may almost take you away.' Coyote was taken; he was thrown out of the doorway. Owl took him along; he carried him along. He said: 'I am Coyote.' Owl was told: 'Let us dance!' Coyote and Owl danced; Coyote killed Owl, who had stolen the children. They started back. He said: 'I killed Owl.' Enough.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 51 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 貓頭鷹偷走了孩子。郊狼說：「我要變成一個孩子。」郊狼在傍晚哭叫。有人對他說：「你弄出難聽的聲音；貓頭鷹說不定會把你帶走。」郊狼被帶走了；他被扔出門外。貓頭鷹把他帶在身邊；他一路帶著他走。他說：「我是郊狼。」有人對貓頭鷹說：「我們來跳舞吧！」郊狼和貓頭鷹跳起舞來；郊狼殺了貓頭鷹，那貓頭鷹曾偷走孩子。他們動身回去。他說：「我殺了貓頭鷹。」夠了。

title.en: Coyote and Deer: The Talking War-Bonnet
title.zh: 郊狼與鹿：會說話的戰盔

region.en: Windy trail where the head is held in the hand (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 風中小道，手托人頭之處（象徵定位）

period: Told by Angi McLaughlin (Lower Kutenai); collected by A. F. Chamberlain, 1891; published 1918 (Boas, BAE Bulletin 59)

source.work: Franz Boas, Kutenai Tales, Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 59 (1918) — No. 37, 'Coyote and Deer'

summary.en: Coyote went along and saw Deer, and thought he would kill him; the wind was blowing and frightened him. He did thus to it, and went on; he stood there holding his head in the hand. Coyote said, 'Is that your father's war bonnet?' — and the thing said, 'What is it? Do you forget that you killed me?' Coyote said, 'I thought it was nothing.' Enough.
summary.zh: 郊狼行路遇鹿，欲殺之；風起，將其嚇退。他如此對付風，繼續前行；途中見一手托之人頭。郊狼問：『這是你父親的戰盔嗎？』人頭答：『什麼？你忘了是你殺了我嗎？』郊狼曰：『我以為無妨。』

sensitivity.note: Condensed paraphrase of a Kutenai tale recorded by Chamberlain (Boas, 1918); not verbatim. Published folk-narrative only. Category 'myth'.

passages.text: He went along; he saw Deer. He thought he would kill him; the wind was blowing and frightened him. He did thus to it; he went on. He stood there holding (in the hand) his head thus. Coyote said: 'Is that your father's war bonnet?' The thing said: 'What is it? Do you forget that you killed me?' Coyote said: 'I thought it was nothing.' Enough.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kutenai Tales, p. 51 (Boas, 1918); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他一路走去；他看見了鹿。他想他要把鹿殺死；風正吹著，使他害怕。他對它如此這般做了；他繼續前行。他站在那裡，這樣用手拿著他的頭。郊狼說：「那是你父親的戰冠嗎？」那東西說：「這是什麼？你忘了是你殺了我嗎？」郊狼說：「我以為那不算什麼。」夠了。

title.en: The Six Days of Creation
title.zh: 六日創造

region.en: Eden plain, Tigris–Euphrates headwaters (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伊甸平原，兩河流域上游（象徵性定位）

period: Genesis 1-2, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 1-2

summary.en: Over six days God calls light, sky, land, plants, sun and moon, animals, and finally humanity — male and female in his own image — out of a formless, watery deep; he surveys it all as very good and hallows the seventh day of rest. For Christian readers the Spirit moving on the waters is read as the Spirit of God active in creation.
summary.zh: 六日之中，神自幽暗深淵依次造出光、穹蒼、大地、草木、日月、走獸，末造人類——按神形像造男造女；神觀其所造盡皆甚好，並定第七日為聖。基督徒讀之，見神的靈運行水面，參贊化育。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Christianity (and Judaism). Presented as a comparative cosmogony alongside other creation narratives — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters. And God said, Let there be light: and there was light. And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.
passages.zh: 起初，神創造天地。地是空虛混沌，淵面黑暗；神的靈運行在水面上。神說：「要有光」，就有了光。神看光是好的，就把光暗分開了。

passages.text: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it.
passages.zh: 神說：「我們要照著我們的形像、按著我們的樣式造人，使他們管理海裡的魚、空中的鳥、地上的牲畜，和全地。」神就照著自己的形像造人，乃是照著神的形像造他；造男造女。神就賜福給他們，又對他們說：「要生養眾多，遍滿地面，治理這地。」

passages.text: Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them. And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.
passages.zh: 天地萬物都造齊了。到第七日，神造物的工已經完畢，就在第七日歇了他一切的工，安息了。神賜福給第七日，定為聖日；因為在這日，神歇了他一切創造的工，就安息了。

title.en: The Garden of Eden and the First Marriage
title.zh: 伊甸園與第一樁婚姻

region.en: Eden, by the four-headed river (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伊甸園，四河之源（象徵性定位）

period: Genesis 2, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 2

summary.en: The LORD God shapes Adam from dust, breathes life into him, plants Eden with its two fateful trees, and gives him the first command; naming every beast shows him that no partner is found — so God builds Eve from Adam's rib, and the first marriage charter is spoken.
summary.zh: 耶和華神以塵土造亞當，吹生氣使其活；植伊甸園，立二樹，賜首誡。為野地走獸命名之際，配偶終不可得，神遂取亞當之肋骨造夏娃；人要離開父母，與妻子連合，二人成為一體。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The rib-birth and marriage charter are presented as a comparative narrative of humans molded from earth.

passages.text: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul. And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed. And out of the ground made the LORD God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.
passages.zh: 耶和華神用地上的塵土造人，將生氣吹在他鼻孔裡，他就成了有靈的活人。耶和華神在東方的伊甸立了一個園子，把所造的人安置在那裡。耶和華神使各樣的樹從地裡長出來，可以悅人的眼目，其上的果子好作食物；園子當中又有生命樹和分別善惡的樹。

passages.text: And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it. And the LORD God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat: but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
passages.zh: 耶和華神將那人安置在伊甸園，使他修理看守。耶和華神吩咐他說：園中各樣樹上的果子，你可以隨意吃；只是分別善惡樹上的果子，你不可吃，因為你吃的日子必定死。

passages.text: And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; and the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
passages.zh: 耶和華神使他沉睡，他就睡了；於是取下他的一條肋骨，又把肉合起來。耶和華神就用那人身上所取的肋骨造成一個女人，領她到那人跟前。那人說：這是我骨中的骨，肉中的肉，可以稱她為女人，因為她是從男人身上取出來的。因此，人要離開父母，與妻子連合，二人成為一體。

title.en: The Fall: Serpent, Fruit, and Exile
title.zh: 墮落：蛇、禁果與逐出

region.en: Eden, the tree in the midst (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伊甸園，園中樹下（象徵性定位）

period: Genesis 3, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 3

summary.en: The subtle serpent persuades Eve that eating the forbidden fruit brings godlike knowledge instead of death; she and Adam eat, their eyes are opened, and shame arrives. Curses fall on serpent, woman, and ground, and a flaming sword closes Eden — in Christian reading the moment death, toil, and the promise of the woman's seed bruising the serpent's head enter the world.
summary.zh: 狡蛇誘夏娃：食禁果者眼目明亮，如神能知善惡。二人食之，赤裸知羞；蛇、女、地皆受咒詛，耕作汗顏，死亡入世。基於第三章十五節「女人後裔將傷蛇首」，基督教讀之為原始福音，而基路伯與火劍封閉生命樹之路。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Presented as the Hebrew-Christian origin-of-death narrative; serpent imagery tagged as world-serpent is an interpretive act, noted here.

passages.text: Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden? And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die: for God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil. And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.
passages.zh: 耶和華神所造的，惟有蛇比田野一切的活物更狡猾。蛇對女人說：神豈是真說不許你們吃園中所有樹上的果子嗎？蛇對女人說：你們不一定死，因為神知道，你們吃的日子眼睛就明亮了，你們便如神能知道善惡。於是女人見那棵樹的果子好作食物，也悅人的眼目，且是可喜愛的，能使人有智慧，就摘下果子來吃了，又給她丈夫，她丈夫也吃了。

passages.text: And the LORD God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life: and I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel. Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children. And unto Adam he said, cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; in the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
passages.zh: 耶和華神對蛇說：你既做了這事，就必受咒詛，比一切的牲畜野獸更甚；你必用肚子行走，終身吃土。我又要叫你和女人彼此為仇，你的後裔和女人的後裔也彼此為仇；女人的後裔要傷你的頭，你要傷他的腳跟。又對女人說：我必多多加增你懷胎的苦楚，你生產兒女必多受苦楚。又對亞當說：地必為你的緣故受咒詛；你必終身勞苦，才能從地裡得吃的；你必汗流滿面才得糊口，直到你歸了土，因為你是從土而出的；你本是塵土，仍要歸於塵土。

passages.text: And the LORD God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever: therefore the LORD God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken. So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.
passages.zh: 耶和華神說：那人已經與我們相似，能知道善惡；現在恐怕他伸手又摘生命樹的果子吃，就永遠活著。耶和華神便打發他出伊甸園去，耕種他所自出之土。於是把他趕出去了；又在伊甸園的東邊安設基路伯和四面轉動發火焰的劍，要把守生命樹的道路。

title.en: Cain and Abel: The First Death
title.zh: 該隱與亞伯：首樁死亡

region.en: Field east of Eden, land of Nod (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伊甸東野，流浪之地（象徵性定位）

period: Genesis 4, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 4

summary.en: God respects Abel's firstling offering but not Cain's fruit of the ground; sin crouches at the door, and in the field Cain kills his brother — the first death in scripture. Cursed from the earth, marked so none may slay him, Cain wanders east of Eden; Abel's blood crying from the ground became a Christian figure of innocent blood and of the founder of the 'city of man'.
summary.zh: 神悅納亞伯羊羔之祭，不納該隱地裏所出；罪伏於門前，該隱怒而殺弟——聖經首樁死亡。該隱受詛咒漂流，得七倍之護佑記號。其血從地裏哀告，基督教傳統以之喻義人之血，而該隱建城，被解讀為人之城之濫觴。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Christianity and Judaism. Included as the canonical origin-of-death narrative; scholarly framing only.

passages.text: And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the LORD had respect unto Abel and to his offering: but unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell. And the LORD said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.
passages.zh: 亞伯也將他羊群中頭生的和羊的脂油獻上。耶和華看中了亞伯和他的供物，只是看不中該隱和他的供物。該隱就大大地發怒，變了臉色。耶和華對該隱說：「你為什麼發怒？為什麼變了臉色呢？你若行得好，豈不蒙悅納？你若行得不好，罪就伏在門前。」

passages.text: And it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him. And the LORD said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother's keeper? And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground. And now art thou cursed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother's blood from thy hand; when thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength; a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth.
passages.zh: 二人正在田間，該隱起來攻擊他兄弟亞伯，把他殺了。耶和華對該隱說：「你兄弟亞伯在哪裡？」他說：「我不知道！我豈是看守我兄弟的嗎？」耶和華說：「你做了什麼事呢？你兄弟的血有聲音從地裡向我哀告。地開了口，從你手裡接受你兄弟的血。現在你必從這地受咒詛。你種地，地不再給你效力；你必流離飄蕩在地上。」

passages.text: And Cain said unto the LORD, My punishment is greater than I can bear. Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth; and it shall come to pass, that every one that findeth me shall slay me. And the LORD said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the LORD set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him. And Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.
passages.zh: 該隱對耶和華說：「我的刑罰太重，過於我所能當的。你如今趕逐我離開這地，以致不見你面；我必流離飄蕩在地上，凡遇見我的必殺我。」耶和華對他說：「凡殺該隱的，必遭報七倍。」耶和華就給該隱立一個記號，免得人遇見他就殺他。於是該隱離開耶和華的面，去住在伊甸東邊挪得之地。

title.en: The Line of Cain: Shepherds, Singers, Smiths
title.zh: 該隱之系：牧者、歌者、鐵匠

region.en: Land of Nod, city of Enoch (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 流浪之地，以諾城（象徵性定位）

period: Genesis 4, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 4

summary.en: In Cain's exiled line the arts of civilization are founded: Enoch builds the first city, Jabal the tents and cattle of herders, Jubal the harp and organ of music, Tubalcain the forging of brass and iron — while Lamech's boast of a blood-vengeance seventy-sevenfold darkens the lineage. In Christian tradition this culture-registry is shadowed by the city of man, set against the line of Seth that began to call on the name of the LORD.
summary.zh: 文明之藝起於該隱流放之系：以諾築首城，雅八創畜牧帳棚，猶八創琴瑟之音，土八該隱冶銅打鐵；而拉麥誇口復仇七十七倍，血染世系。基督教釋經以人之城對照塞特之系——彼時人才求告耶和華的名。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The inventor catalogue is presented as an etiological genealogy of the crafts.

passages.text: And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch. And Adah bare Jabal: he was the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle. And his brother's name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ. And Zillah, she also bare Tubalcain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron.
passages.zh: 該隱與妻子同房，他妻子就懷孕，生了以諾。該隱建造了一座城，就按著他兒子的名，將那城叫作以諾。亞大生了雅八；雅八就是住帳棚、牧養牲畜之人的祖師。雅八的兄弟名叫猶八；他是一切彈琴吹簫之人的祖師。洗拉又生了土八該隱；他是打造各樣銅鐵利器的祖師。

passages.text: And Lamech said unto his wives, Adah and Zillah, Hear my voice; ye wives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: for I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt. If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold. And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: for God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew. And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.
passages.zh: 拉麥對他兩個妻子說：「亞大、洗拉，聽我的聲音；拉麥的妻子，細聽我的話語：壯年人傷我，我把他殺了；少年人損我，我把他害了。若殺該隱，遭報七倍，殺拉麥，必遭報七十七倍。」亞當又與妻子同房，她就生了一個兒子，起名叫塞特，意思說：「神另給我立了一個兒子代替亞伯，因為該隱殺了他。」塞特也生了一個兒子，起名叫以挪士。那時候，人才求告耶和華的名。

title.en: Enoch Walked with God, and Was Not
title.zh: 以諾與神同行，不見於世

region.en: The patriarchal line of Seth (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 塞特譜系（象徵性定位）

period: Genesis 5 with Jude 14-15, Genesis c. 6th-5th century BCE; Jude 1st century CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Genesis 5 and Jude 1

summary.en: Amid the nine-hundred-year patriarchs of Genesis 5, Enoch alone walks with God, lives 365 years, and simply 'was not; for God took him' — scripture's first bodily translation to heaven. Christian tradition made him the archetype of the rapture, and the Epistle of Jude quotes Enoch as a prophet foretelling the Lord's coming with ten thousands of his saints.
summary.zh: 創世記譜系中壽數近千的族長之間，唯以諾與神同行三百年，三百六十五歲而「不見於世，因神取了他去」——聖經首位活升天者。基督教傳統以之為被提原型；猶大書更引以諾為先知，預言主偕萬聖降臨。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The translation of Enoch is presented alongside other taken-up narratives.

passages.text: And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah: and Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters: and all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years: and Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.
passages.zh: 以諾活到六十五歲，生了瑪土撒拉。以諾生瑪土撒拉之後，與神同行三百年，並且生兒養女。以諾共活了三百六十五歲。以諾與神同行，神將他取去，他就不在世了。

passages.text: And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, to execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.
passages.zh: 亞當的七世孫以諾也曾預言這些人說：「看哪，主帶著他的千萬聖者降臨，要對眾人施行審判，又要使一切不敬虔的人，因他們所妄行的一切不敬虔的事，以及一切不敬虔的罪人所說頂撞他的剛愎話，都受責備。」

title.en: Sons of God and the Nephilim
title.zh: 神之子與拿非利巨人

region.en: Antediluvian earth (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 洪水前之世界（象徵性定位）

period: Genesis 6:1-4, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 6

summary.en: When humanity multiplies, the 'sons of God' take the daughters of men as wives, and their children are the Nephilim — the giants, mighty men of old, men of renown. With this mixing of the divine and human orders God limits the human span to 120 years; Christian interpretive tradition (building on 1 Enoch) read the sons of God as fallen angels, the Watchers who taught forbidden arts and fathered the giants.
summary.zh: 人類繁衍之際，神之子見人之女子美，遂娶為妻；其子即拿非利——上古英武有名之巨人。神於是將人的年日限為一百二十年。基督教釋經（承《以諾一書》）視「神之子」為墮落天使即守望者，教人禁術，生下巨人。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Tagging the sons of God with divine-marriage is an interpretive act comparing divine-human unions across traditions; the giant tag follows the LXX/traditional reading of Nephilim as giants, noted here.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them, that the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose. And the LORD said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.
passages.zh: 當人在世上多起來，又生女兒的時候，神的兒子們看見人的女子美貌，就隨意挑選，娶來為妻。耶和華說：「人既屬乎血氣，我的靈就不永遠住在他裡面；然而他的日子還可到一百二十年。」

passages.text: There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown. And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
passages.zh: 那時有巨人在地上，後來也是如此；那時神的兒子們與人的女子交合生子，那就是上古英武有名的人。耶和華見人在地上罪惡很大，終日所思想的盡都是惡。

title.en: Noah and the Flood
title.zh: 挪亞與大洪水

region.en: The ark, resting on the mountains of Ararat
region.zh: 方舟，止於亞拉臘山

period: Genesis 6-9, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 6-9

summary.en: God, grieved that every imagination of the human heart is evil, resolves to destroy all flesh with a flood and commands the just Noah to build a three-deck ark of gopher wood. The fountains of the great deep break up, rain falls forty days, all life drowns except the ark's eight souls and their beasts; a dove bearing an olive leaf announces the dry land, and God smells Noah's sacrifice, vowing never again to curse the ground, sealing the covenant with a bow in the cloud.
summary.zh: 神見人心所思盡惡，決以洪水滅絕血氣；命義人挪亞造歌斐木三層方舟。大淵泉源裂開，天窗敞開，暴雨四十日，生靈盡滅，唯舟中八口與走獸得存。鴿子銜橄欖葉報干地，神聞馨香之祭，誓言永不咒詛大地，以雲中虹為永約之記。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Christianity and Judaism. Presented as the canonical flood narrative of the cross-tradition deluge cluster — scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually. And it repented the LORD that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart. And the LORD said, I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth; both man, and beast, and the creeping thing, and the fowls of the air; for it repenteth me that I have made them. But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.
passages.zh: 耶和華見人在地上罪惡很大，終日所思想的盡都是惡。耶和華就後悔造人在地上，心中憂傷。耶和華說：「我要將所造的人，從地上除滅，連人帶牲畜、昆蟲，以及空中的飛鳥，都要除滅，因為我造他們後悔了。」惟有挪亞在耶和華眼前蒙恩。

passages.text: Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch. And this is the fashion which thou shalt make it of: The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits. And, behold, I, even I, do bring a flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, from under heaven. But with thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons' wives with thee. Of every living thing of all flesh, two of every sort shalt thou bring into the ark, to keep them alive with thee.
passages.zh: 你要用歌斐木造一隻方舟，分一間一間地造，裡外抹上松香。方舟的造法乃是這樣：要長三百肘，寬五十肘，高三十肘。看哪，我要使洪水氾濫在地上，毀滅天下凡有血氣、有生命氣息的活物。我卻要與你立約；你同你的兒子、妻子、兒婦，都要進入方舟。凡有血肉的活物，每樣兩個，你要帶進方舟，好在你那裡保全生命。

passages.text: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened. And the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights. And the waters prevailed, and were increased greatly upon the earth; and the ark went upon the face of the waters. And the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth; and all the high hills, that were under the whole heaven, were covered. And all flesh died that moved upon the earth: and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.
passages.zh: 當挪亞六百歲，二月十七日那一天，大淵的泉源都裂開了，天上的窗戶也敞開了。四十晝夜降大雨在地上。水勢浩大，在地上大大地往上長，方舟在水面上漂來漂去。水勢在地上極其浩大，天下的高山都淹沒了。凡在地上活動的肉體都死了；他們都從地上被除滅了；只留下挪亞和那些與他同在方舟裡的。

passages.text: And it came to pass at the end of forty days, that Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made: and he sent forth a raven, which went forth to and fro, until the waters were dried up from off the earth. Also he sent forth a dove from him, to see if the waters were abated from off the face of the ground; but the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot, and she returned unto him into the ark. And he stayed yet other seven days; and again he sent forth the dove out of the ark; and, lo, in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.
passages.zh: 過了四十天，挪亞打開他所造的方舟的窗戶，放出一隻烏鴉去；那烏鴉飛來飛去，直到地上的水都乾了。他又從自己那裡放出一隻鴿子去，要看看水從地上退了沒有；但遍地都是水，鴿子找不著落腳之地，就回到方舟他那裡。他又等了七天，再把鴿子從方舟放出去；到了晚上，鴿子回到他那裡，嘴裡叼著一個新擰下來的橄欖葉子，挪亞就知道地上的水退了。

title.en: Noah's Vineyard and the Curse of Canaan
title.zh: 挪亞葡萄園與迦南之咒

region.en: Noah's tent after the flood, near Ararat foothills
region.zh: 洪水後挪亞的帳棚，亞拉臘山麓

period: Genesis 9, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 9

summary.en: After the flood Noah plants a vineyard and lies uncovered in his drunkenness; Ham, father of Canaan, sees and tells his brothers, who walk backward to cover their father. Waking, Noah curses not Ham but Canaan — 'a servant of servants shall he be' — and blesses Shem and Japheth: an etiological curse giving Israelite victory over the Canaanites, later grievously misused; biblical scholars and churches now repudiate its later racial readings.
summary.zh: 洪水後挪亞栽葡萄園，醉臥失衣；含見父赤裸而告二弟，閃與雅弗倒退而進遮蓋之。挪亞醒後咒詛的不是含，而是迦南——「必作奴僕的奴僕」——並祝福閃、雅弗。此為解釋以色列戰勝迦南族的溯源故事；歷史上曾被曲解為種族主義之據，今為教會與學界所唾棄。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. This text's long history of racist 'curse of Ham' misreading is documented and rejected in modern scholarship; included as a boundary-marking curse narrative with that context made explicit.

passages.text: And Noah began to be an husbandman, and he planted a vineyard: and he drank of the wine, and was drunken; and he was uncovered within his tent. And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brethren without. And Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it upon both their shoulders, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces were backward, and they saw not their father's nakedness.
passages.zh: 挪亞作起農夫來，栽了一個葡萄園。他喝了園中的酒便醉了，在帳棚裡赤著身子。迦南的父親含看見他父親赤身，就到外邊告訴他兩個弟兄。於是閃和雅弗拿件衣服搭在肩上，倒退著進去，給他父親蓋上；他們背著臉就看不見父親的赤身。

passages.text: And Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his younger son had done unto him. And he said, Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren. And he said, Blessed be the LORD God of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant. God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.
passages.zh: 挪亞醒了酒，知道小兒子向他所做的事，就說：迦南當受咒詛，必給他弟兄作奴僕的奴僕。又說：耶和華閃的神是應當稱頌的；願迦南作閃的奴僕。願神使雅弗擴張，使他住在閃的帳棚裡；又願迦南作他的奴僕。

title.en: Nimrod and the Tower of Babel
title.zh: 寧錄與巴別塔

region.en: Land of Shinar, plain of Babylon
region.zh: 示拿地，巴比倫平原

period: Genesis 10-11, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 10-11

summary.en: Nimrod, the mighty hunter before the LORD, founds Babel, Erech, Accad, and Nineveh — the beginnings of empire in Shinar. There the whole earth, still of one language, builds a city and a tower whose top may reach heaven, to make a name; the LORD comes down, confounds their speech, and scatters them abroad, leaving the place named Babel. Christian tradition reads the tower as humanity's imperial pride, and Pentecost's gift of tongues as its reversal.
summary.zh: 寧錄為耶和華面前的英勇獵戶，建巴別、以力、亞甲、尼尼微——示拿王國之始。當時天下人口音言語如一，遂築城與通天塔，欲揚己名；耶和華降臨，變亂口音，散眾於全地，遂名巴別。基督教傳統視此塔為人類帝國式狂傲，而五旬節方言恩賜即其逆轉。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as a hubris-and-confusion etiology; the Pentecost reversal is noted as the Christian reading.

passages.text: And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth. He was a mighty hunter before the LORD: wherefore it is said, Even as Nimrod the mighty hunter before the LORD. And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar. Out of that land went forth Asshur, and builded Nineveh.
passages.zh: 古實又生寧錄，他為世上英雄之首。他在耶和華面前是個英勇的獵戶，所以俗語說：像寧錄在耶和華面前是個英勇的獵戶。他國的起頭是巴別、以力、亞甲、甲尼，都在示拿地。他從那地出來往亞述去，建造了尼尼微。

passages.text: And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech. And they said, Go to, let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth. And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men builded. And the LORD said, Behold, the people is one, and they have all one language; and this they begin to do: and now nothing will be restrained from them, which they have imagined to do.
passages.zh: 那時，天下人的口音、言語都是一樣。他們彼此商量說：來吧，我們要作磚，把磚燒透了。他們就拿磚當石頭，又拿石漆當灰泥。他們說：來吧，我們要建造一座城和一座塔，塔頂通天，為要傳揚我們的名，免得我們分散在全地上。耶和華降臨，要看看世人所建造的城和塔。耶和華說：看哪，他們成為一樣的人民，都是一樣的言語，如今既做起這事來，以後他們所要做的事就沒有不成就的了。

passages.text: Go to, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another's speech. So the LORD scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city. Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the LORD did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did the LORD scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.
passages.zh: 我們下去，在那裡變亂他們的口音，使他們的言語彼此不通。於是耶和華使他們從那裡分散在全地上；他們就停工，不造那城了。因為耶和華在那裡變亂天下人的言語，使眾人分散在全地上，所以那城名叫巴別。

title.en: Cain and Abel: The First Murder
title.zh: 該隱與亞伯：第一樁兇案

region.en: Land of Nod, east of Eden (symbolic pin for the wanderer's land)
region.zh: 挪得之地（伊甸以東流浪者之地的象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 4:1-16, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The two sons of Adam and Eve bring offerings; God accepts the shepherd's and rejects the farmer's, and Cain kills his brother in the field. Marked by God so none may kill him, the first murderer becomes a wandering founder.
summary.zh: 亞當夏娃二子獻祭，神悅牧者之祭而拒農者之祭；該隱在田間殺弟。神為其立記號，免人殺之；首殺者遂為流浪而建城者。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; Tetragrammaton rendered 'the LORD'; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Cain knew Abel his brother, and Cain said unto him, 'There is no justice, and there is no Judge, and there is no world to come, and there is no reward for the righteous and punishment for the wicked.' And they strove in the field, and Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.
passages.note: This passage blends a rabbinic aggadic expansion (Genesis Rabbah 22) with the biblical notice of Genesis 4:8; paraphrase of both, not verbatim.
passages.zh: 該隱認識他的兄弟亞伯，該隱對他說：『沒有公義，沒有審判者，沒有來世，義人沒有賞賜，惡人沒有懲罰。』他們在田間爭鬥，該隱起來攻擊他的兄弟亞伯，將他殺了。

passages.text: And the LORD said unto Cain: 'Where is Abel thy brother?' And he said: 'I know not; am I my brother's keeper?' And He said: 'What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto Me from the ground. And now, cursed art thou from the ground, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother's blood from thy hand.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 4:9-11 (public domain).
passages.zh: 耶和華對該隱說：『你兄弟亞伯在哪裡？』他說：『我不知道；我豈是看守我兄弟的嗎？』祂說：『你做了什麼事呢？你兄弟的血有聲音從地裡向我哀告。現在你必從這地受咒詛，這地曾張開它的口，從你手中接受你兄弟的血。』

passages.text: Cain feared that whoever found him would kill him, but God set a mark upon him, that no one should slay him, and he went out from the presence of the LORD and dwelt in the land of Nod, east of Eden. There he built a city and named it after his son. The field had drunk the first blood of human history, and the wandering of the murderer became the founding of the first city. Paraphrase of Genesis 4:12-17 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 4:12-17 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 該隱害怕凡遇見他的都會殺他，但神在他身上立了一個記號，免得人殺他；他就離開耶和華的面，住在伊甸東邊的挪得之地。他在那裡建造了一座城，並以他兒子的名字為城命名。田地飲下了人類歷史上的第一滴血，而殺人者的流浪成了第一座城的建立。改述自《創世記》4:12-17（JPS 1917）；並非逐字照錄。

title.en: Lamech's Boast and the First Crafts
title.zh: 拉麥之歌與最初技藝

region.en: Land of Nod (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 挪得之地（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 4:17-24, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Cain's line founds cities, tents, herds, metallurgy, and music — and escalates vengeance. Lamech sings the first recorded boast-song: 'I have slain a man for wounding me... if Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy and sevenfold.'
summary.zh: 該隱後裔建城、張幕牧畜、鍛造銅鐵、彈琴吹簫；而復仇升級。拉麥唱出首見之誇耀之歌：「傷我者我殺之……該隱遭報七倍，拉麥必遭報七十七倍。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Adah bare Jabal: he was the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle. And his brother's name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and pipe. And Zillah, she also bare Tubal-cain, the forger of every cutting instrument of brass and iron.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 4:20-22 (public domain).
passages.zh: 亞大生了雅八：他是住帳棚、有牲畜之人的祖宗。他兄弟名叫猶八：他是所有彈琴吹簫之人的祖宗。洗拉也生了土八該隱，他是打造各樣銅鐵利器的工匠。

passages.text: Lamech called to his two wives and boasted of his vengeance: he had killed a young man for a wound and would repay injuries seventy-sevenfold — violence multiplying itself down Cain's line. In the same breath, the chapter invents civilization: cities, nomadism, music, and metallurgy all descend from the murderer's family. Paraphrase of Genesis 4:23-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 4:23-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 拉麥呼喚他的兩個妻子，誇耀自己的報復：他因受傷殺了一個少年人，並要報復七十倍——暴力在該隱的血脈中不斷繁衍。就在同一段話中，這一章發明了文明：城市、遊牧、音樂與冶金，全都出自殺人者的家族。改述自《創世記》4:23-24（JPS 1917）；並非逐字照錄。

title.en: Enoch Walked with God, and Was Not
title.zh: 以諾與神同行而不見

region.en: Judean hills (symbolic pin for the silent taking)
region.zh: 猶大山地（無言被取之地的象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 5:21-24, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: In the death-lists of Genesis 5 one man breaks the pattern: Enoch, father of Methuselah, 'walked with God' and was taken without dying — the Bible's first ascension, seeded for the vast apocalyptic books later written under his name.
summary.zh: 創世記五章的死亡譜系中，唯有一人破例：以諾，瑪土撒拉之父，「與神同行」，未死而被取——聖經首次升天，為後世以其名所寫之啟示文學埋下根苗。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah. And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters. And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years. And Enoch walked with God, and he was not; for God took him.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 5:21-24 (public domain).
passages.zh: 以諾活到六十五歲，生了瑪土撒拉。以諾生瑪土撒拉之後，與神同行三百年，並且生兒養女。以諾共活了三百六十五歲。以諾與神同行，神將他取去，他就不在了。

title.en: Noah's Vineyard and the Curse of Canaan
title.zh: 挪亞葡萄園與迦南受咒

region.en: Ararat foothills (symbolic pin; landing region of the ark)
region.zh: 亞拉臘山麓（方舟停靠區之象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 9:18-29, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The world's first vineyard yields the world's first drunkard: Noah lies uncovered in his tent, Ham sees his father's nakedness, and for the act (or its mockery) Noah curses Ham's son Canaan to servitude — the etiological frame the Torah gives for Israel's later relations with the Canaanites.
summary.zh: 世上首座葡萄園造出首位醉者：挪亞赤身臥於帳中，含見父之裸；因所行（或所譏）挪亞咒其子迦南為僕——此為色列後與迦南人關係之釋義框架。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition. The 'curse of Ham' has been misused historically to justify slavery; the record notes the text curses Canaan, not Ham's whole descent, and describes the verse without endorsing later interpretations.

passages.text: And Noah began to be a husbandman, and he planted a vineyard. And he drank of the wine, and was drunken; and he was uncovered within his tent. And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brethren without.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 9:20-22 (public domain).
passages.zh: 挪亞開始作農夫，栽種了一座葡萄園。他喝了園中的酒便醉了，在帳棚裡赤著身子。迦南的父親含看見他父親赤身，就到外邊告訴他的兩個弟兄。

passages.text: Shem and Japheth walked backward with a garment on their shoulders and covered their father without seeing him. Waking, Noah learned what Ham had done and pronounced the curse not on Ham himself but on Ham's youngest son: 'Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.' The passage ends by naming Noah's death at nine hundred and fifty years. Paraphrase of Genesis 9:23-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 9:23-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 閃和雅弗把一件衣服搭在肩上，倒退著走進去，遮蓋了父親的下身，並沒有看見他赤身。挪亞醒來，知道了含所做的事，他所宣告的咒詛不是落在含本人身上，而是落在含最小的兒子身上：「迦南當受咒詛，必給他弟兄作奴僕的奴僕。」這段記載最後提到挪亞死時九百五十歲。此為《創世記》9:23-29（JPS 1917）之改寫，並非逐字引文。

title.en: The Tower of Babel and the Confusion of Tongues
title.zh: 巴別塔與言語變亂

region.en: Babylon, Shinar (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 示拿地巴比倫（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 11:1-9, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: All earth speaks one language and builds a city and a tower 'with its top in heaven, lest we be scattered'. God comes down to look, confuses their language, and scatters them over the earth — the etiological myth of linguistic diversity, aimed at Mesopotamia's ziggurat culture.
summary.zh: 全地同一言語，同建城與塔，「塔頂通天，免得分散」。神降下觀看，變亂其口音，使其分散遍地——語言分歧之釋義神話，鋒芒直指美索不達米亞塔廟文化。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they said: 'Go to, let us build us a city, and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven, and let us make us a name; lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.' And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men builded.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 11:4-5 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他們說：「來吧！我們要建造一座城和一座塔，塔頂通天，為要為自己立名，免得我們分散在全地上。」耶和華降臨，要看看世人所建造的城和塔。

passages.text: The LORD saw that one people with one language could accomplish anything they planned, so He confounded their speech so that no one understood another, halted the building, and scattered them across the earth. The city's name — Babel — is heard as Hebrew 'balal', 'He confounded', punning on the great city Babylon. Paraphrase of Genesis 11:6-9 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 11:6-9 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 耶和華看出，同一個民族、同一種語言，就能成就他們所籌劃的任何事，於是變亂了他們的言語，以致彼此言語不通，使建造的工程停了下來，並把他們分散在全地上。那城名叫巴別，聽來近似希伯來文的「balal」，意為「他變亂了」，是對那座大城巴比倫的雙關語。此為《創世記》11:6-9（JPS 1917）之改寫，並非逐字引文。

title.en: Lech Lecha: Abraham's Call to Go
title.zh: 亞伯拉罕蒙召前往

region.en: Haran to Shechem (route pin at Haran)
region.zh: 自哈蘭至示劍（以哈蘭為路線定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 12:1-9, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: God tells Abram to leave country, kindred, and father's house for a land He will show, promising a great nation, blessing, and a name. Abram obeys at seventy-five, journeys through Canaan, and builds altars at Shechem and Bethel — the founding migration of Israel's history.
summary.zh: 神命亞伯蘭離本土親族父家，往所示之地，許以大國、祝福、大名。亞伯蘭七十五歲即行，經迦南，於示劍、伯特利築壇——以色列歷史之創始遷徙。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Now the LORD said unto Abram: 'Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto the land that I will show thee. And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and be thou a blessing.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 12:1-2 (public domain).
passages.zh: 耶和華對亞伯蘭說：「你要離開本地、本族、父家，往我所要指示你的地去。我必使你成為大國，我必賜福給你，使你的名為大；你也要使別人得福。」

passages.text: Abram went as the LORD had spoken, with Sarai and Lot and all their substance, into the land of Canaan, and passed through to Shechem, to the terebinth of Moreh. The LORD appeared and promised the land to his seed, and he built an altar; then he moved on to the hill country between Bethel and Ai, pitching his tent and calling on the name of the LORD. Paraphrase of Genesis 12:4-9 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 12:4-9 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 亞伯蘭就照著耶和華所吩咐的去了，帶著撒萊、羅得和他們一切所有的，往迦南地去，一路到了示劍地方、摩利的橡樹那裡。耶和華向他顯現，應許把這地賜給他的後裔，他就在那裡築了一座壇；隨後他又遷到伯特利和艾中間的山地，支搭帳棚，求告耶和華的名。此為《創世記》12:4-9（JPS 1917）之改寫，並非逐字引文。

title.en: Sarai in Pharaoh's Court
title.zh: 撒萊在法老宮中

region.en: Egypt, Nile Delta (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 埃及尼羅河三角洲（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 12:10-20, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Famine drives Abram to Egypt; fearing for his life he presents his beautiful wife as his sister, and Pharaoh takes her. Plagues strike Pharaoh's house until the truth is out; Abram is expelled rich — the first of the patriarchal 'sister-wife' episodes that read as foreshadowings of Israel's sojourns.
summary.zh: 饑荒驅亞伯蘭入埃及；恐失性命，以美妻為妹，法老遂取之。法老家遭災，真相大白；亞伯蘭攜財而出——族長「妻妹」敘事之首，預表以色列寄居諸章。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister; that it may be well with me for thy sake, and that my soul may live because of thee. And it came to pass, that, when Abram was come into Egypt, the Egyptians beheld the woman that she was very fair. The princes of Pharaoh also saw her, and praised her to Pharaoh; and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house.
passages.note: Condensed verbatim from JPS 1917, Genesis 12:13-15 (public domain).
passages.zh: 求你這樣說：你是我的妹妹；這樣，因你的緣故，我必得平安，我的性命也因你得以存活。及至亞伯蘭到了埃及，埃及人看見那婦人極其美貌。法老的臣宰也看見了她，就在法老面前誇獎她；那婦人就被帶進法老的王宮。

passages.text: For Sarai's sake the LORD plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues. Pharaoh summoned Abram: 'Why didst thou not tell me that she was thy wife?' and sent him away with his wife and all he had. The epos of Israel's later affliction in Egypt begins, ironically, with its first forefather protected there by plague. Paraphrase of Genesis 12:16-20 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 12:16-20 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 因撒萊的緣故，耶和華降大災於法老和他的家。法老召了亞伯蘭來，說：『你為何沒有告訴我她是你的妻子呢？』便打發他帶著妻子和一切所有的離去。以色列日後在埃及受苦的史詩，說來諷刺，竟以其第一位先祖在埃及因災疫而得保全為開端。此為《創世記》12:16-20（JPS 1917）之改述，非逐字照錄。

title.en: Abram and Lot Divide the Land
title.zh: 亞伯蘭與羅得分地

region.en: Bethel, hill country of Canaan
region.zh: 伯特利，迦南山地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 13, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Herds too large for one land force Abram and his nephew Lot apart. Generous Abram lets Lot choose; Lot picks the well-watered plain of the Jordan, settling near Sodom, while Abram dwells in Canaan and receives the promise of all the land he can see.
summary.zh: 牧畜眾多，地不能容，亞伯蘭與姪羅得分開。亞伯蘭寬宏任其先擇；羅得取約旦滋潤平原，近所多瑪而居；亞伯蘭居迦南，蒙應許舉目所見之地。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Abram said unto Lot: 'Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen; for we are brethren. Is not the whole land before thee? separate thyself, I pray thee, from me: if thou wilt take the left hand, then I will go to the right; or if thou take the right hand, then I will go to the left.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 13:8-9 (public domain).
passages.zh: 亞伯蘭對羅得說：『求你不要與我相爭，你的牧人與我的牧人也不要相爭，因為我們是弟兄。全地不都在你眼前嗎？求你離開我：你若向左，我就向右；你若向右，我就向左。』

passages.text: Lot lifted his eyes to the well-watered plain of the Jordan and journeyed east, pitching toward Sodom, whose men were wicked. After his departure the LORD told Abram to look north, south, east, and west: all the land he saw would be given him and his seed for ever, numerous as the dust of the earth. Paraphrase of Genesis 13:10-17 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 13:10-17 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 羅得舉目，看見約旦河的全平原水源充足，便往東遷移，帳棚漸漸挪移到所多瑪，那地的人卻邪惡。羅得離去之後，耶和華吩咐亞伯蘭舉目，向東南西北觀看：凡他所看見的地，都要賜給他和他的後裔，直到永遠，其後裔多如地上的塵沙。此為《創世記》13:10-17（JPS 1917）之改述，非逐字照錄。

title.en: The War of the Kings and Melchizedek's Bread and Wine
title.zh: 列王之戰與麥基洗德之餅酒

region.en: Valley of Siddim, Dead Sea (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 西訂谷，死海（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 14, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Four eastern kings raid the cities of the plain and carry off Lot; Abram musters 318 retainers, rescues him by night, and refuses all spoil. The mysterious priest-king of Salem, Melchizedek, blesses him with bread and wine — the Bible's first tithe scene and the seed of a whole royal-priestly tradition.
summary.zh: 四東方王掠平原諸城，擄走羅得；亞伯蘭率家丁三百一十八人夜襲救回，不受分毫戰利。撒冷王祭司麥基洗德以餅酒祝之——聖經首次什一奉獻，王祭合一傳統之源。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was priest of God the Most High. And he blessed him, and said: 'Blessed be Abram of God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth; and blessed be God Most High, who hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand.' And he gave him a tenth of all.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 14:18-20 (public domain).
passages.zh: 撒冷王麥基洗德拿出餅和酒來；他是至高神的祭司。他為亞伯蘭祝福，說：『願亞伯蘭蒙至高神、天地的主賜福；願至高神受稱頌，他已將你的仇敵交在你手中。』亞伯蘭就把所得的，拿出十分之一來給他。

passages.text: When Abram defeated the eastern coalition by a night march, the king of Sodom offered him the recovered goods; Abram swore by the LORD, God Most High, that he would not take so much as a sandal-thong, lest the king say 'I have made Abram rich' — save only the shares owed his allies and his men. Paraphrase of Genesis 14:21-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 14:21-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 亞伯蘭趁夜行軍擊敗了東方聯盟之後，所多瑪王要將奪回的財物給他；亞伯蘭指著耶和華、至高神起誓，說連一根鞋帶也不拿，免得所多瑪王說『我使亞伯蘭富足』——只取了他的盟友和隨從所應得的分。此為《創世記》14:21-24（JPS 1917）之改述，非逐字照錄。

title.en: The Covenant Between the Pieces
title.zh: 剖牲之約

region.en: Mamre, Hebron (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 幔利，希伯崙（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 15, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Childless Abram protests that his heir is a servant; God promises seed as the stars and, in a dread-smoking rite of cut animals passing between their halves, seals a covenant foretelling four hundred years of bondage and the deliverance to come — Abraham's first great vision.
summary.zh: 無子的亞伯蘭申訴繼者為僕；神應許後裔如眾星，並於烟與火爐中穿過剖開祭牲之間，立約預告四百年為奴與隨之拯救——亞伯拉罕首次大異象。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And He brought him forth abroad, and said: 'Look now toward heaven, and number the stars, if thou be able to number them'; and He said unto him: 'So shall thy seed be.' And he believed in the LORD; and He counted it to him for righteousness.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 15:5-6 (public domain).
passages.zh: 祂領他走到外邊，說：「你向天觀看，數算眾星，看你能不能數得過來」；又對他說：「你的後裔將要如此。」亞伯蘭信耶和華，耶和華就以此算為他的義。

passages.text: In a deep sleep a dread and great darkness fell on Abram, and God foretold: his seed would be a stranger in a land not theirs, afflicted four hundred years, 'but in the fourth generation they shall come back hither'. Then a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between the pieces of the sacrificed animals — God binding Himself alone while Abram slept. Paraphrase of Genesis 15:12-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 15:12-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在沉沉的沉睡中，有驚人的大黑暗落在亞伯蘭身上，神預言說：他的後裔必寄居在別人的地，受苦四百年，「但到了第四代，他們必回到此地」。隨後有冒煙的爐和燒著的火把從那些獻祭牲畜的肉塊中經過——當亞伯蘭沉睡時，神獨自以自己立約。改寫自《創世記》15:12-21（JPS 1917）；並非逐字照錄。

title.en: Hagar at the Spring: The God Who Sees
title.zh: 夏甲在泉旁：看顧人的神

region.en: Wilderness of Shur, road to Egypt
region.zh: 書珥曠野，往埃及之路

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 16, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Sarai, barren, gives her Egyptian handmaid Hagar to Abram; when Hagar conceives, the two women's rivalry drives the pregnant girl into the wilderness. There an angel finds her by a spring, promises her a countless son, and she becomes the first person in scripture to give God a name: 'El Roi' — the God who sees.
summary.zh: 撒萊不育，以埃及使女夏甲予亞伯蘭；夏甲懷孕，二女相爭，孕者逃入曠野。天使於泉旁遇之，許其子不可勝數；她遂成聖經中首位為神命名者：「看顧人的神」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Hagar's story is also foundational in Islamic tradition (record cross-referenced there).

passages.text: And the angel of the LORD found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur. And he said: 'Hagar, Sarai's handmaid, whence camest thou? and whither goest thou?' And she said: 'I flee from the face of my mistress Sarai.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 16:7-8 (public domain).
passages.zh: 耶和華的使者在曠野的水泉旁，就是往書珥路上的水泉旁遇見她。就說：「撒萊的使女夏甲，你從哪裡來？要往哪裡去？」她說：「我從我的主母撒萊面前逃出來。」

passages.text: The angel promised that her seed would be multiplied beyond counting and named the boy Ishmael, 'God hears'. Hagar answered the first naming-theology in the Bible: 'Thou art a God that seest' — for she said, 'Have I even here seen Him that seeth me?' She returned and bore Abram a son in his eighty-sixth year. Paraphrase of Genesis 16:10-16 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 16:10-16 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 使者應許她的後裔必繁多，不可勝數，並給那男孩起名叫以實瑪利，意即「神聽見」。夏甲回應了聖經中第一個為神命名的神學宣告：「你是看顧人的神」——因為她說：「我在這裡也看見了那看顧我的嗎？」她回去，在亞伯蘭八十六歲那年給他生了一個兒子。改寫自《創世記》16:10-16（JPS 1917）；並非逐字照錄。

title.en: Covenant of Circumcision: The Names Changed
title.zh: 割禮之約：改名之刻

region.en: Mamre, Hebron (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 幔利，希伯崙（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 17, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: God appears to ninety-nine-year-old Abram as El Shaddai, changes his name to Abraham ('father of a multitude') and Sarai's to Sarah, commands circumcision of every male as the covenant's sign 'throughout your generations', and promises the laughter-child Isaac within the year.
summary.zh: 神向九十九歲之亞伯蘭以全能神顯現，改名亞伯拉罕（萬族之父），撒萊改撒拉；命凡男丁割禮為約之記，「世世代代」，並許笑者以撒年內而生。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And I will establish My covenant between Me and thee and thy seed after thee throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee and to thy seed after thee. ... This is My covenant, which ye shall keep, between Me and you and thy seed after thee: every male among you shall be circumcised.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 17:7, 10 (public domain); ellipsis marks omitted verses.
passages.zh: 我要與你並你世世代代的後裔堅立我的約，作永遠的約，是要作你和你後裔的神。……這是我與你並你後裔所立的約，是你們當遵守的：你們中間所有的男子都要受割禮。

passages.text: Abraham fell on his face laughing at the news that a hundred-year-old man and ninety-year-old woman would bear a son, and asked that Ishmael 'might live before Thee'. God answered: the covenant would run through Isaac, born of Sarah, while Ishmael too would father twelve princes and a great nation. That very day Abraham circumcised himself, Ishmael, and every male of his house. Paraphrase of Genesis 17:17-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 17:17-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 亞伯拉罕聽見百歲之人和九十歲的婦人將要生子的消息，就俯伏在地喜笑，並求神使以實瑪利「活在你面前」。神回答說：約要藉撒拉所生的以撒延續，而以實瑪利也必作十二個王子的父，成為大國。就在那一天，亞伯拉罕給自己和以實瑪利，並家中所有的男子都行了割禮。改寫自《創世記》17:17-27（JPS 1917）；並非逐字照錄。

title.en: Three Visitors Under the Terebinths of Mamre
title.zh: 幔利橡樹下之三訪客

region.en: Mamre, Hebron (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 幔利，希伯崙（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 18:1-15, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Abraham runs from his tent to greet three men and serves them a feast; they repeat that Sarah will bear a son. Overhearing from the tent, ninety-year-old Sarah laughs — and God has the last word: 'Is anything too hard for the LORD?'
summary.zh: 亞伯拉罕奔出帳迎三客，設宴款待；三客重申撒拉將生子。撒拉在帳中暗笑——而神有末語：「耶和華豈有難成的事麼？」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The narrative of hospitality (hachnasat orchim) became a foundational rabbinic paradigm of kindness.

passages.text: And the LORD appeared unto him in the plains of Mamre; and he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day; and he lifted up his eyes and looked, and, lo, three men stood over against him; and he saw, and ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed down to the earth.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 18:1-2 (public domain).
passages.zh: 耶和華在幔利的平原向他顯現；他正坐在帳棚門口，那時天氣炎熱；他舉目觀看，見有三個人站在他對面；他一看見，就從帳棚門口跑去迎接他們，俯伏在地。

passages.text: Abraham hurried Sarah to knead cakes, chose a calf, and set curds and milk before the men under the tree. 'Where is Sarah thy wife?' they asked, and repeated the promise. Sarah laughed within the tent, thinking of her worn body and her husband's age, and denied laughing — but the Visitor said: 'Nay; but thou didst laugh.' Paraphrase of Genesis 18:6-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 18:6-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 亞伯拉罕催促撒拉揉麵做餅，又挑了一隻牛犢，並在樹下把凝乳和奶擺在那幾個人面前。「你的妻子撒拉在哪裡？」他們問道，並重申了那應許。撒拉在帳棚裡笑了，想到自己衰殘的身體和丈夫的年紀，便否認自己笑了——但那訪客說：「不然，你實在笑了。」改述自《創世記》18:6-15（JPS 1917）；並非逐字引用。

title.en: Abraham Bargains for Sodom
title.zh: 亞伯拉罕為所多瑪講價

region.en: Overlook toward Sodom from Mamre (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 自幔利遙望所多瑪（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 18:16-33, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: God decides to tell Abraham what He plans for Sodom; Abraham stands before the LORD and haggles the city's minimum righteous population down from fifty to ten, asking: 'Shall not the Judge of all the earth do justly?' The boldest prayer-negotiation in scripture.
summary.zh: 神決意將所多瑪之謀告亞伯拉罕；亞伯拉罕立於耶和華前，將城中義人最低數自五十講至十，問曰：「審判全地的主，豈不行公義麼？」——聖經最大膽之祈禱講價。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Abraham drew near, and said: 'Wilt Thou indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked? Peradventure there be fifty righteous within the city; wilt Thou indeed sweep away and not forgive the place for the fifty righteous that are therein? That be far from Thee to do after this manner, to slay the righteous with the wicked ... Shall not the Judge of all the earth do justly?'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 18:23-25 (public domain); ellipsis marks omitted verse.
passages.zh: 亞伯拉罕近前來，說：「祢果真要把義人和惡人一同剿滅嗎？假若那城裡有五十個義人；祢還要剿滅那地方，不為城裡這五十個義人饒恕他們嗎？將義人與惡人同殺，將義人與惡人一樣看待，這斷不是祢所行的……審判全地的主豈不行公義嗎？」

passages.text: Step by step Abraham talked the LORD down: forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty — 'Oh, let not the LORD be angry, and I will speak yet but this once' — to ten. And the LORD went His way, and Abraham returned to his place. The dialogue models chutzpah in prayer: justice argued with the Judge Himself. Paraphrase of Genesis 18:26-33 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 18:26-33 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 亞伯拉罕一步一步地與耶和華討價還價：四十五個、四十個、三十個、二十個——「求主不要動怒，我再說這一次」——直到十個。耶和華就走了，亞伯拉罕也回到自己的地方去了。這段對話樹立了祈禱中無所畏懼的典範：與審判者本身爭辯公義。改述自《創世記》18:26-33（JPS 1917）；並非逐字引用。

title.en: Lot at the Gate of Sodom
title.zh: 羅得在所多瑪城門

region.en: Sodom (traditional southern Dead Sea shore; symbolic pin)
region.zh: 所多瑪（傳統死海南岸；象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 19:1-11, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Two angels enter Sodom; Lot, like Abraham, runs to greet and feed them. The men of the city surround the house demanding the strangers; Lot offers his daughters instead; the angels strike the mob blind — the night that seals the city's doom.
summary.zh: 二天使入所多瑪；羅得如亞伯拉罕奔迎款待。城中之人圍屋索要客人；羅得竟以二女代之；天使使暴眾目盲——此夜城之厄運已定。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Later tradition read this as the paradigm of cruelty to strangers; the record states the narrative without endorsing later moralizations.

passages.text: And they called unto Lot, and said unto him: 'Where are the men that came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them.' And Lot went out unto them to the door, and shut the door behind him.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 19:5-6 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他們呼叫羅得，對他說：「今夜到你這裡來的那幾個人在哪裡？把他們帶出來，任我們所為。」羅得就出來，到門口眾人那裡，把門關上。

passages.text: Lot pleaded with the crowd as 'brethren' and offered his two daughters, but the men of Sodom pressed upon him. The angels pulled Lot inside, shut the door, and smote everyone at the entrance with blindness, 'both small and great', so that they wearied themselves finding the door. Paraphrase of Genesis 19:8-11 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 19:8-11 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 羅得懇求那群人，稱他們為「弟兄」，並提出把自己的兩個女兒交給他們，但所多瑪的人卻向羅得進逼。天使把羅得拉進屋裡，關上門，又使門口所有的人，無論「老少」，都眼目昏迷，以致他們疲乏地尋找那門。改述自《創世記》19:8-11（JPS 1917）；並非逐字引用。

title.en: The Overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah
title.zh: 所多瑪蛾摩拉之傾覆

region.en: Southern Dead Sea plain (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 死海平原之南（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 19:12-29, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: At dawn the angels hurry Lot, his wife, and two daughters out of the doomed city — 'flee for thy life, look not behind thee'. Fire and brimstone rain from the LORD; Lot's wife disobeys, looks back, and becomes a pillar of salt, while Abraham sees the smoke of the plain rise like a furnace.
summary.zh: 黎明天使催促羅得夫婦與二女出城——「逃命吧，不可回顧」。耶和華降硫磺與火；羅得之妻違命回望，化為鹽柱；亞伯拉罕遠望平原烟氣上騰如燒窯。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he said: 'Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the Plain; escape to the mountain, lest thou be swept away.' The sun rose as Lot entered Zoar, and the LORD rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah brimstone and fire out of heaven, overthrowing the cities and all the plain. Lot's wife looked back from behind him and became a pillar of salt. Abraham rose early that morning and looked down to see the smoke of the land going up as the smoke of a furnace — 'and God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow'. Paraphrase of Genesis 19:23-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 19:17 (public domain). / Paraphrase of Genesis 19:23-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們把二人領到外面之後，那人說：「逃命吧！不要回頭看，也不要在平原上任何地方停留；要逃到山上去，免得你被毀滅。」羅得進入瑣珥的時候，太陽已經升起，耶和華從天上降下硫磺與火在所多瑪和蛾摩拉，毀滅了那些城邑和整個平原。羅得的妻子在他身後回頭一看，就變成了一根鹽柱。亞伯拉罕那天清早起來，俯視那地，見煙氣上騰，如同燒窯的煙一般——「神記念亞伯拉罕，在毀滅之中把羅得送了出去」。改述自《創世記》19:23-29（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Lot's Daughters in the Cave
title.zh: 羅得二女在山洞

region.en: Mountains above Zoar (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 瑣珥上方山地（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 19:30-38, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Fearing to dwell in Zoar, Lot retreats to a mountain cave. His daughters, believing the world's men are destroyed, make their father drunk on two successive nights to preserve their father's line; the sons born are Moab and Ben-ammi — the etiological, unflattering origin of Israel's neighbours the Moabites and Ammonites.
summary.zh: 羅得懼居瑣珥，退至山地洞中。二女以為世間男子盡滅，連續兩夜使父醉臥，以存父嗣；所生為摩押與便亞米——以色列鄰邦摩押亞捫之不榮起源釋義。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the firstborn said unto the younger: 'Our father is old, and there is not a man in the earth to come in unto us after the manner of the whole earth. Come, let us make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, that we may preserve seed of our father.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 19:31-32 (public domain).
passages.zh: 長女對幼女說：「我們的父親老了，地上又沒有男子能按著普世的常規親近我們。來吧，我們讓父親喝酒，然後與他同寢，好從我們的父親存留後裔。」
