passages.text: Each daughter lay with her unknowing father on consecutive nights; both conceived. The elder bore a son named Moab — 'from the father' — ancestor of the Moabites; the younger bore Ben-ammi, father of the Ammonites. The Torah does not spare Israel's ancestors' kin: the nations' origins are told through shame. Paraphrase of Genesis 19:33-38 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 19:33-38 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 兩個女兒接連兩夜分別與不知情的父親同寢；兩人都懷了孕。長女生了一個兒子，名叫摩押——意為「從父親而來」——是摩押人的祖先；幼女生了便亞米，是亞捫人的父親。妥拉並不袒護以色列祖先的親族：這些民族的起源是藉著羞恥之事講述的。改述自《創世記》19:33-38（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Isaac Is Born: God Made Laughter
title.zh: 以撒出生：神使我喜笑

region.en: Beersheba region, Negev
region.zh: 別是巴一帶，南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 21:1-8, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The LORD 'remembered Sarah as He had said' and the hundred-year-old promise is fulfilled: Sarah bears Abraham a son in his old age. They name him Isaac — 'laughter' — and Sarah's earlier cynical laugh becomes a public celebration: 'God hath made laughter for me; every one that heareth will laugh with me.'
summary.zh: 耶和華「照先前所說眷顧撒拉」，百年應許得成：撒拉於亞伯拉罕年老時生子，名以撒（笑）；昔日譏誚之笑化作慶賀：「神使我喜笑，凡聽見的必與我一同喜笑。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Sarah said: 'God hath made laughter for me; every one that heareth will laugh on account of me.' And she said: 'Who would have said unto Abraham, that Sarah should give children suck? for I have borne him a son in his old age.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 21:6-7 (public domain).
passages.zh: 撒拉說：「神使我歡笑；凡聽見的人都要因我而笑。」她又說：「誰能對亞伯拉罕說，撒拉要乳養孩子呢？因為我在他年老的時候給他生了一個兒子。」

passages.text: The LORD visited Sarah as He had promised; she conceived and bore Abraham a son at the set time God had spoken. Abraham named him Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, being a hundred years old. Sarah weaned him, and Abraham made a great feast the day Isaac was weaned. Paraphrase of Genesis 21:1-8 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 21:1-8 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 耶和華照著所應許的眷顧撒拉；她懷了孕，在神所說的定期給亞伯拉罕生了一個兒子。亞伯拉罕給他起名叫以撒，在他第八天給他行了割禮，那時亞伯拉罕一百歲。撒拉給以撒斷奶，以撒斷奶的那一天，亞伯拉罕擺設了盛大的筵席。改述自《創世記》21:1-8（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Hagar and Ishmael Sent Out into the Wilderness of Beersheba
title.zh: 夏甲與以實瑪利被逐於別是巴曠野

region.en: Wilderness of Beersheba, Negev
region.zh: 別是巴曠野，南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 21:9-21, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Sarah demands that Hagar's son be sent away 'for the son of this bondwoman shall not be heir'; God tells Abraham to listen to her. Hagar wanders until the water is spent, lays the dying boy under a bush, and weeps — until God opens her eyes to a well and promises the lad a great nation.
summary.zh: 撒拉求逐夏甲之子，「這使女的兒子不可與我的兒子以撒一同承受產業」；神命亞伯拉罕聽從。夏甲曠野漂流，水盡，將垂死之童置灌木下而泣——神開其目見井，並許此童成大國。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Ishmael's promise is foundational in Islamic tradition as well; cross-reference to islamic records planned.

passages.text: And God heard the voice of the lad; and the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said unto her: 'What aileth thee, Hagar? fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad where he is. Arise, lift up the lad, and hold him fast by thy hand; for I will make him a great nation.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 21:17-18 (public domain).
passages.zh: 神聽見了那孩子的聲音；神的使者從天上呼叫夏甲，對她說：「夏甲，你怎麼了？不要害怕；因為神已經聽見那孩子所在之處的聲音。起來，把孩子抱起來，用手緊緊牽著他；因為我要使他成為大國。」

passages.text: The matter grieved Abraham greatly, 'because of his son', but God confirmed Sarah's demand: 'in Isaac shall thy seed be called'. Hagar departed with bread and a skin of water into the wilderness of Beersheba; when the water was gone she cast the child under a shrub and sat opposite, weeping. Then God opened her eyes to a well; the lad grew in the wilderness, an archer, and took an Egyptian wife. Paraphrase of Genesis 21:11-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 21:11-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 此事因他兒子的緣故，使亞伯拉罕大為憂愁，但神確認了撒拉的要求：「從以撒生的，才要稱為你的後裔」。夏甲帶著餅和一皮袋水，往別是巴的曠野去了；水用盡了，她就把孩子撇在小樹下，自己坐在對面哭泣。於是神使她的眼睛明亮，看見一口井；那少年在曠野漸漸長大，成了弓箭手，並娶了一位埃及女子為妻。改寫自《創世記》21:11-21（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: The Binding of Isaac (Akedah)
title.zh: 捆綁以撒（阿刻達）

region.en: Mount Moriah, Jerusalem (traditional identification with the Temple Mount)
region.zh: 摩利亞山，耶路撒冷（傳統指聖殿山）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 22:1-19, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: God tests Abraham: 'Take now thy son, thine only son... and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there'. Father and son walk up the mountain in silence, the wood on Isaac's back; at the last moment an angel stays the knife, and a ram is offered instead. The Akedah is Judaism's supreme drama of faith and obedience.
summary.zh: 神試驗亞伯拉罕：「帶著你的兒子，就是你獨生的兒子……往摩利亞地去，在那裡把他獻為燔祭。」父子默然上山，柴在以撒背上；刀將落時，天使止之，遂獻公羊。阿刻達為猶太教信心順服之至高戲劇。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Central to Rosh Hashanah liturgy (shofar recalls the ram); treated as narrative, not as endorsement of child sacrifice, which the text itself replaces.

passages.text: And they came to the place which God had told him of; and Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, upon the wood. And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 22:9-10 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他們到了神所指示他的地方；亞伯拉罕在那裡築了壇，把柴擺好，捆綁了他的兒子以撒，放在壇的柴上。亞伯拉罕就伸手拿刀，要殺他的兒子。

passages.text: Isaac had asked the only question on the road — 'the fire and the wood are here, but where is the lamb?' — and Abraham had answered, 'God will provide Himself the lamb'. As the knife rose, the angel of the LORD called twice: 'Lay not thy hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him; for now I know that thou fearest God'. Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in a thicket, and sacrificed it instead. He named the place 'The LORD Will Provide', and the angel swore the great promise anew: 'thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies'. Paraphrase of Genesis 22:7-18 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 22:7-18 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 以撒在路上問了唯一的問題——「火與柴都有了，但燔祭的羊羔在哪裡呢？」——亞伯拉罕回答說：「神必自己預備作燔祭的羊羔」。正當刀舉起時，耶和華的使者兩次呼喚：「你不可在這童子身上下手，一點不可害他；現在我知道你是敬畏神的了」。亞伯拉罕舉目觀看，見一隻公羊兩角扣在稠密的小樹中，就取了那隻公羊獻為燔祭，代替他的兒子。他給那地方起名叫「耶和華必預備」，使者又重申了那偉大的應許：「你的後裔必得著仇敵的城門」。改寫自《創世記》22:7-18（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Sarah Dies: The Purchase of Machpelah
title.zh: 撒拉卒：購麥比拉洞

region.en: Hebron, Cave of Machpelah
region.zh: 希伯崙，麥比拉洞

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 23, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Sarah dies at Kiriat-arba (Hebron) at a hundred and twenty-seven. Abraham negotiates formally with the Hittites and buys the cave of Machpelah from Ephron for four hundred shekels of silver 'current money with the merchant' — the first land Abraham owns in the promised land, a grave.
summary.zh: 撒拉卒於基列亞巴（希伯崙），年一百二十七。亞伯拉罕與赫人正式議價，以四百舍客勒白銀「通用的銀子」購麥比拉洞——應許之地首業，乃一墳墓。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Machpelah (Tomb of the Patriarchs) remains a contested holy site today; record describes text only.

passages.text: And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron; and Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver, which he had named in the audience of the children of Heth, even four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant. ... And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre — that is, Hebron — in the land of Canaan.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 23:16, 19 (public domain); ellipsis marks omitted verses.
passages.zh: 亞伯拉罕聽從了以弗崙；亞伯拉罕就照著以弗崙在赫人面前所說的，把銀子稱給他，就是四百舍客勒銀子，是商人通用的銀子。……此後，亞伯拉罕把他妻子撒拉埋葬在幔利前、麥比拉田間的洞裡——幔利就是希伯崙——在迦南地。

passages.text: Abraham stood before the Hittites as 'a stranger and a settler' and asked for a burial site. Ephron, son of Zohar, publicly offered the cave 'in the presence of the people of the land', inflating the price; Abraham paid the full sum without haggling. The legal formality — witnesses, currency, field and cave with its trees — makes the patriarchs' tomb the first deeded property in Canaan. Paraphrase of Genesis 23:3-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 23:3-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 亞伯拉罕站在赫人面前，自稱是「外人與寄居的」，請求一塊墳地。瑣轄的兒子以弗崙當眾「在本地人面前」提出那洞，抬高價錢；亞伯拉罕沒有討價還價，付足了全數。這法律上的正式手續——見證人、銀錢、連同樹木的田與洞——使族長的墳墓成為迦南地第一份立契的產業。改寫自《創世記》23:3-15（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: A Wife for Isaac: The Servant at the Well
title.zh: 為以撒娶妻：僕人在井旁

region.en: Aram-naharaim, well of Haran
region.zh: 亞蘭拿哈蘭，哈蘭井旁

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 24:1-27, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Abraham sends his eldest servant to his kindred with ten camels, under oath never to take a Canaanite wife for Isaac. At the well the servant prays for a sign: the girl who waters him and his camels is the one. Rebecca's kindness to the camels proves her before a word is spoken.
summary.zh: 亞伯拉罕遣老僕攜十駝往本族，起誓勿為以撒娶迦南女。僕於井旁求兆：願為我與駝飲水者即是。利百加善待駝群，未出一言而自證。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he said: 'O LORD, the God of my master Abraham, send me, I pray Thee, good speed this day, and show kindness unto my master Abraham. Behold, I stand by the fountain of water; and the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water; and let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say: Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and if she say: Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also — let the same be she that Thou hast appointed for Thy servant, even for Isaac.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 24:12-14 (public domain); condensed without ellipsis.
passages.zh: 他說：「耶和華——我主人亞伯拉罕的神啊，求你施恩給我，使我今日遇見好機會，施恩給我主人亞伯拉罕。看哪，我站在井旁；城裡人的女子們正出來打水；我向哪一個女子說：請你拿下水瓶來，給我水喝；她若說：請喝，我也給你的駱駝喝——願那女子就作你所預定給你僕人、就是給以撒的妻。」

passages.text: Before he finished speaking, Rebecca, born of Bethuel, came out with her pitcher, drew water for the stranger, and then ran again to the trough until all ten camels were satisfied. The servant gave her a nose-ring and bracelets and asked whose daughter she was; when she answered, he bowed his head and blessed the LORD who had led him 'in the right way'. Paraphrase of Genesis 24:15-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 24:15-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他話還沒說完，彼土魯所生的利百加就帶著水罐出來，為那陌生人打水，然後又跑到水槽邊，直到十匹駱駝都喝足了。那僕人給她一個鼻環和手鐲，問她是誰的女兒；她回答之後，他低下頭，稱頌那引他「走對路」的耶和華。改寫自《創世記》24:15-27（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Rebecca Chooses: The Betrothal at Haran
title.zh: 利百加自擇：哈蘭許婚

region.en: Haran, house of Bethuel
region.zh: 哈蘭，彼土利之家

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 24:28-67, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The servant retells his mission in Laban's hall and asks for an answer; the family tries to delay, but Rebecca herself decides: 'I will go'. Meeting Isaac meditating in the field at evening, she alights from her camel, veils herself, and enters Sarah's tent — and Isaac is comforted after his mother's death.
summary.zh: 僕在拉班堂中覆述使命，求定奪；家人欲留，利百加自決：「我去」。以撒傍晚在田間默想，利百加下駝蒙面入撒拉之帳——以撒喪母之痛遂得安慰。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they said: 'We will call the damsel, and inquire at her mouth.' And they called Rebecca, and said unto her: 'Wilt thou go with this man?' And she said: 'I will go.' The servant told of the signs at the well and laid out gifts; Laban and Bethuel answered that the matter was 'of the LORD' and could not be gainsaid. Morning gifts changed hands, the family blessed Rebecca to be 'mother of thousands of ten thousands', and she went. Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother, took her as wife, and loved her — and the text notes simply that Isaac was comforted for his mother. Paraphrase of Genesis 24:50-67 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 24:57-58 (public domain). / Paraphrase of Genesis 24:50-67 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們說：「我們把這女子叫來，問問她的口。」他們就叫了利百加來，對她說：「你願意跟這人去嗎？」她說：「我願意去。」那僕人講述井邊的種種徵兆，並擺出禮物；拉班和彼土魯回答說，這事「出於耶和華」，不能反對。次日早晨，禮物易手，家人祝福利百加成為「千萬人的母親」，她便去了。以撒把她帶進他母親撒拉的帳棚，娶她為妻，愛她——經文只簡單記下：以撒因他母親得了安慰。改寫自《創世記》24:50-67（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Abraham's Later Sons and His Death at a Good Old Age
title.zh: 亞伯拉罕後嗣與其壽終

region.en: Mamre, Hebron (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 幔利，希伯崙（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 25:1-11, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: After Sarah's death Abraham takes Keturah, who bears six more sons — ancestors of the eastern tribes. He gives them gifts and sends them east, but gives all he has to Isaac; the sons of the concubines and Isaac himself bury him in Machpelah, where he is gathered to his people 'old and full of years'.
summary.zh: 撒拉卒後，亞伯拉罕娶基土拉，又生六子——東方諸族之祖。亞伯拉罕以財物遣之東去，卻將一切所有予以撒；眾子與以撒同葬之於麥比拉，「年老壽高」歸於本族。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac. But unto the sons of the concubines, that Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts; and he sent them away from Isaac his son, while he yet lived, eastward, unto the east country.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 25:5-6 (public domain).
passages.zh: 亞伯拉罕把他一切所有的都給了以撒。至於亞伯拉罕所有的妾所生的兒子，亞伯拉罕給了他們禮物；趁自己還活著的時候，就打發他們離開他的兒子以撒，往東方的東邊地方去。

passages.text: Keturah's sons — Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, Shuah — would people the caravan routes of Arabia and the East, among them Midian, whose land would later shelter Moses. Abraham died at a hundred seventy-five and was buried by his two principal sons, Isaac and Ishmael, in the cave he had bought. Paraphrase of Genesis 25:1-10 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 25:1-10 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 基土拉的兒子們——心蘭、約珊、米但、米甸、伊施巴、書亞——後來遍居阿拉伯和東方的商隊路線，其中有米甸，他的地日後要庇護摩西。亞伯拉罕一百七十五歲而死，由他的兩個主要兒子以撒和以實瑪利葬在他所買的那洞裡。改寫自《創世記》25:1-10（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: The Call of Abram
title.zh: 亞伯蘭蒙召

region.en: Haran to Shechem, land of Canaan
region.zh: 自哈蘭至示劍（迦南地）

period: Genesis 12, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 12

summary.en: The LORD tells the seventy-five-year-old Abram to leave country, kindred, and father's house for a land he will be shown, promising to make of him a great nation through whom all families of the earth will be blessed. Abram goes, builds altars at Shechem and Bethel, and Christian tradition sees in this migration the founding charter of the pilgrim people of God.
summary.zh: 耶和華對七十五歲的亞伯蘭說：要離開本地、本族、父家，往所指示之地去；應許使他成大國，萬族因他得福。亞伯蘭遵命而行，在示劍、伯特利築壇。基督教傳統視此遷徙為朝聖之民、因信而行之始。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition shared by Judaism and Christianity. Presented as a founding-migration narrative.

passages.text: Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee: and I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: and I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed. So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken unto him.
passages.zh: 耶和華曾對亞伯蘭說：你要離開本地、本族、父家，往我所要指示你的地去：我必叫你成為大國，我必賜福給你，叫你的名為大；你也要叫別人得福：為你祝福的，我必賜福與他；那咒詛你的，我必咒詛他：地上的萬族都要因你得福。亞伯蘭就照著耶和華所吩咐的去了。

passages.text: And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all their substance that they had gathered, and they went forth to go into the land of Canaan; and into the land of Canaan they came. And Abram passed through the land unto the place of Sichem, unto the plain of Moreh. And the LORD appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the LORD, who appeared unto him.
passages.zh: 亞伯蘭帶著他的妻子撒萊，和他兄弟的兒子羅得，並他們所積蓄的一切財物，一同起身往迦南地去；他們就到了迦南地。亞伯蘭經過那地，到了示劍地方、摩利的平原。耶和華向亞伯蘭顯現，說：我要把這地賜給你的後裔：亞伯蘭就在那裡為向他顯現的耶和華築了一座壇。

title.en: Abram's Sister-Wife Deception in Egypt
title.zh: 亞伯蘭埃及謊稱妹妻

region.en: Egypt, Pharaoh's court
region.zh: 埃及，法老宮中

period: Genesis 12, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 12

summary.en: Famine drives Abram to Egypt, where he passes Sarai off as his sister to save his own life; Pharaoh takes her into his house and rewards Abram richly, until plagues fall on the court and the truth is out. The king sends them away unharmed — the first of the twice-told 'sister-wife' tales in which the patriarchs' survival cunning is ironically preserved by the outsiders they deceive.
summary.zh: 饑荒使亞伯蘭下埃及；他懼死，謊稱撒萊為妹。法老娶她入宮，厚賜亞伯蘭；耶和華卻降大災於法老全家。真相既明，法老遣之而去，毫髮無傷——此乃族長「妹妻」雙重敘事之首，倖存之機巧反由受騙的外邦人保全。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as a deception-survival tale type; scholarly framing.

passages.text: And there was a famine in the land: and Abram went down into Egypt to sojourn there. And it came to pass, when he was come near to enter into Egypt, that he said unto Sarai his wife, Behold now, I know that thou art a fair woman to look upon: therefore it shall come to pass, when the Egyptians shall see thee, that they shall say, This is his wife: and they will kill me, but they will save thee alive. Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister: that it may be well with me for thy sake; and my soul shall live because of thee.
passages.zh: 那地遭遇饑荒，亞伯蘭就下埃及去，要在那裡寄居。將近埃及，他就對妻子撒萊說：「看哪，我知道你是容貌俊美的婦人。埃及人看見你必說：『這是他的妻子』，他們就要殺我，卻叫你存活。求你說你是我的妹子，使我因你得平安，我的命也因你存活。」

passages.text: The princes also of Pharaoh saw her, and commended her before Pharaoh: and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house. And he entreated Abram well for her sake. And the LORD plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai Abram's wife. And Pharaoh called Abram and said, What is this that thou hast done unto me? why didst thou not tell me that she was thy wife? now therefore behold thy wife, take her, and go thy way.
passages.zh: 法老的臣宰看見了她，就在法老面前誇獎她，那婦人就被帶進法老的宮去。法老因這婦人就厚待亞伯蘭。耶和華因亞伯蘭妻子撒萊的緣故，降大災與法老和他的全家。法老就召了亞伯蘭來，說：「你這向我作的是什麼事呢？為什麼沒有告訴我她是你的妻子？現在你的妻子在這裡，可以帶她走吧。」

title.en: Melchizedek Blesses Abram
title.zh: 麥基洗德祝福亞伯蘭

region.en: King's Dale, near Salem (Jerusalem)
region.zh: 王谷，撒冷（耶路撒冷）附近

period: Genesis 14, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 14

summary.en: When four eastern kings plunder Sodom and carry off Lot, Abram arms his 318 trained servants, strikes them by night, and brings back all the goods and people. Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, brings out bread and wine and blesses the victor, who gives him a tenth of all — a mysterious priest-king whom Christian tradition (in Hebrews 7) reads as a figure of Christ, the eternal priest, and whose bread and wine echo the Eucharist.
summary.zh: 四王擄掠所多瑪，擄走羅得；亞伯蘭率三百一十八名家丁夜襲，救回人財。撒冷王、至高神的祭司麥基洗德攜餅與酒而出，為他祝福；亞伯蘭將所得十分之一獻上。基督教《希伯來書》以此無譜之王為基督永恆祭司的預表，餅酒亦隱合聖餐。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Melchizedek's Christological reading (Hebrews 7) is noted; presented as a comparative sacred-kingship narrative.

passages.text: And there came one that had escaped, and told Abram the Hebrew; for he dwelt in the plain of Mamre. And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed his trained servants, born in his own house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them unto Dan. And he divided himself against them, he and his servants, by night, and smote them, and pursued them unto Hobah. And he brought back all the goods, and also brought again his brother Lot, and his goods, and the women also, and the people.
passages.zh: 有一個逃出來的人告訴希伯來人亞伯蘭，亞伯蘭正住在幔利的平原。亞伯蘭聽見他姪兒被擄去，就率領他家裡生養的精練壯丁三百一十八人，直追到但。便在夜間，自己同僕人分隊殺敗敵人，又追到大馬色左邊的何把。將被擄掠的一切財物奪回來，連他姪兒羅得和他的財物，以及婦女、人民也都奪回來。

passages.text: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God. And he blessed him, and said, Blessed be Abram of the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth: and blessed be the most high God, which hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. And he gave him tithes of all. And the king of Sodom said unto Abram, Give me the persons, and take the goods to thyself. And Abram said, I will not take from a thread even to a shoelatchet, and that I will not take any thing that is thine.
passages.zh: 又有撒冷王麥基洗德帶著餅和酒出來迎接，他是至高神的祭司。他為亞伯蘭祝福，說：「願天地的主、至高的神賜福與亞伯蘭！至高的神把敵人交在你手裡，是應當稱頌的！」亞伯蘭就把所得的拿出十分之一來，給麥基洗德。所多瑪王對亞伯蘭說：「你把人口給我，財物你自己拿去吧。」亞伯蘭說：「我已經向天地的主、至高的神耶和華起誓：凡是你的東西，就是一根線、一根鞋帶，我都不拿。」

title.en: The Covenant Between the Pieces
title.zh: 切分祭牲之約

region.en: Mamre, near Hebron
region.zh: 幔利，希伯崙附近

period: Genesis 15, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 15

summary.en: In a vision the childless Abram is told his heir will come from his own body and his seed will be as the stars; 'he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness' — the verse Paul makes the cornerstone of justification by faith. Sealing the covenant, Abram cuts the sacrificial animals, falls into a dread darkness, and a smoking furnace and burning lamp pass between the pieces, while prophecy of 400 years of servitude in a strange land is spoken.
summary.zh: 異象中，無子的亞伯蘭得諭：後裔將自其身而出，多如眾星；「亞伯蘭信耶和華，耶和華就以此為他的義」——保羅因信稱義之基石經文。獻祭牲剖分兩半，亞伯蘭沉睡於大黑暗；冒煙的爐並燒著的火把從肉塊中經過，立約為憑，並預言四百年寄居異邦。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Paul's faith-righteousness reading (Romans 4) is the classic Christian use of this text.

passages.text: After these things the word of the LORD came unto Abram in a vision, saying, Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward. And Abram said, LORD God, what wilt thou give me, seeing I go childless? And, behold, the word of the LORD came unto him, saying, This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir. And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be. And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.
passages.zh: 這事以後，耶和華在異象中有話對亞伯蘭說：「亞伯蘭，你不要懼怕！我是你的盾牌，必大大地賞賜你。」亞伯蘭說：「主耶和華啊，我既無子，你還賜我什麼呢？」耶和華又有話對他說：「這人必不成為你的後嗣，你本身所生的才成為你的後嗣。」於是領他走到外邊，說：「你向天觀看，數算眾星，能數得過來嗎？」又對他說：「你的後裔將要如此。」亞伯蘭信耶和華，耶和華就以此為他的義。

passages.text: And he said unto him, Take me an heifer of three years old, and a she goat of three years old, and a ram of three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon. And he took unto him all these, and divided them in the midst, and laid each piece one against another. And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him. And it came to pass, that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold a smoking furnace, and a burning lamp that passed between those pieces. In the same day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto thy seed have I given this land.
passages.zh: 他又對他說：「你為我取一隻三年的母牛，一隻三年的母山羊，一隻三年的公綿羊，一隻斑鳩，一隻雛鴿。」亞伯蘭就取了這些來，每樣劈開分成兩半，一半對著一半地擺列。日頭正落的時候，亞伯蘭沉沉地睡了，忽然有驚人的大黑暗落在他身上。日落天黑，不料有冒煙的爐並燒著的火把從那些肉塊中經過。當那日，耶和華與亞伯蘭立約，說：「我已賜給你的後裔這地。」

title.en: Hagar in the Wilderness
title.zh: 夏甲曠野得見活神

region.en: Wilderness of Shur, well Beerlahairoi
region.zh: 書珥曠野，庇耳拉海萊井

period: Genesis 16 and 21, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 16 and 21

summary.en: Barren Sarai gives her Egyptian maid Hagar to Abram as wife; conceiving, Hagar flees her mistress's harshness into the wilderness, where the angel of the LORD finds her by a spring, promises a countless seed, and names her son Ishmael — 'thou God seest me,' she says, naming the well Beerlahairoi. Cast out later with her son, she sits a bowshot off weeping that she may not see the child die, until God opens her eyes to a well and makes of Ishmael a great nation.
summary.zh: 撒萊使埃及使女夏甲與亞伯蘭同房；夏甲有孕後被苦待而逃至曠野。耶和華的使者在泉旁尋見她，應許後裔無數，並為其子命名以實瑪利；她稱那井為庇耳拉海萊——「看顧人的神」。後母子被逐，坐泣於一箭之遙，神開她的眼得見水井，以實瑪利終成大國。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition shared with Islam (Ishmael as Arab ancestor). Presented comparatively with sensitivity to both traditions.

passages.text: And the angel of the LORD found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur. And he said, Hagar, Sarai's maid, whence camest thou? and whither wilt thou go? And she said, I flee from the face of my mistress Sarai. And the angel of the LORD said unto her, Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands. And the angel of the LORD said unto her, I will multiply thy seed exceedingly, that it shall not be numbered for multitude.
passages.zh: 耶和華的使者在曠野的水泉旁，就是往書珥路上的水泉旁遇見她。就說：撒萊的婢女夏甲，你從哪裡來？要往哪裡去？她說：我從我的主母撒萊面前逃出來。耶和華的使者對她說：你回到你主母那裡，服在她的手下。耶和華的使者又對她說：我必使你的後裔極其繁多，甚至不可勝數。

passages.text: Behold, thou art with child and shalt bear a son, and shalt call his name Ishmael; because the LORD hath heard thy affliction. And she called the name of the LORD that spake unto her, Thou God seest me: for she said, Have I also here looked after him that seeth me? Wherefore the well was called Beerlahairoi.
passages.zh: 看哪，你如今懷了孕，必生一個兒子，你要給他起名叫以實瑪利，因為耶和華聽見了你的苦情。她便稱那對她說話的耶和華的名為「看顧我的神」，因為她說：我在這裡也看見了那看顧我的嗎？所以那井名叫庇耳拉海萊。

passages.text: And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread, and a bottle of water, and gave it unto Hagar, putting it on her shoulder, and the child, and sent her away: and she departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba. And she went, and sat her down over against him a good way off, as it were a bow shot: for she said, Let me not see the death of the child. And God heard the voice of the lad; and God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water; and she went, and filled the bottle with water, and gave the lad drink.
passages.zh: 亞伯拉罕清早起來，拿了餅和一皮袋水，交給夏甲，搭在她的肩上，又把孩子交給她，打發她走。她就走了，在別是巴的曠野中漂流。她走過去，在離孩子對面約一箭之遠的地方坐下，因為她說：我不忍見孩子死。神聽見童子的聲音；神就使她的眼睛明亮，她看見一口水井，便去將皮袋盛滿了水，給童子喝。

title.en: Abraham, the Everlasting Covenant, and Isaac Promised
title.zh: 亞伯拉罕、永約與以撒之諾

region.en: Canaan, at the oaks of Mamre
region.zh: 迦南地，幔利橡樹

period: Genesis 17, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 17

summary.en: When Abram is ninety-nine, God Almighty appears, renames him Abraham — 'father of many nations' — establishes the everlasting covenant sealed in the flesh by circumcision on the eighth day, renames Sarai Sarah, and promises that the ninety-year-old Sarah will bear a son named Isaac with whom the covenant will stand. Abraham falls on his face and laughs; Christian tradition reads the covenant as fulfilled spiritually in Christ, 'the seed of Abraham', in whom all nations are blessed.
summary.zh: 亞伯蘭九十九歲時，全能的神向他顯現，改名亞伯拉罕——「多國之父」——立永約，以割禮為約之記號；撒萊改名撒拉，並應許九十歲的她將生以撒，約要在以撒身上堅立。亞伯拉罕俯伏在地喜笑。基督教傳統視此約在基督——亞伯拉罕的後裔——身上成全，萬國因之得福。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition shared by Judaism and Christianity (and echoed in Islam). Circumcision covenant presented as ritual-origin narrative.

passages.text: And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, the LORD appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect. And I will make my covenant between me and thee, and will multiply thee exceedingly. Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for a father of many nations have I made thee. And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their generations for an everlasting covenant.
passages.zh: 亞伯蘭年九十九歲的時候，耶和華向他顯現，對他說：我是全能的神；你當在我面前行走，作完全人。我就與你立約，使你極其繁多。你的名不再叫亞伯蘭，你的名要叫亞伯拉罕，因為我已立你作多國的父。我要與你並你世世代代的後裔堅立我的約，作永遠的約。

passages.text: This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised. And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you. And God said unto Abraham, As for Sarai thy wife, thou shalt not call her name Sarai, but Sarah shall her name be. And I will bless her, and give thee a son also of her: yea, I will bless her, and she shall be a mother of nations; kings of people shall be of her.
passages.zh: 這就是我與你並你後裔所立的約，是你們當遵守的：你們中間所有的男子都要受割禮。你們要割去陽皮的肉，這是我與你們之間立約的證據。神又對亞伯拉罕說：你的妻子撒萊，不可再叫她的名撒萊，她的名要叫撒拉。我必賜福給她，也要使你從她得一個兒子；是的，我要賜福給她，她也要作多國之母；必有百姓的君王從她而出。

passages.text: Then Abraham fell upon his face, and laughed, and said in his heart, Shall a child be born unto him that is an hundred years old? and shall Sarah, that is ninety years old, bear? And God said, Sarah thy wife shall bear thee a son indeed; and thou shalt call his name Isaac: and I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant, and with his seed after him.
passages.zh: 亞伯拉罕就俯伏在地，笑了，心裡說：一百歲的人還能得孩子嗎？撒拉已經九十歲了，還能生育嗎？神說：不然，你的妻子撒拉確實要給你生一個兒子；你要給他起名叫以撒。我要與他堅立我的約，作永遠的約，並與他之後的後裔立約。

title.en: The Three Visitors and Sarah's Laughter
title.zh: 三客來訪與撒拉的笑

region.en: Tent door at the plains of Mamre
region.zh: 幔利平原，帳棚門口

period: Genesis 18, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 18

summary.en: In the heat of the day Abraham entertains three men under a tree with cakes, a dressed calf, butter, and milk — one of whom is the LORD. They announce that Sarah, past the age of women, will bear a son; Sarah laughs within the tent and denies it, and is told 'Is any thing too hard for the LORD?' Christian iconography reads the three strangers as a foreshadowing of the Trinity, and the episode as the great Old Testament exemplar of hospitality.
summary.zh: 天正熱時，亞伯拉罕以餅、犢、奶油牛奶款待帳棚前的三位客人——其中一位乃是耶和華。他們宣告年老停經的撒拉將生子；撒拉在帳棚內暗笑，被告知「耶和華豈有難成的事麼？」。基督教聖像畫以三客預示三位一體，此事亦為舊約款待之範式。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Trinitarian reading is a Christian interpretive tradition, noted here; the text itself is Jewish scripture.

passages.text: And the LORD appeared unto him in the plains of Mamre: and he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day; and he lift up his eyes and looked, and, lo, three men stood by him: and when he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself toward the ground, and said, My LORD, if now I have found favour in thy sight, pass not away, I pray thee, from thy servant. And Abraham hastened into the tent unto Sarah, and said, Make ready quickly three measures of fine meal.
passages.zh: 耶和華在幔利平原向他顯現；那時正當日頭炎熱，他坐在帳棚門口。他舉目觀看，見有三個人站在他旁邊；他一看見，就從帳棚門口跑去迎接他們，俯伏在地，說：「我主，我若在你眼前蒙恩，求你不要離開僕人而去。」亞伯拉罕急忙進帳棚去見撒拉，說：「你快快預備三細亞細麵。」

passages.text: And they said unto him, Where is Sarah thy wife? And he said, Behold, in the tent. And he said, I will certainly return unto thee according to the time of life; and, lo, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard it in the tent door, which was behind him. Now Abraham and Sarah were old and well stricken in age; and it ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women. Therefore Sarah laughed within herself, saying, After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?
passages.zh: 他們對他說：「你的妻子撒拉在哪裡？」他說：「在帳棚裡。」那人說：「到了生命的時候，我必定回到你這裡來；看哪，你的妻子撒拉必生一個兒子。」撒拉在他後面的帳棚門口聽見了這話。當時亞伯拉罕和撒拉已經年老，年紀老邁；撒拉的月事已經斷絕了。所以撒拉心裡暗笑，說：「我既已衰老，我主也老了，豈還能得這喜樂呢？」

passages.text: And the LORD said unto Abraham, Wherefore did Sarah laugh, saying, Shall I of a surety bear a child, which am old? Is any thing too hard for the LORD? At the time appointed I will return unto thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son. Then Sarah denied, saying, I laughed not; for she was afraid. And he said, Nay; but thou didst laugh.
passages.zh: 耶和華對亞伯拉罕說：「撒拉為什麼暗笑說：『我既已年老，果真能生養嗎？』耶和華豈有難成的事嗎？到了所定的時候，到了生命的時候，我必回到你這裡來，撒拉必生一個兒子。」撒拉就否認，說：「我沒有笑。」因為她害怕。那人說：「不然，你實在笑了。」

title.en: Sodom Overthrown, Lot's Wife a Pillar of Salt
title.zh: 所多瑪傾覆，羅得妻成鹽柱

region.en: Cities of the plain, south Dead Sea (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 平原諸城，死海南端（象徵性定位）

period: Genesis 19, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 19

summary.en: Two angels lodge with Lot in Sodom; the city's men besiege the door demanding the strangers, and Lot offers his daughters in vain before the angels strike the mob blind. At dawn Lot's family is dragged from the city — 'escape for thy life; look not behind thee' — and fire and brimstone rain from the LORD upon Sodom and Gomorrah; Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt. In a cave the daughters make their father drunk and bear Moab and Benammi, founders of Israel's neighboring nations.
summary.zh: 二天使夜宿羅得家；所多瑪人圍門索人，羅得欲以二女代之，天使使眾人眼盲。黎明羅得一家被拉出城——「逃命吧，不可回頭看」——耶和華降硫磺與火；羅得妻回顧，變成鹽柱。後二女於山洞灌醉其父，生摩押與便亞米，即以色列二鄰族之祖。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Presented as a destruction-and-refugee narrative with an incest-founding etiology; later interpretive uses of the Sodom story vary widely and are not endorsed here.

passages.text: But before they lay down, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, compassed the house round, both old and young, all the people from every quarter: and they called unto Lot, and said unto him, Where are the men which came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them. And Lot went out at the door unto them, and shut the door after him, and said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly. But the men put forth their hand, and pulled Lot into the house to them, and shut to the door.
passages.zh: 他們還沒有躺下，城裡的人，就是所多瑪的男人，無論老少，所有從各處來的人，都圍住那房子；他們呼叫羅得，對他說：「今夜到你這裡來的人在哪裡？把他們帶出來給我們，我們要與他們相識。」羅得出來到門口見他們，隨手把門關上，說：「弟兄們，我求你們，不要這樣行惡。」但那些人伸出手來，把羅得拉進屋裡去，就把門關上。

passages.text: And when the morning arose, then the angels hastened Lot, saying, Arise, take thy wife, and thy two daughters, which are here; lest thou be consumed in the iniquity of the city. And while he lingered, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters; the LORD being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city. And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he said, Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain.
passages.zh: 天明的時候，天使催促羅得說：「起來，帶著你在這裡的妻子和兩個女兒出去，恐怕你因這城的罪惡被剿滅。」羅得遲延不走，那些人就抓住他的手，和他妻子的手，並他兩個女兒的手；因為耶和華憐恤他，就把他們領出來，安置在城外。領他們出來以後，那人說：「逃命吧！不要回頭看，也不要在平原上停留。」

passages.text: Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven; and he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground. But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt. And Abraham gat up early in the morning to the place where he stood before the LORD: and he looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and, lo, the smoke of the country went up as the smoke of a furnace.
passages.zh: 當時，耶和華從天上耶和華那裡，將硫磺與火降在所多瑪和蛾摩拉；他傾覆了那些城和全平原，並城裡所有的居民，以及地上所生長的。但他的妻子在他後頭回頭一看，就變成了一根鹽柱。亞伯拉罕清早起來，到了他從前站在耶和華面前的地方；他向所多瑪和蛾摩拉觀看，看哪，那地方的煙氣上騰，如同燒窯的煙一般。

title.en: The Binding of Isaac
title.zh: 以撒被綁獻祭

region.en: Mount Moriah, land of Moriah
region.zh: 摩利亞山地

period: Genesis 22, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 22

summary.en: God tests Abraham: 'Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest... and offer him there for a burnt offering.' On the third day father and son climb Mount Moriah, Isaac bearing the wood and asking where the lamb is; Abraham binds him on the altar and raises the knife before the angel's cry stays his hand, and a ram caught by its horns is offered in the son's place. Christian tradition reads the akedah as a type of the Father's sacrifice of the Son — God who provides himself a lamb.
summary.zh: 神試驗亞伯拉罕：「帶著你的兒子，就是你獨生的兒子，你愛的以撒……把他獻為燔祭。」三日後父子登摩利亞山，以撒背柴，問燔祭的羊羔在哪裏；亞伯拉罕築壇綁子，舉刀欲殺，天使呼叫止手，公羊以角掛於稠密小樹代獻。基督教傳統以此預表聖父犧牲聖子——神必自己預備羔羊。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Judaism and Christianity, both of which hold the akedah as a foundational text of tested faith; the Christian typological reading is noted.

passages.text: And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am. And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of. And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son, and clave the wood for the burnt offering.
passages.zh: 這些事以後，神要試驗亞伯拉罕，就呼叫他說：「亞伯拉罕！」他說：「我在這裡。」神說：「你帶著你的兒子，就是你獨生的兒子，你所愛的以撒，往摩利亞地去，在我所要指示你的山上，把他獻為燔祭。」亞伯拉罕清早起來，備上驢，帶著兩個僕人和他兒子以撒，也劈好了燔祭的柴。

passages.text: And Isaac spake unto Abraham his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I, my son. And he said, Behold the fire and the wood: but where is the lamb for a burnt offering? And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together. And they came to the place which God had told him of; and Abraham built an altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar upon the wood. And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.
passages.zh: 以撒對他父親亞伯拉罕說：「父親哪！」亞伯拉罕說：「我兒，我在這裡。」以撒說：「請看，火與柴都有了，但燔祭的羊羔在哪裡呢？」亞伯拉罕說：「我兒，神必自己預備作燔祭的羊羔。」於是二人同行。他們到了神所指示他的地方，亞伯拉罕在那裡築壇，把柴擺好，捆綁他的兒子以撒，放在壇的柴上。亞伯拉罕就伸手拿刀，要殺他的兒子。

passages.text: And the angel of the LORD called unto him out of heaven, and said, Abraham, Abraham: and he said, Here am I. And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me. And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns: and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son.
passages.zh: 耶和華的使者從天上呼叫他說：「亞伯拉罕！亞伯拉罕！」他說：「我在這裡。」天使說：「你不可在這童子身上下手，一點不可害他。現在我知道你是敬畏神的了，因為你沒有將你的兒子，就是你獨生的兒子，留下不給我。」亞伯拉罕舉目觀看，不料，有一隻公羊兩角扣在稠密的小樹中。亞伯拉罕就取了那隻公羊來，獻為燔祭，代替他的兒子。

title.en: Abraham Buys the Cave of Machpelah
title.zh: 亞伯拉罕購麥比拉洞

region.en: Hebron (Kirjatharba), Canaan
region.zh: 希伯崙（基列亞巴），迦南地

period: Genesis 23, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 23

summary.en: Sarah dies at Hebron at 127, and the wandering Abraham, 'a stranger and a sojourner' among the Hittites, negotiates publicly at the city gate for Ephron's field and the cave of Machpelah, paying 400 shekels of silver — the patriarchs' only owned piece of the promised land, where Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah, and (by Jacob's wish) Jacob are buried. The site remains a shrine to this day, shared and contested.
summary.zh: 撒拉於希伯崙享壽一百二十七歲而終。寄居異地的亞伯拉罕在城門口眾人面前，以四百舍客勒銀子購以弗崙田間的麥比拉洞——族長在應許之地唯一的產業。亞伯拉罕、撒拉、以撒、利百加、利亞並雅各皆葬於此。聖地至今仍是共享而紛爭不斷之所。

sensitivity.note: The Hebron tomb remains a live religious site for Jews and Muslims; the record covers only the ancient narrative.

passages.text: And Sarah was an hundred and seven and twenty years old: these were the years of the life of Sarah. And Sarah died in Kirjatharba; the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan: and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her. And Abraham stood up from before his dead, and spake unto the sons of Heth, saying, I am a stranger and a sojourner with you: give me a possession of a buryingplace with you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.
passages.zh: 撒拉享壽一百二十七歲，這是撒拉一生的歲數。撒拉死在迦南地的基列亞巴，就是希伯崙。亞伯拉罕為她哀慟哭號。亞伯拉罕從死人面前起來，對赫人說：「我在你們中間是外人，是寄居的。求你們在這裡給我一塊地，我好埋葬我的死人，使她不在我眼前。」

passages.text: And Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the audience of the children of Heth, saying, Nay, my lord, hear me: the field give I thee, and the cave that is therein, I give it thee; in the presence of the sons of my people give I it thee: bury thy dead. And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron; and Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver, which he had named, four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant. And the field, and the cave that is therein, were made sure unto Abraham for a possession of a buryingplace.
passages.zh: 赫人以弗崙在赫人面前回答亞伯拉罕說：「不然，我主請聽。我送給你這塊田，連田間的洞也送給你，在我同族的人面前都給你，可以埋葬你的死人。」亞伯拉罕聽從了以弗崙，照著他在赫人面前所說的，把買賣通用的銀子平了四百舍客勒給以弗崙。於是，那塊田和田間的洞就定準歸與亞伯拉罕作墳地。

title.en: Rebekah at the Well
title.zh: 井旁的利百加

region.en: City of Nahor, Mesopotamia (Haran region)
region.zh: 拿鶴城，美索不達米亞（哈蘭一帶）

period: Genesis 24, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 24

summary.en: Abraham sends his eldest servant sworn by the LORD to find Isaac a wife from his own kindred; at the evening well the servant prays for a sign — the girl who offers water to him and his ten camels — and before he finishes speaking Rebekah arrives and does exactly that. Betrothal gifts, Laban's welcome, her decisive 'I will go', and Isaac's taking her into Sarah's tent close the longest and gentlest chapter in Genesis.
summary.zh: 亞伯拉罕遣老僕起誓，回本族為以撒娶妻。僕人至井旁禱告求記號——凡遞水予他並十駝飲者即所選之女。話未完，利百加出現，恰如此行。聘禮既下，利百加說「我去」，與以撒相遇於暮色田野，入撒拉帳棚成婚，以撒得安慰。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The well sign is a divination-adjacent test, tagged as oracle-divination with that interpretive caveat.

passages.text: And Abraham said unto his eldest servant of his house, that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh: and I will make thee swear by the LORD, the God of heaven, and the God of the earth, that thou shalt not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell: but thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son Isaac.
passages.zh: 亞伯拉罕對管理他全業最老的僕人說：「請你把手放在我大腿底下。我要叫你指著耶和華天地的主起誓，不要為我兒子娶這迦南地中的女子為妻，就是我居住之地的女子。你要往我本地本族去，為我的兒子以撒娶一個妻子。」

passages.text: And he made his camels to kneel down without the city by a well of water at the time of the evening, even the time that women go out to draw water. And he said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day. And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: let the same be she that thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac.
passages.zh: 他叫駱駝跪在城外一口水井旁，那時正是傍晚，就是婦女出來打水的時候。他說：「耶和華我主人亞伯拉罕的神啊，求你今日使我遇見好機會。事情將是這樣：我對哪個少女說：『請你放下水瓶，讓我喝一點』，她若說：『請喝，我也給你的駱駝喝』，願那女子就是你為你僕人以撒所預定的。」

passages.text: And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder. And the damsel was very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her: and she went down to the well, and filled her pitcher, and came up. And she said, Drink, my lord: and she hasted, and let down her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him drink. And when she had done giving him drink, she said, I will draw water for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.
passages.zh: 他話還沒有說完，不料，利百加肩頭上扛著水瓶出來，她是彼土利所生的，彼土利是亞伯拉罕的兄弟拿鶴的妻子密迦的兒子。那少女容貌極其俊美，還是處女，沒有男人親近過她。她下到井旁，打滿了水瓶，又上來。她說：「我主請喝。」就急忙把水瓶托在手上，給他喝。給他喝足了，她又說：「我也要為你的駱駝打水，直到牠們喝足了。」

title.en: Jacob and Esau: Birthright for Pottage
title.zh: 雅各與以掃：長子名分換紅湯

region.en: Canaan, Isaac's tents
region.zh: 迦南地，以撒帳棚

period: Genesis 25, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 25

summary.en: Rebekah's twins struggle in her womb; the oracle answers 'two nations are in thy womb, and the elder shall serve the younger'. Esau is born red and hairy, Jacob grasping his heel; the hunter and the quiet tent-dweller divide their parents' love, and one famished evening Esau sells his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of red lentil pottage, 'thus Esau despised his birthright.'
summary.zh: 利百加腹中雙子相爭，神諭答曰：「兩國在你腹內……將來大的要服事小的。」以掃渾身有毛而紅，雅各手抓其踵。善獵者與安靜帳棚者各得父母偏愛；一日以掃打獵困乏，以紅豆湯將長子名分賣給雅各——「以掃輕看了他長子的名分」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The twin-oracle tag of sibling-creators is interpretive — the pair found rival nations (Israel and Edom), noted here.

passages.text: And Isaac intreated the LORD for his wife, because she was barren: and Rebekah his wife conceived. And the children struggled together within her; and she said, If it be so, why am I thus? And she went to enquire of the LORD. And the LORD said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.
passages.zh: 以撒因他妻子不生育，就為她祈求耶和華；耶和華應允了他的祈求，他的妻子利百加就懷了孕。孩子們在她腹中彼此相爭，她就說：「若是這樣，我為什麼活著呢？」她就去求問耶和華。耶和華對她說：「兩國在你腹中，兩族要從你身上分出來；這族必強於那族，將來大的要服事小的。」

passages.text: And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb. And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau. And after that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esau's heel; and his name was called Jacob. And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents. Now Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob.
passages.zh: 她生產的日子到了，腹中果然是雙胞胎。先出來的渾身發紅，如同穿了毛衣，他們就給他起名叫以掃。隨後他兄弟也出來了，他的手抓住以掃的腳跟，因此給他起名叫雅各。兩個孩子漸漸長大，以掃善於打獵，常在田野；雅各為人安靜，常住在帳棚裡。以撒愛以掃，因為常吃他的野味；利百加卻愛雅各。

passages.text: And Jacob sod pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he was faint: and Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint. And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright. And Esau said, Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me? And Jacob said, Swear to me this day; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob. Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; thus Esau despised his birthright.
passages.zh: 雅各熬了湯，以掃從田野回來，疲乏不堪。以掃對雅各說：「我疲乏了，求你把我這紅湯給我吃。」因此以掃又叫以東。雅各說：「你今日把長子的名分賣給我吧。」以掃說：「我將要死，這長子的名分於我有什麼益處呢？」雅各說：「你今日對我起誓吧。」以掃就向他起誓，把長子的名分賣給了雅各。於是雅各把餅和紅豆湯給了以掃；以掃就這樣輕看了他長子的名分。

title.en: Jacob Steals the Firstborn Blessing
title.zh: 雅各竊取長子祝福

region.en: Isaac's tent at Beersheba
region.zh: 別是巴，以撒的帳棚

period: Genesis 27, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 27

summary.en: Blind old Isaac, wanting venison before blessing Esau, is outmaneuvered by Rebekah: Jacob brings kid-meat dressed as game, goatskins cover his smooth hands and neck, and the dying-speech blessing is irrevocably given — 'the voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.' Esau returns to a bitter cry that cannot be undone; Isaac gives him a lesser doom of the sword and the wilderness, and Esau resolves to kill Jacob.
summary.zh: 老眼昏花的以撒欲食野味後祝福以掃，利百加設計：雅各仿野味烹羊羔，羊皮裹手貼頸。祝福出口不可挽回——「聲音是雅各的聲音，手卻是以掃的手」。以掃歸來放聲大哭，只得次等命定：靠刀劍度日；遂懷恨欲殺雅各，雅各亡命哈蘭。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as the classic doomed-blessing (irrevocable word) tale; the moral ambiguity of the deception is part of the text's long interpretive history.

passages.text: And Rebekah spake unto Jacob her son, saying, Behold, I heard thy father speak unto Esau thy brother, saying, Bring me venison, and make me savoury meat, that I may eat, and bless thee before the LORD before my death. Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command thee. Go now to the flock, and fetch me from thence two good kids of the goats; and I will make them savoury meat for thy father, such as he loveth: and thou shalt bring it to thy father, that he may bless thee before his death.
passages.zh: 利百加對她兒子雅各說：「我聽見你父親對你哥哥以掃說：『你去為我打些野味來，做成美味給我吃，我好在我死以前，在耶和華面前給你祝福。』我兒，現在你要聽我的話，照我所吩咐你的去行。你到羊群那裡去，從那裡給我拿兩隻肥美的山羊羔來，我好為你父親做成他所喜愛的美味；你拿去給你父親吃，使他在未死以前給你祝福。」

passages.text: And Rebekah took goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau, which were with her in the house, and put them upon Jacob her younger son: and she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck. And Jacob said unto his father, I am Esau thy first born. And Isaac said, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son. And Jacob went near; and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau. And he discerned him not; so he blessed him.
passages.zh: 利百加就把家中她大兒子以掃的好衣服拿來，給小兒子雅各穿上；又把山羊羔的皮包在雅各的手上和頸項的光滑處。雅各對他父親說：「我是你的長子以掃。」以撒說：「我兒，請你近前來，讓我摸摸你。」雅各就挨近他父親；以撒摸著他，說：「聲音是雅各的聲音，手卻是以掃的手。」以撒沒有認出他來，於是為他祝福。

passages.text: And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the LORD hath blessed: therefore God give thee of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine: let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee: be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother's sons bow down to thee: cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee. And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
passages.zh: 他又近前來，以撒就與他親嘴；聞到他衣服上的香氣，就為他祝福說：「看哪，我兒的香氣如同耶和華賜福之田地的香氣一樣。願神賜你天上的甘露、地上的肥土，並許多的五穀新酒。願多民事奉你，多國跪拜你；願你作你弟兄的主，你母親的兒子向你跪拜。凡咒詛你的，願他受咒詛；為你祝福的，願他蒙福。」以撒為雅各祝福完畢，雅各的哥哥以掃正從打獵回來。

title.en: Jacob's Ladder at Bethel
title.zh: 雅各的天梯與伯特利

region.en: Bethel (Luz), on the road to Haran
region.zh: 伯特利（路斯），往哈蘭路上

period: Genesis 28, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 28

summary.en: Fleeing Esau, Jacob sleeps on a stone at a nameless place and dreams of a ladder set on earth whose top reaches heaven, angels ascending and descending, and the LORD standing above it promising land, countless seed, and safe return. Waking, he cries 'Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not', sets the stone up as a pillar, anoints it, and names the place Bethel, the house of God — vowing the tenth and, in Christian reading, seeing in the ladder Christ the bridge between heaven and earth (John 1:51).
summary.zh: 雅各逃離以掃，枕石而臥，夢見天梯立地通天，神的使者上去下來，耶和華立於梯上應許土地、後裔與平安歸回。醒來呼曰：「耶和華真在這裏，我竟不知道！」遂立石為柱、澆油其上，名其地為伯特利——神的家。基督教釋經以梯喻基督，天地之間的橋（約翰福音一51）。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The ladder-as-Christ reading is the Christian interpretive tradition, noted here.

passages.text: And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep. And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it. And, behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, I am the LORD God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed.
passages.zh: 他來到一個地方，因為太陽落了，就在那裡過夜；便拿那地方的石頭枕在頭下，在那裡躺臥睡了。他作夢，見有一個梯子立在地上，梯子的頂端通天，又有神的使者在梯子上上去下來。看哪，耶和華站在梯子以上，說：「我是耶和華你祖亞伯拉罕的神，也是以撒的神；你現在躺臥之地，我要賜給你和你的後裔。」

passages.text: And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of. And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not. And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven. And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it. And he called the name of that place Bethel.
passages.zh: 「看哪，我與你同在，你無論往哪裡去，我必保佑你，也必領你歸回這地；我必不離棄你，直到我成全了向你應許的話。」雅各睡醒了，說：「耶和華真在這裡，我竟不知道！」他就懼怕，說：「這地方何等可畏！這不是別的，乃是神的殿，也是天的門。」雅各清早起來，把他枕頭的石頭立作柱子，澆油在上面。他就給那地方起名叫伯特利。

title.en: Seven Years for Rachel, Deceived by Leah
title.zh: 為拉結服事七年，被利亞所欺

region.en: Haran, land of the people of the east
region.zh: 哈蘭，東方之地

period: Genesis 29-30, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 29-30

summary.en: At Haran's well Jacob rolls away the stone, kisses Rachel, and weeps; he serves Laban seven years for her, 'and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her' — only to wake after the wedding feast and find Leah, veiled, in the dark. He gains Rachel a week later by serving seven years more. The two rival wives and their maids bear the twelve sons of Israel, Leah's womb opened because she was hated and Rachel's at last with Joseph.
summary.zh: 雅各在哈蘭井旁推石飲羊，吻拉結而哭；為她服事拉班七年，「因深愛拉結，就看這七年如同幾天」——婚宴翌晨才發現黑暗中竟是利亞。再服七年始得拉結。二妻與二使女為他生下以色列十二支派；利亞因失寵而蒙眷顧，拉結終生約瑟。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Deceiver deceived; the divine-marriage tag is loose (a marriage-quest narrative), noted here.

passages.text: And while he yet spake with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep; for she kept them. And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, that Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother's brother. And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept. And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's brother, and that he was Rebekah's son: and she ran and told her father.
passages.zh: 雅各正和他們說話的時候，拉結領著她父親的羊來了，因為那些羊是她牧放的。雅各一看見他母舅拉班的女兒拉結，又看見他母舅拉班的羊群，就上前把井口的石頭挪開，飲了他母舅拉班的羊群。雅各與拉結親嘴，就放聲而哭。雅各告訴拉結，自己是她父親的外甥，是利百加的兒子；拉結就跑去告訴她父親。

passages.text: And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter. And Laban said, It is better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man: abide with me. And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her. And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her. And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me?
passages.zh: 雅各喜愛拉結，就說：「我願為你小女兒拉結服事你七年。」拉班說：「我把她給你，勝過給別人；你與我同住吧。」雅各就為拉結服事了七年；因為他深愛拉結，就看這七年如同幾天。到了晚上，拉班將他的女兒利亞送來給雅各，雅各就與她同房。到了早晨，一看，竟是利亞；雅各就對拉班說：「你向我做的是什麼事呢？」

passages.text: And Laban said, It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn. Fulfil her week, and we will give thee this also for the service which thou shalt serve with me yet seven other years. And he went in also unto Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him yet seven other years. And when the LORD saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb: but Rachel was barren. And God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and opened her womb. And she conceived, and bare a son; and said, God hath taken away my reproach: and she called his name Joseph.
passages.zh: 拉班說：我們這地方沒有把小的先給大的規矩。你為這一個滿了七日，我們就把那一個也給你，你再與我同住七年，作為服事我的工價。雅各也與拉結同房，並且愛拉結勝過愛利亞，又服事拉班七年。耶和華見利亞失寵，就使她生育，拉結卻不生育。神記念拉結，應允了她，使她能生育。她就懷孕生子，說：神除去了我的羞恥；就給他起名叫約瑟。

title.en: The Flight from Laban and the Mizpah Covenant
title.zh: 逃離拉班與米斯巴之約

region.en: Mount Gilead, east of the Jordan
region.zh: 基列山，約旦河東

period: Genesis 31, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 31

summary.en: Told by God to return, Jacob slips away while Laban is shearing sheep; Rachel steals her father's household gods and hides them in camel's furniture, sitting on them and pleading the custom of women. Warned in a dream, Laban pursues, searches, finds nothing, and the two raise a heap of stones — Galeed and Mizpah — swearing the LORD watch between them when they are absent one from another.
summary.zh: 神諭雅各歸回，趁拉班剪羊毛之際潛逃；拉結偷了父親家中的神像，藏於駱駝馱簍，坐在其上託詞「身上不便」。拉班夢中被神警告，追及基列，搜遍帳棚而不得。二人累石為證，立約於米斯巴——「願耶和華在你我中間鑒察」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Boundary-covenant etiology of the Mizpah heap.

passages.text: And Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his wives upon camels; and he carried away all his cattle, and all his goods which he had gotten, for to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan. And Laban went to shear his sheep: and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father's. And Jacob stole away unawares to Laban the Syrian, in that he told him not that he fled.
passages.zh: 雅各起來，叫他的兒子和妻子都騎上駱駝；又帶著他在巴旦亞蘭所積蓄的一切牲畜和財物，往迦南地他父親以撒那裏去了。當時拉班剪羊毛去了，拉結偷了她父親家中的神像。雅各背著亞蘭人拉班偷偷走了，並沒有告訴他。

passages.text: And it was told Laban on the third day that Jacob was fled. And he took his brethren with him, and pursued after him seven days' journey; and they overtook him in the mount Gilead. And God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream by night, and said unto him, Take heed that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad. And now, though thou wouldest needs be gone, because thou sore longedst after thy father's house, yet wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?
passages.zh: 到第三日，有人告訴拉班說：雅各逃跑了。拉班帶領他的眾弟兄去追趕，追了七日，在基列山就追上了。夜間，神到亞蘭人拉班那裏，在夢中對他說：你要小心，不可與雅各說好說歹。現在你雖然想你父家，不得不去，為甚麼又偷了我的神像呢？

passages.text: Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel's furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found them not. And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of women is upon me. And he searched but found not the images. Now therefore come thou, let us make a covenant, I and thou; and let it be for a witness between me and thee. And Mizpah; for he said, The LORD watch between me and thee, when we are absent one from another.
passages.zh: 拉結已經把神像藏在駱駝的馱簍裏，便坐在上頭。拉班摸遍了那帳棚，並沒有摸著。拉結對她父親說：現在我身上不便，不能在你面前起來，求我主不要生氣。這樣，拉班搜尋神像，竟沒有搜出來。來罷，你我二人可以立約，作你我中間的證據。又叫米斯巴，意思說：我們彼此離別以後，願耶和華在你我中間鑒察。

title.en: Jacob Wrestles at Peniel
title.zh: 雅各在毗努伊勒摔跤

region.en: Ford of the Jabbok river
region.zh: 雅博渡口

period: Genesis 32-33, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 32-33

summary.en: Sick with fear of Esau's four hundred men, Jacob sends everything across the Jabbok and is left alone; a man wrestles with him till daybreak, touches the hollow of his thigh, and blesses him when Jacob will not let go — 'thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.' Jacob calls the place Peniel, 'for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved', and limps for life; the children of Israel do not eat the sinew that shrank. The next day the brothers embrace and weep.
summary.zh: 雅各懼以掃四百人，將家眷財物渡過雅博河，獨自留下；有個人與他摔跤直到黎明，摸其大腿窩，雅各緊抓不放求祝福——「你的名不要再叫雅各，要叫以色列，因為你與神與人較力，都得了勝。」雅各名其地為毗努伊勒：「我面對面見了神，我的性命仍得保全」，從此瘸腿；以色列人不吃大腿窩的筋。翌日兄弟相擁而泣。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The name-change and the food prohibition are the ritual-origin elements; interpretive traditions differ on who the wrestler is.

passages.text: And he rose up that night, and took his two wives, and his two womenservants, and his eleven sons, and passed over the ford Jabbok. And he took them, and sent them over the brook, and sent over that he had. And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him.
passages.zh: 他夜間起來，帶著兩個妻子、兩個使女，並十一個兒子，都過了雅博渡口。他打發他們過河，又打發所有的都過去。只剩下雅各一人。有一個人來和他摔跤，直到黎明。那人見自己勝不過他，就摸他的大腿窩；雅各的大腿窩正在摔跤的時候就扭了。

passages.text: And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me. And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob. And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed. And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved. And as he passed over Penuel the sun rose upon him, and he halted upon his thigh.
passages.zh: 那人說：天黎明了，容我去罷。雅各說：你不給我祝福，我就不容你去。那人說：你名叫甚麼？他說：我名叫雅各。那人說：你的名不要再叫雅各，要叫以色列；因為你與神與人較力，都得了勝。雅各便給那地方起名叫毗努伊勒，意思說：我面對面見了神，我的性命仍得保全。日頭剛出來的時候，雅各經過毗努伊勒，他的大腿就瘸了。

passages.text: And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau came, and with him four hundred men. And he passed over before them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother. And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept. And Esau said, I have enough, my brother; keep that thou hast unto thyself. And Jacob said, Nay, I pray thee, if now I have found grace in thy sight, then receive my present at my hand.
passages.zh: 雅各舉目觀看，見以掃來了，後頭跟著四百人。他便在他們前頭過去，一連七次俯伏在地，直到就近他哥哥。以掃跑來迎接他，將他抱住，又摟著他的頸項與他親嘴，兩個人就哭了。以掃說：「兄弟啊，我的已經夠了，你的仍歸你吧。」雅各說：「不然，我若在你眼前蒙恩，就求你從我手裡收下我的禮物。」

title.en: Dinah and the Massacre of Shechem
title.zh: 底拿與示劍屠城

region.en: Shechem, city of Hamor
region.zh: 示劍，哈抹之城

period: Genesis 34, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 34

summary.en: Shechem, the Hivite prince's son, takes and defiles Dinah, then loves her and asks for her in marriage. Jacob's sons answer deceitfully: all the men of the city consent to circumcision as the price of intermarriage; on the third day, while they are sore, Simeon and Levi put the city to the sword, spoil it, and carry off wives, children, and wealth. Jacob fears the land will rise against him; his sons answer coldly, 'Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?'
summary.zh: 示劍玷污底拿，後因愛她求婚。雅各眾子以詭詐回答：全城男丁為通婚受割禮；第三日眾人疼痛之際，西緬與利未提劍屠城，擄掠財物婦孺。雅各懼迦南人聚集攻滅全家，眾子冷冷回答：「他豈可待我們的妹子如同妓女麼？」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as a violation-and-vengeance narrative; the massacre is presented without endorsement, and Jacob's rebuke is part of the text.

passages.text: And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land. And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her. And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel. And Shechem spake unto his father Hamor, saying, Get me this damsel to wife.
passages.zh: 利亞給雅各所生的女兒底拿出去，要見那地的女子們。那地的主希未人哈抹的兒子示劍看見她，就拉住她，與她同寢，玷辱了她。示劍的心繫戀雅各的女兒底拿，喜愛這女子，甜言蜜語地安慰她。示劍對他父親哈抹說：「求你為我聘這女子為妻。」

passages.text: And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and said, because he had defiled Dinah their sister: We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; for that were a reproach unto us: but in this will we consent unto you: If ye will be as we be, that every male of you be circumcised. And unto Hamor and unto Shechem his son hearkened all that went out of the gate of his city; and every male was circumcised.
passages.zh: 雅各的兒子們因為示劍玷污了他們的妹子底拿，就用詭詐的話回答示劍和他父親哈抹，說：「我們不能把我們的妹子給沒有受割禮的人為妻，因為那是我們的羞辱。惟有一件才可以應允：若你們所有的男丁都受割禮，和我們一樣。凡從他城門出入的人，都聽從了哈抹和他兒子示劍的話，於是凡出城門的男丁都受了割禮。

passages.text: And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males. And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem's house, and went out. The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and spoiled the city, because they had defiled their sister. And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land.
passages.zh: 到第三天，眾人正在疼痛的時候，雅各的兩個兒子，就是底拿的哥哥西緬和利未，各拿刀劍，趁著眾人想不到的時候來到城中，把一切男丁都殺了。又用刀殺了哈抹和他兒子示劍，把底拿從示劍家裡帶出來就走了。雅各的兒子們因為他們的妹子受了玷污，就來到被殺的人那裡，擄掠那城。雅各對西緬和利未說：「你們連累我，使我在這地的居民中有了臭名。」

title.en: Tamar and the Pledges of Judah
title.zh: 他瑪與猶大的信物

region.en: Road to Timnath, by Adullam
region.zh: 往亭拿路上，亞杜蘭附近

period: Genesis 38, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 38

summary.en: Er dies, Onan refuses to raise up seed to his brother and dies, and Judah withholds young Shelah from Tamar — so Tamar veils herself as a shrine prostitute at the road gate, takes Judah's signet, bracelets, and staff as pledge, and conceives. Accused of harlotry and dragged out to be burned, she produces the pledges: 'she hath been more righteous than I,' Judah admits. Of the twins Pharez and Zarah, Pharez carries the line to David — and, in Matthew's genealogy, to Jesus.
summary.zh: 珥死，俄南不肯為兄立後而死，猶大又扣下示拉；他瑪遂蒙面扮妓，坐在往亭拿的路口，取猶大的印、帶子與杖為當頭而懷孕。被告淫亂拉出要燒時，她出示信物；猶大說：「她比我更有義。」其孿生子法勒斯攜猶大支派血統至大衛，馬太福音家譜更達於耶穌。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Levirate law and pledge-trickery narrative; the messianic lineage reading (Matthew 1) is noted.

passages.text: And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Tamar. And Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD; and the LORD slew him. And Judah said unto Onan, Go in unto thy brother's wife, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother. And Onan knew that the seed should not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother's wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother. And the thing which he did displeased the LORD: wherefore he slew him also.
passages.zh: 猶大為長子珥娶妻，名叫他瑪。猶大的長子珥在耶和華眼中看為惡，耶和華就叫他死了。猶大對俄南說：「你當與你哥哥的妻子同房，向她盡你為弟的本分，為你哥哥生子立後。」俄南知道生子不歸自己，所以同房的時候便遺在地，免得給他哥哥留後。俄南所做的在耶和華眼中看為惡，耶和華也就叫他死了。

passages.text: And she put her widow's garments off from her, and covered her with a vail, and wrapped herself, and sat in an open place, which is by the way to Timnath; for she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given unto him to wife. When Judah saw her, he thought her to be an harlot; because she had covered her face. And she said, Wilt thou give me a pledge, till thou send it? And he said, What pledge shall I give thee? And she said, Thy signet, and thy bracelets, and thy staff that is in thine hand. And he gave it her, and came in unto her, and she conceived by him.
passages.zh: 他瑪見示拉已經長大，還沒有娶她為妻，就脫了她作寡婦的衣裳，用帕子蒙著臉，又遮住身體，坐在亭拿路上的伊拿印城門口。猶大看見她，以為是妓女，因為她蒙著臉。他瑪說：「你要與我同寢，把什麼給我呢？」他說：「我從羊群裡取一隻山羊羔送給你。」他瑪說：「在未送以先，你願意給我一個當頭嗎？」他說：「我給你什麼當頭呢？」他瑪說：「你的印、你的帶子，和你手裡的杖。」猶大就給了她，與她同寢，她就從猶大懷了孕。

passages.text: And it came to pass about three months after, that it was told Judah, saying, Tamar thy daughter in law hath played the harlot; and also, behold, she is with child by whoredom. And Judah said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt. When she was brought forth, she sent to her father in law, saying, By the man, whose these are, am I with child: and she said, Discern, I pray thee, whose are these, the signet, and bracelets, and staff. And Judah acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son.
passages.zh: 約過了三個月，有人告訴猶大說：「你的兒婦她瑪作了妓女，且因行淫有了身孕。」猶大說：「把她拉出來，燒了她。」她瑪被拉出來的時候，便打發人去見她的公公，說：「這些東西是誰的，我就是從誰懷的孕。請你認一認，這印、這帶子、這杖，都是誰的？」猶大承認說：「她比我更有義，因為我沒有將她給我的兒子示拉。」

title.en: Joseph's Dreams and the Coat in the Pit
title.zh: 約瑟的夢與坑中的彩衣

region.en: Dothan, hills of Canaan
region.zh: 多坍，迦南山丘

period: Genesis 37, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 37

summary.en: Israel's coat of many colours marks his love for Joseph, and the seventeen-year-old's two dreams — sheaves bowing to his sheaf, sun, moon, and eleven stars bowing to him — sharpen the brothers' hatred. Sent to check on them at Dothan, he is stripped, thrown into a dry pit, and sold by Judah's counsel to Ishmaelite traders for twenty pieces of silver; the brothers dip the coat in goat's blood, and Jacob refuses comfort, 'I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning.'
summary.zh: 以色列為約瑟作彩衣，十七歲的少年連得二夢——禾捆下拜，日月十一星下拜——招致兄長嫉恨。奉父命赴多坍探望，兄長們剝其彩衣，投之於無水的坑，經猶大提議，以二十舍客勒銀子賣給以實瑪利商人。眾兄以羊羔血染彩衣，雅各不肯受安慰：「我必悲哀著下陰間到我兒子那裏。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The dreams function as true prophecy in the narrative arc.

passages.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours. And when his brethren saw that their father loved him more than all his brethren, they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him. And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it his brethren: and they hated him yet the more. For, behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.
passages.zh: 以色列原來愛約瑟過於愛他的眾子，因為約瑟是他年老生的；他給約瑟做了一件彩衣。約瑟的哥哥們見父親愛約瑟過於愛他們，就恨約瑟，不與他說和睦的話。約瑟做了一夢，告訴他哥哥們，他們就越發恨他。約瑟對他們說：「請聽我所做的夢：我們在田裡捆禾稼，我的捆起來站著，你們的捆來圍著我的捆下拜。」

passages.text: And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me. And he told it to his father, and to his brethren: and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth? And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.
passages.zh: 後來他又做了一夢，也告訴他的哥哥們說：「看哪，我又做了一夢，夢見太陽、月亮，與十一個星向我下拜。」約瑟將這夢告訴他父親和他哥哥們，他父親就責備他說：「你做的這是什麼夢！難道我和你母親、你弟兄果然要來俯伏在地，向你下拜嗎？」他哥哥們都嫉妒他，他父親卻把這話存在心裡。

passages.text: And when they saw him afar off, even before he came near unto them, they conspired against him to slay him. And Reuben heard it, and he delivered him out of their hands; and said, Let us not kill him. And they stript Joseph out of his coat, his coat of many colours that was on him: and they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit was empty, there was no water in it. And Judah said unto his brethren, Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites. And they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.
passages.zh: 他們遠遠地看見他，趁他還沒有走近他們，就商議要害死他。流便聽見了，要救他脫離他們的手，說：「我們不可害他的性命。」他們就剝了他的外衣，就是他穿的那件彩衣，把他丟在坑裡；那坑是空的，裡頭沒有水。猶大對眾弟兄說：「我們不如將他賣給以實瑪利人。」他們就把約瑟從坑裡拉上來，講定二十舍客勒銀子，把約瑟賣給以實瑪利人。他們就把約瑟帶到埃及去了。

title.en: Joseph and Potiphar's Wife
title.zh: 約瑟與波提乏之妻

region.en: Potiphar's house, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及，波提乏家中

period: Genesis 39, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 39

summary.en: Sold to Potiphar, captain of Pharaoh's guard, Joseph prospers so that all his master's house is blessed through him; made overseer of everything, he refuses the master's wife day by day — 'how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?' — until, catching her grip on his garment, he flees leaving it in her hand. Her false cry convicts him before her husband, and the innocent slave is cast into the prison where the king's prisoners are bound.
summary.zh: 約瑟被賣給法老的內臣波提乏，事事蒙福，治理全家；卻日日拒絕主母——「我怎能作這大惡，得罪神呢？」終有一日，主母抓其衣裳，他棄衣而逃。主母誣告，主人怒而將無辜的奴隸下在監裏，與王的囚犯同囚。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Chastity-falsely-accused tale type; the trickster tag applies to the wife's deception.

passages.text: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites. And his master saw that the LORD was with him, and that the LORD made all that he did to prosper in his hand. And Joseph found grace in his sight, and he served him: and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.
passages.zh: 約瑟被帶下埃及去。有一個埃及人，是法老的內臣、護衛長波提乏，從那些以實瑪利人手下買了他去。他主人見耶和華與他同在，又見耶和華使他手裡所辦的盡都順利。約瑟就在主人眼前蒙恩，伺候他主人，並且主人派他管理家務，把一切所有的都交在他手裡。

passages.text: And it came to pass after these things, that his master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me. But he refused, and said unto his master's wife, Behold, my master wotteth not what is with me in the house, and he hath committed all that he hath to my hand; there is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
passages.zh: 這事以後，約瑟主人的妻以目送情給約瑟，說：「你與我同寢吧！」約瑟不從，對他主人的妻說：「看哪，一切家務，我主人都不知道，他把所有的都交在我手裡。在這家裡沒有比我大的，並且他沒有留下一樣不交給我，只留下了你，因為你是他的妻子。我怎能作這大惡，得罪神呢？」

passages.text: And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out. That she called unto the men of her house, and spake unto them, saying, See, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us. And she laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home. And Joseph's master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison. But the LORD was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
passages.zh: 她抓住他的衣裳，說：「與我同寢吧。」他卻把衣裳留在她手裡，逃出去，跑到外頭去了。她便叫了家裡的人來，對他們說：「看哪，他帶了一個希伯來人進到我們這裡，要戲弄我們。」她把他的衣裳收著，直到她主人回家。約瑟的主人把他拿住，下在監裡，就是王的囚犯被囚的地方；他就在那裡坐監。但耶和華與約瑟同在，向他施恩，使他在監獄長眼前蒙恩。

title.en: The Butler's Dream in Pharaoh's Prison
title.zh: 法老監中酒政之夢

region.en: Prison of the captain of the guard, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及，護衛長監中

period: Genesis 40, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 40

summary.en: Pharaoh's chief butler and baker offend him and are bound in Joseph's prison; both dream, and Joseph — 'Do not interpretations belong to God?' — reads the vine with three branches as three days to restoration, and the three white baskets eaten by birds as three days to hanging. All falls out on Pharaoh's birthday; yet the restored butler forgets Joseph for two full years.
summary.zh: 法老的酒政與膳長得罪主人被囚，同夜各得一夢。約瑟說「解夢不是出於神麼」——葡萄三枝即三日復職，頭上三筐白餅被飛鳥吃盡即三日被掛。果然應驗於法老生日；然而復職的酒政竟忘了約瑟，一忘兩年。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Dream-interpretation narrative.

passages.text: And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, which were bound in the prison. And Joseph came in unto them in the morning, and looked upon them, and, behold, they were sad. And they said unto him, We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it. And Joseph said unto them, Do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you.
passages.zh: 他們二人同夜各做一夢，各夢都有講解，就是埃及王的酒政和膳長，被囚在監裡的。早晨約瑟來到他們那裡，看他們，見他們面帶愁容。他們對他說：「我們做了一夢，沒有人能解。」約瑟對他們說：「解夢豈不是出於神嗎？請你們將夢告訴我。」

passages.text: In my dream, behold, a vine was before me; and in the vine were three branches: and it was as though it budded, and her blossoms shot forth; and the clusters thereof brought forth ripe grapes: and Pharaoh's cup was in my hand: and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand. And Joseph said unto him, This is the interpretation of it: The three branches are three days: yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thine head, and restore thee unto thy place.
passages.zh: 我夢見在我面前有一棵葡萄樹；樹上有三根枝子，好像發了芽，開了花，上頭的葡萄都成熟了：法老的杯在我手中，我就拿葡萄擠在法老的杯裡，將杯遞在法老手中。約瑟對他說：「這就是夢的講解：三根枝子就是三天；三天之內，法老必提你出監，叫你官復原職。」

passages.text: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said unto Joseph, I also was in my dream, and, behold, I had three white baskets on my head: and in the uppermost basket there was of all manner of bakemeats for Pharaoh; and the birds did eat them out of the basket upon my head. And Joseph answered and said, This is the interpretation thereof: The three baskets are three days: yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee. And it came to pass the third day, which was Pharaoh's birthday. Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.
passages.zh: 膳長見夢解得好，就對約瑟說：「我也做了一夢，見我頭上頂著三筐白餅；最上面的筐子裡有為法老烤的各樣食物；有飛鳥來吃我頭上筐子裡的食物。」約瑟回答說：「這就是夢的講解：三個筐子就是三天；三天之內，法老必斬斷你的頭，把你掛在木頭上；必有飛鳥來吃你身上的肉。」到了第三天，正是法老的生日。然而酒政卻不記念約瑟，竟忘了他。

title.en: Pharaoh's Dreams and Joseph as Vizier
title.zh: 法老之夢與約瑟為相

region.en: Pharaoh's court, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及法老宮廷

period: Genesis 41, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 41

summary.en: Two years on, Pharaoh dreams of seven fat kine devoured by seven lean kine and of seven full ears blasted by seven thin, and none of Egypt's magicians can read it. The butler remembers Joseph, who is brought from the dungeon, shaved and changed, and declares 'It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace' — seven years plenty, then seven years famine. Pharaoh sets the ring on Joseph's hand, clothes him in fine linen, names him Zaphnathpaaneah, and rides him in the second chariot; the storehouses of Egypt are filled against the famine.
summary.zh: 兩年後，法老夢見七肥牛被七瘦牛所吞，七好穗被七枯穗所滅；埃及術士皆不能解。酒政想起約瑟，遂自監中提出，剃頭換衣入宮。約瑟說：「這不在乎我，神必將平安的話回答法老。」——七豐年後七荒年。法老將手上戒指戴在約瑟手上，賜名撒發那忒巴內亞，使其乘副車巡行埃及全地，倉廩囤糧以備荒年。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The foreign vizier narrative; the second-chariot investiture is the kingship element.

passages.text: And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and, behold, he stood by the river. And, behold, there came up out of the river seven well favoured kine and fatfleshed; and they fed in a meadow. And, behold, seven other kine came up after them out of the river, ill favoured and leanfleshed; and the ill favoured and leanfleshed kine did eat up the seven well favoured and fat kine. And he slept and dreamed the second time: and, behold, seven ears of corn came up upon one stalk, rank and good; and, behold, seven thin ears and blasted with the east wind sprung up after them.
passages.zh: 過了整整兩年，法老做夢：夢見自己站在河邊。看哪，從河裡上來七隻母牛，又美又肥壯，在蘆葦中吃草。看哪，隨後又有七隻母牛從河裡上來，又醜陋又乾瘦；那又醜陋又乾瘦的母牛吃盡了那又美又肥壯的七隻母牛。他又睡著，第二次做夢：看哪，一株麥子上長了七個穗子，又飽滿又佳美；看哪，隨後又長出七個穗子，又細弱又被東風吹焦了。

passages.text: Then spake the chief butler unto Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day. And there was there with us a young man, an Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard; and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams; and it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it was. Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.
passages.zh: 那時，酒政對法老說：「我今日想起我的罪來。從前有我們同在的，有一個希伯來少年人，是護衛長的僕人；我們告訴他，他就為我們解夢；他所解的，果然應驗了。」法老便打發人召約瑟，他們就急忙把他從監裡提出來；他剃了頭，換了衣裳，進到法老面前。

passages.text: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace. The seven good kine are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one. Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt: and there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land. Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.
