passages.zh: 約瑟回答法老說：「這不在乎我，神必將平安的話回答法老。」七隻好母牛是七年，七個好穗子也是七年；這夢乃是一個。看哪，埃及全地必來七個大豐年，隨後又要來七個荒年，甚至在埃及地都忘了先前的豐收，全地必被饑荒所滅。所以法老當揀選一個有見識、有智慧的人，派他治理埃及地。

passages.text: And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is? And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath shewed thee all this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou art: thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou. And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph's hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck; and he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee.
passages.zh: 法老對臣僕說：「像這樣的人，有神的靈在他裡頭，我們豈能找得著呢？」法老對約瑟說：「神既將這事都指示你，可見沒有人像你這樣有見識、有智慧。你可以掌管我的家，我的民都必聽從你的話，惟獨在寶座上我比你大。」法老就摘下手上打印的戒指，戴在約瑟的手上，給他穿上細麻衣，把金鍊戴在他的頸項上；又叫約瑟坐他的副車，喝道的在前呼叫說：「跪下。」

title.en: The Silver Cup in Benjamin's Sack
title.zh: 便雅憫袋中的銀杯

region.en: Joseph's house, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及，約瑟府中

period: Genesis 42-44, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 42-44

summary.en: When ten brothers bow before the governor of Egypt begging corn, they do not know him, but he remembers his dreams and tests them: Simeon bound, corn returned with their money, Benjamin demanded. On the second visit Joseph weeps in private at the sight of his brother, feasts them, then hides his silver divining cup in Benjamin's sack; the cup is 'found', Judah offers himself as surety — 'let thy servant abide instead of the lad' — and the trap of mercy is sprung.
summary.zh: 十個哥哥向埃及宰相俯伏糴糧，不識其人，約瑟卻記得幼年的夢，並試驗他們：捆西緬、還銀糧、索便雅憫。再來時，約瑟見幼弟而暗自飲泣，設宴款待，又將銀杯藏於便雅憫袋中；搜出後，猶大以己身代之——「求你容僕人住下，替這童子作我主的奴僕」——憐憫的網羅已然張開。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The cup is used for divination in the narrative detail; tagged accordingly.

passages.text: Now when Jacob saw that there was corn in Egypt, Jacob said unto his sons, Why do ye look one upon another? And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is corn in Egypt: get you down thither, and buy for us from thence. And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph's brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth. And Joseph saw his brethren, and he knew them, but made himself strange unto them; and he remembered the dreams which he dreamed of them.
passages.zh: 雅各見埃及有糧，就對兒子們說：「你們為什麼彼此觀望呢？」又說：「我聽見埃及有糧，你們可以下去，從那裡為我們買些來。」那時治理埃及地的是約瑟，糶糧給那地眾民的就是他。約瑟的哥哥們來了，臉伏於地，向他下拜。約瑟看見他哥哥們，就認得他們，卻裝作生人，向他們說些嚴厲的話，又想起從前所做關於他們的夢。

passages.text: And Joseph made haste; for his bowels did yearn upon his brother: and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there. And he commanded the steward of his house, saying, Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put every man's money in his sack's mouth. And put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack's mouth of the youngest, and his corn money. And he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
passages.zh: 約瑟愛弟之情發動，就急忙尋找可哭之地，進入自己的屋裡，哭了一場。他吩咐家宰說：「把這些人的口袋裝滿糧食，盡著他們所能帶的，又把各人的銀子放在各人的口袋裡。並將我的銀杯和那少年人糴糧的銀子，一同裝在他的口袋裡。」家宰就照約瑟所說的話行了。

passages.text: Then they speedily took down every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack. And he searched, and began at the eldest, and left at the youngest: and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack. Then they rent their clothes, and laded every man his ass, and returned to the city. And Judah said, What shall we say unto my lord? Now therefore, I pray thee, let thy servant abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren. For how shall I go up to my father, and the lad be not with me?
passages.zh: 於是他們各人急忙把口袋卸在地上，各人打開口袋。家宰就搜查，從年長的起，到年幼的為止，那杯竟在便雅憫的口袋裡搜出來。他們就撕裂衣服，各人把馱子抬在驢上，回城去了。猶大說：「我們對我主說什麼呢？現在求你容僕人住下，替這童子作我主的奴僕，叫童子和他哥哥們一同上去。若童子不和我同去，我怎能上去見我父親呢？」

title.en: I Am Joseph: Reunion in Goshen
title.zh: 我是約瑟：歌珊重逢

region.en: Goshen, land of Egypt
region.zh: 埃及歌珊地

period: Genesis 45-46, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 45-46

summary.en: Unable to restrain himself before all his retinue, Joseph cries 'Cause every man to go out from me' and reveals himself weeping aloud — 'I am Joseph; doth my father yet live?' He forgives: 'ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to save much people alive.' Pharaoh sends wagons, the stunned Jacob's spirit revives, and at Beersheba God appears to Israel in visions of the night promising to go down with him and bring him up again. Father and son fall on each other's necks in Goshen.
summary.zh: 約瑟在隨從面前不能再自禁，喊道「人都要離開我出去」，放聲大哭表明身份：「我是約瑟！我父親還在麼？」他饒恕他們：「從前你們的意思是要害我，但神的意思原是好的，要保全許多人的性命。」法老遣車接眷；雅各聞言心裏甦醒，在別是巴夜間異象中得神應許同行下埃及。父子在歌珊相擁而泣。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The descent into Egypt founds the Israel-in-Egypt cycle that Exodus continues.

passages.text: Then Joseph could not refrain himself before all them that stood by him; and he cried, Cause every man to go out from me. And there stood no man with him, while Joseph made himself known unto his brethren. And he wept aloud: and the Egyptians and the house of Pharaoh heard. And Joseph said unto his brethren, I am Joseph; doth my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him; for they were troubled at his presence.
passages.zh: 約瑟在左右站著的人面前，情不自禁，吩咐一聲說：「人都要離開我出去！」約瑟向弟兄們相認的時候，並沒有一人站在他面前。他就放聲大哭，埃及人和法老家中的人都聽見了。約瑟對他的弟兄們說：「我是約瑟，我的父親還在嗎？」他弟兄不能回答，因為在他面前都驚惶。

passages.text: And Joseph said unto his brethren, Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said, I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt. Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life. So now it was not you that sent me hither, but God: and he hath made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and a ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.
passages.zh: 約瑟對他的弟兄們說：「請你們近前來。」他們就近前來。他說：「我是你們的兄弟約瑟，就是你們所賣到埃及的。現在，不要因為把我賣到這裡而自憂自恨，這是神差我在你們以先來，為要保全生命。這樣看來，差我到這裡來的不是你們，乃是神。他又使我如法老的父，作他全家的主，並埃及全地的宰相。

passages.text: And Israel took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices unto the God of his father Isaac. And God spake unto Israel in the visions of the night, and said, Jacob, Jacob. And he said, Here am I. And he said, I am God, the God of thy father: fear not to go down into Egypt; for I will there make of thee a great nation: I will go down with thee into Egypt; and I will also surely bring thee up again.
passages.zh: 以色列帶著他一切所有的起行，來到別是巴，就獻祭給他父親以撒的神。神在夜間的異象中對以色列說：「雅各，雅各。」他說：「我在這裡。」神說：「我是神，就是你父親的神。你下埃及去不要害怕，因為我必使你在那裡成為大族。我要和你同下埃及去，也必定帶你上來。」

title.en: Jacob's Last Words: The Sceptre of Judah
title.zh: 雅各遺言：猶大的杖

region.en: Jacob's bed, land of Goshen, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及歌珊地，雅各床前

period: Genesis 47-49, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 47-49

summary.en: Gathering his twelve sons at his deathbed 'to tell you that which shall befall you in the last days', Jacob blesses and characterizes each tribe in turn: Reuben unstable as water, Simeon and Levi scattered for the massacre, Judah a lion's whelp of whom 'the sceptre shall not depart... until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be' — the verse Christian tradition reads messianically of Christ — and Joseph the fruitful bough of double blessing. He charges burial in Machpelah and dies, and is mourned by all Egypt seventy days.
summary.zh: 臨終召集十二子「把你們日後必遇的事告訴你們」：流便如水滾沸不得居首，西緬利未因屠城分散，猶大如小獅——「圭必不離猶大，杖必不離他兩腳之間，直等細羅來到，萬民都必歸順」——基督教傳統以此為彌賽亞基督之預言；約瑟則是多結果子的樹枝，蒙雙倍祝福。遺命葬麥比拉洞，埃及為其哀哭七十日。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Shiloh verse is one of the most contested messianic readings in scripture; the Christian tradition's reading is noted alongside the tribal-blessing frame.

passages.text: And Jacob called unto his sons, and said, Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days. Reuben, thou art my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, the excellency of dignity, and the excellency of power: unstable as water, thou shalt not excel. Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations. O my soul, come not thou into their secret; for in their anger they slew a man, and in their selfwill they digged down a wall.
passages.zh: 雅各叫了他的兒子們來，說：「你們都來聚集，我好把你們日後必遇的事告訴你們。流便哪，你是我的長子，是我力量強壯的時候生的，本當大有尊榮，權力超眾，但你放縱如水，必不得居首位。西緬和利未是弟兄，他們的刀劍是殘忍的器具。我的靈啊，不要與他們同謀；我的心哪，不要與他們聯絡；因為他們趁怒殺害人命，任意砍斷牛腿大筋。

passages.text: Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father's children shall bow down before thee. Judah is a lion's whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up? The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.
passages.zh: 猶大啊，你弟兄們必讚美你；你手必掐住仇敵的頸項；你父親的兒子們必向你下拜。猶大是個小獅子；我兒啊，你抓了食便上去。你屈下身去，臥如公獅，蹲如母獅，誰敢惹你？圭必不離猶大，杖必不離他兩腳之間，直等細羅來到，萬民都必歸順。

passages.text: Joseph is a fruitful bough, even a fruitful bough by a well; whose branches run over the wall: the archers have sorely grieved him, and shot at him, and hated him: but his bow abode in strength, and the arms of his hands were made strong by the hands of the mighty God of Jacob. Benjamin shall ravin as a wolf: in the morning he shall devour the prey, and at night he shall divide the spoil. All these are the twelve tribes of Israel: and this is it that their father spake unto them, and blessed them; every one according to his blessing he blessed them.
passages.zh: 約瑟是多結果子的樹枝，是泉旁多結果的枝子；他的枝條探出牆外。弓箭手將他苦害，向他射箭，逼迫他。但他的弓仍舊堅硬，他的手健壯敏捷，這是因以色列的牧者，以色列的磐石，就是雅各的大能者。便雅憫是個撕掠的狼，早晨要吃他所抓的，晚上要分他所奪的。這一切是以色列的十二支派；這也是他們的父親對他們所說的話，並為他們所祝的福，都是按著各人的福分為他們祝福。

title.en: The Mourning of Egypt and Joseph's Bones
title.zh: 埃及哀榮與約瑟遺骨

region.en: Goshen to Machpelah, funeral road beyond Jordan
region.zh: 歌珊至麥比拉洞，約旦河外送葬之路

period: Genesis 50, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 50

summary.en: Joseph embalms his father and leads chariots and horsemen, all the elders of Egypt, in a seven-day lamentation at the threshingfloor of Atad — so grievous the Canaanites name it Abelmizraim — before burying Jacob in Machpelah. Then the brothers, fearing revenge, send word of Jacob's command; Joseph weeps and answers 'am I in the place of God?' Dying at 110, Joseph takes an oath of the children of Israel that God will surely visit them and they shall carry up his bones from hence — the oath that Exodus and Joshua will honor.
summary.zh: 約瑟以香料薰父遺體，率法老諸臣與車馬，在約旦河外的亞達禾場哀哭七日，迦南人驚呼「這是埃及人一場極大的哀哭」，遂名亞伯麥西。雅各葬於麥比拉。諸兄懼報復遣使求赦，約瑟哭泣而答「我豈能代替神呢」。約瑟享壽一百一十歲而終，臨終令以色列人起誓：神必眷顧你們，你們要把我的骸骨從這裏搬上去。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The bones-oath frames the Exodus cycle that follows.

passages.text: And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father: and the physicians embalmed Israel. And forty days were fulfilled for him; for so are fulfilled the days of those which are embalmed: and the Egyptians mourned for him threescore and ten days. And Joseph went up to bury his father: and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt, and there went up with him both chariots and horsemen: and it was a very great company.
passages.zh: 約瑟吩咐伺候他的醫生用香料薰他父親，醫生就用香料薰了以色列。薰屍的常例是四十天，那四十天滿了，埃及人為他哀哭了七十天。約瑟為他父親哀哭了七十天。約瑟要上去埋葬他父親，於是他所有的臣僕、他父家的長老，以及埃及地的眾長老，都與他一同上去。又有車輛馬兵和他一同上去，那一隊人甚多。

passages.text: And they came to the threshingfloor of Atad, which is beyond Jordan, and there they mourned with a great and very sore lamentation: and he made a mourning for his father seven days. And when the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, This is a grievous mourning to the Egyptians: wherefore the name of it was called Abelmizraim, which is beyond Jordan. For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah.
passages.zh: 他們到了約但河對岸的亞達禾場，就在那裡大大地號咷痛哭，極其悲傷；約瑟為他父親哀哭了七天。住那地的迦南人看見亞達禾場上的哀哭，就說：「這是埃及人一場極大的哀哭。」因此那地方名叫亞伯麥西，是在約但河東。他的兒子們把他搬到迦南地，葬在幔利前麥比拉田間的洞裡。

passages.text: And when Joseph's brethren saw that their father was dead, they said, Joseph will peradventure hate us, and will certainly requite us all the evil which we did unto him. And Joseph said unto them, Fear not: for am I in the place of God? But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive. And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and God will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob. And Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.
passages.zh: 約瑟的哥哥們見父親死了，就說：「或者約瑟懷恨我們，照著我們從前待他一切的惡，足足地報復我們。」約瑟對他們說：「不要害怕，我豈能代替神呢？從前你們的意思是要害我，但神的意思原是好的，要保全許多人的性命，成就今日的光景。」約瑟對他的弟兄們說：「我要死了，但神必定看顧你們，領你們從這地上去，到他起誓所應許給亞伯拉罕、以撒、雅各之地。」約瑟叫以色列的子孫起誓說：「神必定看顧你們；你們要把我的骸骨從這裡搬上去。」

title.en: The Midwives and the Baby in the Ark of Bulrushes
title.zh: 收生婆與蘆葦箱中的嬰孩

region.en: Nile riverbank, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及，尼羅河畔

period: Exodus 1-2, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 1-2

summary.en: A Pharaoh 'which knew not Joseph' enslaves Israel and orders every Hebrew boy drowned in the river; the midwives Shiphrah and Puah fear God and disobey, telling him Hebrew women deliver before they arrive. A Levite mother hides her goodly son three months, then sets him in a slime-sealed ark of bulrushes among the flags, where Pharaoh's daughter finds him, has pity, and — through the quick tongue of his watchful sister — pays his own mother to nurse him, naming him Moses, 'because I drew him out of the water.'
summary.zh: 「不認識約瑟的新王」壓迫以色列，下令溺殺希伯來男嬰；收生婆施弗拉與普阿敬畏神而不從。利未女子藏子三月，後將其放入塗石漆石油的蘆葦箱，置於河邊蘆荻中。法老女兒發現嬰孩，動了憐憫之心；其姊機敏召來生母代哺。公主為其命名摩西——「因我把他從水裏拉出來」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Judaism and Christianity. The exposed-hero-on-water is presented alongside other river-escape birth narratives.

passages.text: And the king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, of which the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah: and he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live. But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive. Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.
passages.zh: 埃及王對希伯來的收生婆說：一個名叫施弗拉，一個名叫普阿；又說：「你們為希伯來婦人收生，若是男孩，就把他殺了；若是女孩，就留她存活。」但收生婆敬畏神，不照埃及王的吩咐行，竟存留男孩的性命。因此神厚待收生婆；百姓多起來，極其強盛。

passages.text: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi. And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months. And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river's brink. And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him.
passages.zh: 有一個利未家的人娶了一個利未女子為妻。那女人懷孕，生了一個兒子，見他俊美，就把他藏了三個月。後來不能再藏，就取了一個蒲草箱，抹上石漆和石油，將孩子放在裡頭，把箱子擱在河邊的蘆荻中。孩子的姐姐遠遠站著，要知道他究竟怎麼樣。

passages.text: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it. And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews' children. Then said his sister to Pharaoh's daughter, Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee? And she called the child's mother. And the child grew, and she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.
passages.zh: 法老的女兒來到河邊洗澡，她看見蘆荻中的箱子，就打發一個婢女拿來。她打開箱子，看見那孩子；孩子哭了。她就可憐他，說：「這是希伯來人的一個孩子。」孩子的姐姐對法老的女兒說：「我去在希伯來婦人中叫一個奶媽來，為你奶這孩子，可以不可以？」她便叫了孩子的母親來。孩子漸長，婦人把他帶到法老的女兒那裡，就作了她的兒子。她給孩子起名叫摩西，意思說：「因我把他從水裡拉出來。」

title.en: Moses Slays the Egyptian and Flees to Midian
title.zh: 摩西殺埃及人而逃米甸

region.en: Egypt to Midian, by the well
region.zh: 自埃及至米甸井旁

period: Exodus 2, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 2

summary.en: Grown up in Pharaoh's house but going out to look on his brethren's burdens, Moses kills an Egyptian smiting a Hebrew and hides him in the sand; the next day a Hebrew challenges him — 'who made thee a prince and a judge over us?' — and the deed is known, so he flees to Midian. At a well he drives off shepherds harassing Jethro's seven daughters, waters their flock, and marries Zipporah, naming his son Gershom, 'I have been a stranger in a strange land'; meanwhile Israel's cry rises to God, who remembers his covenant.
summary.zh: 摩西在法老宮中長大，卻出去看弟兄的重擔；見埃及人打希伯來人，便殺之藏於沙中。次日被同族揭破——「誰立你作我們的首領和審判官呢？」——遂逃往米甸。在井旁驅散欺凌葉忒羅七女之牧羊人，為其羊群飲水，娶西坡拉為妻，生子革舜——「我在外邦作了寄居的」。以色列人在捆鎖中歎息哀求，神記念祂的約。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as the fugitive-prince-to-shepherd phase of the hero cycle.

passages.text: And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren. And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand. And he said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known. Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.
passages.zh: 後來，摩西長大，他出去到他弟兄那裡，看他們的重擔，見一個埃及人打希伯來人的一個弟兄。他左右觀看，見沒有人，就把埃及人打死了，藏在沙土裡。那人說：「誰立你作我們的首領和審判官呢？難道你要殺我，像殺那埃及人嗎？」摩西便懼怕，說：「這事必是被人知道了。」法老聽見這事，就想殺摩西；但摩西躲避法老，逃往米甸地居住，坐在一口井旁。

passages.text: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father's flock. And the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock. And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter. And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land. And it came to pass in process of time, that the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and their cry came up unto God by reason of the bondage. And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
passages.zh: 米甸的祭司有七個女兒；她們來打水，打滿了槽，要飲父親的羊群。有牧羊的人來，把她們趕走了，摩西卻起來幫助她們，又飲了她們的羊群。摩西甘心和那人同住；那人把他的女兒西坡拉給摩西為妻。西坡拉生了一個兒子，摩西給他起名叫革舜，意思說：「因我在外邦作了寄居的。」過了多年，以色列人因作苦工，就歎息哀求，他們的哀聲達於神。神聽見他們的哀聲，就記念他與亞伯拉罕、以撒、雅各所立的約。

title.en: The Burning Bush and the Name I AM
title.zh: 焚而不毀的荊棘與「自有永有者」

region.en: Horeb, the mountain of God
region.zh: 何烈山，神的山

period: Exodus 3-4, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 3-4

summary.en: Keeping Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses turns aside to see why a bush burns and is not consumed, and the LORD calls from within it, appointing him to bring Israel out of Egypt into a land flowing with milk and honey. Moses' three refusals — Who am I? What is your name? I am slow of speech — are answered by 'I AM THAT I AM', three signs (rod to serpent, leprous hand, water to blood), and Aaron as his mouth; Jesus later grounds his own divine claims on this name.
summary.zh: 摩西牧羊至何烈山，見荊棘被火燒著卻未燒燬，便轉過去看；耶和華從荊棘裏呼叫，差他領以色列出埃及，入流奶與蜜之地。摩西三度推辭——我算甚麼？你叫甚麼名字？我拙口笨舌——神以「我是自有永有的」答之，並賜三個神蹟記號，以亞倫為其口。耶穌後來正是以此名自證其神聖身份。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The divine name is treated with reverence in both Judaism and Christianity; quoted here as public-domain scripture in a comparative framing.

passages.text: And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed. And Moses said, I will now turn aside, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt. And when the LORD saw that he turned aside to see, God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here am I. And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
passages.zh: 耶和華的使者從荊棘裡火焰中向摩西顯現。摩西觀看，不料，荊棘被火燒著，卻沒有燒毀。摩西說：「我要過去看這大異象，這荊棘為何沒有燒壞呢？」耶和華神見他過去要看，就從荊棘裡呼叫說：「摩西！摩西！」他說：「我在這裡。」神說：「不要近前來。當把你腳上的鞋脫下來，因為你所站之地是聖地。」

passages.text: And the LORD said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows; and I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey. Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.
passages.zh: 耶和華說：「我的百姓在埃及所受的困苦，我實在看見了；他們因受督工的轄制所發的哀聲，我也聽見了。我原知道他們的痛苦，我下來是要救他們脫離埃及人的手，領他們出了那地，到美好、寬闊、流奶與蜜之地。故此，我要打發你去見法老，使你可以將我的百姓以色列人從埃及領出來。」

passages.text: And Moses said unto God, Behold, when I come unto the children of Israel, and shall say unto them, The God of your fathers hath sent me unto you; and they shall say to me, What is his name? what shall I say unto them? And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you. And the LORD said furthermore unto him, Put now thine hand into thy bosom. And he put his hand into his bosom: and when he took it out, behold, his hand was leprous as snow.
passages.zh: 摩西對神說：「我到以色列人那裡，對他們說：『你們祖宗的神打發我到你們這裡來。』他們若問我說：『他叫什麼名字？』我要對他們說什麼呢？」神對摩西說：「我是自有永有的」；又說：「你要對以色列人這樣說：『那自有的打發我到你們這裡來。』」耶和華又對他說：「現在把你的手放在懷裡。」他就把手放在懷裡，及至抽出來，不料，手長了大痲瘋，有雪那樣白。

passages.text: And Moses said unto the LORD, O my LORD, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant: but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue. And the LORD said unto him, Who hath made man's mouth? have not I the LORD? Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say. And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses, and he said, Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well. And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people: and he shall be, even he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God.
passages.zh: 摩西對耶和華說：「主啊，我素日不是能言的人，就是從你對僕人說話以後，也是這樣。我本是拙口笨舌的。」耶和華對他說：「誰造人的口呢？誰使人口啞、耳聾、目明、眼瞎呢？豈不是我耶和華嗎？現在去吧，我必賜你口才，指教你所當說的話。」耶和華向摩西發怒說：「不是有你的哥哥利未人亞倫嗎？我知道他是能言的；現在他出來迎接你，他一見你，心裡就歡喜。你要將當說的話傳給他；我也要賜你和他口才，又要指教你們所當行的事。他要替你對百姓說話；你要以他當作口，他要以你當作神。」

title.en: Zipporah at the Night Inn
title.zh: 西坡拉於夜間客店

region.en: Wayside inn, road from Midian to Egypt
region.zh: 米甸往埃及路旁客店

period: Exodus 4:24-26, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 4

summary.en: One of scripture's strangest three verses: on the road back to Egypt the LORD meets Moses and seeks to kill him, until Zipporah takes a sharp stone, circumcises her son, and casts the foreskin at his feet — 'Surely a bloody husband art thou to me' — and so he lets him go. Commentators read it as the unfinished circumcision of Moses' son endangering the covenant-bearer; the blood rite averts the night attack.
summary.zh: 聖經中最奇異的三節經文：歸埃及途中，耶和華遇見摩西，想要殺他；西坡拉急取火石刀，為兒子行割禮，丟在摩西腳前說——「你真是我的血郎了」——神便放他。釋經者以為：未行割禮之子危及立約者之身，血禮解夜間之危。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. An obscure and much-debated episode; presented as a covenant-blood narrative.

passages.text: And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him. Then Zipporah took a sharp stone, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me. So he let him go: then she said, A bloody husband thou art, because of the circumcision.
passages.zh: 摩西在路上住宿的地方，耶和華遇見他，想要殺他。西坡拉就拿一塊火石，割下他兒子的陽皮，丟在摩西腳前，說：「你真是我的血郎了。」這樣，耶和華才放了他。西坡拉說：「你因割禮就是血郎了。」

title.en: Let My People Go: Bricks Without Straw
title.zh: 容我的百姓去：無草製磚

region.en: Pharaoh's court and brickfields, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及法老宮廷與磚窯

period: Exodus 5, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 5

summary.en: Moses and Aaron demand a three-day journey to sacrifice, and Pharaoh answers 'Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice? I know not the LORD, neither will I let Israel go' — then doubles the cruelty by cutting the straw supply while keeping the brick quota, so the officers are beaten and the people blame Moses. The tale of bricks made without straw became the proverb of impossible demands, and the crushed people turn on their deliverer: 'ye have made our savour to be abhorred.'
summary.zh: 摩西亞倫求三日行程往曠野獻祭；法老答「耶和華是誰，使我聽他的話？我不認識耶和華」——反下令不再供草，磚數如常，官長被責打，百姓怨懟摩西。「無草製磚」自此成為不可能之要求之成語；受壓的百姓反咬其拯救者：「你們使我們在法老眼前可憎。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Pharaoh's divine-king denial frames the contest of kingships.

passages.text: And afterward Moses and Aaron went in, and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness. And Pharaoh said, Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice to let Israel go? I know not the LORD, neither will I let Israel go. And the king of Egypt said unto them, Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, let the people from their works? get you unto your burdens.
passages.zh: 此後，摩西和亞倫進去見法老，對他說：「以色列的神耶和華如此說：容我的百姓去，在曠野向我守節。」法老說：「耶和華是誰，使我聽他的話，容以色列人去呢？我不認識耶和華，也不容以色列人去。」埃及王又對他們說：「摩西、亞倫，你們為甚麼叫百姓曠工呢？你們去擔你們的擔子罷。」

passages.text: And Pharaoh commanded the same day the taskmasters of the people, and their officers, saying, Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves. And the tale of the bricks, which they did make heretofore, ye shall lay upon them; ye shall not diminish ought thereof: for they be idle. And the taskmasters hasted them, saying, Fulfil your works, your daily tasks, as when there was straw.
passages.zh: 當日，法老吩咐督工的和官長說：「你們不可照常把草給百姓作磚，叫他們自己去撿草。他們素常作磚的數目，你們仍舊向他們要，一點不可減少；因為他們是懶惰的。」督工的催著他們說：「你們當日完你們的工，與從前有草一樣。」

passages.text: Then the officers of the children of Israel came and cried unto Pharaoh, saying, Wherefore dealest thou thus with thy servants? There is no straw given unto thy servants, and they say to us, Make brick: and, behold, thy servants are beaten; but the fault is in thine own people. But he said, Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and do sacrifice to the LORD. And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood in the way, as they came forth from Pharaoh: and they said unto them, The LORD look upon you, and judge; because ye have made our savour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh.
passages.zh: 以色列人的官長就來哀求法老說：「為甚麼這樣待你的僕人？不把草給你的僕人，又對我們說：『作磚罷！』看哪，你的僕人挨了打，其實是你自己百姓的錯。」但法老說：「你們是懶惰的，你們是懶惰的，所以你們說：『容我們去祭祀耶和華。』他們從法老那裏出來的時候，遇見摩西、亞倫站在對面，就對他們說：「願耶和華鑒察你們，施行判斷；因你們使我們在法老眼前有了臭名。」

title.en: Aaron's Rod Swallows the Sorcerers' Rods
title.zh: 亞倫的杖吞了術士的杖

region.en: Pharaoh's court, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及法老宮廷

period: Exodus 7, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 7

summary.en: Before Pharaoh, Aaron casts down his rod and it becomes a serpent; the Egyptian wise men and sorcerers match the sign with their enchantments — 'but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods.' The court duel of magic opens the plague cycle, and the hardened heart of Pharaoh begins its long, strange refrain.
summary.zh: 法老面前，亞倫丟杖變蛇；埃及的博士和術士也用邪術照樣而行——「但亞倫的杖吞了他們的杖」。這場法術對決揭開災禍的序幕；法老剛硬的心，自此成為奇特的反覆疊句。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Egyptian court sorcery is presented as the narrative foil, not endorsed; the witch tag follows the text's own category of enchanters.

passages.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying, When Pharaoh shall speak unto you, saying, Shew a miracle for you: then thou shalt say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and cast it before Pharaoh, and it shall become a serpent. And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and they did so as the LORD had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh, and before his servants, and it became a serpent.
passages.zh: 耶和華曉諭摩西、亞倫說：「法老若對你們說：『你們行件奇事罷！』你就吩咐亞倫說：『把杖丟在法老面前，使杖變作蛇。』」摩西、亞倫進去見法老，就照耶和華所吩咐的行。亞倫把杖丟在法老和臣僕面前，杖就變作蛇。

passages.text: Then Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers: now the magicians of Egypt, they also did in like manner with their enchantments. For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods. And he hardened Pharaoh's heart, that he hearkened not unto them; as the LORD had said.
passages.zh: 於是法老召了博士和術士來；埃及的術士也用邪術照樣而行。他們各人丟下自己的杖，杖就變作蛇；但亞倫的杖吞了他們的杖。法老心裏剛硬，不肯聽從他們，正如耶和華所說的。

title.en: The Ten Plagues of Egypt
title.zh: 埃及十災

region.en: Land of Egypt, Nile to palace
region.zh: 埃及全地，尼羅河至王宮

period: Exodus 7-10, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 7-10

summary.en: Blood turns the Nile to stench; frogs swarm into ovens and kneadingtroughs; dust becomes lice the magicians cannot copy — 'this is the finger of God'; flies divide Goshen from the palaces; murrain kills the cattle; boils break the magicians' standing; thunder, fire-mingled hail, locusts on the east wind, and a darkness 'which may be felt' for three days fall in turn, each answered by a partial concession and a re-hardened heart — 'that thou mayest know that there is none like me in all the earth.'
summary.zh: 尼羅河化為血腥；青蛙入爐灶揉麵盆；塵土變虱，術士不能複製——「這是神的手段」；成群蒼蠅分別歌珊與王宮；瘟疫斃牲畜；瘡使術士站不住；雷雹夾火；東風捲來蝗蟲；三日黑暗「似乎可以摸得著」。每一次半讓步之後心便再剛硬——「好叫你知道普天下沒有像我的」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The plague cycle is presented as narrative; modern scholarship reads it against Egyptian natural hazards without adjudicating the theological claim.

passages.text: And all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood. And the fish that was in the river died; and the river stank, and the Egyptians could not drink of the water of the river. And the LORD spake unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch forth thine hand with thy rod over the streams, over the rivers, and over the ponds, and cause frogs to come up upon the land of Egypt. And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt; and the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt. And the magicians did so with their enchantments, and brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt.
passages.zh: 河裏的水都變作血了。河裏的魚死了，河也腥臭了，埃及人就不能吃這河裏的水。耶和華曉諭摩西說：「你對亞倫說：『把你的杖伸在江、河、池以上，使青蛙到埃及地上來。』」亞倫便伸杖在埃及的諸水以上，青蛙就上來，遮滿了埃及地。術士也用他們的邪術照樣而行，叫青蛙上了埃及地。

passages.text: And Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod, and smote the dust of the earth, and it became lice in man, and in beast; all the dust of the land became lice throughout all the land of Egypt. And the magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not: so there were lice upon man, and upon beast. Then the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God: and Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them.
passages.zh: 亞倫便伸出手中的杖，擊打地上的塵土，塵土就在人身上和牲畜身上成了蝨子；全地的塵土都在埃及全地變作蝨子。術士也用他們的邪術照樣行，想要生出蝨子，卻是不能；於是人身上和牲畜身上都有了蝨子。術士就對法老說：「這是神的手段。」法老心裡剛硬，不肯聽從他們。

passages.text: And Moses stretched forth his rod toward heaven: and the LORD sent thunder and hail, and the fire ran along upon the ground; and the LORD rained hail upon the land of Egypt. So there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation. Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, was there no hail. And Pharaoh sent, and called for Moses and Aaron, and said unto them, I have sinned this time: the LORD is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.
passages.zh: 摩西向天伸杖，耶和華就打雷下雹，有火閃到地上；耶和華降雹在埃及地上。於是有了雹，又有火攙雜在雹中，極其厲害，自從埃及建國以來，遍地的埃及沒有見過這樣的。惟有以色列人所住的歌珊地沒有冰雹。法老打發人召了摩西、亞倫來，對他們說：「這一次我犯了罪了；耶和華是公義的，我和我的百姓是邪惡的。」

passages.text: And Moses stretched forth his rod over the land of Egypt, and the LORD brought an east wind upon the land all that day, and all that night; and when it was morning, the east wind brought the locusts. For they covered the face of the whole earth, so that the land was darkened; and they did eat every herb of the land. And the LORD said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt. And there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days: they saw not one another, neither rose any from his place for three days: but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.
passages.zh: 摩西向埃及地伸杖，耶和華就使東風颳在地上，那一日一夜；到了早晨，東風把蝗蟲颳了來。蝗蟲遮滿了地面，地都黑暗了；牠們吃盡了地上一切的菜蔬。耶和華對摩西說：「你向天伸杖，使埃及地黑暗，這黑暗似乎摸得著。」埃及遍地就烏黑了三天：三天之久，人不能相見，誰也不敢起來離開本處；惟有以色列人的住處都有光。以色列人的住處都有光。

title.en: The Passover and the Midnight Strike
title.zh: 逾越節與半夜之擊

region.en: Goshen and Egypt, night of the Exodus
region.zh: 歌珊與埃及，出埃及之夜

period: Exodus 11-12, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 11-12

summary.en: Each household takes a lamb without blemish, kills it at evening, marks lintel and doorposts with hyssop-dipped blood, and eats it in haste — loins girded, staff in hand, unleavened bread and bitter herbs. At midnight the LORD smites all the firstborn of Egypt, from Pharaoh's throne-heir to the captive in the dungeon; there is not a house without one dead, and a weeping Egypt thrusts Israel out with jewels of silver and gold. 'It is the LORD's passover' becomes the founding feast, kept forever; Christians read the unblemished lamb's blood as foreshadowing Christ, 'our passover', and the Last Supper is a Passover meal.
summary.zh: 各家取無殘疾羔羊，傍晚宰殺，以牛膝草蘸血塗門楣門框，束腰拿杖急速而食——無酵餅、苦菜。半夜，耶和華擊殺埃及一切長子，自法老長子至牢中囚徒；無一家不死一人，埃及舉國大哭，催促以色列速速離去，並以金銀相贈。「這是耶和華的逾越節」成為永遠遵守的定例。基督教視無瑕疵羔羊之血預表基督——「我們逾越節的羔羊」，而主的晚餐正是一次逾越節筵席。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition central to Judaism (Passover) and Christianity (Last Supper typology); presented as ritual-origin narrative with both readings noted.

passages.text: In the tenth day of this month they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to the house of their fathers, a lamb for an house. Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take it out from the sheep, or from the goats: and ye shall keep it up until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it in the evening. And they shall take of the blood, and strike it on the two side posts and on the upper door post of the houses, wherein they shall eat it.
passages.zh: 本月十日，你們各人要按著父家取一隻羊羔，一家一隻。你們的羊羔要無殘疾、一歲的公羊，或從綿羊裡取，或從山羊裡取，都可以。要留到本月十四日，在黃昏的時候，以色列全會眾把羊羔宰了。各家要取點血，塗在吃羊羔的房屋左右的門框上和門楣上。

passages.text: And thus shall ye eat it; with your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste: it is the LORD's passover. For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am the LORD. And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.
passages.zh: 你們吃羊羔當腰間束帶，腳上穿鞋，手中拿杖，趕緊地吃；這是耶和華的逾越節。因為那夜我要巡行埃及地，把埃及地一切頭生的，無論是人是牲畜，都擊殺了；又要敗壞埃及一切的神。我是耶和華。這血要在你們所住的房屋上作記號；我一見這血，就越過你們去。我擊殺埃及地頭生的時候，災殃必不臨到你們身上滅你們。

passages.text: And Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said unto them, Draw out and take you a lamb according to your families, and kill the passover. And ye shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the bason, and strike the lintel and the two side posts with the blood that is in the bason; and none of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning. And it came to pass, that at midnight the LORD smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.
passages.zh: 摩西召了以色列的眾長老來，對他們說：「你們要按著家口取出羊羔，把這逾越節的羊羔宰了。拿一把牛膝草，蘸盆裡的血，打在門楣上和左右的門框上；你們誰也不可出自己的房門，直到早晨。到了半夜，耶和華把埃及地所有的長子，就是從坐寶座的法老，直到被擄囚在監裡之人的長子，以及一切頭生的牲畜，盡都殺了。」

passages.text: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead. And he called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, Rise up, and get you forth from among my people, both ye and the children of Israel; and go, serve the LORD, as ye have said. Also take your flocks and your herds, as ye have said, and be gone; and bless me also. And the people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneadingtroughs being bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders.
passages.zh: 法老夜間起來，他和他的眾臣僕，以及所有埃及人，都起來了；埃及有大哀號，因為沒有一家不死一個人的。夜間，他召了摩西、亞倫來，說：「起來，連你們帶以色列人，從我民中出去，照你們所說的，去事奉耶和華。也照你們所說的，帶著你們的羊群牛群走吧；並要為我祝福。」百姓就拿著沒有酵的生麵，把摶麵盆包在衣服中，扛在肩上。

title.en: Pillar of Cloud and Fire, with the Bones of Joseph
title.zh: 雲柱火柱與約瑟的骸骨

region.en: Succoth to Etham, edge of the wilderness
region.zh: 疏割至以倘，曠野邊緣

period: Exodus 13, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 13

summary.en: Rather than the short Philistine road and its war, God leads the harnessed people the long way by the wilderness of the Red Sea; Moses carries the bones of Joseph, honoring the oath of Genesis 50. The LORD goes before them by day in a pillar of cloud and by night in a pillar of fire — the visible presence that guides, shades, and lights the march.
summary.zh: 神不領百姓走近捷的非利士道路，恐怕他們遇戰而回，卻繞道紅海曠野而行；摩西攜約瑟骸骨同去，履行創世記末章的誓言。耶和華日間在雲柱中領路，夜間在火柱中光照——那可見的同在，引導、遮蔽、照看整支行列。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The cloud-and-fire presence is a classic theophany form.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt: but God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red sea: and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt. And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.
passages.zh: 法老容百姓去的時候，非利士地的道路雖近，神卻不領他們從那裡走；因為神說：「恐怕百姓遇見打仗後悔，就回埃及去。」所以神領百姓繞道而行，走紅海曠野的路。以色列人出埃及地，都帶著兵器上去。摩西把約瑟的骸骨一同帶去；因為約瑟曾嚴嚴地叫以色列人起誓，說：「神必眷顧你們；你們要把我的骸骨從這裡一同帶上去。」

passages.text: And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night: he took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.
passages.zh: 日間，耶和華在雲柱中領他們的路；夜間，在火柱中光照他們，使他們日夜都可以行走：日間雲柱，夜間火柱，總不離開百姓的面前。

title.en: The Crossing of the Red Sea
title.zh: 過紅海

region.en: Shore of the Red Sea, Egypt (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 紅海之濱，埃及（象徵性定位）

period: Exodus 14, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 14

summary.en: Trapped between Pharaoh's six hundred chariots and the sea, Israel cries out — 'were there no graves in Egypt?' — and Moses answers the great line: 'Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD.' The angel and pillar of cloud move behind to darken the Egyptians; a strong east wind drives the sea back all night, and Israel crosses on dry ground with the waters a wall on either hand. The morning watch finds the chariot wheels dragging; the sea returns and covers the host — 'there remained not so much as one of them.'
summary.zh: 法老六百輛戰車迫近，以色列被夾於海與軍之間，哀呼「難道在埃及沒有墳地嗎？」摩西答以千古名句：「不要懼怕，只管站住，看耶和華今天向你們所要施行的救恩。」天使與雲柱移至其後；東風整夜吹海，海水分開，以色列行於乾地，水在他們左右作了牆垣。晨更時埃及車輪脫落，海水復合，全軍覆沒——「連一個也沒有剩下」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Presented as the central deliverance narrative of the Exodus cycle.

passages.text: And when Pharaoh drew nigh, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and, behold, the Egyptians marched after them; and they were sore afraid: and the children of Israel cried out unto the LORD. And they said unto Moses, Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever. The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.
passages.zh: 法老臨近的時候，以色列人舉目看見埃及人趕來，就甚懼怕，向耶和華哀求。他們對摩西說：「難道因為埃及地沒有墳墓，你把我們帶來死在曠野嗎？」摩西對百姓說：「不要懼怕，只管站住，看耶和華今天向你們所要施行的救恩：因為你們今天所看見的埃及人，必永遠不再看見了。耶和華必為你們爭戰，你們只管靜默，不要作聲。」

passages.text: And the angel of God, which went before the camp of Israel, removed and went behind them; and the pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them: and it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel; and it was a cloud and darkness to them, but it gave light by night to these: so that the one came not near the other all the night. And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.
passages.zh: 在以色列營前行走的神的使者，轉到他們後邊去；雲柱也從他們前邊轉到他們後邊立住：在埃及營和以色列營中間有雲柱；一邊是黑雲，一邊是黑夜，卻使這邊整夜光明：以致這營和那營整夜彼此不得相近。摩西向海伸杖，耶和華便用大東風，使海水一夜退去，水便分開，海就成了乾地。

passages.text: And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left. And the Egyptians pursued, and went in after them to the midst of the sea, even all Pharaoh's horses, his chariots, and his horsemen. And the LORD overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea. And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them. But the children of Israel walked upon dry land in the midst of the sea.
passages.zh: 以色列人下海中走乾地：水在他們的左右作了牆垣。埃及人追趕他們，法老一切的馬匹、車輛，和馬兵，都跟著下到海中。耶和華在海中推翻了埃及人。水就回流，淹沒了車輛和馬兵，以及那些跟著以色列人下海、法老的全軍；連一個也沒有剩下。以色列人卻在海中走乾地。

title.en: The Song of the Sea and Miriam's Timbrels
title.zh: 海之歌與米利暗的手鼓

region.en: Seashore after the crossing
region.zh: 過海後的海岸

period: Exodus 15, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 15

summary.en: Moses and Israel sing the oldest poem in scripture: 'I will sing unto the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea... Who is like unto thee, O LORD, among the gods?' Miriam the prophetess takes a timbrel and all the women follow with dances, answering the refrain — the founding victory hymn of the tradition, sung and set to music from ancient liturgy to Handel.
summary.zh: 摩西與以色列眾人歌頌聖經中最古的詩篇：「我要歌頌耶和華，因他大大戰勝，將馬和騎馬的投在海中……耶和華啊，眾神之中誰能像你？」女先知米利暗手拿鼓，眾婦女隨她擊鼓跳舞應和——這是傳統的得勝之歌，自古禮儀至韓德爾的神劇，傳唱不絕。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The victory hymn is the founding song of the tradition.

passages.text: Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the LORD, and spake, saying, I will sing unto the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea. The LORD is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God, and I will prepare him an habitation; my father's God, and I will exalt him. The LORD is a man of war: the LORD is his name. Pharaoh's chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red sea.
passages.zh: 那時，摩西和以色列人向耶和華唱這歌，說：我要向耶和華歌唱，因他大大戰勝，將馬和騎馬的投在海中。耶和華是我的力量、我的詩歌，也成了我的拯救。這是我的神，我要讚美他；是我父親的神，我要尊崇他。耶和華是戰士，他的名是耶和華。法老的車輛、軍兵，耶和華已拋在海中；他特選的軍長都沉於紅海。

passages.text: Who is like unto thee, O LORD, among the gods? who is like thee, glorious in holiness, fearful in praises, doing wonders? Thou stretchedst out thy right hand, the earth swallowed them. Thou in thy mercy hast led forth the people which thou hast redeemed: thou hast guided them in thy strength unto thy holy habitation. The LORD shall reign for ever and ever.
passages.zh: 耶和華啊，眾神之中誰能像你？誰能像你至聖至榮，可頌可畏，施行奇事？你伸出右手，地便吞滅他們。你憑慈愛領了你所贖的百姓；你憑能力引他們到了你的聖所。耶和華必作王，直到永永遠遠。

passages.text: And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances. And Miriam answered them, Sing ye to the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously; the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.
passages.zh: 亞倫的姐姐女先知米利暗，手裡拿著鼓；眾婦女也跟她出去拿鼓跳舞。米利暗應聲說：你們要歌頌耶和華，因他大大戰勝，將馬和騎馬的投在海中。

title.en: Bitter Waters Made Sweet at Marah
title.zh: 瑪拉苦水變甜

region.en: Marah and Elim, wilderness of Shur
region.zh: 瑪拉與以琳，書珥曠野

period: Exodus 15:22-27, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 15

summary.en: Three days without water end at Marah, whose springs are too bitter to drink; the people murmur 'What shall we drink?' and Moses cries to the LORD, who shows him a tree that, cast into the waters, makes them sweet. There the first wilderness statute is given — 'I am the LORD that healeth thee' — and Elim follows with its twelve wells and seventy palms, a green resting place on the edge of the desert.
summary.zh: 三日無水之後至瑪拉，水苦不能飲；百姓埋怨「我們喝甚麼呢？」摩西呼求耶和華，神指示一棵樹，丟入水中水就變甜了。在那裏頒下曠野第一條律例——「我耶和華是醫治你的」。隨後以琳有十二股水泉、七十棵棕樹，是曠野邊上的綠洲歇息處。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Wells-and-palms etiology of the wilderness stations.

passages.text: So Moses brought Israel from the Red sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water. And when they came to Marah, they could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they were bitter: therefore the name of it was called Marah. And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink? And he cried unto the LORD; and the LORD shewed him a tree, which when he had cast into the waters, the waters were made sweet: there he made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there he proved them.
passages.zh: 摩西領以色列人從紅海往前行，到了書珥的曠野，在曠野走了三天，找不著水。到了瑪拉，不能喝那裡的水，因為水苦，所以那地名叫瑪拉。百姓就向摩西發怨言，說：我們喝什麼呢？摩西呼求耶和華，耶和華指示他一棵樹。他把樹丟在水裡，水就變甜了。耶和華在那裡為他們定了律例、典章，在那裡試驗他們。

passages.text: And said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the LORD thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the LORD that healeth thee. And they came to Elim, where were twelve wells of water, and threescore and ten palm trees: and they encamped there by the waters.
passages.zh: 又說：你若留意聽耶和華你神的話，又行我眼中看為正的事，留心聽我的誡命，守我一切的律例，我就不將所加與埃及人的疾病加在你身上，因為我耶和華是醫治你的。他們到了以琳，在那裡有十二股水泉，七十棵棕樹；他們就在那裡的水邊安營。

title.en: Bread from Heaven: Manna and Quails
title.zh: 天上來的糧：嗎哪與鵪鶉

region.en: Wilderness of Sin, between Elim and Sinai
region.zh: 汛的曠野，以琳與西奈之間

period: Exodus 16, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 16

summary.en: Hunger makes the freed slaves dream of Egypt's fleshpots; the LORD rains bread from heaven, and quails cover the camp at evening. The small round thing 'as small as the hoar frost on the ground' is gathered an omer a head — he who gathered much had nothing over, and he who gathered little had no lack — breeding worms if hoarded, doubling on the sixth day, absent on the seventh: the daily bread that teaches the sabbath. An omer is laid up before the Testimony 'for your generations', and Israel eats manna forty years.
summary.zh: 饑餓使自由的奴隸懷念埃及的肉鍋；耶和華賜天糧，晚間鵪鶉飛來遮滿營地。早晨露水蒸發後，野地面上有如霜樣的小圓物——嗎哪。按飯量各取一俄梅珥——多收的沒有餘，少收的也沒有缺；留到早晨就生蟲變臭，第六日收雙份，第七日無。每天的分糧教曉安息日；一俄梅珥存於法櫃前「為後世代」，以色列吃嗎哪四十年。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The manna rule is the sabbath's first practical teaching; the omer pot is its memorial rite.

passages.text: And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness: and the children of Israel said unto them, Would to God we had died by the hand of the LORD in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots, and when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger. Then said the LORD unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.
passages.zh: 以色列全會眾在曠野向摩西、亞倫發怨言，說：巴不得我們早死在埃及地耶和華的手下；那時我們坐在肉鍋旁邊，吃得飽足。你們將我們領出來，到這曠野，是要叫這全會眾都餓死啊！耶和華對摩西說：我要將糧食從天降給你們。百姓可以出去，每天收每天的分，我好試驗他們遵不遵我的法度。

passages.text: And it came to pass, that at even the quails came up, and covered the camp: and in the morning the dew lay round about the host. And when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness there lay a small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground. And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. And Moses said unto them, This is the bread which the LORD hath given you to eat.
passages.zh: 到了晚上，有鵪鶉飛來，遮滿了營；早晨在營的四圍有露水。露水上升之後，不料，野地面上有細小圓形的東西，細小如地上的霜。以色列人看見，就彼此說：「這是嗎哪。」因為他們不知道是什麼。摩西對他們說：「這就是耶和華賜給你們吃的餅。」

passages.text: And when they did mete it with an omer, he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack. And Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning. Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank. And it came to pass, that on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for one man. And Moses said, To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the LORD: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning. Six days ye shall gather it; but on the seventh day, which is the sabbath, in it there shall be none.
passages.zh: 他們用俄梅珥量一量，多收的沒有餘，少收的也沒有缺。摩西說：「不許什麼人留到早晨。」然而他們不聽摩西的話，有人留到早晨，就生蟲變臭了。到第六天，他們收了雙倍的餅，每人兩俄梅珥。摩西說：「明天是聖安息日，是向耶和華守的。今天你們要烤的就烤了，要煮的就煮了；所剩下的都留到早晨。」六天你們可以收取，但第七天是安息日，那一天必沒有了。

passages.text: And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey. And Moses said, This is the thing which the LORD commandeth, Fill an omer of it to be kept for your generations; that they may see the bread wherewith I have fed you in the wilderness. As the LORD commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept. And the children of Israel did eat manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited.
passages.zh: 以色列家給這食物起名叫嗎哪：它像芫荽子，是白色的；滋味如同攙蜜的薄餅。摩西說：「耶和華所吩咐的是這樣：要將一俄梅珥嗎哪留到世世代代，使他們可以看見我領你們在曠野所給你們吃的餅。」耶和華怎樣吩咐摩西，亞倫就照樣將嗎哪放在法版前存留。以色列人吃嗎哪共四十年，直到他們到了有人居住之地。

title.en: Water from the Rock at Massah and Meribah
title.zh: 何烈磐石出水

region.en: Rephidim, near Horeb
region.zh: 利非訂，何烈山附近

period: Exodus 17, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 17

summary.en: Thirst drives the people to stone-throwing mutiny — 'Is the LORD among us, or not?' — and God answers by standing on the rock in Horeb for Moses to strike: water gushes for the people and cattle. The place is named Massah and Meribah, temptation and strife, the standing etiology of both a spring and the sin of testing God.
summary.zh: 乾渴令百姓幾乎用石頭打死摩西——「耶和華是在我們中間不是？」神答以：祂要站在何烈山的磐石那裏，摩西擊打磐石，水就從磐石流出，使百姓和牲畜都喝。那地方名叫瑪撒（試探）、米利巴（爭鬧）——一處水泉與一宗試探神之罪的永久起源。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Rock-spring etiology; Paul later reads the rock as a type of Christ.

passages.text: And there was no water for the people to drink. Wherefore the people did chide with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink. And the people thirsted there for water; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst? And Moses cried unto the LORD, saying, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me.
passages.zh: 百姓沒有水喝。因此百姓與摩西爭鬧，說：「給我們水喝吧。」百姓在那裡渴求水，就向摩西發怨言，說：「你為什麼將我們從埃及領出來，使我們和我們的兒女並牲畜都渴死呢？」摩西呼求耶和華說：「我向這百姓該怎樣行呢？他們幾乎要拿石頭打死我。」

passages.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Go on before the people, and take with thee of the elders of Israel; and thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river, take in thine hand, and go. Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel. And he called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the LORD, saying, Is the LORD among us, or not?
passages.zh: 耶和華對摩西說：「你走在百姓前頭，帶著以色列的幾個長老；你手裡要拿著你先前擊打河水的杖，前去。看哪，我必在何烈的磐石那裡站在你面前；你要擊打磐石，從磐石裡必有水流出來，使百姓可以喝。」摩西就在以色列的長老眼前這樣行了。他給那地方起名叫瑪撒，又叫米利巴，因以色列人爭鬧，又因他們試探耶和華，說：「耶和華是在我們中間不是？」

title.en: Amalek and the Hands Held Up
title.zh: 亞瑪力之戰與舉手之禱

region.en: Top of the hill at Rephidim
region.zh: 利非訂山頂

period: Exodus 17:8-16, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 17

summary.en: Amalek attacks Israel in the wilderness, and Moses, enthroned on a stone at the hilltop with the rod of God, raises his hands — while they are held up Israel prevails, when they drop Amalek does; Aaron and Hur steady the weary arms until sunset. Joshua wins the battle with the sword; the victory is written in a book, an altar is named Jehovahnissi — the LORD my banner — and war with Amalek is sworn 'from generation to generation.'
summary.zh: 亞瑪力人在曠野攻擊以色列。摩西手握神的杖登上山頂，坐在石頭上舉手——手舉起以色列就得勝，手下垂亞瑪力就得勝；亞倫與戶珥扶住疲憊的雙臂直到日落。約瑟夫——約書亞以刀劍得勝；戰績寫於書上，築壇名耶和華尼西——耶和華是我旌旗——並起誓必世世代代與亞瑪力人爭戰。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The eternal-war clause against Amalek has a heavy later interpretive history; presented as text, with the raised-hands intercession the episode's most-cited element.

passages.text: Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim. And Moses said unto Joshua, Choose us out men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to morrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in mine hand. And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.
passages.zh: 那時，亞瑪力人來，在利非訂與以色列人爭戰。摩西對約書亞說：「你為我們選出人來，出去與亞瑪力人爭戰：明天我手裡要拿著神的杖，站在山頂上。」摩西何時舉手，以色列人就得勝；何時垂手，亞瑪力人就得勝。

passages.text: But Moses' hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun. And Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword. And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it Jehovahnissi: for he said, Because the LORD hath sworn that the LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.
passages.zh: 但摩西的手發沉，他們就搬石頭來，放在他以下，他就坐在上面。亞倫與戶珥扶著他的手，一個在這邊，一個在那邊，他的手就穩住，直到日落的時候。約書亞用刀殺了亞瑪力王和他的百姓。摩西築了一座壇，起名叫耶和華尼西，因為他說：耶和華已經起了誓，必世世代代和亞瑪力人爭戰。

title.en: Jethro's Counsel: Judges by Thousands and Tens
title.zh: 葉忒羅獻策：設立千夫長

region.en: Camp before the mount of God
region.zh: 神山前的營地

period: Exodus 18, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 18

summary.en: Jethro arrives with Zipporah and the boys, hears the Exodus story, blesses the LORD — 'now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods' — and sacrifices with the elders. Watching Moses judge the people alone from morning to evening, the old priest of Midian delivers the classic counsel of delegation: able men who fear God as rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens; hard cases only to Moses. Moses hears him, and the judicial structure of Israel is born from a foreign father-in-law's advice.
summary.zh: 葉忒羅攜西坡拉與二子來見，聽出埃及之事，稱頌耶和華——「我如今知道耶和華比萬神都大」——並與長老同席獻祭。見摩西自朝至暮獨自審判百姓，這位米甸老祭司獻上授權分層的千古良策：選敬畏神、誠實無妄之人作千夫長、百夫長、五十夫長、十夫長；難斷之事才呈摩西。以色列司法制度自此而生，竟出於異邦岳父之口。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The first judicial hierarchy of Israel, credited to a Midianite priest.

passages.text: And Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness which the LORD had done to Israel, whom he had delivered out of the hand of the Egyptians. And Jethro said, Blessed be the LORD, who hath delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh. Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods: for in the thing wherein they dealt proudly he was above them. And Jethro, Moses' father in law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God: and Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses' father in law before God.
passages.zh: 葉忒羅因耶和華待以色列的一切好處，就是拯救他們脫離埃及人的手，便甚歡喜。葉忒羅說：耶和華是應當稱頌的；他救了你們脫離埃及人和法老的手。我現今得知，耶和華比萬神都大，因為在他們驕傲的事上，他勝過他們。摩西的岳父葉忒羅把燔祭和平安祭獻給神。亞倫和以色列的眾長老都來了，與摩西的岳父在神面前吃飯。

passages.text: And when Moses' father in law saw all that he did to the people, he said, What is this thing that thou doest to the people? why sittest thou thyself alone, and all the people stand by thee from morning unto even? And Moses' father in law said unto him, The thing that thou doest is not good. Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.
passages.zh: 摩西的岳父看見他向百姓所做的一切事，就說：你向百姓做的是什麼事呢？你為什麼獨自坐著，眾百姓從早到晚都站在你的左右呢？摩西的岳父對他說：你這做的不好。你和這些百姓必都疲憊；因為這事太重，你獨自一人辦理不了。

passages.text: Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens: and let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear the burden with thee. So Moses hearkened to the voice of his father in law, and did all that he had said.
passages.zh: 並要從百姓中揀選有才能的人，就是敬畏神、誠實無妄、恨不義之財的人，派他們作千夫長、百夫長、五十夫長、十夫長，管理百姓，叫他們隨時審判百姓，大事都要呈到你這裡，小事他們自己可以審判。這樣，你就輕省些，他們也可以同當此任。於是，摩西聽從他岳父的話，按著他所說的去行。

title.en: Thunder and Law at Mount Sinai
title.zh: 西奈雷霆與律法

region.en: Mount Sinai
region.zh: 西奈山

period: Exodus 19-20, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 19-20

summary.en: On the third day, with the people washed and fenced off from the mount under pain of death, thunder and lightning, a thick cloud, a trumpet exceeding loud, and a trembling mountain: 'the LORD descended upon it in fire, and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace.' From the mount God speaks the Ten Commandments — no other gods, no graven image, no vain name, the sabbath, honour of parents, the four 'thou shalt nots' of killing, adultery, theft, false witness, and no coveting — until the terrified people beg Moses: 'Speak thou with us... but let not God speak with us, lest we die.'
summary.zh: 第三日，雷轟閃電、密雲遍山、角聲甚大，全營盡皆發顫；「耶和華在火中降於山上，山的煙氣上騰，如燒窯一般」。神從山上宣講十誡——除我以外不可有別神、不可拜偶像、不可妄稱神名、守安息日、當孝敬父母、不可殺人、姦淫、偷盜、作假見證、不可貪婪——百姓戰兢求摩西：「求你和我們說話……不要神和我們說話，恐怕我們死亡。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition central to Judaism and Christianity. The Decalogue is quoted as public-domain scripture in comparative framing.

passages.text: And it came to pass on the third day in the morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of the trumpet exceeding loud; so that all the people that was in the camp trembled. And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the LORD descended upon it in fire: and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mount quaked greatly. And when the voice of the trumpet sounded long, and waxed louder and louder, Moses spake, and God answered him by a voice.
passages.zh: 到了第三天早晨，在山上有雷轟、閃電，和密雲，並且角聲甚大，營中的百姓盡都發顫。西奈全山冒煙，因為耶和華在火中降於山上。山的煙氣上騰，如燒窯一般，遍山大大地震動。角聲漸漸地高而又高，摩西就說話，神有聲音答應他。

passages.text: And God spake all these words, saying, I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt have no other gods before me. Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth. Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain. Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
passages.zh: 神吩咐這一切的話說：我是耶和華你的神，曾將你從埃及地為奴之家領出來。除了我以外，你不可有別的神。不可為自己雕刻偶像，也不可做什麼形像彷彿上天、下地，和地底下、水中的百物。不可妄稱耶和華你神的名。當記念安息日，守為聖日。

passages.text: Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee. Thou shalt not kill. Thou shalt not commit adultery. Thou shalt not steal. Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour. Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour's.
passages.zh: 當孝敬父母，使你的日子在耶和華你神所賜你的地上得以長久。不可殺人。不可姦淫。不可偷盜。不可作假見證陷害人。不可貪戀人的房屋；也不可貪戀人的妻子、僕婢、牛驢，並他一切所有的。

passages.text: And all the people saw the thunderings, and the lightnings, and the noise of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking: and when the people saw it, they removed, and stood afar off. And they said unto Moses, Speak thou with us, and we will hear: but let not God speak with us, lest we die. And Moses said unto the people, Fear not: for God is come to prove you, and that his fear may be before your faces, that ye sin not. And the people stood afar off, and Moses drew near unto the thick darkness where God was.
passages.zh: 眾百姓見雷轟、閃電、角聲、山上冒煙，就都發顫，遠遠地站立，對摩西說：「求你和我們說話，我們必聽；不要神和我們說話，恐怕我們死亡。」摩西對百姓說：「不要懼怕；因為神降臨是要試驗你們，叫你們時常敬畏他，不致犯罪。」於是百姓遠遠地站立；摩西就挨近神所在的幽暗之中。

title.en: The Golden Calf and the Broken Tables
title.zh: 金牛犢與摔碎的法版

region.en: Camp below Mount Sinai
region.zh: 西奈山下的營地

period: Exodus 32, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 32

summary.en: With Moses forty days on the mount, the people demand of Aaron 'Up, make us gods which shall go before us'; the golden earrings of the women go into the fire and out comes a molten calf — 'These be thy gods, O Israel' — with a feast, eating, drinking, and playing. God offers to consume them and make a nation of Moses, who pleads for his people by the oath sworn to Abraham and turns the LORD from his wrath. Coming down with the tables written by the finger of God, he sees the calf, shatters the tables at the mount's foot, burns and powders the idol into the drinking water, and the sons of Levi — 'Who is on the LORD's side?' — put three thousand men to the sword; Moses offers to be blotted out of God's book for his people.
summary.zh: 摩西四十日未下山，百姓聚集對亞倫說：「起來，為我們作神像在我們前面引路。」眾人的金耳環入火，出來一隻金牛犢——「以色列啊，這是領你出埃及地的神」——築壇獻祭，坐下吃喝，起來玩耍。神欲滅絕之而另立摩西為大國；摩西以向亞伯拉罕所起的誓代求，神回心轉意。摩西攜神手所寫之石版下山，見犢像怒碎其版於山下，將金牛焚燒磨成粉末撒在水面上叫以色列人喝。利未子孫聞「凡屬耶和華的，都要到我這裏來」，當日殺約三千人。摩西甚至求從神冊上塗抹己名以贖民罪。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The idol-making episode is the paradigmatic transgression narrative; the internal violence is part of the text, presented without endorsement.

passages.text: And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him, Up, make us gods, which shall go before us. And Aaron said unto them, Break off the golden earrings, which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters, and bring them unto me. And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. And they rose up early on the morrow, and offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.
passages.zh: 百姓見摩西遲延不下山，就大家聚集到亞倫那裏，對他說：「起來！為我們做神像，可以在我們前面引路。」亞倫對他們說：「你們去摘下你們妻子、兒女耳上的金環，拿來給我。」百姓就都摘下他們耳上的金環，拿來給亞倫。亞倫從他們手裏接過來，鑄了一隻牛犢，用雕刻的器具做成。他們就說：「以色列啊，這是領你出埃及地的神。」次日清早，百姓起來獻燔祭和平安祭，就坐下吃喝，起來玩耍。

passages.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation. And Moses besought the LORD his God, and said, LORD, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand? Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, thy servants, to whom thou swarest by thine own self. And the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people.
passages.zh: 耶和華吩咐摩西說：「下去吧，因為你的百姓，就是你從埃及地領出來的，已經敗壞了。現在你不要攔阻我，我要向他們發烈怒，將他們滅絕，使你的後裔成為大國。」摩西便懇求耶和華他的神說：「耶和華啊，你為甚麼向你的百姓發烈怒呢？這百姓是你用大力和大能的手從埃及地領出來的。求你記念你的僕人亞伯拉罕、以撒、以色列。你曾指著自己起誓說：『我必使你們的後裔像天上的星那樣多，並且我所應許的這全地，必給你們的後裔，他們要永遠承受為業。』」於是耶和華後悔，不把所說的禍降與他的百姓。

passages.text: And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount. And he took the calf which they had made, and burnt it in the fire, and ground it to powder, and strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it. And Moses said, Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him. And there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.
passages.zh: 摩西挨近營前就看見牛犢，又看見人跳舞，便發烈怒，把兩塊版扔在山下摔碎了，又將他們所鑄的牛犢用火焚燒，磨得粉碎，撒在水面上，叫以色列人喝。摩西說：「凡屬耶和華的，都要到我這裏來！」於是利未的子孫都到他那裏聚集。那天百姓中被殺的約有三千。

passages.text: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin: and now I will go up unto the LORD; peradventure I shall make an atonement for your sin. And Moses returned unto the LORD, and said, Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made them gods of gold. Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin--; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written. And the LORD said unto Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.
passages.zh: 到了第二天，摩西對百姓說：「你們犯了大罪。我如今要上耶和華那裏去，或者可以為你們贖罪。」摩西回到耶和華那裏，說：「唉！這百姓犯了大罪，為自己做了金像。倘或你肯赦免他們的罪……不然，求你從你所寫的冊上塗抹我的名。」耶和華對摩西說：「誰得罪我，我就從我的冊上塗抹誰的名。」

title.en: Show Me Thy Glory: Moses in the Cleft of the Rock
title.zh: 求你顯出你的榮耀：磐石穴中的摩西

region.en: Tent of meeting and cleft rock, Sinai
region.zh: 西奈會幕與磐石穴

period: Exodus 33-34, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 33-34

summary.en: After the calf, God threatens to send an angel instead of himself; Moses pitches the tent of meeting outside the camp, where the LORD speaks with him 'face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend.' Bold from grace, Moses asks, 'I beseech thee, shew me thy glory'; he is hidden in a cleft of the rock, covered by the divine hand, and allowed to see only the back parts — 'for there shall no man see me, and live.' Renewing the tables, the LORD proclaims his name: 'The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering...' and when Moses descends, the skin of his face shines so that the people are afraid, and he wears a veil.
summary.zh: 金牛犢事件後，神揚言遣使者代行；摩西在營外支搭會幕，耶和華在那裏與他面對面說話，如人與朋友說話。摩西膽敢求告：「求你顯出你的榮耀。」神將他藏在磐石穴中，用手遮蔽，只許他看見神的背——「因為人見我的面不能存活」。重鑿法版之際，耶和華宣告己名：「耶和華，耶和華，是有憐憫有恩典的神，不輕易發怒……」摩西下山時，面皮因與神說話而發光，百姓懼怕，他便用帕子蒙臉。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The veiled shining face is among the most-cited theophany texts in Christian interpretation (2 Corinthians 3).

passages.text: And it came to pass, as Moses entered into the tabernacle, the cloudy pillar descended, and stood at the door of the tabernacle, and the Lord talked with Moses. And all the people saw the cloudy pillar stand at the tabernacle door: and all the people rose up and worshipped, every man in his tent door. And the LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend.
passages.zh: 摩西進入會幕的時候，雲柱降下來，立在會幕的門口，耶和華便與摩西說話。眾百姓看見雲柱立在會幕門口，就都起來，各人在自己帳棚的門口下拜。耶和華與摩西面對面說話，好像人與朋友說話一般。

passages.text: And he said, I beseech thee, shew me thy glory. And he said, I will make all my goodness pass before thee, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before thee. And he said, Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live. And the LORD said, Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon a rock: and it shall come to pass, while my glory passeth by, that I will put thee in a clift of the rock, and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by: and I will take away mine hand, and thou shalt see my back parts: but my face shall not be seen.
passages.zh: 摩西說：求你顯出你的榮耀給我看。耶和華說：我要顯我一切的恩慈，在你面前經過，宣告我的名。又說：你不能看見我的面，因為人見我的面不能存活。耶和華說：看哪，在我這裡有地方，你要站在磐石上。我的榮耀經過的時候，我必將你放在磐石穴中，用我的手遮掩你，等我過去；然後我要將我的手收回，你就得見我的背，卻不得見我的面。

passages.text: And the LORD descended in the cloud, and stood with him there, and proclaimed the name of the LORD. And the LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth, keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty. And Moses made haste, and bowed his head toward the earth, and worshipped.
passages.zh: 耶和華在雲中降臨，和摩西一同站在那裡，宣告耶和華的名。耶和華在他面前宣告說：耶和華，耶和華，是有憐憫有恩典的神，不輕易發怒，並有豐盛的慈愛和誠實，為千萬人存留慈愛，赦免罪孽、過犯，和罪惡，萬不以有罪的為無罪。摩西急忙伏地下拜。

passages.text: And he was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights; he did neither eat bread, nor drink water. And he wrote upon the tables the words of the covenant, the ten commandments. And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in Moses' hand, when he came down from the mount, that Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him. And when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come nigh him.
passages.zh: 摩西在耶和華那裡四十晝夜，也不吃飯也不喝水。耶和華將這約的話，就是十條誡，寫在兩塊版上。摩西手裡拿著兩塊法版下西乃山的時候，不知道自己的面皮因耶和華和他說話就發了光。亞倫和以色列眾人看見摩西的面皮發光，就怕挨近他。

title.en: Grasshoppers Before Giants: The Evil Report
title.zh: 巨人身如蚱蜢：惡信事件

region.en: Hebron to Kadesh, brook of Eshcol
region.zh: 希伯崙至加低斯，以實各谷

period: Numbers 13-14, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 4: Numbers, chapters 13-14

summary.en: Twelve spies return from Canaan bearing a single grape-cluster between two on a staff — 'surely it floweth with milk and honey' — but ten of them report walled cities and giants, 'and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.' The congregation weeps, plots a return to Egypt, and stones Caleb and Joshua for their defiance; for this cowardice the whole generation is sentenced to die in the wilderness, one year for each day of scouting — forty years — and an unauthorized assault the next morning is routed at Hormah.
summary.zh: 十二探子自迦南歸來，抬著兩人扛的一掛葡萄——「果然是流奶與蜜之地」——但其中十人報告堅城巨人，「我們在自己眼中如蚱蜢，在他們眼中亦然」。全會眾哀哭，欲回埃及，並用石頭打死持相反意見的迦勒與約書亞；探地四十日，一年抵一日，整整一代人被判死於曠野；翌晨擅自行動者敗於何珥瑪。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The giant tag follows the Anakim report; presented as the covenant-generation's failure narrative.

passages.text: And they came unto the brook of Eshcol, and cut down from thence a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they bare it between two upon a staff; and they brought of the pomegranates, and of the figs. And they returned from searching of the land after forty days. And they told him, and said, We came unto the land whither thou sentest us, and surely it floweth with milk and honey; and this is the fruit of it. Nevertheless the people be strong that dwell in the land, and the cities are walled, and very great: and moreover we saw the children of Anak there.
passages.zh: 他們到了以實各谷，從那裡砍了葡萄樹的一枝，上頭有一掛葡萄，兩個人用槓抬著，又帶了些石榴和無花果來。過了四十天，他們窺探那地才回來。他們回報說：我們到了你所打發我們去的那地，果然是流奶與蜜之地；這就是那地的果子。然而住那地的民強壯，城邑也堅固寬大，並且我們在那裡看見了亞衲族的人。

passages.text: And Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it. But the men that went up with him said, We be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we. And they brought up an evil report of the land which they had searched, saying, The land, through which we have gone to search it, is a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof; and all the people that we saw in it are men of a great stature. And there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.
passages.zh: 迦勒在摩西面前安撫百姓，說：我們立刻上去得那地吧！我們足能得勝。但那些和他同去的人說：我們不能上去攻擊那民，因為他們比我們強壯。探子中有人論到所窺探之地，向以色列人報惡信，說：我們所窺探、經過之地是吞吃居民之地，我們在那裡所看見的人民都身量高大。我們在那裡看見亞衲族人，就是偉人；他們是偉人的後裔。據我們看，自己就如蚱蜢一樣；據他們看，我們也是如此。

passages.text: And all the congregation lifted up their voice, and cried; and the people wept that night. And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron: and the whole congregation said unto them, Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt! or would God we had died in this wilderness! And they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt. But all the congregation bade stone them with stones.
passages.zh: 全會眾都放聲呼喊，百姓那一夜就哭了。以色列眾人向摩西、亞倫發怨言，全會眾對他們說：「巴不得我們早死在埃及地，或是死在這曠野！他們彼此說：我們不如立一個首領，回埃及去吧。但全會眾吩咐要用石頭打死他們二人。

passages.text: And the LORD said, I have pardoned according to thy word: but as truly as I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the LORD. Because all those men which have seen my glory, and have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice; surely they shall not see the land which I sware unto their fathers. Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and your children shall wander in the wilderness forty years, until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness. After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years.
passages.zh: 耶和華說：「我照著你的話赦免了他們。然而我指著我的永生起誓，遍地要被我的榮耀充滿。因為那些見過我榮耀、又在這曠野試探我這十次、不聽我話的人，他們斷不得看見我向他們祖宗所起誓應許之地。你們的屍首必倒在這曠野；你們的兒女必在曠野飄流四十年，直到你們的屍首在曠野消滅。按你們窺探那地的日數，共四十日，一日頂一年，你們要擔當罪孽四十年。

title.en: Korah's Rebellion and the Opening Earth
title.zh: 可拉叛變與裂開的地

region.en: Camp in the wilderness of Paran
region.zh: 巴蘭曠野營地

period: Numbers 16, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 4: Numbers, chapter 16

summary.en: Korah, a Levite, and 250 princes of renown confront Moses and Aaron — 'Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy.' Moses proposes the censer test before the LORD; when the glory appears, the earth opens her mouth and swallows Korah, Dathan, and Abiram with their households, fire consumes the 250 incense-bearers, and 14,700 die by plague before Aaron runs between the living and the dead with his censer — the archetype of rebellion against a sacred order.
summary.zh: 利未人可拉與二百五十個有名望的首領反抗摩西亞倫——「你們擅自專權，全會眾既是聖潔的」。摩西提出以香爐試驗；耶和華的榮光顯現後，地開口吞滅可拉、大坍、亞比蘭和他們的家眷，火燒滅二百五十個拿香爐的人，其後瘟疫又死一萬四千七百人，直到亞倫拿香爐站於活人死人中間止——這是反抗神聖秩序的原型故事。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as the paradigmatic rebellion-against-order narrative; the mass death is textual, not endorsed.

passages.text: Now Korah, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, took men: and they rose up before Moses, with certain of the children of Israel, two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown: and they gathered themselves together against Moses and against Aaron, and said unto them, Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and the LORD is among them: wherefore then lift ye up yourselves above the congregation of the LORD?
passages.zh: 利未的曾孫、哥轄的孫子、以斯哈的兒子可拉，和流便子孫中以利押的兒子大坍、亞比蘭，帶著人來，在摩西面前起來，同以色列會眾中的二百五十個首領，就是會中有名望、被選入會中的人，一同聚集攻擊摩西、亞倫，說：「你們擅自專權了！全會眾個個既是聖潔，耶和華也在他們中間，你們為什麼自高，超過耶和華的會眾呢？」

passages.text: This do; Take you censers, Korah, and all his company; and put fire therein, and put incense in them before the LORD to morrow: and it shall be that the man whom the LORD doth choose, he shall be holy. And Korah gathered all the congregation against them unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: and the glory of the LORD appeared unto all the congregation. And the LORD spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying, Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment.
passages.zh: 你們這樣行：可拉和他一黨的人要拿香爐來，明日把火盛在其中，把香放在上面，在耶和華面前獻上；耶和華揀選誰，誰就為聖潔。可拉招聚全會眾到會幕門口，要攻擊他們二人；耶和華的榮光就向全會眾顯現。耶和華對摩西、亞倫說：「你們離開這會眾，我好在轉眼之間把他們滅絕。」

passages.text: And it came to pass, as he had made an end of speaking all these words, that the ground clave asunder that was under them: and the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods. They, and all that appertained to them, went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed upon them: and they perished from among the congregation. And there came out a fire from the LORD, and consumed the two hundred and fifty men that offered incense.
passages.zh: 摩西剛說完了這一切話，他們腳下的地就裂開，地開了口，把他們和他們的家眷，並一切屬可拉的人丁、財物，都吞了下去。他們和一切屬他們的，都活活地墜落陰間，地口在他們上頭照舊合閉，他們就從會中滅亡。又有火從耶和華那裡出來，燒滅了那獻香的二百五十個人。

title.en: Moses Strikes the Rock and Is Barred from the Land
title.zh: 摩西擊磐石而被拒於應許地之外

region.en: Water of Meribah-Kadesh, desert of Zin
region.zh: 米利巴水，尋的曠野

period: Numbers 20, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 4: Numbers, chapter 20

summary.en: Forty years of murmuring later, at Kadesh the waterless congregation falls on Moses and Aaron again. God commands Moses to speak to the rock; instead, in fury — 'Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?' — he strikes it twice. Water gushes, but the LORD's sentence falls on the leaders: 'Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel... ye shall not bring this congregation into the land.' Moses' one great failure, the reason he never sets foot in Canaan.
summary.zh: 四十年怨懟之後，加低斯缺水，會眾再度攻擊摩西亞倫。神吩咐摩西「吩咐磐石出水」；他卻怒斥「你們這些背叛的人聽著，我們為你們使水從這磐石中流出來麼？」並擊打磐石兩下。水雖湧出，判詞卻落在領袖身上：「因為你們不信我，不在以色列人眼前尊我為聖……必不得領這會眾進我所賜給他們的地。」摩西一生的最大失誤，令他終身未入迦南。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The water-striking is the tradition's classic case of a holy act done wrongly.

passages.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying, Take the rod, and gather thou the assembly together, thou, and Aaron thy brother, and speak ye unto the rock before their eyes; and it shall give forth his water, and thou shalt bring forth to them water out of the rock: so thou shalt give the congregation and their beasts drink. And Moses and Aaron gathered the congregation together before the rock, and he said unto them, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?
