And Moses lifted up his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twice: and the water came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their beasts also.
passages.zh: 耶和華曉諭摩西說：「你拿著杖，和你哥哥亞倫一同招聚會眾，在他們眼前吩咐磐石發出水來；這樣，你就為他們使水從磐石流出，給會眾和他們的牲畜喝。」摩西、亞倫就招聚會眾到磐石前，摩西對他們說：「你們這些背叛的人聽我說：我們為你們使水從這磐石中流出來嗎？」摩西舉手，用杖擊打磐石兩下，就有許多水流出來，會眾和他們的牲畜都喝了。

passages.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses and Aaron, Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them. This is the water of Meribah; because the children of Israel strove with the LORD, and he was sanctified in them.
passages.zh: 耶和華對摩西、亞倫說：「因為你們不信我，不在以色列人眼前尊我為聖，所以你們必不得領這會眾進我所賜給他們的地去。」這水名叫米利巴水，是因以色列人向耶和華爭鬧，耶和華就在他們中間顯為聖。

title.en: Aaron Dies on Mount Hor
title.zh: 亞倫死於何珥山

region.en: Mount Hor, land of Edom
region.zh: 何珥山，以東地

period: Numbers 20:22-29, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 4: Numbers, chapter 20

summary.en: Denied passage by Edom — 'thou shalt not pass by me, lest I come out against thee with the sword' — Israel turns south, and the sentence on Aaron is carried out: before the whole congregation Moses, Aaron, and Eleazar climb Mount Hor, where Aaron is stripped of his priestly garments, which are put on his son, and the first high priest dies on the summit. All Israel mourns thirty days — the succession rite of the priesthood in a single, stark scene.
summary.zh: 以東王拒絕借道——「你不可從我這裏經過，恐怕我帶刀出去攻擊你」——以色列繞道南行。神對亞倫的判詞在此執行：摩西、亞倫、以利亞撒在全會眾眼前登上何珥山；亞倫的祭司聖衣被脫下，穿在其子以利亞撒身上，首任大祭司死於山頂。全以色列為他哀哭三十日——一幕簡峻的祭司職傳承之禮。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The garment-stripping is the succession rite element.

passages.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses and Aaron in mount Hor, by the coast of the land of Edom, saying, Aaron shall be gathered unto his people: for he shall not enter into the land which I have given unto the children of Israel, because ye rebelled against my word at the water of Meribah. Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up unto mount Hor: and strip Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son: and Aaron shall be gathered unto his people, and shall die there.
passages.zh: 耶和華在靠近以東地的何珥山對摩西、亞倫說：「亞倫要歸到他列祖那裡。他必不得進入我所賜給以色列人的地，因為你們在米利巴水違背了我的命令。你要帶亞倫和他的兒子以利亞撒上何珥山，把亞倫的聖衣脫下，給他的兒子以利亞撒穿上。亞倫必歸到他列祖那裡，死在那裡。」

passages.text: And Moses did as the LORD commanded: and they went up into mount Hor in the sight of all the congregation. And Moses stripped Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son; and Aaron died there in the top of the mount: and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mount. And when all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, they mourned for Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.
passages.zh: 摩西就照耶和華所吩咐的行。三人當著全會眾的眼前上了何珥山。摩西把亞倫的聖衣脫下，給他的兒子以利亞撒穿上，亞倫就死在山頂那裡。於是摩西和以利亞撒下了山。全會眾，就是以色列全家，見亞倫已經死了，便為亞倫哀哭了三十天。

title.en: The Brazen Serpent: Look and Live
title.zh: 銅蛇：仰望得生

region.en: Wilderness march between Mount Hor and Moab
region.zh: 何珥山至摩押之間的曠野行軍路

period: Numbers 21:4-9, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 4: Numbers, chapter 21

summary.en: Weary of manna — 'our soul loatheth this light bread' — the people curse God and Moses, and fiery serpents sweep the camp until many die. At their confession Moses prays, and God's cure is an image: a serpent of brass set on a pole, 'and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.' Jesus fixes on this image for his own death — 'as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up.'
summary.zh: 百姓厭惡嗎哪——「我們的心厭惡這淡薄的食物」——出言攻擊神與摩西，火蛇進入營中，咬死許多人。認罪之後摩西代求；神的醫治竟是一個像：銅蛇掛在杆上，「被咬的一望這銅蛇就活了」。耶穌以此喻己之受難——「摩西在曠野怎樣舉蛇，人子也必照樣被舉起來」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The lifted serpent is a contested image (later destroyed by Hezekiah as Nehushtan); both the biblical and Johannine readings are noted.

passages.text: And they journeyed from mount Hor by the way of the Red sea, to compass the land of Edom: and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way. And the people spake against God, and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread. And the LORD sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.
passages.zh: 他們從何珥山起行，往紅海那條路走，要繞過以東地。百姓因這路難行，心中甚是煩躁，就怨讟神和摩西說：「你們為什麼把我們從埃及領出來，使我們死在曠野呢？這裡沒有糧，沒有水，我們的心厭惡這淡薄的食物。」於是耶和華使火蛇進入百姓中間，蛇就咬他們。以色列人中死了許多。

passages.text: Therefore the people came to Moses, and said, We have sinned, for we have spoken against the LORD, and against thee; pray unto the LORD, that he take away the serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people. And the LORD said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live. And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.
passages.zh: 百姓到摩西那裡，說：「我們怨讟耶和華和你，有罪了。求你禱告耶和華，叫這些蛇離開我們。」於是摩西為百姓禱告。耶和華對摩西說：「你製造一條火蛇，掛在杆子上；凡被咬的，一望這蛇，就必得活。」摩西便製造一條銅蛇，掛在杆子上；凡被蛇咬的，一望這銅蛇就活了。

title.en: The Talking Ass of Balaam
title.zh: 巴蘭的驢開口說話

region.en: Road from Pethor to Moab
region.zh: 自毗奪往摩押的路上

period: Numbers 22, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 4: Numbers, chapter 22

summary.en: Balak king of Moab, terrified of Israel, sends rewards of divination to the famous Mesopotamian seer Balaam: 'he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed.' God first refuses the journey, then lets Balaam ride — and the angel of the LORD stands drawn-sword in the road three times, seen by Balaam's ass but not by the seer himself; crushed foot, beatings, and at last the LORD opens the ass's mouth: 'What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?' Only then Balaam's eyes are opened.
summary.zh: 摩押王巴拉克懼以色列，帶卦金禮聘美索不達米亞名先知巴蘭：「你為誰祝福，誰就得福；你咒詛誰，誰就受咒詛。」神先拒絕他前行，後許他騎驢而去；耶和華的使者三次持刀立於路上——驢看見了，先知卻看不見。驢被擊打，最後神叫驢開口：「我向你行了甚麼，你竟打我這三次？」巴蘭的眼目這才明亮。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The speaking animal is tagged transformation as the nearest motif; noted as an interpretive choice.

passages.text: He sent messengers therefore unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor, which is by the river of the land of the children of his people, to call him, saying, Behold, there is a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me: come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me: for I wot that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed. And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed with the rewards of divination in their hand.
passages.zh: 他就差遣使者往大河邊的毗奪去，到比珥的兒子巴蘭本鄉那裡，召他來，說：「有一宗民從埃及出來，遮滿地面，與我對居。這民比我強盛，現在求你來為我咒詛他們，或者我能得勝，攻打他們，趕出此地。因為我知道，你為誰祝福，誰就得福；你咒詛誰，誰就受咒詛。」摩押的長老和米甸的長老手裡拿著卦金，到了巴蘭那裡。

passages.text: And God's anger was kindled because he went: and the angel of the LORD stood in the way for an adversary against him. Now he was riding upon his ass, and his two servants were with him. And the ass saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way, and his sword drawn in his hand: and the ass turned aside out of the way. And when the ass saw the angel of the LORD, she thrust herself unto the wall, and crushed Balaam's foot against the wall: and he smote her again. And when the ass saw the angel of the LORD, she fell down under Balaam: and Balaam's anger was kindled, and he smote the ass with a staff.
passages.zh: 神因他去就發了怒；耶和華的使者站在路上敵擋他。他騎著驢，有兩個僕人跟隨他。驢看見耶和華的使者站在路上，手裡有拔出來的刀，就從路上跨進田間。驢看見耶和華的使者，就貼靠牆，將巴蘭的腳擠傷了；巴蘭又打驢。驢看見耶和華的使者，就臥在巴蘭底下；巴蘭發怒，用杖打驢。

passages.text: And the LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and she said unto Balaam, What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times? And Balaam said unto the ass, Because thou hast mocked me: I would there were a sword in mine hand, for now would I kill thee. And the ass said unto Balaam, Am not I thine ass, upon which thou hast ridden ever since I was thine unto this day? was I ever wont to do so unto thee? And he said, Nay. Then the LORD opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way, and his sword drawn in his hand: and he bowed down his head, and fell flat on his face.
passages.zh: 耶和華叫驢開口，對巴蘭說：我向你行了什麼，你竟打我這三次呢？巴蘭對驢說：因為你戲弄我，我恨不能手中有刀，把你殺了。驢對巴蘭說：我不是你從小時直到今日所騎的驢嗎？我素常向你這樣行過嗎？巴蘭說：沒有。當時，耶和華使巴蘭的眼目明亮，他就看見耶和華的使者站在路上，手裡有拔出來的刀，巴蘭便低頭俯伏在地。

title.en: Balaam's Oracles: How Shall I Curse Whom God Hath Not Cursed?
title.zh: 巴蘭的詩歌：我怎能咒詛神未咒詛的？

region.en: High places of Baal, top of Pisgah, Moab
region.zh: 巴力的邱壇，毗斯迦山頂，摩押

period: Numbers 23-24, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 4: Numbers, chapters 23-24

summary.en: On seven altars with seven bullocks and seven rams, hired to curse, Balaam can only bless: 'How shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed?... Behold, I have received commandment to bless: and he hath blessed; and I cannot reverse it.' Balak rages through three sites; the third oracle sees the spirit of God upon the seer, who falls into a trance and sings 'How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob' and the great messianic line — 'there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel' — read by Christian tradition of Christ, and echoed by the Magi's star.
summary.zh: 巴蘭在七座壇上以七牛七羊獻祭，受聘咒詛卻只能祝福：「我怎能咒詛神所未咒詛的呢？……我受命祝福，神也曾賜福，我不能推翻。」巴拉克三次更換觀景之處而三度受挫。第三次時神的靈臨到先知，他入異象而歌：「雅各啊，你的帳棚何等華美」，更唱出彌賽亞名句——「有星要出於雅各，有杖要興於以色列」——基督教傳統讀之為基督，東方博士之星亦呼應此言。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The star-oracle is one of the most-used messianic proof-texts; the Christian reading is noted.

passages.text: And Balaam said unto Balak, Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven oxen and seven rams. And Balak did as Balaam had spoken. And the LORD put a word in Balaam's mouth, and said, Return unto Balak, and thus thou shalt speak. And he took up his parable, and said, Balak the king of Moab hath brought me from Aram, out of the mountains of the east, saying, Come, curse me Jacob, and come, defy Israel. How shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed? or how shall I defy, whom the LORD hath not defied? for from the top of the rocks I see him, and from the hills I behold him: lo, the people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations.
passages.zh: 巴蘭對巴勒說：你在這裡給我築七座壇，為我預備七隻公牛，七隻公羊。巴勒照巴蘭的話行了。耶和華將話傳給巴蘭，又說：你回到巴勒那裡，要如此如此說。巴蘭便題起詩歌說：巴勒引我出亞蘭，摩押王引我出東山，說：來啊，為我咒詛雅各；來啊，怒罵以色列。神沒有咒詛的，我焉能咒詛？耶和華沒有怒罵的，我焉能怒罵？我從高峰看他，從小山望他；這是獨居的民，不列在萬民中。

passages.text: And Balak said unto Balaam, What hast thou done unto me? I took thee to curse mine enemies, and, behold, thou hast blessed them altogether. And he answered and said, Must I not take heed to speak that which the LORD hath put in my mouth? And Balak said unto him, Come, I pray thee, with me unto another place, from whence thou mayest see them: thou shalt see but the utmost part of them, and shalt not see them all: and curse me them from thence.
passages.zh: 巴勒對巴蘭說：你向我做的是什麼事呢？我領你來咒詛我的仇敵，不料，你竟為他們祝福。他回答說：耶和華傳給我的話，我能不謹慎傳說嗎？巴勒對他說：來吧，我領你往別處去，在那裡可以看見他們；你不能全看見，只能看見他們邊界上的人，在那裡為我咒詛他們。

passages.text: And he took up his parable, and said, Rise up, Balak, and hear; hearken unto me, thou son of Zippor: God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good? Behold, I have received commandment to bless: and he hath blessed; and I cannot reverse it. He hath not beheld iniquity in Jacob, neither hath he seen perverseness in Israel: the LORD his God is with him, and the shout of a king is among them.
passages.zh: 巴蘭便題起詩歌說：巴勒，你起來聽；西撥的兒子，你聽我言。神非人，必不致說謊，也非人子，必不致後悔。他說話豈不照著行呢？他發言豈不要成就呢？我奉命祝福；神也曾賜福，此事我不能翻轉。他未見雅各中有罪孽，也未見以色列中有奸惡。耶和華他的神和他同在；有歡呼王的聲音在他們中間。

passages.text: And Balaam lifted up his eyes, and he saw Israel abiding in his tents according to their tribes; and the spirit of God came upon him. And he took up his parable, and said, the man whose eyes are open hath said: He hath said, which heard the words of God, which saw the vision of the Almighty, falling into a trance, but having his eyes open: How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel! I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel. Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee.
passages.zh: 巴蘭舉目，看見以色列人照著支派居住。神的靈就臨到他身上，便題起詩歌說：眼目閉住的人說，得聽神的言語，得見全能者的異象，眼目睜開而仆倒的人說：雅各啊，你的帳棚何等華美！以色列啊，你的帳幕何其華麗！我看他卻不在現時；我望他卻不在近日。有星要出於雅各，有杖要興於以色列。為你祝福的，願他蒙福；咒詛你的，願他受咒詛。

title.en: Moses on Nebo: Shown the Land, Buried by God
title.zh: 摩西登尼波：遙望美地，神親自埋葬

region.en: Mount Nebo, Pisgah, over against Jericho
region.zh: 尼波山，毗斯迦，對著耶利哥

period: Deuteronomy 34, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 5: Deuteronomy, chapter 34

summary.en: At 120, with eyes undimmed, Moses climbs Nebo and the LORD shows him all the promised land — Gilead to Dan, Judah to the utmost sea, the plain of Jericho to Zoar — with the verdict 'thou shalt not go over thither.' 'So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the LORD: and he buried him in a valley... but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.' Israel weeps thirty days; Joshua, filled with the spirit of wisdom by the laying on of hands, succeeds him; 'there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face.'
summary.zh: 摩西一百二十歲，眼目沒有昏花，登尼波山；耶和華把基列全地直到但、猶大全地直到西海、耶利哥平原直到瑣珥都指給他看——「你卻不得過去到那裏」。「耶和華的僕人摩西死在摩押地，正如耶和華所說的。耶和華將他埋葬……只是到今日沒有人知道他的墳墓。」以色列哀哭三十日；約書亞因摩西按手被智慧的靈充滿而繼任；「以色列中再沒有興起先知像摩西的，他是耶和華面對面所認識的」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The unknown grave (and the archangel's dispute over his body in Jude 9) has made Moses a locus of apocryphal imagination.

passages.text: And Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto the mountain of Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is over against Jericho. And the LORD shewed him all the land of Gilead, unto Dan, and all Naphtali, and the land of Ephraim, and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah, unto the utmost sea, and the south, and the plain of the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, unto Zoar. And the LORD said unto him, This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, saying, I will give it unto thy seed: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither.
passages.zh: 摩西從摩押平原登尼波山，上了那與耶利哥相對的毗斯迦山頂。耶和華把基列全地直到但，拿弗他利全地，以法蓮、瑪拿西的地，猶大全地直到西海，南地和棕樹城耶利哥的平原，直到瑣珥，都指給他看。耶和華對他說：「這就是我向亞伯拉罕、以撒、雅各起誓應許之地，說：『我必將這地賜給你的後裔。』現在我使你眼睛看見了，你卻不得過到那裡去。」

passages.text: So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the LORD. And he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Bethpeor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day. And Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated. And the children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days.
passages.zh: 於是，耶和華的僕人摩西死在摩押地，正如耶和華所說的。耶和華將他埋葬在摩押地、伯毗珥對面的谷中，只是到今日沒有人知道他的墳墓。摩西死的時候年一百二十歲；眼目沒有昏花，精神沒有衰敗。以色列人在摩押平原為摩西哀哭了三十日。

passages.text: And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses. And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face, in all the signs and the wonders, which the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt.
passages.zh: 嫩的兒子約書亞因為摩西曾按手在他頭上，就被智慧的靈充滿，以色列人便聽從他，照著耶和華吩咐摩西的行了。以後以色列中再沒有興起先知像摩西的，他是耶和華面對面所認識的，耶和華打發他在埃及地行各樣神蹟奇事。

title.en: The Ark Halts the Jordan and the Twelve Stones
title.zh: 約櫃止住約旦河水與十二塊石頭

region.en: Jordan crossing, opposite Jericho
region.zh: 約旦河渡口，正對耶利哥

period: Joshua 3-4, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapters 3-4

summary.en: The flood-swollen Jordan parts the instant the priests bearing the ark of the covenant step into the brim — 'the waters which came down from above stood and rose up upon an heap' — and the whole nation passes on dry ground, echoing the Red Sea. Twelve stones from the riverbed are pitched at Gilgal 'for a memorial unto the children of Israel for ever', so that when children ask 'What mean these stones?' the crossing will be told again; the manna ceases the next day.
summary.zh: 抬約櫃的祭司腳一入約旦河水邊，上游之水「在極遠之處停住，立起成壘」——漲水的約旦河立時斷流，全國行於乾地，呼應過紅海。眾人從河底取十二塊石頭立於吉甲「作以色列人永遠的紀念」，使後代子孫問「這些石頭是甚麼意思」時，故事得以重述；翌日嗎哪止息。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The twelve-stone memorial is a classic sacred-place etiology.

passages.text: And it shall come to pass, as soon as the soles of the feet of the priests that bear the ark of the LORD, the LORD of all the earth, shall rest in the waters of Jordan, that the waters of Jordan shall be cut off from the waters that come down from above; and they shall stand upon an heap. And as they that bare the ark were come unto Jordan, and the feet of the priests that bare the ark were dipped in the brim of the water, (for Jordan overfloweth all his banks all the time of harvest,) that the waters which came down from above stood and rose up upon an heap very far from the city Adam, that is beside Zaretan: and those that came down toward the sea of the plain, even the salt sea, failed, and were cut off: and the people passed over right against Jericho.
passages.zh: 等到抬普天下主耶和華約櫃的祭司把腳站在約但河水裡，約但河的水，就是從上往下流的水，必然斷絕，立起成壘。抬約櫃的祭司來到約但河，他們的腳一入水（原來約但河在收割的日子漲過兩岸），那從上往下流的水便在極遠之地、撒拉但旁的亞當城那裡停住，立起成壘；那往平原的海，就是鹽海，往下流的水全然斷絕。於是百姓在耶利哥的對面過去了。

passages.text: And the LORD spake unto Joshua, saying, Take you hence out of the midst of Jordan, out of the place where the priests' feet stood firm, twelve stones, and ye shall carry them over with you. That this may be a sign among you, that when your children ask their fathers in time to come, saying, What mean ye by these stones? Then ye shall answer them, That the waters of Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD; and these stones shall be for a memorial unto the children of Israel for ever.
passages.zh: 耶和華曉諭約書亞說：「你從約但河中，就是從祭司腳站定的地方，取十二塊石頭帶過去。這可以在你們中間作證據，日後你們的子孫問你們說：『這些石頭是甚麼意思？』你們就對他們說：『這是因為約但河的水在耶和華的約櫃前斷絕；約櫃過約但河的時候，約但河的水就斷絕了。這些石頭要作以色列人永遠的紀念。』」

passages.text: And it came to pass, when the priests that bare the ark of the covenant of the LORD were come up out of the midst of Jordan, and the soles of the priests' feet were lifted up unto the dry land, that the waters of Jordan returned unto their place, and flowed over all his banks, as they did before. And the people came up out of Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamped in Gilgal. And he spake unto the children of Israel, saying, When your children shall ask their fathers in time to come, saying, What mean these stones? Then ye shall let your children know, saying, Israel came over this Jordan on dry land.
passages.zh: 抬耶和華約櫃的祭司從約但河裡上來，腳掌剛落旱地，約但河的水就流回原處，仍舊漲過兩岸，像先前一樣。正月初十日，百姓從約但河裡上來，在吉甲安營。他對以色列人說：「日後你們的子孫問他們的父親說：『這些石頭是甚麼意思？』你們就告訴你們的子孫說：『以色列人曾走乾地過這約但河。』」

title.en: Rahab and the Scarlet Cord
title.zh: 喇合與朱紅線繩

region.en: Jericho, house upon the town wall
region.zh: 耶利哥，城牆上的房屋

period: Joshua 2, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapter 2

summary.en: Two spies lodge with Rahab the harlot on Jericho's wall; when the king's men come, she hides them under flax stalks on the roof and misdirects the pursuers to the fords. Confessing that the news of the Red Sea has already melted Canaan's hearts — 'for the LORD your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath' — she bargains for her family's lives, and the spies bind the deal with an oath and a scarlet cord in her window. Matthew names her an ancestress of Christ, and Hebrews and James both cite her faith and works.
summary.zh: 兩名探子夜宿城牆上的妓女喇合家中；王派人捉拿時，她將他們藏在房頂的麻秸中，引追捕者往渡口去。她承認紅海的神蹟早已令迦南人心都消化——「耶和華你們的神本是上天下地的神」——便為全家討命。使者以誓言與窗上的朱紅線繩為憑。馬太福音將她列為基督先祖，希伯來書與雅各書皆引其信心與行為。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. A Canaanite woman's oath-bound protection ruse; her role in the messianic genealogy is noted.

passages.text: And Joshua the son of Nun sent out of Shittim two men to spy secretly, saying, Go view the land, even Jericho. And they went, and came into an harlot's house, named Rahab, and lodged there. And it was told the king of Jericho, saying, Behold, there came men in hither to night of the children of Israel to search out the country. And the king of Jericho sent unto Rahab, saying, Bring forth the men that are come to thee. And the woman took the two men, and hid them, and said thus, There came men unto me, but I wist not whence they were.
passages.zh: 嫩的兒子約書亞從什亭暗暗打發兩個人作探子，吩咐說：「你們去窺探那地和耶利哥。」他們就去了，來到一個名叫喇合的妓女家裡，就在那裡住宿。有人告訴耶利哥王說：「看哪，今夜有以色列人來到這裡，要窺探這地。」耶利哥王就打發人到喇合那裡，說：「把那來到你這裡的人交出來。」那女人卻將那兩個人藏了，如此說：「確實有人來到我這裡，我卻不知道他們是從哪裡來的。」

passages.text: And she said unto the men, I know that the LORD hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you. For we have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red sea for you, when ye came out of Egypt. And as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man, because of you: for the LORD your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath.
passages.zh: 她又對那兩個人說：「我知道耶和華已經把這地賜給你們，並且因你們的緣故，我們都驚懼，這地所有的居民因你們的緣故都膽戰心驚。因為我們聽見耶和華怎樣在你們出埃及的時候為你們使紅海的水乾了。我們一聽見這些事，心就消化了，因你們的緣故，再沒有人有膽氣了；因為耶和華你們的神，本是上天下地的神。

passages.text: Now therefore, I pray you, swear unto me by the LORD, since I have shewed you kindness, that ye will also shew kindness unto my father's house, and give me a true token: and that ye will save alive my father, and my mother, and my brethren, and my sisters, and all that they have, and deliver our lives from death. And the men answered her, Our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business. Then she let them down by a cord through the window: for her house was upon the town wall, and she dwelt upon the wall.
passages.zh: 現在我祈求你們，既然我恩待了你們，請你們指著耶和華向我起誓，也要恩待我父家，並給我一個確實的憑據：要救活我的父母、弟兄、姊妹，和他們一切所有的，拯救我們的性命脫離死亡。」那兩個人對她說：「你若不洩漏我們這件事，我們願以性命代替你們的性命。」於是，她用繩子將他們從窗戶縋下去；因為她的房子在城牆上，她就住在城牆上。

title.en: The Captain of the LORD's Host
title.zh: 耶和華軍隊的元帥

region.en: Plains before Jericho
region.zh: 耶利哥平原

period: Joshua 5:13-15, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapter 5

summary.en: Scouting Jericho's walls, Joshua meets a man with a drawn sword and demands his allegiance: 'Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?' The answer reframes the whole campaign — 'Nay; but as captain of the host of the LORD am I now come' — and Joshua falls on his face and worships, told to loose his shoe, 'for the place whereon thou standest is holy', Moses' burning bush a generation earlier.
summary.zh: 約書亞在耶利哥附近觀看城牆，見一人手裏有拔出來的刀，便問：「你是幫助我們呢，是幫助我們敵人呢？」回答重新定義了整場戰役：「不是的，我來是要作耶和華軍隊的元帥。」約書亞就俯伏在地拜他，並被吩咐脫鞋——「因為你所站的地方是聖的」——正如一代之前的焚而不毀之荊棘。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Christian interpretation debates whether the captain is an angel or the pre-incarnate Christ; both readings noted.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when Joshua was by Jericho, that he lifted up his eyes and looked, and, behold, there stood a man over against him with his sword drawn in his hand: and Joshua went unto him, and said unto him, Art thou for us, or for our adversaries? And he said, Nay; but as captain of the host of the LORD am I now come. And Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and did worship, and said unto him, What saith my Lord unto his servant? And the captain of the LORD's host said unto Joshua, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy. And Joshua did so.
passages.zh: 約書亞靠近耶利哥的時候，舉目觀看，見有一個人手裡拔出刀來，站在對面。約書亞走到他那裡，問他說：「你是幫助我們的，還是幫助我們敵人的？」他回答說：「不是的，我現在來，是要作耶和華軍隊的元帥。」約書亞就俯伏在地敬拜，說：「我主有什麼話吩咐僕人？」耶和華軍隊的元帥對約書亞說：「把你腳上的鞋脫下來，因為你所站的地方是聖的。」約書亞就照著做了。

title.en: The Walls of Jericho Fall
title.zh: 耶利哥城牆倒塌

region.en: Jericho, city of palm trees
region.zh: 耶利哥，棕樹之城

period: Joshua 6, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapter 6

summary.en: The straitly-shut city falls to a liturgy, not a siege: silent armed men, seven priests with ram's-horn trumpets and the ark, one circuit a day for six days — and on the seventh, seven circuits, a long blast, and Joshua's command 'Shout; for the LORD hath given you the city.' The wall falls down flat; Rahab and hers are led out; the city is burned and its treasures treasured up for the LORD; and Joshua lays a builder's curse on whoever rebuilds Jericho.
summary.zh: 門戶緊閉的城不是被攻破而是被禮儀傾覆：武裝之人靜默前行，七位祭司吹羊角號抬約櫃繞城，六日每日一圈；第七日繞城七圈，角聲拖長，約書亞下令「呼喊吧，因為耶和華已經把城交給你們了」。城牆便塌陷。喇合一家被帶出；全城被焚，金銀銅鐵歸入耶和華府庫；約書亞起誓咒詛重建此城之人。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The ban (herem) passages are presented as text; modern readers must reckon with the conquest violence they record.

passages.text: Now Jericho was straitly shut up because of the children of Israel: none went out, and none came in. And the LORD said unto Joshua, See, I have given into thine hand Jericho, and the king thereof, and the mighty men of valour. And ye shall compass the city, all ye men of war, and go round about the city once. And seven priests shall bear before the ark seven trumpets of rams' horns: and the seventh day ye shall compass the city seven times, and the priests shall blow with the trumpets.
passages.zh: 耶利哥因以色列人的緣故，緊緊關閉，無人出入。耶和華對約書亞說：「看哪，我已經把耶利哥、它的王，和勇猛的戰士都交在你手中了。你們一切戰士要圍繞這城，每天繞城一次，六日都要這樣行。七個祭司要拿七個羊角號走在約櫃前；到第七日，你們要繞城七次，祭司也要吹號。

passages.text: And it came to pass at the seventh time, when the priests blew with the trumpets, Joshua said unto the people, Shout; for the LORD hath given you the city. And the city shall be accursed, even it, and all that are therein, to the LORD: only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all that are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers that we sent.
passages.zh: 到了第七次，祭司吹號的時候，約書亞對百姓說：「呼喊吧，因為耶和華已經把這城賜給你們了。這城和其中所有的，都要歸耶和華為當毀滅的物；只有妓女喇合與她家中所有的可以存活，因為她藏了我們所打發的使者。

passages.text: So the people shouted when the priests blew with the trumpets: and it came to pass, when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, and the people shouted with a great shout, that the wall fell down flat, so that the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city. And they utterly destroyed all that was in the city, both man and woman, young and old, and ox, and sheep, and ass, with the edge of the sword. But Joshua had said unto the two men that had spied out the country, Go into the harlot's house, and bring out thence the woman, and all that she hath, as ye sware unto her. And Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive, and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day.
passages.zh: 於是百姓在祭司吹號的時候呼喊；百姓一聽見號聲，就大聲呼喊，城牆便塌陷了，百姓就上去進城，各人直往前行，攻取了那城。他們用刀劍將城中所有的盡行毀滅，無論男女老少，以及牛、羊、驢。約書亞曾對那窺探這地的兩個人說：你們進那妓女的家，照你們向她所起的誓，將那女人和她所有的都帶出來。約書亞卻保全了妓女喇合和她父家，使她住在以色列中，直到今日。

title.en: Achan and the Valley of Achor
title.zh: 亞干與亞割谷

region.en: Ai, near Bethel; valley of Achor
region.zh: 艾城，伯特利附近；亞割谷

period: Joshua 7, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapter 7

summary.en: One man's loot defeats an army: Achan of Judah takes a goodly Babylonish garment, 200 shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold from the banned spoil of Jericho, and hides it in his tent. Three thousand men flee before little Ai, and Joshua tears his clothes before the ark — 'Alas, O LORD God, wherefore hast thou at all brought this people over Jordan?' — until the LORD names the sin: Israel has taken the accursed thing. Lot by lot the tribe, family, household, and man are taken; Achan confesses, and he, his family, and his goods are stoned and burned in the valley of Achor — 'trouble' — the heap of stones standing over both.
summary.zh: 一個人的贓物令全軍敗北：猶大人亞干取了耶利哥當滅之物——美好的示拿衣服、二百舍客勒銀子、五十舍客勒金子——藏在帳棚地裏。三千以色列人竟敗於小小的艾城；約書亞撕裂衣服伏在約櫃前——「哀哉，主耶和華啊，你為何領這民過約旦河？」——直到神指明：以色列犯了罪。按支派、宗族、家室、人丁被拈出；亞干認罪，與家眷財物在亞割谷（「連累」之意）被石頭打死焚燒，堆石為記。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The collective punishment is part of the recorded text and is presented without endorsement.

passages.text: But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the LORD was kindled against the children of Israel. So there went up thither of the people about three thousand men: and they fled before the men of Ai. And the men of Ai smote of them about thirty and six men: wherefore the hearts of the people melted, and became as water. And Joshua rent his clothes, and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark of the LORD until the eventide, he and the elders of Israel, and put dust upon their heads.
passages.zh: 但以色列人在當毀滅的物上犯了罪：因為猶大支派中，謝拉的曾孫、撒底的孫子、迦米的兒子亞干取了當毀滅的物；耶和華的怒氣就向以色列人發作。於是百姓中上去那裡的約有三千人；他們在艾城的人面前逃跑。艾城的人擊殺了他們約三十六人；因此百姓的心就消化，如同水一般。約書亞便撕裂衣服，他和以色列的長老在耶和華的約櫃前俯伏在地，直到晚上，又把塵土撒在頭上。

passages.text: And the LORD said unto Joshua, Get thee up; wherefore liest thou thus upon thy face? Israel hath sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: for they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also. Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies, but turned their backs before their enemies, because they were accursed: neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you.
passages.zh: 耶和華對約書亞說：起來！你為何這樣俯伏在地呢？以色列人犯了罪，也違背了我所吩咐他們的約；因為他們取了當毀滅的物，又偷竊，又行詭詐。因此以色列人在仇敵面前站立不住，在仇敵面前轉背逃跑，因為他們成了當毀滅的；你們若不把當毀滅的物從你們中間除掉，我就不再與你們同在了。

passages.text: And Achan answered Joshua, and said, Indeed I have sinned against the LORD God of Israel, and thus and thus have I done: When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent. And Joshua said, Why hast thou troubled us? the LORD shall trouble thee this day. And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones. Wherefore the name of that place was called, The valley of Achor, unto this day.
passages.zh: 亞干回答約書亞說：我實在得罪了耶和華以色列的神，我所做的事是如此如此：我在所奪的財物中看見一件美好的巴比倫衣服、二百舍客勒銀子、一條重五十舍客勒的金子，我就貪愛這些，便拿去了；如今藏在我帳棚裡的地中。約書亞說：你為何連累我們呢？今日耶和華必叫你受連累。以色列眾人就用石頭打死他，又用火焚燒，將他們用石頭打死之後，就用火燒了。因此那地方的名直到今日還叫亞割谷。

title.en: The Gibeonites' Mouldy Bread Trick
title.zh: 基遍人的陳乾餅計謀

region.en: Gibeon, in the hills near Jerusalem
region.zh: 基遍，耶路撒冷附近山地

period: Joshua 9, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapter 9

summary.en: The Hivites of Gibeon 'did work wilily': dressing as ambassadors with old sacks, rent wine bottles, clouted shoes, and mouldy bread, they win from Joshua a sworn league by claiming to come 'from a very far country' — because of the fame of the LORD. Three days later the truth emerges: they are next-door neighbors. Bound by the princes' oath, Israel spares them and the Gibeonites become hewers of wood and drawers of water 'unto this day' — the treaty made by deception yet kept by oath.
summary.zh: 基遍的希未人「設詭計」：自扮使者，取舊口袋、破裂的皮酒袋、補過的鞋和發黴的餅，自稱從「極遠之地」而來——因聞耶和華的名聲——騙得約書亞指起誓立約。三日後真相敗露：他們原是近鄰。因起過誓，以色列存留他們性命，基遍人從此「為會眾劈柴挑水，直到今日」——以詭計立的約，卻以誓言守到底。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The famous deception-treaty narrative; the oath's binding force despite the fraud is the interpretive crux.

passages.text: And when the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done unto Jericho and to Ai, they did work wilily, and went and made as if they had been ambassadors, and took old sacks upon their asses, and wine bottles, old, and rent, and bound up; and old shoes and clouted upon their feet, and old garments upon them; and all the bread of their provision was dry and mouldy. And they went to Joshua unto the camp at Gilgal, and said unto him, and to the men of Israel, We be come from a far country: now therefore make ye a league with us.
passages.zh: 基遍的居民聽見約書亞向耶利哥和艾城所行的事，就施詭計，假裝使者，把舊口袋馱在驢上，又帶著破裂縫補的舊皮酒袋；腳上穿的是舊鞋，補了又補，身上穿的是舊衣服；他們所帶的食物都乾了，長了霉。他們到吉甲的營中見約書亞，對他和以色列人說：我們從遠方來，現在求你與我們立約。

passages.text: And they said unto him, From a very far country thy servants are come because of the name of the LORD thy God: for we have heard the fame of him, and all that he did in Egypt. This our bread we took hot for our provision out of our houses on the day we came forth to go unto you; but now, behold, it is dry, and it is mouldy: and these bottles of wine, which we filled, were new; and, behold, they be rent: and these our garments and our shoes are become old by reason of the very long journey.
passages.zh: 他們對他說：你的僕人因耶和華你神的名，從極遠之地而來；因為我們聽見了他的名聲，以及他在埃及所行的一切事。我們出來要往你們這裡來的那日，從家裡帶出來的這餅還是熱的；現在看哪，都乾了，長了霉；我們盛酒的這皮袋本是新的，現在看哪，都破裂了；我們這衣服和鞋子，也因路途甚遠而舊了。

passages.text: And the men took of their victuals, and asked not counsel at the mouth of the LORD. And Joshua made peace with them, and made a league with them, to let them live: and the princes of the congregation sware unto them. And it came to pass at the end of three days after they had made a league with them, that they heard that they were their neighbours. And Joshua called for them, and he spake unto them, saying, Wherefore have ye beguiled us, saying, We are very far from you, when ye dwell among us?
passages.zh: 那些人便拿了些食物，並沒有求問耶和華。約書亞就與他們講和，與他們立約，容他們活著；會眾的首領也向他們起誓。他們與他們立約之後，過了三天，才聽說他們是近鄰，住在他們中間。約書亞便召了他們來，對他們說：你們為什麼欺哄我們說：我們離你們甚遠呢？其實你們就住在我們中間。

title.en: Sun, Stand Thou Still over Gibeon
title.zh: 日頭啊，你要停在基遍

region.en: Valley of Ajalon, road to Bethhoron
region.zh: 亞雅崙谷，上伯和崙之道

period: Joshua 10:12-14, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapter 10

summary.en: Five Amorite kings besiege Gibeon for making peace with Israel; marching all night up from Gilgal, Joshua sees the battle turning into a long pursuit and prays in the sight of all Israel: 'Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon.' 'And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed... and hasted not to go down about a whole day' — 'and there was no day like that before it or after it, that the LORD hearkened unto the voice of a man', while great hailstones from heaven kill more than the sword.
summary.zh: 五王聯兵圍攻與以色列結好的基遍；約書亞自吉甲徹夜急行軍救援，見戰事轉為漫長追擊，便在以色列眾人眼前禱告：「日頭啊，你要停在基遍；月亮啊，你要止在亞雅崙谷。」「日頭果然停住，月亮止住……不急速下落，約有一日之久」——「耶和華聽人的禱告，沒有像這日的」；同時天上降大冰雹，被雹打死的比刀殺的還多。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Tagged with sun-capture for the sun-stopping motif shared with solar-capture tales cross-culturally; noted as an interpretive cross-tag.

passages.text: Therefore the five kings of the Amorites, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon, gathered themselves together, and went up, they and all their hosts, and encamped before Gibeon, and made war against it. So Joshua ascended from Gilgal, he, and all the people of war with him; and Joshua came unto them suddenly, and went up from Gilgal all night. And the LORD discomfited them before Israel, and slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon.
passages.zh: 於是亞摩利人的五個王，就是耶路撒冷王、希伯崙王、耶末王、拉吉王、伊磯倫王，大家聚集，率領他們的眾軍上去，對著基遍安營，攻打基遍。約書亞就從吉甲上去，他和一切打仗的百姓都與他同去；約書亞忽然來到他們那裏，從吉甲上去，終夜行軍。耶和華在以色列人面前使他們潰亂，在基遍大大地殺敗他們。

passages.text: Then spake Joshua to the LORD in the day when the LORD delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel, Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon. And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the nation had avenged themselves upon their enemies. Is not this written in the book of Jasher? So the sun stood still in the midst of heaven, and hasted not to go down about a whole day. And there was no day like that before it or after it, that the LORD hearkened unto the voice of a man: for the LORD fought for Israel.
passages.zh: 當耶和華將亞摩利人交付以色列人的日子，約書亞就向耶和華禱告，在以色列人眼前說：日頭啊，你要停在基遍；月亮啊，你要止在亞雅崙谷。於是日頭停留，月亮止住，直到國民向仇敵報了仇。這事豈不是寫在雅煞珥書上嗎？日頭在天當中停留，不急速下落，約有一日之久。在這日以前，這日以後，耶和華聽人的禱告，沒有像這日的，是因耶和華為以色列爭戰。

title.en: As for Me and My House: Joshua's Covenant at Shechem
title.zh: 至於我和我家：約書亞在示劍立約

region.en: Shechem, before the sanctuary of God
region.zh: 示劍，神聖所前

period: Joshua 24, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapter 24

summary.en: At Shechem the dying Joshua gathers all the tribes before God and recites the whole sacred history — Terah's household serving other gods, the call of Abraham, Egypt, the sea, Balaam's baffled curse, the hornet sent before Israel — and puts the choice to the people: 'choose you this day whom ye will serve... but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.' The people swear, Joshua writes the words in the book of the law of God and sets up a great stone under an oak as witness, and dismisses them — 'and it came to pass after these things, that Joshua the son of Nun died.'
summary.zh: 臨終的約書亞在示劍召集眾支派立在神面前，重述整部聖史——他拉家事奉別神、亞伯拉罕蒙召、埃及、紅海、巴蘭受挫的咒詛、為以色列先行之神使——並將抉擇擺在百姓面前：「今日就可以選擇所要事奉的……至於我和我家，我們必定事奉耶和華。」百姓起誓；約書亞將這話寫在神的律法書上，在橡樹下立一塊大石頭作見證，隨即解散會眾——「這些事以後，耶和華的僕人約書亞死了」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Covenant-renewal liturgy; the Shechem assembly echoes Genesis's altar sites.

passages.text: And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, and called for the elders of Israel, and for their heads, and for their judges, and for their officers; and they presented themselves before God. And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods. And I took your father Abraham from the other side of the flood, and led him throughout all the land of Canaan, and multiplied his seed, and gave him Isaac.
passages.zh: 約書亞將以色列的眾支派聚集在示劍，召了以色列的長老、族長、審判官，並官長來，他們就站在神面前。約書亞對眾民說：耶和華以色列的神如此說：古時你們的列祖，就是亞伯拉罕的父親他拉，和拿鶴的父親，住在大河那邊，事奉別神。我將你們的父親亞伯拉罕從大河那邊帶來，領他走遍迦南全地，又使他的子孫眾多，把以撒賜給他。

passages.text: And ye went over Jordan, and came unto Jericho: and the men of Jericho fought against you; and I delivered them into your hand. And I have given you a land for which ye did not labour, and cities which ye built not, and ye dwell in them; of the vineyards and oliveyards which ye planted not do ye eat. Now therefore fear the LORD, and serve him in sincerity and in truth: and put away the gods which your fathers served on the other side of the flood, and in Egypt; and serve ye the LORD.
passages.zh: 你們過了約但河，到了耶利哥；耶利哥人與你們爭戰，我也把他們交在你們手裏。我賜給你們地土，非你們所修治的；我賜給你們城邑，非你們所建造的，你們卻住在其中；又得吃非你們所栽種的葡萄園、橄欖園。現在你們要敬畏耶和華，誠心實意地事奉他，將你們列祖在大河那邊和在埃及所事奉的神除掉，去事奉耶和華。

passages.text: And if it seem evil unto you to serve the LORD, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD. And the people answered and said, God forbid that we should forsake the LORD, to serve other gods; for the LORD our God, he it is that brought us up and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage. So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day; and Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God, and took a great stone, and set it up there under an oak, that was by the sanctuary of the LORD. And Joshua said unto all the people, Behold, this stone shall be a witness unto us; for it hath heard all the words of the LORD which he spake unto us.
passages.zh: 若是你們以事奉耶和華為不好，今日就可以選擇所要事奉的：是你們列祖在大河那邊所事奉的神呢？是你們所住這地之亞摩利人的神呢？至於我和我家，我們必定事奉耶和華。百姓回答說：我們斷不敢離棄耶和華去事奉別神；因耶和華我們的神曾將我們和我們列祖從埃及地的為奴之家領出來。當日約書亞就與百姓立約；約書亞將這些話都寫在神的律法書上，又將一塊大石頭立在橡樹下耶和華的聖所旁邊。約書亞對眾民說：看哪，這石頭可以向我們作見證；因為耶和華所吩咐我們的一切話，這石頭都聽見了。

title.en: Gideon and the Fleece of Wool
title.zh: 基甸與羊毛之兆

region.en: Oak at Ophrah, winepress of the Abiezrites
region.zh: 俄弗拉的橡樹，亞比以謝人的酒榨

period: Judges 6, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 7: Judges, chapter 6

summary.en: Threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it from Midian's grasshopper-hordes, the least of a poor family is hailed by an angel: 'The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.' Fire from a rock consumes his offering; by night he throws down his father's altar of Baal — and his father's sneer, 'if he be a god, let him plead for himself,' renames him Jerubbaal. Twice-tested with a fleece of wool — wet fleece on dry ground, then dry fleece on wet — the doubting deliverer musters Israel.
summary.zh: 在酒榨裏藏躲米甸人的基甸——家中最貧、父家最微小的——竟被使者稱為「大能的勇士」。磐石出火燒盡祭物；夜間他拆下父親的巴力祭壇，其父譏誚道：「他若是神，卻有人拆毀他的壇，讓他為自己爭論吧」，基甸遂名耶路巴力。羊毛之兆兩次試驗——毛上有露、四地皆乾；翌夜反是——懷疑的拯救者終於召集以色列。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The fleece test is the classic sign-seeking divination in scripture; noted as such.

passages.text: And there came an angel of the LORD, and sat under an oak which was in Ophrah, that pertained unto Joash the Abiezrite: and his son Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress, to hide it from the Midianites. And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him, and said unto him, The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour. And Gideon said unto him, Oh my Lord, if the LORD be with us, why then is all this befallen us? and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of?
passages.zh: 耶和華的使者到了俄弗拉，坐在亞比以謝族人約阿施的橡樹下。約阿施的兒子基甸正在酒醡那裡打麥子，為要防備米甸人。耶和華的使者向他顯現，對他說：「大能的勇士啊，耶和華與你同在。」基甸對他說：「主啊，耶和華若與我們同在，我們何至遭遇這一切事呢？我們的列祖向我們所說的那些奇事在哪裡呢？」

passages.text: Then the angel of the LORD put forth the end of the staff that was in his hand, and touched the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and there rose up fire out of the rock, and consumed the flesh and the unleavened cakes. And it came to pass the same night, that the LORD said unto him, Take thy father's young bullock, and throw down the altar of Baal that thy father hath, and cut down the grove that is by it. And Joash said unto all that stood against him, Will ye plead for Baal? will ye save him? he that will plead for him, let him be put to death whilst it is yet morning: if he be a god, let him plead for himself, because one hath cast down his altar.
passages.zh: 耶和華的使者伸出手內的杖，杖頭挨了肉和無酵餅，就有火從磐石中出來，燒盡了肉和無酵餅。當那夜，耶和華吩咐他說：「你取你父親的牛犢，並拆毀你父親為巴力所築的壇，砍下壇旁的木偶。」約阿施對一切站立攻擊他的人說：「你們是為巴力爭論嗎？你們要救他嗎？誰為他爭論，趁早將誰處死。巴力若果是神，有人拆毀他的壇，讓他為自己爭論吧。」

passages.text: And Gideon said unto God, If thou wilt save Israel by mine hand, as thou hast said, Behold, I will put a fleece of wool in the floor; and if the dew be on the fleece only, and it be dry upon all the earth beside, then shall I know that thou wilt save Israel by mine hand, as thou hast said. And it was so: for he rose up early on the morrow, and thrust the fleece together, and wringed the dew out of the fleece, a bowl full of water. And Gideon said unto God, let me prove, I pray thee, but this once with the fleece; let it now be dry only upon the fleece, and upon all the ground let there be dew. And God did so that night.
passages.zh: 基甸對神說：「你若果照著所說的話，藉我手拯救以色列人，我就把一團羊毛放在禾場上：若單是羊毛上有露水，別的地方都是乾的，我就知道你必照著所說的話，藉我手拯救以色列人。」次日早晨，基甸起來，將羊毛擠一擠，從羊毛中擰出滿盆的露水來。基甸又對神說：「求你再讓我用羊毛試一次：單是羊毛是乾的，別的地方都有露水。」那夜神也照樣行了。

title.en: Gideon's Three Hundred: Trumpets, Pitchers, Lamps
title.zh: 基甸三百勇士：號筒、瓦罐與火把

region.en: Well of Harod, valley of Jezreel
region.zh: 哈律泉旁，耶斯列谷

period: Judges 7, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 7: Judges, chapter 7

summary.en: 'The people that are with thee are too many' — 32,000 are cut to 10,000, then to 300, chosen for lapping water like dogs. Sneaking to the enemy's edge, Gideon overhears a sentry's dream: a barley cake rolling into the Midianite camp and flattening a tent. At the middle watch the three hundred blow trumpets, smash pitchers to reveal hidden lamps, and cry 'The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon' — and the vast host turns its own swords on itself and flees, with princes Oreb and Zeeb taken on the way.
summary.zh: 「跟隨你的人太多」——三萬二千人先減至一萬，再以舔水如狗之法留下三百。基甸潛至敵營邊緣，聽見哨兵之夢：一塊大麥餅滾入米甸營中，將帳幕撞倒。三更之時，三百人吹角、打破瓦罐露出暗藏的火把，高呼「耶和華和基甸的刀」——敵營自相殘殺而潰逃，途中俄立、西伊伯二王被擒。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The enemy's prophetic dream is the divination element.

passages.text: And the LORD said unto Gideon, The people that are with thee are too many for me to give the Midianites into their hands, lest Israel vaunt themselves against me, saying, Mine own hand hath saved me. So he brought down the people unto the water: and the LORD said unto Gideon, Every one that lappeth of the water with his tongue, as a dog lappeth, him shalt thou set by himself. And the number of them that lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, were three hundred men.
passages.zh: 耶和華對基甸說：「跟隨你的人過多，我不能將米甸人交在他們手中，免得以色列人向我誇大說：『是我們自己的手救了我們。』」於是基甸領他們下到水旁。耶和華對基甸說：「凡用舌頭舔水，像狗舔的，要使他單站在一處。」用手捧著舔水的，數目共有三百人。

passages.text: And when Gideon was come, behold, there was a man that told a dream unto his fellow, and said, Behold, I dreamed a dream, and, lo, a cake of barley bread tumbled into the host of Midian, and came unto a tent, and smote it that it fell, and overturned it, that the tent lay along. And his fellow answered and said, This is nothing else save the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel: for into his hand hath God delivered Midian, and all the host.
passages.zh: 基甸到了，就聽見一人將夢告訴同伴說：「我作了一夢，夢見一個大麥餅滾入米甸營中，到了帳幕，將帳幕撞倒，帳幕就翻轉傾覆了。」那同伴回答說：「這不是別的，乃是約阿施的兒子基甸的刀；神已將米甸和全軍都交在他的手中。」

passages.text: And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put a trumpet in every man's hand, with empty pitchers, and lamps within the pitchers. So Gideon, and the hundred men that were with him, came unto the outside of the camp in the beginning of the middle watch; and they blew the trumpets, and brake the pitchers that were in their hands. And they cried, The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon. And they stood every man in his place round about the camp; and all the host ran, and cried, and fled. And the three hundred blew the trumpets, and the LORD set every man's sword against his fellow, even throughout all the host.
passages.zh: 基甸就將三百人分作三隊，把角和空瓶交在各人手裡，瓶內都藏著火把。基甸和跟隨他的一百人，在三更之初才到營旁，就吹角，打破手中的瓶。他們喊著說：「耶和華的刀！基甸的刀！」他們各人就站在營的四周各處；全營的人都亂竄，呼喊逃跑。三百人就吹角，耶和華使全營的人用刀互相擊殺。

title.en: Honey from the Lion: Samson's Riddle
title.zh: 獅中之蜜：參孫的謎語

region.en: Vineyards of Timnath, wedding feast
region.zh: 亭拿的葡萄園，婚宴

period: Judges 14, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 7: Judges, chapter 14

summary.en: A young lion roars against Samson on the road to Timnath; the Spirit of the LORD comes mightily upon him and he rends it barehanded, saying nothing. Returning later, he finds a swarm of bees and honey in the carcass, takes some, and at the wedding feast puts thirty companions a riddle with thirty changes of garments at stake: 'Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness.' Betrayed by his wife's seven days of weeping, the Philistines answer; Samson, his riddle solved by treachery, pays his wager with garments won from thirty men he slays at Ashkelon.
summary.zh: 往亭拿路上，少壯獅子向參孫吼叫；耶和華的靈大大感動他，他赤手撕裂獅子如撕小羊，未曾告知父母。後來獅子屍身中竟有蜜蜂與蜜，他取了蜜吃。婚宴上他向三十個伴郎出謎，以三十件裡衣外衣為彩：「吃的從吃者出來，甜的從強者出來。」七日之內，其妻哭逼他洩題；非利士人得答案，參孫以亞實基倫三十人所殺之衣償注。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The lion-slaying strongman narrative; the riddle is the classic trick-bet.

passages.text: Then went Samson down, and his father and his mother, to Timnath, and came to the vineyards of Timnath: and, behold, a young lion roared against him. And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and he rent him as he would have rent a kid, and he had nothing in his hand: but he told not his father or his mother what he had done. And after a time he returned to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcase of the lion: and, behold, there was a swarm of bees and honey in the carcase of the lion.
passages.zh: 參孫下到亭拿，他的父母也一同下去，來到亭拿的葡萄園；看哪，有一隻少壯獅子向他吼叫。耶和華的靈大大感動參孫，他雖然手無器械，卻將獅子撕裂，如同撕裂山羊羔一樣；只是他沒有告訴父母自己所做的事。過了些日子，他回去要娶那女子，就轉向路旁去看那獅子的屍體；看哪，獅子的屍體內有一群蜜蜂和蜜。

passages.text: And Samson said unto them, I will now put forth a riddle unto you: if ye can certainly declare it me within the seven days of the feast, and find it out, then I will give you thirty sheets and thirty change of garments: but if ye cannot declare it me, then shall ye give me thirty sheets and thirty change of garments. And he said unto them, Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness. And they could not in three days expound the riddle.
passages.zh: 參孫對他們說：我如今要給你們出一個謎語；你們若能在七日筵宴之內確實猜出，告訴我，我就給你們三十件裡衣、三十套衣裳；你們若不能告訴我，你們就給我三十件裡衣、三十套衣裳。參孫對他們說：吃的從吃者出來，甜的從強者出來。他們三日不能猜出這謎語的意思。

title.en: Delilah's Silver and Samson's Shorn Strength
title.zh: 大利拉的銀錢與參孫剃下的髮

region.en: Valley of Sorek
region.zh: 梭烈谷

period: Judges 16, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 7: Judges, chapter 16

summary.en: The Philistine lords offer Delilah eleven hundred pieces of silver apiece to find the secret of the strongman's power. Three times Samson plays the game with lies — green withs, new ropes, the woven web — and three times bursts free; but pressed daily until his soul is vexed to death, he tells all his heart: the Nazirite vow, no razor upon his head. Sleep on her knees, a shave of the seven locks, and he wakes not knowing 'the LORD was departed from him'; his eyes are put out, and he grinds in the prison house at Gaza while his hair begins to grow again.
summary.zh: 非利士人的首領各以一千一百舍客勒銀子買通大利拉，探問大能者之力的秘密。參孫三度以謊言戲弄——青繩、新繩、織布的緯線——三度掙脫；終因日日糾纏「煩得要死」，傾心吐意：拿細耳人之誓，未剃之髮。枕膝而眠，七綹髮被剃；醒來不知「耶和華已離開他」。雙眼被剜，在迦薩監裏推磨，而頭髮漸漸又長起來。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The broken vow and the betrayed secret; the seduction-betrayal tale type.

passages.text: And it came to pass afterward, that he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah. And the lords of the Philistines came up unto her, and said unto her, Entice him, and see wherein his great strength lieth, and by what means we may prevail against him, that we may bind him to afflict him; and we will give thee every one of us eleven hundred pieces of silver. And Delilah said to Samson, Tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth.
passages.zh: 後來，參孫在梭烈谷喜愛一個女子，名叫大利拉。非利士人的首領上去見那女子，對她說：求你引誘參孫，探探他因何有這麼大的力氣，我們用何法能勝他，好捆綁他苦害他；我們每人就給你一千一百舍客勒銀子。大利拉對參孫說：求你告訴我，你因何有這麼大的力氣。

passages.text: And Samson said unto her, If they bind me with seven green withs that were never dried, then shall I be weak, and be as another man. Then the lords of the Philistines brought up to her seven green withs which had not been dried, and she bound him with them. Now there were men lying in wait, abiding with her in the chamber. And she said unto him, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he brake the withs, as a thread of tow is broken when it toucheth the fire. So his strength was not known.
passages.zh: 參孫回答她說：人若用七條未乾的青繩子捆綁我，我就軟弱，像別人一樣。於是非利士人的首領拿了七條未乾的青繩子來交給她，她就用繩子捆綁參孫。當時有人預先埋伏在婦人的內室裡。婦人對他說：參孫哪，非利士人拿你來了。參孫就掙斷繩子，如掙斷經火的麻線一般。這樣，他力氣的根由還是沒有人知道。

passages.text: And it came to pass, when she pressed him daily with her words, and urged him, so that his soul was vexed unto death; that he told her all his heart, and said unto her, There hath not come a razor upon mine head; for I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother's womb: if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man. And she made him sleep upon her knees; and she called for a man, and she caused him to shave off the seven locks of his head; and she began to afflict him, and his strength went from him. And she said, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he awoke out of his sleep, and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the LORD was departed from him.
passages.zh: 大利拉天天用話催逼他，甚至他心裡煩悶要死；參孫就把心中所藏的都告訴了她，對她說：向來沒有人用剃頭刀剃我的頭，因為我自出母胎就歸神作拿細耳人；若剃了我的頭髮，我的力氣就離開我，我便軟弱，像別人一樣。大利拉使參孫枕著她的膝睡覺，叫了一個人來，剃除他頭上的七條髮綹；於是大利拉開始苦害他，他的力氣就離開他了。大利拉說：參孫哪，非利士人拿你來了。參孫從睡中醒來，心裡說：我要像前幾次出去活動身體。他卻不知道耶和華已經離開他了。

title.en: Samson's Death Between the Pillars of Dagon
title.zh: 參孫死於大袞廟兩柱之間

region.en: Temple of Dagon, Gaza
region.zh: 迦薩，大袞神廟

period: Judges 16:23-31, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 7: Judges, chapter 16

summary.en: At a great sacrifice to Dagon — 'our god hath delivered Samson our enemy into our hand' — the blind captive is summoned to make sport and set between the pillars of the packed temple, three thousand on the roof. Feeling for the pillars that bear the house, Samson prays once more: 'O Lord God, remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once.' He bows himself with all his might; the house falls on the lords and all the people — 'so the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life.'
summary.zh: 非利士人為大袞神設大筵獻祭——「我們的神將仇敵參孫交在我們手中」——召瞎眼的囚犯出來戲耍，置於擠滿人群的廟宇兩柱之間，房頂還有三千人。參孫憑觸覺摸到撐屋之柱，向神作最後禱告：「主耶和華啊，求你眷念我，求你賜我這一次的力量。」他曲身盡力，房屋倒塌壓死首領與眾人——「參孫死時所殺的人比活著所殺的還多」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Dagon festival setting; the death-at-victory is among the most famous martyrdom images in the tradition.

passages.text: Then the lords of the Philistines gathered them together for to offer a great sacrifice unto Dagon their god, and to rejoice: for they said, Our god hath delivered Samson our enemy into our hand. And it came to pass, when their hearts were merry, that they said, Call for Samson, that he may make us sport. And they set him between the pillars. And Samson said unto the lad that held him by the hand, Suffer me that I may feel the pillars whereupon the house standeth, that I may lean upon them.
passages.zh: 非利士人的首領聚集，要向他們的神大袞獻大祭，並且歡樂；因為他們說：我們的神將我們的仇敵參孫交在我們手中了。眾人正心中歡樂的時候，就說：叫參孫來，在我們面前戲耍戲耍。於是將參孫從監裡提出來，他就戲耍。他們把他安置在兩柱之間。參孫對牽他手的童子說：求你讓我摸著支撐這殿的柱子，我要靠一靠。

passages.text: Now the house was full of men and women; and all the lords of the Philistines were there; and there were upon the roof about three thousand men and women, that beheld while Samson made sport. And Samson called unto the LORD, and said, O Lord God, remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once, O God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes. And Samson took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house stood. And Samson said, Let me die with the Philistines. And he bowed himself with all his might; and the house fell upon the lords, and upon all the people that were therein. So the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life.
passages.zh: 那時，房子裡充滿了男女，非利士人的眾首領也都在那裡；屋頂上約有三千男女，觀看參孫戲耍。參孫向耶和華呼求說：「主耶和華啊，求你記念我，求你只這一次賜我力量，神啊，使我一舉為我這兩隻眼睛向非利士人報仇。」參孫就抱住支撐房子的兩根中間柱子。參孫說：「我願與非利士人同死。」他就盡力屈身，房子便倒塌在眾首領和所有在裡面的人身上。這樣，他死時所殺的人，比他活著時所殺的還多。

title.en: Ruth, Boaz, and the Line of David
title.zh: 路得、波阿斯與大衛的家系

region.en: Fields of Bethlehem, city gate
region.zh: 伯利恆的田間與城門

period: Book of Ruth, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 8: Ruth

summary.en: Famine drives Elimelech of Bethlehem to Moab, where he and his sons die, leaving Naomi and the Moabite widow Ruth. Ruth's vow — 'whither thou goest, I will go... thy God my God' — carries her to Bethlehem's harvest fields, where she gleans behind Boaz's reapers, lies at his feet at the threshing floor, and is redeemed by him at the gate by the custom of the shoe. Their son Obed fathers Jesse, father of David — the Moabite widow grafted into the messianic line, and (in Matthew) an ancestress of Christ.
summary.zh: 饑荒使伯利恆人以利米勒移居摩押，他和兩子相繼死去，留下拿俄米與摩押寡婦路得。路得的誓言——「你往哪裏去，我也往那裏去……你的神就是我的神」——帶她到伯利恆的禾場，跟在波阿斯的收割人後面拾取麥穗，夜宿打穀場伏其腳下，最後在城門口按脫鞋之例由他買贖成婚。其子俄備得生耶西，耶西生大衛——摩押寡婦嫁接進彌賽亞家譜，馬太福音中亦為基督先祖。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The grafted genealogy is the messianic-legend element.

passages.text: And Ruth said, Intreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following after thee: for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God: where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried: the LORD do so to me, and more also, if ought but death part thee and me. And she clave unto her. So they two went until they came to Bethlehem.
passages.zh: 路得說：「不要催我離開你，或轉回不跟隨你：因為你往哪裡去，我也往哪裡去；你在哪裡住宿，我也在哪裡住宿；你的民就是我的民，你的神就是我的神；你在哪裡死，我也在哪裡死，也葬在那裡。除非死能使你我相離，不然，願耶和華重重地降罰與我。」於是路得緊隨著她。二人同行，直到來到伯利恆。

passages.text: And Ruth the Moabitess said unto Naomi, Let me now go to the field, and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace. Then said Boaz unto Ruth, Hearest thou not, my daughter? Go not to glean in another field: all that thou hast done unto thy mother in law since the death of thine husband, and how thou hast left thy father and thy mother, and the land of thy nativity, and art come unto a people which thou knewest not heretofore, the LORD recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the LORD God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust.
passages.zh: 摩押女子路得對拿俄米說：「讓我現在往田間去，我在誰眼前蒙恩，就跟在誰身後拾取麥穗。」波阿斯對路得說：「我女兒啊，你沒有聽見嗎？不要往別人的田裡拾取麥穗。自從你丈夫死後，凡你向婆婆所行的，以及你怎樣離開父母和本地，來到素不認識的民中，這一切事，人全都告訴我了。願耶和華照你所行的賞賜你，你來投靠耶和華以色列神的翅膀下，願你滿得他的賞賜。」

passages.text: And she answered, I am Ruth thine handmaid: spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman. And he said, Fear not; I will do to thee all that thou requirest. So she lay at his feet until the morning. Now this was the manner in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing, for to confirm all things; a man plucked off his shoe, and gave it unto his neighbour: and this was a testimony in Israel. So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife. And she bare a son. And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it. And the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
passages.zh: 她回答說：「我是你的婢女路得：求你用你的衣襟遮蓋你的婢女，因為你是一個至近的親屬。」他說：「不要懼怕；凡你所要求的，我必為你行。」於是路得躺在他腳邊，直到早晨。從前在以色列中，關於贖業和交易的事，有這樣的規矩：為要定準一切的事，人便脫下鞋子，交給鄰舍：這在以色列中作為憑證。於是波阿斯娶了路得，路得就作了他的妻子。她生了一個兒子。拿俄米把孩子抱在懷中，作了他的養母。鄰舍的婦女給孩子起名說：「拿俄米得了一個兒子」；她們就給他起名叫俄備得：他是耶西的父親，耶西是大衛的父親。

title.en: Hannah's Prayer and the Loaned Son
title.zh: 哈拿的禱告與借出的兒子

region.en: Shrine of the LORD at Shiloh
region.zh: 示羅，耶和華的殿

period: 1 Samuel 1-2, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 9: 1 Samuel, chapters 1-2

summary.en: Barren and provoked by her rival, Hannah prays at Shiloh with moving lips and no voice until the old priest Eli takes her for drunk; her vow — a son given to the LORD all his days, no razor on his head — is granted, and Samuel is lent to the LORD 'as long as he liveth.' Her song, 'My heart rejoiceth in the LORD... he raiseth up the poor out of the dust,' becomes the Magnificat's model, echoed by Mary a millennium later.
summary.zh: 被對頭激怒的哈拿在示羅默默禱告，嘴唇微動卻無聲，以致老祭司以利誤以為她醉酒。她起誓：若得子，必終身獻與耶和華，不用剃刀剃其頭。神應允她，撒母耳就此「終身歸與耶和華」。她的頌歌——「我的心因耶和華快樂……祂從灰塵裏抬舉貧寒人」——千年後成為馬利亞《尊主頌》的範本。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The vowed-birth narrative; Hannah's song is the literary ancestor of the Magnificat (Luke 1), noted.

passages.text: And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the LORD, and wept sore. And she vowed a vow, and said, O LORD of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thine handmaid, but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.
passages.zh: 她心裡愁苦，就向耶和華禱告，痛哭不已。她許願說：「萬軍之耶和華啊，你若垂顧婢女的苦情，記念我，不忘記婢女，賜給婢女一個男孩，我必使他終身歸與耶和華，不用剃頭刀剃他的頭。」

passages.text: Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken. And Eli said unto her, How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee. And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD. Then Eli answered and said, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him.
passages.zh: 原來哈拿是在心裡說話；只有嘴唇在動，卻聽不見聲音：因此以利以為她喝醉了。以利對她說：「你要醉到幾時呢？你應該把酒戒了。」哈拿回答說：「我主啊，不是這樣，我是心裡愁苦的婦人：我沒有喝清酒濃酒，乃是在耶和華面前傾心吐意。」以利回答說：「你平平安安地回去吧：願以色列的神允准你向他所求的。」

passages.text: And Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the LORD, mine horn is exalted in the LORD: my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies; because I rejoice in thy salvation. The LORD killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. The LORD maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up. He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory. Wherefore it came to pass, when the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, that she bare a son, and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the LORD.
passages.zh: 哈拿禱告說：我的心因耶和華快樂；我的角因耶和華高舉。我的口向仇敵張開；我因耶和華的救恩歡欣。耶和華使人死，也使人活，使人下陰間，也使人往上升。耶和華使人貧窮，也使人富足，使人卑微，也使人高貴。他從灰塵裡抬舉貧寒人，從糞堆中提拔窮乏人，使他們與王子同坐，得著榮耀的座位。哈拿懷孕的日期滿了，就生了一個兒子，給他起名叫撒母耳，說：因為這是我從耶和華那裡求來的。

title.en: The Voice in the Night at Shiloh
title.zh: 示羅夜間的呼喚

region.en: Temple of the LORD, Shiloh
region.zh: 示羅，耶和華的殿

period: 1 Samuel 3, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 9: 1 Samuel, chapter 3

summary.en: When 'the word of the LORD was precious in those days; there was no open vision', a boy sleeping beside the ark hears his name called three times and runs each time to the old priest Eli, who at last divines the caller and coaches the answer: 'Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth.' The message is doom on Eli's house for his sons' abomination, which Samuel must speak with his face toward the ground — the first open vision, and the founding scene of prophecy in Israel.
summary.zh: 「當那些日子，耶和華的言語稀少，不常有異象」；睡在約櫃旁的童子三度聽見自己被呼喚，三度奔向老祭司以利，以利終於明白呼喚者是誰，教他回答：「請說，僕人敬聽。」信息是對以利家的審判——因其子行惡他未禁止——撒母耳必須臉伏於地說出。這是第一個公開的異象，也是以色列先知職的奠基場景。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The night-call is the founding prophecy scene; 'Speak, LORD' is the tradition's classic answer of obedience.

passages.text: And the child Samuel ministered unto the LORD before Eli. And the word of the LORD was precious in those days; there was no open vision. And it came to pass at that time, when Eli was laid down in his place, and his eyes began to wax dim, that he could not see; and ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was, and Samuel was laid down to sleep; that the LORD called Samuel: and he answered, Here am I. And he ran unto Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou calledst me. And he said, I called not; lie down again.
passages.zh: 童子撒母耳在以利面前事奉耶和華。當那些日子，耶和華的言語稀少，不常有默示。一日，以利睡臥在自己的地方，他的眼睛昏花，看不分明；神的燈在耶和華殿內約櫃那裡還沒有熄滅，撒母耳已經睡了；耶和華呼喚撒母耳。撒母耳回答說：我在這裡！就跑到以利那裡，說：你呼喚我，我在這裡。以利回答說：我沒有呼喚你，你去睡吧。

passages.text: And the LORD called Samuel again the third time. And he arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou didst call me. And Eli perceived that the LORD had called the child. Therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth. So Samuel went and lay down in his place. And the LORD came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.
passages.zh: 耶和華第三次呼喚撒母耳。撒母耳起來，到以利那裡，說：你呼喚我，我在這裡。以利才明白是耶和華呼喚童子。因此以利對撒母耳說：你仍去睡吧；若再呼喚你，你就說：耶和華啊，請說，僕人敬聽。撒母耳就去，仍睡在原處。耶和華又來站著，像前三次呼喚說：撒母耳啊！撒母耳啊！撒母耳回答說：請說，僕人敬聽。

passages.text: And the LORD said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house. And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him. And he said, It is the LORD: let him do what seemeth him good. And Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground.
passages.zh: 耶和華對撒母耳說：我在以色列中必行一件事，叫聽見的人都必耳鳴。到了那日，我必向以利家成就我所說的一切事。撒母耳就把一切話都告訴了以利，並沒有隱瞞。以利說：這是出於耶和華，願他憑自己的意旨而行。撒母耳漸漸長大，耶和華與他同在，使他所說的話一句都不落空。

title.en: David and Goliath
title.zh: 大衛與歌利亞

region.en: Valley of Elah
region.zh: 以拉谷

period: 1 Samuel 17, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 9: 1 Samuel, chapters 16-17

summary.en: The giant champion of Gath, six cubits and a span, brags across the valley for forty days until the youngest son of Jesse, sent with cheeses for his soldier brothers, hears the defiance: 'who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?' Refusing Saul's unproved armor, he takes five smooth stones from the brook and answers the giant's curse: 'Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear... but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts.' One sling-stone in the forehead fells Goliath, whom David beheads with his own sword — the young shepherd whose humility and faith in the anointing (1 Sam 16) mark him out for the throne.
summary.zh: 迦特巨人歌利亞身高六肘零一虎口，四十日隔谷叫陣。奉父命送乳酪給從軍兄長的耶西幼子大衛聽其挑戰，怒言「這未受割禮的非利士人是誰呢？竟敢向永生神的軍隊罵陣」。拒穿未經試驗的王甲，取五塊溪中光滑石子，答曰：「你來攻擊我，是靠著刀槍和銅戟；我來攻擊你，是靠著萬軍之耶和華的名。」一石中額，巨人撲倒；大衛以巨人之刀割其首——受膏的牧童自此嶄露頭角。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The underdog-versus-giant archetype of Western storytelling.

passages.text: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span. And he had an helmet of brass upon his head, and he was armed with a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of brass. And he stood and cried unto the armies of Israel, and said unto them, am not I a Philistine, and ye servants to Saul? choose you a man for you, and let him come down to me. And when Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.
passages.zh: 從非利士營中出來一個討戰的人，名叫歌利亞，是迦特人，身高六肘零一虎口；頭戴銅盔，身穿鎧甲，甲重五千舍客勒銅。他站立，向以色列的軍隊喊叫說：我不是非利士人嗎？你們不是掃羅的僕人嗎？可以從你們中間揀選一人，使他下到我這裡來。掃羅和以色列眾人聽見非利士人的這些話，就驚惶，極其害怕。

passages.text: And David said to Saul, Let no man's heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine. Thy servant kept his father's sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock: and I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth: thy servant slew both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God.
passages.zh: 大衛對掃羅說：人都不必因那非利士人膽怯；你的僕人要去與那非利士人戰鬥。你僕人為父親放羊，有時來了獅子，有時來了熊，從群中銜一隻羊羔去，我就追趕牠，擊打牠，將羊羔從牠口中救出來；你僕人曾打死獅子和熊；這未受割禮的非利士人向永生神的軍隊罵陣，也必像獅子和熊一般。

passages.text: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd's bag which he had, even in a scrip; and his sling was in his hand. And the Philistine said unto David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field. Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied. This day will the LORD deliver thee into mine hand.
passages.zh: 他手中拿著杖，又從溪中挑選了五塊光滑的石頭，放在他所帶的牧人袋裡，就是他的囊中；手中拿著甩石的機弦。那非利士人對大衛說：「你到我這裡來，我要把你的肉給空中的飛鳥和田野的走獸吃。」大衛對那非利士人說：「你來攻擊我，是靠著刀、槍和盾牌；但我來攻擊你，是靠著萬軍之耶和華的名，就是你所辱罵的以色列軍隊的神。今日耶和華必將你交在我手裡。」

passages.text: And it came to pass, when the Philistine arose, and came, and drew nigh to meet David, that David hastened, and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine. And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth. So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and smote the Philistine, and slew him; but there was no sword in the hand of David. Therefore David ran, and stood upon the Philistine, and took his sword, and drew it out of the sheath thereof, and slew him, and cut off his head therewith.
passages.zh: 那非利士人起身，前來迎著大衛走近的時候，大衛急忙迎著那非利士人，向著軍隊跑去。大衛把手伸入囊中，從那裡取出一塊石頭，用機弦甩去，打中那非利士人的額，石頭穿入他的額內；他就面伏於地。這樣，大衛用機弦和石頭勝了那非利士人，打中他，將他殺死；只是大衛手中沒有刀。因此大衛跑去，站在那非利士人身上，將他的刀從鞘中拔出，將他殺死，並用那刀割下他的頭。

title.en: David Spares the LORD's Anointed in the Cave
title.zh: 大衛洞中不殺耶和華的受膏者

region.en: Wilderness of Engedi, rocks of the wild goats
region.zh: 隱基底曠野，野羊磐石

period: 1 Samuel 24, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 9: 1 Samuel, chapter 24

summary.en: Hunting David with three thousand men, Saul enters a cave to relieve himself — the very cave where David and his men wait in the dark. His men beg him to strike: 'the day of which the LORD said unto thee, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand.' David cuts only the skirt of the king's robe, and even that smites his heart; when Saul emerges, David calls after him, bows to the earth, and holds up the cut cloth — 'the LORD forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the LORD's anointed.' Saul weeps aloud: 'Thou art more righteous than I.'
summary.zh: 掃羅率三千精兵追捕大衛至隱基底，進洞解手——正是大衛與隨從藏身的洞穴。部下催促：「耶和華曾應許將仇敵交在你手。」大衛只割下王的衣角，心中隨即自責；待掃羅出洞，大衛呼喊叩拜，高舉割下之布——「我的主乃是耶和華的受膏者，我萬不敢伸手害他」。掃羅放聲大哭：「你比我公義。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The spared-anointed scene defines the tradition's ethics of kingship and restraint.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when Saul was returned from following the Philistines, that it was told him, saying, Behold, David is in the wilderness of Engedi. Then Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and went to seek David and his men upon the rocks of the wild goats. And he came to the sheepcotes by the way, where was a cave; and Saul went in to cover his feet: and David and his men remained in the sides of the cave.
passages.zh: 掃羅追趕非利士人回來之後，有人告訴他說：「看哪，大衛在隱基底的曠野。」掃羅就從以色列眾人中挑選了三千精兵，率領他們往野山羊的磐石那裡去，尋索大衛和他的手下。他來到路旁的羊圈，那裡有一個洞；掃羅進去大解，大衛和他的手下正藏在洞的深處。

passages.text: And the men of David said unto him, Behold the day of which the LORD said unto thee, Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand, that thou mayest do to him as it shall seem good unto thee. Then David arose, and cut off the skirt of Saul's robe privily. And it came to pass afterward, that David's heart smote him, because he had cut off Saul's skirt. And he said unto his men, The LORD forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the LORD's anointed, to stretch forth mine hand against him, seeing he is the anointed of the LORD.
passages.zh: 大衛的手下對他說：「看哪，耶和華曾對你說：『看哪，我要將你的仇敵交在你手裡，你可以隨意待他。』」於是，大衛起來，暗暗地割下掃羅外袍的衣襟。隨後，大衛因為割下掃羅的衣襟，心中自責。他對手下說：「耶和華萬不容我這樣做，伸手害我的主，就是耶和華的受膏者，因為他是耶和華的受膏者。」

passages.text: David also arose afterward, and went out of the cave, and cried after Saul, saying, My lord the king. And when Saul looked behind him, David stooped with his face to the earth, and bowed himself. And David said to Saul, Behold, this day thine eyes have seen how that the LORD had delivered thee to day into mine hand in the cave: and some bade me kill thee: but mine eye spared thee; and I said, I will not put forth mine hand against my lord; for he is the LORD's anointed. Moreover, my father, see, yea, see the skirt of thy robe in my hand: for in that I cut off the skirt of thy robe, and killed thee not, know thou and see that there is neither evil nor transgression in mine hand.
passages.zh: 此後，大衛也起來，走出洞去，在掃羅後面呼叫說：「我主，我王！」掃羅回頭觀看，大衛就屈身，臉伏於地叩拜。大衛對掃羅說：「看哪，今日你親眼看見，耶和華在洞中將你交在我手裡；有人叫我殺你，我卻愛惜你，說：『我萬不敢伸手害我的主，因為他是耶和華的受膏者。』我父啊，請看，請看你外袍的衣襟在我手中：我割下你外袍的衣襟，卻沒有殺你，由此你可以知道、可以看見，我手中既沒有惡意，也沒有過犯。」

title.en: Thou Art the Man: David, Bathsheba, and Nathan's Lamb
title.zh: 你就是那人：大衛、拔示巴與拿單的羊羔

region.en: Roof of the king's house, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，王宮屋頂

period: 2 Samuel 11-12, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 10: 2 Samuel, chapters 11-12

summary.en: Staying home when kings go to war, David sees Bathsheba washing from his roof, takes her, and when she conceives has her husband Uriah the Hittite — who will not leave his army's tents even drunk — sent to the front to die under a letter he unknowingly carries. The prophet Nathan traps the king with the parable of the poor man's one ewe lamb devoured by the rich man; David's rage at the thief is met with the bluntest sentence in scripture: 'Thou art the man... the sword shall never depart from thine house.' David answers, 'I have sinned against the LORD.'
summary.zh: 列王出戰之時，大衛卻留在耶路撒冷；從屋頂看見沐浴的拔示巴，將她接來；她懷孕後，大衛設計害死忠於軍營的丈夫烏利亞——烏利亞竟親手帶著自己死刑的書信上戰場。先知拿單以富戶奪窮人唯一羊羔的比喻套住王；大衛怒斥該死之際，拿單直言：「你就是那人……刀劍必永不離開你的家。」大衛答：「我得罪耶和華了。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Nathan's parable is the model of prophetic indictment; the royal abuse of power is the transgression element.

passages.text: And it came to pass in an eveningtide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king's house: and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon. And David sent and enquired after the woman. And one said, Is not this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite? And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in unto him, and he lay with her. And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.
passages.zh: 到了傍晚，大衛從床上起來，在王宮的平頂上行走；從平頂上看見一個婦人在沐浴，那婦人容貌甚美。大衛打發人去打聽那婦人是誰。有人說：「這不是以連的女兒、赫人烏利亞的妻子拔示巴嗎？」大衛就打發使者去，將她接來；她來到他那裡，他就與她同寢。那婦人懷了孕，就打發人去告訴大衛說：「我懷了孕。」

passages.text: And it came to pass in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah. And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die. And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and the men of the armies of the children of Israel slew Uriah the Hittite also. So David sent and inquired after the woman. And David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and went in unto her, and lay with her: and she bare a son.
passages.zh: 到了早晨，大衛寫信給約押，託烏利亞親手送去。他在信中寫道：要把烏利亞派到戰事最激烈的前線，你們便從他身邊退後，使他被擊殺而死。城裡的人出來與約押交戰；以色列眾軍的士兵也殺了赫人烏利亞。於是，大衛差人去打聽那婦人的事。大衛安慰他的妻子拔示巴，進去與她同寢，她就生了一個兒子。

passages.text: And the LORD sent Nathan unto David. And he came unto him, and said unto him, There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor. The rich man had exceeding many flocks and herds: but the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own meat, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter. And David's anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, the man that hath done this thing shall surely die.
passages.zh: 耶和華差遣拿單去見大衛。拿單到了他那裡，對他說：有一座城裡有兩個人，一個富有，一個貧窮。那富人有極多的羊群牛群；那窮人除了買來養活的一隻小母羊羔之外，別無所有。這羊羔與他和他兒女一同長大；吃他桌上的食物，喝他杯中的水，躺在他懷裡，在他看來如同女兒一般。大衛就向那人大大發怒，對拿單說：做這事的人該死。

passages.text: And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul; and I gave thee thy master's house, and thy master's wives into thy bosom; wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the LORD, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife. Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house. And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD.
passages.zh: 拿單對大衛說：你就是那人。耶和華—以色列的神如此說：我膏你作以色列的王，救你脫離掃羅的手；又將你主人的家業賜給你，將你主人的妻妾交在你懷裡；你為何藐視耶和華的命令，行他眼中看為惡的事呢？你借刀殺了赫人烏利亞，又娶了他的妻為妻。所以，刀劍必永不離開你的家。大衛對拿單說：我得罪了耶和華。

title.en: Solomon's Dream: An Understanding Heart
title.zh: 所羅門之夢：求智慧的心

region.en: High place of Gibeon
region.zh: 基遍的邱壇

period: 1 Kings 3, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 11: 1 Kings, chapter 3

summary.en: Offering a thousand burnt offerings at Gibeon, the young king dreams that God says 'Ask what I shall give thee' — and asks not for long life, riches, or his enemies' lives, but 'an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad.' The speech pleases the LORD, who grants wisdom 'so that there was none like thee before thee' with riches and honour thrown in; the immediately following judgment between the two mothers and the living child makes the gift famous.
summary.zh: 少年王在基遍獻一千犧牲作燔祭，夢中神對他說：「你願我賜你甚麼？你可以求。」他不求長壽、不求富貴、不求滅絕仇敵，只求「能辨別是非的心，可以判斷你的民」。此話使主喜悅：賜他空前絕後的智慧，並附贈富貴尊榮。緊隨其後的兩母爭子、智斷活孩之案，使這恩賜名揚天下。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The dream-inquiry is the wisdom-kingship charter scene.

passages.text: In Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream by night: and God said, Ask what I shall give thee. And Solomon said, And now, O LORD my God, thou hast made thy servant king instead of David my father: and I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in. And thy servant is in the midst of thy people which thou hast chosen, a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude.
passages.zh: 在基遍，夜間夢中，耶和華向所羅門顯現；神說：你願我賜你什麼，你可以求。所羅門說：如今，耶和華—我的神啊，你使僕人接續我父親大衛作王，但我還只是個幼童，不知道該如何出入。僕人住在你所揀選的民中，這民眾多，多得不可勝數，也無法計算。

passages.text: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people? And the speech pleased the LORD, that Solomon had asked this thing. And God said unto him, Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies; but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern judgment; behold, I have done according to thy words: lo, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee. And I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour.
passages.zh: 所以求你賜僕人一顆明辨的心，可以判斷你的民，能辨別是非；不然，誰能判斷你這眾多的民呢？所羅門所求的這番話，蒙主喜悅。神對他說：因為你求這事，不為自己求長壽，不為自己求財富，也不求滅絕你仇敵的性命，只為自己求明辨的心，可以聽訟斷案；看哪，我照你的話而行：我賜你一顆智慧明辨的心，以致在你以前沒有像你的，在你以後也沒有像你的興起。你所沒有求的，我也賜給你，就是財富和尊榮。

title.en: The Queen of Sheba Tests Solomon
title.zh: 示巴女王考問所羅門

region.en: Solomon's court, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，所羅門宮廷

period: 1 Kings 10, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 11: 1 Kings, chapter 10

summary.en: Hearing Solomon's fame, the queen of Sheba comes with a great caravan of spices, gold, and precious stones 'to prove him with hard questions' — and 'Solomon told her all her questions: there was not any thing hid from the king.' Seeing his wisdom, table, ministers, and the ascent to the temple, 'there was no more spirit in her': 'behold, the half was not told me: thy wisdom and prosperity exceedeth the fame which I heard.' Jesus later names her one of the risen dead who will condemn that generation — 'a greater than Solomon is here.'
summary.zh: 示巴女王聞所羅門之名，攜香料、金子、寶石大隊而來，「要用難解的話試問所羅門」——「所羅門王將她所問的都答上了，沒有一句不明白、不能答的」。她見王的智慧、席上的珍饈、群臣的排場、上殿的臺階，便神不守舍：「我所聽見的還不及一半……你的智慧和你的福分越過我所聽見的風聲。」耶穌後來稱她將在審判時起來定那世代的罪——「看哪，在這裏有一人比所羅門更大」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition shared with Ethiopian royal legend (Menelek cycle) and Islam; the riddle-test is the divination element.

passages.text: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to prove him with hard questions.
