And she came to Jerusalem with a very great train, with camels that bare spices, and very much gold, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart. And Solomon told her all her questions: there was not any thing hid from the king, which he told her not.
passages.zh: 示巴女王聽見所羅門因耶和華之名而有的名聲，就來要用難解的問題考問他。她帶著極多的隨從來到耶路撒冷，又有駱駝馱著香料、極多的金子和寶石；她到了所羅門那裡，就把心裡所有的事都與他談論。所羅門將她所問的一切都回答了她；沒有一件事是王隱瞞不告訴她的。

passages.text: And when the queen of Sheba had seen all Solomon's wisdom, and the house that he had built, and the meat of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel, and his cupbearers, and his ascent by which he went up unto the house of the LORD; there was no more spirit in her. And she said to the king, It was a true report that I heard in mine own land of thy acts and of thy wisdom. Howbeit I believed not the words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it: and, behold, the half was not told me: thy wisdom and prosperity exceedeth the fame which I heard.
passages.zh: 示巴女王見所羅門一切的智慧，和他所建造的宮室，他席上的珍饈美味，群臣分列而坐，僕人兩旁侍立，以及他們的衣服裝飾，和酒政的服飾，又見他上耶和華殿的臺階，就詫異得神不守舍。對王說：我在本國裡所聽見論到你的事和你的智慧實在是真的。我先不信那些話，及至我來親眼見了，才知道人所告訴我的還不到一半。你的智慧和你的福分越過我所聽見的風聲。

passages.text: And she gave the king an hundred and twenty talents of gold, and of spices very great store, and precious stones: there came no more such abundance of spices as these which the queen of Sheba gave to king Solomon. And king Solomon gave unto the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked, beside that which Solomon gave her of his royal bounty.
passages.zh: 於是示巴女王將一百二十他連得金子和寶石，與極多的香料，送給所羅門王。她送給王的香料，以後奉來的不再有這樣多。所羅門王按示巴女王所帶來的，還她禮物，另外照她一切所要所求的，都送給她。

title.en: Elijah on Carmel: The God That Answereth by Fire
title.zh: 以利亞在迦密山：降火顯應的神

region.en: Mount Carmel
region.zh: 迦密山

period: 1 Kings 18, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 11: 1 Kings, chapter 18

summary.en: After three drought years, Elijah confronts Ahab — 'Art thou he that troubleth Israel?' — and the 450 prophets of Baal on Carmel in a public fire-contest: 'the God that answereth by fire, let him be God.' Baal's prophets shout, leap, and cut themselves till blood gushes while Elijah mocks — 'cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth.' Elijah's drenched altar, its trench filled three times over, is licked dry by the fire of the LORD; the people fall on their faces — 'The LORD, he is the God' — and the prophets of Baal are slain at the brook Kishon, with rain ending the drought.
summary.zh: 三年旱災後，以利亞在迦密山上與亞哈和四百五十名巴力先知公開比試：「降火顯應的神就是神。」巴力先知大聲求告、四圍踴躍、用刀槍自割直到流血，以利亞譏誚：「大聲求告吧！他是神，或默想，或走路，或睡覺，你們當叫醒他。」以利亞重修毀壞的壇，澆水三次淹滿溝渠；耶和華降火燒盡燔祭、木柴、石頭、塵土並溝裏的水。眾民俯伏在地：「耶和華是神！耶和華是神！」巴力先知被殺於基順河邊，天降大雨，旱災終結。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The fire-contest is the classic prophetic duel; the deaths of the Baal prophets are textual and presented without endorsement.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said unto him, Art thou he that troubleth Israel? And he answered, I have not troubled Israel; but thou, and thy father's house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of the LORD, and thou hast followed Baalim. And Elijah came unto all the people, and said, How long halt ye between two opinions? if the LORD be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.
passages.zh: 亞哈見了以利亞，便說：使以色列遭災的就是你嗎？以利亞回答說：使以色列遭災的不是我，乃是你和你父家；因為你們離棄耶和華的誡命，去隨從巴力。以利亞前來對眾民說：你們心持兩意要到幾時呢？若耶和華是神，就當順從耶和華；若巴力是神，就當順從巴力。眾民一言不答。

passages.text: And they took the bullock which was given them, and they dressed it first; for ye are many; and call on the name of your gods, but put no fire under. And they took the bullock which was given them, and they dressed it, and called on the name of Baal from morning even until noon, saying, O Baal, hear us. But there was no voice, nor any that answered. And they leaped upon the altar which was made. And it came to pass at noon, that Elijah mocked them, and said, Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth, and must be awaked. And they cried aloud, and cut themselves after their manner with knives and lancets, till the blood gushed out upon them.
passages.zh: 他們把所給他們的公牛犢預備好了，因為你們人數眾多，可以先挑選；當求告你們神的名，卻不要點火。他們把所給他們的公牛犢預備好了，就求告巴力的名，從早晨直到中午，說：巴力啊，求你應允我們！卻沒有聲音，沒有應允的。他們在所築的壇四圍踴跳。到了正午，以利亞嬉笑他們，說：大聲求告吧！因為他是神，他或默想，或走到一邊，或行路，或睡覺，你們當叫醒他。他們大聲求告，按著他們的規矩，用刀槍自割、自刺，直到身體流血。

passages.text: And Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, and with the stones he built an altar in the name of the LORD: and he made a trench about the altar, as great as would contain two measures of seed. And he said, Fill four barrels with water, and pour it on the burnt sacrifice, and on the wood. And it came to pass at the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice, that Elijah the prophet came near, and said, LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that thou art God in Israel. Then the fire of the LORD fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench. And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces: and they said, The LORD, he is the God; the LORD, he is the God.
passages.zh: 以利亞照著雅各子孫支派的數目，取了十二塊石頭，用這些石頭為耶和華的名築一座壇，在壇的四圍挖溝，可容穀種二細亞。又說：你們用四個桶盛滿水，倒在燔祭和柴上。到了獻晚祭的時候，先知以利亞近前來，說：亞伯拉罕、以撒、以色列的神，耶和華啊，求你今日使人知道你是以色列的神。於是，耶和華降下火來，燒盡燔祭、木柴、石頭、塵土，又燒乾溝裡的水。眾民看見了，就俯伏在地，說：耶和華是神！耶和華是神！

title.en: The Chariot of Fire: Elijah Taken Up
title.zh: 火戰車：以利亞升天

region.en: Jordan crossing, east of Jericho
region.zh: 約旦河渡口，耶利哥之東

period: 2 Kings 2, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 12: 2 Kings, chapter 2

summary.en: Elijah's last walk from Gilgal to Jericho and the Jordan — 'tarry here, I pray thee' answered three times by 'as the LORD liveth... I will not leave thee' — ends at the river where his rolled mantle strikes the waters apart. Across, he offers his successor whatever he asks; Elisha asks the impossible thing, 'a double portion of thy spirit', granted only if he sees the taking. 'Behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.' Elisha's cry — 'My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof!' — and the fallen mantle parting the river again seal the succession.
summary.zh: 以利亞末程自吉甲經伯特利、耶利哥至約旦河，三次說「你在這裏等候」，三次得答「我指著永生的耶和華起誓，必不離開你」。過河時捲起的外衣打水，水便左右分開。彼岸他讓繼任者隨意求；以利亞沙求那難求之事——「願感動你的靈加倍地感動我」。「忽然有火車火馬將二人隔開，以利亞就乘旋風升天去了。」以利亞沙呼喊：「我父啊！以色列的戰車馬兵啊！」拾起外衣打水，河又分開，傳承就此立定。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The whirlwind-taking is one of scripture's two bodily ascensions, echoed at the Transfiguration with Moses.

passages.text: And Elijah said unto Elisha, Tarry here, I pray thee; for the LORD hath sent me to Bethel. And Elisha said unto him, As the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. So they went down to Bethel. And Elijah said unto him, Elisha, tarry here, I pray thee; for the LORD hath sent me to Jericho. And he said, As the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. So they came to Jericho. And Elijah said unto him, Tarry, I pray thee, here; for the LORD hath sent me to Jordan. And he said, As the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. And they two went on.
passages.zh: 以利亞對以利沙說：耶和華差我往伯特利去，你可以在這裡等候。以利沙說：我指著永生的耶和華，又敢在你面前起誓，我必不離開你。於是二人下到伯特利。以利亞對以利沙說：耶和華差我往耶利哥去，你可以在這裡等候。以利沙說：我指著永生的耶和華，又敢在你面前起誓，我必不離開你。於是二人到了耶利哥。以利亞對以利沙說：耶和華差我往約但河去，你可以在這裡等候。以利沙說：我指著永生的耶和華，又敢在你面前起誓，我必不離開你。於是二人一同前往。

passages.text: And Elijah took his mantle, and wrapped it together, and smote the waters, and they were divided hither and thither, so that they two went over on dry ground. And it came to pass, when they were gone over, that Elijah said unto Elisha, Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken away from thee. And Elisha said, I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me. And he said, Thou hast asked a hard thing: nevertheless, if thou see me when I am taken from thee, it shall be so unto thee; but if not, it shall not be so.
passages.zh: 以利亞將自己的外衣捲起來，用以打水，水就左右分開，二人走乾地而過。他們過去之後，以利亞對以利沙說：「我未曾被接去離開你，你要我為你做甚麼，只管求我。」以利沙說：「願感動你的靈加倍地感動我。」以利亞說：「你所求的難得。雖然如此，我被接去離開你的時候，你若看見我，就必得著；不然，就得不著了。」

passages.text: And it came to pass, as they still went on, and talked, that, behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven. And Elisha saw it, and he cried, My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof. And he saw him no more: and he took hold of his own clothes, and rent them in two pieces. He took up also the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and went back, and stood by the bank of Jordan; and he took the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and smote the waters, and said, Where is the LORD God of Elijah? and when he also had smitten the waters, they parted hither and thither: and Elisha went over.
passages.zh: 他們正走著說話，忽有火車火馬將二人隔開，以利亞就乘旋風升天去了。以利沙看見，就呼叫說：「我父啊！我父啊！以色列的戰車馬兵啊！」以後不再見他了。於是以利沙把自己的衣服撕為兩片。他拾起以利亞身上掉下來的外衣，回去站在約旦河邊；他用以利亞身上掉下來的外衣打水，說：「耶和華以利亞的神在哪裡呢？」打水之後，水也左右分開，以利沙就過來了。

title.en: Naaman Washes in the Jordan
title.zh: 乃縵在約旦河沐浴

region.en: Samaria and the Jordan river
region.zh: 撒瑪利亞與約旦河

period: 2 Kings 5, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 12: 2 Kings, chapter 5

summary.en: A captive Israelite girl tells her Syrian mistress that the prophet in Samaria could heal the leprous general Naaman. Sent with ten talents of silver, Naaman is furious when Elisha will not even come out, sending only a word: 'Go and wash in Jordan seven times.' The proud commander — 'Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?' — is argued down by his servants, dips seven times, 'and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.' Jesus cites him: 'many lepers were in Israel... and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.'
summary.zh: 被擄的以色列小女子告訴主母：撒瑪利亞的先知必能醫治大將軍乃縵的大痲瘋。乃縵攜十他連得銀子前來，先知竟連面也不見，只遣人傳話：「去在約旦河中沐浴七回。」驕傲的元帥大怒——「大馬士革的河亞罷拿與法珥法豈不比以色列的一切水更好嗎？」——經僕人勸解，下河七次，「他的肉復原，好像小孩子的肉，他就潔淨了」。耶穌引此例：「以色列中有許多長大痲瘋的……內中除了敘利亞國的乃縵，沒有一個得潔淨的。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The sevenfold washing is the healing-rite element; the skin restoration tagged transformation.

passages.text: Now Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honourable, because by him the LORD had given deliverance unto Syria: he was also a mighty man in valour, but he was a leper. And the Syrians had gone out by companies, and had brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little maid; and she waited on Naaman's wife. And she said unto her mistress, Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy.
passages.zh: 亞蘭王的元帥乃縵在他主人面前為尊為大，因耶和華曾藉他使亞蘭人得勝；他又是大能的勇士，只是長了大痲瘋。先前亞蘭人成群地出去，從以色列國擄了一個小女子，這女子就服事乃縵的妻。她對主母說：「巴不得我主人去見撒瑪利亞的先知，必能治好他的大痲瘋。」

passages.text: So Naaman came with his horses and with his chariot, and stood at the door of the house of Elisha. And Elisha sent a messenger unto him, saying, Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean. But Naaman was wroth, and went away, and said, Behold, I thought, He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the LORD his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper. Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? may I not wash in them, and be clean?
passages.zh: 於是乃縵帶著車馬到了以利沙的家，站在門前。以利沙打發一個使者對他說：「你去在約旦河中沐浴七回，你的肉就必復原，而得潔淨。」乃縵卻發怒走了，說：「我想他必定出來見我，站著求告耶和華他神的名，在患處以上搖手，治好這大痲瘋。大馬色的河亞罷拿和法珥法豈不比以色列的一切水更好嗎？我在那裡沐浴不得潔淨嗎？」

passages.text: Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God: and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean. And he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him: and he said, Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel: now therefore, I pray thee, take a blessing of thy servant.
passages.zh: 於是乃縵下去，照著神人的話，在約旦河裡沐浴七回；他的肉復原，好像小孩子的肉，他就潔淨了。乃縵帶著一切跟隨他的人，回到神人那裡，站在他面前，說：「如今我知道，除了以色列之外，普天下沒有神。現在求你收點僕人的禮物。」

title.en: The Still Small Voice on Horeb
title.zh: 何烈山上的微小的聲音

region.en: Cave in Horeb, the mount of God
region.zh: 何烈山洞，神的山

period: 1 Kings 19, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 11: 1 Kings, chapter 19

summary.en: Fleeing Jezebel's death threat after Carmel, the burnt-out prophet lies under a juniper tree in the wilderness and asks to die; an angel twice feeds him for a forty-day walk to Horeb. There comes a great and strong wind that breaks the rocks — 'but the LORD was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the LORD was not in the earthquake: and after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.' The classic contrast of spectacle and whisper, re-read in the Gospels' quiet birth and stillness.
summary.zh: 迦密山得勝後，以利亞因耶洗別追殺而逃，在曠野羅騰樹下求死；天使兩次供餅，使他走了四十晝夜到何烈山。隨之有大風崩裂山巖——「耶和華卻不在風中；風後地震，耶和華卻不在其中；地震後有火，耶和華也不在火中；火後有微小的聲音。」這是壯觀與低語的經典對照，也常被讀入福音書中安靜降生的馬槽。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The still small voice is the tradition's classic corrective to spectacle-religion.

passages.text: But he himself went a day's journey into the wilderness, and came and sat down under a juniper tree: and he requested for himself that he might die; and said, It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers. And as he lay and slept under a juniper tree, behold, then an angel touched him, and said unto him, Arise and eat. And he looked, and, behold, there was a cake baken on the coals, and a cruse of water at his head; and he did eat and drink, and laid him down again. And the angel of the LORD came again the second time, and touched him, and said, Arise and eat; because the journey is too great for thee. And he arose, and did eat and drink, and went in the strength of that meat forty days and forty nights unto Horeb the mount of God.
passages.zh: 他自己在曠野走了一日的路程，來到一棵羅騰樹下，就坐在那裡求死，說：「耶和華啊，罷了！求你取我的性命，因為我不勝於我的列祖。」他就躺下睡了。忽有天使摸他，說：「起來吃吧！」他觀看，見頭旁有一瓶水與炭火燒的餅，他就吃了喝了，仍然躺下。耶和華的使者第二次來摸他，說：「起來吃吧！因為你當走的路甚遠。」他就起來吃了喝了，仗著這飲食的力量，走了四十晝夜，到了神的山，就是何烈山。

passages.text: And, behold, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the LORD; but the LORD was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the LORD was not in the earthquake: and after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice. And it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out, and stood in the entering in of the cave. And, behold, there came a voice unto him, and said, What doest thou here, Elijah?
passages.zh: 看哪，耶和華經過，有一陣大而強的風將山裂開，把耶和華面前的磐石打碎；但耶和華不在風中。風後有地震；但耶和華不在地震中。地震後有火；但耶和華不在火中。火後有微小的聲音。以利亞聽見，就用外衣蒙住臉，出去站在洞口。看哪，有聲音向他說：以利亞，你在這裡做什麼？

title.en: Nebuchadnezzar's Dream of the Great Image
title.zh: 尼布甲尼撒夢見大像

region.en: Palace of Babylon
region.zh: 巴比倫王宮

period: Daniel 2, c. 2nd century BCE, setting 6th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 27: Daniel, chapter 2

summary.en: The king demands that his wise men tell him a dream he has forgotten, on pain of being cut in pieces; Daniel, after prayer, rehearses the dream itself: a great image with head of gold, breast and arms of silver, belly and thighs of brass, legs of iron, feet of iron and clay, broken by a stone cut without hands that becomes a mountain filling the earth — the succession of empires and a kingdom that shall stand for ever, the West's classic vision of history's sequence.
summary.zh: 王忘記所夢，卻命術士講解，違者剁碎。但以理禱告後竟能重述其夢：大像頭是金的、胸臂是銀、肚腹腰是銅、腿是鐵、腳是半鐵半泥，被非人手鑿出來的石頭砸碎，石頭變成充滿天下的大山——歷代帝國的興替與一座永遠長存的國度，是西方史觀的經典意象。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Apocalyptic historiography; the empire-sequence is a founding typology of Western periodization.

passages.text: And in the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams, wherewith his spirit was troubled, and his sleep brake from him. And the king commanded to call the magicians, and the astrologers, and the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans. And the king said unto them, I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit was troubled to know the dream. The king answered and said to the Chaldeans, The thing is gone from me: if ye will not make known unto me the dream, with the interpretation thereof, ye shall be cut in pieces, and your houses shall be made a dunghill.
passages.zh: 尼布甲尼撒在位第二年，尼布甲尼撒做了夢，他的靈裡煩亂，睡意離他而去。王吩咐召來術士、占星家、行邪術的和迦勒底人。王對他們說：我做了一個夢，我心裡煩亂，要知道這夢的意思。王回答迦勒底人說：這事我已忘了；你們若不將夢和夢的講解告訴我，就必被砍成碎塊，你們的房屋必成為糞堆。

passages.text: Then Daniel went to his house, and made the thing known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions, that they would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret. Then was the secret revealed unto Daniel in a night vision. Then Daniel answered, Thou, O king, sawest, and behold a great image. This great image, whose brightness was excellent, stood before thee; and the form thereof was terrible. This image's head was of fine gold, his breast and his arms of silver, his belly and his thighs of brass, his legs of iron, his feet part of iron and part of clay.
passages.zh: 於是但以理回到自己家中，將這事告訴他的同伴哈拿尼雅、米沙利、亞撒利雅，要他們為這奧祕向天上的神求憐憫。於是這奧祕在夜間的異象中向但以理顯明。但以理回答說：王啊，你觀看，見有一個大像。這大像極其光耀，站在你面前；形狀甚是可怕。這像的頭是精金的，胸膛和膀臂是銀的，肚腹和腰是銅的，腿是鐵的，腳是半鐵半泥的。

passages.text: Thou sawest till that a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces together. Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken to pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors; and the wind carried them away, that no place was found for them: and the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth. This is the dream; and we will tell the interpretation thereof before the king.
passages.zh: 你觀看，見有一塊非人手鑿出來的石頭打在這像半鐵半泥的腳上，把腳砸碎。於是鐵、泥、銅、銀、金都一同砸碎，變成如夏天禾場上的糠秕；風把它們吹散，無處可尋。打碎這像的石頭變成一座大山，充滿全地。這就是那夢；我們要在王面前講解它的意思。

title.en: The Fiery Furnace of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego
title.zh: 沙得拉、米煞、亞伯尼歌的火窯

region.en: Plain of Dura, Babylon
region.zh: 巴比倫省杜拉平原

period: Daniel 3, c. 2nd century BCE, setting 6th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 27: Daniel, chapter 3

summary.en: At the dedication of a sixty-cubit golden image, all the nations fall down at the sound of cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and dulcimer — except three Jewish officers, who answer the king, 'our God whom we serve is able to deliver us... But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods.' Bound and cast into a furnace heated seven times hotter, they are seen unbound, walking in the fire with a fourth 'like the Son of God'; Nebuchadnezzar blesses their God, 'who hath sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him.'
summary.zh: 金像落成之日，萬民聞樂聲俱俯伏敬拜——唯三位猶太官員不肯，答王：「我們所事奉的神能將我們從烈火的窯中救出來……即或不然，王啊，你當知道我們決不事奉你的神。」被捆起來投入燒著七倍的窯中，王竟見四人於火中行走，未被捆綁，「那第四個的相貌好像神子」。王因此稱頌差遣使者救護倚靠祂之僕人的神。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The defiant three are among the tradition's archetypal martyrs of conscience.

passages.text: Then an herald cried aloud, To you it is commanded, O people, nations, and languages, that at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up: and whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.
passages.zh: 那時，傳令官大聲呼喊說：各方、各國、各族的人哪，有令傳與你們：你們一聽見角、笛、琵琶、琴、瑟、笙和各樣樂器的聲音，就當俯伏敬拜尼布甲尼撒王所立的金像；凡不俯伏敬拜的，必立時扔在烈火的窯中。

passages.text: Nebuchadnezzar spake and said unto them, Is it true, O Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, do not ye serve my gods, nor worship the golden image which I have set up? Now if ye be ready that at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the image which I have made; well: but if ye worship not, ye shall be cast the same hour into the midst of a burning fiery furnace; and who is that God that shall deliver you out of my hands? Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, answered and said to the king, O Nebuchadnezzar, we are not careful to answer thee in this matter. If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace: but if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
passages.zh: 尼布甲尼撒對他們說：沙得拉、米煞、亞伯尼歌，你們不事奉我的神，也不敬拜我所立的金像，是真的嗎？如今你們若準備好，一聽見角、笛、琵琶、琴、瑟、笙和各樣樂器的聲音，就俯伏敬拜我所造的像，那倒好；若不敬拜，必立時扔在烈火的窯中；有什麼神能救你們脫離我的手呢？沙得拉、米煞、亞伯尼歌回答王說：尼布甲尼撒啊，在這件事上我們不必回答你。即便如此，我們所事奉的神能將我們從烈火的窯中救出來；即或不然，王啊，你當知道，我們決不事奉你的神，也不敬拜你所立的金像。

passages.text: Then was Nebuchadnezzar full of fury, and commanded that they should heat the furnace one seven times more than it was wont to be heated. And these three men fell down bound into the midst of the burning fiery furnace. Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonied, and rose up in haste, and spake, and said unto his counsellors, Did not we cast three men bound into the midst of the fire? He answered and said, Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of God. Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the mouth of the burning fiery furnace, and spake, and said, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, ye servants of the most high God, come forth, and come hither. Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, came forth of the midst of the fire.
passages.zh: 當時尼布甲尼撒滿心忿怒，吩咐人把窯燒熱，比尋常更加七倍。這三個人被捆著，落在烈火的窯中。那時尼布甲尼撒王驚奇，急忙起來，對他的謀士說：「我們捆著扔在火裡的，豈不是三個人嗎？」他回答說：「看哪，我見有四個人，並沒有捆綁，在火中行走，也沒有受傷；那第四個的相貌好像神子。」於是尼布甲尼撒就近烈火窯門，說：「至高神的僕人沙得拉、米煞、亞伯尼歌，出來，上這裡來吧。」沙得拉、米煞、亞伯尼歌就從火中出來了。

title.en: Mene, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin: The Hand on the Wall
title.zh: 彌尼彌尼提克勒烏法珥新：牆上的手

region.en: Belshazzar's feast hall, Babylon
region.zh: 巴比倫，伯沙撒宴會廳

period: Daniel 5, c. 2nd century BCE, setting 6th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 27: Daniel, chapter 5

summary.en: Drinking from the looted temple vessels of Jerusalem and praising gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone, Belshazzar sees fingers of a man's hand write on the plaster: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN. None of the wise men can read it; Daniel, refusing the offered rewards, reads the doom — 'God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it... Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting... Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians.' That night the king is slain, and Darius the Median takes the kingdom — the classic image of judgment spelled at the height of the feast.
summary.zh: 伯沙撒用耶路撒冷聖殿中被擄的金銀器皿飲酒，讚美金銀銅鐵木石之神；忽然有人手的指頭在王宮粉牆上寫字。術士皆不能讀；但以理拒受賞賜，直讀讖語——「神已數算你國的年日到此完畢……你被秤在天平裏，顯出你的虧欠……你的國分裂，歸與瑪代人和波斯人」。當夜王被殺，瑪代人大利烏取國。歷代以來，「伯沙撒的筵席」即盛宴與審判並存的經典意象。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The mene-tekel judgment is a founding image of hubris-and-fall.

passages.text: Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and drank wine before the thousand. Belshazzar, whiles he tasted the wine, commanded to bring the golden and silver vessels which his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem; that the king, and his princes, his wives, and his concubines, might drink therein. They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone. In the same hour came forth fingers of a man's hand, and wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaister of the wall of the king's palace: and the king saw the part of the hand that wrote.
passages.zh: 伯沙撒王為他的一千大臣設擺盛筵，與這一千人對面飲酒。伯沙撒飲酒歡暢的時候，吩咐人將他父尼布甲尼撒從耶路撒冷殿中所掠的金銀器皿拿來，王與大臣、皇后、妃嬪好用這器皿飲酒。他們飲酒，讚美金、銀、銅、鐵、木、石所造的神。當時，忽有人的指頭顯出，在王宮與燈臺相對的粉牆上寫字。王看見寫字的指頭。

passages.text: Then was king Belshazzar greatly troubled, and his countenance was changed in him, and his lords were astonied. And Daniel answered and said before the king, Let thy gifts be to thyself, and give thy rewards to another; yet I will read the writing unto the king, and make known to him the interpretation. And this is the writing that was written, MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN. This is the interpretation of the thing: MENE; God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it. TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting. PERES; Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians.
passages.zh: 伯沙撒王就甚驚惶，臉色改變，他的大臣也都驚奇。但以理在王面前回答說：「你的贈品可以歸你自己，你的賞賜可以歸給別人；我卻要為王讀這文字，把講解告訴王。所寫的文字是：彌尼，彌尼，提客勒，烏法珥新。講解是這樣：彌尼，就是神已經數算你國的年日，到此完畢。提客勒，就是你被稱在天平裡，顯出你的虧欠。毗勒斯，就是你的國分裂，歸與瑪代人和波斯人。」

passages.text: Then commanded Belshazzar, and they clothed Daniel with scarlet, and put a chain of gold about his neck, and made a proclamation concerning him, that he should be the third ruler in the kingdom. In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain. And Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old.
passages.zh: 伯沙撒下令，人就把紫袍給但以理穿上，把金鍊給他戴在頸項上，又傳令使他在國中位列第三。當夜，迦勒底王伯沙撒被殺。瑪代人大利烏年六十二歲，取了迦勒底國。

title.en: Daniel in the Lions' Den
title.zh: 但以理在獅坑中

region.en: Lions' den, Babylon under Darius
region.zh: 巴比倫大利烏年間的獅坑

period: Daniel 6, c. 2nd century BCE, setting 6th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 27: Daniel, chapter 6

summary.en: Rivals who can find no fault in Daniel except 'concerning the law of his God' trick Darius into a thirty-day prayer ban — 'whosoever shall ask a petition of any God or man for thirty days, save of thee, O king, he shall be cast into the den of lions.' Knowing the decree is signed, Daniel goes home and prays as before, windows open toward Jerusalem, three times a day. The unchangeable law of the Medes and Persians costs him the den; the sealed stone, the king's sleepless night, and the morning cry 'is thy God, whom thou servest continually, able to deliver thee from the lions?' meet with 'My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths.'
summary.zh: 找不到但以理任何把柄的政敵，設計誘使大利烏簽發三十日禱告禁令——凡在王以外求告神或人的，必被扔進獅坑。但以理明知禁令已簽，仍回家照常一日三次禱告，窗戶開向耶路撒冷。按瑪代波斯不可更改之法，他被投入獅坑；封石、王徹夜禁食、清晨的呼喚「你所常事奉的神，祂必救你」——得答「我的神差遣使者封住獅子的口」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The lions' den is the archetype of faithful civil disobedience; the accusers' fate is textual, presented without endorsement.

passages.text: Then these presidents and princes assembled together to the king, and said thus unto him, King Darius, live for ever. All the presidents of the kingdom, the governors, and the princes, the counsellors, and the captains, have consulted together to establish a royal statute, and to make a firm decree, that whosoever shall ask a petition of any God or man for thirty days, save of thee, O king, he shall be cast into the den of lions. Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it be not changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not.
passages.zh: 那時，總長和總督紛紛聚集來見王，說：「願大利烏王萬歲！國中的總長、欽差、總督、謀士和巡撫彼此商議，要立一條堅定的禁令，三十日內，不拘何人，若在王以外，或向神或向人求什麼，就必扔在獅子坑中。王啊，現在求你立這禁令，加蓋玉璽，使禁令決不更改，照瑪代和波斯人的例，是不可更改的。」

passages.text: Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime. Then these men assembled, and found Daniel praying and making supplication before his God. Then answered they and said before the king, That Daniel, which is of the children of the captivity of Judah, regardeth not thee, O king, nor the decree that thou hast signed, but maketh his petition three times a day.
passages.zh: 但以理知道這禁令蓋了玉璽，就到自己家裡（他樓上的窗戶開向耶路撒冷），一日三次，雙膝跪在他神面前，禱告感謝，與素常一樣。那些人就紛紛聚集，見但以理在他神面前祈禱懇求。他們便進到王前，提王的禁令，說：「王啊，三十日內不拘何人，若在王以外，或向神或向人求什麼，必被扔在獅子坑中。王不是在這禁令上蓋了玉璽嗎？」王回答說：「實有這事，照瑪代和波斯人的例，是不可更改的。」他們對王說：「王啊，那被擄之猶大人中的但以理不理你，也不遵你蓋了玉璽的禁令，他竟一日三次祈禱。」

passages.text: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions. And a stone was brought, and laid upon the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that the purpose might not be changed concerning Daniel. Then the king went to his palace, and passed the night fasting: neither were instruments of musick brought before him: and his sleep went from him.
passages.zh: 於是王下令，人就把但以理帶來，扔在獅子坑中。有人搬石頭放在坑口，王用自己的璽和大臣的印封閉那坑，使懲辦但以理的事毫無更改。王就回宮去，終夜禁食，無人拿樂器到他面前，並且睡不著覺。

passages.text: Then the king arose very early in the morning, and went in haste unto the den of lions. And when he came to the den, he cried with a lamentable voice unto Daniel: and the king spake and said to Daniel, O Daniel, servant of the living God, is thy God, whom thou servest continually, able to deliver thee from the lions? Then said Daniel unto the king, O king, live for ever. My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.
passages.zh: 次日黎明，王就起來，急忙往獅子坑那裡去。臨近坑邊，哀聲呼叫但以理，對但以理說：「永生神的僕人但以理啊，你所常事奉的神能救你脫離獅子嗎？」但以理對王說：「願王萬歲！我的神差遣使者，封住獅子的口，叫獅子不傷我；因我在神面前無辜，我在王面前也沒有行過虧損的事。」但以理從坑裡被繫上來，身上毫無傷損，因為信靠他的神。

title.en: Esther: For Such a Time as This
title.zh: 以斯帖：為現今的機會

region.en: Royal court of Ahasuerus, Shushan
region.zh: 亞哈隨魯王宮，書珊城

period: Esther 3-8, c. 4th-2nd century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 17: Esther, chapters 3-8

summary.en: When Mordecai refuses to bow to Haman, the Agagite plots genocide by lot — 'they cast Pur, that is, the lot' — against all the Jews of the empire. Mordecai's message to the queen, who risks death to enter unbidden, frames the book's moral: 'who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?' Esther's two banquets turn the tables: the enemy is named, and Haman hangs on the very fifty-cubit gallows he built for Mordecai; the festival of Purim commemorates the reversal — the unhidden God working through hidden means.
summary.zh: 末底改不肯向哈曼跪拜，哈曼遂以擲籤（普珥）謀滅帝國全境的猶太人。末底改託人傳話給冒死違例進見的皇后——「焉知你得了王后的位分不是為現今的機會麼？」以斯帖設宴二次，當眾指認仇敵；哈曼終被掛在他為末底改所備的五十肘木架上。普珥節至今紀念這場反轉——那未提名的神藉隱藏的手段成就拯救。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition central to Judaism (Purim) and honored in Christianity; the genocidal plot is textual history of the story-world, not endorsement.

passages.text: And all the king's servants, that were in the king's gate, bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence. And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of wrath. And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had shewed him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus. In the first month, that is, the month Nisan, in the twelfth year of king Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, that is, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month, to the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar.
passages.zh: 在朝門的一切臣僕都跪拜哈曼，因為王如此吩咐；惟獨末底改不跪不拜。哈曼見末底改不跪不拜，他就怒氣填胸。他們已將末底改的本族告訴哈曼，他以為下手害末底改一人是小事，就要滅絕亞哈隨魯王通國所有的猶大人，就是末底改的本族。亞哈隨魯王十二年正月，就是尼散月，人在哈曼面前，按日日月月掣普珥，就是掣籤，要定何月何日為吉，擇定了十二月，就是亞達月。

passages.text: And Mordecai commanded to answer Esther, Think not with thyself that thou shalt escape in the king's house, more than all the Jews. For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy father's house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this? Then Esther bade them return Mordecai this answer, Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish.
passages.zh: 末底改託人回覆以斯帖說：「你莫想在王宮裡強過一切猶大人，得免這禍。此時你若閉口不言，猶大人必從別處得解脫，蒙拯救；你和你父家必致滅亡。焉知你得了王后的位分不是為現今的機會嗎？」以斯帖就吩咐人回報末底改說：「你當去招聚書珊城所有的猶大人，為我禁食三晝三夜，不吃不喝；我和我的宮女也要這樣禁食。然後我違例進去見王，我若死就死吧！」

passages.text: So the king and Haman came to banquet with Esther the queen. Then Esther the queen answered and said, If I have found favour in thy sight, O king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request: for we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. And the king Ahasuerus answered and said unto Esther the queen, Who is he, and where is he, that durst presume in his heart to do so? And Esther said, The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman. And Harbonah, one of the chamberlains, said before the king, Behold also, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman had made for Mordecai, who had spoken good for the king, standeth in the house of Haman. Then the king said, Hang him thereon. So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai.
passages.zh: 王帶著哈曼來赴王后以斯帖的筵席。王后以斯帖回答說：「我若在王眼前蒙恩，王若以為美，我所願的，是願王將我的性命賜給我；我所求的，是求王將我的本族賜給我。因我和我的本族被賣了，要剪除殺戮滅絕我們。亞哈隨魯王問王后以斯帖說：「擅敢起意如此行的是誰？這人在哪裡呢？」以斯帖說：「仇人敵人就是這惡人哈曼！」哈曼在王和王后面前就甚驚惶。王便大怒，起來離開酒席往御園去了。哈曼見王定意要加罪與他，就起來，求王后以斯帖救命。王從御園回到酒席之處，見哈曼伏在以斯帖所靠的榻上；王說：「他竟在皇宮內、在我面前凌辱王后嗎？」這話一出王口，人就蒙了哈曼的臉。有一個伺候王名叫哈波拿的太監說：「哈曼為那救王有功的末底改做了五丈高的木架，現今立在哈曼家裡。」王說：「把哈曼掛在其上。」於是人將哈曼掛在他為末底改所預備的木架上。

title.en: Job: The Wager, the Whirlwind, and Restoration
title.zh: 約伯：賭注、旋風與復得

region.en: Land of Uz (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 烏斯地（象徵性定位）

period: Book of Job, c. 6th-4th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 18: Job, chapters 1-2 and 38-42

summary.en: 'Doth Job fear God for nought?' — in the heavenly court the Satan wagers that the righteous man will curse God if the hedge is stripped; in one day Job loses oxen, sheep, camels, servants, and all ten children, and answers, 'the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.' From his ash-heap of boils he argues with three friends until God answers out of the whirlwind with the wild, unanswerable catalogue of creation — 'Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth?' Job repents in dust; his fortunes are doubled, and 'in all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly' stands as the tradition's classic problem of suffering and disinterested piety.
summary.zh: 「約伯敬畏神，豈是無故呢？」——天庭之上，撒但與神立賭：若挪去四圍的籬笆，義人必當面棄掉神。一日之間，約伯失去牛羊駱駝僕婢與十個兒女，卻回答：「賞賜的是耶和華，收取的也是耶和華；耶和華的名是應當稱頌的。」坐在爐灰中以瓦片刮身，他與三友辯論不止，直至神從旋風中以創造萬物的無可抗辯詰問作答——「我立大地根基的時候，你在哪裏呢？」約伯在塵土中懊悔；末後的恩典加倍，苦難與無故敬虔之謎自此長懸於傳統之中。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition shared with Judaism and Christianity; the wager frames the problem of theodicy.

passages.text: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came also among them. And the LORD said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it. And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil? Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, Doth Job fear God for nought? But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face. And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.
passages.zh: 有一天，神的眾子來侍立在耶和華面前，撒但也來在其中。耶和華問撒但說：「你從哪裡來？」撒但回答耶和華說：「我從地上走來走去，往返而來。」耶和華問撒但說：「你曾用心察看我的僕人約伯沒有？地上再沒有人像他完全正直，敬畏神，遠離惡事。」撒但回答耶和華說：「約伯敬畏神，豈是無故呢？你且伸手毀他一切所有的，他必當面棄掉你。」耶和華對撒但說：「凡他所有的都在你手中；只是不可伸手加害於他。」

passages.text: And there was a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house: and there came a messenger unto Job, and said, The Sabeans fell upon them, and have slain the servants with the edge of the sword. While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep. While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Chaldeans made out three bands, and fell upon the camels. While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house: and, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee. Then Job arose, and rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped, and said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.
passages.zh: 有一天，他的兒女正在他們長兄的家裡吃飯喝酒，就有報信的來見約伯，說：「示巴人忽然闖來，用刀殺了僕人。」他還在說話的時候，又有人來說：「神的火從天上降下，把羊群燒滅了。」他還在說話的時候，又有人來說：「迦勒底人分作三隊，忽然闖來，襲擊駱駝。」他還在說話的時候，又有人來說：「你的兒女正在他們長兄的家裡吃飯喝酒，不料，有狂風從曠野颳來，擊打房屋的四角，房屋倒塌在少年人身上，他們就都死了；惟有我一人逃脫，來報信給你。」約伯便起來，撕裂外袍，剃了頭，伏在地上下拜，說：「我赤身出於母胎，也必赤身歸回；賞賜的是耶和華，收取的也是耶和華；耶和華的名是應當稱頌的。」

passages.text: So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown. And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself withal; and he sat down among the ashes. Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die. But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.
passages.zh: 於是撒但從耶和華面前退去，擊打約伯，使他從腳掌到頭頂長滿毒瘡。約伯就拿一塊瓦片刮自己的身體，坐在灰燼之中。他的妻子對他說：「你仍然持守你的純正嗎？你咒詛神，死了吧！」約伯卻對她說：「你說話像愚頑的婦人一樣。難道我們從神手裡得福，不也受禍嗎？」在這一切事上，約伯並沒有以嘴唇犯罪。

passages.text: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said, Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge? Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me. Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding. Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it? And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before. So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than the beginning.
passages.zh: 於是耶和華從旋風中回答約伯，說：「誰用無知的言語使我的旨意暗昧不明？你要如勇士束腰；我問你，你可以回答我。我立大地根基的時候，你在哪裡呢？你若明白，只管說吧。你若知道，是誰定地的尺度？是誰把準繩拉在其上？」約伯為他的朋友祈禱的時候，耶和華就使約伯從苦境轉回，並且耶和華賜給他的，比他從前所有的加倍。這樣，耶和華後來賜福給約伯，比先前更多。

title.en: Jonah, the Great Fish, and Nineveh's Repentance
title.zh: 約拿、大魚與尼尼微悔改

region.en: Joppa, the sea, and Nineveh on the Tigris
region.zh: 約帕、大海與底格里斯河畔的尼尼微

period: Book of Jonah, c. 5th-4th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 32: Jonah

summary.en: Commanded to preach against wicked Nineveh, Jonah flees by ship to Tarshish; a great tempest, a lot that falls on him, and his own surrender — 'take me up, and cast me forth into the sea' — end with the mariners fearing the LORD and the prophet swallowed three days and nights by a great fish, praying 'out of the belly of hell cried I'. Vomited onto dry land, he preaches through Nineveh, the whole city from king to cattle repents in sackcloth — and Jonah sulks under his gourd, angry that God relents: 'Thou hast had pity on the gourd... and should not I spare Nineveh, that great city?' Jesus takes him as the sign of his own death and resurrection: 'as Jonah was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.'
summary.zh: 奉命斥責尼尼微的約拿卻搭船逃往他施；狂風大作，掣籤落在約拿身上，他自願被拋入海——水手們因而敬畏耶和華；先知被大魚吞下三日三夜，從「陰間的深處」禱告。吐在旱地後，他穿城宣告，全城從王到牲畜披麻悔改——而約拿卻在蓖麻樹下發怒，怨神憐惜尼尼微。耶穌以約拿自比：「約拿三日三夜在大魚肚腹中，人子也要這樣三日三夜在地裏頭。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition shared with Judaism, Christianity and Islam. The fish-swallowing is among the most contested literal/figurative texts; both readings coexist.

passages.text: Now the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying, Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me. But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD, and went down to Joppa; and he found a ship going to Tarshish: so he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it. But the LORD sent out a great wind into the sea, and there was a mighty tempest in the sea, so that the ship was like to be broken. And they said every one to his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.
passages.zh: 耶和華的話臨到亞米太的兒子約拿，說：「你起來，往尼尼微大城去，向其中的居民呼喊，因為他們的惡達到我面前。」約拿卻起來，要逃往他施去躲避耶和華，下到約帕；他遇見一隻船要往他施去，就付了船價，下到船裡。然而耶和華使海中起大風，海就狂風大作，甚至船幾乎破壞。船上的人彼此說：「來吧，我們掣籤，看看這災臨到我們是因誰的緣故。」於是他們掣籤，籤落在約拿身上。

passages.text: And he said unto them, I am an Hebrew; and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, which hath made the sea and the dry land. Then said they unto him, What shall we do unto thee, that the sea may be calm unto us? And he said unto them, Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you. So they took up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea: and the sea ceased from her raging. Then the men feared the LORD exceedingly, and offered a sacrifice unto the LORD, and made vows. Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
passages.zh: 他對他們說：「我是希伯來人；我敬畏耶和華，那創造滄海旱地之天上的神。」他們就對他說：「我們當向你怎樣行，才能使海浪平靜呢？」他對他們說：「你們將我抬起來，拋在海中，海就平靜了；我知道你們遭遇這大風暴，是因我的緣故。」於是他們將約拿抬起，拋在海中，海的狂浪就平息了。那些人便大大敬畏耶和華，向耶和華獻祭，並且許願。耶和華安排了一條大魚吞了約拿。約拿在魚腹中三日三夜。

passages.text: Then Jonah prayed unto the LORD his God out of the fish's belly, and said, I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the LORD, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice. For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me. And the LORD spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.
passages.zh: 約拿在魚腹中禱告耶和華他的神，說：「我遭遇患難求告耶和華，你就應允我；從陰間的深處呼求，你就俯聽我的聲音。你將我投下深淵，就是海的深處；大水環繞我，你的波浪洪濤都漫過我身。」耶和華吩咐魚，魚就把約拿吐在旱地上。

passages.text: And Jonah began to enter into the city a day's journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown. So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them. For word came unto the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and he covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes. And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not. Then said the LORD, Thou hast had pity on the gourd, for the which thou hast not laboured... and should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons?
passages.zh: 約拿進城，走了一日的路程，宣告說：「再過四十日，尼尼微必傾覆了。」尼尼微人便信服神，宣告禁食，從最大的到最小的都穿上麻衣。這消息傳到尼尼微王那裡，他就從寶座上起來，脫下朝服，披上麻布，坐在灰中。神察看他們的行為，見他們離開惡道，神就後悔，不把所說的災禍降與他們。耶和華說：「這蓖麻，你尚且愛惜，你並沒有為它勞苦……我豈能不愛惜尼尼微這大城呢？其中不能分辨左手右手的有十二萬多人。」

title.en: Isaiah's Call: Holy, Holy, Holy
title.zh: 以賽亞蒙召：聖哉聖哉聖哉

region.en: Temple vision, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，聖殿異象

period: Isaiah 6, c. 8th century BCE, written c. 8th-6th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 23: Isaiah, chapter 6

summary.en: In the year king Uzziah died, Isaiah sees the LORD on a high throne, the temple's posts shaking, smoke filling the house, and six-winged seraphim crying to one another: 'Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.' Undone by unclean lips, he is purged with a live coal from the altar and volunteers for the hardest commission in scripture — to preach until hearts are fat and ears heavy. This thrice-holy has entered the Christian liturgy as the Sanctus, sung at every Eucharist.
summary.zh: 烏西雅王駕崩那年，以賽亞得見主坐在高高的寶座上，殿門檻震動，煙雲充滿殿宇，六翼撒拉弗彼此呼喊：「聖哉！聖哉！聖哉！萬軍之耶和華，祂的榮光充滿全地。」他自覺嘴唇不潔，被壇上的紅炭沾口得潔淨，隨即受命傳講最艱難的信息——直到百姓心蒙脂油、耳朵發沉。這三重聖哉進入基督教禮儀成為《聖哉經》，每主日聖餐中傳唱。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The temple vision is the charter of prophetic calling; the Sanctus adoption is noted.

passages.text: In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the LORD sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple. Above it stood the seraphims: each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly. And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory. And the posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke.
passages.zh: 當烏西雅王崩的那年，我見主坐在高高的寶座上，他的衣裳垂下，遮滿聖殿。其上有撒拉弗侍立，各有六個翅膀：用兩個翅膀遮臉，兩個翅膀遮腳，兩個翅膀飛翔。彼此呼喊說：「聖哉！聖哉！聖哉！萬軍之耶和華，他的榮光充滿全地。」因呼喊者的聲音，門檻的根基震動，殿裡充滿了煙雲。

passages.text: Then said I, Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts. Then flew one of the seraphims unto me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar: and he laid it upon my mouth, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged. Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.
passages.zh: 那時我說：「禍哉！我滅亡了！因為我是嘴唇不潔的人，又住在嘴唇不潔的民中，又因我眼見大君王萬軍之耶和華。」有一撒拉弗飛到我面前，手裡拿著紅炭，是用火剪從壇上取下來的，將炭沾我的口，說：「看哪，這炭沾了你的嘴，你的罪孽便除掉，你的罪惡就赦免了。」我又聽見主的聲音說：「我可以差遣誰呢？誰肯為我們去呢？」我說：「我在這裡，請差遣我。」

title.en: Ezekiel's Whirlwind: Wheels Within Wheels
title.zh: 以西結的旋風：輪中套輪

region.en: River Chebar, Babylonian captivity
region.zh: 迦巴魯河邊，巴比倫被擄之地

period: Ezekiel 1, c. 6th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 26: Ezekiel, chapter 1

summary.en: By the river Chebar among the exiles, the heavens open on the priest Ezekiel: a whirlwind from the north, a fire infolding itself, four living creatures with four faces each — man, lion, ox, eagle — and beside them wheels 'as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel', full of eyes, moving straight forward wherever the spirit would go. Above the firmament, the likeness of a throne, 'as the appearance of a sapphire stone', and upon it the likeness of the glory of the LORD — the vision that carried the divine presence into exile and became the West's most imaged heaven-scape (and, in the Book of Revelation, the four living creatures again).
summary.zh: 被擄之地迦巴魯河邊，天向祭司以西結開了：北方颳來旋風，火中攙著光輝；四活物各有四臉——人、獅、牛、鷹——旁有「輪中套輪」的輪子，滿圈有眼，靈往哪裏去就直行。穹蒼之上彷彿藍寶石寶座，其上有耶和華榮耀的形像——神的同在由此被帶入被擄之地，也成為西方天界圖像的源頭（啟示錄中的四活物再現此景）。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The chariot-vision (merkabah) is restricted from esoteric study in some Jewish circles; presented here as public-domain text.

passages.text: Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I was among the captives by the river of Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God. And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire.
passages.zh: 三十年四月初五日，我在迦巴魯河邊被擄的人中，天就開了，得見神的異象。我觀看，見狂風從北方颳來，隨著有一朵包括閃爍火的大雲，周圍有光輝，從其中的火內發出好像光耀的精金。

passages.text: Also out of the midst thereof came the likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance; they had the likeness of a man. And every one had four faces, and every one had four wings. As for the likeness of their faces, they four had the face of a man, and the face of a lion, on the right side: and they four had the face of an ox on the left side; they four also had the face of an eagle. And their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot.
passages.zh: 又從其中顯出四個活物的形像來。他們的形狀是這樣：有人的形像，各有四個臉面，四個翅膀。至於臉的形像：右邊各有人的臉，左邊各有牛的臉，又各有鷹的臉。他們的腿是直的，腳掌好像牛犢之蹄。

passages.text: The appearance of the wheels and their work was like unto the colour of a beryl: and they four had one likeness; and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel. And their rings were full of eyes round about them four. And when the living creatures went, the wheels went by them: and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up. And above the firmament that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone: and upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD.
passages.zh: 輪的形狀和顏色好像水蒼玉。四輪都是一個樣式，形狀和作法好像輪中套輪。輪輞周圍滿有眼睛。活物行走，輪也在旁邊行走；活物從地上升，輪也都上升。在他們頭以上的穹蒼之上，有寶座的形像，彷彿藍寶石；在寶座形像以上，有彷彿人的形狀坐在其上。這就是耶和華榮耀的形像。

title.en: The Valley of Dry Bones
title.zh: 枯骨谷異象

region.en: Open valley in the spirit-vision
region.zh: 靈異象中的平原

period: Ezekiel 37, c. 6th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 26: Ezekiel, chapter 37

summary.en: Carried in the spirit to a valley strewn with very dry bones, Ezekiel is asked the impossible question — 'Son of man, can these bones live?' — and answers with faith's hedge: 'O Lord GOD, thou knowest.' At his prophesying, bone comes to bone, sinews and flesh and skin cover them, and breath enters the slain: 'an exceeding great army.' The vision is interpreted in the text as Israel's restoration from exile, and in Christian reading as the general resurrection — spiritual death and revival made anatomical.
summary.zh: 靈帶以西結到滿是極其枯乾骸骨的平原，神問：「人子啊，這些骸骨能復活嗎？」他答以信心的界線：「主耶和華啊，你是知道的。」他一發預言，骨與骨便互相聯絡，有筋有肉有皮遮蔽，氣息進入被殺之人——「成了極大的軍隊」。經文明言這是以色列從被擄歸回的異象；基督教讀之為普遍復活的預表——屬靈的死而復甦以解剖之形呈現。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The resurrection tag is the traditional Christian reading; the text's own reading is national restoration, noted.

passages.text: The hand of the LORD was upon me, and carried me out in the spirit of the LORD, and set me down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones, and caused me to pass by them round about: and, behold, there were very many in the open valley; and, lo, they were very dry. And he said unto me, Son of man, can these bones live? And I answered, O Lord GOD, thou knowest.
passages.zh: 耶和華的手按在我身上，耶和華的靈將我帶出去，將我放在遍滿骸骨的山谷中，又使我從骸骨的四圍經過。看哪，在平原的骸骨極其眾多，而且極其枯乾。他對我說：「人子啊，這些骸骨能復活嗎？」我回答說：「主耶和華啊，你知道。」

passages.text: Again he said unto me, Prophesy upon these bones, and say unto them, O ye dry bones, hear the word of the LORD. Thus saith the Lord GOD unto these bones; Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and ye shall live: and I will lay sinews upon you, and will bring up flesh upon you, and cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and ye shall live. So I prophesied as I was commanded: and as I prophesied, there was a noise, and behold a shaking, and the bones came together, bone to his bone. And when I beheld, lo, the sinews and the flesh came up upon them, and the skin covered them above.
passages.zh: 他又對我說：「你要向這些骸骨說預言，對它們說：『枯乾的骸骨啊，要聽耶和華的話。』主耶和華對這些骸骨如此說：『看哪，我必使氣息進入你們裡面，你們就要活了。我必給你們加上筋，使肉長在其上，又用皮包裹你們，將氣息放在你們裡面，你們就要活了。』」於是我遵命說預言；正說預言的時候，有響聲，看哪，有震動，骸骨便彼此連結，骨與骨相接。我觀看的時候，看哪，筋和肉長在其上，皮也包裹在上面。

passages.text: Then he said unto me, Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel: behold, they say, Our bones are dried, and our hope is lost: we are cut off for our parts. Therefore prophesy and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, and bring you into the land of Israel. And ye shall know that I am the LORD, when I have opened your graves, O my people, and brought you up out of your graves, and shall put my spirit in you, and ye shall live.
passages.zh: 他對我說：「人子啊，這些骸骨就是以色列全家。看哪，他們說：『我們的骸骨枯乾了，我們的指望失去了，我們滅絕淨盡了。』所以你要說預言，對他們說：『主耶和華如此說：看哪，我的民哪，我必開你們的墳墓，使你們從墳墓中出來，領你們進入以色列地。我的民哪，當我開你們的墳墓，使你們從墳墓中出來的時候，你們就知道我是耶和華。我必將我的靈放在你們裡面，你們就要活了。』」

title.en: The Potter and the Clay
title.zh: 窯匠與泥土

region.en: Potter's gate, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，窯匠的門口

period: Jeremiah 18, c. 7th-6th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 24: Jeremiah, chapter 18

summary.en: Sent down to watch a potter working at the wheel, Jeremiah sees a marred vessel remade 'another vessel, as seemed good to the potter' — and hears the lesson: 'Behold, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel.' The oracle underwrites the tradition's deepest debate on fate: at what instant God speaks to pull down a nation, if it turns from evil He relents; if the planted nation does evil, He reconsiders. Paul builds Romans 9 on the potter's freedom.
summary.zh: 耶利米奉命下到窯匠家中，見他在輪上作器皿；器皿壞了，他就另作別的器皿，「看怎樣好，就怎樣作」——信息隨之而來：「以色列家啊，泥在窯匠的手中怎樣，你們在我的手中也怎樣。」此諭開出傳統中關於預定最深的辯論：神何時說要拔出拆毀，若那國轉離其惡，祂必後悔不降災禍。保羅在羅馬書九章正以窯匠的自由立論。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The potter-clay simile is a shared image with Mesopotamian (Enki/Ninhursag) and other clay-humans clusters; tagged accordingly.

passages.text: The word which came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying, Arise, and go down to the potter's house, and there I will cause thee to hear my words. Then I went down to the potter's house, and, behold, he wrought a work on the wheels. And the vessel that he made of clay was marred in the hand of the potter: so he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.
passages.zh: 耶和華的話臨到耶利米說：「你起來，下到窯匠的家裡去，我在那裡要使你聽我的話。」我就下到窯匠的家裡去，看哪，他正在輪上做器皿。窯匠用泥做的器皿在他手中壞了，他就照著自己看為好的，又用這泥另做了一個器皿。

passages.text: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, O house of Israel, cannot I do with you as this potter? saith the LORD. Behold, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel. At what instant I shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up, and to pull down, and to destroy it; if that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.
passages.zh: 耶和華的話又臨到我說：「以色列家啊，我豈不能像這窯匠待你們一樣嗎？耶和華說：看哪，泥在窯匠手中怎樣，你們在我手中也怎樣，以色列家啊。我論到一邦或一國說，要拔出、拆毀、毀壞；我所論到的這邦若轉離他們的惡，我就後悔，不將我本想降與他們的災禍降與他們。

title.en: The Annunciation and the Magnificat
title.zh: 天使報喜與尊主頌

region.en: Nazareth, Galilee
region.zh: 加利利，拿撒勒

period: Gospel of Luke, c. 80-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 1

summary.en: Gabriel, sent from God, greets the virgin Mary of Nazareth — 'Hail, thou that art highly favoured' — and announces a son who will sit on David's throne with a kingdom without end. To her question, 'How shall this be?' the angel answers with the Holy Ghost coming upon her, and Mary consents: 'Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.' Visiting Elisabeth she bursts into the Magnificat, 'My soul doth magnify the Lord', modeled on Hannah's song — the charter scene of the gospel's infancy cycle.
summary.zh: 加百列奉差往拿撒勒向童女馬利亞問安——「蒙大恩的女子」——宣告她的兒子要坐大衛的寶座，國無窮盡。她問「我沒有出嫁，怎麼有這事呢？」天使答以聖靈臨到她身上；馬利亞便順服：「我是主的使女，情願照你的話成就在我身上。」探望伊利莎白之際，她唱出《尊主頌》——「我心尊主為大」——本於哈拿之歌，成為福音嬰孩敘事的基石。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of the highest sensitivity (annunciation of the virgin birth). Presented as a comparative miraculous-birth narrative — scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: And in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth, to a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary. And the angel came in unto her, and said, Hail, thou that art highly favoured, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women. And the angel said unto her, Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favour with God. And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS. He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David: and he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end.
passages.zh: 到了第六個月，天使加百列奉神差遣，往加利利的一座城去，這城名叫拿撒勒，到一個童女那裡，她已經許配給大衛家的一個人，名叫約瑟；童女的名字叫馬利亞。天使進去，對她說：「蒙大恩的女子，願你平安！主與你同在，你在婦女中是有福的。」天使對她說：「馬利亞，不要害怕，因為你在神面前已經蒙恩了。看哪，你要懷孕生子，要給他起名叫耶穌。他要為大，稱為至高者的兒子；主神要把他祖大衛的寶座賜給他；他要作雅各家的王，直到永遠；他的國也沒有窮盡。」

passages.text: Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God. For with God nothing shall be impossible. And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. And the angel departed from her.
passages.zh: 馬利亞對天使說：「我還沒有出嫁，怎麼會有這事呢？」天使回答說：「聖靈要臨到你身上，至高者的能力要蔭庇你；因此，所要生的聖者必稱為神的兒子。因為在神沒有不可能的事。」馬利亞說：「看哪，我是主的婢女；情願照你的話成就在我身上。」於是天使就離開她去了。

passages.text: And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. For he hath regarded the low estate of his handmaiden: for, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. He hath shewed strength with his arm; he hath scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts. He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree. He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away.
passages.zh: 馬利亞說：「我的靈魂尊主為大，我的靈以神我的救主為樂。因為他顧念他婢女的卑微；看哪，從今以後，萬代都要稱我有福。他用膀臂施展大能；他驅散那心中妄想的驕傲人。他叫有權柄的失位，叫卑賤的升高。他叫飢餓的得飽美食；叫富足的空手回去。

title.en: The Birth of John the Baptist
title.zh: 施洗約翰的誕生

region.en: Temple and hill country of Judaea
region.zh: 聖殿與猶太山地

period: Gospel of Luke, c. 80-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 1

summary.en: The priest Zacharias, burning incense in the temple, is told by Gabriel that his aged wife Elisabeth will bear a son filled with the Holy Ghost from the womb, who will go before the Lord 'in the spirit and power of Elias.' Doubting, Zacharias is struck dumb until the day of fulfillment; when the child is born and the relatives expect him to be called Zacharias, the father writes on a table: 'His name is John' — and his mouth is opened, and he prophecies.
summary.zh: 祭司撒迦利亞在殿中燒香時，加百列宣告其年老妻子伊利莎白將生一子，從母腹裏就被聖靈充滿，「要有以利亞的心志能力」行在主前面。他因不信而啞巴，直到事情成就之日。孩子生下，親族欲沿父名；父親寫字板答道：「他的名字是約翰」——口立時開了，即被聖靈充滿說預言。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The vowed miraculous birth echoes Sarah, Hannah, and Samson's mother.

passages.text: There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judaea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia: and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth. And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. And they had no child, because that Elisabeth was barren, and they both were now well stricken in years.
passages.zh: 猶太王希律的時候，亞比雅班裡有一個祭司，名叫撒迦利亞；他的妻子是亞倫的後裔，名叫以利沙伯。他們二人在神面前都是義人，遵行主的一切誡命禮儀，無可指摘。只是他們沒有孩子，因為以利沙伯不生育，兩個人又都年紀老邁了。

passages.text: And there appeared unto him an angel of the Lord standing on the right side of the altar of incense. But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John. For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord, and shall drink neither wine nor strong drink; and he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother's womb. And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
passages.zh: 有主的一個天使顯現，站在香壇的右邊。天使對他說：「撒迦利亞，不要害怕，因為你的祈禱已經被聽見了；你的妻子以利沙伯要給你生一個兒子，你要給他起名叫約翰。他在主面前將要為大，淡酒濃酒都不喝；從母腹裡就被聖靈充滿了。他必有以利亞的心志能力，行在主的前面，叫為父的心轉向兒女，叫悖逆的人轉從義人的智慧；又為主預備合用的百姓。」

passages.text: And Zacharias said unto the angel, Whereby shall I know this? for I am an old man, and my wife well stricken in years. And the angel answering said unto him, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God; and am sent to speak unto thee, and to shew thee these glad tidings. And, behold, thou shalt be dumb, and not able to speak, until the day that these things shall be performed, because thou believest not my words. And his mouth was opened immediately, and his tongue loosed, and he spake, and praised God.
passages.zh: 撒迦利亞對天使說：「我憑著什麼可以知道這事呢？我已經老了，我的妻子也年紀老邁了。」天使回答說：「我是站在神面前的加百列，奉差而來對你說話，將這好信息報給你。看哪，到了時候，這些事必然應驗；只因你不信我的話，你必啞巴，不能說話，直到這事成就的日子。」他的口立時開了，舌頭也舒展了，就說出話來，稱頌神。

title.en: Joseph's Dream: Fear Not to Take Mary
title.zh: 約瑟的夢：大膽娶過馬利亞來

region.en: Nazareth
region.zh: 拿撒勒

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 1

summary.en: Mary is found with child 'of the Holy Ghost' before she and Joseph come together; the just carpenter, unwilling to make her a public example, resolves to put her away quietly — until the angel of the LORD appears in a dream: 'Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost... thou shalt call his name JESUS.' He wakes and takes her as his wife, fulfilling Isaiah's 'Behold, a virgin shall be with child... they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us.'
summary.zh: 馬利亞未婚而「從聖靈懷了孕」；義人約瑟不願明明羞辱她，想暗中休了她——夢中主的使者顯現：「大衛的子孫約瑟，不要怕，只管娶過你的妻子馬利亞來，因她所懷的孕是從聖靈來的……你要給他起名叫耶穌。」約瑟醒了就遵命娶她，應驗先知所言：「必有童女懷孕生子，人要稱他的名為以馬內利」——神與我們同在。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Dream-guidance is a recurring mechanism of the infancy narratives.

passages.text: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost. Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily. But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.
passages.zh: 耶穌基督降生的事記在下面：他母親馬利亞已經許配了約瑟，還沒有迎娶，馬利亞就從聖靈懷了孕。她丈夫約瑟是個義人，不願意明明地羞辱她，想要暗暗地把她休了。正思念這事的時候，看哪，有主的使者向他夢中顯現，說：「大衛的子孫約瑟，不要怕，只管娶過你的妻子馬利亞來，因她所懷的孕是從聖靈來的。」

passages.text: And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us. Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife.
passages.zh: 她將要生一個兒子，你要給他起名叫耶穌，因他要將自己的百姓從罪惡裡救出來。這一切的事成就，是要應驗主藉先知所說的話，說：必有童女懷孕生子，人要稱他的名為以馬內利（以馬內利翻出來就是神與我們同在）。約瑟醒了，起來，就遵著主使者所吩咐的，把他的妻子娶過來。

title.en: The Magi Follow the Star
title.zh: 博士跟隨明星

region.en: Jerusalem to Bethlehem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷至伯利恆

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 2

summary.en: Wise men from the east, having seen 'his star', come to Jerusalem asking 'Where is he that is born King of the Jews?' Herod, troubled with all Jerusalem, learns from the scribes that Bethlehem is the place, then sends the Magi as unwitting agents; the star goes before them and stands over the house, where they fall down and worship, offering gold, frankincense, and myrrh — gifts later read as king, God, and sacrificial death — and are warned in a dream to go home another way.
summary.zh: 東方博士見「他的星」而來，問道：「那生下來作猶太人之王的在哪裏？」希律不安，全城也不安；文士據先知書指明伯利恆。希律密召博士查明星出現之時，遣他們往尋。星竟在他們前頭行，直停到小孩子的地方；他們俯伏敬拜，獻上黃金、乳香、沒藥——歷代釋之為君王、真神與受死之預表——夢中被警，遂從別路回國。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The star-guided journey is tagged constellation-origin for comparison with star-omen narratives cross-culturally; noted as interpretive.

passages.text: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem, saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him. When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him. And when he had gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people together, he demanded of them where Christ should be born.
passages.zh: 當希律王的時候，耶穌生在猶太的伯利恆。有幾個博士從東方來到耶路撒冷，說：那生下來作猶太人之王的在哪裡？我們在東方看見他的星，特來拜他。希律王聽見了，就心裡不安；耶路撒冷合城的人也都不安。他就召齊了祭司長和民間的文士，問他們說：基督當生在何處？

passages.text: When they had heard the king, they departed; and, lo, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was. When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy. And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense and myrrh. And being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way.
passages.zh: 他們聽見王的話就去了。在東方所看見的那星忽然在他們前頭行，直行到小孩子的地方，就在上頭停住了。他們看見那星，就大大地歡喜。進了房子，看見小孩子和他母親馬利亞，就俯伏拜那小孩子，揭開寶盒，拿黃金、乳香、沒藥為禮物獻給他。博士因為在夢中被主指示不要回去見希律，就從別的路回本地去了。

title.en: Flight into Egypt and the Slaughter of the Innocents
title.zh: 逃往埃及與伯利恆屠嬰

region.en: Bethlehem to Egypt and back
region.zh: 伯利恆至埃及再返

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 2

summary.en: Warned by an angel, Joseph takes mother and child by night to Egypt — 'Out of Egypt have I called my son' — while Herod, mocked by the Magi, kills every boy of two years and under in Bethlehem and its coasts, fulfilling Rachel's weeping in Ramah. At Herod's death a dream calls the family back; fearing Archelaus, they settle in Nazareth. The massacre made the Holy Family the archetype of the refugee, and the Holy Innocents the first martyrs of the calendar.
summary.zh: 天使警示，約瑟攜母嬰夜奔埃及——「我從埃及召出我的兒子來」；被博士愚弄的希律大怒，將伯利恆及四境兩歲以內的男孩全都殺盡，應驗拉結哭兒之預言。希律死後，夢中得召返國；因懼亞基老，便退居拿撒勒。聖家自此成為逃難者的原型，無辜嬰孩則成為曆法上最早的殉道者。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The massacre of children is presented as narrative; the Holy Innocents' day remains part of several calendars.

passages.text: And when they were departed, behold, the angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him. When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt: and was there until the death of Herod: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt have I called my son.
passages.zh: 他們去後，有主的使者向約瑟夢中顯現，說：起來！帶著小孩子同他母親逃往埃及，住在那裡，等我吩咐你；因為希律必尋找小孩子，要除滅他。約瑟就起來，夜間帶著小孩子和他母親往埃及去，住在那裡，直到希律死了。這是要應驗主藉先知所說的話，說：我從埃及召出我的兒子來。

passages.text: Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men. Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying, In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.
passages.zh: 希律見自己被博士愚弄，就大大發怒，差人將伯利恆城裡並四境所有的男孩，照著他向博士仔細查問的時候，凡兩歲以裡的，都殺盡了。這就應了先知耶利米的話，說：在拉瑪聽見號咷大哭的聲音，是拉結哭她兒女，不肯受安慰，因為他們都不在了。

passages.text: But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appeareth in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel. But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judaea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of God in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee: and he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.
passages.zh: 希律死了以後，有主的使者在埃及向約瑟夢中顯現，說：起來！帶著小孩子和他母親往以色列地去。只因聽見亞基老接著他父親希律作了猶太王，就怕往那裡去，又在夢中被主指示，便往加利利境內去了，到了一座城，名叫拿撒勒，就住在那裡。這是要應驗先知所說，他將稱為拿撒勒人的話了。

title.en: Simeon and the Nunc Dimittis
title.zh: 西面與西面頌

region.en: Temple, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷聖殿

period: Gospel of Luke, c. 80-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 2

summary.en: Forty days after the birth, the family brings the child to the temple with a pair of turtledoves. Simeon, 'just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel', is promised by the Holy Ghost that he shall not see death before he sees the Lord's Christ; taking the child in his arms he blesses God: 'Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word: for mine eyes have seen thy salvation' — and to Mary the first sword-warning: 'a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also.'
summary.zh: 降生後四十日，聖家攜一對斑鳩上殿行潔淨禮。義人西面素常盼望以色列的安慰者，聖靈啟示他未死之前必看見主的基督；他抱嬰孩頌讚：「主啊，如今可以照你的話，釋放僕人安然去世，因為我的眼睛已經看見你的救恩。」並向馬利亞預言首柄劍：「你自己的心也要被刀刺透。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The presentation rite underlies Candlemas.

passages.text: And, behold, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Ghost was upon him. And it was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord's Christ. And he came by the Spirit into the temple: and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him after the custom of the law, then took he him up in his arms, and blessed God, and said, Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word: for mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; a light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel.
passages.zh: 看哪，在耶路撒冷有一個人，名叫西面；這人又公義又虔誠，素常盼望以色列的安慰者來到，又有聖靈在他身上。他得了聖靈的啟示，知道自己未死以前，必看見主所立的基督。他受了聖靈的感動，進入聖殿；正遇見耶穌的父母抱著孩子進來，要照律法的規矩辦理，西面就用手接過他來，稱頌神說：主啊，如今可以照你的話，釋放僕人安然去世；因為我的眼睛已經看見你的救恩，就是你在萬民面前所預備的：是照亮外邦人的光，又是你民以色列的榮耀。

passages.text: And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him. And Simeon blessed them, and said unto Mary his mother, Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel; and for a sign which shall be spoken against; (yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also,) that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.
passages.zh: 約瑟和孩子的母親因這些話就希奇。西面給他們祝福，又對孩子的母親馬利亞說：看哪，這孩子被立，是要叫以色列中許多人跌倒，許多人興起；又要作毀謗的話柄；（你自己的心也要被刀刺透，）叫許多人心裡的意念顯露出來。

title.en: The Voice Crying in the Wilderness
title.zh: 曠野呼喊的聲音

region.en: Wilderness of Judaea, banks of the Jordan
region.zh: 猶太曠野，約旦河畔

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 3

summary.en: Clothed in camel's hair with a leathern girdle, eating locusts and wild honey, John the Baptist preaches in the wilderness of Judaea, 'Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand', and all Judaea comes to be baptized in Jordan confessing their sins. To the Pharisees and Sadducees he is ungentle — 'O generation of vipers' — and to all he points past himself: 'I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear.'
summary.zh: 約翰身穿駱駝毛的衣服，腰束皮帶，吃蝗蟲野蜜，在猶太曠野傳道：「天國近了，你們應當悔改！」耶路撒冷和猶太全地的人都到約旦河受洗，承認罪。他對法利賽人與撒都該人疾言厲色——「毒蛇的種類」——並將人指向他之後的那位：「我用水給你們施洗，叫你們悔改；但那在我以後來的，能力比我更大，我就是給他提鞋也不配。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The baptism of repentance is the ritual-origin element; John's Elijah-like dress echoes 2 Kings 1:8.

passages.text: In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, and saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey.
passages.zh: 那時，有施洗的約翰出來，在猶太的曠野傳道，說：天國近了，你們應當悔改！這人就是先知以賽亞所說的，他說：在曠野有人聲喊著說：預備主的道，修直他的路！這約翰身穿駱駝毛的衣服，腰束皮帶，吃的是蝗蟲、野蜜。

passages.text: Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about Jordan, and were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins. But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance.
passages.zh: 那時，耶路撒冷和猶太全地，並約但河一帶地方的人，都出去到約翰那裡，承認他們的罪，在約但河裡受他的洗。約翰看見許多法利賽人和撒都該人也來受洗，就對他們說：毒蛇的種類！誰指示你們逃避將來的忿怒呢？你們要結出果子來，與悔改的心相稱。

passages.text: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire: whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.
passages.zh: 我實在是用水給你們施洗，叫你們悔改；但那在我以後來的，能力比我更大，我就是給他提鞋也不配；他要用聖靈與火給你們施洗。他手裡拿著簸箕，要揚淨他的場，把麥子收在倉裡，把糠用不滅的火燒盡了。

title.en: The Baptism of Jesus
title.zh: 耶穌受洗

region.en: Jordan river, at Bethabara
region.zh: 約旦河，伯大尼外

period: Gospels of Matthew and John, c. 80-100 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 3; Book 43: John, chapter 1

summary.en: Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized by John, who demurs — 'I have need to be baptized of thee' — and the voice of the Father and the descending Spirit like a dove mark the scene as the tradition's trinitarian theophany: 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.' John's witness frames it: 'Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.'
summary.zh: 耶穌從加利利來到約旦河受約翰的洗；約翰自認不配而辭——「我當受你的洗」——當下天開了，聖靈彷彿鴿子降下，父的聲音自天而來：「這是我的愛子，我所喜悅的。」約翰的見證為其框架：「看哪，神的羔羊，除去世人罪孽的。」傳統視此景為三一神顯。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Central rite of Christianity; presented as comparative theophany.

passages.text: Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him. But John forbad him, saying, I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me? And Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. Then he suffered him. And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him: and lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
passages.zh: 當下，耶穌從加利利來到約但河，見了約翰，要受他的洗。約翰想要攔住他，說：我當受你的洗，你反倒上我這裡來嗎？耶穌回答說：你暫且許我，因為我們理當這樣盡諸般的義。於是約翰許了他。耶穌受了洗，隨即從水裡上來；天忽然為他開了，他就看見神的靈彷彿鴿子降下，落在他身上；從天上有聲音說：這是我的愛子，我所喜悅的。

passages.text: The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world. And John bare record, saying, I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it abode upon him. And I knew him not: but he that sent me to baptize with water, the same said unto me, Upon whom thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and remaining on him, the same is he which baptizeth with the Holy Ghost. And I saw, and bare record that this is the Son of God.
passages.zh: 次日，約翰看見耶穌來到他那裡，就說：「看哪，神的羔羊，除去世人罪孽的。」約翰又作見證說：「我曾看見聖靈彷彿鴿子從天降下，住在他的身上。我先前不認識他，只是那差我來用水施洗的對我說：『你看見聖靈降下住在誰身上，誰就是用聖靈施洗的。』我看見了，就作見證說：這是神的兒子。」

title.en: The Temptation in the Wilderness
title.zh: 曠野受試探

region.en: Wilderness of Judaea; temple pinnacle (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 猶太曠野；聖殿殿頂（象徵性定位）

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 4

summary.en: Led by the Spirit into the wilderness and fasting forty days and forty nights, Jesus is tempted three times by the devil: stones to bread ('Man shall not live by bread alone'), a leap from the temple's pinnacle ('Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God'), and the kingdoms of the world offered for one act of worship ('Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve'). The devil leaves, angels minister — the archetype of the tested hero in the Christian imagination.
summary.zh: 耶穌被聖靈引到曠野，禁食四十晝夜；魔鬼三度試探——命石頭變餅（「人活著不是單靠食物」）、自殿頂跳下（「不可試探主你的神」）、以萬國榮華換一拜（「撒但退去吧！因為經上記著說：當拜主你的神，單要事奉他」）。魔鬼離去，天使來伺候——這是基督教想像中受試煉英雄的原型。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The temptation scene is the tradition's master-text on evil's persuasive forms.

passages.text: Then was Jesus led up of the spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil. And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungred. And when the tempter came to him, he said, If thou be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread. But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
passages.zh: 當時，耶穌被聖靈引到曠野，受魔鬼的試探。他禁食四十晝夜，後來就餓了。那試探人的進前來，對他說：「你若是神的兒子，可以吩咐這些石頭變成食物。」耶穌卻回答說：「經上記著說：人活著，不是單靠食物，乃是靠神口裡所出的一切話。」

passages.text: Then the devil taketh him up into the holy city, and setteth him on a pinnacle of the temple, and saith unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning thee. Jesus said unto him, It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God. Again, the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain, and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them; and saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me. Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve. Then the devil leaveth him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him.
passages.zh: 魔鬼就帶他進了聖城，叫他站在殿頂上，對他說：「你若是神的兒子，可以跳下去，因為經上記著說：他要為你吩咐他的使者。耶穌對他說：「經上又記著說：不可試探主你的神。」魔鬼又帶他上了一座極高的山，將世上的萬國與萬國的榮華都指給他看，對他說：「你若俯伏拜我，我就把這一切都賜給你。」耶穌說：「撒但，退去吧！因為經上記著說：當拜主你的神，單要事奉他。」於是魔鬼離了耶穌，有天使來伺候他。

title.en: Fishers of Men: The Calling of the First Disciples
title.zh: 得人如得魚：首批門徒蒙召

region.en: Sea of Galilee, shore of Capernaum
region.zh: 加利利海，迦百農岸邊

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 4

summary.en: Settling at Capernaum by the sea, in Zebulun and Naphtali, 'the people which sat in darkness saw great light', Jesus begins preaching 'Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand' — and walking by the sea calls two pairs of fishermen brothers: 'Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.' Simon Peter and Andrew, then James and John the sons of Zebedee, straightway leave nets, boats, and father, and follow him; his fame spreads through all Syria as he heals 'all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.'
