And Thomas answered and said unto him, My LORD and my God. Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
passages.zh: 過了八日，門徒又在屋裡，多馬也和他們同在。那時門都關了，耶穌來站在當中，說：「願你們平安。」然後對多馬說：「伸過你的指頭來，看我的手；伸出你的手來，探入我的肋旁。不要疑惑，總要信。」多馬回答他說：「我的主，我的神。」耶穌對他說：「多馬，你因看見了我才信；那沒有看見就信的有福了。」

title.en: Mary Mistakes the Risen Christ for the Gardener
title.zh: 馬利亞誤認園丁

region.en: Garden by the sepulchre, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，墳墓旁的園子

period: Gospel of John, c. 90-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 43: John, chapter 20

summary.en: Weeping outside the empty tomb, Mary Magdalene stoops to see two angels in white — 'Woman, why weepest thou?' — then turns and sees a figure she takes for the gardener, even offering to carry the body away herself. One word breaks through: 'Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master.' Sent to tell the brethren 'I ascend unto my Father, and your Father', she becomes the first apostle of the resurrection — 'the apostle to the apostles.'
summary.zh: 馬利亞站在空墳外哭，低頭見兩位白衣天使問「婦人，你為甚麼哭？」；轉身見一人，誤認為是園丁，甚至願親自把遺體搬走。一聲呼名穿透一切：「耶穌說：馬利亞。她轉過身來，用希伯來話對他說：拉波尼（就是夫子的意思）。」受差去向弟兄報信「我要升上去見我的父，也是你們的父」——她成為復活信息的第一位使者，「使徒的使徒」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The first-witness scene underlies the honorific 'apostle to the apostles'.

passages.text: But Mary stood without at the sepulchre weeping: and as she wept, she stooped down, and looked into the sepulchre, and seeth two angels in white sitting, the one at the head, and the other at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain. And they say unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? She saith unto them, Because they have taken away my LORD, and I know not where they have laid him.
passages.zh: 馬利亞卻站在墳墓外面哭。哭的時候，她低頭往墳墓裡看，就見兩個天使穿著白衣，在安放耶穌身體的地方坐著，一個在頭，一個在腳。他們就對她說：「婦人，你為什麼哭？」她對他們說：「因為有人把我主挪了去，我不知道他們把他放在哪裡。」

passages.text: And when she had thus said, she turned herself back, and saw Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus. Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away. Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master. Jesus saith unto her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God. Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the LORD, and that he had spoken these things unto her.
passages.zh: 說了這話，她就轉過身來，看見耶穌站在那裡，卻不知道是耶穌。耶穌對她說：「婦人，為什麼哭？你找誰呢？」她以為他是園丁，就對他說：「先生，若是你把他移了去，請告訴我你把他放在哪裡，我便去取他。」耶穌對她說：「馬利亞。」她就轉過身來，用希伯來話對他說：「拉波尼！」（就是「夫子」的意思。）耶穌對她說：「不要摸我，因我還沒有升上去見我的父。你往我弟兄那裡去，告訴他們說，我要升上去見我的父，也是你們的父；見我的神，也是你們的神。」抹大拉的馬利亞就去告訴門徒說，她已經看見了主，又將主對她說的這些話告訴他們。

title.en: The Ascension from the Mount of Olives
title.zh: 橄欖山升天

region.en: Mount of Olives, near Jerusalem
region.zh: 橄欖山，近耶路撒冷

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 1

summary.en: Forty days of risen appearances end as 'he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.' Two men in white apparel ask the gazing disciples, 'why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus... shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven' — and the company returns to Jerusalem to pray in the upper room, one hundred and twenty strong, awaiting the promise of the Spirit.
summary.zh: 四十日復活顯現終結之時，「他就被取上升，有一朵雲彩把他接去」。兩個白衣人問呆望天空的門徒：「加利利人哪，你們為甚麼站著望天呢？這離開你們被接升天的耶穌……他怎樣往天上去，你們還要怎樣來。」眾人回耶路撒冷，在樓上房間同心合意恆切禱告——一百二十人等候聖靈的應許。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The ascension is celebrated as a principal feast; the return-promise frames Christian eschatology.

passages.text: And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight. And while they looked stedfastly toward heaven as he went up, behold, two men stood by them in white apparel; which also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.
passages.zh: 說了這話，他們正看的時候，他就被取上升，有一朵雲彩把他接去，便看不見他了。當他往上去，他們定睛望天的時候，忽然有兩個人身穿白衣，站在旁邊，說：「加利利人哪，你們為什麼站著望天呢？這離開你們被接升天的耶穌，你們見他怎樣往天上去，他還要怎樣來。」

passages.text: Then returned they unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is from Jerusalem a sabbath day's journey. And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes. These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren.
passages.zh: 有一座山，名叫橄欖山，離耶路撒冷不遠，約有安息日可走的路程。當下，門徒從那裡回耶路撒冷去，進了城，就上了所住的一間樓房；在那裡有彼得、約翰、雅各、安得烈、腓力、多馬、巴多羅買、馬太、亞勒腓的兒子雅各、奮銳黨的西門。這些人同著幾個婦人和耶穌的母親馬利亞，並耶穌的弟兄，都同心合意地恆切禱告。

title.en: Ananias and Sapphira Lie to the Holy Ghost
title.zh: 亞拿尼亞與撒非喇欺哄聖靈

region.en: Jerusalem, apostles' feet
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，使徒腳前

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 5

summary.en: In the community where 'neither said any of them that ought of the things which he possessed was his own', Ananias and Sapphira sell land, keep back part of the price, and present the rest as the whole. Peter's rebuke — 'thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God' — is followed by sudden death, his, then three hours later hers at the same feet; 'great fear came upon all the church.' The young church's feared and debated tale of concealed giving.
summary.zh: 在「沒有一人說他的東西有一樣是自己的」的團體中，亞拿尼亞夫婦賣田產，私自留下幾分，其餘放在使徒腳前充作全數。彼得斥責——「你不是欺哄人，是欺哄神了」——隨即仆倒斷氣；三小時後妻子在同樣腳前同樣倒下。「全教會和聽見這事的人都甚懼怕。」初期教會最令人戰慄、也最被爭論的隱匿奉獻故事。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The deaths are presented as narrative without endorsement.

passages.text: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession, and kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles' feet. But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land? Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power? why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God. And Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost: and great fear came on all them that heard these things.
passages.zh: 有一個人，名叫亞拿尼亞，同他的妻子撒非喇賣了田產，把價銀私自留下幾分，他的妻子也知道，其餘的幾分拿來放在使徒腳前。彼得說：「亞拿尼亞！為什麼撒但充滿了你的心，叫你欺哄聖靈，把田地的價銀私自留下幾分呢？田地還沒有賣，不是你自己的嗎？既賣了，價銀不是你作主嗎？你怎麼心裡起這意念呢？你不是欺哄人，是欺哄神了。」亞拿尼亞聽見這話，就仆倒，斷了氣；聽見的人都甚懼怕。

passages.text: And it was about the space of three hours after, when his wife, not knowing what was done, came in. And Peter answered unto her, Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much? And she said, Yea, for so much. Then Peter said unto her, How is it that ye have agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? behold, the feet of them which have buried thy husband are at the door, and shall carry thee out. Then fell she down straightway at his feet, and yielded up the ghost: and great fear came upon all the church.
passages.zh: 約過了三小時，他的妻子進來，還不知道這事。彼得對她說：「你告訴我，你們賣田地的價銀就是這些嗎？」她說：「就是這些。」彼得說：「你們為什麼同心試探主的靈呢？埋葬你丈夫之人的腳已到門口，他們也要把你抬出去。」她立刻仆倒在彼得腳前，斷了氣。聽見的人都甚懼怕。

title.en: The Stoning of Stephen, First Martyr
title.zh: 首位殉道者司提反被石頭打死

region.en: Outside the city walls, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷城外

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapters 6-7

summary.en: Full of the Holy Ghost, Stephen sees 'the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God'; the council stops their ears, casts him out, and stones him — with the clothes laid at the feet of the young man Saul, consenting. Stephen's last words fold the tradition's martyrdom pattern: 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit... Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.' The persecution scatters the church, and the gospel spreads.
summary.zh: 滿得聖靈的司提反舉目望天，見「天開了，人子站在神的右邊」；公會捂耳呼喊，把他推到城外用石頭打——見證人把衣裳放在旁邊的少年人掃羅腳前。司提反臨終呼求確立殉道模式：「求主耶穌接收我的靈魂……主啊，不要將這罪歸於他們。說了這話，就睡了。」教會遭大逼迫四散，福音反得廣傳。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The prototype martyr; the Saul connection is the hinge of the Damascus conversion.

passages.text: When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth. But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God, and said, Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.
passages.zh: 他們聽見這些話，就極其惱怒，向他咬牙切齒。但他被聖靈充滿，定睛望天，看見神的榮耀，又看見耶穌站在神的右邊，就說：「看哪，我看見天開了，人子站在神的右邊。」

passages.text: Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord, and cast him out of the city, and stoned him: and the witnesses laid down their clothes at a young man's feet, whose name was Saul. And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep. And Saul was consenting unto his death. And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judaea and Samaria.
passages.zh: 眾人大聲喊叫，摀著耳朵，齊心擁上前去，把他推出城外，用石頭打他。作見證的人把衣裳放在一個少年人腳前，那少年名叫掃羅。他們用石頭打司提反的時候，他呼求神說：「主耶穌，求你接收我的靈魂。」他又跪下，大聲喊著說：「主啊，不要將這罪歸於他們。」說了這話，他就睡了。掃羅也贊同他被害。從那日起，耶路撒冷的教會大遭逼迫，門徒都分散到猶太和撒瑪利亞各處去。

title.en: Philip and the Ethiopian Eunuch
title.zh: 腓利與埃提阿伯太監

region.en: Desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza
region.zh: 耶路撒冷下迦薩的路上

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 8

summary.en: Sent by an angel onto the desert road, Philip catches the treasurer of Candace, queen of Ethiopia, reading Isaiah in his chariot — 'Understandest thou what thou readest?... How can I, except some man should guide me?' Philip preaches Jesus from the suffering servant passage; at the water by the road the eunuch asks, 'what doth hinder me to be baptized?' — and is baptized, going on his way rejoicing, while Philip is caught away by the Spirit. African Christianity has long claimed this as its founding charter.
summary.zh: 使者差腓利上那條通往迦薩的曠野路，追上埃提阿伯女王干大基手下總管銀庫的太監——他正坐在車上誦讀以賽亞書。「你所念的，你明白嗎？……沒有人指教我，怎能明白呢？」腓利便從受苦僕人的經文傳講耶穌；路旁有水，太監問「我受洗有甚麼妨礙呢？」——受洗後歡歡喜喜走路，腓利被主的靈提了去。非洲教會久以本章為建基憲章。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Ethiopian eunuch is honored in Ethiopian Orthodox memory as the bearer of the faith.

passages.text: And the angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert. And he arose and went: and, behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem for to worship, was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet. Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot. And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me?
passages.zh: 有主的一個使者對腓利說：「起來，向南走，往那從耶路撒冷下迦薩的路上去。」那路是曠野。他就起身去了。不料，有一個埃提阿伯人，是個有大權的太監，在埃提阿伯女王干大基手下總管銀庫，他上耶路撒冷禮拜去了，現在回來，坐在車上念先知以賽亞的書。聖靈對腓利說：「你貼近那車走。」腓利就跑上前去，聽見他念先知以賽亞的書，便問他說：「你所念的，你明白嗎？」他說：「沒有人指教我，怎能明白呢？」

passages.text: Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus. And as they went on their way, they came unto a certain water: and the eunuch said, See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized? And Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him. And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing.
passages.zh: 腓利就開口從這經上起，對他傳講耶穌。二人正往前走，到了有水的地方，太監說：「看哪，這裡有水，我受洗有什麼妨礙呢？」腓利說：「你若是一心相信，就可以。」他回答說：「我信耶穌基督是神的兒子。」於是吩咐車站住，腓利和太監二人同下水裡去，腓利就給他施洗。從水裡上來，主的靈把腓利提了去，太監也不再見他了，就歡歡喜喜地走路。

title.en: Saul on the Road to Damascus
title.zh: 掃羅在大馬士革路上

region.en: Road near Damascus
region.zh: 大馬士革近郊路上

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 9

summary.en: Breathing threatenings and slaughter, the persecutor travels to Damascus with warrants for 'this way'; suddenly a light from heaven shines around him and he falls to earth: 'Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?... I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.' Led blind into the city, he is met three days later by the disciple Ananias — 'a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles' — receives his sight like scales falling, is baptized, and straightway preaches Christ in the synagogues.
summary.zh: 口吐威嚇兇殺話的逼迫者，持大祭司公文往大馬士革捉拿「信奉這道的人」；忽然天上有大光四面照著他，他就仆倒在地：「掃羅，掃羅，你為甚麼逼迫我？……我就是你所逼迫的耶穌。你用腳踢刺是難的。」被拉進城，三日看不見、不吃不喝；門徒亞拿尼亞奉命去按手——「他是我所揀選的器皿，要在外邦人和君王並以色列人面前宣揚我的名」——鱗狀的東西掉下，他就看見，起來受洗，隨即在各會堂宣講耶穌。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The conversion is the hinge of Christian universalism; tagged theophany for the heavenly light and voice.

passages.text: And Saul, yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went unto the high priest, and desired of him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem. And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven: and he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
passages.zh: 掃羅仍然向主的門徒口吐威嚇凶殺的話，去見大祭司，求文書給大馬色的各會堂，若是找著信奉這道的人，無論男女，都准他捆綁帶到耶路撒冷。掃羅行路，將近大馬色，忽然有光從天上四面照著他。他就仆倒在地，聽見有聲音對他說：「掃羅，掃羅，你為什麼逼迫我？」他說：「主啊，你是誰？」主說：「我就是你所逼迫的耶穌。你踢刺是難的。」

passages.text: And Saul arose from the earth; and when his eyes were opened, he saw no man: but they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus. And he was three days without sight, and neither did eat nor drink. And there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and to him said the Lord in a vision, Ananias. And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the street which is called Straight, and enquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul, of Tarsus: for, behold, he prayeth.
passages.zh: 掃羅從地上起來，睜開眼睛，竟不能看見什麼。有人拉他的手，領他進了大馬色。三日不能看見，也不吃也不喝。在大馬色有一個門徒，名叫亞拿尼亞。主在異象中對他說：「亞拿尼亞。」主對他說：「起來，往直街去，在猶大的家裡，訪問一個大數人，名叫掃羅，他正禱告。」

passages.text: But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel: for I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name's sake. And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost. And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.
passages.zh: 但主對他說：「你只管去！他是我所揀選的器皿，要在外邦人和君王，並以色列人面前宣揚我的名。我也要指示他，為我的名必須受許多的苦難。」亞拿尼亞就去了，進入那家，把手按在掃羅身上，說：「兄弟掃羅，在你來的路上向你顯現的主，就是耶穌，打發我來，叫你能看見，又被聖靈充滿。」他的眼睛上好像有鱗立刻掉下來，他就能看見，於是起來受了洗。

title.en: Peter's Sheet Vision and Cornelius's Household
title.zh: 彼得的布異象與哥尼流一家

region.en: Rooftop at Joppa; Caesarea
region.zh: 約帕房頂；該撒利亞

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 10

summary.en: Praying hungry on a rooftop, Peter falls into a trance: heaven opens, a great sheet knitted at four corners descends full of unclean beasts, and a voice commands, 'Rise, Peter; kill, and eat' — 'What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common', thrice repeated. Sent for by Cornelius, the God-fearing centurion, Peter preaches in Caesarea and the Holy Ghost falls on the uncircumcised hearers — 'Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?' The charter of the Gentile mission.
summary.zh: 屋頂禱告時餓了的彼得魂遊象外：天開了，四角垂下的大布縑滿俗物與不潔之物，聲音說「彼得，起來，宰了吃」——「神所潔淨的，你不可當作俗物」，一連三次。羅馬百夫長哥尼流遣人相請；彼得在該撒利亞講道，聖靈降在一切未受割禮的聽道者身上——「這些人既受了聖靈，與我們一樣，誰能禁止用水給他們施洗呢？」外邦宣教的憲章自此立定。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The sheet vision is the tradition's charter of universality and the overturning of purity codes.

passages.text: Peter went up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour: and he became very hungry, and would have eaten: but while they made ready, he fell into a trance, and saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending upon him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth: wherein were all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air. And there came a voice to him, Rise, Peter; kill, and eat. But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean. And the voice spake unto him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common. This was done thrice: and the vessel was received up again into heaven.
passages.zh: 彼得約在午正上房頂去禱告：覺得餓了，想要吃。那家的人正預備飯的時候，彼得魂遊象外，看見天開了，有一物降下，好像一塊大布，繫著四角，縋在地上，裡面有地上各樣四足的走獸和野獸，並爬物和天空的飛鳥。又有聲音向他說：「彼得，起來，宰了吃！」彼得卻說：「主啊，這是不可的！凡俗物和不潔淨的物，我從來沒有吃過。」第二次有聲音向他說：「神所潔淨的，你不可當作俗物。」這樣一連三次，那物隨即收回天上去了。

passages.text: While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word. And they of the circumcision which believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost: for they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God. Then answered Peter, Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we? And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord.
passages.zh: 彼得還說這話的時候，聖靈降在一切聽道的人身上。那些奉割禮、和彼得同來的信徒，見聖靈的恩賜也澆在外邦人身上，就都希奇；因聽見他們說方言，稱讚神為大。於是彼得說：「這些人既受了聖靈，與我們一樣，誰能禁止用水給他們施洗呢？」就吩咐奉主耶穌的名給他們施洗。

title.en: The Angel Breaks Peter Out of Prison
title.zh: 天使救彼得出監

region.en: Herod's prison, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，希律的監牢

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 12

summary.en: Intending to bring Peter forth after Passover, Herod keeps him sleeping bound with two chains between soldiers — while the church prays without ceasing. The angel smites Peter on the side, the chains fall off, the iron gate 'opened to them of his own accord'; Peter thinks it a vision until the angel departs and he stands alone in the street — 'Now I know of a surety, that the LORD hath sent his angel' — and comes to Mary's house where the praying church can hardly believe the knocking is really him.
summary.zh: 希律要在逾越節後提彼得出來辦他，彼得卻被兩條鐵鏈鎖著睡在二兵士之間——教會卻為他切切禱告神。使者拍他的肋旁，鐵鏈脫落；「臨街的鐵門就自己開了」；他以為見異象，直到天使離開，才獨立街中——「我現在真知道主差遣他的使者，救我脫離希律的手」——到了馬利亞家門口，禱告的人群竟不敢相信真是他敲門。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The prison-delivery is a classic angelic-rescue type.

passages.text: Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him. And when Herod would have brought him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains: and the keepers before the door kept the prison. And, behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison: and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.
passages.zh: 彼得因此被囚在監裡；但教會卻為他不住地禱告神。希律將要提他出來的前一夜，彼得被兩條鐵鍊鎖著，睡在兩個兵丁當中；看守的人也在門外看守。忽然，有主的一個使者站在旁邊，屋裡有光照耀，天使拍彼得的肋旁，拍醒了他，說：「快快起來！」那鐵鍊就從他手上脫落下來。

passages.text: When they were past the first and the second ward, they came unto the iron gate that leadeth unto the city; which opened to them of his own accord: and they went out, and passed on through one street; and forthwith the angel departed from him. And when Peter was come to himself, he said, Now I know of a surety, that the LORD hath sent his angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod. And when he had considered the thing, he came to the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying.
passages.zh: 過了第一層第二層監牢，就來到臨街的鐵門，那門自己開了。他們出來，走過一條街，天使便離開他去了。彼得醒悟過來，說：「我現在真知道主差遣他的使者，救我脫離希律的手。」彼得想了一想，就往那稱呼馬可的約翰、他母親馬利亞家去；在那裡有好些人聚集禱告。

title.en: Midnight Hymns in the Philippian Jail
title.zh: 腓立比監中的半夜歌聲

region.en: Philippi, Macedonia
region.zh: 馬其頓，腓立比

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 16

summary.en: Answering a night vision — 'a man of Macedonia... Come over into Macedonia, and help us' — Paul crosses to Europe, converts the purple-seller Lydia, and after an exorcism is beaten and jailed with Silas. At midnight they pray and sing; an earthquake opens every door and looses every band; the suicide-minded jailer is stopped — 'Do thyself no harm: for we are all here' — asks 'what must I do to be saved?', washes their stripes, and is baptized with all his house the same hour of the night.
summary.zh: 應夜間異象——「有一個馬其頓人站著求他說：請你過到馬其頓來幫助我們」——保羅渡海入歐洲，使賣紫色布疋的呂底亞歸主；因趕鬼被棍打下監。半夜與西拉禱告唱詩，大地震動，眾門全開、鎖鏈鬆開；欲自刎的禁卒被喝止——「不要傷害自己，我們都在這裏」——問「我當怎樣行才可以得救？」當夜洗淨他們的傷，全家立時受洗。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Macedonian call is the charter of the gospel's entry into Europe.

passages.text: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us. And after he had seen the vision, immediately we endeavoured to go into Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord had called us for to preach the gospel unto them. And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul. And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought us, saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there.
passages.zh: 在夜間有異象現與保羅：有一個馬其頓人站著求他說：「請你過到馬其頓來幫助我們。」保羅既看見這異象，我們隨即想要往馬其頓去，以為神召我們傳福音給那裡的人聽。有一個賣紫色布疋的婦人，名叫呂底亞，是推雅推喇城的人，素來敬拜神。她聽見了，主就開導她的心，叫她留心聽保羅所講的話。她和她一家既領了洗，便求我們說：「你們若以為我是真信主的，請到我家裡來住。」

passages.text: And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them. And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed. And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled. But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.
passages.zh: 約在半夜，保羅和西拉禱告，唱詩讚美神，眾囚犯也側耳而聽。忽然，地大震動，甚至監牢的地基都搖動了，監門立刻全開，眾囚犯的鎖鍊也都鬆開了。禁卒一醒，看見監門全開，以為囚犯已經逃走，就拔刀要自殺。保羅大聲呼叫說：「不要傷害自己！我們都在這裡。」

passages.text: Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas, and brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved? And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house. And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway. And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.
passages.zh: 禁卒叫人拿燈來，就跳進去，戰戰兢兢地俯伏在保羅、西拉面前，又領他們出來，說：「二位先生，我當怎樣行才可以得救？」他們說：「當信主耶穌，你和你一家都必得救。」他們就把主的道講給他和他全家的人聽。當夜，就在那時候，禁卒把他們帶去，洗他們的傷；他和屬乎他的人立時都受了洗。於是禁卒領他們上自己家裡去，給他們擺上飯。他和全家，因為信了神，都很喜樂。

title.en: Paul at the Areopagus: The Unknown God
title.zh: 保羅在亞略巴古：未識之神

region.en: Mars Hill, Athens
region.zh: 雅典，亞略巴古

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 17

summary.en: In the city wholly given to idolatry, philosophers of the Epicureans and Stoicks summon the 'babbler' to Mars' hill, 'for all the Athenians... spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.' Paul's address builds on their own altar: 'TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you' — God who made the world dwells not in temples made with hands, has 'determined the times before appointed', and 'now commandeth all men every where to repent', guaranteeing judgment 'by that man whom he hath ordained.'
summary.zh: 在滿城偶像的雅典，伊壁鳩魯與斯多亞學士把這「胡言亂語的」帶到亞略巴古——「雅典人和住在那裏的客人都不顧別的事，只或談說，或聽聽新聞」。保羅的講章由他們自己的祭壇起筵：「未識之神。你們所不認識而敬拜的，我現在告訴你們」——創造天地的神不住人手所造的殿，已預定時期，「如今卻吩咐各處的人都要悔改」，並藉祂所立定的人按公義審判天下。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Areopagus speech is the classic model of cross-cultural apologetics.

passages.text: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry. Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection. And they took him, and brought him unto Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof thou speakest, is?
passages.zh: 保羅在雅典等候他們的時候，看見滿城都是偶像，就心裡著急。於是有以彼古羅和斯多亞兩門的哲學家與他爭論。有的說：「這胡言亂語的要說什麼？」有的說：「他似乎是傳說外邦鬼神的。」這話是因保羅傳講耶穌與復活的道。他們就把他帶到亞略巴古，說：「你所講的這新道，我們也可以知道是什麼嗎？」

passages.text: Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars' hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious. For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you. God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands; neither is worshipped with men's hands, as though he needed any thing.
passages.zh: 保羅站在亞略巴古當中，說：「眾位雅典人哪，我看你們凡事很敬畏鬼神。我遊行的時候，觀看你們所敬拜的，遇見一座壇，上面寫著『未識之神』。你們所不認識而敬拜的，我現在告訴你們。創造宇宙和其中萬物的神，既是天地的主，就不住人手所造的殿，也不用人手服事，好像缺少什麼。

title.en: Shipwreck at Malta: The Viper and the Gods
title.zh: 馬耳他海難：毒蛇與「他是神」

region.en: Island of Melita (Malta)
region.zh: 米利大島（馬耳他）

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapters 27-28

summary.en: Fourteen days tossed by the Euroclydon with neither sun nor stars, all hope gone, Paul stands amid the crew and announces his night-visiting angel: 'Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.' The ship runs aground; soldiers spare the prisoners; all swim or float ashore at Melita, where a viper fastens on Paul's hand — 'No doubt this man is a murderer' — and he shakes it off unharmed, so that the islanders change their verdict to 'he was a god', and Publius's father is healed.
summary.zh: 被「友拉革羅」狂風拋蕩十四日，不見日頭星辰，得救的指望都絕了——保羅卻在眾人中宣告夜間天使的話：「保羅，不要害怕，你必定站在該撒面前；並且與你同船的人，神都賜給你了。」船擱淺，兵士保全囚犯；全船二百七十六人或游或浮抵岸。保羅拾柴生火，毒蛇咬住其手——「這人必是個兇手」——他竟甩進火裏毫無損傷，島人改口說他是神；部百流的父親亦蒙醫治。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The sea-voyage is the most detailed itinerary in Acts; the viper scene is a classic sign.

passages.text: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon. And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive. And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship; and the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship. And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away. But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me. And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man's life among you, but of the ship. For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve, saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.
passages.zh: 不多幾時，狂風從島上撲下來；那風名叫友拉革羅。船被風抓住，敵不住風，我們就任風颳去。我們被風浪逼得甚急，第二天眾人就把貨物拋在海裡；到第三天，他們又親手把船上的器具拋棄了。太陽和星辰多日不顯露，又有狂風大浪催逼，我們得救的指望就都絕了。眾人多日沒有吃什麼，保羅就出來站在他們中間，說：「眾位，你們本該聽我的話。現在我還勸你們放心，你們的性命一個也不失喪，惟獨失喪這船。因我所屬所事奉的神，他的使者昨夜站在我旁邊，說：『保羅，不要害怕，你必定站在該撒面前，並且與你同船的人，神都賜給你了。』」

passages.text: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore. And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves. And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape. But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and they escaped all safe to land.
passages.zh: 到了天亮，他們不認識那地方，但見一個海灣，有岸可登，就商議能否把船攏進去。但遇著兩水夾流的地方，就把船擱了淺；船頭膠住不動，船尾被浪的猛力衝壞。兵丁的意思要把囚犯殺了，恐怕有洑水脫逃的。但百夫長要救保羅，不准他們任意而行，於是吩咐會洑水的，先跳下水去上陸；其餘的人可以用板子或船上的零碎東西上岸。這樣，眾人都得了救，上了岸。

passages.text: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita. And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand. And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live. And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm. Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.
passages.zh: 他們脫險之後，才知道那島名叫米利大。保羅拾起一捆柴，放在火上，有一條毒蛇因為熱了出來，咬住他的手。土人看見那毒蛇懸在他手上，就彼此說：「這人必是個兇手，雖然從海裡脫險，天理還不容他活著。」他卻把那毒蛇甩在火裡，並沒有受傷。眾人等著看他腫起來，或是忽然仆倒死了；看了多時，見他無害，就轉念說：「他是個神。」

title.en: Eutychus Falls from the Third Loft
title.zh: 猶推古從三樓窗戶墜落

region.en: Troas, upper chamber
region.zh: 特羅亞，樓上聚會所

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 20

summary.en: The church meets on the first day of the week to break bread, 'ready to depart on the morrow; and he continued his speech until midnight' — and in the lamplit window sits the youth Eutychus, who 'sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.' Paul goes down, embraces him, and his life is restored; the breaking of bread resumes till daybreak, 'and they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.'
summary.zh: 七日的頭一日聚會擘餅——「保羅因為要次日起行，就講論直到半夜」——燭光中坐在窗臺的少年猶推古沉睡墜樓，「扶他起來，已經死了」。保羅下去伏在他身上抱著說「不要發慌，他的靈魂還在」；隨後回到樓上擘餅直到天亮——「有人把那童子活活的領來，他們得安慰不小。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The first-day breaking-of-bread meeting is cited for the early Lord's-day practice.

passages.text: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight. And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together. And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.
passages.zh: 七日的第一日，門徒聚在一處擘餅，保羅因為次日要起行，就與他們講論，直講到半夜。他們聚會的那座樓上，有許多燈燭。有一個少年人名叫猶推古，坐在窗臺上，困倦沉睡；保羅講了多時，少年人睡熟了，就從三層樓上掉下去，扶起他來，已經死了。

passages.text: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him. When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed. And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.
passages.zh: 保羅下去，伏在他身上，抱著他說：「你們不要發慌，他的生命還在身上。」保羅又上去，擘餅吃了，談論許久，直到天亮，這才走了。有人把那少年人活活地領來，眾人得了不少的安慰。

title.en: The Twins in the Womb: Esau and Jacob
title.zh: 母腹中的雙生：以掃與雅各

region.en: Beersheba region, Negev
region.zh: 別是巴一帶，南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 25:19-26, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Rebecca, barren for twenty years, conceives after Isaac's prayer — and the children struggle within her. God's oracle settles the nation's future: 'two nations are in thy womb... and the elder shall serve the younger'. The red, hairy Esau and the smooth heel-grasping Jacob are born.
summary.zh: 利百加不育二十年，以撒祈禱後懷孕——二子在腹中相爭。神諭定兩國之運：「兩國在你腹內……大的要服事小的。」紅髮多毛的以掃與光滑抓腳跟的雅各出生。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the LORD said unto her: 'Two nations are in thy womb, and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.' And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb. And the first came forth ruddy, all over like a hairy mantle; and they called his name Esau. And after that came forth his brother, and his hand had hold on Esau's heel; and his name was called Jacob.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 25:23-26 (public domain), lightly condensed.
passages.zh: 耶和華對她說：「兩國在你腹內，兩族要從你身上出來；這族必強於那族，將來大的要服事小的。」她生產的日子到了，腹中果然是雙子。先出來的渾身有毛，如同皮衣，他們就給他起名叫以掃。隨後又生出他的兄弟，手抓住以掃的腳跟，因此給他起名叫雅各。

title.en: A Pot of Red Stew: Jacob Buys the Birthright
title.zh: 一鍋紅湯：雅購長子名分

region.en: Beersheba region, Negev
region.zh: 別是巴一帶，南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 25:27-34, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The quiet tent-dweller Jacob cooks stew while the hunter Esau comes in famished. Jacob prices the stew at the birthright; Esau swears it away, eats, and 'despised his birthright' — the transaction that will govern both brothers' fates.
summary.zh: 安靜住帳的雅各煮湯，打獵歸來的以掃飢極。雅各以湯索長子名分；以掃起誓賣之，喫了，竟「輕看他長子的名分」——此交易定兩兄弟之命運。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Esau said: 'Behold, I am at the point to die; and what profit shall the birthright do to me?' And Jacob said: 'Swear to me first'; and he swore unto him; and he sold his birthright unto Jacob. And Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way. Thus Esau despised his birthright.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 25:32-34 (public domain).
passages.zh: 以掃說：「我將要死，這長子的名分於我有什麼益處呢？」雅各說：「你今日先對我起誓吧。」以掃就對他起了誓，把長子的名分賣給雅各。雅各便給以掃餅和紅豆湯；以掃吃了喝了，便起來走了。這就是以掃輕看了他長子的名分。

title.en: Isaac Digs Wells and Names Peace at Beersheba
title.zh: 以撒掘井，別是巴立誓

region.en: Gerar and Beersheba, Negev
region.zh: 基拉耳與別是巴，南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 26, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: In another famine Isaac is told 'go not down into Egypt'; like his father he passes his wife off as his sister to Abimelech, is caught, and protected. Repeatedly expelled from wells he has dug, he withdraws peaceably until at Beersheba his oath and a shared feast bind the Philistine king; there the LORD appears and renews the oath of Abraham.
summary.zh: 又逢饑荒，神命以撒「不要下埃及去」；如父，他向亞比米勒稱妻為妹，被識破而受護。屢掘井屢被逐，一再退讓；至別是巴，與非利士王立誓共宴；耶和華顯現，重申亞伯拉罕之誓。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the herdmen of Gerar did strive with Isaac's herdmen, saying: 'The water is ours.' And he called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him. And they digged another well, and strove for that also; and he called the name of it Sitnah. And he removed from thence, and digged another well; and for that they strove not.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 26:20-22 (public domain); condensed.
passages.zh: 基拉耳的牧人與以撒的牧人爭競，說：「這水是我們的。」以撒就給那井起名叫埃色，因為他們與他相爭。以撒的僕人又挖了一口井，他們又為這井爭競，因此以撒給這井起名叫西提拿。以撒離開那裡，又挖了一口井，他們不為這井爭競了。

passages.text: Abimelech came with his captain to force a treaty: 'Let there be now an oath betwixt us'. Isaac made a feast, they sware and parted in peace; that same day his servants found water. He named the place Beersheba — 'well of the oath' — and there the LORD appeared by night, saying 'I am the God of Abraham thy father: fear not', renewing the covenant blessing. Paraphrase of Genesis 26:26-25 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 26:16-33 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 亞比米勒帶著他的軍長前來，要強迫立約：「現在讓我們彼此起誓吧。」以撒設宴款待，他們便起了誓，和平地分手；就在同一天，他的僕人找到了水。他給那地方起名叫別是巴——「起誓之井」——上主就在那裡夜間向他顯現，說：「我是你父親亞伯拉罕的神，不要懼怕」，並重申了聖約的祝福。改寫自《創世記》26:26-25（JPS 1917）；並非逐字照錄。

title.en: The Stolen Blessing: Isaac, Jacob, and Esau
title.zh: 竊取祝福：以撒雅各以掃

region.en: Beersheba region, Negev
region.zh: 別是巴一帶，南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 27, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Blind old Isaac asks Esau for venison before giving him the deathbed blessing. Rebecca overheard and directs Jacob in goatskins and borrowed robes; Isaac's hands smell of 'the smell of a field which the LORD hath blessed', and he blesses Jacob by mistake. Esau arrives too late, weeps a great and exceeding bitter cry, and only a lesser blessing remains — so he hates Jacob and resolves to kill him.
summary.zh: 目盲老以撒命以掃獻野味後受臨終祝福。利百加竊聞，令雅各披山羊皮衣扮兄；以撒嗅其香，「如耶和華賜福之田」，遂誤祝雅各。以掃遲至，放聲大慟，僅得次等祝福；於是恨雅各，圖殺之。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said: 'The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.' And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau's hands; so he blessed him.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 27:22-23 (public domain).
passages.zh: 雅各走近他父親以撒；以撒摸了他，說：「聲音是雅各的聲音，手卻是以掃的手。」以撒沒有認出他來，因為他的手上有毛，像他哥哥以掃的手一樣；於是就給他祝福了。

passages.text: Jacob lied outright — 'I am Esau thy firstborn' — served the savoury meat, and received the blessing: heaven's dew, fatness of earth, nations bowing, cursers cursed. Esau returned, and 'when Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob... Esau his son cried with an exceeding great and bitter cry': 'Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?' Isaac gave him fatness of earth and the sword's life, adding the prophecy that the yoke would one day be broken from his neck. Esau consoled himself by planning Jacob's death; Rebecca sent her younger son away to her brother Laban's house. Paraphrase of Genesis 27:24-45 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 27:24-45 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 雅各公然撒謊——「我是你的長子以掃」——端上美味，領受了祝福：天上的甘露、地上的肥美、萬國向他跪拜、咒詛他的必受咒詛。以掃回來了，「以撒為雅各祝福完畢以後……他兒子以掃就放聲大哭，哭得極其悲痛」：「你沒有為我留下一份祝福嗎？」以撒給了他地上的肥美和靠刀劍度日的生活，又加上預言說，那軛終有一日要從他頸上斷開。以掃以謀劃殺害雅各來安慰自己；利百加便打發她的小兒子前往她哥哥拉班的家。改寫自《創世記》27:24-45（JPS 1917）；並非逐字照錄。

title.en: Jacob's Ladder at Bethel
title.zh: 雅各的天梯在伯特利

region.en: Bethel, hill country of Canaan
region.zh: 伯特利，迦南山地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 28:10-22, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Fleeing his brother, Jacob sleeps at 'the place' with a stone for pillow and dreams of a stairway set on earth with angels ascending and descending on it. Above it stands the LORD, renewing Abraham's promise; waking, Jacob says 'Surely the LORD is in this place, and I knew it not', names it Bethel, and vows a tenth of all he has.
summary.zh: 逃兄的雅各在「那地方」以石為枕而眠，夢見梯立於地，天使在梯上上去下來。耶和華立於其上，重申亞伯拉罕之應許；醒而曰「這地方我竟不知道」，名之伯特利，並許什一奉獻。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a standing-stone (matzevah) etiology for Bethel's sanctuary; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it. And, behold, the LORD stood beside him, and said: 'I am the LORD, the God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 28:12-13 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他作夢，見有一個梯子立在地上，梯子的頂端通天；又見神的天使在梯子上上去下來。看哪，上主站在他旁邊，說：「我是上主，你父親亞伯拉罕的神，也是以撒的神：你所躺臥之地，我要賜給你和你的後裔。」

passages.text: Jacob awoke in awe: 'How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God'. He set the stone as a pillar, poured oil on it, and vowed: if God kept him on the road and brought him home in peace, 'then shall the LORD be my God', this stone God's house, and a tenth of all his. The dream-strairway remains the image of traffic between heaven and earth in Jewish and Christian tradition alike. Paraphrase of Genesis 28:16-22 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 28:16-22 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 雅各醒來，心生敬畏：「這地方何等可畏！這裡不是別的，正是神的殿。」他把那石頭立作柱子，澆油在其上，並許願說：若神保佑他一路平安、領他平平安安回家，「上主就必作我的神」，這石頭必作神的殿，凡他所擁有的，他必獻上十分之一。這夢中的階梯，在猶太與基督宗教傳統中 alike 始終是天地之間往來的意象。改寫自《創世記》28:16-22（JPS 1917）；並非逐字照錄。

title.en: Jacob Meets Rachel at the Well of Haran
title.zh: 雅各井旁遇拉結

region.en: Well of Haran, Aram-naharaim
region.zh: 哈蘭井旁，亞蘭拿哈蘭

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 29:1-12, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Jacob arrives at a well in the East where flocks wait for a stone too heavy for one man. He asks the shepherds for Laban's whereabouts; as he speaks, Rachel arrives with her father's sheep. Jacob rolls the stone away with one effort, waters the flock, and kisses her — weeping aloud at finding his kinswoman.
summary.zh: 雅各至東方井旁，羊群待石，一人不能移。雅各問牧者拉班所在；言語間拉結驅羊而至。雅各一舉移石，飲羊，與拉結親嘴——認得親族，放聲而哭。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Jacob rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother's brother. And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept. And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's brother (kinsman), and that he was Rebecca's son; and she ran and told her father.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 29:10-12 (public domain), lightly condensed.
passages.zh: 雅各把石頭從井口滾開，飲了他母親的哥哥拉班的羊群。雅各與拉結親吻，放聲而哭。雅各告訴拉結，他是她父親的親屬，是利百加的兒子；拉結就跑回去告訴她父親。

title.en: The Deceiver Deceived: Seven Years for Rachel, Then Leah
title.zh: 欺人者受欺：七年得拉結，先得利亞

region.en: Haran, Aram-naharaim
region.zh: 哈蘭，亞蘭拿哈蘭

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 29:13-30, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Jacob serves seven years for Rachel, 'and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her'. At the wedding night Laban substitutes the veiled elder daughter Leah; in the morning Jacob cries 'Why hast thou beguiled me?' and must serve seven more years — the trickster of the birthright cheated exactly as he cheated.
summary.zh: 雅各為拉結服事七年，「因深愛拉結，就看這七年如同幾天」。婚夜拉班以蒙面之長女利亞代之；晨起雅各呼曰「你為什麼欺哄我？」須再服事七年——昔日欺父賣名者，今遭同等之欺。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her. Laban gathered the men of the place and made a feast; in the evening he gave Jacob Leah his daughter, and Jacob went in to her. In the morning, 'behold, it was Leah', and Jacob demanded an explanation; Laban answered that the elder must marry first. 'Fulfil her week, and we will give thee this also' — so Jacob completed the bridal week and took Rachel too, serving Laban seven years more. Paraphrase of Genesis 29:22-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 29:20 (public domain). / Paraphrase of Genesis 29:22-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 雅各為拉結服事了七年；因他深愛拉結，這七年在他看來不過幾天。拉班召集了那地方的人，擺設筵席；到了晚上，他將女兒利亞交給雅各，雅各便與她同房。到了早晨，「不料，竟是利亞」，雅各便要求一個解釋；拉班回答說，大女兒必須先出嫁。「你為她滿了這七日，我們就把這個也給你」——於是雅各滿了那新婚的七日，也娶了拉結，又為拉班再服事七年。改述《創世記》29:22-30（JPS 1917）；非逐字照錄。

title.en: The Sons Are Born: Names from the Nursery of Rivalry
title.zh: 眾子出生：相爭搖籃中的命名

region.en: Haran, Aram-naharaim
region.zh: 哈蘭，亞蘭拿哈蘭

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 29:31-30:13, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: God 'opened' the unloved Leah's womb and closed Rachel's; a naming war in verse follows — Reuben ('the LORD hath looked upon my affliction'), Simeon ('He heard'), Levi ('this time will my husband be joined unto me'), Judah ('this time will I praise the LORD'). Rachel envies and gives Jacob her handmaid Bilhah for Dan and Naphtali; Leah answers with Zilpah for Gad and Asher.
summary.zh: 神使失寵的利亞生育，閉拉結之腹；遂展開命名之詩——流便（「耶和華看見我的苦情」）、西緬（「耶和華聽見」）、利未（「這回丈夫必與我聯合」）、猶大（「這回我要讚美耶和華」）。拉結妒而以辟拉予雅各生但拿弗他利；利亞以悉帕生迦得亞設。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The naming verses are the tribal etiologies of Israel's twelve sons.

passages.text: And Leah conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Reuben; for she said: 'Because the LORD hath looked upon my affliction; for now my husband will love me.' And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said: 'Because the LORD hath heard that I am hated, He hath therefore given me this son also'; and she called his name Simeon.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 29:32-33 (public domain).
passages.zh: 利亞懷孕生子，就給他起名叫流便；因為她說：「耶和華看見了我的苦情；如今我丈夫必愛我。」她又懷孕生子，說：「耶和華因為聽見我失寵，所以又賜給我這個兒子」；就給他起名叫西緬。

passages.text: Third came Levi, 'now this time will my husband be joined unto me'; fourth, Judah — 'this time will I praise the LORD', the name of Israel's royal tribe. When Rachel saw she bore none, she gave Bilhah to Jacob as surrogate; Bilhah bore Dan ('God hath judged me') and Naphtali ('wrestlings of God'). Leah, no longer bearing, answered with Zilpah's Gad ('a troop cometh') and Asher ('happy am I'). Paraphrase of Genesis 29:34-30:13 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 29:34-30:13 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 第三個是利未，「如今這一次我丈夫必與我聯合」；第四個是猶大——「這一次我要讚美耶和華」，這便是以色列王族的名字。拉結見自己沒有生子，就把辟拉給雅各作代孕之母；辟拉生了但（「神伸了我的冤」）和拿弗他利（「我與神較力」）。利亞不再生育，便以悉帕所生的迦得（「萬幸」）和亞設（「我有福了」）作為回應。改述《創世記》29:34-30:13（JPS 1917）；非逐字照錄。

title.en: The Mandrake Bargain and the Birth of Issachar and Zebulun
title.zh: 風茄交易與以薩迦西布倫出生

region.en: Wheat harvest, Haran
region.zh: 割麥之時，哈蘭

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 30:14-21, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Reuben finds mandrakes — the love-apples of folklore — in the wheat harvest; Rachel asks for them, and Leah's answer is barbed: 'Wouldst thou take my son's mandrakes...?' The sisters trade: Rachel sells a night with Jacob for the fruit, and Leah bears a fifth and sixth son, Issachar and Zebulun, plus daughter Dinah. Rachel, at last, 'remembered' God and bore Joseph.
summary.zh: 流便割麥時得風茄——民間傳說之情果；拉結求之，利亞譏曰：「你為你兒子的風茄……？」姊妹交易：拉結以一夜易果；利亞生第五第六子——以薩迦、西布倫，並女底拿。拉結終蒙「眷顧」，生約瑟。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Motif 'folk-magic' interpretive for the mandrake love-charm lore (cf. Song 7:13).

passages.text: And Rachel said to Leah: 'Give me, I pray thee, of thy son's mandrakes.' And she said unto her: 'Is it a small matter that thou hast taken my husband? and wouldest thou take away my son's mandrakes also?' And Rachel said: 'Therefore he shall lie with thee tonight for thy son's mandrakes.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 30:14-15 (public domain).
passages.zh: 拉結對利亞說：「請把你兒子的風茄給我一些。」利亞對她說：「你奪了我的丈夫還算小事嗎？你又要奪我兒子的風茄嗎？」拉結說：「因此，為你兒子的風茄，今夜他可以與你同寢。」

passages.text: Jacob, told of the bargain, lay with Leah, who bore Issachar ('a reward', 'hire') and Zebulun ('dwelling') and afterwards Dinah. Then 'God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and opened her womb', and she bore Joseph, saying 'The LORD shall add to me another son'. Paraphrase of Genesis 30:16-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 30:16-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 雅各得知這樁交易，便與利亞同寢，利亞就生了以薩迦（「價值」、「雇價」）和西布倫（「同住」），之後又生了底拿。後來「神顧念拉結，應允了她，使她能生育」，她就生了約瑟，說：「願耶和華再給我添一個兒子。」改述《創世記》30:16-24（JPS 1917）；非逐字照錄。

title.en: The Speckled Flocks: Jacob Outwits Laban
title.zh: 斑點羊群：雅各勝拉班

region.en: Haran, Aram-naharaim
region.zh: 哈蘭，亞蘭拿哈蘭

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 30:25-43, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Jacob asks only the speckled, spotted, and dark cattle as his wage; Laban agrees — then removes them all. Jacob answers with peeled wands before the watering troughs (folk selective breeding) and by breeding the strongest animals, 'and the man increased exceedingly' — until Laban's sons grow angry and Laban's face turns against him.
summary.zh: 雅各只求有斑有紋的牲畜為工價；拉班應允——隨即盡除去。雅各以削皮枝置水槽前（民間擇配法），又擇強壯者配種，「就極其發大」——直至拉班眾子怒而拉班色變。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Jacob took him rods of fresh poplar, and of the almond and of the plane-tree; and peeled white streaks in them, laying the white which was in the rods before the flocks in the gutters at the watering troughs where the flocks came to drink. And the flocks conceived before the rods; and the flocks brought forth straked, speckled, and spotted.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 30:37-39 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 雅各取了新生的楊樹枝、杏樹枝和楓樹枝，將枝上的皮剝出白色的條紋，把枝中白色的部分顯露出來，插在羊群前的水溝裡、飲羊的水槽中，就是羊群來喝水的地方。羊群在枝子前交配；羊群就生出有紋的、有斑的和有點的。

passages.text: Laban changed Jacob's wages ten times, but the angel of God later told Jacob in a dream that He had seen Laban's dealings. Jacob bred only the strong among the speckled, putting his own flocks apart, 'so the feebler were Laban's, and the stronger Jacob's'; the man grew very rich in flocks, men-servants, maids, camels, and asses. Paraphrase of Genesis 30:41-43 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 30:41-43 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 拉班十次更改雅各的工價，但神的天使後來在夢中告訴雅各，祂已看見拉班的所作所為。雅各只讓羊群中肥壯的來交配，把自己的羊群另放一處，「這樣，瘦弱的就歸拉班，肥壯的就歸雅各」；這人因羊群、僕婢、駱駝和驢而極其富有。改寫自《創世記》30:41-43（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: The Flight from Laban and the Pillar at Mizpah
title.zh: 逃離拉班與米斯巴之柱

region.en: Mizpah, Gilead highlands
region.zh: 米斯巴，基列山地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 31, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Told in a dream to 'return unto the land of thy fathers', Jacob slips away with his family while Laban is shearing sheep; Rachel steals her father's household teraphim and hides them in the camel's saddle. Laban pursues, searches the tents, and misses the idols in his daughter's saddle — then the two make a watch-peace at Mizpah: 'The LORD watch between me and thee, when we are absent one from another.'
summary.zh: 雅各夢中得諭「回你父親之地」，趁拉班剪羊毛攜家而逃；拉結竊父家神像藏於駝鞍。拉班追至，搜帳不得——偶像正藏其女鞍中。二人在米斯巴立守望之約：「願耶和華在你我中間鑒察。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Laban said to Jacob: 'What hast thou done, that thou hast stolen away unawares to me, and carried away my daughters as captives of the sword? ... Wherefore didst thou flee secretly, and steal away from me; and didst not tell me, that I might have sent thee away with mirth, and with songs, with tabret, and with harp?'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 31:26-27 (public domain), ellipsis marks omitted clause.
passages.zh: 拉班對雅各說：「你做了什麼事呢？你背著我偷走了，又把我的女兒們帶走，如同用刀劍擄去的一般。……你為什麼暗暗地逃跑，偷著走，並不告訴我，叫我可以歡樂、唱歌、擊鼓、彈琴地送你回去呢？」

passages.text: Laban searched Rachel's tent and found nothing — she sat on the camel's saddle and pleaded the custom of women. Enraged, Jacob recited twenty years of service, losses, and Laban's wage-cheating; Laban proposed a covenant. They raised a heap of stones and a pillar at Galeed/Mizpah, swore by the God of Abraham and the god of Nahor, and parted with a feast — Jacob returning toward Canaan with a family of eleven sons. Paraphrase of Genesis 31:34-54 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 31:34-54 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 拉班搜了拉結的帳棚，什麼也沒找到——她坐在駱駝的鞍上，以婦人的習俗為由推託。雅各憤而陳述二十年來的服事、所受的損失，以及拉班如何欺騙他的工價；拉班於是提議立約。他們在迦累得／米斯巴立起一堆石頭和一根柱子，指著亞伯拉罕的神和拿鶴的神起誓，並以筵席分別——雅各帶著十一個兒子的家眷返回迦南。改寫自《創世記》31:34-54（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: The All-Night Wrestle at Peniel
title.zh: 毘努伊勒通宵摔跤

region.en: Ford of Jabbok, Gilead
region.zh: 雅博渡口，基列

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 32:23-33, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Left alone at night at the ford of Jabbok, Jacob wrestles a 'man' until the rising of the sun; the stranger touches the hollow of his thigh and demands release, but Jacob answers: 'I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.' He receives the name Israel — 'thou hast striven with God and with men, and hast prevailed' — and limps for the rest of his life.
summary.zh: 夜半獨處雅博渡口，雅各與一「人」摔跤直到日出；那人摸其大腿窩，求離去，雅各答：「你不給我祝福，我就不容你去。」遂得新名以色列——「你與神與人較力，都得了勝」——終身跛行。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Also explains the Israelite food custom of not eating the thigh sinew.

passages.text: And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was strained, as he wrestled with him. And he said: 'Let me go, for the day breaketh.' And he said: 'I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 32:24-26 (public domain).
passages.zh: 只剩下雅各一人；有一個人與他摔跤，直到黎明。那人見自己勝不過他，就摸了他的大腿窩；雅各的大腿窩正在摔跤的時候就扭了。那人說：「天黎明了，容我去吧。」雅各說：「你不給我祝福，我就不容你去。」

passages.text: 'What is thy name?' — 'Jacob.' — 'Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel; for thou hast striven with God and with men, and hast prevailed.' Jacob named the place Peniel, 'the face of God', for he had seen God face to face and lived; the sun rose on him as he passed over, limping upon his thigh. 'Therefore the children of Israel eat not the sinew of the thigh which is upon the hollow of the thigh, unto this day.' Paraphrase of Genesis 32:27-33 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 32:27-33 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「你名叫什麼？」——「雅各。」——「你的名不要再叫雅各，要叫以色列；因為你與神與人較力，都得了勝。」雅各給那地方起名叫毗努伊勒，就是「神的面」，因為他面對面見了神，性命仍得保全；他經過那地時，日頭照在他身上，他的大腿卻瘸了。「故此，以色列人不吃大腿窩的筋，直到今日。」改寫自《創世記》32:27-33（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Jacob and Esau Embrace
title.zh: 雅各與以掃相擁

region.en: Road to Shechem, land of Canaan
region.zh: 往示劍之路，迦南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 33, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Dreading his brother's four hundred men, Jacob bows seven times to the earth as Esau approaches — and Esau runs to meet him, embraces him, falls on his neck, and kisses him; and they weep. The stolen blessing ends not in blood but in weeping reconciliation, refusal of gifts turned gracious, and a parting: 'let me leave... with thee some of the folk that are with me' accepted at last.
summary.zh: 雅各懼兄四百人，分七隊俯伏；以掃奔而迎之，抱其頸與之親嘴，二人哭泣。竊來的祝福不終於血而終於泣中復和；推辭的禮物終被收下，兄弟分道：「願在你我中間有一些跟從我的人。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him; and they wept. Esau asked about the children and the droves; Jacob said he had come to find grace in his lord's eyes, and pressed gifts on him — 'take, I pray thee, my blessing that is brought to thee; because God hath dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough'. They parted, Esau to Seir, Jacob to Succoth and then Shechem, where he bought ground and built an altar he called El-elohe-Israel — 'God, the God of Israel'. Paraphrase of Genesis 33:5-20 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 33:4 (public domain). / Paraphrase of Genesis 33:5-20 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 以掃跑來迎接他，將他抱住，又摟著他的頸項與他親嘴；二人就哭了。以掃問起孩子和牲畜群；雅各說他來是要在我主眼前蒙恩，並再三請他收下禮物——「求你收下我帶來給你的禮物；因為神恩待我，使我充足」。他們就此分別，以掃往西珥去，雅各往疏割去，又到了示劍，在那裡買了地，築了一座壇，起名叫伊利伊羅伊以色列——「神，以色列的神」。改寫自《創世記》33:5-20（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Dinah and the Sons of Jacob at Shechem
title.zh: 底拿與雅各眾子在示劍

region.en: Shechem, land of Canaan
region.zh: 示劍，迦南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 34, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Prince Shechem violates Jacob's daughter Dinah, then loves her. Jacob's sons answer treacherously: circumcision of every male in the city as bride-price; on the third day, while the men are sore, Simeon and Levi slaughter the city and the brothers plunder it. Jacob protests only the practical consequence — 'ye have brought trouble on me' — and the chapter ends in ominous silence.
summary.zh: 示劍王子玷辱雅各之女底拿，後而愛之。雅各眾子以詭計應之：全城男丁受割禮為聘禮；第三日，眾疼痛之際，西緬利未盡誅其城，兄弟擄掠。雅各只怪後果——「你們連累了我」——章末黯然無語。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The narrative presents the deception and massacre through the text's own morally ambiguous voice.

passages.text: And Jacob's sons came in from the field when they heard it; and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacob's daughter; for such thing ought not to be done.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 34:7 (public domain).
passages.zh: 雅各的眾子聽見了這事，就從田間回來；那些人憂傷，並且極其忿怒，因為他行了愚妄的事在以色列中，與雅各的女兒同寢；這樣的事本不當行。

passages.text: The sons answered Shechem's plea 'with guile': 'We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised' — let every male be circumcised, 'and will not their cattle and their substance and all their beasts be ours?' On the third day Simeon and Levi, Dinah's full brothers, took each man his sword and slew all the males; the rest plundered the city. Jacob said to Simeon and Levi: 'Ye have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land.' Paraphrase of Genesis 34:13-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 34:13-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 眾子以「詭詐」回答示劍的懇求：「我們不能做這事，把我們的妹妹給未受割禮的人」——讓所有的男丁都受割禮，「他們的牲畜、財物和一切牲口豈不都歸我們嗎？」到了第三天，西緬和利未，就是底拿的同母兄弟，各人拿著刀劍，殺了所有的男丁；其餘的人擄掠了那城。雅各對西緬和利未說：「你們連累我，使我在這地的居民中有了臭名。」改寫自《創世記》34:13-30（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: God at Bethel Again: Burying the Foreign Gods
title.zh: 神再於伯特利：埋葬外邦神像

region.en: Bethel, hill country of Canaan
region.zh: 伯特利，迦南山地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 35:1-15, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: God tells Jacob to go up to Bethel and dwell there. Jacob orders the household: 'Put away the strange gods that are among you' — and they hand over the teraphim and earrings, which he buries under the terebinth at Shechem. At Bethel God appears again, blesses him, and confirms: 'thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name.'
summary.zh: 神命雅各上伯特利居住。雅各命全家：「除掉你們中間的外邦神」——眾人交出神像與耳環，雅各埋於示劍橡樹下。神在伯特利再次顯現祝福，堅立其名：「你的名原是雅各，從今以後不要再叫雅各，要叫以色列。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they gave unto Jacob all the strange gods which were in their hand, and the rings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the terebinth which was by Shechem. And they journeyed; and a terror of God was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 35:4-5 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他們就把手中一切外邦的神像，和耳上的環子，都交給雅各；雅各把它們藏在示劍旁邊的篤耨香樹下。他們便起行；神使周圍的城邑都甚驚恐，他們就沒有追趕雅各的眾子。

passages.text: Jacob built an altar at Bethel — El-beth-el, 'God of Bethel', where God had revealed Himself in flight. Deborah, Rebecca's nurse, died and was buried under the oak below Bethel, called Allon-bacuth, 'oak of weeping'. God appeared again upon his return from Paddan-aram, blessed him, and re-named him Israel, repeating the older promises of nation and land. Paraphrase of Genesis 35:6-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 35:6-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 雅各在伯特利築了一座壇——伊勒伯特利，就是「伯特利的神」，就是神在他逃亡時向他顯現的地方。利百加的乳母底波拉死了，葬在伯特利下邊的橡樹下，那樹名叫亞倫巴古，就是「哭泣的橡樹」。神在他從巴旦亞蘭回來時又向他顯現，賜福給他，並重新給他起名叫以色列，重複了先前關於國民與土地的應許。改寫自《創世記》35:6-15（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Rachel Dies in Childbirth: Benjamin the Son of Sorrow
title.zh: 拉結產難而逝：便俄尼便雅憫

region.en: Road to Ephrath (Bethlehem)
region.zh: 往以法他（伯利恆）之路

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 35:16-20, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Rachel travails hard on the road to Ephrath; the midwife tells her 'this is also a son'. Dying, she names him Ben-oni, 'son of my sorrow'; Jacob renames him Benjamin, 'son of the right hand'. Jacob sets a pillar on her grave 'which is there unto this day', and Rachel's tomb by Bethlehem becomes a shrine of memory — and of biblical prophecy's weeping mother.
summary.zh: 拉結於往以法他路上產難；收生婆曰：「又得一子。」臨終名子便俄尼，「憂患之子」；雅各改名便雅憫，「右手之子」。雅各立柱於其墳，「直到今日」——伯利恆旁拉結之墓遂成記憶之所，亦是聖經預言中哭泣之母。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Rachel's tomb remains a contested pilgrimage site; record describes text only.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when she was in hard labour, that the mid-wife said unto her: 'Fear not; for now thou shalt have another son.' And it came to pass, as her soul was in departing — for she died — that she called his name Ben-oni; but his father called him Benjamin. And Rachel died, and was buried in the way to Ephrath — the same is Bethlehem.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 35:17-19 (public domain), lightly condensed.
passages.zh: 她生產艱難的時候，收生婆對她說：「不要怕；你現在又要得一個兒子了。」她靈魂將要離去的時候——因為她死了——就給他起名叫便俄尼；但他父親給他起名叫便雅憫。拉結死了，葬在往以法他的路上——以法他就是伯利恆。

title.en: Cain and Abel: The Raven Teaches Burial (Qur'an)
title.zh: 該隱與亞伯：烏鴉教埋葬（古蘭經）

region.en: Mecca / Medina recitation contexts (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥加／麥地那誦經語境（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-Ma'idah 5:27-31; Rodwell translation 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 5:27-31

summary.en: Recite to them the story of Adam's two sons: each offers a sacrifice, God accepts Abel's and rejects Cain's, who declares he will kill his brother. Abel's hands stay clean — 'God accepts only from the God-fearing'; Cain kills him, and a raven sent by God scratches the earth to show him how to bury his brother's body, and he repents in shame.
summary.zh: 古蘭經囑述阿丹二子之事：各獻祭品，真主納亞伯之祭而拒該隱之祭；該隱遂起殺弟之心。亞伯自言只敬畏者之祭被納；該隱殺之，真主遣烏鴉刨土，示以埋葬之法，該隱慚悔。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; presented via a public-domain nineteenth-century translation for comparative study, not as religious claim. Motif tagging is interpretive; 'origin-of-death' here marks the first human murder, not a universal death-origin myth.

passages.text: Recite to them truly the story of the two sons of Adam. Each of them made an offering, and it was accepted from one of them and not accepted from the other. The rejected brother said, 'I will surely slay thee.' The other answered, 'God accepts only from the God-fearing; even if thou stretch out thy hand against me to slay me, I will not stretch out mine against thee, for I fear God, the Lord of all creatures. I would rather thou shouldst bear my sin and thine own, and become an inmate of the Fire — such is the reward of the unjust.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 5:27-29 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你要將亞當兩個兒子的故事，真實地講給他們聽。他們各人獻了一份祭品，從其中一人被接納，從另一人卻不被接納。被拒絕的兄弟說：「我必定要殺你。」另一人回答說：「神只接納敬畏神的人；即使你伸手要殺我，我也不會伸手殺你，因為我敬畏神，萬物的主宰。我寧願你擔負我的罪和你自己的罪，而成為火獄的居民——這是不義者的報應。」

passages.text: His soul persuaded him to slay his brother, and he slew him, and became one of the lost. Then God sent a raven which scratched in the ground to show him how he might hide his brother's naked corpse. 'Woe is me!' he cried, 'am I unable to be like this raven, and to hide the body of my brother?' And he became one of the repentant. On account of this We commanded the children of Israel that whoever slays a soul, unless for a soul slain or for corruption done in the earth, it shall be as if he slew all mankind; and whoever saves one alive, it shall be as if he saved all mankind.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 5:30-32 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他的靈魂慫恿他殺害自己的兄弟，他便殺了他，成了虧折的人之一。隨後，真主派遣一隻烏鴉在地上刨土，向他顯示如何掩埋兄弟赤裸的屍體。他喊道：「哀哉！我竟不能像這隻烏鴉一樣，掩埋我兄弟的屍體嗎？」於是他成了悔罪的人之一。因此，我命令以色列的子孫：凡殺一命者，除非因一命被殺或因地上的敗壞，就如同殺了全人類；凡救活一命者，就如同救活了全人類。

title.en: Hud Sent to 'Ad: The Wind That Destroyed a Nation
title.zh: 呼德遣於阿德：滅族的暴風

region.en: Al-Ahqaf, southern Arabia, dune country of the vanished 'Ad (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 南阿拉伯阿赫格夫沙丘地帶（阿德人故地；象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs al-A'raf 7:65-72, Hud 11:50-60; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Suras 7 and 11

summary.en: To 'Ad, a people who built strong places in every valley and carved houses from the mountains, God sent their brother Hud, saying 'Worship God; you have no god but Him.' The chiefs answered that strength and violence were theirs, and asked which of the gods he would have them worship. Hud called them to ask pardon and to trust; they mocked him as a fool and liar — and when the fateful day came, a piercing wind blew seven nights and eight days, and the mightiest, arrogant people were left like hollow palm-trunks.
summary.zh: 阿德人於每谷建堅堡，自山中鑿屋；真主遣其兄弟呼德教之敬拜真主。諸侯自誇強力暴行，譏呼德為愚者謊者。報應之日，烈風連吹七夜八日，強傲之民如棕櫚枯幹，仆地而亡。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition, presented via public-domain translation; the 'Ad destruction is treated within Islam as a historical warning, not myth.

passages.text: And to 'Ad We sent their brother Hud. He said, 'O my people, worship God: ye have no other god than Him. Will ye not fear Him?' The unbelieving chiefs of his people answered, 'We see thee in folly, and we think thou art one of the liars. Shall we quit our gods at thy word? We see not that thou hast spoken truth; thou art one of the mockers.' He said, 'O my people, there is no folly in me; I am a messenger from the Lord of all creatures. The messages of my Lord I bring you, and I am your faithful counsellor.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:65-68 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我派遣了他們的兄弟呼德去教化阿德人。他說：「我的族人啊，你們當崇拜真主：除祂之外，你們別無他神。你們難道不敬畏祂嗎？」他族人中不信道的首領們回答說：「我們看你確是愚妄的，我們認為你是一個說謊的人。我們豈能因你的話而捨棄我們的神明？我們看不出你說了真話；你不過是一個嘲弄者。」他說：「我的族人啊，我並非愚妄；我是萬物的主的使者。我向你們傳達我主的使命，我是你們忠實的勸告者。」

passages.text: 'Do ye build a landmark on every high place to amuse yourselves? And get you strong places, haply to abide for ever? And when you seize, do you seize as tyrants? Fear God and me, and fear Him who hath aided you with what ye know — with cattle and children and gardens and springs.' Then they said, 'Thou hast come to turn us from what our fathers worshipped, and to obtain the chiefdom in the land; we believe thee not.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 26:128-136 combined with 11:50-62 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「你們豈要在每一處高地建築標誌以自娛？你們豈要建造堅固的居所，或許能永居其中？你們捉拿人時，豈要像暴君一樣捉拿嗎？你們當敬畏真主和我，當敬畏那以你們所知的——牲畜、子嗣、園圃和泉源——援助你們的主。」於是他們說：「你來是要使我們背離我們祖先所崇拜的，並要在這地方取得統治權；我們不相信你。」

passages.text: And when the fateful day came upon them, a piercing wind blew during seven nights and eight days, and it laid those people low; and thou mightest have seen them lying prostrate as though they had been trunks of hollow palm-trees. 'Ad believed not their Lord: away with 'Ad, the people of Hud! And We saved him and those who believed with him by Our mercy, from an ignominious chastisement.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 11:58-67, 69:6-7 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當那注定之日降臨他們時，一陣刺骨的狂風吹了七夜八日，把那群人吹倒在地；你或許會看見他們倒臥著，彷彿是空心棕櫚樹的樹幹。「阿德人不信他們的主：阿德人——呼德的族人——滅亡了！我以我的慈憫，拯救了他和與他一同信道的人，免於可恥的懲罰。

title.en: Salih and the She-Camel of Thamud
title.zh: 撒利哈與賽莫德人的母駝

region.en: Hijr / Al-Hijr, carved rock dwellings of Thamud, north Arabia (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 北阿拉伯希季爾岩鑿居所（賽莫德人故地；象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs 7:73-79, 11:61-68, 26:141-159; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Suras 7, 11, 26

summary.en: To Thamud, who cut grand houses from the mountains, God sent their brother Salih with a sign: a she-camel of God, to be let alone to pasture on God's earth and to drink in turn with the people at the rock. Nine wicked men hamstrung her; Salih said, 'Enjoy your dwellings three days — this is a threat that shall not be belied'; and the cry of punishment seized them, and they lay dead in their houses, overthrown in their own dwellings.
summary.zh: 賽莫德人鑿山為巨宅；真主遣其兄弟撒利哈，並以真主母駝為兆，令其任牧於主地，與民輪流飲水。九個惡徒斷其腳筋；撒利哈言：『你們可居宅三日，此約必不爽。』刑聲臨之，眾仆死於宅中。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation used for comparative study.

passages.text: And to Thamud We sent their brother Salih. He said, 'O my people, worship God: ye have no other god than Him. Now hath a clear sign come to you from your Lord — this she-camel of God is a sign to you. Let her alone to feed on God's earth, and touch her with no harm, lest a grievous chastisement seize you.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:73 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我派遣了他們的兄弟撒立哈去教化賽莫德人。他說：「我的族人啊，你們當崇拜真主：除祂之外，你們別無他神。如今從你們的主確已有一個明顯的蹟象降臨你們——這頭真主的母駝是給你們的蹟象。任她在真主的大地上吃草，你們不可傷害她，以免嚴厲的懲罰降臨你們。」

passages.text: And Salih said, 'She shall have her portion of water, and ye shall have your portion of water on an appointed day; and drive her not to harm with any harm of the day, lest the punishment of a great day seize you.' But the people hamstrung her and denied themselves the mercy of God's sign: 'Call down upon us what thou dost threaten, if thou art one of the sent.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 54:28-29 and 26:155-157 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 撒立哈說：「她有一份飲水，你們也有一份飲水，在指定的日子；你們不可為害而驅趕她，以免大日的懲罰降臨你們。」但那些人宰割了她，並使自己失去了真主蹟象的慈憫：「你若真是被派遣的使者，就把你所警告的降給我們吧。」

passages.text: Salih said, 'Enjoy yourselves in your dwellings three days more: this is a threat that shall not be belied.' And when Our commandment came, We saved Salih and those who believed with him, by a mercy from Us, from the ignominy of that day. Thy Lord is the Strong, the Mighty; and the cry of punishment overtook those who dealt unjustly, and in the morning they lay dead in their houses, prostrate as though they had never dwelt in them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 11:65-67 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 撒立哈說：『你們在自己的住處再享受三天吧：這是一個不會被否認的警告。』當我的命令降臨時，我以我的慈憫，從那日的恥辱中拯救了撒立哈和與他一同信道的人。你的主確是強有力的、萬能的；刑罰的呼喊襲擊了那些行不義的人，清晨他們便倒斃在自己的房屋中，俯伏在地，彷彿他們從未在其中居住過。

title.en: Lut's Guests: Angels in the City of Sodom
title.zh: 魯特之客：天使入所多瑪城

region.en: Southern Dead Sea plain (Sodom; symbolic pin)
region.zh: 死海南平原（所多瑪故地；象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs 11:69-83, 15:51-77, 7:80-84; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Suras 11, 15, 7

summary.en: Abraham's angel-guests travel on to Lut, who is grieved by them and shrinks from the task of protecting them. The men of the city come crowding with evil intent; the angels say, 'Fear not — we are sent to the guilty people'; they tell Lut to travel by night with his family, 'and let none of you turn round,' for a cry will strike the wicked at dawn, and the city is rained on with stones of baked clay.
summary.zh: 亞伯拉罕的天使客人續行至魯特處，魯特為之愁苦，憂難保護。城人聚集行惡；天使言：『勿懼——我們是遣往惡民者。』囑魯特夜間攜眷而行，『勿回頭』；黎明刑聲擊惡人，天雨燒結之石。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; presented via public-domain translation; historical destruction narrative within Islam, not myth.

passages.text: And when the messengers came to the family of Lut, he said to them, 'Verily ye are strangers.' They said, 'Nay, but we have come to thee about that concerning which they doubted; and we have come to thee with the truth, and we are surely truthful messengers. Travel with thy family in the night, and follow thou after them, and let none of you turn round; and go whither ye are commanded.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 15:61-65 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當使者們來到魯特的家時，他對他們說：『你們確是陌生人。』他們說：『不然，我們是為他們所懷疑的事來見你的；我們帶著真理來見你，我們確是誠實的使者。你當帶著你的家人在夜間出發，你跟在他們後面走，你們中任何人都不許回頭；你們當往所命令的地方去。』

passages.text: And the people of the city came joyously to him. He said, 'These are my guests; disgrace me not, and fear God, and shame me not.' They said, 'Have we not forbidden thee to entertain any of the nations?' And those who were in the city said, 'We will surely drive them out, or they shall return unto us.' Then We saved him and his family, all save his wife, who was left behind; and We rained on them a rain — and evil was the rain of those who had been warned.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 27:55-58 and 7:82-84 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 城裡的居民歡歡喜喜地來到他那裡。他說：『這些是我的客人；你們不要使我蒙羞，你們當敬畏真主，不要使我羞愧。』他們說：『我們不是曾禁止你接待任何人嗎？』城裡的人說：『我們必定把他們驅逐出去，否則他們必須回到我們這裡來。』於是我們拯救了他和他的家人，唯有他的妻子除外，她留在了後方；我們降下大雨在他們身上——被警告者的雨真惡劣。

passages.text: The angels said, 'O Lut, verily we are messengers of thy Lord; they shall not touch thee. And when the commandment of thy Lord came, We made those in it the overturned; and We rained on them stones of baked clay, one on another, marked with thy Lord, nor are they far from the evildoers.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 11:81-83 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 天使們說：『魯特啊，我們確是你主的使者；他們絕不能傷害你。』當你主的命令降臨時，我們使那城中的人天翻地覆；我們降下層層疊疊的陶土石在他們身上，那些石頭上帶著你主的印記，它們離行惡的人並不遠。

title.en: Shu'ayb and the Merchants of Midian
title.zh: 舒阿卜與米甸的商人

region.en: Madyan, oasis towns of NW Arabia (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 西北阿拉伯米甸綠洲（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs 7:85-93, 11:84-95, 26:177-190; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Suras 7, 11, 26

summary.en: To Midian God sent their brother Shu'ayb: 'Give just weight and measure, defraud not men of their goods, and do not evil in the land after it has been set in order.' The people answer that their fathers' religion is enough and that his prayer would be their ruin; Shu'ayb warns that a day is coming when a disgraceful punishment will strike the liars, and a scorching wind, 'the punishment of the day of shadowing heat,' leaves them as though they had never dwelt there.
summary.zh: 真主遣舒阿卜於米甸：『當以公平秤斗，勿克扣他人財物，勿於整頓之地作惡。』民答以祖宗教為足，其祈禱反為禍害。舒阿卜預言欺人者必遭恥刑；灼熱之風襲之，民如未嘗居此。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation used for comparative study.

passages.text: And to Madyan We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said, 'O my people, worship God: ye have no other god than Him. There hath come to you a clear proof from your Lord. Give weight and measure with fairness, and do not defraud men of their goods, and do not do evil in the land after it hath been set in order. This is better for you if ye are believers.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:85 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我們曾派遣他們的兄弟舒阿卜到麥德彥去。他說：『我的宗族啊，你們當崇拜真主：你們除他之外絕無別的神。從你們的主發出的明證確已降臨你們。你們當公平地給足秤量，不要剋扣人們的財物，不要在地方秩序安定之後在其中作惡。如果你們是信士，這對你們是更好的。』

passages.text: They said, 'O Shu'ayb, doth thy prayer enjoin upon thee that we should leave what our fathers worshipped, or that we should not do with our wealth what we please? Thou art surely the mild, the right-directed one.' He said, 'O my people, have I not brought you clear proofs? Ye would have me abandon what my Lord hath revealed; and how could I desire aught contrary to it? I counsel you nothing but what is right, and I am no helper for you except through God.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 11:87-88 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們說：『舒阿卜啊，你的祈禱是命令我們放棄我們祖先所崇拜的嗎？還是命令我們不可以隨意處置我們的財產呢？你確是溫和的、循規蹈矩的人。』他說：『我的宗族啊，難道我沒有帶給你們明證嗎？你們要我放棄我的主所啟示給我的嗎？我怎能違背它而有所企求呢？我只願盡力改良，我的成功只靠真主；我只信賴他，我只歸依他。』

passages.text: They schemed against him: 'We will surely drive him out and those who believe with him'; and when Our commandment came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us, and the cry of punishment seized those who dealt unjustly, and in the morning they lay in their houses prostrate, as though they had never dwelt there. Away with Madyan, as 'Thamud hath passed away!'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:88-92 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們設計陷害他：『我們必將把他和與他一同信道的人驅逐出去』；當我們的命令降臨時，我們以出自我們的慈恩拯救了舒阿卜和與他一同信道的人，而刑罰的吼聲襲擊了那些行不義的人，清晨時他們在自己的房屋中俯伏著，彷彿他們從未在那裡居住過。麥德彥滅亡了，正如『賽莫德已經逝去！』

title.en: Ibrahim Smashes the Idols: 'Ask This Big One'
title.zh: 易卜拉欣碎偶像：「問問那個大的」

region.en: Ur/Harran idol-house and the fire of Nimrod (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 烏爾／哈蘭偶像堂與努哈德之火（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs 21:51-70, 37:83-98, 6:74-79; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Suras 21, 37, 6

summary.en: Ibrahim says to his father Azar, 'Takest thou idols for gods? I see thee and thy people in manifest error'; by night he watches a star, a moon and a sun set, and says, 'I love not those that set.' At the idol-feast he cries, 'What worship ye? They hear not when ye call, and can profit you nothing.' He breaks the lesser idols, leaves the greatest, and when the people demand it he mockingly bids them ask the big one who did it — then calls on God: 'If Thou openest a way for the fire, let it not burn me,' and the fire is made cool and safe.
summary.zh: 易卜拉欣問父阿宰爾：『你以偶像為神麼？』夜觀星月日落而拒之。逢拜偶像之節，他責問眾人所拜者；碎小偶像，留最大者。眾問孰為之，他嘲答：『問那個大的。』遂呼主：『若火開路，勿使焚我』，火反涼而無害。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; presented via public-domain translation; the fire miracle is treated within Islam as history.

passages.text: When he said to his father, 'Azar, takest thou idols for gods? I see thee and thy people in a manifest error.' And thus did Ibrahim show his people the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth. And when the night overshadowed him, he saw a star, and said, 'This is my Lord'; but when it set he said, 'I love not those that set.' And when he saw the moon rising he said, 'This is my Lord'; but when it set he said, 'Unless my Lord guide me I shall surely go astray.' And when he saw the sun rising he said, 'This is greater — this is my Lord'; but when it set he said, 'O my people, verily I am clear of what ye associate with God.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 6:74-78 and 21:51-52 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當時他對他的父親說：『阿扎爾啊，你竟把偶像當作神靈嗎？我見你和你的族人確在明顯的迷誤之中。』易卜拉欣就這樣向他的族人展示了天地的主權。當黑夜籠罩他時，他看見一顆星，便說：『這是我的主』；但當它落下時，他說：『我不喜愛那些落下的。』當他看見月亮升起時，他說：『這是我的主』；但當它落下時，他說：『除非我的主引導我，我必定走入迷途。』當他看見太陽升起時，他說：『這更大——這是我的主』；但當它落下時，他說：『我的族人啊，我確與你們所配給真主的東西無干。』
