passages.text: So he broke them in pieces, all but the greatest of them, that they might return to it. 'What!' they said, 'who hath done this to our gods? Truly he is one of the unjust.' They said, 'We heard a youth make mention of them, one called Ibrahim.' He said, 'Who hath done this? Answer, if ye have sense.' They said, 'It was done by a youth, a young man, one called Ibrahim.' He said, 'Then was it ye who made these things your gods? They said, 'We found our fathers worshipping them.' He said, 'Do ye then worship what ye yourselves carve, and God created you and what ye make?'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 21:57-62 and 37:85-96 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是他把它們打得粉碎，只留下其中最大的那一個，以便他們回轉到它那裡。他們說：『怎麼！是誰對我們的神靈做了這事？他確是不義者之一。』他們說：『我們聽見一個青年提到它們，他名叫易卜拉欣。』他說：『是誰做了這事？你們若有理智，就回答吧。』他們說：『是一個青年做的，一個年輕人，名叫易卜拉欣。』他說：『那麼，是你們把這些東西當作你們的神靈嗎？』他們說：『我們發現我們的祖先崇拜它們。』他說：『那麼，你們崇拜你們自己所雕刻的，而真主創造了你們和你們所製造的嗎？』

passages.text: They said, 'Burn him and help your gods'; and they strove to lay the fire on him; but We made the fire to be cool and safe for him. They designed a plot against him, but We made them the greatest losers. 'Verily,' said he, 'I am going where my Lord will guide me. Lord, give me a righteous family.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 21:68-72 and 37:97-100 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們說：『燒死他，幫助你們的神靈吧』；他們竭力把火堆在他身上；但我們使火對他成為清涼而安全的。他們設計陷害他，但我們使他們成為最大的虧折者。他說：『我確要前往我的主將引導我的地方。主啊，求你賜我一個正直的後裔。』

title.en: The Sacrifice of Ismail: The Dream and the Ransom
title.zh: 易司馬儀之獻祭：夢與贖代

region.en: Mina valley near Mecca (traditional site of the sacrifice; symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥加附近米那谷（傳統獻祭地；象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah as-Saffat 37:99-113; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 37:99-113

summary.en: Ibrahim, having wished peace on himself and his old age, sees in a dream that he shall sacrifice his son. 'My son, I have seen in sleep that I shall sacrifice thee: now consider what thou seest right.' Ismail answers, 'My father, do what thou art bidden; thou shalt find me, please God, one of the patient.' Father and son yield themselves to God; God ransoms the boy with a grand victim, and leaves 'peace' upon Ibrahim among later generations.
summary.zh: 易卜拉欣得夢示將獻其子。他問子：『我在夢中見獻你為祭，你意如何？』易司馬儀答：『父親，行主所命；若主意欲，你必見我堅忍。』父子皆順服；真主以大牲贖之，並使易卜拉欣在後世享平安。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the dream-sacrifice underlies the festival of Id al-Adha (topic: festival story). Presented via public-domain translation.

passages.text: And he said, 'Verily I am going where my Lord will guide me. Lord, give me one of the righteous.' Wherefore We announced to him a boy endued with patience. And when he was grown, and reached the age of running with him, Ibrahim said, 'O my son, verily I have seen in sleep that I should sacrifice thee: now consider what thou seest right.' He said, 'O my father, do what thou art bidden; thou shalt find me, please God, one of the patient.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 37:99-102 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他說：『我確要前往我的主將引導我的地方。主啊，求你賜我一個正直的。』於是我們向他報以一個有耐心的男孩。當他長大，達到與他一同奔走之年齡時，易卜拉欣說：『我的兒子啊，我確在夢中看見我應犧牲你：現在你看看你認為怎樣。』他說：『我的父親啊，你奉命行事吧；若真主意欲，你將發現我是有耐心的人之一。』

passages.text: And when they had yielded themselves to God's will, and he had laid him down on his forehead, We called to him, 'O Ibrahim, thou hast indeed fulfilled the vision. Thus do We reward the righteous: this was indeed a trial manifest.' And We ransomed him with a grand victim, and We left this blessing for him among the later generations: 'Peace be on Ibrahim!'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 37:103-109 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他們倆都順服真主的旨意，而他把他放倒在他的額頭上時，我們呼喚他：『易卜拉欣啊，你確已實現了那個夢。我們就這樣報酬行善的人：這確是一個明顯的考驗。』我們以一個重大的犧牲贖回了他，我們在後世的人中為他留下了這祝福：『願平安降於易卜拉欣！』

title.en: Raising the Foundations of the Kaaba
title.zh: 易卜拉欣父子重建天房基石

region.en: Mecca, site of the Kaaba (literal pin)
region.zh: 麥加天房故址（實際定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs al-Baqarah 2:124-141, Ibrahim 14:35-41; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 2:124-131 and 14:35-41

summary.en: God tries Ibrahim with commands, and he fulfils them. 'I will make thee an imam of men'; 'And of my seed?' — 'My covenant reacheth not the evildoers.' When Ibrahim and Ismail raise the foundations of the house: 'Our Lord, accept it of us; make us Muslims, and our seed a Muslim people; and show us our rites of pilgrimage, and be merciful to us.' And they pray for a messenger in their seed to recite God's signs and teach the Book — the prayer answered in Muhammad.
summary.zh: 真主以數事試易卜拉欣，他全數履行。『我必立你為眾人之師表』——『我的子孫呢？』——『我的約不及作惡者。』父子築天房基石時祈禱：『主啊，求你悅納；使我們順服，使我們的子孫成順服之民；指示我們朝覲的儀節。』並為子孫中一位使者祈禱——即穆罕默德。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the Meccan sanctuary's foundations, celebrated in pilgrimage rites; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And when his Lord had tested Ibrahim with certain commands, and he had fulfilled them, He said, 'Verily I will make thee an imam of men.' Said he, 'And of my seed?' God said, 'My covenant reacheth not the evildoers.' And when Ibrahim and Ismail raised the foundations of the house, they prayed, 'Our Lord, accept it of us, for thou art the Hearing, the Knowing. Our Lord, make us Muslims to thee, and of our seed a people of Muslims to thee, and teach us our holy rites, and be turned towards us, for thou art the Relenting One, the Merciful.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 2:124-128 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他的主以若干命令考驗易卜拉欣，而他完成了它們時，祂說：「我必使你成為世人的伊瑪目。」他說：「也使我的一些後裔嗎？」真主說：「我的盟約不達於不義之人。」當易卜拉欣與易司馬儀立起房屋的根基時，他們祈禱說：「我們的主啊，求你接納我們吧，你確是全聽的、全知的。我們的主啊，求你使我們成為順服你的人，也使我們的一些後裔成為順服你的民族，並教導我們我們的宗教儀式，求你眷顧我們，你確是至赦的、至慈的。」

passages.text: 'Our Lord, raise up among them a messenger, one of themselves, who shall rehearse thy signs to them and teach them the Book and the Wisdom, and purify them; for thou art the Mighty, the Wise.' And who but a fool would turn from the faith of Ibrahim? Him We chose in this world, and in the next he shall be one of the just.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 2:129-130 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「我們的主啊，求你在他們中間派遣一位使者，出自他們自身，向他們宣讀你的跡象，教導他們經典與智慧，並淨化他們；你確是至剛的、至睿的。」除了愚人，誰會背離易卜拉欣的信仰呢？我在今世揀選了他，在後世他必屬於正直之人。

passages.text: When Ibrahim said, 'O my Lord, make this land secure, and turn me and my sons away from the worship of idols; save me and those born to me from worshipping idols. My Lord, forgive me and my parents and all who on the day of account shall enter my house; and forgive the believers, men and women.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 14:35-41 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當易卜拉欣說：「我的主啊，求你使這地方安寧，求你使我與我的子孫遠離崇拜偶像；求你保護我與我所生的人免於崇拜偶像。我的主啊，求你赦宥我、我的父母，以及一切在清算之日進入我家的人；並赦宥信士，無論男女。」

title.en: The Covenant of Alast: 'Am I Not Your Lord?'
title.zh: 艾萊斯之約：「我不是你們的主嗎？」

region.en: Primeval assembly before creation (symbolic pin at Mecca)
region.zh: 受造前的原初集會（象徵性定位於麥加）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-A'raf 7:172-173; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 7:172-173

summary.en: When the Lord drew forth from the children of Adam, from their loins, their seed, and made them bear witness concerning themselves: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said, 'Yes, we bear witness' — lest on the day of resurrection men should say, 'We were indeed heedless of this,' or say, 'Our fathers joined gods to God, and we were but their seed after them.' All souls answered in the primeval covenant; the prophets come to remind, not to impose.
summary.zh: 主從阿丹的背脊中取出子孫，令他們自作見證：『我不是你們的主嗎？』他們答：『不然，我們作證。』——免得復活日有人說『我們曾忽視此事』，或說『祖宗曾以物配主，我們不過是後裔』。原初之約人人曾答；列聖之來，只是提醒。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the 'covenant of alast' is a cardinal doctrine. Public-domain translation; interpretive motif tagging noted.

passages.text: And when thy Lord drew forth from the children of Adam, out of their loins, their posterity, and made them bear witness against themselves — 'Am I not your Lord?' — they said, 'Yes, we do bear witness.' Lest ye should say on the day of resurrection, 'Verily we were heedless of this'; or lest ye should say, 'Our fathers, indeed, formerly joined gods with God, and we were their posterity after them: wilt thou then destroy us for the doings of the vain ones?'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:172-173 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當你的主從阿丹的子孫的腰脊中取出他們的後裔，並使他們為自己作證——「我不是你們的主嗎？」——他們說：「是的，我們作證。」以免你們在復活之日說：「我們確曾疏忽此事」；或以免你們說：「我們的祖先從前確曾以物配主，而我們是他們之後的後裔：你豈要因那些妄為之人的所作所為而毀滅我們嗎？」

passages.text: Thus do We make clear our signs: haply they may return to us. And there were men among mankind who took for themselves equals to God, and loved them as they should love God; but they who believe love God more ardently. Had the wrongdoers but seen, when they behold the punishment, that power altogether is God's, and that God is vehement in punishing.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:174-175 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我如此闡明我的跡象，或許他們會歸返於我。人類中有些人為自己樹立與真主同等的，像愛真主那樣愛它們；但信士們愛真主更為深切。不義之人若在看見刑罰時能看見，一切權力全歸真主，真主的懲罰確是嚴厲的。

title.en: The Sabbath Fish: Swimmers on the Forbidden Day
title.zh: 安息日之魚：禁日泳現的魚群

region.en: A seaside town of the Israelites (symbolic pin, Sinai coast)
region.zh: 以色列人濱海之城（象徵性定位於西奈海岸）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-A'raf 7:163-166; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 7:163-166

summary.en: Ask them about the city that stood by the sea: its people broke the Sabbath — the fish came to them on their Sabbath-day in shoals, on other days they came not. So God made trial of them by their evil-doing. A God-fearing band said, 'Why preach ye to a people God is about to destroy?' The preachers answered that they might make a defence before their Lord, and perchance fear; and when the sinners forgot the warning, God delivered those who forbade evil and seized the wrongdoers with terrible punishment for their rebellion.
summary.zh: 問他們那座海濱之城：其民犯安息日之禁——安息日魚群成隊浮近，平日不至。真主以其惡行試之。敬畏者問：『何必教誨主將毀滅之民？』傳教者答：『或可在主前有辯詞，或能敬畏。』惡人既忘警示，主救止惡者，以極刑懲悖逆者。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation; the fish-test is a qisas-style etiological episode within the Israelite lore of the Qur'an.

passages.text: Ask them also concerning the city that stood by the sea, how its people transgressed on the Sabbath, when their fish came to them on the Sabbath-day in shoals, but on other days came not; and thus did We make trial of them because they did wickedly. And a God-fearing band among them said, 'Why warn ye a people whom God is about to destroy or to punish with a severe punishment?' They said, 'To clear ourselves before your Lord; and haply they may fear Him.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:163-164 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你也問他們關於那臨海的城市，其居民如何在安息日違法，那時他們的魚在安息日成群來到他們面前，而在別的日子卻不來；我如此考驗他們，因為他們作惡。他們中有一敬畏真主的團體說：「你們為何勸誡一個真主將要毀滅或以嚴厲刑罰懲治的民族呢？」他們說：「為在你們的主面前表明我們無罪；或許他們會敬畏祂。」

passages.text: And when they had forgotten what they were reminded of, We delivered those who forbade wrong, and We visited the evildoers with a grievous punishment because of their exceeding sin. And when they proudly persisted in that which was forbidden, We said to them, 'Be ye apes, driven away and rejected.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:165-166 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他們忘記了所受的勸誡時，我拯救了那些禁止作惡的人，並因他們過分犯罪，以嚴厲的刑罰懲治了不義的人。當他們傲慢地堅持被禁止之事時，我對他們說：『你們變成被驅逐、被棄絕的猿猴吧。』

title.en: The Cow of the Israelites: The Killer Named by the Blow
title.zh: 以色列人的母牛：擊之而兇手自明

region.en: Israelite camp after the Exodus (symbolic pin, Sinai)
region.zh: 以色列人出埃及後的營地（象徵性定位於西奈）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-Baqarah 2:67-73; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 2:67-73

summary.en: Moses tells his people that God commands them to sacrifice a heifer. They tease him: 'Makest thou a laughing-stock of us?' — and pile on qualifications, a cow neither old nor young, yellow, full of sound, unbroken, to plough the earth and water the tilth. They slaughter her at last with much ado; God says: 'Strike the slain one with part of her' — and the murdered man stands up and names his killer. 'Thus God raiseth the dead and showeth you his signs, that haply ye may be warned.'
summary.zh: 穆薩傳主命：宰一母牛。眾人嘲弄戲耍，層層加條件——不老不少、純黃、鳴聲悅耳、未曾耕田運水者。最終勉強宰之。主諭：『以牛之一部分擊死者。』被殺者遂起而指認兇手。『主如此使死人復活，示以其蹟，俾爾悟之。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the episode explains the surah's title 'The Cow'. Public-domain translation used.

passages.text: And when Moses said to his people, 'God hath commanded you to sacrifice a heifer,' they said, 'Dost thou make us a laughing-stock?' He said, 'God forbid that I should be one of the foolish.' They said, 'Pray for us to thy Lord that he would make it clear to us what her colour is.' He answered, 'God saith, The cow shall be yellow, a rich yellow, pleasing to those who see it.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 2:67-69 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當穆薩對他的族人說：『真主命令你們宰一頭母牛』時，他們說：『你把我們當作笑柄嗎？』他說：『求真主護佑，我豈可成為愚人之一。』他們說：『請為我們向你的主祈求，讓他為我們闡明她的顏色。』他回答說：『真主說，這牛應是黃色的，是濃黃的，使見者喜悅。』

passages.text: They said, 'Pray for us to thy Lord that he would make clear to us what cow she is, for the cow is alike with us; and if God will we shall be guided rightly.' Moses said, 'God saith, She shall be a cow neither old nor young, but of middle age between the two; and do ye what ye are bidden.' They said, 'Pray thy Lord to show us what her colour is to be.' He answered, 'He saith, A cow, sturdy, goodly to behold, unbroken, to plough the earth or water the tilth, a cow without blemish.' They said, 'Now hast thou brought the truth'; and they sacrificed her — though little enough they were minded to do it.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 2:70-73 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們說：『請為我們向你的主祈求，讓他為我們闡明她是怎樣的牛，因為在我們看來，牛都是一樣的；若真主意欲，我們必得正道。』穆薩說：『真主說，她應是一頭不老也不幼的牛，而是介於兩者之間的中齡牛；你們當遵命而行。』他們說：『請向你的主祈求，讓他指示我們她的顏色如何。』他回答說：『他說，是一頭健壯、悅目、未經役使、不曾耕田也不曾灌溉田地的牛，是一頭毫無瑕疵的牛。』他們說：『如今你帶來了真理』；於是他們宰了她——儘管他們本不大願意去做。

passages.text: And when ye had slain a man and contended among yourselves about him, God brought forth what ye had hidden. So We said, 'Strike the slain one with part of her.' So God raised the dead to life, and showed you his signs, that haply ye may be warned.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 2:72-73 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當時你們殺了一個人，並為他互相爭執，而真主揭露出了你們所隱瞞的。於是我們說：『用她的一部分打那被殺的人。』真主如此使死者復活，並向你們顯示他的跡象，以便你們受到勸誡。

title.en: Joseph's Dreams and the Coat of Many Colours
title.zh: 約瑟的夢與彩衣

region.en: Valley of Hebron, land of Canaan
region.zh: 希伯崙谷，迦南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 37:1-11, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Israel loves the son of his old age more than all his children and makes him a long-sleeved coat. Joseph's sheaves-dream and stars-dream — 'I have dreamed a dream more; behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars bowed down to me' — make even Jacob rebuke him, 'while his father observed the saying.'
summary.zh: 以色列愛年老所生之子過於眾子，為他作長袖彩衣。約瑟的捆禾之夢與星辰之夢——「我又做了一夢，夢見太陽月亮與十一個星向我下拜」——連雅各也責備他，「卻把這話存在心裡」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said: 'Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.' And he told it to his father, and to his brethren; and his father rebuked him, and said unto him: 'What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth?'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 37:9-10 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他又做了一夢，告訴他的哥哥們說：『看哪，我又做了一夢；看哪，太陽、月亮和十一顆星都向我下拜。』他把這夢告訴了他父親和他的哥哥們；他父親責備他說：『你所做的這是什麼夢？難道我和你母親並你的哥哥們真要來俯伏在地向你下拜嗎？』

title.en: Doth Not the Coat Bear Witness? Joseph Sold from the Pit
title.zh: 彩衣為證：約瑟被賣離坑

region.en: Dothan valley, land of Canaan
region.zh: 多坍谷，迦南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 37:12-36, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Jacob sends Joseph to find his brothers past Shechem to Dothan; they see him from afar — 'behold, this dreamer cometh' — and conspire to kill him. Reuben stays their hands by casting him into a pit; while Reuben is away, Judah's plan sells him to Midianite-Ishmaelite caravan traders for twenty pieces of silver. The brothers dip the coat in goat blood; Jacob rends his clothes and refuses comfort.
summary.zh: 雅各遣約瑟尋兄，經示劍至多坍；眾兄遠見——「那作夢的來了」——謀殺之。流便攔阻，投之於坑；流便離去，猶大之計以二十塊銀子賣之予米甸以實瑪利商隊。眾兄以羊血染彩衣；雅各撕裂衣服，不肯受安慰。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they said one to another: 'Behold, this dreamer cometh. Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pit; and we will say: An evil beast hath devoured him; and we shall see what will become of his dreams.' And Reuben heard it, and delivered him out of their hand, and said: 'Let us not take his life.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 37:19-21 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他們彼此說：『看哪，那做夢的來了。來吧，我們現在把他殺了，丟在某個坑裡；我們就說：有惡獸把他吃了；且看他的夢將來怎樣。』流便聽見了，就把他從他們手中救出來，說：『我們不可害他的性命。』

passages.text: Reuben planned to return and rescue him, but found the pit empty. Judah proposed profit over murder: 'What profit is it if we slay our brother? Come, and let us sell him'. They drew Joseph up and sold him for twenty pieces of silver to merchantmen bound for Egypt, then slaughtered a kid of the goats and dipped the coat in its blood, sending it to their father with the question, 'This have we found: know now whether it be thy son's coat or no.' Jacob rent his clothes and mourned: 'I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning' — 'and all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted.' Paraphrase of Genesis 37:26-35 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 37:26-35 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 流便原打算回去救他，卻發現坑是空的。猶大提議與其殺害，不如圖利：「我們殺了我們的兄弟有甚麼益處呢？來吧，我們把他賣了。」他們把約瑟拉上來，以二十塊銀子把他賣給往埃及去的商人，然後宰了一隻公山羊，把外袍浸在血裡，送到他們父親那裡，問道：「這是我們撿到的：請認一認，這是不是你兒子的外袍。」雅各撕裂衣服哀悼：「我要悲悲慘慘地下陰間去，到我兒子那裡」——「他的眾兒女都起來安慰他，他卻不肯受安慰。」改述自《創世記》37:26-35（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Judah and Tamar: The Firstborn Debt
title.zh: 猶大與他瑪：長子之債

region.en: Timnah, Judean foothills
region.zh: 亭拿，猶大山地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 38, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Judah's first two sons die after wronging Tamar; he withholds his third from her. Tamar disguises herself as a veiled cult prostitute at the road to Timnah, conceives by Judah, and is about to be burned for harlotry until she produces his seal, cord, and staff: 'Discern, I pray thee, whose these be.' Judah answers: 'She is more righteous than I' — and Perez, ancestor of David, is born.
summary.zh: 猶大長次二子因得罪他瑪而死；他扣下三子不予她。他瑪喬裝蒙面廟妓於往亭拿路口，與猶大同寢有孕；被判為妓當焚，乃出示猶大之印、帶子與杖：「請認一認，這是誰的？」猶大答：「她比我更有義」——其後法勒斯生，為大衛之祖。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Levirate custom (yibbum) etiology; Judah's royal line runs through Tamar's Perez.

passages.text: And it came to pass about three months after, that it was told Judah, saying: 'Tamar thy daughter-in-law hath played the harlot; and also, behold, she is with child by whoredom.' And Judah said: 'Bring her forth, and let her be burnt.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 38:24 (public domain).
passages.zh: 約過了三個月，有人告訴猶大說：「你的兒婦他瑪作了妓女；而且，看哪，她因行淫而懷了孕。」猶大說：「把她拉出來，燒了她。」

passages.text: When she was brought forth she sent to her father-in-law the pledges taken in her disguise: 'By the man, whose these are, I am with child; discern, I pray thee, whose these be'. Judah recognized them and confessed; Tamar bore twins, and at the birth Zerah put out a hand first with a scarlet thread, but Perez pushed through before him — the name Perez meaning 'breach', the line through which David and the kings of Judah descend. Paraphrase of Genesis 38:25-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 38:25-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 她被拉出來的時候，便把她喬裝時所取的憑據送給她的公公：「這些東西是誰的，我就是從誰懷的孕；請你認一認，這印、帶子、杖是誰的。」猶大認出這些東西，便承認了；他瑪生了雙胞胎，生產的時候，謝拉先伸出一隻手，收生婆便繫上一條朱紅線，但法勒斯卻搶先在他之前出來——法勒斯這名字意為「破口」，大衛與猶大諸王正是從這一支派而出。改述自《創世記》38:25-30（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Joseph and Potiphar's Wife
title.zh: 約瑟與波提乏之妻

region.en: Potiphar's house, Egypt (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 波提乏家中，埃及（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 39, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The LORD is with Joseph in Potiphar's house, where he rises to overseer of all. His master's wife seizes his garment day after day; he refuses and flees, leaving it in her hand — evidence enough for the lie. Joseph is cast into the king's prison, where 'the keeper of the prison looked not to any thing that was under his hand, because the LORD was with him.'
summary.zh: 耶和華與約瑟同在波提乏家中，升至總管。主母日日扯其衣；他拒絕而逃，衣留其手——足為偽證。約瑟被囚於王囚，而「司獄不查他手下的事，因為耶和華與他同在」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And she caught him by his garment, saying: 'Lie with me'; and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out. And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and was fled forth, that she called unto the men of her house.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 39:12-14 (public domain), lightly condensed.
passages.zh: 她抓住他的衣裳，說：「與我同寢吧」；他卻把衣裳留在她手裡，逃出去，跑到外邊。她見他把衣裳留在她手裡，逃到外邊，便叫了家裡的人來。

passages.text: She showed the household the 'Hebrew' her husband had brought 'to mock us', producing the garment; Potiphar put Joseph into the prison where the king's prisoners were bound. Even there God was with him, giving him favour with the keeper, who committed all the prisoners to his care — 'because the LORD was with him; and that which he did, the LORD made it to prosper.' Paraphrase of Genesis 39:14-23 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 39:14-23 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 她把丈夫帶回來「戲弄我們」的「希伯來人」指給家裡的人看，又拿出那件衣裳；波提乏便把約瑟下在監裡，就是王的囚犯被囚的地方。即使在那裡，神也與他同在，使他在獄長眼前蒙恩，獄長便把所有的囚犯都交在他手裡——「因為耶和華與他同在；他所做的，耶和華都使他順利。」改述自《創世記》39:14-23（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: The Cupbearer and the Baker Dream in Prison
title.zh: 酒政膳長在獄中作夢

region.en: King's prison, Egypt (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 王之囚，埃及（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 40, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Pharaoh's butler and baker offend him and land in Joseph's block, each with a dream the same night. Joseph reads both: in three days Pharaoh will lift up the cupbearer's head and restore him, and hang the baker. Joseph begs the restored servant to 'remember me... and mention me unto Pharaoh' — and the butler forgets him for two full years.
summary.zh: 法老的酒政膳長得罪王，同囚於約瑟處，同夜各得一夢。約瑟解之：三日後法老必提酒政的頭復其職，而掛起膳長。約瑟求復職者「得的好處時候，求你記念我……在法老面前題說我」——酒政竟忘了他整整兩年。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Joseph said unto him: 'This is the interpretation of it: the three branches are three days; yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thine head, and restore thee unto thine estate; and thou shalt deliver Pharaoh's cup into his hand, after the former manner when thou wast his butler. But think on me when it shall be well with thee, and show kindness, I pray thee, unto me, and make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 40:12-14 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 約瑟對他說：「這夢的講解是這樣：三根枝子就是三天；三天之內，法老必提你出監，使你官復原職；你仍要把法老的杯遞在他手中，像先前作他酒政的時候一樣。但你得好处的時候，求你記念我，施恩於我，在法老面前提說我，救我出這監牢。」

passages.text: The baker told his dream of birds eating baskets of baked foods from his head, and Joseph read death: 'within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh'. The third day was Pharaoh's birthday; the predictions came true exactly — 'and he gave the cup into the butler's hand; and he hanged the chief baker... yet did not the butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.' Paraphrase of Genesis 40:16-23 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 40:16-23 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 膳長述說他的夢，夢見有飛鳥從他頭上吃籃中的烤食，約瑟便解讀為死亡：「三天之內，法老必從你身上斬下你的頭，把你掛在木頭上；飛鳥必吃你的肉。」第三天正是法老的生日；預言絲毫不差地應驗了——「把杯交在酒政手中；又把膳長掛了起來……然而酒政卻不記念約瑟，竟忘了他。」改述《創世記》40:16-23（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Seven Kinds and Seven Ears: Pharaoh's Dreams
title.zh: 七母牛與七麥穗：法老之夢

region.en: Pharaoh's palace, Egypt (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 法老王宮，埃及（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 41:1-40, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Pharaoh dreams of seven fat kine eaten by seven lean and of seven good ears devoured by seven thin ones; his magicians fail. At last the butler remembers his fault, and Joseph, shaved and changed, stands before the throne: the doubled dream means the thing is certain — seven years of plenty, seven of famine. 'Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise' — and Pharaoh appoints him: 'there is none so discreet and wise as thou.'
summary.zh: 法老夢七肥牛被七瘦牛所吞，七好穗被七枯穗所食；術士皆不解。酒政終想起己過，約瑟剃面更衣立於御前：夢乃成雙，其事已定——七豐年七饑年。「法老當揀選一個有見識有智慧的人」——法老遂立之：「像這樣的人，有神的靈在他裡頭，我們豈找得著呢？」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying: 'It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.' ... Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt; and there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 41:16, 29-30 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 約瑟回答法老說：「這不在乎我：神必給法老一個平安的答覆。」……看哪，埃及全地必來七個大豐年；此後又要起七個荒年；埃及地的一切豐收必被忘記；饑荒必耗盡那地。

passages.text: Joseph advised storing a fifth of the harvest in the plenty years. Pharaoh told his servants no one had God's spirit like this man, and made him ruler of his house: 'only in the throne will I be greater than thou'. He set his signet on Joseph's hand, clothed him in fine linen, hung a gold chain on him, and rode the second chariot with the cry 'Bow the knee!' — naming him Zaphenath-paneah and giving him Asenath, daughter of Potipherah priest of On, as wife. Paraphrase of Genesis 41:34-45 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 41:34-45 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 約瑟建議在豐年把收成的五分之一積存起來。法老對臣僕說，沒有人像這人一樣有神的靈，便立他治理自己的家：「只有在寶座上我比你大」。他把印戒戴在約瑟手上，給他穿上細麻衣，把金鍊掛在他頸上，又讓他乘坐第二輛車，有人在前呼喊「跪下！」——給他起名叫撒發那忒巴內亞，又把安城祭司波提非拉的女兒亞西納給他為妻。改述《創世記》41:34-45（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Spies from Canaan: The Brothers Before the Vizier
title.zh: 迦南來的間諜：眾兄在宰相前

region.en: Granaries of Egypt (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 埃及糧倉（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 42, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Famine drives ten brothers down for grain. The ruler they bow to, not recognizing, is Joseph; he remembers his dreams, speaks harshly as an 'interpreter of secrets', accuses them of spying, and tests them — Simeon bound, the rest sent home with grain and their money hidden in their sacks. 'And they said one to another: We are verily guilty concerning our brother', and Reuben's old reproach returns.
summary.zh: 饑荒驅十兄下埃及糴糧。他們所拜而不識的統治者正是約瑟；約瑟記起夢，以「解夢者」姿態嚴詞相待，指其為間諜，加以試煉——綁西緬，餘者糴糧返家，銀子皆藏袋中。「他們彼此說：我們在兄弟身上實在有罪」，流便舊責重提。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land. And Joseph's brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth. And Joseph saw his brethren, and he knew them, but made himself strange unto them, and spake roughly unto them.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 42:6-7 (public domain).
passages.zh: 約瑟是治理那地的官長，也是賣糧給那地眾民的。約瑟的哥哥們來了，臉伏於地向他下拜。約瑟看見他的哥哥們，就認得他們，卻裝作陌生人，對他們說嚴厲的話。

passages.text: He demanded they bring the youngest brother to prove their words, keeping Simeon bound 'before their eyes'; then commanded their sacks filled — and each man's money was returned secretly within it. At the inn one opened his sack and found the silver, 'and their heart failed them, and they were afraid, saying one to another: What is this that God hath done unto us?' Home, they told Jacob everything; he refused to let Benjamin go, crying: 'Me have ye bereaved... Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye will take Benjamin away.' Paraphrase of Genesis 42:9-38 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 42:9-38 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他要求他們把最小的弟弟帶來，以證實他們的話，並當著「他們眼前」把西緬捆綁；隨後吩咐把他們的袋子裝滿——又把各人的銀子暗中放回各人的袋裡。在客店裡，有一人打開袋子，發現了銀子，「他們的心就驚惶，彼此害怕，說：『神向我們作的是什麼事呢？』」回到家裡，他們把一切事都告訴了雅各；雅各不肯讓便雅憫去，哭喊說：「你們使我喪失了……約瑟沒有了，西緬也沒有了，你們又要帶便雅憫走。」改述《創世記》42:9-38（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Judah's Pledge and the Feast at the Ruler's Table
title.zh: 猶大作保與宰相席上之宴

region.en: Granaries of Egypt (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 埃及糧倉（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 43, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Famine forces the issue. Judah pledges himself for Benjamin's safety and brings double money, balm, honey, and nuts. Joseph, seeing his full brother, orders a feast: the brothers are seated in birth-order, Benjamin's portions are five times the others', and Joseph asks after 'your father, the old man of whom ye spake, is he yet alive?' — and turns aside to weep.
summary.zh: 饑荒迫其決斷。猶大以身作保，攜雙倍銀、香料、蜜與榛子攜便雅憫往。約瑟見同母之弟，設宴款待：眾兄按長幼而坐，便雅憫所得五倍於人；約瑟問「你們所說你們父親那老人還在麼」——側身而泣。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he asked them of their welfare, and said: 'Is your father well, the old man of whom ye spake? Is he yet alive?' And they answered: 'Thy servant our father is in good health, he is yet alive.' And he lifted up his eyes, and saw Benjamin his brother, his mother's son, and said: 'God be gracious unto thee, my son.' And Joseph made haste; for his bowels did yearn upon his brother; and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 43:27-30 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 他問他們安好，說：「你們所說的老人家，你們的父親平安嗎？他還在嗎？」他們回答說：「你僕人我們的父親平安，他還在。」他舉目看見他同母的兄弟便雅憫，就說：「我兒，願神賜恩給你。」約瑟急忙離開，因為他對兄弟的心腸如火焚燒；他找地方去哭；便進了內室，在那裡痛哭。

title.en: The Silver Cup in the Sack of Benjamin
title.zh: 便雅憫袋中銀盃

region.en: Road out of Egypt (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 出埃及之路（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 44:1-17, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Joseph's steward hides the divining silver cup in Benjamin's grain-sack. Overtaken by pursuit, the brothers protest innocence — 'with whomsoever of thy servants it be found, let him die' — and it is found exactly in the youngest's sack. They rend their clothes and return together to the house, thrown down before the ruler.
summary.zh: 約瑟的管家將占卜銀盃藏於便雅憫袋中。追兵至，眾兄自稱清白——「在誰那裡搜出來，就叫他死」——而杯恰在幼弟袋中。他們撕裂衣服，同回宰相之屋，俯伏於地。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he searched, and began at the eldest, and left at the youngest; and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack. Then they rent their clothes, and laded every man his ass, and returned to the city. Joseph's steward hides the divining silver cup in Benjamin's grain-sack.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 44:12-13 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他搜索，從最年長的開始，到最年幼的為止；結果那杯在便雅憫的袋裡被搜出來。於是他們撕裂衣服，各人把糧食馱在驢上，回城去了。約瑟的管家把占卜用的銀杯藏在便雅憫的糧袋裡。

title.en: Judah's Speech: I Will Be Surety for the Lad
title.zh: 猶大之言：我為這童子作保

region.en: Vizier's hall, Egypt (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 宰相之堂，埃及（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 44:18-34, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The longest speech in Genesis: Judah recounts the father who refused to part with the last son of his beloved wife, 'and now if thou take this also... it shall come to pass that when he seeth that the lad is not with us, he will die'. Judah offers himself as slave in the boy's place — and Joseph can no longer restrain himself.
summary.zh: 創世記最長演說：猶大述說那位不肯讓愛妻幼子離開的父親，「現在若把這個也帶去……他見沒有童子，就必死」。猶大以身代之為奴——約瑟再也抑制不住。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Thy servant my father said unto us: 'Ye know that my wife bare me two sons; and the one went out from me, and I said: Surely he is torn in pieces; and I saw him not since.' ... Now therefore when I come to thy servant my father, and the lad be not with us; seeing that his life is bound up in the lad's life; it shall come to pass, when he seeth that the lad is not with us, that he will die.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 44:27-31 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 你僕人我父親對我們說：『你們知道我的妻子給我生了兩個兒子；一個離開我出去了，我說：他必定是被撕碎了；此後我沒有見到他。』……如今我回到你僕人我父親那裡，若童子不與我們同在；因為他的性命與童子的性命相連；他見童子不在我們這裡，就必死。

passages.text: 'Let thy servant, I pray thee, abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren. For how shall I go up to my father, if the lad be not with me?' The man who had once proposed selling his brother now gave himself in exchange — and the test of the brothers was passed. Paraphrase of Genesis 44:33-34 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 44:33-34 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 『求你容你僕人代替童子留下，作我主的奴僕；讓童子與他哥哥們一同上去。因為童子若不與我同在，我怎能上去見我父親呢？』那曾提議出賣自己兄弟的人，如今竟以自己相換——兄弟們的考驗就此通過了。改述自《創世記》44:33-34（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: I Am Joseph: The Revelation and the Descent Decreed
title.zh: 我是約瑟：相認與受命下埃及

region.en: Vizier's hall, Egypt (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 宰相之堂，埃及（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 45, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Joseph sends every Egyptian out and weeps aloud: 'I am Joseph; doth my father yet live?' His brothers are terrified to silence; he forgives in theological terms — 'be not grieved... for God did send me before you to preserve life'. Pharaoh hears of it and provides wagons; Jacob's spirit revives: 'Joseph my son is yet alive: I will go and see him before I die.'
summary.zh: 約瑟遣退埃及人，放聲大哭：「我是約瑟！我的父親還在麼？」眾兄驚惶失語；他以神學釋怨——「不要憂愁……這是神差我在你們前頭來，為要保全生命」。法老聞之賜車；雅各的靈甦醒：「約瑟還在，趁我未死以先，我要去見他一面。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Joseph said unto his brethren: 'I am Joseph; doth my father yet live?' And his brethren could not answer him; for they were troubled at his presence. And Joseph said unto his brethren: 'Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said: I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt. Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither; for God did send me before you to preserve life.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 45:3-5 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 約瑟對他的弟兄們說：『我是約瑟；我的父親還活著嗎？』他的弟兄們不能回答他，因為他們在他面前驚惶。約瑟對他的弟兄們說：『請你們近前來。』他們就近前來。他說：『我是你們的兄弟約瑟，就是你們賣到埃及的。現在你們不要因為把我賣到這裡來而憂愁，也不要自恨；因為是神差我在你們以先來，為要保全生命。』

title.en: The Descent into Egypt: Seventy Souls
title.zh: 下埃及：七十人

region.en: Land of Goshen, Nile Delta
region.zh: 歌珊地，尼羅河三角洲

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 46, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: At Beer-sheba Jacob offers sacrifices, and God speaks in visions of the night: 'fear not to go down into Egypt; for I will there make of thee a great nation... and Joseph shall put his hand upon thine eyes.' The family — seventy souls by the census — comes to Goshen; Joseph meets his father falling on his neck, 'and he wept on his neck a good while.'
summary.zh: 雅各在別是巴獻祭，神夜間異象中說：「不要害怕下埃及去，因為我必使你在那裡成為大國……約瑟必給你送終。」全家——按名數算七十人——至歌珊；約瑟迎見其父，伏在他頸項上「哭了許久」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he said: 'I am God, the God of thy father; fear not to go down into Egypt; for I will there make of thee a great nation. I will go down with thee into Egypt; and I will also surely bring thee up again: and Joseph shall put his hand upon thine eyes.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 46:3-4 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他說：『我是神，是你父親的神；不要害怕下埃及去；因為我必使你在那裡成為大族。我必與你一同下埃及；也必領你上來；約瑟必把手按在你的眼睛上。』

passages.text: The genealogy of the seventy is recited by house. Judah was sent ahead to point out Goshen; Joseph harnessed his chariot and went up to meet Israel his father, and 'he presented himself unto him; and he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while'. Israel said: 'Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, because thou art yet alive.' Paraphrase of Genesis 46:5-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 46:5-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 七十人的家譜按各家被誦述。猶大被差遣先行，指明歌珊地；約瑟套上他的車，上去迎接他的父親以色列，『他就顯現於他面前；伏在他頸項上，伏在他頸項上哭了許久』。以色列說：『我既得見你的面，知道你還活著，如今我死也甘心了。』改述自《創世記》46:5-30（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Jacob Blesses Pharaoh and Settles in Goshen
title.zh: 雅各祝福法老，安居歌珊

region.en: Land of Goshen, Nile Delta
region.zh: 歌珊地，尼羅河三角洲

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 47:1-12, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Five brothers present themselves and ask for the land of Goshen as shepherds' pasture; Pharaoh grants it. The aged Jacob is brought before the throne and blesses Pharaoh — 'and Pharaoh said unto Jacob: How old art thou?' — 'The days of the years of my pilgrimage are an hundred and thirty years... few and evil have the days of the years of my life been.'
summary.zh: 五兄自薦，求歌珊為牧羊之業；法老允之。老雅各被引至御前為法老祝福——「法老問雅各說：你平生的年日是多少呢？」——「我寄居在世的年日是一百三十歲……我平生的年日又少又苦。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Pharaoh said unto Jacob: 'How old art thou?' And Jacob said unto Pharaoh: 'The days of the years of my pilgrimage are an hundred and thirty years; few and evil have the days of the years of my life been, and have not attained unto the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.' And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from before Pharaoh.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 47:8-10 (public domain).
passages.zh: 法老問雅各說：「你平生的年日是多少呢？」雅各對法老說：「我寄居在世的年日是一百三十歲；我平生的年日又少又苦，不及我列祖在世寄居的年日。」雅各又給法老祝福，就從法老面前出去了。

title.en: The Younger Above the Elder: Ephraim and Manasseh
title.zh: 幼者居上：以法蓮與瑪拿西

region.en: Land of Goshen, Nile Delta
region.zh: 歌珊地，尼羅河三角洲

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 48, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Near death, Jacob adopts Joseph's two Egyptian-born sons as his own. He crosses his hands — right hand on Ephraim the younger — and Joseph tries to correct him: 'Not so, my father'. But Israel answers, as if foreseeing the next generation's history: 'I know it, my son, I know it; he also shall become a people... but his younger brother shall be greater than he.'
summary.zh: 臨終之際，雅各收約瑟兩個埃及所生之子為己子。他交叉雙手——右手按幼者以法蓮——約瑟欲纠正：「不是這樣，我父。」以色列答，如預知下一代歷史：「我知道，我兒，我知道；他也必成為一族……只是他的兄弟將來比他還大。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. 'By thee shall Israel bless' made the Friday-night blessing of sons.

passages.text: And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim's head, who was the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh's head, guiding his hands wittingly; for Manasseh was the firstborn. And when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it was evil in his eyes; and he held up his father's hand, to remove it from Ephraim's head unto Manasseh's head.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 48:14, 17 (public domain); verse 17 condensed.
passages.zh: 以色列伸出右手來，按在以法蓮的頭上（以法蓮乃是次子），又剪搭過左手來，按在瑪拿西的頭上（瑪拿西原是長子）。約瑟見他父親把右手按在以法蓮的頭上，就不喜悅，便提起他父親的手，要從以法蓮的頭上挪到瑪拿西的頭上。

passages.text: Joseph said, 'Not so, my father; for this is the firstborn'; but Israel refused: 'I know it, my son, I know it; he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great; howbeit his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations'. The blessing formula 'God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh' entered Jewish households permanently. Paraphrase of Genesis 48:18-20 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 48:18-20 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 約瑟對他父親說：「我父，不是這樣；這本是長子。」以色列卻不肯，說：「我知道，我兒，我知道；他也必成為一族，也必昌大；只是他的兄弟將來比他還大，他兄弟的後裔要成為多族。」祝福的語句「願神使你如以法蓮、瑪拿西一樣」就此永久進入猶太人的家庭。此為《創世記》48:18-20（JPS 1917）的意譯，並非逐字照錄。

title.en: Jacob Blesses His Twelve Sons
title.zh: 雅各祝福十二子

region.en: Land of Goshen, Nile Delta
region.zh: 歌珊地，尼羅河三角洲

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 49:1-28, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Israel gathers his sons: 'that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days'. Reuben is 'unstable as water'; Simeon and Levi are cursed for the sword at Shechem; Judah receives the royal oracle — 'the sceptre shall not depart from Judah... until Shiloh come' — while Zebulun, Issachar, Dan, Gad, Asher, Naphtali, Joseph, and Benjamin each get their tribe's character in poetry.
summary.zh: 以色列召集眾子：「把你們日後必遇的事告訴你們。」流便「如水滾沸」；西緬利未因示劍之刀受咒；猶大得王者諭言——「圭必不離猶大……直到細羅來到」——而西布倫、以薩迦、但、迦得、亞設、拿弗他利、約瑟、便雅憫各得支派之詩。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Judah's oracle underlies later messianic expectation; recorded as text.

passages.text: Judah, thee shall thy brethren praise; thy hand shall be on the neck of thine enemies; thy father's sons shall bow down before thee. ... The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the obedience of the peoples be.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 49:8, 10 (public domain); ellipsis marks omitted verse.
passages.zh: 猶大啊，你弟兄們必讚美你；你手必掐住仇敵的頸項；你父親的兒子們必向你下拜。……圭必不離猶大，杖必不離他兩腳之間，直等細羅來到，萬民都必歸順。

passages.text: Joseph's blessing is the longest: 'Joseph is a fruitful bough, a fruitful bough by a fountain; his branches run over the wall... from thence is the shepherd, the stone of Israel'. Benjamin is 'a wolf that raveneth'. Then, 'All these are the twelve tribes of Israel... and he charged them, and said unto them: Bury me with my fathers' — in the cave of Machpelah. Paraphrase of Genesis 49:22, 27, 28-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 49:22-33 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 約瑟的祝福最長：「約瑟是多結果子的樹枝，是泉旁多結果的枝子；他的枝條探出牆外……這是牧者、以色列的磐石所出。」便雅憫是「撕掠的狼」。隨後又說：「這一切是以色列的十二支派……他又囑咐他們，對他們說：『我將要歸到我列祖那裏，你們要將我葬在……』」——即麥比拉洞中。此為《創世記》49:22、27、28-29（JPS 1917）的意譯，並非逐字照錄。

title.en: The Funeral of Jacob and the Bones of Joseph
title.zh: 雅各葬禮與約瑟骸骨

region.en: Cave of Machpelah, Hebron
region.zh: 麥比拉洞，希伯崙

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 49:29-50:26, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Jacob dies and is embalmed after the manner of Egypt; a huge funeral procession of elders and chariots carries him to Machpelah, the Canaanites at the threshing-floor of Atad marvelling at 'a grievous mourning'. The brothers fear retribution; Joseph answers: 'ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good'. At a hundred and ten he dies, making his kin swear to carry his bones up — 'and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.'
summary.zh: 雅各死，照埃及例薰屍；長老與戰車大隊護送至麥比拉，亞達禾場迦南人驚歎「埃及人一場極大的哀哭」。眾兄懼報復；約瑟答：「從前你們的意思是要害我，但神的意思原是好的。」一百一十歲而卒，令親族起誓攜其骸骨上去——「收殮在棺材裡，停在埃及。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Joseph's bones motif returns in Exodus 13:19 and Joshua 24:32.

passages.text: And Joseph said unto his brethren: 'Fear not; for am I in the place of God? But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 50:19-20 (public domain).
passages.zh: 約瑟對他的弟兄們說：「不要害怕；我豈能代替神呢？從前你們的意思是要害我，但神的意思原是好的，要保全許多人的性命，成就今日的光景。」

passages.text: Joseph and his father's household wept seven days at the threshing-floor of Atad beyond the Jordan. Then Joseph returned to Egypt, living to see Ephraim's children of the third generation; he told his brethren: 'God will surely remember you, and bring you out of this land... and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.' He died at a hundred and ten and was embalmed and coffined in Egypt — awaiting the exodus his oath presupposed. Paraphrase of Genesis 50:4-26 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 50:4-26 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 約瑟和他父親的眷屬在約旦河外的亞達禾場哀哭了七天。之後約瑟回到埃及，活著見到以法蓮第三代的子孫；他對弟兄們說：「神必眷顧你們，領你們從這地上去……你們要把我的骸骨從這裡搬上去。」他死時一百一十歲，在埃及被薰屍、收殮入棺——等候著他的誓言所預設的出埃及。此為《創世記》50:4-26（JPS 1917）之改寫，非逐字原文。

title.en: Yusuf and the Ripped Shirt in the House of the Aziz
title.zh: 優素福與被撕破的襯衫

region.en: Egypt, house of the Aziz (lord of the storehouses; symbolic pin)
region.zh: 埃及糧政大臣府邸（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah Yusuf 12:21-34; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 12:21-34

summary.en: The buyer, an officer of Egypt, tells his wife to lodge the boy honourably — 'we may adopt him as a son.' The lady seeks him, and he resists her; God's sign turns him from evil, and when the husband finds them at the door, the wife accuses him: 'There is no punishment for a husband, unless she whose husband hath wronged her, or she is one of the erring' — but a witness suggests the proof of the shirt: if hers is torn in front she speaks truth, if behind, she lies. Torn from behind, Yusuf is cleared; she is confessed of her guilt.
summary.zh: 買者（埃及官員）命妻款待此童：『或可收為義子。』夫人勾引之，優素福拒絕。丈夫見狀，夫人誣告；見證者建議驗襯衫之證：若她前襟撕裂，她說真話；若後襟撕裂，她說謊。後襟撕裂，優素福被證清白，夫人自認其過。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And he who bought him, who was of Egypt, said to his wife, 'Give him an honourable abode; it may be that he will be useful to us, or we may adopt him as a son.' And thus did We settle the affairs of Yusuf in the land, and that We might teach him the interpreting of tales; and God is potent over his affairs, but most men know it not.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 12:21 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那買下他的埃及人對他的妻子說：「你當優待他的居所；或許他對我們有用，或者我們可以收他為子。」我們就這樣使優素福在大地上安頓，並使他學會解釋夢兆；真主對他的事務確是萬能的，但大多數人並不知道。

passages.text: And she in whose house he was sought to seduce him, and fastened the doors, and said, 'Come hither.' He said, 'God forbid! Verily my Lord hath made my abode good. The unjust shall not prosper.' Verily she desired him, and he had desired her, had he not seen a proof of his Lord. Thus did We turn evil from him, for he was one of Our chosen servants.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 12:23-24 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 她——他就在她家中——引誘他，並關上門戶，說：「你來吧。」他說：「求真主護佑！我的主確已使我的居所安好。不義的人不會成功。」她確已傾慕他，他也傾慕她，若非他看見了他主的明證。我們就這樣使他遠離邪惡，他確是我們揀選的僕人之一。

passages.text: And when her lord came to the door, she said, 'What shall be the punishment of one who would do evil to thy wife, but prison or a painful punishment?' Said Yusuf, 'She it was who sought to seduce me.' And a witness of her household said, 'If his shirt be torn in front, then she speaketh truth, and he is of the liars; but if it be torn behind, then she lieth, and he is of the truthful.' And when her lord saw his shirt torn behind, he said, 'This is a device of you women; truly your devices are grievous. O Yusuf, let this pass; and thou, ask pardon for thy fault, for thou hast been of the faulty.' And women of the city said, 'The wife of the Aziz hath sought her servant: he hath smitten her heart with love; we plainly see that she is in a manifest error.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 12:25-30 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當她的丈夫來到門口，她說：「想要害你妻子的人，除了監禁或痛苦的刑罰，還該受什麼懲罰呢？」優素福說：「是她引誘我。」她家中一個證人說：「若他的襯衫是從前面撕破的，那她說的是實話，他便是說謊的人；若是從後面撕破的，那她便說謊，他便是說實話的人。」當她的丈夫看見他的襯衫是從後面撕破的，便說：「這是你們女人的計謀；你們的計謀確是重大的。優素福啊，你撇開這事吧；你——為你的過失求饒吧，你確是有過失的人。」城中的婦女們說：「阿齊茲的妻子引誘她的僕人：他已用愛情擊中了她的心；我們明明看出她是在明顯的迷誤之中。」

passages.text: And when she heard their wiles she prepared a banquet for them, and gave to each a knife, and said to Yusuf, 'Come forth and show thyself to them.' And when they saw him they praised him greatly, and cut their hands with the knives and said, 'God keep us! This is no man: this is none other than a gracious angel.' She said, 'This is he for whom ye blamed me: I sought to seduce him, but he shrank back; and now if he doth not what I order him, he shall surely be imprisoned, and be among the abject.' He said, 'O my Lord, prison is dearer to me than that which they invite me to. And if thou turn not their wiles from me, then shall I yearn towards them and become one of the ignorant.' His Lord heard him, and turned their wiles from him: verily He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 12:31-34 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當她聽見她們的計議，便為她們預備了筵席，給每人一把刀，並對優素福說：「你出來，讓她們看看你。」當她們看見他，便大大讚美他，並用刀割了自己的手，說：「真主保佑！這不是凡人：這不過是一位仁慈的天使。」她說：「這就是你們為他責備我的人：我引誘他，他卻退避了；如今他若不做我命令他的事，他必被監禁，必成為卑賤的人。」他說：「我的主啊，監禁比她們所召我做的事更令我喜愛。你若不为我擋開她們的計謀，我便會傾向她們，成為無知的人。」他的主聽了他，為他擋開了她們的計謀：祂確是全聽的、全知的。

title.en: Two Prisoners, Two Dreams: The Interpreter in the Dungeon
title.zh: 獄中二囚二夢：地牢裡的解夢者

region.en: Egyptian state prison (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 埃及國家監獄（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah Yusuf 12:36-42; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 12:36-42

summary.en: Two young men enter the prison with Yusuf. One dreams of pressing wine; the other dreams of birds eating bread from his head. 'Tell us its interpretation, for we see that thou art a doer of good.' Yusuf preaches first — many gods are better, or one God? — then interprets: one shall pour wine for his lord, the other shall be crucified and birds shall eat from his head. The matter is decreed; the freed man forgets Yusuf for years in the prison.
summary.zh: 二少年與優素福同入獄。一人夢榨酒，另一人夢鳥啄其頭上之餅。他們請優素福解夢；優素福先勸誡（諸神更好還是一神更好？），再釋夢：一人將為君斟酒，另一人將被釘十字架而鳥啄其頭。事已注定；獲釋者竟將優素福忘於獄中多年。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And two young men went to prison with him. One of them said, 'I saw in a dream that I was pressing wine'; and the other said, 'I saw in a dream that I was carrying bread on my head, of which the birds were eating. Tell us its interpretation, for we see that thou art a doer of good.' Yusuf answered, 'O my two fellow-prisoners, many sorts of food are better than these, and the fear of God is better... O my fellow-prisoners, are sundry lords better than the one Almighty, All-powerful God? Those whom ye worship beside Him are mere names which ye and your fathers have invented: God hath sent down no warrant for them. Judgment belongeth to God alone; He hath commanded that ye worship none but Him — the right faith; but most men know it not.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 12:36-40 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有兩個青年與他一同入獄。其中一人說：「我夢見我在榨酒」；另一人說：「我夢見我頭上頂著麵包，有鳥來吃。請告訴我們這夢的解釋，因為我們看出你是行善的人。」優素福回答：「我的兩位獄友啊，許多種食物比這些更好，敬畏真主更好……我的兩位獄友啊，眾多的主更好呢，還是獨一全能、統御萬物的真主更好？你們除祂之外所崇拜的，只是你們和你們的祖先所捏造的名目：真主並未為它們降下任何憑證。判決只歸真主；祂命令你們只崇拜祂——這才是正信；但大多數人並不知道。」

passages.text: O my two fellow-prisoners, as to one of you, he shall pour out wine for his lord to drink; and as for the other, he shall be crucified and the birds shall eat from off his head. The matter is decreed for which ye inquired. And he said to him whom he judged to be the freer of the two, 'Remember me before thy lord'; but Satan caused him to forget his Lord's remembrance, and he tarried several years in the prison.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 12:41-42 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「同獄的兩位難友啊，你們中的一人將為他的主人斟酒；至於另一人，則將被釘死在十字架上，飛鳥要從他的頭上啄食。你們所詢問的事，已經判定了。」他對他所判定為兩人中將獲釋的那一位說：「請在你主人面前替我提起我」；但撒旦使他忘記了向他主人提起，於是他又在獄中逗留了好幾年。

title.en: Seven Fat Kine and Seven Green Ears: From Dungeon to Throne
title.zh: 七肥牛與七青穗：從地牢到高位

region.en: Egypt, throne hall of Pharaoh (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 埃及法老王宮（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah Yusuf 12:43-57; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 12:43-57

summary.en: The king dreams that seven fat kine are devoured by seven lean, and of seven green ears of corn and seven withered. His courtiers call it 'confused dreams'; the freed prisoner remembers Yusuf at last and goes to the prison: 'Tell us of the seven fat kine...' Yusuf answers with the interpretation — seven years of plenty, then seven of hardship, then a year of release — and claims nothing for himself but that God has taught him. The king asks his freedom; the woman and the women confess, and Yusuf is set over the storehouses of Egypt.
summary.zh: 國王夢七肥牛被七瘦牛吞食，又夢七青穗與七枯穗。臣們稱之為『亂夢』；獲釋者終於想起優素福，往獄中相告。優素福釋夢：七年豐年、七年荒年、再一年解困——並自言解夢乃主所授。國王欲釋其出獄；夫人與眾婦人認罪，優素福遂掌埃及糧政。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And the king said, 'I saw in a dream seven fat kine which seven lean kine devoured; and seven green ears of corn and others withered. O chiefs, explain to me my dream, if ye can interpret a dream.' They said, 'They are confused dreams, and we do not know the interpretation of such dreams.' And he of the two who was freed, and who, after the space of years, remembered, said, 'I will tell you its interpretation, therefore send me.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 12:43-45 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 國王說：「我夢見七頭肥牛，被七頭瘦牛吞吃了；又夢見七穗青麥，和另外一些枯乾的。眾首領啊，如果你們能圓夢，請為我解說我的夢。」他們說：「這是些混亂的夢，我們不懂得這類夢的解說。」兩人中那獲釋的、經過數年之後記起此事的人說：「我將告訴你們這夢的解說，請派我去。」

passages.text: Yusuf, O man of truth, tell us of the seven fat kine which seven lean kine devoured, and of the seven green ears and the others withered, that I may return to the people, and that they may know. He said, 'Seven years shall ye sow, as ye sow: and the corn which ye reap, leave in the ear, except a little which ye eat. Then shall come after this seven grievous years, which shall eat up what ye have laid up for them, all but a little which ye shall have reserved. Then shall come after this a year of ease, in which men shall press the juice, and in which they shall return to their former state.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 12:46-49 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「優素福啊，誠實的人啊，請告訴我們那七頭肥牛被七頭瘦牛吞吃的事，以及七穗青麥和另外一些枯乾的麥穗，好讓我回去告訴眾人，使他們知道。」他說：「你們要耕種七年，照常耕種；你們所收割的麥子，除了少許供你們食用之外，都要留在穗上。此後將要來七個荒年，要把你們為它們所儲存的一切吃盡，只除你們所保留的少許。此後將要來一個豐年，人們在其中榨取果汁，在其中恢復往日的境況。」

passages.text: And the king said, 'Bring him to me.' And when the messenger came to him he said, 'Return to thy lord and say to him, What meanest thou by the affair of the women who cut their hands? My lord knoweth their wiles.' The king said to the women, 'What was your intent when ye sought to seduce Yusuf?' They said, 'God forbid! We know no evil of him.' The wife of the Aziz said, 'Now hath the truth come to light: I seduced him, and he is of the truthful.' 'O my Lord, prison is dearer to me than that whereto these women invite me... Let me die rather; or take me out of their reach.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 12:50-53 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 國王說：「把他帶到我這裡來。」當使者來到他那裡時，他說：「你回去見你的主人，對他說：那些割破自己手的婦女是怎麼回事？我的主人深知她們的詭計。」國王對那些婦女說：「你們企圖誘惑優素福時，是何居心？」她們說：「真主不容！我們知道他毫無邪惡。」阿齊茲的妻子說：「如今真相已經顯露：是我誘惑了他，而他確是誠實的人。」「我的主啊，監獄比這些婦女所召我去的更令我喜愛……不如讓我死去；或者使我能擺脫她們的糾纏。」

passages.text: And the king said, 'Bring him to me: I will take him for my own service.' And when he had conversed with him he said, 'This day shalt thou be firmly seated with us, and honoured with our trust.' And Yusuf said, 'Set me over the storehouses of the land, for I am able to keep them, and skilled to do it.' And thus did We settle Yusuf in the land, and he had possessions therein at his pleasure: We bestow Our mercy on whom We will, and We cause not the reward of the righteous to be lost.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 12:54-56 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 國王說：「把他帶到我這裡來，我要讓他專為我效力。」當他與他交談之後，他說：「今日起你將在我們這裡位居要職，並受我們的信任與敬重。」優素福說：「請派我管理國家的糧倉，因為我善於保管，且精於此道。」我們就這樣使優素福安居於此地，他在其中隨意享有產業：我們將我們的慈恩賜予我們所意欲的人，我們不使行善者的報酬徒然失落。

title.en: The Cup in Benjamin's Sack and the Shirt That Restored Sight
title.zh: 便雅憫囊中金杯與復明之衣

region.en: Egyptian granary and Canaan (symbolic pin at Cairo)
region.zh: 埃及糧倉與迦南（象徵性定位於開羅）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah Yusuf 12:58-99; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 12:58-99

summary.en: Yusuf's brothers come for corn; he knows them, they know him not. He demands their brother as hostage, binds the drinking-cup in Benjamin's saddlebag, and keeps him in Egypt. Jacob weeps till his eyes whiten, yet says, 'I only complain of my grief and my sorrow to God; I know from God what ye know not.' When the brothers return, Yusuf reveals himself: 'No blame on you this day'; sends his shirt to be laid on Jacob's face — and sight returns. The family comes down to Egypt, and Yusuf raises his parents on the throne, and they fall down prostrate: the dream of the eleven stars fulfilled.
summary.zh: 優素福的兄長們來糴糧；他認得他們，他們卻不識他。他以弟弟為質，將酒杯藏於便雅憫的行囊，將他留於埃及。雅各哭到眼白，只向主訴愁。兄弟復返，優素福亮明身份：『今日你們無罪』；遣襯衫置於雅各面上——他重見光明。家眷下埃及；優素福扶父母升於寶座，眾人俯首——十一星之夢應驗。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And Yusuf's brethren came and presented themselves before him; and he knew them, but they knew him not. And when he had furnished them with their provision he said, 'Bring me a brother of yours from your father... and remember me, when ye are become settled in wealth and prosperity.' And they said, 'We will strive to obtain him from his father; verily we will do it.' And he said to his servants, 'Put their merchandise into their sacks'; and when they had done this he said to one of them, 'Place my drinking-cup in the sack of their brother Benjamin.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 12:58-62, 70 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 優素福的兄弟們來了，來到他面前；他認出了他們，他們卻不認識他。當他為他們備好糧食之後，他說：「把你們同父的一位兄弟帶來給我……當你們安居富足之時，請記得我。」他們說：「我們一定竭力向他父親求得他；我們必定做到。」他對他的僕人們說：「把他們的貨物放進他們的糧袋裡」；當他們這樣做了之後，他又對其中一人說：「把我的飲杯放在他們兄弟便雅憫的糧袋裡。」

passages.text: And Jacob turned away from them and wept, and he said, 'O my sorrow for Yusuf!' And his eyes became white with mourning, and he was now oppressed with grief. They said, 'By God! wilt thou not cease to remember Yusuf till thou art wasted to a very skeleton, or dead?' He said, 'I only complain of my grief and my sorrow to God, and I know from God what ye know not. Go and make inquiries concerning Yusuf and his brother, and despair not of the mercy of God; for only the unbelieving despair of God's mercy.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 12:84-87 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 雅各轉身離開他們，哭泣著說：『哀哉，我為優素福而悲傷！』他的眼睛因哀愁而變白，心中充滿憂傷。他們說：『指真主發誓！你難道不肯停止記念優素福，直到你消瘦成一副枯骨，或者死去嗎？』他說：『我只向真主訴說我的悲傷與哀愁，我從真主那裡知道你們所不知道的。你們去探問優素福和他的弟弟，不要對真主的慈恩絕望；因為只有不信道的人才對真主的慈恩絕望。』

passages.text: And when they had presented themselves they said, 'O Aziz, adversity hath visited us and our family... Restore us our brother.' And when Yusuf had clothed himself, and was going to depart, his brother said... And when they had taken their departure, Yusuf said, 'O ye men, we will demand of you your brother.' And when he had made ready their loads, he said, 'What did ye do with my drinking-cup?' They said, 'We have been unjust and guilty.' He said, 'Let no one of us be blamed this day... God forgiveth him whom He pleaseth; He is the Knowing, the Wise.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 12:88-92 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他們來到他面前時，他們說：『阿齊茲啊，災難降臨了我們和我們的家族……請把我們的弟弟還給我們。』當優素福穿戴完畢，正要離去時，他的弟弟說……當他們動身離去時，優素福說：『眾人啊，我們要向你們索回你們的弟弟。』當他為他們備好糧食時，他說：『你們把我的飲水杯怎麼了？』他們說：『我們是不義的，是有罪的。』他說：『今日我們中誰也不要受責備……真主赦免他所意欲的人；他是全知的，是至睿的。』

passages.text: And he said, 'This my shirt carry, and lay it on my father's face, and he shall recover his sight; then come to me with all your family.' And when the caravan had departed their father said, 'I surely smell the breath of Yusuf.' And when the bearer of the tidings came he laid it on his face and he recovered his sight, and said, 'Did I not tell you that I know from God what ye know not?' And when they came before Yusuf, he took his father to him, and said, 'Come into Egypt in safety, please God.' And he raised his parents on the throne, and they fell prostrate before him and said, 'O Yusuf, this is indeed the interpretation of my dream of aforetime: my Lord hath made it true; and He hath shown me favour, and hath brought me forth from prison, and brought you out of the desert, after that Satan had stirred up discord between me and my brethren.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 12:93-100 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他說：『你們把這件襯衫帶去，把它蒙在我父親的臉上，他就會恢復視力；然後帶著你們全家來見我。』當商隊出發離去後，他們的父親說：『我確實聞到了優素福的氣息。』當報喜的人來到時，他把襯衫蒙在他臉上，他便恢復了視力，說：『我不是告訴過你們嗎？我從真主那裡知道你們所不知道的。』當他們來到優素福面前時，他把父親接到身邊，說：『請你們平安地進入埃及，若真主意欲。』他讓他的父母登上寶座，他們便向他俯伏行禮，說：『優素福啊，這確實是我從前那個夢的解釋：我的主已使它成真；他確已施恩於我，把我從監獄裡帶出來，並在撒旦在我和我的兄弟們之間挑起紛爭之後，把你們從沙漠中帶出來。』

title.en: The Basket on the Nile: Musa Nursed by His Own Mother
title.zh: 尼羅河上的木箱：母親乳養的穆薩

region.en: Nile river at Pharaoh's palace, Egypt (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 埃及法老宮旁的尼羅河（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs al-Qasas 28:3-13, Ta-Ha 20:37-40; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 28:3-13

summary.en: Pharaoh exalts himself in the land and makes its people into sects, weakening a party of them, slaying their sons and sparing their women; God wills to favour the oppressed. We reveal to the mother of Musa: 'Suckle him, and when thou fearest for him, cast him into the water, and fear not nor grieve — We will restore him to thee, and make him one of Our messengers.' Pharaoh's household finds him; the wife would have him for a son. All nurses' milk is refused — then his sister says: 'Shall I show you a family who shall nurse him for you?' And so God restored him to his mother, that her eye might be refreshed and she grieve no more.
summary.zh: 法老在國中高傲，分民為派，屠男嬰而留女嬰；真主意欲恩澤受欺者。啟示穆薩之母：『哺育之；若懼，投之於水——我必還你，並立之為使者。』法老家眷拾之，其妻欲收為子。眾乳母皆不合口——其姊獻策，母子重逢，母眼復悅，不再憂傷。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: We rehearse to thee with truth a story of Moses and Pharaoh, for the sake of those who believe. Verily Pharaoh exalted himself in the earth and made its people into sects, weakening a party of them, slaying their sons and letting their women live: for he was one of the agents of corruption. And We wished to be gracious to those who were weakened in the land, and to make them leaders and to make them the heirs, and to settle a power on them in the land, and to show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts what they feared from them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 28:3-6 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我本著真理，為信道的人們，向你敘述穆薩和法老的故事。法老確實在世上妄自尊大，把其人民分成派別，削弱其中的一夥，屠殺他們的兒子，讓他們的婦女存活：因為他是作惡者之一。我欲施恩於那些在地方上被削弱的人，使他們成為領袖，使他們成為繼承者，並使他們在地方上得勢，並讓法老、哈曼和他們的軍隊看到他們所畏懼的事。

passages.text: And We revealed to the mother of Moses: 'Suckle him, and when thou fearest for him, cast him into the water, and fear not and grieve not, for We will restore him to thee, and we will make him one of Our messengers.' And the family of Pharaoh found him, and he became to them an enemy and a sorrow; for Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts were sinners. And Pharaoh's wife said, 'This boy shall be a delight to my eye and to thee — slay him not; haply he may be useful to us, or we may take him for a son; and they knew not what they did.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 28:7-9 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我啟示穆薩的母親說：『給他哺乳吧，當你為他擔憂時，就把他投入水中，不要害怕，不要憂愁，因為我必把他還給你，我必使他成為我的使者之一。』法老的家人發現了他，他便成了他們的仇敵和憂患；因為法老、哈曼和他們的軍隊確是罪人。法老的妻子說：『這孩子將是我和你的眼目之樂——不要殺他；或許他對我們有用，或者我們可以收他為子；他們並不知道自己在做什麼。』

passages.text: And in the morning an iniquitous affliction came on the heart of the mother of Moses: verily she had all but made him public, had We not confirmed her heart that she might be one of the believers. And she said to his sister, 'Follow him.' And she watched him from afar off, and they perceived it not. And they prevented his being nursed by the nurses, until his sister came and said, 'Shall I point out to you a family who shall nurse him for you and who shall advise him?' And thus We restored him to his mother, that her eye might be refreshed, and that she might not be grieved, and that she might know that the promise of God is true.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 28:10-13 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 到了早晨，穆薩母親的心上降臨了不義的憂苦：若不是我堅定她的心，使她成為信道者之一，她幾乎要把他公開了。她對他的姐姐說：『跟隨他吧。』她便從遠處注視著他，而他們並未察覺。他們阻止乳母給他哺乳，直到他的姐姐走來說：『我可以向你們指出一個家庭，他們會為你們哺育他，並且會善待他嗎？』我就這樣把他還給了他的母親，使她眼目清涼，使她不再憂愁，也使她知道真主的應許是真實的。

title.en: The Slaying of the Egyptian and Flight to Midian
title.zh: 殺埃及人與逃往米甸

region.en: Egyptian town and Midian wells (symbolic pin at Sinai oasis)
region.zh: 埃及城鎮與米甸水井（象徵性定位於西奈綠洲）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-Qasas 28:14-28; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 28:14-28

summary.en: Musa comes to manhood, endowed with wisdom and knowledge. Going into the city unmarked, he finds two fighting, one of his party and one of his foes, and the oppressed calls on him for help; he strikes the Egyptian and kills him. 'This is the work of Satan; he is a manifest misleader.' A man from the far end of the city brings word that the chiefs are plotting to slay him; he flies to Midian. At the well, two girls drive back their flock; he waters for them, and their father offers him eight or ten years of service for a marriage portion — and he takes the road to Egypt again, 'with a watchful eye.'
summary.zh: 穆薩成年，智慧知識俱足。入城遇兩人相鬥，受欺者求援；他擊倒埃及人。『此乃魔之所為——他確是明顯的迷誤者。』城中遠端有人報信：長老們欲殺他。他逃往米甸。井旁見二女驅羊後退，他為她們飲羊；其父以八年或十年為聘，許女嫁之。他重返埃及之路，『眼觀四方』。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And when Moses came to full age and strength, We endowed him with wisdom and knowledge: and thus do We reward the beneficent. And he entered the city at a time when its inhabitants were careless of him, and there he found two men fighting, the one of his own religion and the other of his foes; and he who was of his own religion called on him for help against him who was of his foes. And Moses struck him with his fist and killed him. He said, 'This is the work of Satan; and he is a manifest and open misleader.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 28:14-15 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當穆薩長大成人、身強力壯之時，我賜予他智慧與知識；我如此報償行善之人。他趁城中居民不留意他時進入城中，在那裡看見兩人爭鬥，一人屬於他的宗教，另一人屬於他的仇敵；屬於他宗教的那人向他求助，以對抗屬於他仇敵的那人。穆薩用拳頭擊打那人，將他打死。他說：『這是撒旦的作為；他確是明顯公開的迷誤者。』

passages.text: He said, 'O my Lord, I have unjustly slain a soul, therefore forgive me.' And God forgave him; for He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. He said, 'O my Lord, because thou hast forgiven me and shown me favour, I will never again be the helper of the guilty.' And in the morning he was in the city, fearing and cautious; and he who had asked his help the day before, cried out to him for help. Moses said to him, 'Truly thou art a manifest deceiver.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 28:16-18 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他說：『我的主啊，我確已不義地殺害了一個人，求你饒恕我。』真主便饒恕了他；因為祂是至赦的、至慈的。他說：『我的主啊，因為你饒恕了我、施恩於我，我絕不再做犯罪之人的幫手。』次日清晨，他在城中，心懷畏懼、謹慎提防；昨日向他求助的那人又向他呼喊求救。穆薩對他說：『你確是明顯的欺騙者。』

passages.text: And when he would have laid hands on him who was an enemy to them both, he said, 'O Moses, dost thou desire to slay me, as thou didst slay a person yesterday? Thou desirest nothing but to become a tyrant in this land, and desirest not to become a director of the right.' And a man came from the city's remotest part, running, and said, 'O Moses, the chiefs are deliberating about thee, to slay thee; depart hence; I am one of those who wish thee well.' And he went out of the city, afraid and cautious, and said, 'O Lord, deliver me from the unjust people.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 28:19-21 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他想要對那與他們二人為敵的人動手時，那人說：『穆薩啊，你難道想像昨日殺人那樣殺我嗎？你只想在這地方成為暴君，並不想成為引導正道的人。』有一人從城的極遠處跑來，說：『穆薩啊，首領們正在商議如何殺你；你快離開此地吧；我確是為你著想的人之一。』他便懷著畏懼、謹慎地出了城，說：『主啊，求你救我脫離不義的民眾。』

passages.text: And when he came to the waters of Midian he found a company of men watering, and he found beside them two women keeping back their flocks. He said, 'What are ye about?' They said, 'We cannot water our flocks until the shepherds drive off theirs; and our father is very old.' And he watered their flocks, then turned back into the shade, and said, 'O my Lord, I stand in need of the good which thou shalt send down to me.' And the daughters came to him... and their father said, 'I desire to marry thee to one of these my two daughters on condition that thou serve me eight years, or if thou complete ten, it shall be of thy own free gift.' He said, 'Let it be so between me and thee: whichever of the two terms I fulfil, let there be no injustice to me; and God is witness of what I say.' And Moses said, 'Now will I depart with a watchful eye.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 28:23-28 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他來到麥德彥的水邊時，發現一群人正在飲水，又發現他們旁邊有兩個女子攔著她們的羊群。他說：『你們在做什麼？』她們說：『我們要等牧人們把羊群趕走後才能飲羊；我們的父親年紀很老了。』他便替她們飲了羊，然後退到蔭涼處，說：『我的主啊，我確需要你降給我的任何好處。』那兩個女兒來到他面前……她們的父親說：『我願將這兩個女兒中的一個嫁給你，條件是你為我工作八年，你若做滿十年，那是你自願的。』他說：『你我之間就這樣約定吧：無論我完成這兩個期限中的哪一個，都不得對我不義；真主見證我所說的話。』穆薩說：『現在我將謹慎提防地啟程。』

title.en: The Burning Bush in Tuwa: 'Verily I Am Thy Lord'
title.zh: 圖窪的焚荊棘：「我確是你的主」

region.en: Tuwa, the sacred valley of Mount Sinai (literal pin)
region.zh: 西奈山聖谷圖窪（實際定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs Ta-Ha 20:9-24, al-Qasas 28:29-35, al-Qasas 27:7-12; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 20:9-24 and 28:29-35

summary.en: After the term is fulfilled, Moses journeys with his family and sees a fire in the valley of Tuwa. 'I see a fire: haply I may bring you a lighted brand, or may find guidance at the fire.' The voice calls: 'Moses! I am thy Lord — put off thy shoes, for thou art in the sacred valley Tuwa.' He is given two signs: the rod that becomes a serpent, and the hand white but unharmed, thrust into the bosom. 'Go to Pharaoh, for he hath rebelled.' 'And my brother Aaron — make him my helper.' 'Thou shalt be aided through thy brother.'
summary.zh: 穆薩攜家旅行，見圖窪谷中有火光：『或可取火，或可尋得指引。』有聲呼喚：『穆薩！我確是你的主——脫掉你的鞋，你確在聖谷圖窪。』賜兩件徵兆：杖化蛇，手入懷則白而無害。『去見法老，他確已暴虐。』『求你使兄長亞倫相助。』『你必得兄之助。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the divine speech at the burning bush; public-domain translation.

passages.text: Hath the story of Moses reached thee? When he saw a fire, and said to his family, 'Wait ye here, for I see a fire in the distance; haply I may bring you a lighted brand from it, or may find at the fire some guidance.' And when he came up to it, a voice called to him, 'O Moses, verily I am thy Lord; therefore put off thy shoes, for thou art in the sacred valley Tuwa. And I have chosen thee: hearken then to what shall be revealed.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 20:9-13 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 穆薩的故事可曾傳到你？當時他看見一處火光，便對他的家人說：『你們在此等候，我確看見遠處有火光；或許我能從那裡給你們帶來一個火把，或在火旁找到一些指引。』當他走近火光時，有聲音呼喚他：『穆薩啊，我確是你的主；所以你脫下你的鞋，因為你身處聖谷圖瓦。我已揀選了你：所以你要聽取將要啟示的事。』

passages.text: Verily I am God: there is no God but Me: therefore worship Me, and observe prayer in my remembrance... And what is that in thy right hand, O Moses? He said, 'It is my staff: I lean on it; and with it I beat down leaves for my flock; and other uses have I for it.' He said, 'Cast it down, O Moses.' And he cast it down, and behold it became a serpent which ran along. He said, 'Take it and fear not: We will restore it to its former state. And put thy hand into thy bosom: it shall come forth white, but unharmed: — another sign... Go thou to Pharaoh, for he hath rebelled with excess of rebellion.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 20:14-24 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我確是真主：除我之外，別無真主：所以你要崇拜我，並為記念我而謹守禮拜……穆薩啊，你右手裡的是什麼？他說：『這是我的手杖：我倚靠它；我用它為我的羊群打落樹葉；我還有其他用途。』祂說：『穆薩啊，把它扔下。』他便把它扔下，忽然它變成了一條蜿蜒爬行的蛇。祂說：『拿起它，不要害怕：我將使它恢復原狀。把你的手放進你的懷裡：它將出來時潔白，卻毫無損傷：——這是另一個蹟象……你到法老那裡去吧，他確已過分地叛逆了。』

passages.text: And when he came up to it he was called: 'O Moses, verily I am thy Lord; therefore put off thy shoes, for thou art in the sacred valley Tuwa... And what is that in thy right hand, O Moses? He said, 'It is my staff: on it I lean; and with it I beat down leaves for my flock.' He said, 'Cast it down, O Moses.' And he cast it down, and behold, it was a serpent that ran along. He said, 'Take it and fear not: We will restore it to its former state.' He said, 'My Lord, I have slain a man of them, and I fear lest they slay me; and my brother Aaron is more eloquent than I; send him therefore with me as an aider to confirm me; verily I fear that they will treat me as an impostor.' God said, 'We will strengthen thine arm by thy brother, and they shall not touch you: with Our signs, ye twain and those who follow you, shall be victorious.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 28:29-35 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他走近那火時，有聲音呼喚說：「穆薩啊，我確是你的主，你當脫下你的鞋，因為你身處神聖的山谷圖瓦……穆薩啊，你右手裡的是什麼？」他說：「這是我的手杖：我倚靠它；我用它為我的羊群打落樹葉。」主說：「穆薩啊，把它扔下。」他便把它扔下，看哪，它竟成了一條蜿蜒爬行的蛇。主說：「拿起它，不要害怕：我們將使它恢復原狀。」他說：「我的主啊，我曾殺死他們中的一個人，我怕他們會殺我；我的兄弟哈倫比我更能言善辯；求你派他與我同去，作我的助手以證實我；我實在怕他們會把我當作騙子。」真主說：「我們將藉你的兄弟增強你的臂力，他們絕不能傷害你們：憑著我的蹟象，你們二人以及追隨你們的人，必將勝利。」

title.en: The Magicians Cast Down: Serpents, Belief, and the Gibbet
title.zh: 眾術士俯首：蛇變、歸信與十字架

region.en: Egyptian arena before Pharaoh (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 埃及法老前的競技場（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs ash-Shu'ara 26:10-51, al-A'raf 7:103-126; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 26:10-51

summary.en: Pharaoh assembles the magicians for a day of festival; they ask, 'Shall we have a reward if we conquer?' Moses says, 'Cast what ye have to cast'; and they cast down their cords and staves — and through their magic it seemed to him that they were running. Then Moses casts his rod, and it swallows up their lying shows. The magicians fall prostrate: 'We believe in the Lord of all creatures, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.' Pharaoh threatens the gibbet and mutilation; they answer that their Lord's grace they have already attained, 'and Thou art the vengeful of the vengeful.'
summary.zh: 法老召集術士於節日；他們問：『若得勝可有賞？』穆薩說：『扔下你們要扔的。』繩杖落地——幻術之中似在奔跑。穆薩擲杖，杖竟吞其所現。術士俯首：『我們信萬物之主、穆薩與亞倫之主。』法老以磔刑斷手相威；他們答：『我主之恩已獲；你是報復者中之報復者。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And when Moses said, 'Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of all creatures; I speak to you only what is true: send away with me the children of Israel.' He said, 'Did we not nurture thee among us as a child? And thou didst dwell among us years of thy life... and thou hast done the deed which thou hast done, and thou hast been of the ungrateful.' He said, 'I did it indeed, and I was one of those who erred... and I fled from you when I feared you, but my Lord hath given me judgment, and hath made me one of His Apostles.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 26:16-21 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當穆薩說：「法老啊，我確是萬物之主的使者；我只對你們說真話：請你放以色列的子孫與我同去。」法老說：「我們豈不是在你幼年時在我們中間撫養了你嗎？你曾在我們中間度過了你生命中的許多年……你做了你所做的那件事，你是忘恩負義的人。」他說：「我確實做了那件事，我當時是迷誤的人之一……當我畏懼你們時，我便逃離了你們，但我的主賜予我判斷力，並使我成為祂的使者之一。」

passages.text: Pharaoh said, 'If thou puttest forth any god, other than me, I will certainly make thee one of the imprisoned.' Moses said, 'What! though I show thee that which is manifest?' He said, 'Show it me then, if thou art of the truthful.' So he threw down his rod, and lo, it was a serpent which moved along; and he drew out his hand, and lo, it was white to the beholders. Pharaoh said to his nobles, 'Truly this is a skilled enchanter: he wisheth to drive you out of your land by his enchantments; what do ye advise?' They said, 'Put him and his brother off for a while, and send to the cities men who shall assemble all the skilful magicians.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 26:29-37 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 法老說：「你若捨我而另立任何神靈，我必定把你投入監獄。」穆薩說：「即使我向你顯示明顯的蹟象，你也要這樣做嗎？」法老說：「你若說的是實話，就把它顯示給我看吧。」於是他扔下他的手杖，看哪，它竟成了一條游動的蛇；他抽出他的手，看哪，它在觀看者眼前是白色的。法老對他的貴族們說：「這確是一個嫻熟的術士：他想用他的法術把你們逐出你們的土地；你們有什麼建議？」他們說：「暫且把他和他的兄弟擱置一旁，並派人到各城去召集所有嫻熟的術士。」

passages.text: And the magicians came to Pharaoh: 'Shall we indeed be rewarded if we conquer?' He said, 'Yes, and moreover shall ye be of those near my person.' They said, 'O Moses, wilt thou first throw down thy rod, or shall we throw down ours?' Moses said, 'Do ye throw it down first'; and when they threw it down they enchanted the eyes of the people, and dismayed them, for they had wrought a great feat of magic. Then We revealed to Moses, 'Throw down thy rod'; and lo, it swallowed up what they had devised of falsehood. So the enchanters fell down prostrate and said, 'We believe in the Lord of all creatures, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 26:41-48 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 術士們來到法老面前：「如果我們得勝，我們真會得到報酬嗎？」他說：「是的，而且你們還將成為我身邊的近臣。」他們說：「穆薩啊，你先扔下你的手杖，還是我們先扔？」穆薩說：「你們先扔吧」；當他們扔下時，他們迷惑了眾人的眼睛，使他們驚恐，因為他們施展了巨大的法術。於是我們啟示穆薩：「扔下你的手杖」；看哪，它吞掉了他們所捏造的虛假之物。於是術士們俯伏叩拜說：「我們信仰萬物之主，穆薩和哈倫的主。」

passages.text: Pharaoh said, 'Ye believe on Him before I have given you leave! Verily this is a device which ye have devised in this city, that ye may drive out its inhabitants... But I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you all.' They said, 'Verily we shall return to our Lord; but Thou takest vengeance on us only because we have believed on the signs of our Lord when they have come to us. O our Lord, pour out upon us patience, and make us die in submission to thy will.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 26:49-51 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 法老說：「你們竟未經我允許就信仰了他！這確是你們在這城中策劃的陰謀，以便把城中的居民逐出……但我必定將你們的手腳交叉砍斷，並把你們全都釘死在十字架上。」他們說：「我們確將歸於我們的主；你懲罰我們，只因我們信仰了我們的主的蹟象，當它們降臨我們之時。我們的主啊，求你傾注忍耐於我們，並使我們順服你的旨意而死。」

title.en: The Sea Divide: Pharaoh Drowns Watching the Signs
title.zh: 海水分開：法老溺亡於追擊

region.en: Red Sea crossing, Gulf of Suez (literal pin)
region.zh: 紅海渡越，蘇伊士灣（實際定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs ash-Shu'ara 26:52-68, Ta-Ha 20:77-79; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 26:52-68

summary.en: We reveal to Moses: 'Go forth with my servants by night, for ye will be pursued.' Pharaoh sends heralds into the cities: 'These are a small company, yet they have enraged us, and we are a numerous host, watchful.' The two parties come in sight of one another, and the followers of Moses say, 'We shall certainly be pursued.' 'By no means, for my Lord is with me: He will guide me.'
