The sea is cleft in two — each way like a great rampart — and the others are made to follow: the whole host is drowned. Pharaoh says, 'I believe that there is no God but He in whom the children of Israel believe... and I am of those who submit' — 'What! now? when hitherto thou hast rebelled and been of the doers of damage.' The body is left on the shore a sign to after times.
summary.zh: 啟示穆薩：『夜間率僕出走，你們必被追趕。』法老遣使於諸城：『此輩人少，卻激怒我們；我們人多勢眾。』兩軍相望，隨從者言：『我們必被追上。』『不然，我的主同我在一起，他將引導。』海分為二——各如巨大城垣——法老追隨而入，全軍覆沒。臨溺之際，法老信而順服——『現在才信嗎？你早已悖逆。』其屍留於岸，以為後世之鑒。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the drowning of Pharaoh is treated within Islam as a historical deliverance; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And We revealed to Moses, saying, 'Go forth with my servants by night, for ye will be pursued.' And Pharaoh sent heralds into the cities: 'Verily these are a small company, and they have enraged us; and we are a numerous host well prepared.' So We compelled them to quit their gardens and their fountains, and their treasures and their splendid dwellings. Thus it was: and We gave them to the children of Israel for an inheritance.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 26:52-59 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我們啟示穆薩說：「你當率我的僕人們夜行而出，你們必將被追趕。」法老派遣傳令者到各城去：「這些人確是一小群人，他們激怒了我們；而我們是一支準備充分的龐大軍隊。」於是我們迫使他們離開他們的園圃和泉源，以及他們的財寶和華美的住所。事情就是這樣：我們把它們賜給以色列的子孫作為遺產。

passages.text: And the people of Pharaoh pursued them at sunrise. And when the two parties were within sight of one another, those who were with Moses said, 'We shall surely be pursued.' Moses said, 'By no means, for my Lord is with me, and will guide me.' And We revealed to Moses, saying, 'Smite the sea with thy rod.' And when he smote it, it was divided into two parts, and each part was like a huge mound. And We made the others to come up in that place; and We saved Moses and all who were with him; and We drowned the others.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 26:60-66 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 法老的人眾在日出時追趕他們。當兩隊人馬彼此相望的時候，與穆薩同在的人說：『我們必定要被追上了。』穆薩說：『絕不然，我的主確是與我同在的，他必引導我。』我啟示穆薩說：『你用你的手杖擊打海。』當他擊打它的時候，海就分開成為兩部分，每一部分都像巨大的土丘。我使另一夥人在那個地方前來；我拯救了穆薩和所有與他同在的人；我淹沒了另一夥人。

passages.text: Pharaoh said, 'O chiefs, I know not that ye have any god beside me: light a fire for me, O Haman, and bake clay, and build me a tower that I may mount up to the God of Moses; for verily I think that he is a liar.' And the drowning overtook him: 'I believe that there is no God but He in whom the children of Israel believe, and I am of those who submit to Him.' 'What! now? when hitherto thou hast rebelled and been of the doers of damage. This day will We save thee in thy body only, that thou mayest be a sign to those who shall come after thee: for verily many among mankind are regardless of Our signs.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 28:38, 10:90-92 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 法老說：『眾首領啊，我知道除我之外，你們並沒有別的神明：哈曼啊，你為我點火燒泥，為我築一座高塔，好讓我攀登上去見穆薩的神；因為我確信他是一個說謊的人。』於是溺亡臨到了他：『我確信，除以色列子孫所信仰的那位之外，別無神明，我確是歸順他的人。』『什麼！現在才信嗎？你以前確曾違抗，並且是作惡的人。今日我僅保全你的身體，好使你成為後世之人的鑒戒：因為人類中確有許多人疏忽我的蹟象。』

title.en: Musa and Khidr at the Meeting of the Two Seas
title.zh: 穆薩與花德爾於兩海交會處

region.en: Al-Majma', the place where the two seas meet (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 兩海交會之處（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-Kahf 18:60-82; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 18:60-82

summary.en: Moses says to his servant, 'I will not cease until I reach the place where the two seas meet, though I journey years.' At the rock they forget the fish, which takes its way in the sea; at morning Moses says, 'This is the very place.' They find one of Our servants whom God has taught knowledge from Himself. Moses asks to follow and learn; the man warns, 'Thou canst not bear with me patiently — how canst thou bear what thou hast not comprehended?' Three deeds follow: the scuttled ship, the slain boy, the raised wall. And the meaning: the ship belonged to poor toilers, a tyrant king was at sea; the boy was bound for evil deeds and unbelief; the wall was orphans', their treasure beneath — 'thy Lord willed that they should reach their maturity and bring forth their treasure as a mercy from thy Lord. And I did it not of mine own accord.'
summary.zh: 穆薩對僕人說：『我必行至兩海交會處，縱行多年。』至磐石處忘了魚，魚遂入海；清晨穆薩道：『此即其所。』遇主之僕，主曾以己之知識授之。穆薩求隨從學習；對方警告：『你不能耐我——你何能耐所不解之事？』三事隨之：鑿船、殺童、扶牆。義理：船乃貧者之財，海上暴君將奪；童子父母皆信主，恐其悖逆忘恩；牆屬孤兒，寶藏於下——『你的主意欲他們成年取出寶藏，出於你的主的恩慈。並非我自作主張。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the identity of the 'servant of God' (Khidr) is a matter of tafsir tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And when Moses said to his servant, 'I will not cease until I reach the place where the two seas meet, though I journey years'; and when they had reached the meeting-place of the two seas, they forgot their fish, and he took his way in the sea freely. And when they had passed on, Moses said to his servant, 'Bring us our morning meal, for we are weary with this journey.' He said, 'Dost thou see what has happened? When we repaired to the rock for repose, then verily I forgot the fish — and none but Satan caused me to forget it — and he took his way into the sea in a wondrous sort.' Moses said, 'It was for this we waited'; and they went back again, retracing their footsteps.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 18:60-64 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當時穆薩對他的僕人說：『我絕不停止，直到我到達兩海交匯之處，即使我要旅行許多年。』當他們到達兩海交匯之處時，他們忘了他們的魚，那魚便自在地游入海中。當他們走過之後，穆薩對他的僕人說：『拿我們的早餐來吧，我們確因這趟旅行而疲倦了。』他說：『你可曾看見所發生的事？當我們在磐石旁休息的時候，我確忘了那魚——只有撒旦使我忘了它——那魚便奇妙地游入海中。』穆薩說：『這正是我們所尋求的』；於是他們折返，循著自己的足跡回去。

passages.text: Then they found one of Our servants unto whom We had given mercy from Ourself, and unto whom We had given knowledge proceeding from Ourself. And Moses said to him, 'Shall I follow thee, that thou mayest teach me, for instruction's sake, some of what thou hast been taught?' He said, 'Verily thou wilt be unable to bear with me patiently: and how canst thou bear patiently that which thou hast not comprehended?' Moses said, 'If I ask thee aught concerning this, when thou hast taught me, then befriend me not: thou hast an excuse for leaving me.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 18:65-70 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是他們發現了我的一個僕人，我曾賜予他來自我的恩惠，並曾賜予他來自我的知識。穆薩對他說：『我可以跟隨你嗎？好讓你把你所受的教導，本著教誨之意，教給我一些。』他說：『你確不能耐心地忍受我。你怎能耐心地忍受你所不能理解的事呢？』穆薩說：『如果我在此事上向你問了什麼，當你已教導我之後，就不要再與我為友：你已有離開我的理由了。』

passages.text: They proceeded on their way until they embarked on board a vessel, and he scuttled it. 'What! hast thou scuttled it that thou mayest drown its crew? Now hast thou done a strange thing.' He said, 'Did I not tell thee that thou couldst not bear with me patiently?' And they travelled on till they met a youth, and he slew him. Moses said, 'Hast thou slain him who is innocent, and for no cause? Now hast thou wrought a grievous thing.' And they travelled on till they came to a city, and they asked its food of the inhabitants, but they refused them hospitality... And they found there a wall which was about to fall, and he set it upright.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 18:71-77 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們繼續前行，直到他們登上一艘船，他卻把它鑿穿。『什麼！你把它鑿穿，是要淹死它的船員嗎？你確已做了一件怪事。』他說：『我不是告訴過你，你不能耐心地忍受我嗎？』他們繼續前行，直到他們遇見一個青年，他就殺了他。穆薩說：『你殺了一個無辜的人，而且毫無緣由嗎？你確已做了一件嚴重的事。』他們繼續前行，直到他們來到一座城市，他們向居民求食，但他們拒絕款待他們……他們在那裡發現一堵將要倒塌的牆，他就把它扶正。

passages.text: He said, 'This is the parting between me and thee. I will tell thee the meaning of that which thou couldst not bear with patience. As to the vessel, it belonged to poor men who toiled upon the sea; and I was minded to render it unsound, for there was after them a king who seized every vessel by force. And as to the youth, his parents were believers, and we feared lest he should stir them up to rebellion and unbelief; and we desired that their Lord might give them in his place a child more pure than he, and more kindly. And as to the wall, it belonged to two orphan youths of the city, and beneath it was a treasure hidden which belonged to them; and their father was a righteous man: and thy Lord willed that they should reach the age of strength and bring forth their treasure as a mercy from thy Lord. And I did it not of mine own accord: such is the interpretation of that which thou couldst not bear with patience.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 18:78-82 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他說：『這是我與你之間的分別。我要告訴你那些你不能耐心忍受之事的意思。至於那艘船，它屬於一些在海上勞作的窮人；我想使它有缺陷，因為他們之後有一位國王，強行奪取每一艘船。至於那個青年，他的父母是信士，我們怕他會使他們陷於叛逆與不信；我們希望他們的主以一個比他更純潔、更慈祥的孩子代替他賜給他們。至於那堵牆，它屬於城中兩個孤兒青年，牆下埋藏著屬於他們的寶藏；他們的父親是一個正直的人：你的主願意他們達到壯年，並取出他們的寶藏，作為來自你的主的恩惠。我並非自作主張做這些事：這就是那些你不能耐心忍受之事的意思。』

title.en: Shiphrah and Puah Defy Pharaoh
title.zh: 施弗拉與普阿違抗法老

region.en: Egypt, Nile Delta (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 埃及尼羅河三角洲（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-8th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Exodus 1:15-22, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Pharaoh orders the Hebrew midwives Shiphrah and Puah to kill every boy at birth; 'but the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men-children alive.' Asked why, they answer that the vigorous Hebrew women deliver before the midwife comes — 'and God dealt well with the midwives... and He made them houses.'
summary.zh: 法老命希伯來收生婆施弗拉普阿於產時殺男嬰；「但是收生婆敬畏神，不照埃及王的吩咐行，竟存留男孩的性命」。被問何以如此，答以希伯來婦人健壯，收生婆未到已生——「神厚待收生婆……為她們成立家室。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the midwives said unto Pharaoh: 'Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women; for they are lively, and are delivered ere the midwife come unto them.' And God dealt well with the midwives; and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty. And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that He made them houses.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Exodus 1:19-21 (public domain).
passages.zh: 收生婆對法老說：「因為希伯來婦人與埃及婦人不同；她們本是健壯的，收生婆還沒有到，她們已經生產了。」神厚待收生婆；百姓多起來，極其強盛。收生婆因為敬畏神，神便叫她們成立家室。

title.en: The Babe in the Bulrushes
title.zh: 蒲草箱中的嬰孩

region.en: Nile riverbank (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 尼羅河畔（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-8th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Exodus 2:1-10, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: A Levite woman hides her beautiful son three months, then sets him in an ark of bulrushes — the same word, tebah, as Noah's — among the flags by the river's brink. Pharaoh's daughter draws him out, hires the mother as nurse, and names him Moshe, 'because', she said, 'I drew him out of the water.'
summary.zh: 利未婦人藏其俊美之子三月，置於蒲草箱——與挪亞方舟同字tebah——河邊蘆葦中。法老之女撈起，僱其母為乳母，名之摩西，「因我把他從水裡拉出來」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And when she had opened it, she saw the child; and behold, a boy that wept. And she had compassion on him, and said: 'This is one of the Hebrews' children.' ... And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moshe, and said: 'Because I drew him out of the water.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Exodus 2:6, 10 (public domain); condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 她打開箱子，看見那孩子；不料，是個男孩在哭。她就憐憫他，說：「這是希伯來人的一個孩子。」……孩子漸長，她把他帶到法老的女兒那裏，他就作了她的兒子。她給孩子起名叫摩西，說：「因我把他從水裏拉出來。」

title.en: Moses Flees to Midian and the Well of the Seven Daughters
title.zh: 摩西逃往米甸與七女之井

region.en: Well of Midian, Sinai approaches
region.zh: 米甸井旁，西奈道中

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-8th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Exodus 2:11-22, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Moses, grown, goes out to his brethren and kills the Egyptian striking a Hebrew, burying him in the sand — 'and he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian'. Pharaoh seeks his life; he flees to Midian, drives off shepherds from Jethro's seven daughters at the well, marries Zipporah, and names his firstborn Gershom: 'I have been a stranger in a strange land.'
summary.zh: 摩西長大，出至弟兄那裡，殺欺壓希伯來人的埃及人，埋於沙中——「他左右觀看，見沒有人，就把埃及人打死了」。法老尋索性命；他逃至米甸，於井旁趕走牧羊人，救葉忒羅七女，娶西坡拉，長子名革順：「我在外邦作了寄居的。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock. And they came to Reuel their father, and he said: 'How is it that ye are come so soon today?' ... And he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter. And she bore a son, and he called his name Gershom; for he said: 'I have been a stranger in a strange land.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Exodus 2:17-22 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 有牧羊的人來，把她們趕走了；但摩西起來幫助她們，又飲了她們的羊群。她們回到父親流珥那裏，他說：「你們今日怎麼回來得這麼快呢？」……他就把他的女兒西坡拉給摩西為妻。她生了一個兒子，摩西給他起名叫革舜；因為他說：「我在外邦作了寄居的。」

title.en: Zipporah's Knife: A Bridegroom of Blood in the Inn
title.zh: 西坡拉之刀：客旅中血的新郎

region.en: Lodging on the road from Midian to Egypt
region.zh: 米甸往埃及路上宿處

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-8th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Exodus 4:18-31, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: On the way back to Egypt, 'the LORD met him, and sought to kill him'. Zipporah takes a flint, circumcises her son, and touches Moses' feet with the foreskin: 'Surely a bridegroom of blood art thou to me' — one of the Bible's most cryptic episodes, an etiology of circumcision and a night-vision of divine danger.
summary.zh: 歸埃及路上，「耶和華遇見他，想要殺他」。西坡拉取火石刀，為兒子行割禮，以陽皮觸摩西的腳：「你因割禮就是血郎了。」——聖經最隱晦篇章之一，割禮釋義與神聖危險之夜象。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And it came to pass on the way at the lodging-place, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him. Then Zipporah took a flint, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet; and she said: 'Surely a bridegroom of blood art thou to me.' So He let him alone.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Exodus 4:24-26 (public domain), lightly condensed.
passages.zh: 在路途中住宿的時候，耶和華遇見他，想要殺他。西坡拉就拿一塊火石，割下她兒子的陽皮，丟在他腳前，說：「你真是我的血郎了。」這樣，耶和華才放了他。

title.en: Jethro's Counsel: Organizing the Judges
title.zh: 葉忒羅獻策：設立審判官

region.en: Camp before Rephidim, wilderness of Sinai
region.zh: 利非丁前營地，西奈曠野

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-8th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Exodus 18, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Jethro, priest of Midian, brings Zipporah and the boys to Moses, hears the tale of the exodus, blesses the LORD, and offers sacrifice with the elders. Seeing Moses judging alone from morning to night, he warns: 'Thou wilt surely wear away... The thing that thou doest is not good.' His plan — rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, tens, judging small matters — founds Israel's judiciary, and the peace-offering precedent.
summary.zh: 米甸祭司葉忒羅送西坡拉與二子至摩西，聞出埃及之事，頌耶和華，與長老獻祭。見摩西自朝至暮獨審眾民，諫曰：「你必疲憊……你這作得不好。」其策——立千夫長百夫長五十夫長十夫長，審小事——立以色列司法之基，並獻平安祭之例。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God be with thee: be thou for the people toward God, and bring thou the causes unto God. And thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating unjust gain; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Exodus 18:19-21 (public domain).
passages.zh: 現在你要聽我的話，我為你出個主意，願神與你同在：你要替百姓到神面前，將案件奏告神。又要從百姓中揀選有才能的人，就是敬畏神、誠實無妄、恨不義之財的人，派他們作千夫長、百夫長、五十夫長、十夫長，管理百姓。

title.en: Thunder and Thick Cloud: The LORD Descends on Sinai
title.zh: 雷轟密雲：耶和華降臨西奈

region.en: Mount Sinai (traditional Jebel Musa; symbolic pin)
region.zh: 西奈山（傳統耶別穆薩；象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-8th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Exodus 19, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: On the third day of consecration there are thunders and lightnings, a thick cloud, and the voice of a shofar exceeding loud; 'and mount Sinai was altogether on smoke, because the LORD descended upon it in fire'. The people tremble, bounds are set about the mountain, and the whole nation hears God speak — the covenant's cosmic overture.
summary.zh: 自潔第三日，雷轟閃電，密雲，角聲甚大；「西奈全山冒烟，因為耶和華在火中降於山上」。百姓發顫，山之四界限定，全民聽神說話——立約之宇宙序曲。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Read annually at Shavuot.

passages.text: And it came to pass on the third day, when it was morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of a horn exceeding loud; and all the people that were in the camp trembled. And Moses brought forth the people out of the camp to meet God; and they stood at the nether part of the mount. Now mount Sinai was altogether on smoke, because the LORD descended upon it in fire; and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mount quaked greatly.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Exodus 19:16-18 (public domain).
passages.zh: 到了第三天早晨，山上有雷轟、閃電和密雲，並且角聲甚大；營中的百姓盡都發顫。摩西率領百姓出營迎接神；他們都站在山下。西奈全山冒煙，因為耶和華在火中降於山上；山的煙氣上騰，如燒窯一般，遍山大大震動。

title.en: The Ten Words Spoken from the Mountain
title.zh: 山中所說十誡

region.en: Mount Sinai (traditional Jebel Musa; symbolic pin)
region.zh: 西奈山（傳統耶別穆薩；象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-8th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Exodus 20:1-17, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: God speaks the Ten Words directly: no other gods, no graven image, no vain oath of His name, the Sabbath rest, honouring parents, and the prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft, false witness, and coveting — 'all the people perceived the thunderings... and they said unto Moses: Speak thou with us, and we will hear; but let not God speak with us, lest we die.'
summary.zh: 神親言十誡：獨一神、不可偶像、不可妄稱名、守安息、孝父母，與殺人、姦淫、偷盜、作假見證、貪婪諸禁——「眾百姓見雷轟閃電……就對摩西說：求你和我們說話，我們必聽；不要神和我們說話，恐怕我們死亡。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: I am the LORD thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt have no other gods before Me. Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour... but the seventh day is a sabbath unto the LORD thy God. Honour thy father and thy mother... Thou shalt not murder. Thou shalt not commit adultery. Neither shalt thou steal. Neither shalt thou bear false witness... Neither shalt thou covet. And all the people perceived the thunderings, and the lightnings, and the voice of the horn, and the mountain smoking. Paraphrase of Exodus 20:8-18 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Exodus 20:2-3 (public domain). / Paraphrase of Exodus 20:8-18 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我是耶和華你的神，曾將你從埃及地、從為奴之家領出來。你在我面前不可有別的神。當記念安息日，守為聖日。六日要勞碌……但第七日是向耶和華你神當守的安息日。當孝敬你的父親和母親……不可殺人。不可行淫。也不可偷盜。也不可作假見證……也不可貪戀。眾百姓都看見雷轟、閃電、角聲和山上冒煙。出埃及記二十章八至十八節意譯（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: We Will Do and We Will Hear: The Covenant Sealed with Blood
title.zh: 我們必行必聽：以血立約

region.en: Mount Sinai (traditional Jebel Musa; symbolic pin)
region.zh: 西奈山（傳統耶別穆薩；象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-8th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Exodus 24, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Moses writes 'all the words of the LORD', builds an altar and twelve pillars, dashes half the blood against the altar, and reads the Book of the Covenant. The people answer with the famous twofold oath: 'All that the LORD hath spoken will we do, and obey.' Blood is sprinkled on the people; the elders see the God of Israel and eat and drink.
summary.zh: 摩西將「耶和華一切所吩咐的」寫下，築壇立十二根柱子，以一半血灑壇，誦約書。百姓以雙重誓言應之：「耶和華所吩咐的，我們都必遵行。」血灑於民；長老們看見以色列的神，又喫又喝。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. 'Na'aseh venishma' became the paradigmatic declaration of Jewish obedience.

passages.text: And he took the book of the covenant, and read in the audience of the people; and they said: 'All that the LORD hath spoken will we do, and obey.' And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said: 'Behold the blood of the covenant, which the LORD hath made with you in agreement with all these words.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Exodus 24:7-8 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他又拿起約書，念給百姓聽；他們說：『耶和華所吩咐的，我們都必遵行，也必聽從。』摩西取血，灑在百姓身上，說：『看哪，這是立約的血，是耶和華按這一切話與你們立約的憑據。』

passages.text: Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders of Israel went up; 'and they saw the God of Israel; and there was under His feet the like of a paved work of sapphirine stone... and upon the nobles of the children of Israel He laid not His hand... and they beheld God, and did eat and drink.' Moses then went up alone into the cloud, six days veiled, on the seventh called — forty days and nights. Paraphrase of Exodus 24:9-18 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Exodus 24:9-18 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 摩西、亞倫、拿答、亞比戶，並以色列七十位長老都上去；『他們看見以色列的神；祂腳下彷彿有藍寶石鋪就的明淨之物……祂的手不加害以色列的貴胄……他們觀看神，又吃又喝。』隨後摩西獨自上山進入雲中，雲遮蓋六日，第七日蒙召——共四十晝夜。出埃及記二十四章九至十八節意譯（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: The Golden Calf: Making Gods in the Silence
title.zh: 金牛犢：靜默中造神

region.en: Camp at Sinai (traditional Jebel Musa; symbolic pin)
region.zh: 西奈山下營地（傳統耶別穆薩；象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-8th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Exodus 32, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: With Moses forty days on the mountain, the people demand: 'Up, make us gods which shall go before us'. Aaron casts the gold into a calf; the people eat, drink, and 'rose up to make merry'. God threatens to destroy them and start again with Moses; Moses descends, breaks the tablets at the foot of the mountain, burns the calf, grinds it to powder, and makes Israel drink its water — while three thousand fall by the sword of the Levites.
summary.zh: 摩西山上四十日，百姓要求：「起來，為我們作神像，可以在我們前面引路。」亞倫熔金成犢；百姓坐下喫喝，「起來玩耍」。神欲滅之另立摩西；摩西下山，於山腳摔碎法版，焚犢磨粉，撒入水中令以色列人喝——利未人之刀殺三千人。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Read on the fast day following Yom Kippur haftarah cycle.

passages.text: And he took the calf which they had made, and burnt it with fire, and ground it to powder, and strewed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it. And Moses said unto Aaron: 'What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought a great sin upon them?'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Exodus 32:20-21 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他取來他們所鑄的牛犢，用火焚燒，磨成粉末，撒在水面上，叫以色列人喝。摩西對亞倫說：『這百姓向你做了什麼，你竟使他們陷在大罪裡？』

passages.text: While the people feasted, the LORD told Moses: 'Go, get thee down; for thy people have corrupted themselves'. Moses prayed — 'Turn from Thy fierce wrath, and repent of this evil against Thy people... Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel' — and 'the LORD repented of the evil which He said He would do'. Descending with Joshua, Moses heard the singing, saw the calf and the dancing, and hurled the tablets down, shattering them at the mountain's foot. He stood in the gate crying: 'Whoso is on the LORD's side, come unto me!' and the sons of Levi gathered to him. Paraphrase of Exodus 32:7-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Exodus 32:7-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 百姓正在宴樂之時，耶和華對摩西說：『下去吧；你的百姓已經敗壞了。』摩西禱告——『求你轉意，不發你的烈怒，後悔不降這災禍與你的百姓……求你記念亞伯拉罕、以撒、以色列』——於是『耶和華就後悔，不把所說的災禍降與祂的百姓』。摩西與約書亞一同下山，聽見歌唱之聲，看見牛犢和跳舞的人，便將兩塊石版扔下，在山腳摔碎了。他站在營門中呼喊：『凡屬耶和華的，都到我這裡來！』利未的子孫都聚集到他那裡。出埃及記三十二章七至二十九節意譯（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Show Me, I Pray Thee, Thy Glory
title.zh: 求你顯出你的榮耀

region.en: Tent of meeting outside the camp, Sinai
region.zh: 營外相會之幕，西奈

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-8th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Exodus 33:12-34:35, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: After the calf, Moses intercedes in the tent of meeting, 'and the LORD would speak unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend'. Moses asks to see God's glory; he is hid in a rock's cleft and shown only the back parts, and the Name is proclaimed: 'The LORD, the LORD, merciful and gracious, long-suffering'. New tablets are cut, the covenant is renewed, and Moses returns with a shining face veiled before the people.
summary.zh: 金牛犢之後，摩西在相會幕中代求，「耶和華與摩西面對面說話，如人與朋友說話一般」。摩西求見榮耀；藏於磐石穴，只見背，並聽名之宣示：「耶和華，耶和華，是有憐憫有恩典的神，不輕易發怒」。新法版重立，約復定；摩西帶著發光之面歸回，面帕蒙之於民前。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The thirteen divine attributes (Exod 34:6-7) are recited in Selichot penitential liturgy.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of the testimony in Moses' hand... that Moses knew not that the skin of his face sent forth beams while He talked with him. And when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face sent forth beams; and they were afraid to come nigh him.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Exodus 34:29-30 (public domain).
passages.zh: 摩西手裡拿著兩塊法版，從西奈山下來的時候……摩西不知道自己的面皮因耶和華和他說話就發了光。亞倫和以色列眾人看見摩西，見他面皮發光，就怕挨近他。

passages.text: Moses asked: 'I pray Thee, show me Thy glory.' The answer defines visibility itself: 'Thou canst not see My face... I will put thee in a cleft of the rock, and will cover thee with My hand... and thou shalt see My back; but My face shall not be seen.' Then, descending with the second tablets, Moses passed before the LORD proclaiming the thirteen attributes of mercy — the theological charter Judaism recites in every season of repentance. Paraphrase of Exodus 33:18-23; 34:6-8 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Exodus 33:18-23; 34:6-8 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 摩西說：「求你顯出你的榮耀給我看。」那回答界定了可見性本身：「你不能看見我的面……我必將你放在磐石穴中，用我的手遮掩你……你就得見我的背，卻不得見我的面。」隨後，摩西帶著第二塊法版下山，從耶和華面前經過，宣告憐憫的十三種屬性——這是猶太教在每個悔改季節所誦念的神學憲章。出埃及記三十三章十八至二十三節、三十四章六至八節之釋義（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Strange Fire: The Death of Nadab and Abihu
title.zh: 凡火：拿答亞比戶之死

region.en: Tent of meeting, wilderness of Sinai
region.zh: 相會之幕，西奈曠野

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE (Priestly source); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Leviticus 10:1-7, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: On the first day of the priesthood, Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu 'took each of them his censer, and put fire therein, and laid incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the LORD, which He had not commanded them' — and fire from the LORD consumes them. Aaron is silent: 'And Aaron held his peace.'
summary.zh: 祭司就任首日，亞倫二子拿答亞比戶「各拿香爐，盛上火，加上香，在耶和華面前獻上凡火，是耶和華沒有吩咐他們的」——遂有火從耶和華面前出來，吞滅他們。亞倫靜默：「亞倫就默默不言。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then Moses said unto Aaron: 'This is it that the LORD spoke, saying: Through them that are nigh unto Me I will be sanctified; and before all the people I will be glorified.' And Aaron held his peace. And Moses said... 'let not your heads go uncovered, neither rend your clothes, lest ye die, and lest wrath come upon all the people.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Leviticus 10:3, 6 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 於是摩西對亞倫說：「這就是耶和華所說：『我在親近我的人中要顯為聖；在眾民面前，我要得榮耀。』」亞倫就默默不言。摩西又說……「不可蓬頭散髮，也不可撕裂衣裳，免得你們死亡，又免得耶和華向全會眾發怒。」

title.en: The Spirit on the Seventy Elders, and Eldad and Medad
title.zh: 靈降七十長老與伊勒達米達

region.en: Camp in the wilderness of Paran
region.zh: 巴蘭曠野營地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Numbers 11:16-30, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Burdened by the people's weeping for meat, Moses cries: 'I am not able to bear all this people alone'. God tells him to gather seventy elders at the tent; the spirit that rests on him is placed on them, and they prophesy — but do not continue. Two men left in the camp, Eldad and Medad, prophesy in the camp itself; Joshua would have them restrained, and Moses answers with the ideal of shared prophecy: 'Would God that all the LORD's people were prophets.'
summary.zh: 百姓因要肉而泣，摩西呼曰：「管理這百姓的責任太重了，我獨自當不起。」神命於幕前集七十長老；降於摩西的靈分與之，他們受感說話——卻不再繼續。營中還有伊勒達米達二人受感說話；約書亞欲禁之，摩西以共承預言之理想答：「惟願耶和華的百姓都受感說話。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And there ran a young man, and told Moses, and said: 'Eldad and Medad do prophesy in the camp.' And Joshua the son of Nun, the minister of Moses from his youth up, answered and said: 'My lord Moses, restrain them.' And Moses said unto him: 'Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the LORD's people were prophets, that the LORD would put His spirit upon them!'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Numbers 11:27-29 (public domain).
passages.zh: 有個少年人跑來告訴摩西說：「伊利達、米達在營裡說預言。」摩西的幫手，嫩的兒子約書亞，就是摩西所揀選的，說：「請我主摩西禁止他們。」摩西對他說：「你為我的緣故嫉妒人嗎？惟願耶和華的百姓都受感說話，願耶和華把他的靈降在他們身上！」

title.en: Quails at Kibroth-hattaavah: Meat That Became a Plague
title.zh: 基博羅哈他瓦的鵪鶉：成疫之肉

region.en: Kibroth-hattaavah, wilderness of Paran
region.zh: 基博羅哈他瓦，巴蘭曠野

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Numbers 11:31-35, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: A wind brings quails from the sea two cubits deep upon the camp; the people gather heaps, and while the meat is 'yet between their teeth' the LORD smites them with a very great plague. The place is named Kibroth-hattaavah, 'graves of lust', 'because there they buried the people that lusted' — the etiology of a greed punished by satiety.
summary.zh: 風自海刮鵪鶉散於營旁約二肘；百姓聚斂成堆，肉「還在牙齒之間」未嚼盡，耶和華即以極重之疫擊之。其地名基博羅哈他瓦，「貪慾之墳」，「因為他們在那裡葬埋那起貪慾之心的人」——貪得而飽即死之釋義。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And while the flesh was yet between their teeth, ere it was chewed, the wrath of the LORD was kindled against the people, and the LORD smote the people with a very great plague. And he called the name of that place Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people that lusted.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Numbers 11:33-34 (public domain).
passages.zh: 肉在他們牙齒之間尚未嚼爛，耶和華的怒氣就向百姓發作，耶和華用極重的災殃擊殺了那民。那地方便叫做基博羅哈他瓦，因為他們在那裡葬埋了那些起貪慾之心的人。

title.en: The Spies and the Bad Report of Canaan
title.zh: 窺探迦南與惡信

region.en: Hebron and Eshcol, land of Canaan
region.zh: 希伯崙與以實各谷，迦南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Numbers 13-14, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Twelve scouts bring back grapes of Eshcol — 'and they came unto the brook of Eshcol, and cut down from thence a branch with one cluster of grapes' — and news of giants. Ten give the bad report that demoralizes Israel; Caleb and Joshua stand alone. The nation weeps and threatens to stone them; God decrees forty years of wandering, a year for each day — the generation that left Egypt will not enter.
summary.zh: 十二探子攜以實各谷葡萄而歸——「砍了葡萄的一枝，用兩個人抬著」——並述巨人之地。十人報惡信喪以色列之膽；迦勒約書亞獨持異議。全民夜哭欲以石擊之；神判四十年漂流，一日抵一年——出埃及的一代不得入。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they told him, and said: 'We came unto the land whither thou sentest us, and surely it floweth with milk and honey; and this is the fruit of it. Howbeit the people that dwell in the land are fierce, and the cities are fortified, and very great... and there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, come of the giants; and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Numbers 13:27-33 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 他們告訴摩西說：「我們到了你所打發我們去的那地，果然是流奶與蜜之地；這就是那地的果子。然而住那地的民強壯，城邑也堅固寬大……我們在那裡看見了巨人，就是亞衲族人，是巨人的後裔；據我們看自己就如蚱蜢一樣，據他們看我們也是如此。」

passages.text: Caleb silenced the people: 'Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able'. But the congregation wept that night. Joshua and Caleb rent their clothes — 'if the LORD delight in us, then He will bring us into this land... rebel not against the LORD, neither fear ye the people of the land' — and the assembly moved to stone them. The glory of the LORD appeared, and the sentence fell: 'Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness... and your children shall be shepherds in the wilderness forty years.' Paraphrase of Numbers 14:6-39 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Numbers 14:6-39 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 迦勒使百姓安靜，說：「我們立刻上去得那地吧！我們足能得勝。」但全會眾那一夜都哭號。約書亞和迦勒撕裂衣裳——「耶和華若喜悅我們，就必將我們領進那地……不要背叛耶和華，也不要怕那地的居民」——會眾卻要拿石頭打死他們。耶和華的榮光顯現，判語就臨到：「你們的屍首必倒在這曠野……你們的兒女必在曠野飄流四十年。」民數記十四章六至三十九節之釋義（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Korah's Rebellion and the Earth That Opened
title.zh: 可拉之叛與裂地

region.en: Camp in the wilderness of Paran
region.zh: 巴蘭曠野營地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE (Priestly); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Numbers 16, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Korah, with Dathan, Abiram, and 250 princes, challenges Moses and Aaron: 'all the congregation are holy'. Moses proposes a censer-test before the LORD. When God threatens the whole assembly, Moses and Aaron fall on their faces; the ground splits and swallows the rebels alive, fire consumes the censers' men, and the bronze censers are hammered into a covering for the altar as a memorial sign.
summary.zh: 可拉與大坍亞比蘭並二百五十名首領挑戰摩西亞倫：「全會眾個個既是聖潔的」。摩西提香爐之試。神欲滅全會眾之際，摩西亞倫俯伏；地遂裂開活吞叛逆者，火滅持香爐之人，銅香爐被錘成片包壇作記號。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And it came to pass, as he made an end of speaking all these words, that the ground did cleave asunder that was under them. And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their households, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods. So they, and all that appertained to them, went down alive into the pit; and the earth closed upon them, and they perished from among the assembly.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Numbers 16:31-33 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他說完這一切話，他們腳下的地就裂開。地張開了口，把他們和他們的家眷，並一切屬可拉的人丁和財物，都吞了下去。這樣，他們和一切屬他們的，都活活地墜入陰間；地就在他們上面合攏，他們便從會眾中滅亡了。

title.en: Aaron's Staff Blossoms: Almonds Overnight
title.zh: 亞倫杖開花：一夜杏花

region.en: Tent of meeting, wilderness of Paran
region.zh: 相會之幕，巴蘭曠野

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE (Priestly); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Numbers 17, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: To end the murmuring against the priesthood, each prince brings a staff, Aaron's among them, laid overnight before the testimony. In the morning Aaron's staff 'had budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded ripe almonds' — a living, fruiting sign within one night. The staff is kept before the testimony 'for a token against the children of rebellion'.
summary.zh: 為止會眾對祭司之怨，各支派首領各取杖，亞倫之杖在內，一夜置於法櫃前。清晨亞倫的杖「已經發了芽，生了花苞，開了花，結了熟杏」——一夜之間活而結果之兆。杖存於法櫃前，「給叛逆之子留作記號」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses went into the tent of the testimony; and, behold, the staff of Aaron for the house of Levi was blossomed, and put forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded ripe almonds. And Moses brought out all the rods from before the LORD unto all the children of Israel; and they looked, and took every man his rod.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Numbers 17:23-24 (public domain).
passages.zh: 第二天，摩西進法櫃的帳幕去；不料，利未族亞倫的杖已經發了芽，生了花苞，開了花，結了熟杏。摩西就把所有的杖從耶和華面前拿出來，給以色列眾人看；他們看見了，各人就把自己的杖取回去。

title.en: The Bronze Serpent in the Wilderness
title.zh: 曠野中的銅蛇

region.en: Road around Edom, wilderness
region.zh: 繞以東之路，曠野

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Numbers 21:4-9, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Complaining against God and Moses on the Edom detour, Israel is plagued by 'fiery serpents' whose bitings kill many. The people confess; God tells Moses to make a serpent and set it on a pole — 'and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he seeth it, shall live'. Moses makes one of brass; the image, named Nehushtan, later stood in the Temple until Hezekiah smashed it.
summary.zh: 以色列繞以東而行，怨神與摩西，遂遭「火蛇」之咬，死者甚多。百姓認罪；神命摩西造一蛇掛在杆上——「凡被咬的，一望這蛇，就必活」。摩西造銅蛇；其像名尼忽士坦，後立於聖殿，至希西家拆毀。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. 2 Kings 18:4 records Hezekiah's destruction of the Nehushtan as idolatrous image.

passages.text: And the people came to Moses, and said: 'We have sinned, because we have spoken against the LORD, and against thee; pray unto the LORD, that He take away the serpents from us.' And Moses prayed for the people. And the LORD said unto Moses: 'Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole; and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he seeth it, shall live.' And Moses made a serpent of brass, and set it upon the pole; and if a serpent had bitten any man, when he looked unto the serpent of brass, he lived.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Numbers 21:7-9 (public domain).
passages.zh: 百姓到摩西那裏，說：「我們怨讟耶和華和你，有罪了；求你禱告耶和華，叫這些蛇離開我們。」於是摩西為百姓禱告。耶和華對摩西說：「你製造一條火蛇，掛在杆子上；凡被咬的，一望這蛇，就必得活。」摩西便製造一條銅蛇，掛在杆子上；凡被蛇咬的，一望這銅蛇，就活了。

title.en: Balaam's Donkey Sees the Angel
title.zh: 巴蘭的驢看見天使

region.en: Road to Moab, plains of Moab
region.zh: 往摩押之路，摩押平原

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Numbers 22:21-41, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Balak's messengers hire Balaam son of Beor to curse Israel. God permits the journey but is 'sore displeased'; the angel stands in the way with drawn sword. The donkey sees — swerves, crushes Balaam's foot against a wall, and lies down — until it speaks with a man's voice: 'What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?' Then Balaam's eyes are opened and he falls on his face.
summary.zh: 巴勒的使者雇巴蘭咒以色列。神許其行卻「發怒」；使者持刀立於路上。驢看見——偏行，擠傷巴蘭腳於牆，臥地不起——直至開口如人言：「我向你行了什麼，你竟打我這三次？」巴蘭眼乃開，俯伏在地。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The talking animal motif parallels cross-tradition seer-hindrance tales.

passages.text: Then the LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and she said unto Balaam: 'What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?' And Balaam said unto the ass: 'Because thou hast mocked me; I would there were a sword in my hand, for now I had killed thee.' And the ass said unto Balaam: 'Am not I thine ass, upon which thou hast ridden all thy life long unto this day? was I ever wont to do so unto thee?' And he said: 'Nay.' Then the LORD opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and he bowed his head, and fell on his face.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Numbers 22:28-31 (public domain).
passages.zh: 耶和華叫驢開口，對巴蘭說：「我向你做了甚麼，你竟打我這三次呢？」巴蘭對驢說：「因為你戲弄我；我恨不得手中有刀，現在就把你殺了。」驢對巴蘭說：「我不是你從小時直到今日所騎的驢嗎？我素常向你這樣行過嗎？」巴蘭說：「沒有。」當時，耶和華使巴蘭的眼目明亮，他就看見耶和華的使者站在路上，手裏有拔出來的刀；巴蘭便低頭，俯伏在地。

title.en: Balaam's Blessings: From the Camp Seen from the Heights
title.zh: 巴蘭的祝福：自高處望營

region.en: Heights of Moab over the plains
region.zh: 摩押高地，俯瞰平原

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Numbers 23-24, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: On seven altars with seven bulls and seven rams, Balaam can only bless: 'How shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed?' Three oracles praise Israel from Balak's vantage points, climaxing in the famous stream: 'How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, thy dwellings, O Israel' — the prayer with which synagogues open each morning — and a star-oracle of a future ruler.
summary.zh: 七壇七公牛七公羊之上，巴蘭唯能祝福：「神沒有咒詛的，我焉能咒詛？」三篇神諭自巴勒的高處讚以色列，至其名句：「雅各啊，你的帳棚何等華美！以色列啊，你的帳幕何其華麗！」——會堂每日晨禱之引詩——並有未來君王之星諭。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Numbers 24:17 star-prophecy read messianically in later tradition.

passages.text: And he took up his parable, and said: 'How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, thy dwellings, O Israel! As valleys stretched out, as gardens by a river-side, as tent-trees planted of the LORD, as cedars beside the waters.' Balak built altars at Bamoth-baal and Peor's height, sacrificing on each before Balaam spoke; each time the blessing came instead of the curse. Balaam protested: 'Have I now any power at all to speak anything? The word that God putteth in my mouth, that shall I speak.' The final oracle looks forward: 'there shall step forth a star out of Jacob, and a sceptre shall rise out of Israel'. Balak struck his hands together and sent the seer home in anger. Paraphrase of Numbers 23-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Numbers 24:5-6 (public domain). / Paraphrase of Numbers 23-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他便題起詩歌說：「雅各啊，你的帳棚何等華美！以色列啊，你的帳幕何其華麗！如接連的山谷，如河旁的園子，如耶和華所栽的沉香樹，如水邊的香柏木。」巴勒在巴末巴力和毗珥的高處築壇，每次在巴蘭開口前獻祭；每一次臨到的都是祝福，而不是咒詛。巴蘭申辯說：「我豈能擅自說甚麼呢？神將甚麼話傳給我，我就說甚麼。」最後的預言指向將來：「有星要出於雅各，有杖要興於以色列。」巴勒拍掌，怒氣沖沖地把這先見打發回家去了。此為《民數記》第二十三至二十四章（JPS 1917）的意譯，並非逐字照錄。

title.en: Phinehas's Zeal and the Covenant of Peace
title.zh: 非尼哈之熱心與平安之約

region.en: Camp at Shittim, plains of Moab
region.zh: 什亭營地，摩押平原

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE (Priestly); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Numbers 25:1-18, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Israel is seduced into Baal-peor's worship by the daughters of Moab. While a plague rages and the whole congregation weeps at the tent of meeting, Zimri brings a Midianite woman to his tent in the sight of Moses and the assembly. Phinehas takes a spear, follows them in, and thrusts both through — 'and the plague was stayed'. God grants him a 'covenant of peace' and an everlasting priesthood.
summary.zh: 以色列為摩押女子所誘事巴力毘珥。瘟疫肆行、會眾在幕前哭泣之際，心利攜米甸婦人入帳，在摩西與會眾眼前。非尼哈執矛，隨之入內，將二人刺透——「瘟疫就止住了」。神賜他「平安的約」與永遠的祭司職。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The episode has been invoked historically in ethically troubling ways; record states the text without endorsement.

passages.text: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned My wrath away from the children of Israel, in that he was very jealous for My sake among them... wherefore say: Behold, I give unto him My covenant of peace; and it shall be unto him, and to his seed after him, the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Numbers 25:11-13 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 祭司亞倫的孫子、以利亞撒的兒子非尼哈，使我向以色列人所發的怒消了，因他在他們中間，以我的忌邪為心……因此你要說：看哪，我將我平安的約賜給他；這約要給他和他的後裔，作為永遠當祭司職任的約。

title.en: Moses Dies in the Land of Moab: Viewed from Pisgah
title.zh: 摩西死於摩押：毘斯迦山上所望

region.en: Mount Nebo, Pisgah, Moab
region.zh: 尼波山，毘斯迦，摩押

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Deuteronomy 34, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: From Pisgah's top God shows Moses all the promised land — 'I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither' — and the greatest of the prophets dies there at a hundred and twenty, 'and there hath not arisen a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses'. He is buried 'in the valley... over against Beth-peor; and no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.'
summary.zh: 神自毘斯迦山頂將應許全地指示摩西——「我使你眼睛看見了，你卻不得過去那裡」——最偉大的先知死於該地，年一百二十，「以後以色列中再沒有興起先知像摩西的」。他葬於「摩押地……伯毘珥對面的谷中；只是到今日沒有人知道他的墳墓」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died; his eye was not dimmed, nor his natural force abated. And the children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days... And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Deuteronomy 34:7-10 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 摩西死的時候年一百二十歲；他的眼睛沒有昏花，精神也沒有衰敗。以色列人在摩押平原為摩西哀哭了三十日……此後以色列中再沒有興起先知像摩西的，他是耶和華面對面所認識的。

title.en: Hear, O Israel: The Shema and the Wanderer's Credo
title.zh: 以色列啊你要聽：示瑪與遊子信經

region.en: Plains of Moab (setting of Moses' discourse)
region.zh: 摩押平原（摩西講話之場景）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Deuteronomy 6:4-9; 26:5-10, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The core declaration of Judaism — 'Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one' — with the command to bind the words 'for a sign upon thy hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes' and write them on doorposts. Paired with the first-fruits credo recited by every Israelite farmer: 'A wandering Aramean was my father; and he went down into Egypt... and the LORD brought us forth out of Egypt with a mighty hand.'
summary.zh: 猶太教核心宣告——「以色列啊，你要聽！耶和華我們神是獨一的主」——並命將話語「為記號在你手上，為記號在你兩眼之間」，寫在門框上。配以每位以色列農夫初熟果子時所誦信經：「我祖原是一個將亡的亞蘭人，下到埃及寄居……耶和華就用大能的手領我們出了埃及。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Shema recited twice daily; tefillin and mezuzah are living ritual obligations derived from these verses.

passages.text: Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one. And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be upon thy heart... And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thy hand, and they shall be for frontlets between thine eyes. And thou shalt write them upon the door-posts of thy house, and upon thy gates.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Deuteronomy 6:4-9 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 以色列啊，你要聽：耶和華我們的神是獨一的耶和華。你要盡心、盡性、盡力愛耶和華你的神。我今日所吩咐你的這些話，都要記在心上……也要繫在手上為記號，戴在額上為經文。又要寫在你房屋的門框上，並你的城門上。

passages.text: And thou shalt come unto the priest... and say: 'I profess this day unto the LORD thy God, that I am come unto the land which the LORD swore unto our fathers for to give us.' And thou shalt say: 'A wandering Aramean was my father; and he went down into Egypt... and the LORD brought us forth out of Egypt with a mighty hand, and with an outstretched arm... and He hath brought us into this place, and hath given us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.' Paraphrase of Deuteronomy 26:3-9 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Deuteronomy 26:3-9 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你要到祭司那裡……說：『我今日向耶和華你的神明認，我已來到耶和華向我們列祖起誓應許賜給我們的地。』你要說：『我祖原是一個將亡的亞蘭人；他下到埃及去……耶和華用大能的手和伸出來的膀臂，將我們從埃及領出來……又領我們到了這地方，將這流奶與蜜之地賜給我們。』此為申命記二十六章三至九節之釋義（JPS 1917），非逐字引文。

title.en: Give Ear, O Heavens: The Song of Moses
title.zh: 諸天哪側耳：摩西之歌

region.en: Plains of Moab (setting of Moses' discourse)
region.zh: 摩押平原（摩西講話之場景）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Deuteronomy 32:1-43, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Israel's deathbed national poem: heaven and earth summoned as witnesses; the Rock, 'His work is perfect'; the eagle stirring her nest; Israel grown fat and forsaking the Rock of its salvation; the appointed wrath and the compassion at the end — 'I kill, and I make alive'. 'And Moses spoke in the ears of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song.'
summary.zh: 以色列臨終國詩：召天地為證；磐石，「他的作為完全」；攪動巢窩的鷹；以色列肥壯而離棄救他的磐石；命定的震怒與末後的憐憫——「我使人死，我使人活」。「摩西將這一篇歌的話都說與以色列全會眾聽。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Deut 32 is read in the annual Torah cycle (Ha'azinu).

passages.text: Give ear, O ye heavens, and I will speak; and let the earth hear the words of my mouth. My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew; as the small rain upon the tender herb, and as the showers upon the grass. For I will proclaim the name of the LORD; ascribe ye greatness unto our God. The Rock, His work is perfect; for all His ways are justice; a God of faithfulness and without iniquity, just and right is He.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Deuteronomy 32:1-4 (public domain).
passages.zh: 諸天哪，側耳，我要說話；願地也聽我口中的言語。我的教訓要淋漓如雨，我的言語要滴落如露，如細雨降在嫩草上，如甘霖降在菜蔬中。我要宣告耶和華的名；你們要將大德歸與我們的神。祂是磐石，祂的作為完全；祂所行的無不公平；是誠實無偽的神，又公義，又正直。

passages.text: Jeshurun waxed fat and kicked — 'then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation'. The poem foretells scattering and a remnant, then turns: 'I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal'. It closes with the nations called to praise His people — 'Sing aloud, O ye nations, of His people; for He doth avenge the blood of His servants'. Paraphrase of Deuteronomy 32:15-43 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Deuteronomy 32:15-43 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 耶書崙漸漸肥胖，踢跳——『便離棄造他的神，輕看救他的磐石』。這詩預言分散與餘民，繼而轉折：『我使人死，我使人活；我損傷，我也醫治』。末了呼召列國讚美祂的百姓——『你們外邦人，當與主的百姓一同歡呼；因祂要伸祂僕人流血的冤』。此為申命記三十二章十五至四十三節之釋義（JPS 1917），非逐字引文。

title.en: The Golden Calf and the Return of Musa
title.zh: 金牛犢與穆薩歸返

region.en: Camp beneath Mount Sinai (literal pin)
region.zh: 西奈山下營地（實際定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs 7:148-155, 20:83-98; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Suras 7:148-155 and 20:83-98

summary.en: In Moses' absence his people make a calf of their ornaments, a body with a lowing sound. 'This is your god and the god of Moses, whom he hath forgotten' — they said so though they had not seen him. Aaron warns them: 'Ye are only being proved thereby; your Lord is the God of Mercy, therefore follow me and obey my counsel.' When Moses returns in anger, he seizes his brother by the head: 'Why hast thou dishonoured them, and hast not waited for me?' Aaron answers that the people were near slaying him. The Samiri confesses — he took a handful of dust from the track of the messenger and threw it in, and thus his soul suggested it to him: 'Go thy way: it shall be for thee in this life to say, Touch me not; and there is a period for thee that shall not be delayed.'
summary.zh: 穆薩離開期間，眾人以飾物鑄成牛犢，有哞哞之聲。『這是你們的神，穆薩的神，他忘了它。』亞倫勸誡：『這不過是考驗；你們的主確是至慈的主。』穆薩歸返盛怒，揪住兄長的頭。撒米里認罪——他取使者足跡上的一把土投入，我靈如此教唆我。『你去吧，你今生只可說『莫觸我』，你的結局已定，不得延緩。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And after his departure the people of Moses made a calf of their ornaments, a body which lowed. Did they not see that it could not speak to them, nor guide them to any way? They took it for worship and did wrong. And when they had repented, and saw that they had erred, they said, 'Unless our Lord have mercy on us and forgive us, we shall surely be of the lost.' And when Moses returned to his people full of wrath and indignation, he said, 'Evil is it that ye have done in my absence after my departure: have ye anticipated your Lord's commandment?' And he threw down the tablets, and seized his brother by the head and dragged him to him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:148-150 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 摩西離去之後，他的族人用首飾鑄造了一頭牛犢，是一個能發出叫聲的軀體。他們難道沒有看見它不能對他們說話，也不能指引他們任何道路嗎？他們把它當作神來崇拜，因而做了錯事。當他們悔悟，並看出自己確已迷誤時，他們說：『若我們的主不憐憫我們、不赦宥我們，我們必定成為虧折的人。』當摩西滿懷憤怒與憂傷回到他的族人那裡時，他說：『你們在我離去之後所做的，真是惡劣：你們竟要搶先於你們主的命令嗎？』於是他摔下法版，抓住他兄弟的頭，把他拖向自己。

passages.text: And when Moses said to Aaron, 'O my brother, why hast thou dishonoured them, and hast not followed me? Hast thou disobeyed my command?' Aaron said, 'O son of my mother, lay not hold on me by the beard nor by the head, for I feared lest thou shouldst say, Thou hast caused division among the children of Israel, and hast not regarded my word.' And the Samiri said, 'I saw what they saw not: therefore I took a handful of dust from the track of the messenger, and cast it in: and thus my soul suggested it to me.' Moses said, 'Get thee gone! thy portion in this life shall be to say, Touch me not; and for thee is a period which shall not be delayed: and look at thy god to which thou hast continued so devoted: we will burn it and scatter its ashes in the sea.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 20:94-97 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當穆薩對哈倫說：「我的兄長啊，你為何羞辱了他們，不追隨我呢？你違背了我的命令嗎？」哈倫說：「我母親的兒子啊，你不要揪我的鬍鬚，也不要揪我的頭，我確怕你說：『你在以色列的子孫中製造了分裂，沒有顧及我的話。』」撒米里說：「我看見了他們所未見的：我從使者的蹤跡中取了一把塵土，把它投了進去：我的靈魂如此向我建議。」穆薩說：「你走吧！你在今世的份額就是說：『不要碰我』；你還有一個期限，那是不可延遲的：你看你所一直虔誠事奉的神吧：我們必將它焚燒，把它的灰燼撒在海裡。」

passages.text: And when the anger of Moses was appeased, he took up the tables: and in the writing of them was guidance and mercy to those who fear their Lord. And Moses chose out of his people seventy men to come to an appointed time with Us... and the followers of Moses said, 'We will not believe thee until we see God plainly.' And a thunderbolt took them as they looked on. Then he raised him up after that, and Moses prostrated himself and said, 'I turn to thee in repentance, and I am the first of believers.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:154-155 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當穆薩的怒氣平息之後，他拿起了法版：法版的書寫中有引導和慈憫，賜予那些敬畏他們的主的人。穆薩從他的族人中揀選了七十人，來赴與我們所定的約期……穆薩的追隨者說：「我們絕不相信你，直到我們明明地看見真主。」當他們觀看的時候，雷電擊中了他們。此後他使他甦醒過來，穆薩俯伏叩拜說：「我向你悔罪，我是首先歸信的人。」

title.en: Forty Nights at Sinai: The Tablets and the Word
title.zh: 西奈四十夜：法版與言語

region.en: Mount Sinai / Jabal Musa (literal pin)
region.zh: 西奈山／穆薩山（實際定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs 7:142-147, 20:114; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 7:142-147

summary.en: We appointed thirty nights for Moses, and completed them with ten, so that the term of his Lord was fulfilled — forty nights. 'And Moses said to Aaron his brother, Take my place among my people, and act rightly, and follow not the way of the mischief-makers.' He came at the appointed time and his Lord spoke with him: 'O my Lord, show me thyself, that I may look upon thee' — 'Thou shalt not see me: but look upon the mountain; if it stand firm in its place, then shalt thou see me.' And when his Lord appeared on the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Moses fell down in a swoon.
summary.zh: 主為穆薩定三十夜，加以十夜成全其主之期——四十夜。穆薩囑亞倫代行善事。主期已至，主與之言語。穆薩求見主：『你必不能見我；但看那座山，若山堅立原處，你便得見。』主顯現於山時，山化為塵，穆薩昏倒於地。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the theophany at Sinai; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And We appointed thirty nights for Moses, and completed them with ten; and the term of his Lord was fulfilled, forty nights. And Moses said to Aaron his brother, 'Take my place among my people, and act rightly, and follow not the way of the mischief-makers.' And when Moses came at Our appointed time, and his Lord spoke with him, he said, 'O my Lord, show me thyself, that I may look upon thee.' He said, 'Thou shalt not see me: but look upon the mountain; if it stand firm in its place, then shalt thou see me.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:142-143 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我們為穆薩規定了三十夜，又以十夜補足它；他主的期限就滿了，共四十夜。穆薩對他的兄弟哈倫說：「你在我族人中代替我，你要行正道，不要追隨作惡者的道路。」當穆薩在我們所定的時間來到，他的主與他說話時，他說：「我的主啊，求你顯示你自己，讓我看看你。」他說：「你不能看見我：但你看那座山；如果它穩立於原位，那麼你就能看見我。」

passages.text: And when his Lord appeared on the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Moses fell down in a swoon. And when he came to himself he said, 'Glory to Thee! I turn to Thee in repentance, and I am the first of believers.' And God said, 'O Moses, I have chosen thee above mankind by My messages and by My speaking to thee: take what I have given thee, and be of the thankful.' And We ordained for him in the tables admonition concerning all things, and clear directions of all things; 'Take them with strength, and command thy people to observe the best of them... And I will show thee the dwelling of the wicked.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:143-145 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他的主在山上的時候，祂使山崩碎成塵，穆薩昏倒過去。當他甦醒過來時，他說：「讚美你！我向你悔罪，我是首先歸信的人。」真主說：「穆薩啊，我以我的使命和我對你的說話，使你超越世人：你拿我所賜給你的，要做感恩的人。」我們在法版中為他規定了關於萬事的勸誡，和關於萬事的明確指示；「你要用力拿住它們，並命令你的族人遵守其中最好的……我將指示你惡人的居所。」

passages.text: And We wrote for him upon the tables an admonition concerning all things, and an explanation of all things. We said, 'Take them with strength, and command thy people to observe the best of them.' And I will show thee the abode of the wicked.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:145 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我們在法版上為他寫下了關於萬事的勸誡，和關於萬事的解釋。我們說：「你要用力拿住它們，並命令你的族人遵守其中最好的。」我將指示你惡人的居所。

title.en: Talut's Army and the Slingstone of Dawud
title.zh: 塔魯特之軍與達五德的石彈

region.en: Valley of Tannin, Judah (traditional site of the duel; symbolic pin)
region.zh: 猶地亞坦寧谷（傳統對決地；象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-Baqarah 2:246-251; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 2:246-251

summary.en: The chiefs of Israel demand a king: 'Why should we not fight for the path of God when we are driven forth from our dwellings and our children?' Their prophet answers that God has set up Talut, 'the wealthy among you in wealth and person.' They protest his wealth; the sign of the Ark is given — tranquillity from the Lord, the relics of the house of Moses and Aaron borne by angels. Talut tests them at the river: those who drink are not of him, save those who take a handful. Dawud, a youth, slays Jalut (Goliath); God gives him the kingdom and wisdom, and teaches him what He wills.
summary.zh: 以色列首領求王：『主道臨頭，為何不戰？』先知答：主已立塔魯特為王。眾以其富有而不滿；約櫃為兆——主的安寧與穆薩亞倫家眷的遺物，由天使抬來。塔魯特於河邊考驗軍隊；飲者非其人，僅手掬者除外。少年達五德擊斃 Jalut（歌利亞）；主賜其國與智慧。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation; the Qur'anic account of Talut/Dawud differs in details from 1 Samuel.

passages.text: And did you not know the chiefs of the children of Israel, after Moses, when they said to a prophet of theirs, 'Raise up for us a king, and we will fight for the cause of God'? He said, 'May it not be that when fighting is ordained for you, ye will not fight?' They said, 'And why should we not fight for the cause of God, since we are driven forth from our dwellings and our children?' And when fighting was commanded for them they turned back, except a few of them. And God knoweth the doers of wrong.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 2:246 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你豈不知道穆薩之後以色列的子孫中的首領們嗎？當時他們對他們的一位先知說：「為我們立一個王，我們就為真主的事業而戰。」他說：「或許當戰鬥被規定給你們的時候，你們不會戰鬥吧？」他們說：「我們為何不為真主的事業而戰呢？我們已被逐出家園，離開我們的子女。」當戰鬥被命令給他們的時候，他們就轉身退卻了，只有他們中的少數人例外。真主知道作惡的人。

passages.text: And their prophet said to them, 'God hath raised Talut to be your king.' They said, 'How shall he be king over us? We have a better right to kingship than he, and he is not gifted with abundance of wealth.' He said, 'God hath chosen him before you, and hath increased him largely in knowledge and person: and God bestoweth His kingdom on whom He pleaseth; and God is ample in bounty, and He knoweth all.' And their prophet said to them, 'Now shall the sign of his kingdom be, that a coffer shall come unto you in which is tranquillity from your Lord, and the relics left by the family of Moses and the family of Aaron, borne by the angels: herein shall be a sign to you if ye are believers.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 2:247-248 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們的先知對他們說：『真主已興起塔魯特作你們的王。』他們說：『他怎能統治我們呢？我們比他更有資格為王，他也沒有豐富的財富。』他說：『真主已在你們之中揀選了他，並大大增進了他的學識與體魄；真主以其國度賜予祂所意欲的人；真主是寬恩的，是全知的。』他們的先知又對他們說：『他的國度的徵象是：有一個約櫃將降臨你們，其中有從你們的主降下的安寧，並有穆薩的家族和哈倫的家族所遺留的遺物，由天使們抬著：如果你們是信士，此中確有給你們的徵象。』

passages.text: And when Talut had marched forth with his forces he said, 'God will prove you at the river: he who drinketh of it shall not be of me, but he who tasteth it not, he shall be of me.' And they drank thereof, except a few of them. And when he had crossed it, he and those who believed with him, they said, 'We have no power this day against Jalut and his forces.' But they who held that they should one day meet God said, 'How many a small band hath overcome a numerous host, by the help of God! for God is with the patient.' And when they went forth against Jalut and his forces they said, 'O our Lord, pour out constancy upon us, and make us firm of foot, and help us against the unbelievers.' And they put them to flight by the help of God: and David slew Jalut; and God gave him the kingdom, and wisdom, and taught him what He would.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 2:249-251 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當塔魯特率領他的軍隊出征時，他說：『真主將在河邊考驗你們：誰飲了河水，誰就不屬於我；誰不嘗那水，誰就屬於我。』他們都飲了那水，只有少數人例外。當他渡過了河，他和與他同信的人們說：『我們今日無力對抗賈魯特和他的軍隊。』但那些確信他們終有一日要與真主相會的人說：『多少微小的隊伍，憑著真主的援助，戰勝了眾多的軍隊！真主確是與堅忍者同在的。』當他們出去迎戰賈魯特和他的軍隊時，他們說：『我們的主啊！求祢傾注堅忍於我們，求祢使我們的腳步堅定，求祢援助我們對抗不信道的民眾。』他們憑著真主的援助使他們敗逃：達伍德殺死了賈魯特；真主賜予他國度和智慧，並教導他所意欲的。

title.en: The Two Litigants at Dawud's Door
title.zh: 達五德門前的兩個訴訟者

region.en: Jerusalem, court of David (literal pin)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷達五德宮廷（實際定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah Sad 38:21-26; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 38:21-26

summary.en: Has there come to thee the story of the two litigants who climbed the wall into the chamber? When they went in to Dawud and he feared them, they said, 'Fear not: we are two litigants — one of us hath wronged the other: judge between us with truth, and deviate not from the right, and guide us to the even way. This my brother hath ninety and nine sheep, and I have one; and he hath made me give up my own sheep, and hath prevailed against me in argument.' Dawud judges that he hath wronged — and sees that it is his own trial. He asks pardon of his Lord, falls down prostrate, and turns to Him.
summary.zh: 訴訟者二人攀牆入室的故事。二人入見達五德，他畏懼；他們說：『勿懼：我們是訴訟者——我倆之一欺負了另一個。這兄弟有九十九隻母羊，我只一隻，他卻要佔有我的，並以言辭勝我。』達五德斷其為欺——方知此乃自己的考驗。他求主赦宥，俯首叩拜，而悔悟歸主。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the parable-episode underlies tafsir discussions of David's affair with Bathsheba; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And has the story of the two disputants come to thee, when they mounted the wall of the upper chamber? When they went in to David and he was alarmed at them, they said, 'Fear not: we are two litigants; one of us hath wronged the other: judge thou between us with truth, and deviate not from what is right, and guide us to the even way. Verily this my brother hath ninety and nine sheep, and I have one sheep; and he hath said, Make it over to me, and hath pressed me hard in the matter.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 38:21-23 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那兩個爭訟者的故事曾傳到你嗎？當時他們越過樓閣的牆垣。當他們進去見達伍德，他因他們而驚恐，他們說：『不要害怕：我們是兩個爭訟者；我們中一人虧負了另一人：求你以真理在我們之間判決，不要偏離正道，並引導我們走上正路。我這兄弟確有九十九隻母羊，而我只有一隻母羊；他說：把它交給我吧，並在這件事上對我強詞奪理。』

passages.text: David said, 'He hath surely wronged thee in asking thine ewe to add to his own ewes: and many of those who share the same calling act unjustly among their fellows, save those who believe and work righteousness: and few are they! And David saw that we had made trial of him, and he asked pardon of his Lord, and fell down prostrate and repented.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 38:24 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 達伍德說：『他確實在要求你把你的母羊加在他的母羊上而虧負了你：許多同業的人確實在彼此之間行不義，唯有那些信道並行善的人例外：而這樣的人是很少的！』達伍德看出我們已考驗了他，他便向他的主求饒，俯伏在地，並且悔悟。

passages.text: So we forgave him this fault; and truly his lot with Us shall be blessed, and a happy resting-place. We said, 'O David! we have made thee a vicegerent on earth: judge therefore between men with truth, and follow not thy desire, for it will lead thee astray from the path of God: for they who go astray from the path of God shall be sorely punished, because they have forgotten the day of account.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 38:25-26 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是我們赦免了他這過失；他確在我們那裡享有恩澤，並有美好的歸宿。我們說：『達伍德啊！我們確已使你成為大地上的代治者：故你當以真理在人間判決，不要順從私慾，以免它使你偏離真主之道：偏離真主之道的人，將因忘卻清算之日而受嚴厲的刑罰。』

title.en: The Wind, the Brass, and the Termites of Sulayman's Death
title.zh: 風、熔銅與白蟻：蘇萊曼之死

region.en: Solomon's court at Jerusalem (literal pin)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷蘇萊曼宮廷（實際定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs Saba 34:12-14, Sad 38:34-40; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 34:12-14

summary.en: The wind is made subject to Solomon: its morning course a month's journey, its evening course a month's; a fountain of molten brass is made to flow at his word; the jinn build for him palaces, images, basins as large as reservoirs and cooking-pots firmly fixed. When We decreed that he should die, nothing told them of his death but the creeping thing of the earth that gnawed his staff; and when he fell down, the jinn saw plainly that had they known the Unseen, they would not have continued in the humiliating punishment. And he turned away from us displeased, and We tried him with an affliction.
summary.zh: 風受制於蘇萊曼：晨行一月之程，暮行一月之程；熔銅之泉因他而流；精靈為他建宮殿、雕像、大如水池的銅盆與固定的烹鍋。主命其死時，除土中爬蟲啃其杖外，無人知其死；他倒下，精靈方知——若知幽玄，必不居辱刑。他轉身棄主而不悅，主試之以災。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation; the death-by-termite legend comes from tafsir expansion.

passages.text: And We made the wind subject to Solomon; its morning course was a month's journey, and its evening course a month's journey: and We made a fountain of molten brass to flow for him; and of the jinn were some who wrought for him by his Lord's permission; and whoever of them swerved aside from Our command, him will We cause to taste of the burning flame. They made for him what he would, synagogues, and images, and basins as large as reservoirs, and cooking-pots firmly fixed.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 34:12-13 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我們使風服從蘇萊曼；它的晨行是一個月的路程，它的晚行是一個月的路程：我們又使熔銅的泉源為他流出；精靈中有奉他們的主的命令為他工作的；他們中誰偏離我們的命令，我們就使他嘗受烈火的刑罰。他們為他製造他所意欲的：禮拜堂、雕像、如水池般大的盆，以及固定的鍋爐。

passages.text: And when We had decreed that he should die, nothing informed them of his death, save the creeping thing of the earth which ate up his staff; and when he fell down, the jinn saw plainly that if they had known that which is hidden, they would not have remained in base and ignominious servitude. And he turned himself away from us displeased, and We tried him with affliction.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 34:14 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當我判定他死亡之時，除了那啃食他手杖的大地爬蟲之外，沒有任何事物向他們告知他的死訊；當他倒下時，精靈們才明白，倘若他們知曉那隱祕之事，他們便不會停留在卑賤而可恥的服侍之中。他滿懷不悅地轉身離我們而去，我們便以苦難考驗他。

passages.text: And we had already tried the man Solomon, and placed a body on his throne: then did he turn to Us in penitence. He said, 'O my Lord, pardon me, and give me a kingdom which may not be to anyone after me: for Thou art the liberal Bestower.' So We made the wind subject to him, that it ran softly at his bidding whithersoever he directed it; and the demons, every builder and diver, and others chained together. 'This is Our gift: give freely or withhold, as thou wilt, without rendering account.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 38:34-40 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我們確曾考驗過所羅門其人，並將一具軀體置於他的寶座之上：隨後他滿懷悔意地歸向我們。他說：『我的主啊，求你赦免我，並賜我一個在我之後任何人都不配擁有的國度：因為你是慷慨的賜予者。』於是我們使風聽命於他，那風隨他所指引的方向輕柔地吹拂；又使眾魔聽命於他，其中有每一個建築者和潛水者，還有其他被鎖鏈鎖在一起者。『這是我們的恩賜：你當慷慨施予或加以扣留，隨你意願，無須交代。』

title.en: The Hoopoe, the Ants, and the Throne of Sheba
title.zh: 戴勝鳥、螞蟻與示巴王后之座

region.en: Saba / Sheba and Jerusalem (symbolic pin between the two)
region.zh: 示巴與耶路撒冷之間（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-Naml 27:15-44; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 27:15-44

summary.en: We taught Solomon the language of birds. An army of birds is marshalled before him; the hoopoe brings news from Saba of a queen upon a magnificent throne and a sun-worshipping people. Solomon sends a letter: 'In the name of the merciful God — make not yourselves proud against me, but come to me in submission.' The queen sends a gift; Solomon refuses it — 'what God hath given me is better than what he hath given you.' The throne is brought — 'make it like hers before she comes' — and it is done in a twinkling. She enters the palace of glass: 'My Lord, I have been of the unjust: I submit with Solomon to the Lord of all creatures.'
summary.zh: 主教蘇萊曼通鳥語。群鳥集於其前；戴勝鳥自示巴報訊：有一女王，寶座壯麗，民拜太陽。蘇萊曼致書：『奉至仁主之名——勿傲慢，當順服而來。』女王饋禮；蘇萊曼拒之——『主所賜我者勝於賜你者。』寶座被運——『在她來前使其相似』——瞬息即成。她入玻璃宮：『我的主，我確是不義的：我與蘇萊曼一同順服萬物之主。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation; the Bilqis episode is central to Arabic qisas lore.

passages.text: And We gave unto David and Solomon knowledge of the subtle things, and they both said, 'Praise be to God who hath made us excel many of his believing servants!' And Solomon was David's heir; and he said, 'O men, we have been taught the speech of birds, and have had everything given to us: this is the manifest excellence.' And there were marshalled before Solomon his armies of the jinn and men and birds; and they were formed into bands.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 27:15-17 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我們曾賜予大衛和所羅門知曉幽微之事的知識，他們二人說：『讚美真主，他使我們超越了許多信道的僕人！』所羅門是大衛的繼承者；他說：『眾人啊，我們已被教會鳥的語言，並被賜予了一切事物：這確是明顯的優越。』所羅門的軍隊——精靈、人類和鳥類——被列陣於他面前；他們被編排成隊列。

passages.text: Until they came to the valley of the ants: an ant said, 'O ants, enter ye into your abodes, lest Solomon and his armies crush you and perceive it not.' And Solomon smiled at her words. And he said, 'O my Lord, quicken me that I may be thankful for Thy favours... and make me one of thy righteous servants.' And he observed among the birds, and said, 'Why see I not the lapwing? Is he absent? I will surely punish him with a severe punishment, or I will slay him — unless he bring me a just excuse.' And he tarried not long, and said, 'I have found out that which thou knowest not; and I come to thee from Saba with sure tidings. I found a woman ruling over them, provided with everything, and having a magnificent throne: and I found her and her people adoring the sun instead of God, and Satan hath made their works fair seeming to them.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 27:18-24 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 直到他們來到螞蟻的谷地：一隻螞蟻說：『螞蟻們啊，快進入你們的居所，免得所羅門和他的軍隊將你們碾碎，而他們卻渾然不覺。』所羅門因她的話而微笑。他說：『我的主啊，求你激勵我，使我感謝你的恩惠……並使我成為你正直僕人中的一員。』他察看鳥群，說道：『為何我不見那戴勝鳥？它缺席了嗎？我必以嚴厲的懲罰懲治它，或者我必殺死它——除非它給我帶來一個正當的理由。』它並未久留，便說道：『我已發現你所不知之事；我從賽伯邑來到你這裡，帶著確鑿的消息。我發現一個女人統治著他們，她被賜予了一切，並擁有一座宏偉的寶座：我發現她和她的族人崇拜太陽而非真主，撒旦已使他們的行為在他們眼中顯得美好。』

passages.text: And Solomon said, 'I will send to them a present, and will wait to see what the messengers shall bring back.' And when the messenger came to her she said, 'If it be that ye have gifts to offer, I will not accept them... Make it like her throne before she come to me in submission.' And when she came, it was said to her, 'Is this thy throne?' She said, 'As though it were the same.' And she was told, 'Enter the palace'; and when she saw it she thought it a sheet of water, and bared her legs. Then she said, 'O Solomon, I have done wrong to myself, and I submit with Solomon to God the Lord of all creatures.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 27:35-44 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 所羅門說：『我將送給他們一份禮物，並等待看看使者們會帶回什麼。』當使者來到她那裡時，她說：『倘若你們有禮物要奉獻，我不會接受它們……在她前來歸順我之前，使她的寶座變得與之相似。』當她來到時，有人對她說：『這是你的寶座嗎？』她說：『彷彿就是同一個。』有人對她說：『進入宮殿吧』；當她看見它時，她以為那是一片水，便露出了她的雙腿。隨後她說：『所羅門啊，我確已虧負了自己，我與所羅門一同歸順真主，萬物的主宰。』

title.en: Dhul-Qarnayn: West, East, and the Wall of Gog and Magog
title.zh: 左勒蓋爾奈英：西行、東行與雅朱者牆

region.en: Setting and rising places of the sun, Caucasus pass (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 日沉日升之地與高加索隘口（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-Kahf 18:83-98; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 18:83-98

summary.en: They will ask thee about Dhul-Qarnayn ('the two-horned'). He journeyed westward to where the sun sets, and found it set in a spring of black mud; there he found a people: 'God,' he says, 'will punish or reward; we only speak justly.' Then the rising place of the sun, upon a people exposed to the sun's heat. Then he journeyed between two mountains, where he found a people who could hardly understand speech: 'Build thee a rampart between us and Gog and Magog.' He asks for labour — blocks of iron poured over with molten copper; and he says: 'This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord shall come, He shall reduce it to dust; for the promise of my Lord is true.'
summary.zh: 他們問左勒蓋爾奈英（雙角者）。他西行至日落處，見其落入黑泥之泉；遇一民：『主或懲或賞；我只秉公而言。』後至日升處，遇無遮蔽於日光之民。再至兩山之間，遇幾不解語之民：『在雅朱者與馬朱者之間為我築一障。』他求勞力——鐵塊熔銅灌注；『此乃我主的恩慈；我主之期一至，他必使之化為塵土。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; identifications with Alexander the Great are a matter of tafsir debate; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And they will ask thee concerning Dhul-Karnain. Answer, 'I will rehearse to you an account of him.' We made him mighty in the earth, and endowed him with a means to accomplish everything. And he journeyed on a certain journey until he came to the setting place of the sun, and found it to set in a muddy black spring, and found a people near it; and We said, 'O Dhul-Karnain, either chastise this people, or use thy generous treatment towards them.' He said, 'Whoever committeth evil shall be punished, and when he shall be taken away to his Lord, He shall punish him with a punishment which shall not be repeated; but as for him who believeth and worketh righteousness, he shall receive the best of rewards.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 18:83-88 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們將問你關於左勒蓋爾奈英的事。你回答：『我將向你們敘述關於他的一段事蹟。』我們曾使他在大地上擁有權勢，並賜予他成就一切事物的途徑。他踏上了一段旅程，直到他來到太陽的落處，發現它落在一個泥濘的黑色泉眼中，並在附近發現一群人；我們說：『左勒蓋爾奈英啊，你要麼懲治這群人，要麼以你的寬厚對待他們。』他說：『凡作惡者必受懲罰，當他被帶到他的主那裡時，祂將以不再重複的懲罰懲治他；至於信道且行善者，他將獲得最好的報酬。』

passages.text: And he pursued his journey another way. And when he came to the rising-place of the sun, he found it to rise on a people for whom We had provided no shelter from it. And he journeyed on a third journey, till he came between two mountains, and found a people who could hardly understand speech. They said, 'O Dhul-Karnain, verily Gog and Magog shall waste this land: shall we therefore pay thee tribute, on condition that thou build a rampart between us and them?' He said, 'Better than your tribute is the might wherewith my Lord hath strengthened me: help me therefore with strength, and I will set a rampart between you and them.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 18:89-95 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他又循另一條道路前行。當他來到日落之處，發現太陽落在一群人身上，我們未曾為他們提供遮擋。他又踏上第三次旅程，直到他來到兩山之間，發現一群人幾乎聽不懂言語。他們說：『左勒蓋爾奈英啊，雅朱者和馬朱者確實在這個地方作惡，我們可否向你繳納貢賦，條件是你在我們與他們之間築一道屏障？』他說：『我的主所賜予我的力量，比你們的貢賦更好；所以請你們以人力幫助我，我就在你們與他們之間築一道屏障。』

passages.text: Bring me iron in abundance; and when they had filled up the space between the two sides of the mountain, he said, 'Blow with your bellows'; and when he had made it red like fire he said, 'Bring me molten brass that I may pour over it.' And they were not able to scale it, nor could they dig through it. And he said, 'This is a mercy from my Lord: but when the promise of my Lord cometh, He shall make it dust; for the promise of my Lord is sure.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 18:96-98 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 給我拿大量鐵來；當他們填滿了兩山之間的空隙，他說：『用你們的風箱吹吧』；當他使它變得像火一樣紅時，他說：『給我拿熔化的銅來，讓我澆在上面。』他們既無法攀越它，也無法挖穿它。他說：『這是來自我的主的慈恩；但當我的主的應許到來時，祂將使它化為塵土；因為我的主的應許是真實的。』

title.en: The Sleepers of the Cave and Their Dog
title.zh: 山洞的沉睡者與其犬

region.en: Cave site above Ephesus / Jordan (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 以弗所／約旦洞穴（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-Kahf 18:9-26; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 18:9-26

summary.en: The youths who fled to the cave, 'O our Lord, grant us mercy from Thee, and prepare for us our affair aright'; and We drew a veil over their ears for years in the cave. They wake in confusion: 'How long have ye tarried here? — a day, or part of a day.' The number is known to God: 'God knoweth best how long they tarried: His are the secrets of the heavens and the earth.' The sun rises and declines on the right side and the left; the dog stretcheth out its paws in the opening. Say, 'God is best aware how long they tarried: His are the secrets of the heavens and the earth; He is the Seeing, the Hearing!'
summary.zh: 避居山洞的少年們祈禱：『主啊，賜我們恩慈，使我們的事務得正。』主以數年遮蔽其耳於洞中。他們醒來問：『我們住了多久？——一日或半日。』主知其數：『你們的主最知道他們所留的時期。』太陽在洞的右邊左邊升降；犬張爪於洞口。『主最知其時期；諸天與地的秘密屬於祂。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the Seven Sleepers legend shared with Christianity is reworked in the Qur'an; public-domain translation.

passages.text: Now have We set forth to thee a parable of the men who were to be saved? They said, 'Why doth a messenger preach to us?' We said to those who disbelieved them, 'They have perished.' And the men said, 'Go to the cave: your Lord will pour out His mercy upon you, and prepare for you a provision for your journey.' And We drew a veil over their ears, for a number of years, in the cave, and We wakened them again: and We said, 'How long have ye tarried here?' They said, 'A day, or part of a day.' They said, 'Your Lord knoweth best how long ye have tarried: now send one of you with this your coin into the city; and let him find out who therein hath purest food, and let him bring you provision of it; and let him be courteous, and let him not discover you to anyone.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 18:9-19 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我們豈不曾向你敘述那些得救之人的譬喻嗎？他們說：『為何有使者向我們傳道？』我們對那些不信他們的人說：『他們已經滅亡了。』那些人說：『到山洞裡去吧：你們的主將向你們傾注祂的慈恩，並為你們的旅程預備供給。』我們在山洞中蒙住他們的耳朵若干年，然後又喚醒他們：我們說：『你們在這裡逗留了多久？』他們說：『一天，或不到一天。』他們說：『你們的主最知道你們逗留了多久：現在派你們中的一人帶著這些錢幣進城去；讓他查明城中誰的食物最潔淨，讓他帶些供給你們；讓他舉止謙和，不要向任何人洩露你們。』

passages.text: And thou mightest have seen the sun when it arose decline to the right of their cave, and when it went down leave them on the left, while they were in its spacious chamber: this is one of the signs of God. And thou mightest have seen the dog that kept them stretching out its paws in the opening: and hadst thou come upon them thou wouldest surely have turned thy back on them in flight, and have been filled with fear of them. And thus did We rouse them that they might question one another. One of them said, 'How long have ye tarried here?' They said, 'We have tarried a day, or part of a day.' They said, 'Your Lord knoweth best how long ye have tarried: His are the secrets of the heavens and of the earth: He is the Seeing One, the Hearer!'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 18:17-19 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你可能看見太陽升起時偏離他們的洞穴向右，落下時則將他們留在左邊，而他們正處於洞穴的寬敞處：這是真主的跡象之一。你可能看見那守護他們的狗在洞口伸出雙爪：倘若你遇見他們，你必定會轉身逃走，並對他們充滿恐懼。我們就這樣喚醒他們，使他們互相詢問。其中一人說：『你們在這裡逗留了多久？』他們說：『我們逗留了一天，或不到一天。』他們說：『你們的主最知道你們逗留了多久：諸天與大地的奧秘都屬於祂：祂是全視的、全聽的！』

passages.text: They will dispute concerning them among themselves: and they will say, 'Three: and their dog was the fourth.' And others will say, 'Five: and their dog the sixth.' And some will say, 'Seven: and their dog the eighth.' Say, 'My Lord best knoweth the number of them: none but a few shall know them.' Therefore cavil not about them, but ask directions of none in the matter; and say not of anyone of them, 'I will surely place him in Paradise.' And they said, 'We have built a place of worship over them.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 18:22-23 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們將為他們的事互相爭論：有人將說：『三個，他們的狗是第四個。』另有人將說：『五個，他們的狗是第六個。』還有人將說：『七個，他們的狗是第八個。』你說：『我的主最知道他們的數目：只有少數人知道他們。』所以不要為他們爭辯，也不要為此事向任何人請教；不要對他們中的任何人說：『我必將他安置在樂園裡。』他們說：『我們在他們上面建造了一座禮拜場所。』

title.en: Luqman's Counsels to His Son
title.zh: 魯格曼對其子之訓誡

region.en: Land of wisdom-teaching, Nubia/Arabia (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 智慧傳授之地，努比亞／阿拉伯（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah Luqman 31:12-19; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 31:12-19

summary.en: We bestowed wisdom on Luqman, saying, 'Give thanks to God'; for whoever giveth thanks, giveth thanks for his own soul. 'O my son, join not gods with God, for idolatry is a great sin.'
