'O my son, though the good works thou hast done were but the grain of a mustard-seed, and hid in a rock, or in the heavens, or in the earth, God will bring them to light: for God is sagacious and aware. Be constant in prayer, and enjoin the right, and forbid the wrong, and endure patiently whatever befall thee... And be not sparing in walking the earth, nor arrogant: for God loveth not any arrogant, boasting one. Be moderate in thy carriage, and subdue thy voice; for the most disagreeable of voices is the braying of the ass.'
summary.zh: 主授魯格曼智慧：『當感謝真主。』——『子啊，勿以物配主；配主確是大罪。』『子啊，你的善行縱如芥子之微，藏於磐石之中、天中地中，主必顯現之。』『當守拜功，勸善戒惡，堅忍一切變故……行路勿驕傲；主不喜傲慢誇口者。行走當適中，聲音當低沉；最難聽的聲音，確是驢的叫聲。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; Luqman is a wisdom-figure of qisas lore; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And we gave unto Luqman wisdom: 'Give thanks unto God; for whoever giveth thanks, giveth thanks for the good of his own soul; and whoever disbelieveth... verily God is self-sufficient and to be praised.' And when Luqman said to his son, as he admonished him, 'O my son, join not gods with God, for idolatry is a great sin.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 31:12-13 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我們賜予魯格曼智慧：『你要感謝真主；因為誰感謝，感謝是為了他自己靈魂的好處；誰不信……真主確是自足的，確是受讚頌的。』當魯格曼告誡他的兒子時說：『我的兒子啊，不要以物配主，因為偶像崇拜確是大罪。』

passages.text: And we have enjoined man to be kind to his parents: but if they endeavour to persuade thee to join with Me that of which thou hast no knowledge, obey them not. And have kindness towards them in the world's life; but follow Me in the way that is right. To Me shall ye return: and I will declare to you what ye have done. And Luqman said, 'O my son, though the good works thou hast done were but the grain of a mustard-seed, and hid in a rock, or in the heavens, or in the earth, God will bring them to light: for God is sagacious and aware of all things.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 31:14-16 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我曾囑咐世人要善待父母；但若他們竭力勸你以你所不知之物與我並列，你不可順從他們。在今世生活中，你當善待他們；但你要遵循正道跟隨我。你們終將歸返於我，我必將你們的所作所為告訴你們。魯格曼說：『我的兒子啊，即使你所行的善功僅如一粒芥菜種，藏在岩石中，或在天上，或在地下，真主必將它顯露出來：因為真主是明察的，洞悉萬物。』

passages.text: O my son, be constant in prayer, and enjoin that which is right, and forbid that which is wrong, and endure patiently whatever befalleth thee: for this is a bounden duty. And be not sparing in thy discourse, nor arrogant: for God loveth not any one who is proud, boaster. And be moderate in thy carriage, and subdue thy voice; for the most disagreeable of voices is that of the ass.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 31:17-19 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我的兒子啊，你要謹守禮拜，勸人行善，止人作惡，並要耐心忍受所遭遇的一切：這確是應盡的義務。你說話不可吝嗇，也不可傲慢：因為真主不喜愛任何驕傲自誇之人。你行走時要適度，並要壓低你的聲音；因為最難聽的聲音確是驢的叫聲。

title.en: Rahab Hides the Spies and Hangs the Scarlet Cord
title.zh: 喇哈藏探子懸朱紅線繩

region.en: Jericho, house in the city wall
region.zh: 耶利哥，城牆中的房屋

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Joshua 2, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Two spies lodge in the house of Rahab the harlot on Jericho's wall; the king's men come for them, and she hides them under the flax on the roof. She confesses that the land's hearts have melted before Israel's God, and bargains for her family's lives; the spies seal it with a scarlet thread in her window. She becomes an ancestress in the royal line.
summary.zh: 二探子宿於耶利哥城牆上妓女喇哈之家；王之人來捉，她將他們藏於屋頂麻稓中。她自承此地人心因以色列的神消化，為全家族的性命討價；探子以朱紅線繩繫於窗上為記。她後列入王統譜系。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Rahab appears in Matthew's genealogy; counted among converts in rabbinic tradition.

passages.text: And she said unto the men: 'I know that the LORD hath given you the land... for we have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red Sea for you, when ye came out of Egypt... for the LORD your God, He is God in heaven above, and on earth beneath.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Joshua 2:9-11 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 她對那二人說：『我知道耶和華已將這地賜給你們……因為我們聽見耶和華你們出埃及的時候，為你們使紅海的水乾了……因為耶和華你們的神，祂是上天下地的神。』

passages.text: She let them down by a cord through the window, 'for her house was in the side of the wall, and she dwelt upon the wall', and received the oath: 'Behold, when we come into the land, thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window'. As long as her family stayed within the house, they would be safe; the army would blameless hold the covenant. Paraphrase of Joshua 2:15-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Joshua 2:15-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 她用繩子從窗戶把他們縋下去，『因她的房子在城牆邊上，她住在城牆上』，並接受了誓言：『看哪，我們來到這地的時候，你要把這條朱紅線繩繫在窗戶上。』只要她的家人留在屋內，他們便得安全；軍隊必無可指責地守此約定。約書亞記二章十五至二十一節（JPS 1917）之釋義；非逐字引文。

title.en: Jericho's Walls Fall at the Shofar Blast
title.zh: 角聲中耶利哥城牆倒塌

region.en: Jericho, Jordan valley
region.zh: 耶利哥，約旦河谷

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Joshua 6, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The armed men circle the city once a day for six days, priests blowing rams' horns before the ark, the people silent. On the seventh day they circle seven times; 'when the priests blew with the trumpet... the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat.' Rahab's house alone stands spared, and the city is put under the ban (herem).
summary.zh: 持械者一日繞城一次，共六日，祭司抬約櫃吹羊角，百姓靜默。第七日繞城七次；「祭司吹角的時候……百姓大聲呼喊，城牆就塌陷」。唯喇哈之屋蒙存，全城被滅歸於「當滅之物」（禁令）。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The herem passages are discussed critically in modern scholarship; record states the text.

passages.text: And it came to pass at the seventh time, when the priests blew with the horns, Joshua said unto the people: 'Shout; for the LORD hath given you the city.' ... So the people shouted, and they blew with the horns; and it came to pass, when the people heard the sound of the horn, that the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat, whereupon the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Joshua 6:16, 20 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 到了第七次，祭司吹角的時候，約書亞對百姓說：『呼喊吧；因為耶和華已將這城賜給你們了。』……於是百姓呼喊，祭司也吹角；百姓聽見角聲的時候，便大聲呼喊，城牆就塌陷了，於是百姓上去進城，各人直往前行，他們就取了那城。

title.en: Achan's Loot and the Valley of Trouble
title.zh: 亞干的贓物與亞割谷

region.en: Ai and the valley of Achor, land of Canaan
region.zh: 艾城與亞割谷，迦南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Joshua 7, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Israel is routed at Ai because one man kept back spoils under the ban. The tribes pass before the LORD tribe by tribe until Achan of Judah is singled out; he confesses to a Babylonish garment, silver, and gold buried in his tent. He and his household are stoned and burned in the valley of Achor — 'the valley of trouble' — named as a memorial of transgression under holy war law.
summary.zh: 以色列在艾城潰敗，因一人私藏當滅之物。支派逐一經過，亞干屬猶大被指出；他供認藏巴比倫衣服、銀金於帳內。他與全家被石擊火焚於亞割谷——「連累之谷」——為聖戰法下違命之記念。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Joshua said unto Achan: 'My son, give, I pray thee, glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and make confession unto Him; and tell me now what thou hast done; hide it not from me.' And Achan answered Joshua, and said: 'Of a truth I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel... When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish mantle, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Joshua 7:19-21 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 約書亞對亞干說：『我兒，我勸你將榮耀歸給耶和華以色列的神，向祂認罪；現在告訴我你作了什麼事，不要向我隱瞞。』亞干回答約書亞說：『我實在得罪了耶和華以色列的神……我在所奪的財物中，看見一件美好的巴比倫外袍、二百舍客勒銀子、一條重五十舍客勒的金子，我就貪愛這些，便拿去了。』

title.en: The Gibeonites' Mouldy Bread Trick
title.zh: 基遍人的霉餅計

region.en: Gibeon, hill country of Benjamin
region.zh: 基遍，便雅憫山地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Joshua 9, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Neighbouring Hivites of Gibeon send ambassadors in patched wineskins and mouldy bread, claiming to have come 'from a very far country'. Israel's leaders swear peace without asking the mouth of the LORD; three days later the trick is discovered, but the oath stands — the Gibeonites become perpetual hewers of wood and drawers of water 'for the house of my God'.
summary.zh: 附近基遍的希未人遣使者，帶補過的皮酒袋與發霉的餅，自稱「從極遠之地而來」。以色列首領未求耶和華的口便起誓立和；三日後詭計被識破，然誓言有效——基遍人成為永遠劈柴挑水的人，「為我神的殿」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they went to Joshua unto the camp at Gilgal, and said unto him, and to the men of Israel: 'We are come from a far country; now therefore make ye a covenant with us.' And the men of Israel said unto the Hivites: 'Peradventure ye dwell among us; how shall we make a covenant with you?'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Joshua 9:6-7 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他們來到吉甲的營中見約書亞，對他和以色列人說：「我們是從遠方來的；現在請你們與我們立約。」以色列人對希未人說：「恐怕你們住在我們中間，怎能與你們立約呢？」

passages.text: The ambassadors showed their bread — 'it was dry, and had become mouldy cakes' — and their patched wineskins and mended sandals as proof of a long journey. The men 'asked not counsel at the mouth of the LORD' and made peace. Three days later Israel learned they were neighbours; Joshua summoned them and said: 'Wherefore have ye beguiled us?' The oath could not be broken, so they were made servants at the altar — wood and water 'for the house of my God'. Paraphrase of Joshua 9:12-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Joshua 9:12-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 使者拿出他們的餅——「已經乾了，成了發霉的餅」——又拿出他們補過的皮酒袋和修補過的鞋，作為長途跋涉的憑據。那些人「並沒有求問耶和華」，就與他們講和。三天之後，以色列人得知他們是鄰居；約書亞召他們來，說：「你們為什麼欺哄我們呢？」所起的誓不能廢去，於是他們被派在壇前作僕役——為「我神的殿」劈柴打水。此為約書亞記9:12-27（JPS 1917）之改述，非逐字引用。

title.en: Sun, Stand Thou Still upon Gibeon
title.zh: 日頭啊，你要停在基遍

region.en: Gibeon and the valley of Aijalon
region.zh: 基遍與亞雅崙谷

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Joshua 10:1-15, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Five Amorite kings besiege Gibeon for its treaty with Israel; the LORD hurls great stones from heaven. In the middle of the battle Joshua speaks to the sun and the moon — 'Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Aijalon. And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed... and hastened not to go down about a whole day.'
summary.zh: 五亞摩利王因基遍與以色列立約而攻之；耶和華自天降大冰雹。戰中雅各向日月發言——「日頭啊，你要停在基遍；月亮啊，你要止在亞雅崙谷。日頭果然停住，月亮止住……不急速下落，約有一日之久。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Cross-cluster 'sun captured' motif.

passages.text: Then spoke Joshua to the LORD in the day when the LORD delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel; and he said in the sight of Israel: 'Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Aijalon.' And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies... And there was no day like that before it or after it, that the LORD hearkened unto the voice of a man; for the LORD fought for Israel.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Joshua 10:12-14 (public domain).
passages.zh: 當耶和華將亞摩利人交付以色列人的那日，約書亞在以色列人眼前向耶和華禱告說：「日頭啊，你要停在基遍；月亮啊，你要止在亞雅崙谷。」於是日頭停留，月亮止住，直到百姓向仇敵報了仇……在這日以前、這日以後，耶和華聽人的聲音，沒有像這日的，是因耶和華為以色列爭戰。

title.en: Caleb's Eighty-Five-Year Claim on Hebron
title.zh: 迦勒八十五歲索希伯崙

region.en: Hebron, Judean hills
region.zh: 希伯崙，猶大山地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Joshua 14:6-15, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Forty-five years after spying out the land, Caleb comes to Gilgal to claim Moses' oath: 'because I wholly followed the LORD my God'. Though 'as strong this day as... in the day that Moses sent me', he asks the hill country where the Anakim — the very giants that scared the other spies — still dwell, and takes Hebron for his inheritance: 'Give me this mountain.'
summary.zh: 窺地四十五年後，迦勒到吉甲索摩西的誓言：「因為我專心跟從耶和華我的神」。雖「今日我還是強壯，像摩西打發我去的那天」，他求的卻是亞衲族人——當年嚇退探子的巨人——仍居的山地，得希伯崙為業：「求你將耶和華那日應許我的這山給我。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And now, behold, the LORD hath kept me alive, as He spoke, these forty and five years... And now, behold, I am this day fourscore and five years old. As yet I am as strong this day as I was in the day that Moses sent me: as my strength was then, even so is my strength now, for war, and to go out and to come in. Now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the LORD spoke in that day.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Joshua 14:10-12 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 現在，看哪，耶和華照他所應許的，使我存活這四十五年……現在，看哪，我今日八十五歲了。我今日還是強壯，像摩西打發我去的那日一樣；那時我的力量如何，現在我的力量也如何，無論是爭戰，是出入。現在求你將耶和華那日所應許的這山地給我。

title.en: Choose You This Day: Joshua's Covenant Assembly at Shechem
title.zh: 今日就可以選擇：示劍立約大會

region.en: Shechem, land of Canaan
region.zh: 示劍，迦南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Joshua 24, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Old and old, Joshua gathers all Israel at Shechem and rehearses history from Terah's migration to the crossing of the Jordan. Then the charter choice: 'choose you this day whom ye will serve... but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.' The people answer that they will serve the LORD, who has done 'all these great things'; Joshua writes the words in the book of the law of God and sets up a great stone under the terebinth as witness.
summary.zh: 年老的約書亞召集以色列眾人於示劍，數說歷史——自他拉遷徙至過約旦河。隨後是根本抉擇：「今日就可以選擇所要事奉的……至於我和我家，我們必定事奉耶和華。」百姓應允事奉行「這一切大事」的神；約書亞將話寫在神的律法書上，立一塊大石頭在橡樹下作見證。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And if it seem evil unto you to serve the LORD, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell; but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD. And the people answered and said: 'Far be it from us that we should forsake the LORD, to serve other gods.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Joshua 24:15-16 (public domain).
passages.zh: 你們若以為事奉耶和華不好，今日就可以選擇所要事奉的：是你們列祖在大河那邊所事奉的神呢，還是你們所住這地之亞摩利人的神呢？至於我和我家，我們必定事奉耶和華。百姓回答說：「我們斷不敢離棄耶和華去事奉別神。」

title.en: Ehud the Left-Handed and the Dagger for Eglon
title.zh: 左撇子以笏與刺伊磯倫之劍

region.en: Palace of Eglon at Jericho (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伊磯倫王宮，耶利哥（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 3:12-30, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Moab oppresses Israel eighteen years. Ehud, a left-handed Benjamite, makes a two-edged dagger a cubit long and straps it to his right thigh; having delivered tribute to the very fat king Eglon, he returns alone on the pretext of 'a secret errand', and drives the blade — handle and all — into the king's belly while the servants, thinking their master covers his feet, wait respectfully outside. Israel then holds the fords of the Jordan.
summary.zh: 摩押壓制以色列十八年。便雅憫人左手便利的以笏打造一把兩刃劍長一肘，綁在右腿上；獻貢後藉口「奉王命說機密話」獨自返回，將劍——連柄帶刃——刺入極肥胖的伊磯倫王腹中；僕人以為王正在解衣，恭立門外。以色列隨即把守約旦渡口。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Ehud put forth his left hand, and took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly; and the haft also went in after the blade; and the fat closed upon the blade, for he drew not the sword out of his belly; and it came out behind.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 3:21-22 (public domain).
passages.zh: 以笏伸出左手，從右腿上拔出劍來，刺入他的肚腹；連劍柄也隨著劍身進去了；肥肉夾住了劍身，因為他沒有從肚腹裡把劍拔出來；劍從後邊穿出。

passages.text: Ehud escaped past the quarries, sounded the shofar in the hill country of Ephraim, and came down after the people of Israel; he said: 'Follow after me; for the LORD hath delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.' They seized the fords of the Jordan and slew about ten thousand Moabites, 'every lusty man, and every man of valour; and there escaped not a man. So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel; and the land had rest fourscore years.' Paraphrase of Judges 3:26-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Judges 3:26-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 以笏逃過採石場，在以法蓮山地吹響號角，率領以色列人下去；他說：「你們跟隨我，因為耶和華已將你們的仇敵摩押人交在你們手中。」他們佔據約旦河的渡口，擊殺約有一萬摩押人，「都是強壯的勇士，沒有一人逃脫。那日，摩押就被以色列人制伏了；國中太平八十年。」（改述《士師記》3:26-30，JPS 1917；非逐字引用。）

title.en: Deborah, Barak, and the Chariots of Hazor
title.zh: 底波拉巴拉克與夏瑣戰車

region.en: Mount Tabor and river Kishon
region.zh: 他泊山與基順河

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 4, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Deborah the prophetess judges Israel under a palm tree between Ramah and Bethel. She summons Barak: 'Hath not the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded thee... draw toward mount Tabor?' Barak will go only if she goes; she agrees — 'for the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour'. Sisera's nine hundred iron chariots are swept away by the flooded Kishon, and the general himself falls by a woman's hand.
summary.zh: 女先知底波拉在拉瑪伯特利之間的棕樹下治理以色列。她召巴拉：「耶和華以色列的神豈沒有吩咐你……往他泊山去？」巴拉說你若不同去就不去；她應允——「你行的路必得不著榮耀」。西西拉的九百輛鐵車被漲溢的基順河沖去，主帥親自倒在婦人手中。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Barak said unto her: 'If thou wilt go with me, then I will go; but if thou wilt not go with me, I will not go.' And she said: 'I will surely go with thee; notwithstanding, the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the LORD will give Sisera over into the hand of a woman.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 4:8-9 (public domain).
passages.zh: 巴拉對她說：「你若與我同去，我就去；你若不同去，我就不去。」她說：「我必與你同去；然而你所行的路不會為你帶來榮耀，因為耶和華要把西西拉交在一個婦人手中。」

passages.text: Barak went down from Tabor with ten thousand men; the LORD discomfited Sisera and all his chariots with the edge of the sword, and Sisera alighted from his chariot and fled on foot to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite. Deborah and Barak pursued the discomfited army to Harosheth — 'and there was not a man left'. Paraphrase of Judges 4:14-16 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Judges 4:14-16 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 巴拉率一萬人從他泊山下去；耶和華使西西拉和他一切戰車潰亂，在刀劍之前敗逃，西西拉就下車，徒步逃往基尼人希百之妻雅億的帳棚。底波拉和巴拉追趕潰敗的軍隊直到夏羅設——「沒有一人留下」。（改述《士師記》4:14-16，JPS 1917；非逐字引用。）

title.en: Jael, the Milk, and the Tent-Pin
title.zh: 雅億、奶與帳棚橛

region.en: Tent of Heber the Kenite, plain of Esdraelon
region.zh: 基尼人希百之帳棚，以斯德倫平原

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 4:17-22; 5:24-27, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Fleeing on foot, Sisera seeks refuge in Jael's tent. She covers him with a rug, gives him milk instead of the water he asks, and waits until he is asleep; then she takes the workman's hammer and a tent-pin and drives it through his temple into the ground. Barak arrives in pursuit — 'and, behold, Sisera lay dead, and the pin was in his temple'. The Song of Deborah crowns her 'most blessed above women in the tent'.
summary.zh: 徒步逃亡的西西拉入雅億帳中求庇。她以毯蒙他，給他奶而非所求的水，待他睡熟；便取工人的錘與帳棚橛，穿透他的太陽穴釘入地中。巴拉追至——「西西拉已死倒臥，橛子在他鬢邊」。底波拉之歌稱她「帳棚中的婦人比眾婦人何等有福」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: But Jael the wife of Heber took a tent-pin, and took a hammer in her hand, and went softly unto him, and smote the pin into his temples, and fastened it into the ground; for he was fast asleep and weary. So he died. And, behold, as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him, and said unto him: 'Come, and I will show thee the man whom thou seekest.' And he came unto her; and, behold, Sisera lay dead, and the pin was in his temples.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 4:21-22 (public domain).
passages.zh: 希百之妻雅億取了一根帳棚的橛子，手裡拿著錘子，輕輕走到他那裡，把橛子釘入他的鬢角，釘進地裡；因為他沉睡疲乏。他就死了。看哪，巴拉追趕西西拉的時候，雅億出來迎接他，對他說：「來，我把你所尋找的人指給你看。」他就來到她那裡；看哪，西西拉已經死了，橛子還在他的鬢角裡。

title.en: Awake, Awake, Deborah: The Song of Victory
title.zh: 底波拉啊醒起：得勝之歌

region.en: Ramah and Bethel, judge's palm tree
region.zh: 拉瑪與伯特利，士師的棕樹

period: Composed c. 11th-10th c. BCE (archaic Hebrew, among the oldest strata of the Hebrew Bible); recorded in Judges 5; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 5, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: One of the oldest poems in the Hebrew Bible: Deborah and Barak sing that 'when the people offer themselves willingly, bless ye the LORD', rehearse the march of the tribes, curse Meroz for not helping, and crown the battle with Jael's act — 'At her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay.'
summary.zh: 希伯來聖經最古老詩歌之一：底波拉與巴拉唱「百姓甘心犧牲自己之處，你們當稱頌耶和華」，歷數各支派行軍，咒詛未來助戰的米羅斯，以雅億之舉收束——「在她腳前他屈身、仆倒、躺臥」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Judges 5's archaic language places it among the oldest biblical texts (cf. Song of the Sea).

passages.text: Then sang Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam on that day, saying: 'When men let grow their hair in Israel, when the people offer themselves willingly, bless ye the LORD! Hear, O ye kings; give ear, O ye princes; I, unto the LORD will I sing; I will sing praise to the LORD, the God of Israel.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 5:1-3 (public domain).
passages.zh: 那日，底波拉和亞比挪菴的兒子巴拉唱歌說：「以色列中有人留長頭髮，百姓甘心獻上自己，你們要稱頌耶和華！君王啊，要聽；首領啊，要側耳而聽；我要向耶和華歌唱；我要歌頌讚美耶和華——以色列的神。」

passages.text: The poem remembers the Lord going forth from Seir, the earth trembling, the heavens dropping, 'even yon Sinai at the presence of the LORD'; the people volunteered to the battle, Ephraim behind Amalek, Benjamin among the peoples, princes of Machir, Zebulun risking their lives, Naphtali on the heights. The Kishon swept the enemy away: 'the river Kishon swept them away, that ancient river, the river Kishon. O my soul, march on with strength!' Paraphrase of Judges 5:4-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Judges 5:4-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 這詩追念耶和華從西珥而出，大地震動，諸天滴落，「甚至那西奈山也在耶和華面前震動」；百姓自願上陣，以法蓮在亞瑪力之後，便雅憫在眾民之中，瑪吉的領袖，西布倫冒著性命之險，拿弗他利在高處。基順河把仇敵沖走：「基順河把他們沖走，那古老的河，基順河。我的靈啊，奮力前行吧！」（改述《士師記》5:4-21，JPS 1917；非逐字引用。）

title.en: Gideon's Fleece of Wool
title.zh: 基甸的羊毛神蹟

region.en: Ophrah, threshing floor of Joash
region.zh: 俄弗拉，約阿施的打麥場

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 6:11-40, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The angel of the LORD finds the youngest son of Joash threshing wheat in a winepress 'to hide it from the Midianites': 'The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.' Gideon demands signs — first dew on the fleece only, then dry fleece in wet grass — and destroys his father's altar of Baal by night. His father defends him with the classic put-down: 'Will ye plead for Baal? If he be a god, let him plead for himself.'
summary.zh: 耶和華的使者見約阿施幼子在酒醡裡打麥，「為要防備米甸人」：「大能的勇士啊，耶和華與你同在。」基甸求兆——先羊毛獨有露，後草地有露羊毛獨乾——並夜間拆毀其父的巴力壇。其父以名句護子：「你們是為巴力爭論麼？他若是神，讓他為自己爭論吧。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Jerubbaal, 'let Baal plead', becomes Gideon's by-name.

passages.text: And it was so: for he rose up early on the morrow, and pressed the flock together, and put the fleece with the dew on the ground only, and there was dew on all the ground, but on the fleece there was not dew. ... Then Gideon said unto God: 'Let not Thine anger be kindled against me, and I will speak but this once: let me make trial, I pray Thee, but this once with the fleece; let there now be dew on the fleece only, and upon all the ground let there be dry.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 6:38-39 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis; second sign (dry fleece) combined.
passages.zh: 事情果然如此：他次日清早起來，將羊毛擠壓在一起，把羊毛放在地上，羊毛上只有露水，遍地都有露水，惟獨羊毛上沒有露水。……基甸對神說：「求你不要向我發怒，我再說這一次：求你容我再試一次羊毛；如今只叫羊毛上有露水，遍地都乾燥。」

title.en: Three Hundred with Trumpets, Torches, and Jars
title.zh: 三百人持號角火把與瓶

region.en: Spring of Harod, valley of Jezreel
region.zh: 哈律泉，耶斯列谷

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 7, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Thirty-two thousand volunteers are reduced by the LORD's own vetting: first the fearful depart — twenty-two thousand; then the three hundred who lap water like dogs are chosen against a Midianite army 'like locusts'. Armed with trumpets, empty jars, and torches, they surround the camp by night, break the jars at Gideon's signal, and cry 'The sword of the LORD and of Gideon!' The Midianites flee; the sword is 'of the LORD', and the battle turns on noise and light.
summary.zh: 三萬二千志願者經神親自篩減：先懼怕者離去——兩萬二千人；再以舔水如狗的三百人對陣「如同蝗蟲」的米甸大軍。他們以號角空瓶火把夜間圍營，在基甸號令下碎瓶，呼「耶和華和基甸的刀！」米甸人潰逃；刀屬耶和華，戰事成於聲與光。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the three companies blew the horns, and broke the pitchers, and held the torches in their left hands, and the horns in their right hands to blow withal; and they cried: 'The sword of the LORD and of Gideon!' And they stood every man in his place round about the camp; and all the host ran; and they shouted, and put them to flight.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 7:20-21 (public domain).
passages.zh: 三隊的人吹角，打破瓶子，左手拿著火把，右手拿著角吹號；他們喊著說：「耶和華和基甸的刀！」各人站在營的四圍自己的地方；全營的人都亂跑，呼喊，逃跑。

title.en: Abimelech and the Talking Bramble
title.zh: 亞比米勒與會說話的荊棘

region.en: Shechem, land of Canaan
region.zh: 示劍，迦南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 9, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Gideon's son by a Shechemite concubine slays his seventy brothers on one stone and is made king. Jotham, the lone survivor, pronounces the fable of the trees from Mount Gerizim — olive, fig, vine, all refusing kingship, until the bramble accepts with threats of fire — 'and let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon'. The curse works itself out: Abimelech and Shechem destroy each other, and he dies with a millstone-brain wound, begging his armour-bearer to finish him.
summary.zh: 基甸示劍婢所生之子在一塊石上殺七十弟兄而為王。倖存的約坦自基利心山發言樹木寓言——橄欖、無花果、葡萄皆拒王位，直至荊棘以火相脅而受——「願火從荊棘裡出來，燒滅利巴嫩的香柏樹」。咒詛應驗：亞比米勒與示劍同歸於盡，他被磨石擊傷腦，求拿兵器的少年刺死。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Judges 9:56-57 renders the Shechem bloodguilt as divine repayment.

passages.text: And the bramble said unto the trees: 'If in truth ye anoint me king over you, then come and take refuge in my shadow; and if not, let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon.' ... When Abimelech had fought against the city all that day, he took the city, and slew the people that was therein; and he beat down the city, and sowed it with salt.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 9:15, 45 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 荊棘對樹木說：「你們若誠心膏我為王，就來投在我的蔭下；若不然，願火從荊棘裡出來，燒滅黎巴嫩的香柏樹。」……亞比米勒終日攻打那城，就取了那城，殺了城中的居民；又拆毀那城，撒上鹽。

passages.text: At Thebez a woman cast an upper millstone on Abimelech's head and broke his skull; he called hastily to his armour-bearer, 'Draw thy sword and slay me, that men say not of me: A woman slew him', 'and his young man thrust him through, and he died'. 'Thus did God requite the wickedness of Abimelech, which he did unto his father, in slaying his seventy brethren.' Paraphrase of Judges 9:50-56 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Judges 9:50-56 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在提備斯，有一個婦人把一塊上磨石拋在亞比米勒的頭上，打破了他的頭骨；他急忙呼叫拿兵器的少年人說：「拔出你的刀來殺我，免得人議論我說：『是一個婦人殺了他。』」那少年人就用刀刺透他，他就死了。「這樣，神報應亞比米勒向他父親所行的惡，就是殺了他七十個弟兄。」改述自《士師記》9:50-56（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Jephthah's Vow and His Only Child
title.zh: 耶弗他的誓言與獨女

region.en: Mizpah of Gilead, Transjordan
region.zh: 基列的米斯巴，約旦河東

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 11, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The outcast son of a harlot is recalled to lead Gilead against Ammon, and vows: 'Whatsoever cometh forth from the doors of my house to meet me... shall surely be the LORD's, and I will offer it up for a burnt-offering.' He wins the war — 'with a very great slaughter' — and returns to Mizpah, where his only daughter comes dancing with timbrels. Two months she bewails her maidenhood in the mountains; 'and it came to pass at the end of two months, that he did with her according to his vow', and Israel's daughters lament her yearly.
summary.zh: 妓女之子被逐者受召領基列抗亞捫，起誓：「我從我家門口迎接我回來的……必歸耶和華，我也必將他獻為燔祭。」他大敗亞捫——「殺戮甚大」——回到米斯巴，獨女擊鼓跳舞出迎。她於山中兩月哀哭處女之身；「兩月已滿，他照所許的願行了」，以色列女子年年為她哀哭。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Rabbinic tradition debates whether the vow was fulfilled by sacrifice or perpetual virginity; the narrative itself is stark.

passages.text: And when he saw her, he rent his clothes, and said: 'Alas, my daughter! thou hast brought me very low, and thou art among them that trouble me; for I have opened my mouth unto the LORD, and I cannot go back.' And she said unto him: 'My father, thou hast opened thy mouth unto the LORD; do unto me according to that which hath proceeded out of thy mouth.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 11:35-36 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他一看見她，就撕裂衣服，說：「哀哉，我的女兒啊！你使我甚是愁苦，你成了使我煩惱的人；因為我已經向耶和華開口許願，不能收回。」她對他說：「我父啊，你既向耶和華開口，就照你口中所出的向我行吧。」

title.en: A Nazirite Announced: Samson's Birth
title.zh: 拿細耳人的預告：參孫出生

region.en: Zorah, Danite hill country
region.zh: 瑣拉，但支派山地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 13, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The angel of the LORD appears to the barren wife of Manoah: 'thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and no razor shall come on his head; for the child shall be a Nazirite unto God from the womb'. Manoah asks his name and receives only: 'Why askest thou thus after my name, seeing it is hidden?' The angel ascends in the flame of the altar; the child is born and 'the LORD blessed him', named Samson.
summary.zh: 耶和華的使者向瑪挪亞不育之妻顯現：「你必懷孕生一個兒子；不可用剃刀剃他的頭，因為這孩子從母腹裡就歸神作拿細耳人。」瑪挪亞問其名，只答：「你何必問我的名，我名是奇妙的？」使者在壇上火燄中升去；孩子出生，「耶和華賜福與他」，名參孫。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Nazirite rules (Num 6) frame the hero's taboo.

passages.text: And Manoah said unto the angel of the LORD: 'What is thy name, that when thy words come to pass we may do thee honour?' And the angel of the LORD said unto him: 'Wherefore askest thou after my name, seeing it is hidden?' So Manoah took the kid with the meal-offering, and offered it upon the rock unto the LORD; and the angel did wondrously... and the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame of the altar.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 13:17-20 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 瑪挪亞對耶和華的使者說：「你的名是什麼？等你的話應驗了，我們好尊敬你。」耶和華的使者對他說：「你何必問我的名？我的名是奇妙的。」瑪挪亞將山羊羔和素祭獻在磐石上，獻給耶和華；使者行了奇事……耶和華的使者就在壇的火焰中升上去了。

title.en: Honey in the Lion: Samson's Wedding Riddle
title.zh: 獅中之蜜：參孫的婚宴謎語

region.en: Timnah, vineyards of Philistia
region.zh: 亭拿，非利士葡萄園

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 14:1-20, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: On the road to his Philistine bride a young lion roars at Samson; the spirit of the LORD comes on him and he tears it 'as he would have rent a kid'. Later he finds honey in the carcass. At the seven-day feast he bets thirty linen garments on a riddle: 'Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness.' The bride is bullied into betraying the answer; Samson's reply — 'If ye had not plowed with my heifer' — is itself a riddle, and he pays the debt by slaying thirty men of Ashkelon.
summary.zh: 往非利士新娘路上，獅子吼叫向參孫；耶和華的靈感動他，他撕裂獅子「如同撕裂山羊羔」。後在屍內得蜜。七日婚宴上他以三十件裡衣外衣賭一謎語：「喫的從喫者出來，甜的從強者出來。」新娘被逼供出答案；參孫的回話——「你們若非用我的母牛犢耕種」——本身又是一謎，遂殺亞實基倫三十人償債。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The Nazirite touches a corpse — transgression woven into the hero cycle.

passages.text: And the men of the city said unto him on the seventh day before the sun went down: 'What is sweeter than honey? and what is stronger than a lion?' And he said unto them: 'If ye had not plowed with my heifer, ye had not found out my riddle.' And the spirit of the LORD came upon him mightily, and he went down to Ashkelon, and slew of them thirty men, and took their apparel, and gave changes of raiment unto them which expounded the riddle.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 14:18-19 (public domain).
passages.zh: 城裡的人在第七天、日落以前對他說：「有甚麼比蜜還甜呢？有甚麼比獅子還強呢？」他對他們說：「你們若不是用我的母牛犢耕地，就猜不出我的謎語來。」耶和華的靈大大感動他，他就下到亞實基倫，擊殺了他們三十個人，奪了他們的衣裳，將衣裳給了那些解出謎語的人。

title.en: Foxes with Firebrands and the Jawbone of an Ass
title.zh: 帶火把的狐狸與驢腮骨

region.en: Philistine grainfields and Lehi
region.zh: 非利士麥田與利希

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 15, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Denied his wife, Samson catches three hundred foxes, turns them tail to tail with firebrands between, and lets them run through the standing corn of the Philistines. When they burn his wife and her father in revenge, he smites them 'hip and thigh with a great slaughter', then slays a thousand with the fresh jawbone of an ass, naming the place Ramath-lehi. Thirsty, he calls on God; water bursts from the hollow in Lehi.
summary.zh: 妻子被奪，參孫捉三百隻狐狸，尾尾相對，中間捆上火把，放入非利士人站著的禾稼。他們燒其妻與岳父報復，他便「大大殺敗他們，連腿帶腰」；後以未乾的驢腮骨殺千人，地名拉末利希。渴極呼神；神使利希的窪處裂開出水。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he found a new jawbone of an ass, and put forth his hand, and took it, and slew a thousand men therewith. And Samson said: 'With the jawbone of an ass, heaps upon heaps; with the jawbone of an ass have I slain a thousand men.' ... And God clave the hollow place that was in Lehi, and there came water thereout; and when he had drunk, his spirit came again, and he revived.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 15:16, 19 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 他找到一塊未乾的驢腮骨，就伸手拿起來，用它擊殺了一千人。參孫說：「我用驢腮骨殺人成堆，我用驢腮骨擊殺了一千人。」……神使利希的窪處裂開，就有水從其中湧出來；他喝了以後，精神恢復，就甦醒了。

title.en: Delilah's Loom: The Nazirite Sheared
title.zh: 大利拉的織機：剪斷拿細耳人

region.en: Valley of Sorek, Philistine border
region.zh: 梭烈谷，非利士邊境

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 16:4-22, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The Philistine lords offer Delilah eleven hundred shekels for Samson's secret. Three times he mocks her — green withs, new ropes, the weaver's beam — and each test fails while she cries 'thou hast mocked me'. At last, 'pressed daily with her words', he tells her of the Nazirite vow, and she begins to weaken him. His head is shaved on her knees; the LORD departs from him; the Philistines put out his eyes and set him to grind in the prison at Gaza.
summary.zh: 非利士首領許大利拉一千一百舍客勒買參孫的秘密。三次他戲弄她——青繩、新繩、織機的緯線——試而皆敗，她哭「你欺哄我」。末了，因「天天催逼，甚至他心裡煩悶要死」，他說出拿細耳人之願；她開始消磨他。頭髮在她膝上被剃；耶和華離開他；非利士人剜其目，在迦薩監裡推磨。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And she said unto him: 'How canst thou say, I love thee, when thy heart is not with me? thou hast mocked me these three times, and hast not told me wherein thy great strength lieth.' And it came to pass, when she pressed him daily with her words, and urged him, that his soul was vexed unto death; and he told her all his heart, and said unto her: 'There hath not come a razor upon my head; for I have been a Nazirite unto God from my mother's womb; if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 16:15-17 (public domain).
passages.zh: 她對他說：「你既不把心交給我，怎能說你愛我呢？你這三次欺哄我，沒有告訴我你這麼大的力氣從何而來。」她天天用話催逼他，煩擾他，以致他的心裡煩悶得要死；他就把心裡的一切都告訴了她，對她說：「向來沒有人用剃頭刀剃我的頭，因為我從母腹裡就歸神作拿細耳人；若剃了我的頭髮，我的力氣就離開我，我便軟弱，像別人一樣。」

title.en: Between the Pillars: Samson's Death at the Feast of Dagon
title.zh: 雙柱之間：參孫死於大袞之宴

region.en: Temple of Dagon, Gaza (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 大袞神廟，迦薩（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 16:23-31, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The Philistine lords celebrate their god Dagon for delivering Samson and summon the blinded prisoner 'to make sport'. Between the two central pillars the boy leads him, and he prays: 'O Lord GOD, remember me, I pray Thee, and strengthen me, I pray Thee, only this once'. Pushing with all his might he brings the house down on the lords and all the people — 'so the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life' — and his brothers bury him between Zorah and Eshtaol.
summary.zh: 非利士首領聚集宴大袞，慶其神將仇敵交在手中，召盲囚「戲耍」。童子引他立於兩根中柱之間，他禱告：「主耶和華啊，求你眷念我，求你賜我這一次的力量。」盡力推之，房屋倒塌在首領與眾人身上——「他死時所殺的人比活著所殺的還多」——其兄弟將他葬於瑣拉以實陶之間。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Samson called unto the LORD, and said: 'O Lord GOD, remember me, I pray Thee, and strengthen me, I pray Thee, only this once, O God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.' And Samson took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house rested, and leaned upon them, the one with his right hand, and the other with his left. And Samson said: 'Let me die with the Philistines.' And he bowed himself with all his might; and the house fell upon the lords, and upon all the people that were therein.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 16:28-30 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 參孫求告耶和華說：「主耶和華啊，求你記念我，求你只這一次賜我力量，神啊，使我在非利士人身上為我這兩隻眼睛一次報仇。」參孫就抱住那支撐房屋的兩根中間柱子，一手抱一根，右手抱一根，左手抱一根。參孫說：「我情願與非利士人同死。」他就盡力屈身，房屋就倒塌，壓在眾首領和屋內所有的人身上。

title.en: Micah's Silvered Idol and the Danite Theft
title.zh: 米迦的鍍銀神像與但人竊像

region.en: House of Micah in Ephraim; Laish in the far north
region.zh: 以法蓮的米迦之家；極北的拉億

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 17-18, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Micah restores stolen silver to his mother, who dedicates it to a graven image and a molten one; Micah makes a house of gods, an ephod, and ordains his own son priest. A wandering Levite is hired as priest 'for ten pieces of silver a year'. Then five Danite spies, and afterwards six hundred armed men, take the image and the Levite — who goes over gladly — and fall on peaceful Laish, renaming it Dan. 'In those days there was no king in Israel; every man did that which was right in his own eyes.'
summary.zh: 米迦歸還所竊之銀給母親，母親以之鑄成像；米迦設神堂、製以弗得、立己子為祭司。又僱流浪利未人「每年十舍客勒銀子」為祭司。五個但支派探子，繼而六百帶刀者，奪像與利未人——利未人欣然從之——攻陷安居的拉億，改名但。「那時以色列中沒有王，各人任意而行。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the five men that went to spy out the land went up, and came in thither, and took the graven image, and the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image; and the priest stood in the entering of the gate with the six hundred men that were girt with weapons of war. ... And they said unto him: 'Hold thy peace, lay thine hand upon thy mouth, and go with us, and be to us a father and a priest; is it better for thee to be priest unto the house of one man, or that thou be priest unto a tribe and a family in Israel?'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 18:17, 19 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 那五個去窺探那地的人上去，進了那裡，取了雕刻的像、以弗得、家中的神像和鑄成的像；祭司和那六百個佩帶兵器的人一同站在城門口。……他們對他說：「不要作聲，用手摀口，跟我們去吧，作我們的父和祭司；你作一個人家中的祭司好呢，還是作以色列一支派一家族的祭司好呢？」

title.en: The Outrage at Gibeah: A Levite and His Concubine
title.zh: 基便之惡：利未人與其妾

region.en: Gibeah of Benjamin
region.zh: 便雅憫的基比亞

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Judges 19, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: A Levite's concubine plays the harlot and flees to her father's house; he follows and wins her back. Crossing Benjamin by night, no man takes them in until an old man of Gibeah does. The wicked men of the city surround the house 'that we may know him'; the host and the Levite offer the women; the concubine is thrust out and dies at the door. The Levite cuts her into twelve pieces and sends a piece to every tribe of Israel — the call to arms that nearly exterminates Benjamin.
summary.zh: 利未人的妾行淫歸父家；他前往勸回。夜過便雅憫地，無人接宿，直至基比亞一老人。城中匪徒圍屋「我們要與他交合」；主人與利未人皆出女子；妾被推出，死於門前。利未人將她切成十二塊，使人拿著傳送以色列四境——號召各支派，幾乎滅盡便雅憫。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Text contains sexual violence; stated through the narrative's own voice without dramatization.

passages.text: And it came to pass at midnight, that the woman came to the door of the house of her father-in-law, and fell down; there she lay till the light of the morning. ... And her master rose up in the morning, and opened the doors of the house, and went out to go his way; and, behold, the woman his concubine was fallen down at the door of the house, with her hands upon the threshold.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 19:26-27 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 到了半夜，那婦人來到她公公房屋的門口，就仆倒；她躺在那裡，直到天亮。……她的主人早晨起來，開了房屋的門，出去要走他的路；不料，他的妾仆倒在房屋門口，兩手搭在門檻上。

passages.text: He laid her on the ass and journeyed home; then he took a knife and cut her, limb by limb, into twelve pieces, and sent her into all the coasts of Israel with the message: 'Consider it, take counsel, and speak.' All Israel gathered 'as one man, from Dan even to Beer-sheba' — the narrative that leads to the war of Benjamin. Paraphrase of Judges 19:29-30; 20:1 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Judges 19:29-30; 20:1 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他把她放在驢上，起程回家；然後拿出一把刀，將她肢解，切成十二塊，分送以色列全境，並傳話說：「你們當思想、商議、說明。」全以色列便「如同一人，從但到別是巴」聚集起來——這就是引向便雅憫之戰的敘事。此為《士師記》19:29-30；20:1（JPS 1917）的意譯，並非逐字照錄。

title.en: Zakariyya's Prayer and the Silent Sign of Yahya
title.zh: 宰凱里亞的祈禱與啞默之兆

region.en: Jerusalem Temple, mihrab of prayer (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷聖殿祈禱壁龕（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs Ali 'Imran 3:38-41, Maryam 19:2-15; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 3:38-41 and 19:2-15

summary.en: Zakariyya prays: 'O my Lord, give me from Thee a good successor, for Thou art the Hearer of prayer.' The angels call him as he stands praying in the sanctuary: 'God announces to thee Yahya, who shall confirm the word of God.' 'Lord, how shall I have a son when age hath overtaken me, and my wife is barren?' — 'Thus God doth what He pleaseth.' He asks for a sign; the sign is that for three days he shall speak to no man. And God gives him Yahya: 'O Yahya, take the Book with firm purpose' — a devout Lord, chaste, and a prophet of the just.
summary.zh: 宰凱里亞在聖堂祈禱：『主啊，賜我一個善良的繼承者。』天使呼喚他：『主向你報喜——葉海雅，他將證實真主的言語。』『我妻已絕育，我已年邁，怎會得子？』——『主如此命其所欲。』他求徵兆；徵兆是三日不與人言。主賜其葉海雅：『葉海雅啊，當受持經書，意向堅定』——是貞潔的、敬畏的、正直的先知。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: When Zakariyya cried to his Lord, 'O my Lord, leave me not childless; but Thou art the best of heirs.' And We heard him: and We gave him John; and we made his wife right-fitting. Verily they were hasty in coming to good works, and called on Us with love and fear, and were humbled before Us.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 21:89-90 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那時，宰凱里雅向他的主呼求：「我的主啊，求你不要讓我無子；你確是最好的繼承者。」我們便應允了他：賜給他葉哈雅；並使他的妻子成為適宜生育的。他們確是急於行善，懷著愛與敬畏向我們祈求，且在我們面前謙卑。

passages.text: And when he stood up in the sanctuary praying, the angels of God called him and said, 'God announceth to thee Yahya, who shall confirm the Word from God, a prince and chaste, and a prophet, and righteous one of the just.' He said, 'Lord! how shall I have a son, when age hath overtaken me, and my wife is barren?' He said, 'Thus doth God what pleaseth Him.' He said, 'Give me a token, then.' He said, 'The token shall be, that for three days thou shalt speak to no man except by signs.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 3:38-41 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他站在聖所中祈禱時，真主的眾天使呼喚他，說：「真主向你報喜，將賜你葉哈雅，他將證實來自真主的話語，是一位首領、貞潔者、先知，也是義人中的正直者。」他說：「主啊！我年老已至，我的妻子又不育，怎會有兒子呢？」真主說：「真主如此行祂所喜悅的事。」他說：「那麼，求你賜我一個徵兆。」真主說：「徵兆就是：你三日之內不得與人說話，只可用手勢示意。」

passages.text: O Yahya, take the Book with firm purpose. And We bestowed on him wisdom when a child, and a tenderness from Ourself, and purity; and he was devout and kind to his parents; and he was not a rebellious, wicked person. And peace was on him on the day he was born, and the day of his death, and the day when he shall be raised to life.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 19:12-15 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「葉哈雅啊，你當以堅定的意志持守經典。」我們在他年幼時便賜予他智慧，並賜予他來自我們的慈愛與純潔；他虔誠，對父母孝順；他不是叛逆、邪惡之人。願平安降臨於他出生的那日、他死亡的那日，以及他將被復活的那日。

title.en: The Angels Speak to Maryam: 'God Chooseth Thee'
title.zh: 天使對麥爾彥說話：『主揀選了你』

region.en: Nazareth / Jerusalem temple (symbolic pin at Jerusalem)
region.zh: 拿撒勒／耶路撒冷聖殿（象徵性定位於耶路撒冷）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs Ali 'Imran 3:42-47, Maryam 19:16-26; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 3:42-47

summary.en: The angels say to Maryam: 'God hath chosen thee, and made thee pure, and raised thee above all women of the worlds; worship thy Lord, bow thyself down, and adore.' She is told of a Word from Him, Isa the Messiah — 'She said, How shall I have a son whom man hath not touched?' — 'Thus God createth what He pleaseth.' In the withdrawal she meets a spirit in the form of a perfect man: 'I am the messenger of thy Lord, that I may give thee a gift, a faultless boy.'
summary.zh: 天使對麥爾彥說：『主揀選了你，使你純潔，並提拔你超越世界萬民之女；當敬拜你的主。』她被告知主的言語——麥西哈爾撒：『未曾有人觸碰我，我怎會得子？』——『主如此造其所欲者。』她退居時遇一化身完美之人的精靈：『我是你主的使者，將賜你一個無瑕疵的男孩。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; presented via public-domain translation; the Qur'anic virgin birth narrative differs from Christian Gospel accounts.

passages.text: And remember when the angel said, 'O Maryam, verily hath God chosen thee, and purified thee, and chosen thee above the women of the worlds: worship thy Lord, bow thyself down, and adore.' This is one of the announcements of things unseen, which We reveal to thee; for thou wast not with them when they cast their lots with pens, which of them should rear Maryam; nor wast thou with them when they disputed about it.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 3:42-44 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你當記得，當時天使說：「麥爾彥啊，真主確已揀選了你，潔淨了你，並揀選你超越眾世界的婦女：你當崇拜你的主，當叩拜，當鞠躬。」這是未見之事的宣告之一，我們將其啟示給你；因為當他們抽籤，以筆決定誰來撫養麥爾彥時，你並不在他們那裡；當他們為此事爭論時，你也不在他們那裡。

passages.text: When the angels said, 'O Maryam, God announceth to thee the Word from Himself: his name shall be, Messiah, Jesus, the son of Maryam, illustrious in this world and in the next, and of those who are near the presence of God. And he shall speak to men when in the cradle, and in maturity, and shall be one of the just.' She said, 'Lord! how shall I have a son, when man hath not touched me?' He said, 'Thus: God will create what He pleaseth: when He decreeth a thing, He only saith Be, and it is.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 3:45-47 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當時，眾天使說：「麥爾彥啊，真主向你報喜，將賜你來自祂的一句話語：他的名字將是麥西哈·爾撒，麥爾彥之子，在今世與後世皆享有榮耀，且是親近真主之人。他將在搖籃中及壯年時對人說話，並將是義人之一。」她說：「主啊！當男人尚未觸及我時，我怎會有兒子呢？」真主說：「正是如此：真主創造祂所喜悅的：當祂判定一件事時，祂只說『有』，它就有了。」

passages.text: And make mention of Maryam in the Book; when she went apart from her family, eastward, and took a veil to screen herself from them; and We sent Our spirit to her, and he appeared to her in the shape of a perfect man. She said, 'I fly for refuge unto the God of Mercy from thee; if thou fearest Him, begone from me, and approach me not.' He answered, 'I am only a messenger of thy Lord, that I may bestow on thee a boy most pure.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 19:16-19 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你當在經中提及瑪利亞；當時她離開家人，向東而去，並設下帷幕以遮蔽自己，不讓他們看見；我派遣我的靈到她那裡，他就以一個完美男子的形貌向她顯現。她說：『我求你庇護，免受你的侵害，向至慈之主求庇護；你若敬畏他，就離開我，不要靠近我。』他回答說：『我不過是你主的使者，為要賜給你一個純潔的男孩。』

title.en: Under the Palm: Isa Speaks in the Cradle
title.zh: 棕櫚樹下：爾撒搖籃中說話

region.en: Bethlehem / palm grove outside the city (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伯利恆／城外棕櫚林（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah Maryam 19:22-35; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 19:22-35

summary.en: She withdrew with him to a distant place; the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm: 'Would that I had died before this.' A voice from beneath her: 'Grieve not: thy Lord hath provided a rivulet; shake the trunk of the palm and it shall let fall fresh ripe dates; eat and drink, and thine eye be refreshed.' To her people she comes with the child; they charge her. 'I am the servant of God; He hath given me the Book, and made me a prophet: He hath blessed me wheresoever I am, and hath enjoined on me prayer and the poor-rate, so long as I shall live; and to be dutiful to her that beareth me.' 'Peace was on me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I shall be raised to life.'
summary.zh: 她攜子退至遠處；分娩之痛使她靠向棕櫚樹幹：『恨不得我早死了。』樹下有聲呼喚：『勿憂傷；你的主已在下面造出溪流；搖動棕櫚樹幹，必落下鮮熟之椰棗；可吃可飲，眼目舒適。』她抱子至族人前，被責問。『我是真主的僕人：他賜我經典，立我為先知；並命我禮拜施捨，孝敬生我之母。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And she went in private with him to a distant place; and the pains of childbirth came upon her near the trunk of the palm, and she said, 'Would to God I had died before this, and had been a thing forgotten, forgotten of all!' And a voice from beneath her cried to her, 'Grieve not, for thy Lord hath provided a rivulet beneath thee; and shake the trunk of the palm-tree towards thee, and it shall drop fresh ripe dates upon thee. Eat therefore and drink, and thine eye shall be refreshed; and if thou seest any man, say, I have vowed abstinence to the God of Mercy: this day I will not speak with any man.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 19:22-26 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 她便私下帶著他前往一個遙遠的地方；臨產的陣痛在棕櫚樹幹旁臨到她，她說：『但願我在這之前死去，被人全然遺忘，成為一件被遺忘之物！』於是她下方有聲音向她呼喊說：『不要憂傷，你的主已在你下方預備了一條溪流；你向自己搖動棕櫚樹幹，它就會為你落下新鮮成熟的椰棗。你當吃、當飲，你的眼目必得安慰；你若看見任何男子，就說：我已向至慈之主許願守靜：今日我不與任何男子說話。』

passages.text: And she came to her people with him in her bosom. Said they, 'O Maryam, now hast thou done a strange thing: O sister of Aaron, thy father was not a wicked man, neither was thy mother a woman of shame.' And she pointed to the child; but they answered, 'How shall we talk with him who is a child in the cradle?'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 19:27-29 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 她抱著他來到她的族人面前。他們說：『瑪利亞啊，你如今做了一件奇異的事：亞倫的姊妹啊，你的父親並非惡人，你的母親也並非不貞之婦。』她便指向那孩子；但他們回答說：『我們怎能與一個在搖籃中的孩子說話呢？』

passages.text: And the child said, 'Verily I am the servant of God; He hath given me the Book, and made me a prophet: and He hath made me blessed, wheresoever I may be; and He hath enjoined on me prayer and alms-giving, so long as I shall live; and to be dutiful to her that bare me; and hath not made me proud, insolent. And the peace of God was on me the day I was born, and will be the day of my death, and the day when I shall be raised to life. This is Jesus, the son of Mary: this is the truth of which ye are doubtless in doubt.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 19:30-35 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那孩子說：『我確是真主的僕人；他賜給我經典，並使我成為先知：他使我無論身在何處都蒙福；他囑咐我，只要我活著，就要禮拜並施捨；並要孝順生我的母親；他沒有使我成為傲慢、放肆之人。我出生之日，真主的平安臨於我；我死亡之日，以及我復活之日，也必如此。這就是瑪利亞之子耶穌：這就是你們所懷疑的真理。』

title.en: The Table Sent Down to Isa
title.zh: 下降給爾撒的天宴桌

region.en: Galilee, table of the apostles (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 加利利使徒宴桌（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-Ma'idah 5:112-115; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 5:112-115

summary.en: The apostles say: 'O Isa, son of Maryam! can thy Lord send down a table to us from heaven?' He answers: 'Fear God, if ye are believers.' They press — 'We wish to eat thereof, and that our hearts may be assured, and that we may know that thou hast told us the truth.' Isa prays: 'O God our Lord, send down to us from heaven a table, that there may be a festival to the first of us and to the last, and a sign from Thee; and give us means of subsistence, for Thou art the best of providers.' God says: 'I will send it down; but whoever among you shall disbelieve after, I will chastise him with a chastisement wherewith I have chastised no other creature.'
summary.zh: 使徒說：『爾撒啊，你的主能否從天上降下宴桌給我們？』他答：『你們當敬畏主，若你們是信士。』他們堅請——『我們想吃了，使我們的心得定，使我們知道你告訴了我們真理。』爾撒祈禱：『主啊，求你從天上降下宴桌，作為前後眾人的節日，從你而來的蹟象。』主說：『我必降下；但此後不信者，我必以從未懲罰過任何生靈之刑懲之。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation; the surah is named 'The Table' for this episode.

passages.text: Remember when the apostles said, 'O Isa, son of Maryam! can thy Lord send down to us a table furnished from heaven?' He said, 'Fear God if ye are believers.' They said, 'We wish to eat thereof, and that our hearts may be at rest, and that we may know that thou hast told us the truth, and that we may be witnesses of it.' Said Isa, the son of Maryam, 'O God our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, that it may become a festival to us, to the first of us and to the last of us, and a sign from Thee; and give us means of subsistence, for Thou art the best of providers.' And God said, 'Verily I will cause it to descend upon you; and whoever among you believeth not, I will chastise him with a chastisement with which I have chastised no other creature in all the world.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 5:112-114 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Qur'an 5:115 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 記得當時使徒們說：『瑪利亞之子耶穌啊！你的主能從天上降下一桌筵席給我們嗎？』他說：『你們若是有信仰的人，就當敬畏真主。』他們說：『我們願吃那筵席，使我們的心得安寧，使我們知道你對我們說的確是真理，也使我們成為此事的見證。』瑪利亞之子耶穌說：『真主，我們的主啊，求你從天上降下一桌筵席給我們，使它成為我們——我們中先前的人與後來的人——的節慶，並成為來自你的徵象；求你賜我們生計，因為你是最好的供給者。』真主說：『我必使它降臨你們；你們中誰不信，我必以我在全世界未曾懲罰過任何其他受造物的懲罰來懲罰他。』

title.en: The Crucifixion Reframed: 'They Did Not Slay Him'
title.zh: 十字架之重構：『他們未曾殺他』

region.en: Jerusalem, place of the crucifixion (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷受難地（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah an-Nisa 4:156-159; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 4:156-159

summary.en: Their saying: 'We have put to death the Messiah, Jesus the son of Mary, the apostle of God.' But they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but he was represented to them as such: and they who disagree concerning him are in doubt; they have no knowledge concerning him, but follow only probable conjecture; and they did not surely kill him — but God took him up to Himself. And there shall be none of the people of the Book but shall believe in him before his death.
summary.zh: 他們說：『我們確已殺害麥西哈爾撒——麥爾彥之子、真主的使者。』他們未曾殺他，也未把他釘十字架上，但他們以為如此；對他有所爭執的人，都陷於疑惑之中——他們不過憑猜測，確未殺他。真主已把他擢升到自己那裡；信奉天經的人，在他死去之前，都必定信他。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; a doctrinally central divergence from Christian accounts; presented as text, not as a religious claim; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And because of their unbelief and their strong imputing to Maryam a terrible falsehood, and their saying, 'We have slain the Messiah, Jesus the son of Maryam, the apostle of God.' Yet they slew him not, and they crucified him not, but he was represented to them as such; and they who differed concerning him were in doubt: they had no certain knowledge of him, but only followed an opinion; and they did not really kill him. But God took him up to Himself: and God is mighty and wise. And there shall be none of the people of the Book, but shall believe in him before his death: and on the day of resurrection he shall be a witness against them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 4:156-158 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Qur'an 4:159 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 又因為他們不信，並因他們對瑪利亞加以嚴重的誣衊，且因他們說：『我們確已殺死了真主的使者、瑪利亞之子麥西哈耶穌。』然而他們並沒有殺死他，也沒有把他釘死在十字架上，只是使他對他們顯得如此；那些對他意見分歧的人，確在懷疑之中：他們對他並無確切的知識，只是追隨一種猜想；他們並沒有真正殺死他。但真主把他提升到自己那裡：真主是萬能的，是至睿的。信奉天經的人中，沒有一個不在他死前信仰他的：在復活之日，他將作證反對他們。

title.en: Yunus and the Fish: Three Lamps in Darkness
title.zh: 優努斯與大魚：幽暗中的三重黑暗

region.en: Open sea near Nineveh (symbolic pin at Mosul)
region.zh: 尼尼微附近海域（象徵性定位於摩蘇爾）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs 21:87-88, 37:139-148, 10:98; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Suras 21, 37, 10

summary.en: Dhun-Nun flees like a slave into a laden ship; lots are cast and he is of the losers; the fish swallows him. In the triple darkness — of the sea, of the fish, of the night — he cries: 'There is no God but Thou: glory be to Thee: I have done evil.' 'We heard him and delivered him from his grief; and thus do We deliver the faithful.' And God cast him on the dry land; and he had passed by a hundred thousand, or more, of his people: and they believed, and We gave them the enjoyment of this life.
summary.zh: 帶魚的優努斯如奴僕般逃入滿載之船；拈鬮他被中；大魚吞之。三重黑暗——海、魚、夜——他呼喊：『除你外，別無神明；榮耀歸你；我實行不義。』『我們應答他，救他脫離憂患；我如此拯救信士。』主使登岸，並經過他的十萬或更多的族人：他們歸信，我賜他們享受。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation; Jonah is the only prophet to whom a whole surah is not named but appears in the Qur'an with a whole sura named after him.

passages.text: And Dzunnun fled like a runaway slave, and went on board a ship fully laden, and they drew lots, and he was of the losers; and the fish swallowed him, and he was worthy of blame. Had he not been of those who glorify God, he had remained in its belly until the day when men shall be raised from the dead.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 37:140-144 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 而祖努恩像逃亡的奴僕一樣逃走，登上了一艘滿載的船，他們抽籤，他卻是失敗者之一；大魚吞了他，他本是該受責備的。若不是他屬於那些讚頌真主的人，他必留在魚腹中，直到世人從死裡復活的那一日。

passages.text: And Yunus, remember him, when he went away in anger and supposed We had no power over him; and he cried out in darkness, 'There is no God but Thou: glory be to Thee! I have done amiss.' So We heard him and delivered him from his grief, and thus do We deliver the faithful. And We cast him on the bare shore, and he was sick; and We caused a gourd-tree to grow up over him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 21:87-88 and 37:145-146 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你當記念優努斯，那時他忿怒地離去，以為我們對他沒有能力；他在黑暗中呼喊說：『除你之外，別無真主：讚頌歸於你！我確已犯了過錯。』於是我們聽了他的呼求，救他脫離了他的憂愁，我們如此拯救信士。我們把他拋在荒涼的岸上，他正患病；我們使一棵葫蘆樹在他上面生長。

passages.text: And We sent him on a mission to a hundred thousand men, or to a greater number; and they believed, and We gave them the enjoyment of this life for a season. Why hath there not been one city, which on its believing might have reaped the blessing of its faith? — the people of Yunus believed not until they had seen a grievous chastisement; and only Jonah was an exception.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 10:98 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我們派遣他使命於十萬人，或更多的人；他們歸信了，我們使他們享受今世的生活，直到一個時期。為何沒有一座城市，在其歸信時曾收穫其信仰的福澤呢？——優努斯的族人直到看見嚴厲的懲罰才歸信；唯有優努斯是例外。

title.en: Ayyub: The Cry of the Afflicted and the Fountain
title.zh: 安優卜：受苦者的呼喊與泉水

region.en: Land of Uz / Hawran (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 烏茲地／浩蘭（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs 21:83-84, 38:41-44; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Suras 21:83-84 and 38:41-44

summary.en: Ayyub cries to his Lord: 'Evil hath touched me; and Thou art the most merciful of the merciful.' 'We heard him and relieved him of the evil which was on him; and We restored to him his family, and, with them, others of his race, in mercy from Us and a warning to those who serve Us.' And remember Our servant Ayyub, when he cried to his Lord, 'Satan hath touched me with labour and suffering.' 'Strike the earth with thy foot: here is a wash to drink, and cool to bathe in.' And We gave him his family, and the like of them with them — a mercy from Us, and a warning to the understanding.
summary.zh: 安優卜呼其主：『災害已觸及我；你是最慈的施恩者。』『我們應答他，除去其身上的災害；並賜還其家眷，且加以同類者——出於我的恩慈，也是侍奉者的記念。』又念僕人安優卜：『魔鬼以勞苦與災害加於我。』『你用腳踏地：這裡有洗滌的涼水可浴。』我賜還其家眷，並加以同類者——這是我的恩慈，是有悟者的記念。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation; the tafsir tradition fills the Qur'anic brevity with the length of Job's affliction.

passages.text: And remember Our servant Ayyub, when he cried to his Lord, 'The evil one hath touched me with toil and weariness.' We said, 'Strike the earth with thy foot: here is a wash to drink, and cool to bathe in.' And We gave him his family, and the like of them with them, in Our mercy, and as a memorial to men of understanding.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 38:41-43 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你當記念我們的僕人阿優卜，那時他向他的主呼喊說：『惡魔以勞苦和疲憊觸及了我。』我們說：『你用腳踏地：這裡有可飲的洗滌之水，也有可沐浴的清涼。』我們以我們的慈憫，並作為對有理解力之人的記念，賜還他的家屬，以及與他們相似的人。

passages.text: And Ayyub cried to his Lord, 'Evil hath afflicted me, and Thou art the most merciful of the merciful.' And We heard him, and relieved him of the evil under which he laboured; and We restored to him his family, and doubled their number in Our mercy, and as a warning to those who serve Us. And take in thy hand a bundle of rushes and strike therewith, and thou shalt not violate thine oath; for We found him patient: an excellent servant shall he be; for he turned himself towards Us.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 21:83-84 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Qur'an 38:44 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿優卜向他的主呼喊說：『災難確已降臨於我，你是最慈憫的慈憫者。』我們聽了他的呼求，解除他所承受的災難；我們以我們的慈憫，並作為對事奉我們之人的警戒，賜還他的家屬，並使他們的人數加倍。你當手中拿一束燈心草，用它擊打，你便不違背你的誓言；因為我們發現他是堅忍的：一個優秀的僕人；因為他歸向我們。

title.en: Idris: We Raised Him to a High Station
title.zh: 易德里斯：主把他擢升到高處

region.en: Land of the antediluvian prophets (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 洪水前諸先知之地（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs Maryam 19:56-57, al-Anbiya 21:85-86; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 19:56-57

summary.en: Make mention of Idris in the Book; he was a just man and a prophet, and We raised him to a high place. And Ishmael, and Idris, and Dhul-Kifl — all were of the patient: and We made them enter into Our mercy, for they were of the righteous.
summary.zh: 在經中提及易德里斯；他是正直者，是先知；我把他擢升到一個高處。並易司馬儀、易德里斯、左勒蓋爾菲爾——他們都是堅忍者；我使他們進入我的恩慈，因為他們是正直者。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; Idris is identified with Enoch in the tafsir tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And make a mention of Idris in the Book; he was a just person and a prophet; and We took him up into a high place. And we said, 'O Idris, enter into the mercy of thy Lord.' And remember Ishmael, and Idris, and Dhul-Kifl: all were of the patient: and We made them enter into Our mercy, for they were of the righteous.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 19:56-57 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Qur'an 21:85-86 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你當在經典中提及伊德里斯；他是一個正直的人，也是一位先知；我們把他提升到一個崇高的地方。我們說：『伊德里斯啊，你當進入你主的慈憫之中。』你當記念易司馬儀、伊德里斯和祖勒基弗勒：他們都是堅忍者：我們使他們進入我們的慈憫之中，因為他們是行善者。

title.en: The Companions of the Elephant
title.zh: 象軍之眾

region.en: Mecca, year of the Elephant (literal pin)
region.zh: 麥加，象年（實際定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-Fil 105 (Meccan, among the earliest); Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 105

summary.en: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord dealt with the army of the Elephant? Did He not confuse their plans, and turn them into dust-wind? And He sent against them birds in flocks, clay-stones of baked earth, which He cast upon them: and He made them like stubble eaten by cattle.
summary.zh: 你豈未見你的主怎樣處理象軍？他破壞他們的計謀，化為糠粃；並遣群鳥襲之，投以燒結的陶土之石，使眾人如被嚼的草料。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; this is the episode that sets the year of Muhammad's birth; public-domain translation.

passages.text: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord dealt with the army of the Elephant? Did He not make their design go wrong? And He sent against them birds in flocks; clay-stones of baked earth, which He cast upon them; and He made them like stubble eaten by cattle.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 105 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你豈未見你的主怎樣處置象軍呢？難道他沒有使他們的計謀歸於失敗嗎？他差遣成群的飛鳥去攻擊他們；鳥銜著黏土燒成的石塊，向他們投擲；於是使他們如同被牲畜吃剩的殘梗。

title.en: Haman's Tower to Reach the God of Musa
title.zh: 哈曼的高塔：欲登穆薩之神

region.en: Egypt, mud-brick tower of Pharaoh (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 埃及法老的泥磚高塔（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs 28:38, 40:36-37; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Suras 28:38 and 40:36-37

summary.en: Pharaoh says: 'O nobles, I know not that ye have any god beside me: light a fire for me, O Haman, to bake clay, and build me a tower, that I may mount up to the god of Moses, for verily I think him a liar.' And the arrogant designs of Pharaoh in the land, and his perversion of justice, are those on whom God sets the evil; 'O Haman, build me a tower, that I may reach the highways — the highways of the heavens, that I may look upon the God of Moses; for verily I think him a liar.' Thus is made fair-seeming to Pharaoh the evil of his deeds, and he is turned from the way; and the designs of Pharaoh end only in loss.
summary.zh: 法老說：『眾卿啊，除我外，我不知你們另有神明；哈曼啊，為我點火燒磚，為我築一高塔，好登穆薩之神那裡——我認他是撒謊者。』並法老在國中的暴行與偏私——真主使之自負其罪；『哈曼啊，為我築塔，使我達到天路，去看穆薩之神。』法老惡行被美化，被誘離正道；法老的計謀終歸滅亡。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation; the tower episode parallels the Babel legend and is unique to the Qur'anic Haman.

passages.text: And Pharaoh said, 'O nobles, I know not that ye have any god besides me: light me a fire, O Haman, to bake clay, and build me a tower, that I may mount up to the god of Moses, for verily I think that he is of the liars.' And the arrogance which Pharaoh and his host practised in the land, and his perversion of justice, is that on which God shall set the evil.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 28:38 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 法老說：『眾首領啊，我知道除我之外，你們別無神靈。哈曼啊，你為我燒火製磚，為我建築一座高塔，好讓我攀登到穆薩的神那裏，因為我確信他是一個說謊的人。』法老和他的軍隊在地方上妄自尊大，以及他顛倒是非，正是真主將要降下災禍的緣由。

passages.text: And Pharaoh said, 'O Haman, build me a tower, that I may reach the pathways — the pathways of the heavens — that I may look upon the God of Moses, for verily I think him to be a liar.' And thus was made fair-seeming to Pharaoh the evil of his deeds, and he was turned away from the path of God: and the designs of Pharaoh led only to ruin.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 40:36-37 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 法老說：『哈曼啊，你為我建築一座高塔，好讓我到達那些道路——諸天的道路——好讓我仰望穆薩的神，因為我確信他是一個說謊的人。』就這樣，法老惡行的醜惡在他眼中被美化，他背離了真主的道路；法老的計謀只招致毀滅。

title.en: The Believer of the City's Farthest Quarter
title.zh: 城中遠端歸信者

region.en: Unnamed city of the warned (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 被警告的無名之城（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah Ya-Sin 36:13-29; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 36:13-29

summary.en: We send two warners, and they charge them with falsehood; then We send a third, and they say, 'Verily we are sent to you.' 'Ye are only men like ourselves.' 'The God of Mercy hath sent us — obey us.' They accuse them of augury; and a man comes running from the farthest part of the city: 'O my people, believe the messengers.' The people answer that they will surely stone them; the believer asks that he be raised among the righteous — 'Enter thou Paradise! He said, Would that men knew what my Lord hath forgiven me, and hath made me one of the honoured!'
summary.zh: 主遣二使者警誡，反遭斥為謊者；再遣第三位，說：『我們確被遣於你們。』『你們不過與我們相同的人。』『至慈的主遣我們——當順從我們。』人們斥為兇兆；一男子自城中最遠之處跑來：『我的族人啊，當信使者。』人們欲投石；歸信者求立於善人之中——『入樂園吧！』他說：『但願人們知道，我的主赦了我，並使我成為榮貴者。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the 'believer of Ya-Sin' is a favourite qisas figure; public-domain translation.

passages.text: Set forth to them as an example the inhabitants of the city, when the apostles came to it. When We sent two apostles to them and they charged them with imposture, We reinforced them with a third; and they said, 'We are sent to you of God.' They said, 'Ye are but men like us; the God of Mercy hath not sent anything: ye do nothing but lie.' They said, 'Our Lord knoweth that we are sent on a mission to you: and our duty is only plain preaching.' The inhabitants said, 'We augur evil from you: if ye desist not, we will surely stone you, and a grievous punishment shall ye receive from us.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 36:13-18 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你以城中居民為例向他們講述，當時使者們來到那城。當我派遣兩位使者到他們那裏，而他們指控二人為騙子時，我以第三位使者增強他們；他們說：『我們是奉真主之命被派遣到你們這裏來的。』他們說：『你們不過是和我們一樣的凡人；至慈的主並未降下任何事物：你們只是在說謊。』他們說：『我們的主知道我們確是奉命派遣到你們這裏來的：我們的職責只是明白地傳達。』城中居民說：『我們從你們身上看出凶兆：你們若不止息，我們必用石頭砸死你們，你們必遭受我們嚴厲的懲罰。』

passages.text: They said, 'Your augury is with yourselves: if ye be warned, will ye be warned? Ye are a headstrong people.' And a man came running from the farthest part of the city, and said, 'O my people, believe the apostles: believe him who is not solicitous to be rewarded.' The people said, 'We forebode evil from you: if ye cease not, we will stone you, and a grievous punishment shall befall you at our hands.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 36:19-26 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們說：『你們的凶兆在於你們自身：你們若受警告，難道會受警告嗎？你們是冥頑不靈的民眾。』有一個人從城的最遠處奔跑而來，說：『我的族人啊，你們當信奉使者們：信奉那不求報酬的人。』眾人說：『我們從你們身上預感到凶兆：你們若不止息，我們必用石頭砸死你們，你們必遭受我們嚴厲的懲罰。』

passages.text: It was said to the believer, 'Enter thou into the Garden.' He said, 'Would to God that my people had known of that for which my Lord hath forgiven me, and hath made me one of the honoured!' And after him We did not send down any host from heaven upon his people, nor was it meet that We should.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 36:26-29 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有人對那位信士說：『你進入樂園吧。』他說：『但願我的族人知道我的主為我赦免了什麼，並使我成為受尊榮者之一！』在他之後，我沒有降下任何天兵去對付他的族人，我也無需那樣做。

title.en: Hannah Weeps and Vows: The Birth of Samuel
title.zh: 哈拿泣而立願：撒母耳出生

region.en: Shiloh, tent of meeting
region.zh: 示羅，會幕

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Samuel 1:1-28, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Hannah, barren and provoked yearly by her rival, weeps at Shiloh and vows her son to the LORD 'no razor shall come on his head'. Eli the priest takes her moving lips for drunkenness; she answers with dignity. Samuel — 'asked of God' — is born, weaned, and lent to the LORD all the days of his life.
summary.zh: 不育的哈拿年年受對頭激動，在示羅哭求並許願將子歸耶和華「不用剃刀剃他的頭」。祭司以利見其嘴唇動而以為醉；她尊嚴作答。撒母耳——「向神求來的」——出生斷奶，終身借與耶和華。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Read as Rosh Hashanah haftarah.

passages.text: And she vowed a vow, and said: 'O LORD of hosts, if Thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of Thy handmaid, and remember me, and not forget Thy handmaid, but wilt give unto Thy handmaid a man-child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 1:11 (public domain).
passages.zh: 她許願說：「萬軍之耶和華啊，你若垂顧婢女的苦情，記念我，不忘記婢女，賜婢女一個男孩，我必將他終身歸與耶和華，不用剃頭刀剃他的頭。」

passages.text: Eli charged her: 'How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee.' Hannah answered: 'No, my lord; I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit... I have poured out my soul before the LORD.' 'Go in peace', he said, 'and the God of Israel grant thy petition'. When Samuel was born she named him 'because I have asked him of the LORD'; at weaning she brought him with sacrifices to Shiloh and left him with Eli, and 'the child ministered unto the LORD'. Paraphrase of 1 Samuel 1:14-28 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of 1 Samuel 1:14-28 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 以利責備她說：「你要醉到幾時呢？你應該戒酒。」哈拿回答說：「不，我主啊；我是心裡愁苦的婦人……我在耶和華面前傾心吐意。」他說：「你可以平平安安地回去，願以色列的神允准你向祂所求的。」撒母耳出生後，她給他起名，說「因為我從耶和華那裡求來的」；斷奶的時候，她帶著祭物領他到示羅，把他留在以利那裡，「那孩子就在耶和華面前事奉」。改寫自《撒母耳記上》1:14-28（JPS 1917）；並非逐字照錄。

title.en: My Heart Rejoiceth in the LORD: The Song of Hannah
title.zh: 我心因耶和華快樂：哈拿之歌

region.en: Shiloh, tent of meeting
region.zh: 示羅，會幕

period: Composed c. 10th-9th c. BCE (recorded 1 Samuel 2); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Samuel 2:1-10, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Hannah's victory-poem on reversal — the barren bears seven, the full hire themselves out for bread; 'the bows of the mighty men are broken... He raiseth up the poor out of the dust... to make them inherit the throne of glory' — the theological key to the rise of the house of David, echoed in the Magnificat.
summary.zh: 哈拿的得勝詩論逆轉——不生育的生七子，飽足的反作佣人；「勇士的弓都已折斷……他從灰塵裡抬舉貧寒人……使他們與榮耀的寶座同分」——大衛家興起之神學鑰句，尊主頌所仿。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: The bows of the mighty men are broken; and they that stumbled are girded with strength. They that were full have hired out themselves for bread; and they that were hungry have ceased; while the barren hath borne seven; and she that hath many children hath languished. The LORD killeth, and maketh alive; He bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 2:4-6 (public domain).
passages.zh: 勇士的弓都已折斷；跌倒的人以力量束腰。素來飽足的，反作傭人求食；飢餓的，再不飢餓；不生育的，生了七個兒子；多有兒女的，反倒衰微。耶和華使人死，也使人活；使人下陰間，也使人往上升。

title.en: The Ark in the House of Dagon
title.zh: 約櫃在大袞廟中

region.en: Ashdod, temple of Dagon
region.zh: 亞實突，大袞廟

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Samuel 4:1-7:2, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Israel carries the ark into battle 'as a talisman' and is routed; the ark is captured, Eli dies hearing the news, and the child's mother names him Ichabod — 'the glory is departed'. In Ashdod the Philistines set the ark beside Dagon: morning after morning the idol is found fallen, then broken before the ark, and tumors plague the cities until the ark is sent back with guilt-offerings of golden emerods and mice.
summary.zh: 以色列攜約櫃上陣「以為護符」而大敗；約櫃被擄，以利聞訊而死，產婦為子命名以迦博——「榮耀離開以色列了」。在亞實突，非利士人將約櫃置於大袞旁：日日清早神像撲倒，斷碎於櫃前，瘤災遍及諸城，直至以金痔金鼠為賠罪物送回。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And when they of Ashdod arose early on the morrow, behold, Dagon was fallen upon his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD. And they took Dagon, and set him in his place again. And when they arose early on the morrow morning, behold, Dagon was fallen upon his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD; and the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands were cut off upon the threshold; only the trunk of Dagon was left to him.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 5:3-4 (public domain).
passages.zh: 次日，亞實突人清早起來，見大袞仆倒在耶和華的約櫃前，臉伏於地。他們就把大袞抬回，仍立在原處。又次日清早起來，見大袞仆倒在耶和華的約櫃前，臉伏於地，並且大袞的頭和兩手都在門檻上折斷，只剩下大袞的殘體。

passages.text: The hand of the LORD was heavy on Ashdod and on its territory, destroying them with tumors; Ashdod, Gath, and Ekron in turn were smitten, and Ekron cried to send the ark away 'lest it bring us death'. The Philistine priests and diviners devised the return: a new cart with two milch kine, golden images of the tumors and of the mice 'that mar the land', and a trespass-offering. The kine lowed all the way to Beth-shemesh; the men of Beth-shemesh, who looked into the ark, were smitten — and the ark came to rest at Kirjath-jearim in the house of Abinadab. Paraphrase of 1 Samuel 5:6-6:21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of 1 Samuel 5:6-6:21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 耶和華的手重重加在亞實突和其境內，使他們生痔瘡，毀壞他們；亞實突、迦特、以革倫相繼受擊，以革倫人呼喊要把約櫃送走，「免得它害死我們」。非利士的祭司和占卜的商議如何送回：一輛新車，兩隻有乳的母牛，照著痔瘡和「毀壞田地」的老鼠所做的金像，以及贖愆祭。那兩隻母牛一路叫著直走到伯示麥；伯示麥人因窺看約櫃而被擊殺——約櫃最後停在基列耶琳亞比拿達的家中。改寫自《撒母耳記上》5:6-6:21（JPS 1917）；並非逐字照錄。

title.en: Saul Seeks Asses and Finds a Kingdom
title.zh: 掃羅尋驢反得國

region.en: Ramah and Mizpah, land of Benjamin
region.zh: 拉瑪與米斯巴，便雅憫地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Samuel 9-10, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Kish's son Saul, taller by a head than any in Israel, goes searching for strayed asses and arrives at Samuel's town by providence. Samuel, told by God the day before, seats him above the guests, pours oil on his head, and predicts the signs on his road home. The spirit comes on him among the prophets; at Mizpah he is drawn by lot, hiding among the baggage, and acclaimed king: 'God save the king!'
summary.zh: 便雅憫人基士之子掃羅，身量比眾民高過一頭，為尋失驢而至撒母耳之城，實為天意。撒母耳前夜得神諭，請他坐客位之上，以膏油澆其頭，並預言歸途諸兆。靈感動他在先知中說話；米斯巴掣籤被指出，藏於器械中，眾民呼喊「願王萬歲！」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then Samuel took a vial of oil, and poured it upon his head, and kissed him, and said: 'Is it not because the LORD hath anointed thee to be prince over His inheritance? ... And the spirit of the LORD will come mightily upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 10:1, 6 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 撒母耳就拿一瓶膏油，倒在他頭上，與他親嘴，說：「這不是因為耶和華膏你作祂產業的君嗎？……耶和華的靈必大大感動你，你就與他們一同受感說話，你要變為另一個人。」

title.en: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice: Saul and Agag
title.zh: 聽命勝於獻祭：掃羅與亞甲

region.en: Gilgal, land of Israel
region.zh: 吉甲，以色列地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Samuel 15, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Saul is sent to destroy Amalek utterly but spares Agag and the best of the flocks 'to sacrifice'. Samuel's rebirth of the prophetic word — 'Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt-offerings... Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice' — ends Saul's dynasty: 'thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD hath rejected thee'. Samuel hews Agag in pieces before the LORD at Gilgal and mourns for Saul 'unto his dying day'.
summary.zh: 掃羅奉命滅盡亞瑪力人，卻存留亞甲與上好的牛羊「要獻與耶和華」。撒母耳重申預言之道——「耶和華喜悅燔祭和平安祭，豈如喜悅人聽從他的話呢……聽命勝於獻祭」——掃羅王朝至此終結：「你既厭棄耶和華的命令，耶和華也厭棄你」。撒母耳在吉甲耶和華面前將亞甲斬為碎片，為掃羅悲傷「直到死的日子」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Amalek becomes the recurring symbol of genocidal enmity in Jewish memory; record states text only.

passages.text: And Samuel said: 'Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt-offerings and sacrifices, as in hearkening to the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams. For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as idolatry and teraphim. Because thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, He hath also rejected thee from being king.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 15:22-23 (public domain).
passages.zh: 撒母耳說：「耶和華喜悅燔祭和平安祭，豈如喜悅人聽從耶和華的話呢？看哪，聽命勝於獻祭，順從勝於公羊的脂油。悖逆的罪與行邪術的罪相等；頑梗的罪與拜虛神和偶像的罪相同。你既厭棄耶和華的命令，耶和華也厭棄你作王。」

title.en: The Oil of Bethlehem: David Chosen from the Fields
title.zh: 伯利恆的膏油：田間被選的大衛

region.en: Bethlehem, Judah
region.zh: 伯利恆，猶大

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Samuel 16, JPS Tanakh 1917
