summary.en: Sent to Bethlehem with a heifer to anoint a son of Jesse, Samuel passes seven sons before the LORD and is corrected: 'the LORD seeth not as man seeth... the LORD looketh on the heart'. David, the youngest, is fetched from the sheep; 'and the spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward'. The same chapter has the distressed Saul's servants call for a man 'skilful in playing a harp' — David's double call: oil and harp.
summary.zh: 撒母耳持牛犢往伯利恆膏耶西之子，七子一一經過皆非；神糾正：「耶和華不像人看人……人是看外貌，耶和華是看內心。」幼子大衛自羊圈中被召；「從那日起，耶和華的靈就感動大衛」。同章記受攪擾的掃羅之僕薦「善於彈琴」者——大衛的雙重蒙召：膏油與琴。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to. And the LORD said: 'Arise, anoint him; for this is he.' Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren; and the spirit of the LORD came mightily upon David from that day forward.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 16:12-13 (public domain).
passages.zh: 耶西就打發人叫他來。他面色光紅，雙目清秀，容貌俊美。耶和華說：「起來，膏他，因為這就是他。」撒母耳就用角裡的膏油，在他諸兄中膏了他；從這日起，耶和華的靈就大大感動大衛。

title.en: Five Smooth Stones: David and Goliath
title.zh: 五塊光滑石子：大衛與歌利亞

region.en: Valley of Elah, Judean lowlands
region.zh: 以拉谷，猶大低地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Samuel 17, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: For forty days the giant of Gath defies Israel's ranks. The shepherd-boy David, sent with provisions, hears the taunt and volunteers: 'The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion... He will deliver me'. He refuses Saul's armour, chooses five smooth stones from the brook, fells Goliath with one stone, and cuts off his head with the giant's own sword — while the Philistine army flees.
summary.zh: 四十日之久，迦特巨人向以色列軍陣罵陣。送糧的牧童大衛聞言自薦：「耶和華救我脫離獅子和熊的爪，也必救我脫離這非利士人的手。」他拒絕掃羅的戰衣，自溪中揀五塊光滑石子，一石擊倒歌利亞，以巨人自己的刀割其首——非利士全軍潰逃。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Folk-epic of the small against the giant; cross-tradition giant-slayer cluster.

passages.text: And David said unto the Philistine: 'Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast taunted.' ... And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead; and the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell upon his face to the earth.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 17:45, 49 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 大衛對那非利士人說：「你來攻擊我，是靠著刀槍和銅戟；我來攻擊你，是靠著萬軍之耶和華的名，就是你所怒罵帶領以色列軍隊的神。」……大衛用手從囊中掏出一塊石子來，用機弦甩去，打中非利士人的額；石子進入額內，他就仆倒，面伏於地。

title.en: Jonathan's Soul Was Knit to David
title.zh: 約拿單的心與大衛深相契合

region.en: Gibeah of Saul, land of Benjamin
region.zh: 掃羅的基比亞，便雅憫地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Samuel 18:1-4; 19; 20, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The prince strips himself of robe, armour, sword, and bow and gives them to David — 'and it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul'. Saul hurls his spear; Jonathan shields David with the sign of the missing arrows at the field of stones: 'hasten thou, be not stayed'.
summary.zh: 王子將外袍、戰衣、刀、弓、腰帶都給了大衛——「大衛與掃羅說完了話，約拿單的心與大衛的心深相契合，約拿單愛他如同愛自己的性命」。掃羅掄槍刺他；約拿單在田野以射箭之號護衛大衛：「你快跑吧，不要停留。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Jonathan caused David to swear again, for the love that he had to him; for he loved him as he loved his own soul. ... And Jonathan said unto David: 'The LORD be with thee, as He hath been with my father.' ... And Jonathan gave his weapons unto his lad, and said unto his lad: 'Go, carry them to the city.' ... As soon as the lad was gone, David arose out of a place toward the south, and fell on his face to the ground, and bowed himself three times; and they kissed one another, and wept one with another, until David exceeded.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 20:17, 41-42 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 約拿單因愛大衛如同愛自己的性命，就使他再起誓。……約拿單對大衛說：「願耶和華與你同在，如同從前與我父親同在一樣。」……約拿單將自己的兵器交給童子，對童子說：「你拿到城裡去。」……童子一去，大衛就從磐石的南邊起來，俯伏在地，拜了三拜；二人親嘴，彼此哭泣，大衛哭得更慟。

title.en: The Massacre at Nob: Doeg the Edomite
title.zh: 挪伯的屠殺：多益

region.en: Nob, city of priests
region.zh: 挪伯，祭司之城

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Samuel 21-22, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Fleeing, David begs the shewbread from Ahimelech the priest 'as if common' and takes Goliath's sword. Doeg the Edomite, Saul's chief herdsman, sees and reports. Saul orders the priests slain; his servants refuse, and Doeg 'turned and fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons'. Abiathar alone escapes to David, bringing the ephod — and David's guilt: 'I have occasioned the death of all the persons of thy father's house.'
summary.zh: 逃亡的大衛向祭司亞希米勒求「平常的」陳設餅，並取歌利亞的刀。掃羅的司牧長以東人多益目擊而告發。掃羅命殺祭司；僕人不從，多益「伸刀殺了那日八十五人」。唯亞比亞他逃奔大衛，攜以弗得同來——大衛自認其咎：「你父的全家喪命，都是因我的緣故。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the king said to Doeg: 'Turn thou, and fall upon the priests.' And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod. And Nob, the city of the priests, smote he with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, and oxen and asses and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 22:18-19 (public domain).
passages.zh: 王對多益說：「你轉過去，殺那祭司吧。」以東人多益就轉過去殺那祭司，那日殺了穿細麻布以弗得的八十五人。又用刀將祭司城挪伯中的男女、孩童、吃奶的，和牛、驢、羊盡都殺滅。

title.en: Nabal the Fool and Abigail's Beautiful Judgment
title.zh: 拿八愚頑與亞比該的美麗判斷

region.en: Maon and Carmel, Judean wilderness
region.zh: 瑪雲與迦密，猶大曠野

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Samuel 25, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Rich Nabal — 'the fool' — repulses David's men who had guarded his shearers. David moves to slaughter the house; Abigail intercepts him with two hundred loaves and wine and a speech so wise he blesses 'the God of Israel... who sent thee this day to meet me': 'blessed be thy counsel, and blessed be thou'. Nabal's heart dies within him; ten days later 'the LORD smote Nabal, that he died', and David takes Abigail to wife.
summary.zh: 富有的拿八——「愚頑人」——拒絕曾護其剪羊毛者的大衛之僕。大衛率眾欲滅其家；亞比該攜二百餅與酒迎之，言辭明智，大衛頌「以色列的神……今日打發你迎接我」是稱頌：「你的見識值得稱讚，你也當得稱讚」。拿八魂不附體；十日後「耶和華擊打拿八，他就死了」，大衛娶亞比該。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves, and two bottles of wine, and five sheep ready dressed, and five measures of parched corn, and an hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on asses. And she said unto her servants: 'Go on before me; behold, I come after you.' ... And she fell at his feet, and said: 'Upon me, my lord, upon me let this iniquity be; and let thy handmaid, I pray thee, speak in thine ears.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 25:18-19, 24 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 亞比該急忙將二百餅，兩皮袋酒，五隻收拾好了的羊，五細亞烘好了的穗子，一百葡萄餅，二百無花果餅，都馱在驢上。她對僕人說：「你們前頭走，我隨著你們去。」……亞比該就俯伏在他腳前，說：「我主啊，願這罪歸我；求你容婢女向你進言。」

title.en: The Woman of Endor Raises Samuel
title.zh: 隱多珥的女巫召撒母耳

region.en: Endor, north of Shunem
region.zh: 隱多珥，書念之北

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Samuel 28, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The night before Gilboa, with the LORD silent 'by dreams, or by Urim, or by prophets', a disguised Saul — who had himself purged the mediums — seeks the woman of Endor. She conjures 'a god' and sees 'gods ascending out of the earth'; Samuel comes up as an old man wrapped in a robe and pronounces the doom: 'To-morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me.' Saul falls straightway to the ground, full length, faint with fasting.
summary.zh: 基利波戰前之夜，耶和華「藉夢、或烏陵、或先知」都不回答；曾親自剪除交鬼之人的掃羅喬裝求助於隱多珥的女人。她招「一個神」上來，見「有神從地裡上來」；撒母耳如披衣的老人出現，宣告定命：「明日你和你的眾子必與我在一處。」掃羅立刻仆倒在地，身體僵直，因一夜沒有喫飯。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Necromancy is forbidden by Torah (Deut 18); the narrative presents the episode's ambiguity.

passages.text: And Samuel said to Saul: 'Why hast thou disquieted me, to bring me up?' And Saul answered: 'I am sore distressed; for the Philistines make war against me, and God is departed from me.' And Samuel said: 'Wherefore then dost thou ask of me, seeing the LORD is departed from thee... And tomorrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 28:15-19 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 撒母耳對掃羅說：「你為何攪擾我，把我招上來呢？」掃羅回答說：「我甚窘急；因為非利士人攻擊我，神也離開了我。」撒母耳說：「耶和華既已離開你，你為何還問我呢？……明日你和你眾子必與我同在了。」

title.en: Fallen on Gilboa: Saul's Last Day
title.zh: 基利波山之傾覆：掃羅末日

region.en: Mount Gilboa, Jezreel valley
region.zh: 基利波山，耶斯列谷

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Samuel 31; 2 Samuel 1, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The battle goes against Israel; the archers overtake the king and his three sons die. Wounded by the archers, Saul begs his armour-bearer to slay him, then falls on his own sword. The Philistines fasten his body on the wall of Beth-shan; the men of Jabesh-gilead, remembering his first deed as king, rescue the bodies by night and burn and bury them. David's lament — 'How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!' — and his eulogy of Jonathan crown the king he replaced.
summary.zh: 戰事不利，弓箭手追上王，三子皆亡。掃羅中箭重傷，求拿兵器者刺死不從，遂自伏刀上。非利士人將其屍釘在伯珊城牆；基列雅比人念其首位救民之功，夜間取回屍身焚化而葬。大衛作哀歌——「大英雄何竟死亡！約拿單的弓箭非流敵人的血不退縮」——尊榮他所取代的王。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armour-bearer, and all his men, that same day together. ... And they took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons, and brought them to Jabesh, and burnt their bones there, and buried them under the terebinth in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 31:6, 12-13 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 這樣，掃羅死了，他的三個兒子、拿他兵器的人，以及跟隨他的眾人，都在同一日一同死了。……他們取了掃羅的屍身和他眾子的屍首，送到雅比，在那裡將他們的骸骨焚燒，葬在雅比的篤耨樹下，並且禁食七日。

passages.text: An Amalekite brings the news and claims to have given the death-stroke; David orders him slain for 'saying he had destroyed the LORD's anointed'. Then David laments from the Book of Jashar: 'The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places; how are the mighty fallen... ye mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew'. For Jonathan: 'I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan; very pleasant hast thou been unto me... How are the mighty fallen!' Paraphrase of 2 Samuel 1:1-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of 2 Samuel 1:1-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一個亞瑪力人來報信，自稱是他給了致命的一擊；大衛因他「說自己殺了耶和華的受膏者」而下令將他處死。隨後大衛從《雅煞珥書》哀悼說：「以色列的尊榮者在你的高處被殺；大能者何竟仆倒……基利波山哪，願你無露水。」為約拿單，他說：「我兄約拿單哪，我為你悲傷；你向我何等可親……大能者何竟仆倒！」此為撒母耳記下1:1-27（JPS 1917）之釋義，非逐字引文。

title.en: David Dances Before the Ark of the LORD
title.zh: 大衛在耶和華的約櫃前踴躍跳舞

region.en: Jerusalem, city of David
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，大衛城

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 2 Samuel 6, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Bringing the ark up from Kirjath-jearim on a new cart, Uzzah touches it to steady it and dies 'beside the ark of God'. David fears the LORD's presence and defers the journey; three months later it is carried properly, with sacrifices every six paces. The king leaps and dances before the ark in a linen ephod — Michal's scorn at 'the base fellow exposing himself' earns her childlessness.
summary.zh: 自基列耶琳以新車運櫃，烏撒扶櫃而立斃「在神的約櫃旁」。大衛懼耶和華之臨，中止行程；三月後以正法抬行，每六步獻祭。君王穿細麻布以弗得在櫃前踴躍跳舞——米甲譏其「露體」如愚妄人，因而無子到死。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And it was so, that, when they that bore the ark of the LORD had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fatling. And David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was girded with a linen ephod. So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting, and with the sound of the horn.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 2 Samuel 6:13-15 (public domain).
passages.zh: 抬耶和華約櫃的人走了六步，他就獻上一隻牛和一隻肥畜為祭。大衛盡力在耶和華面前跳舞；大衛腰間束著細麻布的以弗得。這樣，大衛和以色列全家歡呼吹角，將耶和華的約櫃抬上來。

title.en: Thou Art the Man: Nathan's Parable of the Ewe Lamb
title.zh: 你就是那人：拿單的羊羔寓言

region.en: Jerusalem, palace of David
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，大衛王宮

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 2 Samuel 11-12, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The king sees Bathsheba bathing, takes her, and has Uriah — loyal soldier of the front lines — killed by his own signed orders 'with the sword of the children of Ammon'. Nathan tells the rich man who took the poor man's one ewe lamb; David's 'the man shall surely die' turns on himself: 'Thou art the man.' The child of the union dies; Solomon is born and 'the LORD loved him'.
summary.zh: 王見拔示巴沐浴而取之，又以其親筆密令使忠誠前線的烏利亞「死在亞捫人的刀下」。拿單以富戶奪貧者唯一羊羔設喻；大衛怒曰「行這事的人該死」，反及其身：「你就是那人。」所生之子死；所羅門生，「耶和華也喜愛他」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Nathan said to David: 'Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel: I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul... wherefore hast thou despised the word of the LORD, to do that which is evil in My sight?'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 2 Samuel 12:7, 9 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 拿單對大衛說：「你就是那個人。耶和華——以色列的神如此說：我膏你作以色列的王，又救你脫離掃羅的手……你為何藐視耶和華的話，行我眼中看為惡的事呢？」

passages.text: The parable: a rich man with many flocks takes a poor neighbour's 'one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and reared... and it lay in his bosom'. David's anger 'was greatly kindled' and he passed the death sentence; Nathan's sentence-echo exposed the king. David confessed 'I have sinned against the LORD'; the penalty fell on the child, who died on the seventh day — while David, having fasted, rose and washed and ate, saying 'he shall not come back to me, but I shall go to him'. Paraphrase of 2 Samuel 12:1-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of 2 Samuel 12:1-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那比喻是：一個富人有許多羊群，卻取了窮鄰居「所買來養活的一隻小母羊羔……那羊羔躺在他懷裡」。大衛的怒氣「大大發作」，判了那人死罪；拿單以判詞的回聲揭露了王。大衛承認「我得罪了耶和華」；刑罰落在孩子身上，孩子於第七日死了——而大衛禁食之後，起來沐浴、進食，說：「他不能回到我這裡來，我卻要往他那裡去。」此為撒母耳記下12:1-24（JPS 1917）之釋義，非逐字引文。

title.en: Absalom in the Oak: The Revolt and the King's Grief
title.zh: 橡樹間的押沙龍：叛亂與王之哀哭

region.en: Forest of Ephraim, east of the Jordan
region.zh: 以法蓮樹林，約旦河東

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 2 Samuel 15-18, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Absalom steals hearts at the gate — 'Thy matters are good... oh that I were judge in the land!' — and has himself acclaimed king at Hebron. David flees over Kidron weeping, his head covered; Absalom's hair catches in the terebinth as his mule passes under, and Joab's darts finish him despite David's own command. The king's cry to the messenger echoes down the ages: 'O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee.'
summary.zh: 押沙龍在城門偷取民心——「你的事有情有理……恨不得我作國中的士師！」——於希伯崙自立為王。大衛蒙頭上基訓逃亡哭泣；押沙龍騎騾經過橡樹下，頭髮被樹枝繞住，約押的槍了結他——雖王曾嚴令存其性命。王對報信者的哭聲流傳千古：「押沙龍，我兒，我兒！恨不得我替你死。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the man said unto Joab: 'Behold, I saw Absalom hanging in a terebinth.' ... And Joab took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the terebinth. ... And Absalom took, and cast him into a great pit in the forest, and raised a very great heap of stones over him.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 2 Samuel 18:10, 14, 17 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 那人對約押說：「看哪，我看見押沙龍懸在一棵篤耨香樹上。」……約押手拿三支短槍，趁押沙龍還活著懸在篤耨香樹上，就刺透了他的心。……他們把押沙龍丟在林中一個大坑裡，又在他身上堆起一大堆石頭。

passages.text: David sat between the two gates while the watchman announced the victory. When he heard the son was dead he went up to the chamber over the gate and wept: 'O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!' Joab rebuked the shamed army — 'thou lovest thine enemies, and hatest thy friends' — and the king arose and sat in the gate. Paraphrase of 2 Samuel 18:24-33; 19:1-8 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of 2 Samuel 18:24-33; 19:1-8 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 大衛坐在兩門之間，守望的人報告了勝利。他聽見兒子死了，就上到城門上的樓閣哭泣說：「我兒押沙龍啊，我兒，我兒押沙龍啊！但願我替你死，押沙龍我兒，我兒啊！」約押責備那蒙羞的軍隊——「你愛你的仇敵，恨你的朋友」——於是王起來，坐在城門口。此為撒母耳記下十八章24至33節、十九章1至8節（JPS 1917）之改述，非逐字引用。

title.en: A Man in White Asks About Islam, Faith, and the Hour
title.zh: 白衣人問：伊斯蘭、信仰與末日

region.en: Medina, among the seated Companions (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那眾聖門弟子之間（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari (d. 870), Kitab al-Iman, no. 50; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Iman, no. 50 — the Hadith of Jibril, narrated by Umar ibn al-Khattab

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: A man with intensely white clothes and intensely black hair, with no trace of journey, comes and sits knee to knee before the Prophet and asks: What is Islam? What is faith? What is excellence (ihsan)? When will the Hour come? The Prophet answers each in turn; the questioner affirms and vanishes. 'That was Jibril, come to teach you your religion.'
summary.zh: 一白衣黑髮之人前來，衣服極白、頭髮極黑，不見旅塵。他與先知膝對膝而坐，問：何為伊斯蘭？何為信仰？何為至善？末日何時？先知逐一作答；問者認可而離去。『那是吉布里勒，來教你們你們的宗教。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original for comparative study, not a religious claim.

passages.text: While we were sitting with the Messenger of God one day, a man came whose clothes were intensely white and whose hair was intensely black; no sign of travel could be seen on him, and none of us knew him. He sat down close to the Prophet, rested his knees against his knees, and placed his palms on his thighs, and said: 'O Muhammad, tell me about Islam.' The Prophet said: 'Islam is that you testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, that you keep up the prayer, pay the poor-due, fast Ramadan, and make the pilgrimage to the House if you are able to find a way.' The man said, 'You have spoken truly.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Iman, no. 50; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一天，我們正坐在真主的使者身旁，忽然來了一個人，他的衣服極白，頭髮極黑；在他身上看不出旅行的跡象，我們中也沒有人認識他。他坐到先知近旁，把雙膝抵著他的雙膝，把雙掌放在自己的大腿上，說道：「穆罕默德啊，告訴我什麼是伊斯蘭。」先知說：「伊斯蘭就是：你作證除真主外別無神靈，穆罕默德是真主的使者；你謹守禮拜，繳納天課，在齋月封齋，若能找到途徑，就朝覲天房。」那人說：「你說得對。」

passages.text: We were amazed that he asked and confirmed him. Then he said: 'Tell me about faith.' He said: 'That you believe in God, and His angels, and His Books, and His messengers, and the Last Day, and that you believe in the decree, its good and its evil.' He said, 'You have spoken truly. Then tell me about excellence.' He said: 'That you worship God as if you saw Him, for if you do not see Him, He surely sees you.' He said, 'You have spoken truly. Then tell me about the Hour.' He said: 'The one questioned knows no more than the questioner.' He said, 'Then tell me about its signs.' He said: 'That the slave-girl shall give birth to her mistress, and that you will see barefoot, naked, destitute shepherds competing in building tall structures.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Iman, no. 50; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我們很驚訝，他竟發問又加以確認。接著他說：「告訴我什麼是信仰。」他說：「就是你信仰真主、他的天使、他的經典、他的使者，以及末日；你信仰前定，無論其善與其惡。」他說：「你說得對。那麼告訴我什麼是至善。」他說：「就是你崇拜真主，彷彿你看見他；因為你雖看不見他，他確是看見你的。」他說：「你說得對。那麼告訴我關於那時辰。」他說：「被問的人並不比問的人知道得更多。」他說：「那麼告訴我它的徵兆。」他說：「就是婢女將生下她的女主，你將看見赤腳、裸身、貧困的牧羊人競相建造高樓。」

passages.text: Then he went away, and I stayed some while. Then he said: 'O Umar, do you know who the questioner was?' I said, 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'That was Jibril, who came to you to teach you your religion.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Iman, no. 50; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 然後他離去了，我停留了一會兒。接著他說：「歐麥爾啊，你知道那問者是誰嗎？」我說：「真主和他的使者最知道。」他說：「那是吉卜利勒，他來教你們你們的宗教。」

title.en: Three Men and the Rock: Each Calls on His Best Deed
title.zh: 三人與磐石：各以其善行求主

region.en: Mountain cave on a journey (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 山間岩洞（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Buyu', no. 2272; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Buyu', no. 2272 — narrated by Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Three men take shelter in a cave; a boulder rolls down and seals the entrance. None can be released except by prayer for his best deed: the first for his duty to his parents; the second for resisting temptation for God's sake; the third for paying a labourer whose wages grew like the earth's increase. Each prayer moves the rock a little, until they come out walking in the sunlight.
summary.zh: 三人避雨入洞；巨石滾落封住洞口。除非各以一生最佳善行祈求，否則無法出洞：第一人為孝敬父母而求；第二人為敬畏主而守戒；第三人為償還長大如土之息的工錢而求。每次祈禱石移一寸，直至三人在陽光中走出。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: Three men were travelling and were overtaken by rain; they came to a mountain and took shelter in a cave, and a boulder of the mountain rolled down and shut them in. They said to one another, 'Nothing can deliver you from this rock but that you pray to God with some righteous deed that belongs to each of you.' One said: 'O God, I had aged parents, and I never gave my children or my wealth drink before them; I rose one night with milk for them and stood by their heads while they slept — if I did that seeking Thy face, relieve us from this rock.' It moved a hand's breadth from the mouth of the cave.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Buyu', no. 2272; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 三個人正在旅行，遇上了雨；他們來到一座山，躲進一個山洞裡，山上一塊巨石滾落下來，把他們封在裡面。他們彼此說：「沒有什麼能救你們脫離這塊石頭，除非你們各人以自己所行的善功向真主祈求。」一人說：「真主啊，我有年邁的雙親，我從不曾先於他們給我的孩子或我的財物喝水；有一夜，我為他們取來奶，站在他們頭旁，而他們正睡著——如果我這樣做是為尋求你的喜悅，就求你使我們脫離這塊石頭。」那石頭從洞口移開了一手之寬。

passages.text: The second said: 'O God, I loved my cousin as deeply as a man can love a woman, and she refused me save for a great sum of money. I laboured until I gathered it, and when I sat between her thighs she said, Fear God, and do not break the seal except lawfully; and I left her, though she was the dearest of all people to me — if I did that seeking Thy face, relieve us.' It moved two hands' breadths. The third said: 'O God, I hired labourers and paid all but one who went away; I sowed his wage, and it grew into wealth of cattle and sheep and wealth. Then he came and said, O servant of God, pay me my wage; and I pointed to the cattle and sheep and camels: take them all. He thought I mocked him, but I gave him the whole — if I did that seeking Thy face, relieve us.' The rock moved from the mouth of the cave, and they came out walking in the sunlight.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Buyu', no. 2272; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 第二人說：『真主啊，我愛我的堂妹，愛得如同一個男人所能愛一個女人那般深切，而她拒絕我，除非我拿出大筆錢財。我辛勤勞作，直到積攢齊了那筆錢，當我坐在她兩腿之間時，她說：敬畏真主，除非合乎律法，否則不要破壞那封印；我便離開了她，儘管她是我最親愛的人——如果我這樣做是為了尋求祢的喜悅，就請祢解救我們吧。』岩石移動了兩手寬的距離。第三人說：『真主啊，我雇了工人，付清了所有人的工錢，只有一人離去未領；我便把他的工錢拿去耕種，它增長成了牛群、羊群和財富。後來他來了，說：真主的僕人啊，請付給我我的工錢；我便指著那些牛、羊和駱駝說：全都拿去吧。他以為我在嘲弄他，但我把全部都給了他——如果我這樣做是為了尋求祢的喜悅，就請祢解救我們吧。』岩石從洞口移開，他們便走了出來，行走在陽光之下。

title.en: The Woman Punished for a Cat
title.zh: 因貓受罰的女子

region.en: Hereafter visions told in Medina (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那所講的後世異象（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Anbiya, no. 3318 (also Kitab al-Ashriba); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3318 — narrated by Ibn Umar

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The Prophet passes by a woman among the punished of the Hereafter who is holding a cat, keeping it captive, neither feeding it nor letting it eat the vermin of the earth until it dies of hunger. The Prophet is asked whether it is one of the jinn; he answers that it is one of the beings punished for imprisoning a cat — a creature that God had allowed to roam and that she failed to feed or free.
summary.zh: 先知見後世受罰者中一女子，手抱一貓，拘禁之，不餵食，也不放其食地上之蟲，直至餓死。人問：是精靈嗎？先知答：是被懲罰的生靈之一——她拘禁真主所任其自由行走之貓，不餵不縱。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: The Messenger of God passed by a woman who was among the punished of the Hereafter, holding a cat she had tethered. She had neither fed it nor given it water to drink, nor had she freed it to eat the creeping things of the earth, until it died of hunger. He was asked whether it was one of the jinn, and he said that it was one of the jinn? He said, 'It was not a jinni: it was a woman among the punished, punished for a cat she had kept captive — she neither fed it nor gave it drink, nor freed it to eat the creatures of the earth, till it died.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3318; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 真主的使者路過一個屬於後世受懲罰者之列的女人，她懷裡抱著一隻她拴住的貓。她既不餵牠，也不給牠水喝，也不放開牠讓牠吃地上的爬蟲，直到牠餓死。有人問他，那是不是精靈中的一個，他說那是精靈中的一個嗎？他說：『那不是精靈：那是一個屬於受懲罰者之列的女人，因一隻她囚禁的貓而受懲罰——她既不餵牠，也不給牠水喝，也不放開牠讓牠吃地上的生物，直到牠死去。』

title.en: A Dog Licking the Sand: Water for a Thirsty Creature
title.zh: 舔沙之犬：給乾渴生靈一口水

region.en: Desert road between wells (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 井間沙漠道（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Musaqat, no. 2363 (variant: Sahih Muslim); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2363 — narrated by Abu Hurayrah

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: A man on a journey finds a well, descends and drinks, and comes out to see a panting dog licking the moist sand for water. The man takes his shoe, fills it with water, and gives the dog to drink; God thanks him and forgives him. The Companions ask whether there is reward even in beasts — 'There is a reward in every living creature.' A sinful woman of the Israelites is told of in the same telling, forgiven for giving water to a dog.
summary.zh: 一人行路遇井，下井飲水，出井見一犬喘息舔沙覓水。此人以鞋盛水飲犬；主感謝他並赦之。聖門弟子問：畜生也有回賜嗎？——『凡有生命之物皆有回賜。』同傳說以色列人一罪婦，因飲犬水而被赦。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: The Messenger of God said: While a man was walking on a road he became very thirsty, and found a well; he descended into it and drank and came out, and there was a dog panting and licking the moist earth for water. The man said to himself, This dog is as thirsty as I was; so he went down into the well, filled his shoe with water, held it in his mouth, climbed out, and gave the dog to drink. God thanked him for that and forgave him. They said, 'O Messenger of God, is there a reward for us in the animals?' He said: 'In every living creature there is a reward.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2363; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 真主的使者說：一個人走在路上，口渴得厲害，發現了一口井；他下到井裡喝了水，出來時，看見一隻狗喘著氣，舔著濕土找水喝。那人自言自語道：這隻狗渴得和我當初一樣；於是他下到井裡，用鞋子盛滿水，銜在嘴裡，爬了上來，給狗喝。真主為此感謝他，並饒恕了他。他們說：『真主的使者啊，我們在動物身上也有回報嗎？』他說：『在每一個有生命的生靈身上都有回報。』

passages.text: A prostitute among the Israelites was forgiven in the same manner: she saw a dog going round a well, about to die of thirst, drew water in her shoe and gave it to drink; and God forgave her for it.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2363 (variant narrations); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 以色列人中有一個妓女也以同樣的方式得到了饒恕：她看見一隻狗繞著一口井打轉，快要渴死了，便用鞋子汲了水給牠喝；真主因此饒恕了她。

title.en: The Last of the People of Hell
title.zh: 火獄居民之最後者

region.en: Medina, teaching among the Companions (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那聖門弟子中的教導（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6571; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6571 — narrated by Ibn Mas'ud

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The last man to leave the Fire will be brought out on hands and knees, and God will say to him: 'Go and enter Paradise.' He comes and finds it full of people and provision: 'My Lord, I find it full of people and provisions.' 'Would you be content, O son of Adam, with the kingdom of a king of the kings of the world?' 'I would be content, my Lord.' Then God laughs, and the man enters — and finds rivers flowing, food bearing fruit, every conceivable provision. He asks for a door and is given one; he goes out, and is told: 'You have been in captivity and then died; enter into the blessing of Paradise forever.'
summary.zh: 火獄居民之最後者，四足爬行而出。主對他說：『去，入樂園吧。』他見樂園滿是人與供給：『主啊，我見其中滿是人與供給。』『亞當的子孫啊，你若得一王中之王的國度可滿足嗎？』——『可滿足，我的主。』主便笑；他入園，見河川流動、果實、各種供給；他求一門而得之，出而復返；告之：『你曾被囚禁而後死去；你將永居樂園之福。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; eschatological imagery kept as spoken in the text.

passages.text: Among the people of Hell there will be he who is the last of them to leave it and the last to enter Paradise; he will come out of the Fire crawling, and God will say to him, 'Go, and enter Paradise.' So he goes and comes to it and finds that it is full of people. He says, 'O Lord, I find it full of people and provision.' God will say to him, 'Would you be content, O son of Adam, if you had the kingdom of a king of the kings of the world?' He will say, 'I would be content, my Lord.' God will say to him, 'Would you be content, O son of Adam, if I gave you the like of the world and as much again?' He will say, 'Yes.' God will laugh at him and say, 'You will have the like of it and ten times as much.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6571; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 火獄的居民中，有一人是他們中最後離開火獄、最後進入樂園的；他將從火中爬出來，真主對他說：『去吧，進入樂園。』他便去了，來到樂園，發現裡面擠滿了人。他說：『主啊，我發現裡面擠滿了人和給養。』真主對他說：『阿丹的子孫啊，若你擁有世上諸王中一位國王的國度，你可滿意？』他說：『我滿意了，我的主。』真主對他說：『阿丹的子孫啊，若我給你與今世相等之物，再加一倍，你可滿意？』他說：『是的。』真主對他笑了，說：『你將得到與之相等之物，再加十倍。』

passages.text: The last man of the people of Hell will be the last of his people to leave the Fire, and the last to enter Paradise; God will say to him, 'O son of Adam, if you had the world and as much again, would you be content?' He will say, 'Yes, my Lord.' Then God will say, 'You ask for less than what I have prepared for you.' Then he enters, and finds rivers flowing and trees bearing fruit, and food, and all sorts of provision. He will ask, 'O Lord, may I enter? I have seen all these things.' He will be told: 'You are not one of those who are shut out.' He goes out and comes back to the door and is told, 'Enter — the Fire has been behind you, and Paradise is before you.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6571 (variant narration); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 火獄居民中最後一人，將是他族人中最後離開火獄、最後進入樂園的；真主對他說：『阿丹的子孫啊，若你擁有今世，再加一倍，你可滿意？』他說：『是的，我的主。』然後真主說：『你所求的，比我為你預備的還要少。』然後他進去，看見河流流淌，樹木結果，有食物，有各種給養。他問：『主啊，我可以進去嗎？我已經看見了這一切。』有人對他說：『你不是那些被拒之門外的人。』他出去，又回到門口，有人對他說：『進去吧——火獄在你身後，樂園在你面前。』

title.en: The Poorest of the People of Paradise
title.zh: 樂園居民中最窮者

region.en: Medina, eschatological teaching (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那末世教導（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6572; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6572 — narrated by Ibn Mas'ud

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The last of the people of Paradise to enter will be a man whom God allows to enter from outside the gate: 'Go and enter Paradise.' He goes, and thinks it is full; he returns: 'My Lord, I found it full.' Then God says: 'Enter Paradise, and you will have the like of the world and ten times more (or ten times like it).' The man says: 'Are you mocking me, or are You laughing at me, O Lord, though You are the King?' — and God laughs. The man then enters Paradise, and whoever of the people of Paradise was under his rule is placed under his power: even the two women of the jinn, who lie on a carpet with him.
summary.zh: 樂園居民之最後入者，自門外被准進入：『去入樂園。』他以為滿了；他返：『主啊，我見其滿。』主說：『入吧，得與世界同等且十倍（或謂十倍於此）。』那人說：『主啊，你在嘲弄我嗎？你是君王啊。』主便笑。他入園，凡樂園中曾居其下者皆歸其治：即精靈中的兩女，與他同臥一毯。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: Among the people of Paradise there will be the last of them to enter it, a man whom God will cause to enter Paradise from outside of the Gate. He will be told, 'Go and enter Paradise.' So he will go and come to it, and think that it is full. He will go back and say, 'O Lord, I found it full.' God will say, 'Go and enter Paradise, for you will have the like of the world and ten times like it.' The man will say, 'Are You mocking me — or are You laughing at me, O Lord, though You are the King?' He will say, 'I am not mocking you, but I am able to do whatever I will.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6572; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 樂園的居民中，最後進入樂園的人，真主將使他從門外進入樂園。有人對他說：『去吧，進入樂園。』他便前去，來到樂園前，心想它已滿了。他回來說道：『主啊，我發現它已滿了。』真主說：『去吧，進入樂園，因為你將擁有與今世相等之物，以及與之相等的十倍。』那人說：『主啊，禰是在戲弄我——還是在嘲笑我，儘管禰是君王？』真主說：『我並非戲弄你，我確能隨意而行。』

passages.text: When he passes the first of the gates of Paradise, he will say, 'O Lord, how great is this!' He will be told, 'This is for you.' He will find what his soul desires and what pleases his eye, and there will be with him two wives from the houris, each of whom will be wearing seventy rows of garments, and the marrow of their shins will be visible through them from the beauty of their faces. Then when he reaches his dwelling he will find rivers flowing beneath it, and wherever he will go there will be rivers.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6572; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他經過樂園的第一道門時，他會說：『主啊，這是何等宏大！』有人對他說：『這是給你的。』他將發現他心靈所渴望、他眼睛所喜悅的一切，他身邊將有兩位仙女為妻，每一位都穿著七十層衣裳，透過衣裳可見她們小腿的骨髓，那是因她們面容之美。當他到達他的居所時，他將發現其下有河流流淌，無論他往何處去，都有河流。

title.en: Seven Whom God Will Shade on the Day Without Shade
title.zh: 無蔭之日蒙主蔭庇的七種人

region.en: Medina, Friday preaching (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那主麻講道（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Adhan, no. 660 (variant: no. 1423); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 660 — narrated by Abu Hurayrah

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Seven people will be shaded by God on the day when there is no shade but His shade: a just ruler; a youth who grew up in the worship of God; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques; two men who love one another for God, meeting and parting upon that love; a man whom a woman of beauty and position calls to sin, and he answers, 'I fear God'; a man who gives in charity and conceals it so that his left hand does not know what his right hand gave; a man who remembers God alone and weeps.
summary.zh: 無蔭之日，主將為七種人設蔭：公道的官長；自幼崇拜主的青年；心繫清真寺者；為主相愛、聚散皆因此愛的兩人；被貌美有勢之女子勾引而答『我懼主』者；施捨隱蔽、左手不知右手所施者；獨處時紀念主而流淚者。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: The Prophet said: Seven are the people whom God will shade with His shade on the day when there is no shade but His shade: a just ruler; a young man who has been brought up in the worship of God; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques when he leaves them until he returns to them; two men who love one another for God's sake, who come together upon that love and part upon it; a man who is called by a woman of rank and beauty for sin, and he says, 'I fear God'; a man who gives in charity and hides it, so much so that his left hand does not know what his right hand has given; and a man who remembers God in solitude and his eyes overflow.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 660; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 先知說：有七種人，真主將在唯有祂的蔭影之日，以祂的蔭影庇護他們：公正的領袖；在崇拜真主中成長的青年；離寺時心繫清真寺、直至歸返的人；為真主之故而互相友愛的兩人，因這愛而相聚，也因這愛而別離；被一位有地位、美貌的女子召去行罪，而他說『我敬畏真主』的人；施捨而隱藏施捨，以至他的左手不知右手所施的人；在獨處中記念真主而雙眼盈淚的人。

title.en: The Truthful Merchant With the Prophets
title.zh: 與先知同列的誠實商人

region.en: Medina, market teaching (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那集市教導（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Buyu', no. 2076; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Buyu', no. 2076 — narrated by Abu Sa'id

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The truthful, trustworthy merchant will be with the prophets, the truthful, and the martyrs. Trading must be free of cheating: whoever deceives in buying and selling is not of the honest; whoever takes falsely is not of the truthful. The Prophet forbade the seller to raise the price and the buyer to lower it at the expense of another, and forbade the intermarriage of the tribes in the days of ignorance. 'The buyer and seller have the choice as long as they have not separated; if they speak truth and make clear, their transaction will be blessed; but if they conceal and lie, the blessing is erased.'
summary.zh: 誠實可靠的商人將與先知、誠實者、烈士同列。買賣不可欺詐：欺人者非誠實者，妄取者非誠實者。先知禁止抬高市價、以損人利己之價壓低；『買賣雙方只要未分開，皆可自由選擇；若誠實明言，其交易蒙福；若隱匿撒謊，福分被抹去。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: The Messenger of God said: The truthful, trustworthy merchant will be with the prophets, the truthful and the martyrs. And the buyer and the seller have the option of the transaction as long as they have not separated; if both of them speak the truth and make it plain, their transaction will be blessed; but if they speak falsehood and conceal anything, then the blessing of their transaction will be erased.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Buyu', no. 2076; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 真主的使者說：誠實可信的商人將與先知、誠實者及殉道者同在。買賣雙方在未分離之前，有權選擇是否成交；若雙方都說真話並說明實情，他們的交易將蒙祝福；但若他們說謊並隱瞞，他們交易的祝福將被抹去。

title.en: The Dinar, the Donkey, and the Neighbor
title.zh: 金幣、驢與鄰居

region.en: Medina, teaching on mutual rights (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那相互權利教導（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Adab, no. 6018 (variant: Sahih Muslim); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Adab, no. 6018 — narrated by Ibn Umar? (traditional attribution: Abu Hurayrah / Ibn Umar narrations)

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Whosoever believes in God and the Last Day should not harm his neighbor; he should offer hospitality; and he should speak good or keep silent. He whose neighbors are not safe from his wrongdoing is not a believer; and no one is safe from the creditor's claims — the dinar, the dirham, the garment, the donkey, the slave — whose owner may ask repayment of any of them. Even a meal may be asked for on behalf of a hungry guest.
summary.zh: 凡信主與末日者，勿傷其鄰；應待客；言善或默然。鄰居不因其惡行而得安寧者非信士；無人能擔保債權不至——金幣、銀幣、衣裳、驢、僕——其主皆可索取。即便是飢餓客人的食膳，也可代為請求。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: The Messenger of God said: He who believes in God and the Last Day should not harm his neighbour; and he who believes in God and the Last Day should honour his guest; and he who believes in God and the Last Day should speak good or keep silent. And no one is safe from the claims of debts — the debt of the dinar, or of the dirham, or of the garment, or of the donkey, or of the camel — unless he is a man who would ask for the repayment of his debts; but if the guest comes hungry, then the householder should feed him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Adab, no. 6018; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 真主的使者說：凡信仰真主與末日者，不應傷害他的鄰居；凡信仰真主與末日者，應款待他的客人；凡信仰真主與末日者，應說好話或保持沉默。沒有人能免於債務的索求——無論是金幣、銀幣、衣物、驢或駱駝的債——除非他是願意索回其債的人；但若客人飢餓而來，則家主應供養他。

title.en: The Camel That Complained to the Prophet
title.zh: 向先知訴苦的駱駝

region.en: Medina outskirts (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那郊外（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Ahkam, no. 2466 (variant narrations); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Ahkam, no. 2466 — narrated by Anas ibn Malik

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The Prophet enters the garden of a man of the Ansar; there is a camel. When it sees the Prophet it groans and its eyes flow with tears; the Prophet goes to it and wipes the place of its tears, and it becomes quiet. 'Who is the owner of this camel? Whose camel is this?' A man of the Ansar says, 'It is mine.' The Prophet says: 'Do you not fear God with regard to this beast which He has put in your possession? It complained to me that you keep it hungry and load it heavily.'
summary.zh: 先知入輔士之園；見一駱駝。駱駝見先知則呻吟，眼含淚；先知至其旁拭其淚，駱駝安靜。『這駱駝的主人是誰？』一輔士答：『是我的。』先知說：『你豈不敬畏主——他賜你此獸？它向我訴苦：你餓它且重負之。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; animal sentience here is a doctrinal claim within the tradition, presented as text.

passages.text: The Prophet once went into the garden of a man of the Ansar, and there was a camel there. When the Prophet came near it, the camel groaned and its eyes flowed with tears. The Prophet came to it and wiped the place of its tears with his hand, and it became quiet. He said, 'Who is the owner of this camel? Whose camel is this?' A man of the Ansar said, 'It is mine, O Messenger of God.' He said: 'Do you not fear God concerning this beast which He has given you to possess? It has complained to me that you keep it hungry and load it beyond its strength.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Ahkam, no. 2466; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 先知曾進入一位輔士的園子，那裡有一隻駱駝。當先知走近牠時，駱駝呻吟，眼中流淚。先知走到牠跟前，用手擦拭牠流淚之處，牠便安靜下來。他說：『這隻駱駝的主人是誰？這是誰的駱駝？』一位輔士說：『它是我的，真主的使者。』他說：『你難道不敬畏真主，關於這隻真主賜你所有的牲畜嗎？牠已向我訴苦，說你讓牠挨餓，並讓牠馱負超出其能力的重擔。』

title.en: Bilal's Call to Prayer After Death
title.zh: 比拉勒死後的宣禮聲

region.en: Mecca, Kaaba courtyard (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥加天房庭院（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7014; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7014 — the Prophet's dream, narrated by Ibn Umar

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The Prophet dreams that he is at the Kaaba, with a man going around it, and another man walking beside him. He asks who they are and is answered: the tall man with red skin and ivory teeth is Ibrahim (Abraham), and the one walking beside him — who looks like Bilal — is the muezzin of Paradise. Waking, the Prophet says: 'This is Bilal, and the tall man is Ibrahim: I have seen the adhan of Paradise and its muezzin.'
summary.zh: 先知夢中在天房處，見一人繞行，另一人與之同行。他問此二人為誰，答曰：高大紅膚、牙如象牙者是易卜拉欣；與之同行者貌似比拉勒——是樂園的宣禮員。醒後先知說：『這是比拉勒，高大者是易卜拉欣：我已見樂園的宣禮及其宣禮員。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: The Prophet said: While I was sleeping I saw myself at the Kaaba, and there was a man beside it going around it. He was tall, with a dark-red complexion, wavy hair, and his two shoulders were like those of a prince; his teeth were like those of a fine ivory comb. Beside him was another man with curly hair and blind in the right eye, resembling Ibn Qatan. The first was walking around the Kaaba, and the other beside him. I asked, 'Who is this man?' It was said, 'He is Ibrahim.' I said, 'And who is the man with him?' It was said, 'He is the Mu'addhin (caller to prayer) of Paradise.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7014; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 先知說：我睡著時，夢見自己在克爾白旁，有一個人繞著它行走。他身材高大，膚色暗紅，頭髮捲曲，兩肩如王侯一般；牙齒如精緻的象牙梳。他身旁另有一人，頭髮捲曲，右眼失明，形貌酷似伊本·卡坦。前者繞行克爾白，另一人跟隨其側。我問：『此人是誰？』有人說：『他是易卜拉欣。』我說：『與他同行的那人是誰？』有人說：『他是樂園的宣禮員。』

passages.text: The Prophet said: 'I saw in a dream that I was at the Kaaba and saw the one who used to walk beside Bilal.' Then Bilal's call to prayer was heard, and the Prophet said, 'I have seen the Mu'addhin of Paradise, and I have heard the adhan from Bilal who has died.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7014 (variant narration of the same dream-cycle); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 先知說：『我在夢中見自己在克爾白，看見那常走在比拉勒身旁的人。』隨後比拉勒的宣禮聲響起，先知說：『我已見到樂園的宣禮員，也已從已逝的比拉勒那裏聽到宣禮。』

title.en: Bathsheba Before the Throne: Solomon Anointed in a Hurry
title.zh: 拔示巴進御前：所羅門急立為王

region.en: Jerusalem, Gihon spring
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，基訓泉

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Kings 1, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Adonijah exalts himself at the stone of Zoheleth while the aged king 'knew not' his bed. Nathan directs Bathsheba to remind David of his oath, then himself enters; David has Solomon ride the king's mule to Gihon, be anointed by Zadok, and the shofar is blown — 'the city was in an uproar'. Adonijah's feast dissolves in fear; Solomon's first act of clemency spares him.
summary.zh: 亞多尼雅在隱羅結旁自高，而老王「不知」床事。拿單教拔示巴提起大衛的誓言，自己隨後進見；大衛命所羅門騎王的騾子下基訓，由撒督膏立，吹角——「城裡的眾民都大聲吹角」。亞多尼雅的宴席聞風潰散；所羅門首行寬仁，存其性命。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Zadok the priest took the horn of oil out of the Tent, and anointed Solomon. And they blew the horn; and all the people said: 'Long live king Solomon.' And all the people came up after him, and the people piped with pipes, and rejoiced with great joy, so that the earth rent with the sound of them.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Kings 1:39-40 (public domain).
passages.zh: 祭司撒督從帳幕中取出盛油的角，膏立了所羅門。他們吹響號角；眾民都說：『願所羅門王萬歲。』眾民都跟隨他上來，百姓吹笛奏樂，歡喜快樂，聲音之大，震裂了大地。

title.en: Give Thy Servant a Listening Heart
title.zh: 求你賜僕人分辨的心

region.en: Gibon, high place
region.zh: 基遍，邱壇

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Kings 3:1-15, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: At Gibeon Solomon offers a thousand burnt-offerings, and the LORD appears to him by night: 'Ask what I shall give thee.' The king asks 'an understanding heart to judge Thy people, that I may discern between good and evil' — no long life, no riches. 'Because thou hast asked this thing... behold, I have done according to thy word' — plus riches and honour thrown in, 'so that there hath not been any among the kings like unto thee'.
summary.zh: 在基遍獻一千燔祭，夜間耶和華向所羅門顯現：「你願我賜你什麼，你可以求。」王求「能分辨是非的心判斷你的民」——不求壽，不求富。「你所求的我已賜給你」——並加富足尊榮，「列王中沒有一個能比你的」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Give Thy servant therefore an understanding heart to judge Thy people, that I may discern between good and evil; for who is able to judge this Thy so great a people? And the speech pleased the LORD, that Solomon had asked this thing. ... Behold, I have given thee a wise and a discerning heart; so that there hath been none like thee before thee, neither shall any arise like unto thee.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Kings 3:9, 12 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 所以求祢賜僕人一顆明辨的心，可以判斷祢的民，能分辨善惡；因為誰能判斷這眾多的祢的民呢？所羅門所求的這事，主喜悅。……看哪，我已賜你聰明智慧的心；在你以前沒有像你的，在你以後也沒有像你的興起。

title.en: Divide the Living Child: The Judgment of Solomon
title.zh: 將活孩子劈成兩半：所羅門的判斷

region.en: Jerusalem, king's court
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，王的公堂

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Kings 3:16-28, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Two harlots both claim one surviving child. Solomon orders a sword — 'Divide the living child in two, and give half unto the one, and half unto the other'. The true mother surrenders her claim — 'give her the child... but don't kill it'; the false consents. 'And all Israel heard of the judgment... and they feared the king; for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him.'
summary.zh: 兩妓女爭一活子。所羅門命取刀——「將活孩子劈成兩半，一半給這婦人，一半給那婦人」。真母捨子——「將孩子給她吧，萬不可殺他」；假母同意。「以色列眾人聽見王這樣判斷，就都敬畏他，因為見他心裡有神的智慧。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then spake the woman whose the living child was unto the king, for her bowels yearned upon her son, and she said: 'O my lord, give her the living child, and in no wise slay it.' But the other said: 'Let it be neither mine nor thine; divide it.' Then the king answered and said: 'Give her the living child, and in no wise slay it: she is the mother thereof.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Kings 3:26-27 (public domain).
passages.zh: 那活孩子的母親因心疼自己的兒子，就對王說：『我主啊，把活孩子給那婦人吧，萬不可殺他。』但那婦人說：『這孩子既不歸我，也不歸你；把他劈了吧。』王回答說：『把活孩子給這婦人，萬不可殺他；這婦人實在是孩子的母親。』

title.en: Will God Indeed Dwell on the Earth? Temple Dedication
title.zh: 神果真住在地上嗎？聖殿奉獻

region.en: Temple Mount, Jerusalem
region.zh: 聖殿山，耶路撒冷

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Kings 8, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The elders, the ark with cherubim-shadowing poles, and the glory-cloud fill the house 'so that the priests could not stand to minister'. Solomon's prayer asks heaven's scandal: 'Behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee; how much less this house that I have builded!' — a house for the Name, for prayer toward it in every calamity, for the stranger who comes from a far country.
summary.zh: 長老、有基路伯蔭影的約櫃與榮光之雲充滿殿，「甚至祭司不能站立供職」。所羅門的禱告直指天之悖論：「天和天上的天尚且不足你居住的，何況我所建的這殿呢！」——為名的殿，為各樣災殃中向殿的祈禱，也為從遠方來的外邦人。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Read as Sukkot haftarah; the dedication prayer structures later Jewish liturgy of petition.

passages.text: But will God in very truth dwell on the earth? Behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee; how much less this house that I have builded! Yet have Thou respect unto the prayer of Thy servant, and to his supplication, O LORD my God, to hearken unto the cry and to the prayer which Thy servant prayeth before Thee this day; that Thine eyes may be open toward this house night and day.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Kings 8:27-29 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 但神果真住在地上嗎？看哪，天和天上的天尚且不足容納祢，何況我所建的這殿呢！然而，主我的神啊，求祢垂顧僕人的禱告祈求，俯聽僕人今日在祢面前所發的呼求與禱告；願祢的眼目晝夜看顧這殿。

title.en: The Queen of Sheba Comes with Hard Questions
title.zh: 示巴女王攜難題而來

region.en: Jerusalem (visiting queen from Sheba, South Arabia)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷（示巴南方來訪女王）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Kings 10:1-13, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Sheba's queen, 'hearing of the fame of Solomon', comes with camels bearing spices, gold, and precious stones, and with hard questions. Everything she sees — the house, the food, the apparel, the burnt-offering — 'there was no more spirit in her': 'It was a true report... the half was not told me.' Gold and spices change hands, and no more spice came 'such as the queen of Sheba gave' until her day's end.
summary.zh: 示巴女王「聽見所羅門的名聲」，攜駱駝馱香料、金子、寶石與難題而來。凡她所見——宮室、飲食、衣服、燔祭——「就詫異得神不守舍」：「我先前的話是真的……我所聽見的，不及一半。」金與香料交易，示巴女王所給的香料「以後再沒有這樣的香料」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Ethiopian tradition identifies her dynasty with Makeda (cross-ref Ethiopian records, not yet present).

passages.text: And when the queen of Sheba had seen all Solomon's wisdom, and the house that he had built, and the food of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel... there was no more spirit in her. And she said to the king: 'It was a true report that I heard in mine own land of thine acts, and of thy wisdom. Howbeit I believed not the words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it; and, behold, the half was not told me.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Kings 10:4-7 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 示巴女王見所羅門一切的智慧，和他所建造的宮室，他席上的珍饈美味，他臣僕的分列而坐，他僕人的侍立，以及他們的服飾……就詫異得神不守舍。她對王說：「我在本國所聽見論你的事和你的智慧，果然是真的。我先前不信那些話，及至我來，親眼看見，才知道人所告訴我的還不到一半。」

title.en: Jeroboam's Calves: The Kingdom Divided
title.zh: 耶羅波安的金牛：國分裂

region.en: Shechem, Bethel, and Dan
region.zh: 示劍、伯特利與但

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Kings 11:26-43; 12, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The prophet Ahijah tears his new cloak into twelve pieces and gives ten to Jeroboam: 'behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon'. After Rehoboam's tyranny ('my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions'), the ten tribes secede. Fearful of Jerusalem's temple, Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan: 'behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt' — the sin the Book of Kings keeps repeating.
summary.zh: 先知亞希雅將新衣撕成十二片，予耶羅波安十片：「看哪，我必將國從所羅門手裡奪回」。羅波安暴政（「我父親用鞭子責打你們，我要用蠍子鞭責打你們」）之後，十支派分離。懼聖殿朝聖，耶羅波安在伯特利與但立金牛犢：「以色列人哪，你們上耶路撒冷去實在難；看哪，這是領你們出埃及地的神。」——列王記不斷重複的罪。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Ahijah laid hold of the new garment that was on him, and rent it in twelve pieces. And he said to Jeroboam: 'Take thee ten pieces; for thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel: Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Kings 11:30-31 (public domain).
passages.zh: 亞希雅將自己身上所穿的那件新衣抓住，撕成十二片。他對耶羅波安說：「你可以拿十片；因為耶和華以色列的神如此說：『看哪，我必將國從所羅門手裡奪回，將十個支派賜給你。』」

passages.text: Rehoboam's arrogance split the united monarchy at Shechem; the people's cry, 'What portion have we in David?', sent the northern tribes home. Jeroboam fortified Shechem, then, fearing pilgrimage would rebind hearts to Jerusalem, cast two calves and installed non-Levitical priests, kept a festival 'in the month which he had devised of his own heart' — and the deuteronomistic verdict — 'this thing became a sin' — follows every northern king's obituary. Paraphrase of 1 Kings 12:1-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of 1 Kings 12:1-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 羅波安的傲慢使統一的王國在示劍分裂；百姓呼喊「我們在大衛裡有什麼分呢？」，使北方各支派各自回家。耶羅波安修築示劍，後來因懼怕朝聖會使人心重新歸向耶路撒冷，便鑄了兩隻牛犢，又立非利未人的祭司，定了一個節期，「在八月，就是他私自所定的月」——而申命記史家的評語——「這事成了罪」——此後追隨每一位北方君王的訃聞。改寫自《列王紀上》12:1-30（JPS 1917）；並非逐字引用。

title.en: The Man of God from Judah and the Lion on the Road
title.zh: 猶大神人與路上之獅

region.en: Bethel, northern kingdom
region.zh: 伯特利，北國

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Kings 13, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: A 'man of God out of Judah' cries against Jeroboam's altar — 'O altar, altar, thus saith the LORD: Behold, a son shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name' — and the altar cracks. Offered a reward, he refuses food or water: 'so was it charged me by the word of the LORD'. An old prophet lies to him, a lion kills him on the road 'but did not eat the ass', and the old prophet buries him: 'the words which he cried... shall surely come to pass.'
summary.zh: 猶大的神人在耶羅波安的壇前呼叫——「壇哪，壇哪！耶和華如此說：大衛家裡必生一個兒子，名叫約西亞」——壇即裂開。受款待而不受：「我奉耶和華的命令，不可喫飯喝水」。老先知以謊言留他，路上獅子咬死他「卻沒有喫驢」，老先知葬之：「他奉耶和華的命指著伯特利壇說的話必定應驗。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And behold, a lion met him by the way, and slew him; and his carcase was cast in the way, and the ass stood by it; the lion also stood by the carcase. And, behold, men passed by, and saw the carcase cast in the way, and the lion standing by the carcase; and they came and told it in the city where the old prophet dwelt.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Kings 13:24-25 (public domain).
passages.zh: 看哪，有獅子在路上遇見他，將他咬死；他的屍首被拋在路上，驢站在屍首旁邊，獅子也站在屍首旁邊。看哪，有人經過，看見屍首拋在路上，獅子站在屍首旁邊，就來到老先知所住的那城裡述說這事。

title.en: The Vineyard of Naboth and the Blood of Jezebel
title.zh: 拿伯的葡萄園與耶洗別的血

region.en: Jezreel, northern kingdom
region.zh: 耶斯列，北國

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Kings 21, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Ahab covets Naboth's ancestral vineyard beside his palace; Naboth refuses — 'The LORD forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee'. Jezebel's forged letters stage a fast and false blasphemy charges; Naboth is stoned, and Ahab takes the field. Elijah meets him: 'Hast thou killed, and also taken possession?... In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine.'
summary.zh: 亞哈貪戀王宮旁拿伯的祖業葡萄園；拿伯拒之：「我敬畏耶和華，萬不敢將我先人留下的產業給你。」耶洗別偽造書信設禁食與假瀆神之罪；拿伯被石擊，亞哈得田。以利亞迎之：「你殺了人，又得他的產業麼？……狗在何處舔拿伯的血，也必在何處舔你的血。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Naboth's ancestral inheritance frames Israelite land law.

passages.text: And Ahab said unto Elijah: 'Hast thou found me, O mine enemy?' And he answered: 'I have found thee; because thou hast sold thyself to do that which is evil in the sight of the LORD. Behold, I will bring evil upon thee, and will utterly sweep away after thee; and will make thine house like the house of Jeroboam... because thou hast provoked Me to anger, and hast made Israel to sin.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Kings 21:20-22 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 亞哈對以利亞說：「我仇敵啊，你找到我了嗎？」他回答說：「我找到你了；因為你賣了自己，行耶和華眼中看為惡的事。看哪，我必降禍與你，將你之後的盡都除滅；我必使你的家像耶羅波安的家……因為你惹我發怒，又使以色列人犯罪。」

title.en: Ravens Feed Elijah by the Brook Cherith
title.zh: 烏鴉在基立溪旁供養以利亞

region.en: Brook Cherith, east of the Jordan
region.zh: 基立溪，約旦河東

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Kings 17:1-7, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The Tishbite announces to Ahab: 'As the LORD... liveth, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word'. God sends him to the brook Cherith to drink of the stream — 'and I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there' — and the ravens bring him bread and flesh morning and evening until the brook dries up.
summary.zh: 提斯比人向亞哈宣告：「我指著所事奉永生耶和華以色列的神起誓，這幾年我若不禱告，必不降露不下雨。」神遣他往基立溪喝水——「我已吩咐烏鴉在那裡供養你」——烏鴉早晚給他餅與肉，直至溪水乾涸。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook. And it came to pass after a while, that the brook dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Kings 17:6-7 (public domain).
passages.zh: 烏鴉早晨給他叼餅和肉來，晚上也叼餅和肉來；他也喝那溪裡的水。過了些日子，溪水乾了，因為那地沒有下雨。

title.en: The Widow's Handful of Meal at Zarephath
title.zh: 撒勒法寡婦的一把麵

region.en: Zarephath, Phoenician coast
region.zh: 撒勒法，腓尼基海岸

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Kings 17:8-24, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Sent to a foreign widow gathering sticks, Elijah asks a morsel; she has only 'a handful of meal in the barrel, and a little oil in the cruse' — enough for one last cake before death. 'Fear not... for thus saith the LORD: The barrel of meal shall not waste.' The jar and cruse never empty. When her son dies, the prophet carries him upstairs and prays three times — 'O LORD my God, let the child's soul come back into his body' — and he revives.
summary.zh: 遣至外邦撿柴寡婦旁，以利亞求一點餅；她只有「罈內的一把麵，瓶裡的一點油」——最後一餐。 「不要懼怕……耶和華如此說：罈內的麵必不減少。」罈與瓶永不空。兒子死時，先知抱他上樓三次禱告——「求你使這孩子的魂仍入他的身體」——孩子復活。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Elijah stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried unto the LORD, and said: 'O LORD my God, I pray Thee, let this child's soul come back into his body.' And the LORD hearkened unto the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came back into his body, and he revived. ... And the woman said to Elijah: 'Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the LORD in thy mouth is truth.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Kings 17:21-24 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 以利亞三次伏在孩子身上，向耶和華呼求說：「耶和華我的神啊，求你使這孩子的靈魂回到他的身體裡。」耶和華垂聽了以利亞的聲音；孩子的靈魂就回到他的身體裡，他便活了。……那婦人對以利亞說：「如今我知道你是神人，耶和華藉你口所說的話是真實的。」

title.en: The God That Answereth by Fire: Carmel
title.zh: 以火應允的神：迦密山

region.en: Mount Carmel, northern coast
region.zh: 迦密山，北部海岸

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Kings 18, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: On Carmel Elijah challenges 450 prophets of Baal: 'call ye on the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the LORD'. They dance and cut themselves till evening; there is 'no voice, nor any that answered'. Elijah repairs the broken altar, drenches the sacrifice three times, and prays — fire falls, consumes wood, stones, dust, and water. 'And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces; and they said: The LORD, He is the God; the LORD, He is the God.'
summary.zh: 在迦密山以利亞挑戰四百五十巴力先知：「求告你們神的名，我也求告耶和華的名」。他們跳舞自割直到傍晚，「沒有聲音，沒有應允的」。以利亞重修毀壞的壇，三次澆透祭牲禱告——火降，燒盡燔祭、木柴、石頭、塵土與水。「眾民看見了，就俯伏在地，說：耶和華是神！耶和華是神！」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then the fire of the LORD fell, and consumed the burnt-offering, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench. And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces; and they said: 'The LORD, He is the God; the LORD, He is the God.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Kings 18:38-39 (public domain).
passages.zh: 於是耶和華的火降下，燒盡了燔祭、木柴、石頭、塵土，又舔盡了溝裡的水。眾民看見了，就俯伏在地，說：「耶和華是神！耶和華是神！」

passages.text: Elijah's taunt became proverbial: 'cry aloud; for he is a god; either he is meditating, or gone aside, or on a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth'. After the fire, the prophets of Baal are seized at the brook Kishon, rain returns — 'there ariseth a little cloud out of the sea, like a man's hand' — and Elijah girds up his loins and runs before Ahab's chariot to Jezreel. Paraphrase of 1 Kings 18:27, 40-46 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of 1 Kings 18:27-46 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 以利亞的譏諷成了諺語：「大聲求告吧！因為他是神；他或默想，或走到一旁，或行路，或睡著了。」火降之後，巴力的先知在基順溪邊被拿住，雨也復返——「有一小片雲從海裡上來，不過如人手那樣大」——以利亞便束起腰來，在亞哈的戰車前跑到耶斯列。此為列王紀上十八章27、40至46節（JPS 1917）的意譯，並非逐字引用。

title.en: The Still Small Voice of Horeb
title.zh: 何烈山微小之聲

region.en: Mount Horeb (Sinai), wilderness
region.zh: 何烈山（西奈），曠野

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 1 Kings 19, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Jezebel's threat sends Elijah a day's journey into the wilderness to lie under a juniper tree and ask to die. An angel touches him twice with cake and water — 'the journey is too great for thee' — and he goes to Horeb, where wind, earthquake, and fire each pass 'but the LORD was not in them', until 'a still small voice'. God sends him back: anoint Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha; seven thousand have not bowed to Baal.
summary.zh: 耶洗別的恐嚇使以利亞逃入曠野一日，躺在一棵羅騰樹下求死。天使兩次以餅水觸之——「這路太遠，你不能走」——他到何烈山；狂風、地震、烈火各有其至，「耶和華卻不在其中」，直至「微小的聲音」。神遣他回去：膏哈薛、耶戶、以利沙；還有七千人未曾向巴力屈膝。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And, behold, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and broke in pieces the rocks before the LORD; but the LORD was not in the wind; and after the wind an earthquake; but the LORD was not in the earthquake; and after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire; and after the fire a still small voice.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Kings 19:11-12 (public domain).
passages.zh: 忽然，耶和華經過，有狂風大作，崩山碎石，耶和華卻不在風中；風後有地震，耶和華卻不在其中；地震後有火，耶和華卻不在火中；火後有微小的聲音。

title.en: Fire from Heaven: Ahaziah's Two Captains of Fifty
title.zh: 天降之火：亞哈謝兩個五十夫長

region.en: Hilltop of Samaria (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 撒瑪利亞山頂（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 2 Kings 1, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Sick Ahaziah sends messengers to consult Baal-zebub, god of Ekron; Elijah intercepts them: 'Is it because there is no God in Israel?' A captain of fifty with his men, sent to fetch the prophet, calls him 'thou man of God' and is consumed by fire from heaven; the second suffers likewise. The third captain falls on his knees — 'let my life, and the life of these fifty, be precious in thy sight' — and Elijah goes down to pronounce the king's death.
summary.zh: 患病的亞哈謝遣使求問以革倫的巴力西卜；以利亞攔阻：「以色列中豈沒有神麼？」五十夫長稱其「神人」而被天火燒滅；第二隊同然。第三個俯伏——「願我的性命與這五十個人的性命在你眼前看為寶貴」——以利亞乃下去宣告王之死。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty: 'If I be a man of God, let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty.' And there came down fire from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 2 Kings 1:10 (public domain). The narrative repeats for the second captain and contrasts the third captain's humility.
passages.zh: 以利亞回答五十夫長說：「我若是神人，願火從天上降下，燒滅你和你那五十人。」於是火從天上降下，燒滅了他和那五十人。

title.en: The Chariot of Fire: Elijah Taken Up
title.zh: 火戰車：以利亞升天

region.en: Jordan crossing toward Jericho (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 過約旦河往耶利哥（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 2 Kings 2:1-18, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Elisha, warned thrice, refuses to leave his master: 'as the LORD liveth... I will not leave thee'. Fifty prophets watch from afar as Elijah smites the Jordan with his rolled mantle and the waters divide. He asks his parting gift; Elisha dares: 'a double portion of thy spirit'. 'A chariot of fire, and horses of fire, appeared... and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.' The mantle falls; Elisha smites the waters — 'and they parted hither and thither; and he went over.'
summary.zh: 以利沙三得警告而不離：「我指著永生的耶和華……起誓，我必不離開你」。五十先知遠觀以利亞捲起外衣打水，水就分開。臨別求恩賜；以利沙敢求：「願感動你的靈加倍的感動我。」「有火車火馬出現……以利亞乘旋風升天去了。」外衣掉下；以利沙打水——「水也左右分開了」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Elijah's non-death seeds the Seder-cup expectation and Malachi's 'returning Elijah' (Mal 3:23).

passages.text: And it came to pass, as they still went on, and talked, that, behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, which parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven. And Elisha saw it, and he cried: 'My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and the horsemen thereof!' And he saw him no more.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 2 Kings 2:11-12 (public domain).
passages.zh: 他們正走著說話，忽然有火車火馬出現，將二人隔開；以利亞就乘旋風升天去了。以利沙看見，就呼叫說：「我父啊！我父啊！以色列的戰車馬兵啊！」此後不再見他了。

title.en: The Widow's Oil That Would Not Stop
title.zh: 倒不盡的寡婦油

region.en: Samaria, prophets' school
region.zh: 撒瑪利亞，先知門徒

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 2 Kings 4:1-7, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: A widow of the prophets' guild, debt-ridden with creditors coming for her two sons, owns one jar of oil. Elisha commands: borrow empty vessels, 'borrow not a few', and pour indoors. She pours until every vessel is full — 'and the oil stayed'. Sold, the oil pays the debt and the family lives 'of the rest'.
summary.zh: 先知門徒的遺孀債台高築，債主來取二子為奴，家中只有一瓶油。以利沙命：借空器皿，「不要少借」，關門倒油。她倒至一切器皿都滿了——「油就止住了」。賣油還債，母子「靠所剩的度日」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And when they were full, she said unto her son: 'Bring me yet a vessel.' And he said unto her: 'There is not a vessel more.' And the oil stayed. Then she came and told the man of God. And he said: 'Go, sell the oil, and pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children of the rest.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 2 Kings 4:6-7 (public domain).
passages.zh: 器皿都滿了，她對兒子說：「再給我拿一個器皿來。」兒子說：「沒有器皿了。」油就止住了。於是她去告訴神人。神人說：「你去賣油還債，你和你的孩子可以靠剩下的度日。」

title.en: The Shunammite's Room and Her Son Twice Given
title.zh: 書念婦人的小樓與兩次得子

region.en: Shunem, Jezreel valley
region.zh: 書念，耶斯列谷

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 2 Kings 4:8-37, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: A great woman of Shunem builds the prophet a small furnished room; offered recompense, she asks nothing — 'I dwell among mine own people'. Elisha promises her a son 'at this season next year', and the child is born. Years later he dies of sunstroke in the harvest field; she lays him on the prophet's bed, rides to Carmel, grips Elisha's feet, and refuses release until the prophet raises the boy — sneeze after sneeze — alive.
summary.zh: 書念的大婦人為先知蓋小樓，陳設床榻桌椅燈；蒙報以恩而不求——「我在本民中安然居住」。以利沙許以明年此時得一子，果然。多年後孩子在田間中暑而死；她將他放在先知的床上，騎驢上迦密山，抓住神人以利沙的腳，不放直到先知使孩子復活——連連打了七個噴嚏。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And when Elisha was come into the house, behold, the child was dead, and laid upon his bed. And he went in therefore, and shut the door upon them twain, and prayed unto the LORD. And he went up, and lay upon the child, and put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands; and he stretched himself upon him; and the flesh of the child waxed warm.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 2 Kings 4:32-34 (public domain).
passages.zh: 以利沙進了屋子，看見孩子死了，放在他的床上。他就進去，把門關上，只有他們兩人在裡面，向耶和華祈禱。他又上去，伏在孩子身上，口對口，眼對眼，手對手；他伏在孩子身上，孩子的身體就漸漸溫暖了。

title.en: Naaman Washes Seven Times in the Jordan
title.zh: 乃縵在約旦河沐浴七次

region.en: Jordan River near Samaria
region.zh: 撒瑪利亞附近的約旦河

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 2 Kings 5, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The Syrian captain, 'a great man... but a leper', hears from an Israelite captive girl of 'the prophet that is in Samaria'. Elisha sends only a messenger — 'go and wash in the Jordan seven times' — and Naaman storms off: 'Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?' His servants' gentle logic prevails; he dips seven times, 'and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.' He takes two mule-loads of Israel's earth home to worship the LORD.
summary.zh: 敘利亞元帥「為尊為大……卻長了大痲瘋」，從以色列擄來的小女子口中得知「撒瑪利亞的先知」。以利沙只遣使者——「去在約旦河中沐浴七回」——乃縵怒而去：「大馬士革的河亞罷拿與法珥法豈不比以色列的一切水更好麼？」僕人婉勸；七次沐浴，「他的肉復原，好像小孩子的肉，就潔淨了」。他馱兩騾子以色列土回國，好獻祭與耶和華。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God; and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean. And he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him; and he said: 'Behold now, I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 2 Kings 5:14-15 (public domain).
passages.zh: 於是乃縵下去，照神人的話，在約但河裡沐浴七次；他的肉復原，好像小孩子的肉，他就潔淨了。他和他的全體隨從回到神人那裡，來到他面前站著，說：「如今我知道，除了以色列之外，普天下沒有神。」

title.en: Horses and Chariots of Fire at Dothan
title.zh: 多坍的火車火馬

region.en: Dothan, northern hill country
region.zh: 多坍，北部山地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 2 Kings 6:8-23, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Elisha keeps foretelling the king of Israel every move of the Syrian army. Surrounded by horses and chariots at Dothan, his servant panics — and the prophet prays: 'open his eyes, that he may see. And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw; and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.' The army is smitten with blindness and led to Samaria, where Elisha forbids slaughter: 'Set bread and water before them... and they went to their master.'
summary.zh: 以利沙頻將敘利亞軍的行動預告以色列王。在多坍被馬兵戰車四面圍困，僕人驚惶——先知禱告：「求你開他的眼目，使他能看見。耶和華開他的眼目，他就看見滿山有火車火馬圍繞以利沙。」敘軍眼目昏迷，被引至撒瑪利亞；以利沙禁止殺戮：「擺設飯，給他們喫了喝……他們就回到主人那裡去了。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Elisha prayed, and said: 'LORD, I pray Thee, open his eyes, that he may see.' And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw; and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha. And as they came down to him, Elisha prayed unto the LORD, and said: 'Smite this people, I pray Thee, with blindness.' And He smote them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 2 Kings 6:17-18 (public domain).
passages.zh: 以利沙禱告說：「耶和華啊，求你開這少年人的眼目，使他能看見。」耶和華開了少年人的眼目，他就看見；見滿山有火車火馬圍繞以利沙。敵人下到以利沙那裡，以利沙向耶和華禱告說：「求你使這民眼目昏迷。」耶和華就照以利沙的話，使他們眼目昏迷。

title.en: The Angel in the Camp: Jerusalem against Sennacherib
title.zh: 營中的天使：耶路撒冷對西拿基立

region.en: Jerusalem walls; Assyrian camp
region.zh: 耶路撒冷城牆；亞述營地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 2 Kings 18-19, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The Rabshakeh taunts Jerusalem in Judean from the wall: 'Hath any of the gods of the nations ever delivered his land?' Hezekiah spreads the letter before the LORD in the Temple and prays: 'save us... that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that Thou art the LORD God, even Thou only'. Isaiah's oracle answers; that night 'the angel of the LORD went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand', and Sennacherib returns to Nineveh, later slain in the house of Nisroch.
summary.zh: 拉伯沙基在牆外用猶大語譏誚：「列國的神有哪一個救他本國脫離亞述王的手呢？」希西家將書信在殿裡展開在耶和華面前禱告：「求你救我們脫離亞述王的手，使天下萬國都知道惟獨你耶和華是神」。以賽亞的諭言回應；當夜「耶和華的使者出去，在亞述營中殺了十八萬五千人」，西拿基立拔營回尼尼微，後在尼斯洛廟裡被殺。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Parallel reliefs (Taylor Prism) preserve the Assyrian version of the siege.

passages.text: And it came to pass that night, that the angel of the LORD went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand; and when men arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses. So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt in Nineveh.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 2 Kings 19:35-36 (public domain).
passages.zh: 當夜，耶和華的使者出去，在亞述營中擊殺了十八萬五千人；清早有人起來，見他們都是死屍。亞述王西拿基立就拔營回去，住在尼尼微。

title.en: The Book Found in the House of the LORD
title.zh: 聖殿裡尋得的律法書

region.en: Temple Mount, Jerusalem
region.zh: 聖殿山，耶路撒冷

period: Narrative set 622 BCE; composed c. 7th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 2 Kings 22-23, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: During Temple repairs under the boy-king Josiah, Hilkiah the priest finds 'a book of the law of the LORD'. The scribe Shaphan reads it to the king, who rends his clothes: 'great is the wrath of the LORD that is kindled against us'. Huldah the prophetess confirms the doom — 'but because thine heart was tender' Josiah dies in peace. Then comes the great purge: idols burned, the high places defiled, Passover kept 'as it is written in the book of this covenant... from the days of the judges', none like it since.
summary.zh: 少年王約西亞修殿時，大祭司希勒家尋得「律法書」。書記沙番讀與王聽，王撕裂衣服：「耶和華向我們大發烈怒」。女先知戶勒大確認災禍——「但因你心裡柔軟」約西亞平安而終。隨後大清除：偶像焚燒、邱壇污穢、照「書上所寫的約」守逾越節——「自從士師……沒有守過這樣的逾越節」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Josiah's reform is a anchor-point for biblical scholarship on Deuteronomy's composition.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when the king had heard the words of the book of the law, that he rent his clothes. And the king commanded... saying: 'Inquire ye of the LORD for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that is found; for great is the wrath of the LORD that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not hearkened unto the words of this book, to do according unto all that which is written concerning us.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 2 Kings 22:11-13 (public domain).
passages.zh: 王聽見律法書上的話，就撕裂衣服。王吩咐……說：「你們去，為我、為民、為猶大眾人，以這所找到的書上的話求問耶和華；因為耶和華向我們所發的烈怒甚大，是因我們列祖沒有聽從這書上的話，沒有照著書上所寫的一切去行。」

title.en: The Burning of the House of the LORD
title.zh: 耶和華殿的焚燒

region.en: Jerusalem, in ruins
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，廢墟

period: Narrative set 587/586 BCE; composed c. 6th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: 2 Kings 25, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: In the eleventh year of Zedekiah the city wall is breached; the king's sons are slain before his eyes, his eyes put out, and he is carried to Babylon in fetters. The Temple, palace, and every great house are burned; the walls are broken down; the vessels of the house of the LORD are cut in pieces and carried off. Gedaliah is set over the remnant and assassinated — and the people, fearing the Chaldeans, go down into Egypt. 'So Judah was carried away captive out of his land.'
summary.zh: 西底家十一年，城被攻破；王眾子在他眼前被殺，他的眼被剜，帶鎖鍊被擄到巴比倫。耶和華的殿、王宮、大宅盡焚；城牆拆毀；聖殿的器皿被切成銅塊擄去。基大利被立管餘民而被殺——眾人懼迦勒底人，下埃及去。「這樣，猶大人被擄離開本地。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The exilic trauma structures Jewish historical memory (Tisha B'Av).

passages.text: And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month... Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, came unto Jerusalem. And he burnt the house of the LORD, and the king's house; and all the houses of Jerusalem, even every great man's house, burnt he with fire. And all the army of the Chaldeans, that were with the captain of the guard, broke down the walls of Jerusalem round about.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 2 Kings 25:8-10 (public domain).
passages.zh: 五月七日，巴比倫王的僕人、護衛長尼布撒拉旦來到耶路撒冷。他焚燒了耶和華的殿和王宮，又用火焚燒耶路撒冷所有的房屋，就是每一座顯貴的宅第。跟隨護衛長的迦勒底全軍又拆毀了耶路撒冷四圍的城牆。

title.en: Seventy Thousand Who Enter Paradise Without Account
title.zh: 無算而入樂園的七萬人

region.en: Medina, teaching on the Weighing (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那關於清算的教導（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tawhid, no. 7437; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tawhid, no. 7437 — narrated by Ibn Abbas

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without account: those who do not draw omens, nor treat by cautery or incantation, but trust their Lord — and a further crowd like them. They are the ones who do not believe in ill omens, do not seek ruqya, do not cauterize, and upon their Lord alone they rely. So many gather that they are said to be like the clouds of the morning.
summary.zh: 我的教民中有七萬人將無算而入樂園：不占卜、不以烙治或咒術治病，而信賴其主——另有與他們相仿的一群。他們不以凶兆為懼、不求符咒、不施烙術，惟倚賴其主。其眾之多，如晨雲。
