sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: The Prophet said: Seventy thousand, or seven hundred thousand, of my nation will enter Paradise without account; they are those who do not treat themselves with ruqya (incantations), nor believe in omens, nor are treated by cautery, and they put their trust in their Lord. Ibn Abbas said: I do not know whether the Prophet said seventy thousand or seven hundred thousand. And Ukkashah was of the same description; so he said, 'O Lord, make me one of them.' The Prophet said, 'You are one of them.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tawhid, no. 7437; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 先知說：我的民族中有七萬人，或七十萬人，將不受清算地進入樂園；他們就是那些不為自己施行魯格葉（咒語）、不信凶兆、不以烙鐵治病，並且信託他們的主的人。伊本·阿巴斯說：我不知道先知說的是七萬還是七十萬。烏卡沙也屬於這一類人；於是他說：『主啊，求你使我成為他們中的一員。』先知說：『你就是他們中的一員。』

title.en: Musa Slaps the Angel of Death
title.zh: 穆薩掌摑死神天使

region.en: Mount Nebo region, Israelite wilderness (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 尼波山地區，以色列曠野（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Fada'il (also Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Jana'iz, no. 1339); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih Muslim, Kitab Fada'il al-Sahabah — narrated by Abu Hurayrah (parallel: Sahih al-Bukhari no. 1339)

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The Angel of Death is sent to Musa; when he meets him, Musa slaps him between the eyes. The angel returns to God: 'You have sent me to a slave who does not want to die.' God restores his eye and says: 'Return to My servant and tell him — put your hand on the back of an ox: you will live for the number of hairs that fall under it.' 'My Lord, then what?' — 'Then death.' Musa asks to be brought near the Holy Land by a stone's throw, and it is said that he was buried there.
summary.zh: 死神天使奉遣至穆薩；相遇之際，穆薩一掌擊其眼間。天使歸主：『你遣我至一不欲死之僕。』主復其眼而諭：『回去告訴我的僕人——把手放在牛背上：其下落毛之數即其壽數。』『我的主，那之後呢？』——『之後便是死。』穆薩求葬於聖地一石之距，相傳其墓即在該地。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; the episode belongs to the 'origin of death' cluster (the Angel's retreat is denied — death is fixed).

passages.text: The Angel of Death was sent to Moses. When he came to Moses, Moses slapped him severely on the eye. The angel returned to his Lord and said, 'You have sent me to a slave who does not want to die.' God restored his eye and said, 'Go back and tell him to place his hand on the back of an ox and to tell you, by the number of hairs that fall under it, how long he will live.' Moses placed his hand on the back of an ox, and the hair that fell under his palm was one: and God said, 'You will live for one hair's worth, and then you will die.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih Muslim, Kitab Fada'il (parallel Sahih al-Bukhari no. 1339); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 死神被派去見穆薩。當他來到穆薩面前時，穆薩重重地打了他眼睛一巴掌。天使回到他的主那裡說：『你派我去見一個不願死亡的僕人。』真主恢復了他的眼睛，說：『回去告訴他，把手放在牛的背上，你按那底下掉落的毛數告訴他，他還能活多久。』穆薩把手放在牛的背上，落在他掌下的毛是一根：真主說：『你將活一根毛的工夫，然後你就會死。』

passages.text: Moses said, 'My Lord, then what?' God said, 'Then death.' Moses said, 'Bring me near the Holy Land by a stone's throw'; and it is said that Moses was buried there, in the land nearest to the Holy Land, so that his place of burial was a stone's throw from Jerusalem.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih Muslim, Kitab Fada'il (parallel Sahih al-Bukhari no. 1339); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 穆薩說：『我的主啊，然後呢？』真主說：『然後就是死亡。』穆薩說：『求你讓我靠近聖地，只差一箭之遙』；據說穆薩就葬在那裡，葬在離聖地最近的地方，因此他的葬身之處距耶路撒冷只有一箭之遙。

title.en: The Jewish Boy at the Point of Death
title.zh: 臨終的猶太男孩

region.en: Medina, sickroom of a Jewish boy (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那猶太男孩病榻（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Jana'iz, no. 1356; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Jana'iz, no. 1356 — narrated by Anas ibn Malik

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: A Jewish boy served the Prophet, and when he fell ill the Prophet went to visit him, sat near his head and said to him: 'Embrace Islam.' The boy looked at his father, who was sitting beside him, and the father said: 'Obey Abu al-Qasim.' And the boy said the testimony: 'I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.' The Prophet went out saying: 'Praise be to God who saved him from the Fire.'
summary.zh: 一猶太男孩服侍先知；男孩病重，先知探視，坐於其頭旁，對他說：『你當入伊斯蘭。』男孩望向坐在旁邊的父親；父親說：『聽阿布·卡西姆的話。』男孩遂念清真言：『我作證除真主外別無神明，穆罕默德是其僕人與使者。』先知出門說：『讚美主，他因得救於火獄。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; interfaith dimension noted for comparative study.

passages.text: A young Jewish boy used to serve the Prophet and used to fetch him water for ablution. One day the boy fell ill, and the Prophet went to visit him, sat near his head, and said to him: 'Embrace Islam.' The boy looked at his father, who was sitting with him, and the father said to him, 'Obey Abu al-Qasim.' And the boy embraced Islam. The Prophet went out of the house saying: 'Praise be to God who saved him from the Fire through me.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Jana'iz, no. 1356; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一個猶太少年常侍奉先知，常為他取水作小淨。有一天這少年病了，先知前去探望他，坐在他頭旁，對他說：『你歸信伊斯蘭吧。』少年望向他身旁坐著的父親，父親對他說：『你聽從阿布·卡西姆的話吧。』於是少年歸信了伊斯蘭。先知走出屋子時說：『讚美真主，他藉著我使這少年脫離了火獄。』

title.en: The Man Who Killed Ninety-Nine Souls
title.zh: 殺了九十九人的男子

region.en: Road between two villages of the Israelites (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 以色列人兩村之間的道路（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Tawbah, no. 2766 (variant: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Da'awat, no. 347); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Tawbah, no. 2766 — narrated by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: A man kills ninety-nine people and asks about the possibility of repentance. A monk says there is no way; a worshipper of God says it is possible — 'Go to such a land, for there are people there who worship God, so worship God as they do.' He sets out; death overtakes him on the road. The angel of mercy and the angel of punishment dispute him; God sends a third angel: measure the distance to the two lands, and to whichever he is nearer, to it he belongs. And the earth is ordered to stretch on one side and draw in on the other: he is found nearer the land of obedience — and he is forgiven.
summary.zh: 一人殺了九十九人，求問可否懺悔。一僧言無路；一敬拜者言可——『往某地，那裡有人敬拜主，你便如他們敬拜主。』他啟程，途中遇死。仁慈天使與懲罰天使相爭；主遣第三位：量兩地之距，其近者屬之。大地奉命一側延伸、一側收攏：其近善地——遂蒙赦宥。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: There was among the people of the Israelites a man who had killed ninety-nine people. He asked about the most learned man of the earth, and was directed to a monk; he came to him and said, 'I have killed ninety-nine people; is there any repentance for me?' The monk said, 'No.' So he killed him, and completed one hundred. Then he asked about the most learned man of the earth, and was directed to a worshipper; and he said to him, 'I have killed a hundred men; is there any repentance for me?' He said, 'Yes; nothing can stand between you and repentance. Go to such and such a land, where there are people who worship God; worship God along with them and do not come back to your land, for it is an evil land.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Tawbah, no. 2766; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 以色列人中有一個人，曾殺害九十九人。他打聽大地上最有學問的人，有人指引他去見一位修士；他來到修士面前說：『我已殺了九十九人；我還有懺悔的機會嗎？』修士說：『沒有。』於是他就殺了修士，湊足了一百人。然後他又打聽大地上最有學問的人，有人指引他去見一位修行者；他對那人說：『我已殺了一百人；我還有懺悔的機會嗎？』那人說：『有；沒有任何東西能阻擋你懺悔。你到某某地方去，那裡有崇拜真主的人；你同他們一起崇拜真主，不要回到你的地方，因為那是邪惡之地。』

passages.text: So he set out, and when he had covered half of the way death overtook him. The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed about him. God commanded the earth on either side to draw near, and He commanded the earth he was nearer to draw near, and the other to draw away; then He said: Measure the distance between them. It was found he was nearer the land he was going to by a hand's breadth; so he was forgiven. It was said to Abu Sa'id: While he was in this state, the breath of death came to him, and the earth was commanded to draw him to the land of righteousness.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Tawbah, no. 2766; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是他啟程出發，當他走完一半路程時，死亡降臨於他。慈恩的天使與懲罰的天使為他爭執。真主命令兩側的土地靠近，又命令他較接近的那片土地靠近，另一片則退開；隨後祂說：量一量兩者之間的距離。結果發現他距離所要前往之地較近，僅差一拃之寬；於是他獲得了赦免。有人對阿布·賽義德說：當他處於這種狀態時，死亡的氣息臨到了他，土地奉命將他拉向正義之地。

title.en: Tamim al-Dari's Voyage: The Island of Dajjal
title.zh: 塔米姆·達里的航海：怪者之島

region.en: Open sea, island of the one-eyed man (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 大洋中獨眼人所在之島（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 2937 (long hadith of al-Jassasah); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Fitan wa Ashrat al-Sa'ah, no. 2937 — narrated by Fatima bint Qays

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Tamim al-Dari, a Christian who came to Islam, tells the Prophet of a voyage: a storm carried their ship to an island where they met a shaggy beast, al-Jassasah (the spy), who ran from them, and a huge man bound with heavy chains in a monastery, who asked them news of the spring of Zarka, of the palm-groves of Baysan, of the lake of Tiberias, of the water of the sea, of the Prophet of the Arabs who had appeared. He announces that he is Dajjal, the Antichrist: 'I shall shortly be permitted to come out, and I shall travel the earth in forty days, leaving no town untouched.' The Prophet tells the story in the mosque, and warns of the signs of the Hour.
summary.zh: 已入教的基督徒塔米姆·達里向先知講述其航行：風暴使船漂至一島，遇一毛茸之獸——『窺探者』（賈薩薩），奔走避人；又於修道院見一鎖以重鏈之巨人，詢問魯克泉、貝桑椰棗林、太巴列湖水、海水、以及阿拉伯新出現之先知的消息。他自言即『大騙子』（丹加勒）：『不久我將獲准出來，四十日內遍行大地，無一城不至。』先知在清真寺講述此事，並警示末時之兆。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; apocalyptic imagery treated as text within the tradition.

passages.text: Tamim al-Dari, a man who was a Christian and came to Islam, told the Prophet of a voyage he made: We sailed in the sea till we were carried by a great wind to an island, and we came to a shaggy beast with thick hair, from whose head we could not see his legs. We said, 'Woe to you, what are you?' It said, 'I am al-Jassasah. Go to this man in the monastery.' And when we came to him he was bound with heavy iron chains. He asked us about news of the spring of Zarka, of the date-palms of Baysan, of the lake of Tiberias, of the water of the sea, of the shepherd of the camels of the Arabs, and of the Prophet of the Arabs who has appeared.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 2937; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 塔米姆·達里原是基督徒，後來歸信伊斯蘭，他向先知講述了自己的一次航行：我們在海上航行，直到一陣大風把我們吹到一座島上，我們遇到一頭毛髮濃密的蓬亂野獸，從牠的頭部看不到牠的腿。我們說：『該死，你是什麼？』牠說：『我是賈薩薩。到修道院裡的那個人那裡去吧。』當我們來到他那裡時，他正被沉重的鐵鏈鎖著。他問我們關於扎爾卡泉的消息、關於拜桑的棗椰樹、關於提比里亞湖、關於海水、關於阿拉伯人駱駝的牧人，以及關於已經出現的阿拉伯人先知的消息。

passages.text: The bound man said: 'I am the Dajjal (Antichrist), and I shall shortly be permitted to come out. I shall travel the earth and shall not leave any town without entering it, except Mecca and Medina. And there will be formed for me a door of the city of Medina. And the unbelievers will be with me, and the believers will know me as a believer knows the boy in his mother's lap.' The Prophet told the story in the mosque on the pulpit, and said: 'I have kept you informed of the Dajjal, and Tamim has told me his story.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 2937; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那被鎖住的人說：『我就是達賈勒（敵基督），不久我就獲准出來。我將走遍大地，凡城鎮無不進入，唯有麥加和麥地那除外。麥地那城會為我形成一道門。不信道者將與我同在，而信士會認出我，正如一個信士認出母親懷中的男孩一樣。』先知在清真寺的講壇上講述了這個故事，並說：『我已把達賈勒的事告知你們，塔米姆也把他的故事告訴了我。』

title.en: Ismail's Doorstep and the Kaaba Builders
title.zh: 易司馬儀的門檻與築天房者

region.en: Mecca, Ismail's dwelling (symbolic pin at the Kaaba)
region.zh: 麥加易司馬儀居所（象徵性定位於天房）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Anbiya, no. 3364-3365; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Anbiya, no. 3364-3365 — narrated by Ibn Abbas

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Ibrahim visits Ismail, who has married a woman of the Jurhum. 'Where is your husband?' — 'He has gone to look for food.' 'Give him my salutation and tell him to change the threshold of his gate' — meaning the wife. On a second visit, after the wife has been changed: 'Is your husband at home? Tell him to keep the threshold of his gate.' And on a third visit the two build together the House: Ibrahim stands on a stone, Ismail hands him the stones — and the stone of Ibrahim still bears the prints of his feet.
summary.zh: 易卜拉欣探視已娶主爾胡姆女子為妻的易司馬儀。『你丈夫在哪裡？』——『出外覓食。』『代我問候他，並告訴他換掉門檻』——意指其妻。換妻後再訪：『告訴他守住門檻。』第三次，父子同建天房：易卜拉欣立於一石之上，易司馬儀遞石——易卜拉欣立足之石至今留有其足印。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: Ibrahim came to his son Ismail, whom he had left with his mother Hagar near the Zamzam well, and asked his wife, 'Where has Ismail gone?' She replied, 'He has gone to hunt for us.' He asked about their living and their condition, and she said, 'We live in misery; we are living in hardship and wretchedness,' and she complained to him. He said, 'When your husband returns, give my salutation to him, and tell him to change the threshold of his gate.' When Ismail came, he seemed to have sensed something, and said, 'Did anyone come to you?' She said, 'Yes, an old man of such and such appearance came and asked me about you, and I told him, and he asked about our livelihood, and I told him that we were in a very hard state.' Ismail said, 'Did he advise you anything?' She said, 'Yes, he commanded me to give you his salutation and said: Change the threshold of your gate.' Ismail said, 'It was my father, and he has commanded me to divorce you. Go back to your family.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Anbiya, no. 3364; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 易卜拉欣來到他的兒子易司馬儀那裡——他先前把易司馬儀和他的母親哈哲爾留在滲滲泉旁——他問他的妻子：『易司馬儀到哪裡去了？』她回答說：『他出去為我們打獵了。』他問起他們的生活和境況，她說：『我們生活在困苦之中；我們過著艱難而悲慘的日子。』她向他訴苦。他說：『等你丈夫回來時，替我向他致意，並告訴他更換他門的門檻。』易司馬儀回來時，似乎察覺到了什麼，便說：『有人來過你們這裡嗎？』她說：『是的，一位如此這般模樣的老人來了，問起你的事，我就告訴了他；他又問起我們的生活，我告訴他我們處境極為艱難。』易司馬儀說：『他囑咐了你什麼嗎？』她說：『是的，他命我向你致意，並說：更換你門的門檻。』易司馬儀說：『那是我父親，他命我與你離婚。你回你的娘家去吧。』

passages.text: Then Ibrahim came again after some years and found a new wife, who treated him well and said they lived in plenty. He told her to give his salutation and to tell her husband to keep the threshold of his gate. Ismail said, 'That was my father, and you are the threshold; he has commanded me to keep you.' Then the two built the House: Ibrahim stood on the stone (Maqam Ibrahim) and Ismail handed him the stones, and Ibrahim laid them until the wall was raised, and they prayed: 'Our Lord, accept this from us.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Anbiya, no. 3365; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 後來，易卜拉欣在若干年後又來了，發現了一位新妻子，她善待他，並說他們生活富足。他吩咐她替他致意，並告訴她丈夫要保留他門的門檻。易司馬儀說：『那是我父親，而你就是那門檻；他命我留住你。』隨後兩人建造了這座房屋：易卜拉欣站在石上（易卜拉欣立足處），易司馬儀把石頭遞給他，易卜拉欣將石頭砌上，直到牆壁築起，他們祈禱說：『我們的主啊，求祢接受我們的這一善功。』

title.en: Created From a Rib: Kindness to Women
title.zh: 造自肋骨：善待婦女

region.en: Medina, teaching during pilgrimage (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那朝覲時的教導（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Nikah, no. 5185 (variant: Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 5186); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Nikah, no. 5185 — narrated by Abu Hurayrah

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day must not hurt his neighbour. And the woman was created from a rib: you will not be able to set her straight in one straight line, but if you take care of her you will benefit; and if you try to straighten her, you will break her, and breaking her is divorcing her. Treat women kindly, for the best of men is he who is best to his wife.
summary.zh: 凡信主與末日者，勿傷其鄰。女子造自肋骨：你無法使其完全正直，若善待之則得益；若強使之直則折之，折之即離婚。善待婦女；男人中之最優者，乃善於待其妻者。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; gender imagery is read here as an ethical metaphor within the tradition's own frame.

passages.text: The Prophet said: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day should not hurt his neighbour; and he said: Treat women kindly, for woman has been created from a rib, and the most crooked part of the rib is the upper part; if you try to straighten it you will break it, and if you leave it as it is, it will remain crooked; so treat women kindly.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Nikah, no. 5185; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 先知說：凡信仰真主與末日者，不可傷害他的鄰居；他又說：你們要善待婦女，因為婦女是由肋骨創造的，而肋骨最彎曲的部分是上端；你若想把它弄直，就會折斷它；你若任其自然，它便依然彎曲；所以你們要善待婦女。

title.en: The Prophet's Swollen Feet in Night Prayer
title.zh: 先知夜禮中的腫足

region.en: Medina, Aisha's chamber (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那阿伊莎的居室（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tahajjud, no. 1127 (variant: no. 4837); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tahajjud, no. 1127 — narrated by Aisha

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Aisha finds the Prophet praying in the night until his feet become swollen. 'Why do you do this, when God has forgiven you your former and latter sins?' He answers: 'Should I not be a thankful servant?' And once when she thinks of the days and nights of prayer, she is told: 'Your body has a right over you, and your family has a right over you — so observe the fast and also break it, and pray and also sleep.'
summary.zh: 阿伊莎見先知夜禮至雙足腫脹。『主已赦你前後之罪，何故如此？』他答：『我豈不當做一感恩的僕人？』又有一夜她想及日夜禮拜之事，被告知：『你的身體對你有權利，你的家屬對你也有權利——當齋戒亦開齋，當禮拜亦睡眠。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: One night the Prophet was engaged in prayer till his feet became swollen. When he was asked, 'Why do you undergo such hardships, although all your past and future sins have been forgiven?' he said: 'Should I not be a thankful servant of God?' And on another occasion he was found praying in the night, and Aisha asked him about his standing so long, and he said: 'I said: Should I not be a grateful servant of God?'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tahajjud, no. 1127; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一夜，先知持續禮拜，直到雙腳腫脹。有人問他：「你為何承受這樣的辛苦，儘管你過去和未來的罪都已蒙赦免？」他說：「我難道不該做真主感恩的僕人嗎？」另有一次，有人發現他在夜間禮拜，阿伊莎問他為何站立如此之久，他說：「我說：我難道不該做真主感恩的僕人嗎？」

passages.text: The deeds most loved by God are those done regularly, even if they are few. And he said to Aisha: 'Your body has a right over you, and your family has a right over you; so observe the fast and also break the fast, and pray at night and also sleep.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tahajjud, no. 1127 (closing tradition); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 真主最喜愛的行為是持之以恆的行為，即使為數不多。他對阿伊莎說：「你的身體對你有權利，你的家人對你有權利；所以你要封齋，也要開齋；要夜間禮拜，也要睡覺。」

title.en: Hudhayfa's Questioning: Signs of the Last Hour
title.zh: 胡達法的追問：末時之兆

region.en: Medina, evening gathering (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那晚間聚會（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7086 (variant: no. 6502); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7086 — narrated by Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: People ask Hudhayfa what good he gathered from the Prophet, and he says he was with him among the Companions and asked about evil: 'O Prophet of God, we were in ignorance and evil, and God has brought this good to us; will there be any evil after this good?' He said: 'Yes.' 'And will there be any good after this evil?' 'Yes, but it will be tainted.' 'And will there be any evil after it?' 'Yes, call to prayer will be heard from it, but the callers are not rightly guided; there will be mountains of reeds.'
summary.zh: 眾人問胡達法從先知處得了什麼；他說曾在聖門弟子中，曾問惡事：『主的先知啊，我們本處於愚昧與惡之中，主降此善於我們；此善之後還有惡嗎？』——『有。』『此惡之後還有善嗎？』——『有，但混雜不純。』『其後還有惡嗎？』——『有：其中將聞宣禮聲，而宣禮者不受正導。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; apocalyptic signs kept as spoken in the text.

passages.text: Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman said: People used to ask the Prophet about good, but I used to ask him about evil, fearing lest it overtake me. I said, 'O Prophet of God, we were in ignorance and evil, and God has brought this good to us; will there be any evil after this good?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And will there be any good after this evil?' He said, 'Yes, but it will be tainted.' I said, 'How will it be tainted?' He said, 'There will be people who will lead others according to a path other than my tradition; you will hear of their acts and disapprove of them.' I said, 'And will there be evil after this good?' He said, 'Yes: callers at the gates of Hell; whoever responds to their call will be thrown into the fire.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7086; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 胡載法·伊本·葉曼說：人們常向先知詢問善事，而我常向他詢問惡事，唯恐惡事臨到我。我說：「真主的先知啊，我們曾處於無知與邪惡之中，真主把這善帶給了我們；這善之後還會有惡嗎？」他說：「有。」我說：「這惡之後還會有善嗎？」他說：「有，但會摻雜。」我說：「如何摻雜？」他說：「會有一些人，引導他人遵循我的傳統之外的道路；你會聽到他們的行為，並加以反對。」我說：「這善之後還會有惡嗎？」他說：「有：火獄門前的召喚者；誰響應他們的召喚，誰就會被投入火中。」

passages.text: I said, 'O Prophet of God, describe them for us.' He said, 'They are from our people, and they will speak our language.' I said, 'What do you command me to do if that should happen?' He said, 'Adhere to the community of the Muslims and their leader.' I said, 'What if they have neither community nor leader?' He said, 'Keep away from all those sects, even if you have to bite the root of a tree until death comes to you while you are in that state.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7086; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我說：「真主的先知啊，請為我們描述他們。」他說：「他們出自我們的人，說我們的語言。」我說：「若此事發生，你命令我怎麼做？」他說：「緊守穆斯林共同體及其領袖。」我說：「若他們既無共同體也無領袖呢？」他說：「遠離所有那些派別，即使你必須咬住樹根，直到死亡降臨於你，而你仍處於那樣的狀態。」

title.en: The Race With Aisha
title.zh: 與阿伊莎賽跑

region.en: Abwa, on the road between Mecca and Medina (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥加麥地那之間的阿布瓦（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sunan Abu Dawud, Kitab al-Adab, no. 2578; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sunan Abu Dawud, Kitab al-Adab, no. 2578 — narrated by Aisha

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The Prophet races with Aisha and she beats him; later, when she has put on weight, she races him again and he wins. 'This is for that' — the earlier victory is repaid. The tale belongs to the Prophet's domestic tenderness, remembered after his death.
summary.zh: 先知與阿伊莎賽跑，她勝了他；日後她體重增加再賽，他勝了她。『這次抵那次』——早先之勝得以償還。此軼事屬先知家庭的溫情，死後猶為人記。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: Aisha said: I raced with the Prophet and beat him in the race. Later, when I had put on weight, I raced with him again, and he beat me. He said: 'This is for that previous race of yours.' The Prophet races with Aisha and she beats him; later, when she has put on weight, she races him again and he wins.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sunan Abu Dawud, Kitab al-Adab, no. 2578; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿伊莎說：我曾與先知賽跑，在比賽中勝過他。後來，當我體重增加後，我又與他賽跑，他勝過了我。他說：「這是抵償你先前那一次賽跑。」先知與阿伊莎賽跑，她勝過他；後來，當她體重增加後，她再次與他賽跑，他贏了。

title.en: Whither Thou Goest: Ruth Gleans in Boaz's Field
title.zh: 你往哪裡去我也去：路得在波阿斯田拾穗

region.en: Bethlehem, fields of Judah
region.zh: 伯利恆，猶大田間

period: Narrative set in the era of the Judges; composed c. 6th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Ruth 1-2, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Famine drives Elimelech's family to Moab; the men die, and Naomi returns home orphaned, telling her daughters-in-law to go back. Ruth's answer is one of the most quoted loyalties in literature: 'Whither thou goest, I will go... thy God my God'. In Bethlehem's barley harvest she gleans in the field of Boaz, who commands the harvesters to leave handfuls on purpose for 'the Moabite damsel'.
summary.zh: 饑荒驅以利米勒家往摩押；男丁盡亡，拿俄米喪夫喪子而歸，勸二媳回娘家。路得之答為文學中著名忠誠：「你往哪裡去，我也往那裡去……你的神就是我的神。」伯利恆割大麥時，她在波阿斯的田裡拾穗；波阿斯吩咐僕人「為那摩押女子留下」一把一把的麥穗。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Ruth is read at Shavuot; her loyalty (chesed) frames the book's theology.

passages.text: And Ruth said: 'Entreat me not to leave thee, and to return from following after thee; for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge; thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God; where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried; the LORD do so to me, and more also, if aught but death part thee and me.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Ruth 1:16-17 (public domain).
passages.zh: 路得說：「不要催我離開你，不要叫我轉回不跟隨你；因為你往哪裡去，我也往哪裡去；你在哪裡住宿，我也在哪裡住宿；你的民就是我的民，你的神就是我的神；你在哪裡死，我也在哪裡死，也葬在那裡；除非死能使你我相離，不然，願耶和華重重地降罰於我。」

passages.text: Boaz told her to keep close to his maidens and drink of the water the young men had drawn: 'The LORD recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to take refuge'. At meal he handed her parched corn, and she 'did eat, and was sufficed, and left thereof'. Naomi read the field's owner as the family's redeemer — a near kinsman. Paraphrase of Ruth 2:8-20 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ruth 2:8-20 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 波阿斯吩咐她緊隨他的使女，並喝少年人所打來的水：「願耶和華照你所行的賞賜你，你來投靠耶和華以色列神的翅膀下，願你滿得他的賞賜。」吃飯時，他把烘了的穗子遞給她，她「吃了，吃飽了，還有餘剩的」。拿俄米看出那田主是這家的至親——一個近親。改述《路得記》2:8-20（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Spread Thy Skirt Over Thy Handmaid: The Threshing Floor
title.zh: 求你用你的衣襟遮蓋僕人：禾場之夜

region.en: Threshing floor of Bethlehem
region.zh: 伯利恆的禾場

period: Narrative set in the era of the Judges; composed c. 6th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Ruth 3, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Naomi sends Ruth, washed and anointed, to the threshing floor by night to 'uncover his feet' and lie down. Waking at midnight, Boaz trembles — 'who art thou?' — 'I am Ruth thine handmaid... for thou art a near kinsman'. He blesses her kindness 'more than at the beginning', names the nearer kinsman obstacle, and loads her with six measures of barley before dawn.
summary.zh: 拿俄米遣沐浴抹膏的路得夜至禾場，「掀開他腳上的被」，躺臥其旁。半夜波阿斯驚起——「你是誰？」——「我是你的婢女路得……因為你是至近的親屬」。他祝福她的恩慈「比先前更大」，指出更近的親屬為難處，天亮前給她六簸箕大麥。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. 'Spread thy skirt' is proposal-language of protection/levirate rights.

passages.text: And it came to pass at midnight, that the man was startled, and turned over; and, behold, a woman lay at his feet. And he said: 'Who art thou?' And she answered: 'I am Ruth thine handmaid; spread therefore thy skirt over thy handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman.' And he said: 'Blessed be thou of the LORD, my daughter; for thou hast shown more kindness in the end than at the beginning.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Ruth 3:8-10 (public domain).
passages.zh: 到了半夜，那人忽然驚醒，翻過身來；不料，有女子躺在他的腳下。他就說：「你是誰？」她回答說：「我是你的婢女路得；求你用你的衣襟遮蓋你的婢女，因為你是一個至近的親屬。」他說：「女兒啊，願你蒙耶和華賜福；你末後的恩比先前更大。」

title.en: Sandals at the Gate: The Kinsman Redeemer
title.zh: 城門口脫鞋：至近的親屬

region.en: Gate of Bethlehem
region.zh: 伯利恆城門口

period: Narrative set in the era of the Judges; composed c. 6th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Ruth 4, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Boaz convenes ten elders at the gate; the nearer kinsman renounces Elimelech's field when it carries Ruth with it — the shoe drawn and given as witness. 'So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife.' Obed is born, and the women bless Naomi: 'The LORD hath not left thee this day without a redeemer' — and the book closes with the genealogy that runs to David.
summary.zh: 波阿斯在城門口召十位長老；更近的親屬因田帶著路得而放棄——脫鞋為證。「波阿斯娶了路得為妻」。俄備得出生，婦女們祝福拿俄米：「耶和華是應當稱頌的，因為今日沒有撇下你無至近的親屬」——書末譜系直達大衛。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Levirate-marriage and sandal exchange are legal custom etiologies.

passages.text: And this was the custom in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning exchanging, to confirm all things: a man drew off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbour; and this was the manner of attestation in Israel. So the near kinsman said unto Boaz: 'Buy it for thee'; and he drew off his shoe.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Ruth 4:7-8 (public domain).
passages.zh: 從前在以色列中要定奪什麼事，或贖或換，有這樣的規矩：這人就要脫鞋給那人；以色列中以此為證據。那至近的親屬就對波阿斯說：「你自己買吧」；於是他把鞋脫下來了。

title.en: Hadassah Who Hid Her Name: Esther Made Queen
title.zh: 隱名的哈大沙：以斯帖封后

region.en: Susa, Persian royal citadel
region.zh: 書珊，波斯王城

period: Narrative set c. 5th-4th c. BCE (Ahasuerus/Xerxes era); composed c. 4th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Esther 1-2, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Ahasuerus's hundred-and-eighty-day banquet ends with Queen Vashti refusing to parade her beauty and losing her throne. Orphaned Hadassah, 'and her Hebrew name was Esther', is gathered into the harem of the citadel at Shushan under Mordecai's watch; she tells 'not her people nor her kindred, for Mordecai had charged her'. The king loves her above all the women, 'and he set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen'. Mordecai overhears an assassination plot and is recorded in the chronicles.
summary.zh: 亞哈隨魯一百八十日大宴，王后瓦實提拒絕展示美貌而失位。孤兒哈大沙——希伯來名以斯帖——在末底改囑咐下入書珊城宮，'不將籍贯宗族告訴人'。王愛她過於眾女，「把王后的冠冕戴在她頭上，立她為王后」。末底改偷聽弒君陰謀，事跡記於王上記錄。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Purim narrative origin; read with noise-making (graggers) at the Megillah.

passages.text: And the king loved Esther more than all the women, and she obtained grace and favour in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Esther 2:17 (public domain).
passages.zh: 王愛以斯帖過於愛眾女，她在王眼前蒙寵愛比眾處女更甚；王就把王后的冠冕戴在她頭上，立她為王后，代替瓦實提。

passages.text: Esther was orphaned, 'the daughter of his father's brother', and 'Mordecai took her for his own daughter'. 'Esther had not made known her people nor her kindred; for Mordecai had charged her that she should not make it known.' In the king's gate Mordecai sat daily to learn her welfare — the careful concealment that makes the rescue to come possible. Paraphrase of Esther 2:5-11 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Esther 2:5-11 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 以斯帖是孤兒，是「他父親的兄弟的女兒」，而「末底改收養她為自己的女兒」。「以斯帖未曾將籍貫宗族告訴人，因為末底改囑咐她不可叫人知道。」末底改天天坐在王門口，要知道她的平安——這番小心的隱瞞，使後來的拯救得以成就。改述《以斯帖記》2:5-11（JPS 1917）；非逐字引用。

title.en: Haman's Lot and the Genocide Decree
title.zh: 哈曼的籤與滅族詔書

region.en: Susa, gate and citadel
region.zh: 書珊，城門與王城

period: Narrative set c. 5th-4th c. BCE; composed c. 4th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Esther 3-4, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Mordecai will not bow to Haman the Agagite; fury builds until Haman casts lots (pur) for the day — the thirteenth of Adar — and wins the king's ring to write the decree of destruction for 'a certain people scattered and dispersed among the peoples... whose laws are diverse from every people'. Mordecai's message to Esther ends: 'who knoweth whether thou art not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?' Esther fasts three days and enters unbidden: 'if I perish, I perish.'
summary.zh: 末底改不跪哈曼；怒氣積至哈曼掣普珥籤定十二月十三日，取得王戒寫滅族詔——針對「散居各國的那一民，他們的律例與萬民不同」。末底改寄語以斯帖：「焉知你得了王位，不是為現今的機會麼？」以斯帖禁食三日，未召擅入：「我若死就死吧。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Purim's fast of Esther and the reading cycle recall this decree.

passages.text: And Mordecai told him to tell Esther: 'Think not with thyself that thou shalt escape in the king's house, more than all the Jews. For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then will relief and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place, but thou and thy father's house will perish; and who knoweth whether thou art not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Esther 4:13-14 (public domain).
passages.zh: 末底改吩咐他去告訴以斯帖：「你莫想在王宮裡強過一切猶大人，得免這禍。此時你若閉口不言，猶大人必從別處得解脫、蒙拯救，你和你父家必至滅亡；焉知你得了王后的位分，不是為現今的機會嗎？」

passages.text: 'Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me... I also and my maidens will fast in like manner; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law; and if I perish, I perish.' For three days the city's Jews fasted 'with fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes'. Paraphrase of Esther 4:15-17; 3:8-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Esther 4:15-17; 3:8-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「你去招聚書珊城所有的猶大人，為我禁食……我和我的宮女也要這樣禁食；然後我違例進去見王；我若死就死吧。」城中猶大人禁食三日，「禁食、哭泣、哀號，多人穿麻衣躺臥在灰中」。以斯帖記四章十五至十七節、三章八至十五節（JPS 1917）之釋義；非逐字引用。

title.en: The Banquets of Wine and the Gallows of Fifty Cubits
title.zh: 酒宴與五十肘木架

region.en: Susa, palace gardens
region.zh: 書珊，王宮園囿

period: Narrative set c. 5th-4th c. BCE; composed c. 4th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Esther 5-7, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Esther invites the king and Haman to a wine-banquet, then to a second; between the two, sleepless Ahasuerus is read the chronicles and learns Mordecai was never rewarded. The king asks Haman: 'What shall be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour?' — and Haman, certain it is himself, prescribes the royal horse and robe, then wears the humiliation home. At the second banquet Esther names the plot, and Haman is hanged on the very gallows he built for Mordecai.
summary.zh: 以斯帖兩次設酒宴請王與哈曼；其間失眠的亞哈隨魯聞記錄而得知末底改未受報賞。王問哈曼：「王所喜悅尊榮的人，當將他如何待呢？」——哈曼自以為是，獻上王服御馬之禮，回家蒙羞。二次宴上以斯帖道破陰謀；哈曼被掛在他為末底改所預備的木架上。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Haman answered the king: 'For the man whom the king delighteth to honour, let the royal apparel be brought which the king useth to wear, and the horse that the king rideth upon... and let the apparel and the horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king's most noble princes, that they may array the man withal whom the king delighteth to honour, and cause him to ride on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaim before him: Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delighteth to honour.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Esther 6:7-9 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 哈曼回答王說：「王所喜悅尊榮的人，當將王常穿的朝服和戴冠的御馬帶來……將朝服和馬交在王極尊貴的一個大臣手中，命他將朝服給王所喜悅尊榮的人穿上，使他騎上馬，走遍城裡的街市，在他面前宣告說：王所喜悅尊榮的人，就如此待他。」

passages.text: At the second banquet Esther unveiled: 'we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed... for we are sold into death'. The king left the chamber in fury; Haman fell on the queen's couch pleading — and the king returned to the accusation, 'Will he even force the queen before me in the house?' Harbonah mentioned the fifty-cubit gallows at Haman's house; 'hang him thereon' — 'so they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai; then was the king's wrath pacified.' Paraphrase of Esther 7:1-10 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Esther 7:1-10 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在第二次筵席上，以斯帖揭露說：「我與我本族被賣了，要剪除……因為我們被賣入死地。」王大怒離席而去；哈曼伏在王后榻前哀求——王回來見狀便說：「他竟敢在我家中凌辱王后嗎？」哈波拿提到哈曼家中那五十肘高的木架；「將他掛在上面」——「於是哈曼被掛在他為末底改所預備的木架上；王的忿怒這才止息。」以斯帖記七章一至十節（JPS 1917）之釋義；非逐字引用。

title.en: Days of Purim: Mordecai's Letters
title.zh: 普珥日：末底改的書信

region.en: Susa and all Persian provinces
region.zh: 書珊與波斯全境

period: Narrative set c. 5th-4th c. BCE; composed c. 4th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Esther 8-9, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Esther's counter-decree lets the Jews defend themselves; Mordecai in royal apparel goes out from the king's presence, 'and the city of Shushan shouted and was glad'. The fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar are fixed by letters 'sent among all the Jews... as days of feasting and joy, and sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor' — Purim instituted, and the book's own name ('these words, the Purim') canonized in the story's last verses.
summary.zh: 以斯帖的對等詔書准猶太人自衛；末底改穿朝服出王門，「書珊城的人民都歡呼快樂」。亞達月十四、十五日由書信定為「設筵歡樂、彼此饋送禮物、賙濟窮人」之日——普珥節設立，書末經文自身（「這就是普珥節」）被收錄於故事之中。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Purim is a living festival; the record describes the institution narrative.

passages.text: Therefore they called these days Purim, after the name of Pur. Therefore because of all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come unto them, the Jews established, and took upon them, and upon their seed, and upon all such as joined themselves unto them, so that it should not fail, that they would keep these two days according to the writing thereof, and according to the appointed time thereof, every year.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Esther 9:26-27 (public domain).
passages.zh: 因此，他們照著「普珥」的名字，稱這兩日為普珥日。所以，因這信上的話，又因他們所看見、所遭遇的事，猶大人立定並擔負在自己和後裔，以及一切歸附他們的人身上，使這兩個日子永不廢去，每年按時照著所寫的、所定的守這兩個日子。

title.en: Daniel Refuses the King's Portion
title.zh: 但以理不食王膳

region.en: Babylon, royal court
region.zh: 巴比倫，王宮

period: Narrative set c. 6th c. BCE (exilic era); composed c. 6th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Daniel 1, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Exiled youths of Judah's royal seed are renamed for Babylon's gods; Daniel resolves 'that he would not defile himself with the king's dainties'. His test of ten days' pulse and water ends with faces 'fairer, and fatter in flesh' than all who ate the king's food — 'and God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom'.
summary.zh: 猶大王室被擄少年被改名歸巴比倫諸神；但以理立志「不以王的膳和王所飲的酒玷污自己」。十日素菜白水的試驗，他們的面貌「比用王膳的一切少年人更加俊美肥胖」——「神在各樣文字學問上賜給他們聰明知識」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And at the end of ten days their countenances appeared fairer, and they were fatter in flesh, than all the youths that did eat of the king's dainties. ... And as for these four youths, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom; and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Daniel 1:15, 17 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 過了十天，見他們的面貌比用王膳的一切少年人更加俊美肥胖。……這四個少年人，神在各樣學問、智慧上賜給他們知識和聰明；但以理又明白各樣的異象和夢兆。

title.en: The Great Image of Nebuchadnezzar's Dream
title.zh: 尼布甲尼撒大像之夢

region.en: Babylon, royal court
region.zh: 巴比倫，王宮

period: Narrative set c. 6th c. BCE; composed c. 6th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Daniel 2, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Nebuchadnezzar demands that his wise men reveal both dream and interpretation; all fail and the decree of death goes out. Daniel prays with his friends and receives the secret 'in a vision of the night'. Before the king he recounts the great image — head of gold, breast of silver, belly of brass, legs of iron, feet of iron and clay — smitten by a stone 'cut out without hands' that fills the whole earth: 'there is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets.'
summary.zh: 尼布甲尼撒命哲士顯明夢與講解；皆不能，殺令已出。但以理與同伴祈禱，夜間異象中得奧秘。他在王前述大像——金頭、銀胸、銅腹、鐵腿、半鐵半泥的腳——被「非人手鑿出來的石頭」擊碎，那石頭變成充滿天下的大山：「天上的神能顯明奧秘的事。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Four-kingdoms schema foundational to Jewish and Christian apocalyptic.

passages.text: Thou, O king, sawest, and, behold, a great image. This image, which was mighty, and whose brightness was surpassing, stood before thee; and the look thereof was terrible. As for that image, the head thereof was of fine gold, its breast and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of brass, its legs of iron, its feet part of iron and part of clay.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Daniel 2:31-33 (public domain).
passages.zh: 王啊，你觀看，見有一個大像。這像甚高，極其光耀，站在你面前；形狀甚是可怕。這像的頭是精金的，胸膛和膀臂是銀的，肚腹和腰是銅的，腿是鐵的，腳是半鐵半泥的。

passages.text: 'Thou sawest till that a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon its feet... and the gold, the silver, the brass, the iron, the clay... became like the chaff of the summer threshing-floors; and the wind carried them away... and the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.' Nebuchadnezzar fell upon his face and exalted Daniel, setting him over the province of Babylon. Paraphrase of Daniel 2:34-49 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Daniel 2:34-49 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「你觀看，見有一塊非人手鑿出來的石頭打在像的腳上……金、銀、銅、鐵、泥……都一同砸得粉碎，成如夏天禾場上的糠秕，被風吹散……打碎這像的石頭變成一座大山，充滿天下。」尼布甲尼撒俯伏在地，尊崇但以理，派他管理巴比倫全省。改述自《但以理書》2:34-49（JPS 1917），非逐字引用。

title.en: The Fourth Man in the Fire
title.zh: 火中的第四人

region.en: Plain of Dura, Babylon
region.zh: 杜拉平原，巴比倫

period: Narrative set c. 6th c. BCE; composed c. 6th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Daniel 3, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: All nations must bow at the music to the golden image on the plain of Dura. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego answer: 'our God... is able to deliver us... but if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods'. Cast bound into the furnace heated sevenfold, they walk unbound in the flames — and the king sees 'a fourth man... like to a son of the gods' walking with them. The fire has 'no smell of fire' upon their clothes.
summary.zh: 樂聲一起，各族都當拜杜拉平原的金像。沙得拉、米煞、亞伯尼歌答：「我們的神能救我們……即或不然，王啊，你當知道我們決不事奉你的神。」被捆著扔進七倍的火窰，他們在火中自由行走——王見「第四個……好像神子」與他們同行。他們衣服上火燎的氣味也沒有。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonished, and rose up in haste, and spoke, and said unto his counsellors: 'Did not we cast three men bound into the midst of the fire?' They answered and said unto the king: 'True, O king.' He answered and said: 'But I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Daniel 3:24-25 (public domain).
passages.zh: 那時，尼布甲尼撒王驚奇，急忙起來，對他的謀士說：「我們豈不是捆了三個人扔在火裡嗎？」他們回答王說：「王啊，是的。」他回答說：「看哪，我見有四個人，並沒有捆綁，在火中行走，也沒有受傷；那第四個的相貌好像神子。」

title.en: Mene, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin: The Hand on the Wall
title.zh: 彌尼彌尼提客勒烏法珥新：牆上的手

region.en: Great hall of Belshazzar's feast, Babylon
region.zh: 伯沙撒宴會大廳，巴比倫

period: Narrative set 539 BCE; composed c. 6th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Daniel 5, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Belshazzar toasts his gods from the vessels of the Jerusalem Temple — 'and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone' — when fingers come forth and write on the plaster. None can read it; the queen mother remembers Daniel. The judgment: 'MENE, God hath numbered thy kingdom... TEKEL, thou art weighed in the balances... PERES, thy kingdom is divided'. That night Belshazzar is slain and Darius the Mede takes the kingdom.
summary.zh: 伯沙撒用耶路撒冷聖殿的器皿飲酒，「讚美金銀銅鐵木石所造的神」——手指顯現於粉牆寫字。無人能讀；太后想起但以理。審判：「彌尼，就是神已經數算你國的年日……提客勒，就是被秤在天平裡顯出你的虧欠……毘勒斯，就是你的國分裂」。當夜伯沙撒被殺，瑪代人大流士取國。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: In the same hour came forth fingers of a man's hand, and wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaster of the wall of the king's palace; and the king saw the palm of the hand that wrote. Then the king's countenance was changed in him, and his thoughts affrighted him; and the joints of his loins were loosed, and his knees smote one against another.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Daniel 5:5-6 (public domain).
passages.zh: 當時，忽有人的指頭顯出，在王宮與燈臺相對的粉牆上寫字；王看見寫字的手掌。於是王的面色改變，他的意念驚嚇他；他的腰骨好像脫節，雙膝彼此相碰。

title.en: Daniel in the Lions' Den
title.zh: 但以理在獅子坑中

region.en: Babylon, den of lions
region.zh: 巴比倫，獅子坑

period: Narrative set c. 6th-5th c. BCE; composed c. 6th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Daniel 6, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Envious presidents frame an irrevocable law: prayer to any god or man but the king for thirty days is lion-food. Daniel, knowing it, opens his windows toward Jerusalem and prays three times a day 'as he did aforetime'. Cast into the den, he is sealed in overnight; at dawn the king cries: 'O Daniel, servant of the living God... is thy God able to deliver thee?' — 'My God hath sent His angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths.' The accusers go in instead, and Darius decrees the God of Daniel 'the living God, and stedfast for ever'.
summary.zh: 嫉妒的總長設立不可更改之令：三十日內凡向王以外的神或人祈禱者，必扔獅坑。但以理知道這禁令，仍面向耶路撒冷開窗，一日三次禱告「與素常一樣」。被扔坑中，封石過夜；黎明王呼：「活神的僕人但以理啊……你的神能救你脫離獅子麼？」——「我的神差遣使者，封住獅子的口。」控告者反倒被扔進去；大流士降旨宣認「活神，永遠長存」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then said Daniel unto the king: 'O king, live for ever. My God hath sent His angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me; forasmuch as before Him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.' ... So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he had trusted in his God.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Daniel 6:21-23 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 但以理對王說：「願王萬歲！我的神差遣使者，封住獅子的口，叫獅子不傷我；因我在神面前無辜，我在王面前也沒有行過虧損的事。」……於是但以理從坑裡被提上來，身上毫無傷損，因為他信靠他的神。

title.en: Four Beasts and the Ancient of Days
title.zh: 四獸與亙古常在者

region.en: Heavenly court (vision; symbolic pin at Babylon)
region.zh: 天庭（異象；以巴比倫象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 6th-2nd c. BCE (vision dated to first year of Belshazzar); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Daniel 7, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Four great beasts rise from the churning sea — lion with eagle's wings, bear, leopard with four wings, and a terrifying fourth with iron teeth and ten horns. 'The Ancient of Days did sit, whose raiment was white as snow, and the hair of His head like pure wool': judgment sits, the books are opened, the fourth beast burns. 'I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like a son of man came with the clouds of heaven... and there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom.'
summary.zh: 四巨獸自攪動的海中上來——鷹翼獅、熊、四翼豹、十角鐵齒的可怕第四獸。「亙古常在者坐著，衣服潔白如雪，頭髮如純淨的羊毛」：審判設立，案卷展開，第四獸焚燒。「我在夜間的異象中觀看，見有一位像人子的，駕著天雲而來……得了權柄、榮耀、國度。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The four-kingdoms vision anchors apocalyptic eschatology in Jewish and Christian tradition.

passages.text: I beheld till thrones were placed, and One that was Ancient of Days did sit; His raiment was as white snow, and the hair of His head like pure wool; His throne was fiery flames, and the wheels thereof burning fire. A fiery stream issued and came forth from before Him; thousand thousands ministered unto Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him; the judgment was set, and the books were opened.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Daniel 7:9-10 (public domain).
passages.zh: 我觀看，見有寶座設立，那亙古常在者坐著；他的衣服潔白如雪，頭髮如純淨的羊毛；他的寶座乃是火焰，其輪乃是烈火。從他面前有火，像河發出；事奉他的有千千，在他面前侍立的有萬萬；審判已經坐堂，案卷都展開了。

passages.text: The son-of-man figure receives 'dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion... which shall not be destroyed'. The vision's angel-interpreter explains the beasts as kings and kingdoms, with the saints of the Most High inheriting at the end. Paraphrase of Daniel 7:13-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Daniel 7:13-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那像人子的形象得了「權柄、榮耀、國度，使各方、各國、各族的人都事奉他：他的權柄是永遠的權柄……必不廢壞」。異象中解釋的天使說明那些獸就是諸王與諸國，至高者的聖民最終要承受國度。改述自《但以理書》7:13-27（JPS 1917），非逐字引用。

title.en: Jonah Flees, the Sea Rages, and the Fish Waits
title.zh: 約拿逃避，海翻騰，大魚等候

region.en: Mediterranean off Joppa (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 約帕外的地中海（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 5th-4th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Jonah 1-2, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Ordered to cry against Nineveh, Jonah rises to flee to Tarshish — 'from the presence of the LORD'. A great wind; the mariners cast lots and find the Hebrew passenger, asleep below: 'What meanest thou, O thou sleeper?' Thrown overboard at his own insistence, 'and the sea ceased from her raging' — and 'the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.' From the deep he prays; the fish vomits him on dry land.
summary.zh: 受命往尼尼微呼喊，約拿卻起身逃往他施——「躲避耶和華」。大風驟起；水手掣籤尋出這希伯來乘客，他在船底沉睡：「你這沉睡的人哪，這是怎樣呢？」依他自己的話被拋入海，海便平靜——「耶和華安排一條大魚吞了約拿；他在魚腹中三日三夜」。他在深處禱告；魚把他吐在旱地上。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Jonah read complete on Yom Kippur afternoon; the fish-belly prayer is penitential.

passages.text: And he said unto them: 'Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you; for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you.' ... So they took up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea; and the sea ceased from her raging. ... And the LORD prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Jonah 1:12, 15, 17 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 他便對他們說：「你們將我抬起，拋入海中，海就會為你們平靜下來；因為我知道，這大風暴臨到你們，是因我的緣故。」……於是他們將約拿抬起，拋入海中；海就止住了狂濤。……耶和華預備了一條大魚吞下約拿；約拿在魚腹中三日三夜。

passages.text: From the belly he prayed: 'I called by reason of mine affliction, unto the LORD... The waters compassed me about, even to the soul; the deep was round about me... yet hast Thou brought up my life from the pit, O LORD my God.' 'And the LORD spoke unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.' Paraphrase of Jonah 2:1-10 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Jonah 2:1-10 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他從魚腹中禱告說：「我因所受的苦難呼求耶和華……眾水環繞我，幾乎淹沒我的性命；深淵圍困我……然而，耶和華我的神啊，你卻將我的性命從坑中救上來。」「耶和華吩咐那魚，魚就把約拿吐在旱地上。」此為約拿書二章一至十節（JPS 1917）之釋義，非逐字引文。

title.en: The Repentance of Nineveh and the Gourd
title.zh: 尼尼微悔改與蓖麻樹

region.en: Nineveh, great city on the Tigris
region.zh: 尼尼微，底格里斯河大城

period: Composed c. 5th-4th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Jonah 3-4, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The second commission succeeds absurdly: one day's preaching and 'the men of Nineveh believed God... from the greatest of them even to the least of them' — even the cattle fast in sackcloth. God relents, and Jonah sulks: 'it displeased Jonah exceedingly'. Under his booth God grows a gourd for shade, then smites it with a worm; Jonah's pity for the plant draws the book's closing question: 'Should not I have pity on Nineveh, that great city... and also much cattle?'
summary.zh: 第二次使命荒謬地成功：一天的呼喊，尼尼微人「信服神……從最大的到至小的」——連牲畜都披麻禁食。神後悔不滅，約拿發怒大大不悅。棚下神使蓖麻生長遮蔭，又以蟲咬之枯；約拿為樹惜命，書末神問：「這尼尼微大城……我豈能不愛惜呢？何況其中……並許多牲畜呢？」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and there made him a booth, and sat under it in the shadow, till he might see what would become of the city. And the LORD God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shadow over his head. ... And God said to Jonah: 'Doest thou well to be angry for the gourd?' ... Then said the LORD: 'Thou hast had pity on the gourd... and should not I have pity on Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons... and also much cattle?'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Jonah 4:5-11 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 約拿出城，坐在城的東邊，在那裡為自己搭了一座棚，坐在棚的蔭下，要看看那城究竟如何。耶和華神預備了一棵蓖麻，使它長高過約拿，好作他頭上的蔭蔽。……神對約拿說：「你因這棵蓖麻發怒，合乎理嗎？」……耶和華又說：「你尚且愛惜這棵蓖麻……我豈能不愛惜尼尼微這大城呢？其中不能分辨左手右手的，有十二萬多人……並有許多牲畜，我豈能不愛惜呢？」

title.en: The Wager in Heaven: Job Loses Everything
title.zh: 天上的賭局：約伯盡失所有

region.en: Land of Uz (location unknown; symbolic pin)
region.zh: 烏斯地（地點不詳；象徵性定位）

period: Frame narrative composed c. 6th-4th c. BCE; poetic core c. 5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Job 1-2; 42, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: 'There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was whole-hearted and righteous'. In the heavenly council 'the satan' — the adversary — challenges his piety as bought: 'Doth Job fear God for nought?' Permission given, four messengers take children, oxen, sheep, and camels — 'and I only am escaped alone to tell thee'. Job rends his mantle: 'The LORD hath given, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.' Struck with boils, he still does not sin 'with his lips' — but the arguments that follow are the longest in the Bible.
summary.zh: 「烏斯地有一個人名叫約伯；那人完全正直，敬畏神，遠離惡事」。天庭會議中，「那撒但」——控告者——指其虔誠為有價：「約伯敬畏神，豈是無故呢？」許可之下，四個報信者相繼而至——兒女牛羊駱駝盡失——「惟有我一人逃脫，來報信給你」。約伯撕裂外袍：「賞賜的是耶和華，收取的也是耶和華；耶和華的名是應當稱頌的。」長瘡而不「以口犯罪」——但其後的辯論是聖經中最長的。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The satan is a member of the divine council in the frame, not the later devil.

passages.text: And the LORD said unto the satan: 'Hast thou set thy heart on My servant Job? for there is none like him in the earth, a whole-hearted and an upright man, one that feareth God, and shunneth evil.' Then the satan answered: 'Doth Job fear God for nought? Hast not Thou made a hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?... But put forth Thy hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will renounce Thee to Thy face.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Job 1:8-11 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 耶和華對那撒但說：「你曾用心察看我的僕人約伯沒有？地上再沒有人像他，他完全正直，敬畏神，遠離惡事。」撒但回答說：「約伯敬畏神，豈是無故呢？你豈不是四面圈上籬笆圍護他和他的家，並他一切所有的嗎？……你且伸手，毀他一切所有的，他必當面棄掉你。」

passages.text: In one day came the Sabeans, fire of God, Chaldeans, and the great wind; 'there came another, and said: Thy sons and thy daughters were eating... and, behold, there came a great wind... and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee'. In the whirlwind-dialogues Job demands a hearing from God; the speeches from the storm answer with snow-critters and crocodiles — 'Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth?' — and Job's answer closes the matter: 'I have heard of Thee by the hearing of the ear; but now mine eye seeth Thee; wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.' Paraphrase of Job 1:13-19; 38-42 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Job 1:13-19; 38-42 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 一日之間，示巴人、神的火、迦勒底人和大風相繼而來；「又有人來說：你的兒女正在吃飯……忽然有大風……擊打那幾個少年人，他們就都死了；惟有我一人在這裡，得以逃脫來報信給你。」在旋風中的對話裡，約伯要求神聽他申辯；從風暴中發出的言語以雪中的走獸與鱷魚作答——「我立大地根基的時候，你在哪裡呢？」——約伯的回答終結了此事：「我從前風聞有你，現在親眼看見你；因此我厭惡自己，在塵土和爐灰中懊悔。」此為約伯記一章十三至十九節、三十八至四十二章（JPS 1917）之釋義，非逐字引文。

title.en: The LORD Turned the Captivity of Job
title.zh: 耶和華使約伯從苦境轉回

region.en: Land of Uz (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 烏斯地（象徵性定位）

period: Frame narrative composed c. 6th-4th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Job 42, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The frame resumes: the LORD rebukes the friends — 'My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends; for ye have not spoken of Me the thing that is right, as hath My servant Job' — and requires a sacrifice with Job as intercessor. 'And the LORD turned the captivity of Job... and the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.' Seven sons and three daughters again; the daughters are named, Jemima, Kezia, and Keren-happuch, 'and there were not found such fair women as the daughters of Job'.
summary.zh: 敘事框架重啟：耶和華責備三友——「我的怒氣向你和你兩個朋友發作，因為你們議論我，不如我的僕人約伯說的是」——並要他們獻祭、由約伯代求。「耶和華就使約伯從苦境轉回……賜給他的比他從前所有的加倍」。又有七子三女；女兒得留名——耶米瑪、基洗亞、基連哈樸——「在那全地的婦女中，找不著像約伯的女兒那樣美貌的」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends; and the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before. ... And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job; and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren. So Job died, being old and full of days.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Job 42:10, 15-17 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 約伯為他的朋友祈禱，耶和華就使約伯從苦境轉回；耶和華賜給約伯的，比他從前所有的加倍。……在那全地，找不到像約伯的女兒們那樣美貌的婦女；她們的父親使她們在弟兄中得產業。此後，約伯年紀老邁，日子滿足而死。

title.en: Ezra Reads the Law to the Weeping People
title.zh: 以斯拉誦律法於哭泣之民

region.en: Water Gate, Jerusalem
region.zh: 水門，耶路撒冷

period: Narrative set c. 444 BCE; composed c. 5th-4th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Nehemiah 8, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: At the water gate all Israel 'gather themselves together with one accord' to hear Ezra the scribe read the law of Moses from morning till midday; the Levites 'caused the people to understand the reading'. The people weep; the leaders' counter-command becomes liturgy: 'This day is holy unto the LORD... go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet... for the joy of the LORD is your strength.' They find written the festival of booths and keep it with branches as not done 'since the days of Jeshua'.
summary.zh: 在水門以色列眾人「如同一人」聚集，從清早到晌午聽文士以斯拉讀摩西的律法書；利未人「使百姓明白所念的」。百姓哭泣；首領的回令成為禮儀：「今日是耶和華你們神的聖日……你們去喫肥美的，喝甘甜的……因靠耶和華而得的喜樂是你們的力量。」他們尋得棚節之例，取枝搭棚，「從嫩的兒子約書亞的時候直到這日，以色列人沒有這樣行過」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Foundational for the synagogue Torah service.

passages.text: And they found written in the law, that the LORD had commanded by Moses, that the children of Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month... So the people went forth, and brought them, and made them every one to sit upon the roof of his house, and in their courts... and in the broad places of the city. And there was very great gladness.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Nehemiah 8:14-17 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 他們在律法書上發現記載著，耶和華曾藉摩西吩咐，以色列人要在七月節住在棚裡……於是百姓出去，將枝條帶來，各人搭棚，有的搭在自己屋頂上，有的搭在院內……有的搭在城裡的寬闊處。眾人都大大歡樂。

title.en: Nehemiah Builds the Wall in Fifty-Two Days
title.zh: 尼希米五十二日重建城牆

region.en: Jerusalem, broken walls
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，殘破城牆

period: Narrative set c. 445 BCE; composed c. 5th-4th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Nehemiah 2; 4; 6, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Nehemiah, cupbearer to Artaxerxes, hears of the broken walls and prays four months; the king notes his sad face — 'why should not my countenance be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers' sepulchres, lieth waste' — and grants leave and timber. Inspecting the ruins by night, he rallies the people, who build 'every one over against his own house' with tool in one hand and weapon in the other. Conspiracy letters cannot stop the work: 'the wall was finished... in fifty and two days'.
summary.zh: 波斯的王酒政尼希米聞城牆倒塌，禁食祈禱四月；王見其面帶愁容——「我列祖墳墓所在的那城荒涼，我豈能面無愁容麼」——賜准與木料。夜間騎牲口巡視廢墟，號召百姓「各對著自己的房屋修造」，一手作工一手拿兵器。仇敵書信未能止工：「城牆修完了……共修了五十二天。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they all of them sought to frighten us, thinking: 'They will let alone the work, that they be not done.' ... But I prayed, and set a watch against them day and night. And I said unto the nobles, and to the rulers and the rest of the people: 'The work is great and large, and we are separated upon the wall, one far from another; in what place thereof ye hear the sound of the horn, resort ye thither unto us; our God shall fight for us.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Nehemiah 6:9; 4:9; 4:19-20 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 他們眾人都想使我們害怕，心裡說：『他們的手必軟弱，以致工作不能成就。』……但我禱告，並派人日夜防備他們。我又對貴冑、官長和其餘的百姓說：『這工程浩大，我們在城牆上彼此相離甚遠；你們聽見角聲在哪裡，就聚集到我們那裡去；我們的神必為我們爭戰。』

title.en: The Birth and the Wet-Nurse of Muhammad
title.zh: 穆罕默德的誕生與乳母

region.en: Mecca and the desert camp of Banu Sa'd (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥加與薩德部族的沙漠營地（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, The Life of Mahomet (1877); Ockley, History of the Saracens (Bohn ed. 1890)

source.work: Simon Ockley, The History of the Saracens (Bohn ed.), Life of Mohammed; Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic)

license: Public domain (English edition 1890; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: Muhammad is born in the Year of the Elephant; his father Abd Allah is already dead, and by the custom of the town his new-born sons are given to the desert. The wet-nurse Halima of Banu Sa'd takes him; his foster-brothers report that two men in white came, opened his breast, took out a black drop and washed his heart in snow; the child returns to his mother, the orphan of Mecca. His grandfather Abd al-Muttalib dotes on him; then, at eight, his uncle Abu Talib takes him in.
summary.zh: 穆罕默德生於象年；其父阿布杜拉已歿。依城中風俗，新生子交沙漠部落乳養；薩德部族乳母哈里瑪收之。其乳兄弟言：二白衣人剖其胸，取出一黑點，以雪洗其心。孤兒歸母；祖父阿布杜·穆塔利卜溺愛之；八歲時叔父阿布·塔里卜收養。

sensitivity.note: Biographical tradition of a living religion; treated as sacred narrative within the tradition. The chest-opening is a cardinal sira miracle; Ockley's rendering reflects early-eighteenth-century English style; paraphrased.

passages.text: In the Year of the Elephant — the year the Lord destroyed Abraha's host with birds throwing baked-clay stones — a son was born to Amina, wife of Abd Allah, who had already died on a trading journey. The child was named Muhammad, 'the praised one'; his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib carried him into the Kaaba, thanked God, and named him as God had chosen. By the custom of the Meccans the new-born were sent out to be nursed in the pure air of the desert, and so the boy passed his first years with the bedouin of Banu Sa'd.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir, Life of Mahomet, 1877; Ockley, 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在象年——就是主以投擲燒泥石的飛鳥毀滅阿伯拉大軍的那一年——阿米娜生了一個兒子，她的丈夫阿卜杜拉已在一趟經商旅途中去世。這孩子取名為穆罕默德，意為「受讚美者」；他的祖父阿卜杜勒·穆塔里布把他抱進克爾白，感謝真主，並以真主所揀選的名字為他命名。依照麥加人的習俗，新生兒要被送到沙漠潔淨的空氣中由乳母哺育，因此這男孩最初的歲月是在薩阿德部族的貝都因人中度過的。

passages.text: His foster-mother Halima told that while he was with her the blessing of God followed the household: the sheep gave abundant milk and the barren year turned rich. Then his foster-brother came running: 'Two men in white have taken my brother of the Quraysh, thrown him down, opened his breast, and searched it.' They ran back and found the child standing pale with terror. He said: 'Two men in white came to me; they opened my belly, and took out a black clot, and threw it away; then they washed my heart with snow until it was clean, and joined it again.' They carried him back to Mecca to his mother.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他的乳母哈利瑪述說，當他在她身邊時，真主的福澤伴隨著這個家庭：羊群產乳豐盛，荒年也變為富足。後來她的乳子跑來說道：『兩個穿白衣的人把我那古萊什的兄弟帶走，把他按倒，剖開他的胸膛，在裡面搜尋。』他們跑回去，見那孩子面色蒼白地站著，滿是驚恐。他說：『兩個穿白衣的人來到我這裡；他們剖開我的肚子，取出一塊黑色的血塊，把它丟掉；然後用雪洗我的心，直到潔淨，又把它合攏回去。』他們把他帶回麥加，交還給他的母親。

passages.text: His mother died on the road returning from a visit to her kin at Yathrib, and the boy was taken by his grandfather, who loved him above all his children: he would sit him by his side at the council, and feed him before himself. When Abd al-Muttalib died, at eight years the boy passed to his uncle Abu Talib, who kept him as his own son — and the orphan of Mecca grew up poor, herding sheep for hire with his brethren.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他的母親在從葉斯里卜探親歸來的途中去世，這男孩便由他的祖父撫養，祖父愛他勝過自己所有的子女：在議事時讓他坐在自己身旁，進食時先餵他，然後自己才吃。阿卜杜勒·穆塔里布去世後，這男孩八歲時轉由他的叔父阿布·塔里布照管，叔父待他如同親生兒子——麥加的這個孤兒便在貧困中長大，與他的兄弟們一同為人牧羊。

title.en: Bahira the Monk Sees the Seal of Prophecy
title.zh: 白希拉修士見聖印

region.en: Busra, on the Syrian caravan road (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 敘利亞商路上的布斯臘（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: At twelve the boy travels with his uncle Abu Talib on a caravan to Syria. At Busra the monk Bahira, who had never before honoured the caravan, invites all to a feast; he examines the child, questions him, and finds behind his shoulder-blade the 'seal of prophethood'. He warns Abu Talib: take him back to Mecca and guard him against the Jews, for a great future awaits him. The monk's forgotten feast-guest has shared the caravan's food — the mark of a true apostle.
summary.zh: 十二歲的男孩隨叔父阿布·塔里卜隨商險赴敘利亞。於布斯臘，修士白希拉從未款待過此商隊，卻設宴邀請全部；他察看此童，問其種種，見其肩胛下有『聖印』。他囑阿布·塔里卜帶回麥加，防猶太人——大前程將至。修士未嘗招待過的客人均分得商隊的食物——此乃真使徒之兆。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; the Bahira episode is a famous recognition scene; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: When Muhammad was twelve years old, his uncle Abu Talib took him on a journey to Syria for trade. On the road, at Busra, there was a monk named Bahira, learned in Christian lore, who had a copy of a book of knowledge. He had never before honoured the passing caravans; but when this caravan drew near, he prepared a feast for it, and sent to them: 'I have made ready food for you, men of Quraysh — masters and servants, young and old, come all.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 穆罕默德十二歲時，他的叔父阿布·塔里布帶他前往敘利亞經商。途中在布斯拉有一位名叫巴希拉的修士，精通基督教典籍，持有一部知識之書的抄本。他從前從未禮遇過往的商隊；但當這支商隊走近時，他為他們預備了筵席，並派人去對他們說：『我為你們備好了食物，古萊什的人們啊——主人與僕人、老與少，全都來吧。』

passages.text: They came and left their merchandise under the trees, and went in to the monk. Bahira looked at them and found nothing to mark them; but he asked whether anyone of the caravan had been left behind. They answered that all had come but a boy, the youngest, who sat with the baggage. He bade them bring him, and looked long at him, and questioned him of his sleep and his affairs and his lineage, and the boy answered well. Then Bahira looked at his back and saw the seal of prophethood between his shoulders — the very mark his book described. He said to Abu Talib: 'Take your nephew back to his country, and guard him carefully against the Jews, for by God, if they see him and know what I know, they will do him evil. A great future awaits this nephew of yours.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們來了，把貨物留在樹下，進去見那位修士。巴希拉打量他們，並未發現任何可作標記之處；但他問商隊中是否有人留在後頭。他們回答說全都來了，只有一個最年幼的少年，正坐在行李旁。他吩咐他們把他帶來，久久地端詳他，問他睡眠、事務與家世，那少年應答得體。於是巴希拉看他的背，見他兩肩之間有先知的印記——正是他書中所描述的那個標記。他對阿布·塔利卜說：『帶你的姪兒回他的家鄉去，小心防範猶太人，因為以真主發誓，若他們見到他，並知道我所知道的，必會加害於他。你這姪兒前程遠大。』

title.en: Khadija's Caravan and the Double Porch
title.zh: 哈蒂嘉的商隊與加倍聘禮

region.en: Mecca, house of Khadija bint Khuwaylid (literal pin)
region.zh: 麥加哈蒂嘉宅（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: The noble merchantwoman Khadija, hearing the honest youth called Al-Amin (the trustworthy), hires him to lead her caravan to Basra. Her slave Maysara follows and sees the trading prosper, and reports the two angels shading him from the sun. Khadija sends a proposal; her father is called to the marriage and given wine, and the dowry is doubled. From this marriage the Prophet receives, years later, the revelation that settles the dowry of daughters.
summary.zh: 高貴的女商人哈蒂嘉，聞誠實青年之名（阿敏——誠實者），雇他領商險赴巴士拉。其僕麥薩拉相隨，見貿易興旺，並報二人為其遮陽。哈蒂嘉求婚；其父被召至婚宴並賜酒；聘禮加倍。多年後先知傳降啟示，確定女兒聘禮。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: Among the nobles of Quraysh was a woman of substance, Khadija daughter of Khuwaylid, who was sought in marriage by many. Hearing of the honest youth — the people called him Al-Amin, the Trustworthy — she offered him the charge of her caravan to Basra, promising him a double wage. He took her goods, and her slave Maysara went with him; and they traded in Syria until the goods were doubled.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 古萊什的貴族中有一位富有的女子，即胡韋利德之女赫蒂徹，許多人向她求婚。她聽聞那位誠實的青年——人們稱他為阿敏，即可信者——便將她的商隊交託他前往巴士拉，許諾給他雙倍的報酬。他帶著她的貨物，她的奴僕邁薩拉與他同行；他們在敘利亞經商，直到貨物倍增。

passages.text: Maysara told her lady when they returned how a cloud shaded Muhammad from the heat wherever he went, and how he ate little and slept little, and how a tree bowed down to shade him in the road. Khadija sent to propose marriage; and she called her father, who had drunk wine, and gave him wine until he was flushed; and the dowry was fixed. And the Prophet, when years later the verse came down fixing the dowry of daughters, said that he had had his portion in the house of Khadija.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們歸來時，邁薩拉告訴他的女主人：無論穆罕默德走到何處，都有一朵雲為他遮擋炎熱；他食少眠少；路上有樹俯身為他遮蔭。赫蒂徹派人前去提親；她喚來她的父親，他已飲了酒，她便給他酒喝，直到他面泛紅暈；聘禮就此議定。而先知在多年之後、規定女兒聘禮的經文降示時說，他在赫蒂徹家中已得了自己的一份。

title.en: Arbitration of the Black Stone
title.zh: 黑石的仲裁

region.en: Kaaba, Mecca (literal pin)
region.zh: 麥加天房（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: The Quraysh rebuild the Kaaba after flood damage, and when the Black Stone is to be set in place the clans nearly come to blows: each wants the honour of carrying it. An old arbiter proposes that the next man to enter through the gate decide. It is Muhammad, then in his thirties; they are content. He spreads his mantle, sets the stone in the midst, and has each clan take an edge, and all carry it together; then he places it with his own hand.
summary.zh: 洪水損毀天房後，古萊氏重修之；黑石復位之際，各部族幾欲相鬥：人人欲承載其榮。一老仲裁建議：由下一位自門入者裁定。乃穆罕默德，時年三十餘；眾皆同意。他鋪開大氅，置石於中，令各部族各執一隅，共同抬運；再親手安放。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: The Quraysh resolved to rebuild the Kaaba, which a flood had damaged. When the work was done and the time came to set the Black Stone in its place, dispute arose: each clan claimed the honour of lifting it. They nearly came to blows; the descendants of Abd al-Dar brought a bowl full of blood, and they took oath upon it that they would fight to the death.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 古萊什人決意重建克爾白，因洪水已使其受損。工程完畢，到了安放黑石於其位的時候，爭執遂起：每個氏族都聲稱有抬起它的榮譽。他們幾乎動起手來；阿卜杜勒·達爾的子孫拿來一只盛滿血的碗，他們對著它起誓，必死戰到底。

passages.text: Then Abu Umayya, the oldest of them, said: 'Make the first man who enters the gate your arbiter.' They looked, and behold — it was Muhammad. When they saw him they said, 'We are content; this is Al-Amin, we accept him.' They told him of the matter, and he said: 'Bring me a garment.' They brought him one, and he took the Black Stone and laid it in the middle of the cloth, and said: 'Let each clan take hold of one side; then all of you, rise up with it together.' And they carried it to its place, and he set it in position with his own hand. And the Quraysh swore that they would never again harbour this resentment.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是他們中年紀最長的阿布·烏麥亞說：『讓第一個從這門進來的人作你們的仲裁者。』他們望去，看哪——正是穆罕默德。他們見到他便說：『我們滿意；這是阿敏，我們接受他。』他們把事情告訴他，他說：『給我拿一件衣服來。』他們拿來一件，他取過黑石，放在布的中間，說道：『讓每個氏族各執一邊；然後你們全體一齊把它抬起。』他們把它抬到它的位置，他親手將它安放妥當。古萊什人發誓，他們絕不再懷此怨恨。

title.en: Khadija and Waraqah: The First Believer
title.zh: 哈蒂嘉與瓦拉嘎：第一位信士

region.en: Mecca, house of Khadija (literal pin)
region.zh: 麥加哈蒂嘉宅（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: Returning from the cave of Hira shaking with fear, Muhammad says: 'Cover me, cover me.' 'What is the matter?' — 'The angel that used to come to Moses has come to me.' Khadija answers: 'God will never disgrace thee; thou keepest thy promises, bearest the burdens, feedest the poor, and protectest the weak.' She wraps him and goes to her cousin Waraqah, an old Christian scribe who has read the Gospels and Hebrew scripture: 'This is the Namus that came to Moses; would that I were young when he is sent.'
summary.zh: 自希拉山洞歸來，穆罕默德戰慄而道：『覆我，覆我。』『何事？』——『昔日臨摩西的天使臨我。』哈蒂嘉答：『主必不使你蒙羞；你守信諾，負重荷，賙濟窮人，扶助弱者。』她裹他，去見其堂兄瓦拉嘎——一位通曉福音與希伯來經典的年邁基督教抄經者：『此乃臨摩西的納木斯；願他受遣時我尚年輕。』

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: He came back to Khadija trembling: 'Cover me, cover me.' She covered him until his fear was past. Then he told her what he had seen: 'The angel that used to come to Moses has come to me.' She said, 'Be of good cheer, for by God He will never bring thee to shame: thou keepest the ties of kinship, bearest the burdens of the weak, givest to the poor, honourest the guest, and helpest against the troubles of justice.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他顫抖著回到赫蒂徹那裡：『給我蓋上，給我蓋上。』她為他蓋上，直到他的恐懼過去。然後他告訴她他所見的：『那曾降臨摩西的天使，已降臨於我。』她說：『你當歡喜，因為以真主發誓，祂絕不會使你蒙羞：你維繫親屬的紐帶，承擔弱者的重負，施予窮人，尊敬客人，並在正義的患難中相助。』

passages.text: Then she went to Waraqah ibn Nawfal, her cousin, a man grown old who had read the Scriptures, and told him. He said: 'Holy, holy! By Him in whose hand is the soul of Waraqah, if thou hast told me the truth, Khadija, there hath come to him the great Namus that came to Moses before, and he is the prophet of this people. Would that I were young, that I might be alive when he is sent forth; would that I might be by his side when they expel him.' She said, 'Will they expel him?' He said, 'Yes; never came a man with that which thou bringest but he was met with hostility; but if I live to that day I will help him.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是她前往瓦拉格·伊本·瑙法勒——她的堂兄，一位曾讀過經典的年邁之人——並告訴了他。他說：「聖哉，聖哉！以瓦拉格靈魂所繫於其手中者起誓，哈蒂嘉啊，若你所言屬實，那曾降臨於摩西之前的偉大『納穆斯』確已降臨於他，他便是這族人的先知。但願我尚年輕，但願他受遣之時我仍活著；但願他們驅逐他時我能在其身旁。」她說：「他們會驅逐他嗎？」他說：「是的；凡帶來你所帶來之物者，從未不遭敵視；但若我活到那日，我必助他。」

title.en: Bilal on the Burning Stones: 'Ahad, Ahad'
title.zh: 比拉勒在烙石上：「唯一，唯一」

region.en: Mecca marketplace of Abu Jahl's torment (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥加阿布·賈希勒刑場（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: The strong young slave Bilal, master of the blacksmiths, is seized by Umayya ibn Khalaf at noon and thrown on the burning sand with a great rock on his chest: 'You will not be released till you die or deny Muhammad and worship al-Lat and al-Uzza.' Bilal answers with the words of Islam only: 'Ahad, ahad' (One, One). The first to be freed by Abu Bakr's gold is Bilal; Abu Bakr buys the tortured slaves of the weak clans — Bilal, the women of Banu Muzayin — and frees them for Islam.
summary.zh: 強健的年輕奴隸比拉勒，正午被烏馬亞·本·哈拉夫抓走，拋於烙沙之上，胸口壓巨石：『不認穆罕默德、拜拉特與烏莎，就不得釋放。』比拉勒惟誦伊斯蘭之言：『唯一，唯一』。第一位被阿布·伯克爾金銀贖出者是比拉勒；阿布·伯克爾購買弱族受刑奴——比拉勒與穆扎因部的女子——釋放之，以奉伊斯蘭。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; torture of early Muslims is part of the received narrative; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: The persecution grew: the weak believers were seized and tortured. Bilal, the black slave of the Banu Jumah, a strong young man, was dragged out into the glare of the burning sand, with a huge rock laid on his chest, and his master cried: 'You shall remain till you die or deny Muhammad and worship al-Lat and al-Uzza.' But Bilal only answered from under the stone: 'Ahad, ahad' — One, One. The tormentors would leave him at nightfall; he was found saying the same words.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 迫害日益加劇：軟弱的信士遭拘捕並受酷刑。比拉勒——朱麥赫族的黑奴，一名強壯的青年——被拖到灼熱沙地的烈日之下，一塊巨石壓在他的胸口，他的主人喊道：「你要一直這樣，直到死去，或否認穆罕默德而崇拜拉特與烏札。」但比拉勒只從石下答道：「阿哈德，阿哈德」——獨一，獨一。折磨者們在夜幕降臨時離他而去；人們發現他仍在說著同樣的話。

passages.text: Abu Bakr, passing, saw him and ransomed him with a slave of stronger body for him, and freed him; and he bought and freed the women of Banu Muzayin who were tortured in the same way. He said: 'I meant by this to defend the weak, and I was distressed for their sake.' And Bilal, the first muezzin of Islam, was to outlive his master by many years, and to stand at last on the roof of the Kaaba when Mecca opened its gates.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿布·伯克爾路過，見到他，便以一名更為強壯的奴隸將他贖出，並釋放了他；他又買下並釋放了穆扎因族中同樣遭受酷刑的婦女們。他說：「我此舉意在保護弱者，我為她們的遭遇而憂傷。」而比拉勒——伊斯蘭的第一位宣禮員——將比他的主人多活許多年，並最終在麥加敞開城門之時，站立於克爾白的屋頂之上。

title.en: The First Migration: Ja'far Before the Negus
title.zh: 首次遷徙：加法爾見尼格斯王

region.en: Abyssinia, court of the Negus at Aksum (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿比西尼亞阿克蘇姆王廷（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: The Quraysh send envoys with gifts to the Negus to have the emigrants returned. Ja'far ibn Abi Talib pleads the case of a people who worshipped idols, ate carrion, and were brought out by a prophet from their midst to the worship of God alone — and who are now accused of forsaking their ancestral religion. The Negus asks for proof; Ja'far recites the opening of Surah Maryam; the Negus weeps till his beard is wet. To the envoys' demand to hear what Jesus is, Ja'far answers that he is the servant of God, His prophet, His spirit, and His word. The Negus refuses to deliver them and returns the gifts.
summary.zh: 古萊氏遣使攜禮見尼格斯王，欲遣返移民。加法爾·本·阿比·塔里卜陳述：一拜偶像、食腐肉之民，由中間出現的先知引導敬拜獨一真主，今被控棄祖教。尼格斯求聽證；加法爾誦《麥爾彥章》開篇；王泣至鬚濕。使者要求聽耶穌是誰；加法爾答：主的僕人、先知、靈、言語。王拒遣返，還禮。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; the Negus episode touches Christian-Muslim relations; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: The Prophet said to his Companions: 'Go to Abyssinia, for there is a king there with whom none is wronged; it is a land of truth — go, till God shall make for you a way out of your distress.' And a company went by sea, among them Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, and were well received in the land of the Negus.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 先知對他的同伴們說：「你們往阿比西尼亞去吧，那裡有一位君王，在他那裡無人受冤屈；那是一片真理之地——去吧，直到真主為你們的困厄開出一條出路。」於是一行人經海路前往，其中有賈法爾·伊本·阿比·塔利卜，他們在奈古斯之地受到善待。
