passages.text: The Quraysh sent Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'a and Amr ibn al-As with gifts to bring the emigrants back. The Negus assembled his bishops; Ja'far said: 'O King, we were a people of idolatry, eating carrion and committing abominations, neglecting kindred and doing evil; then God sent to us a prophet from among us, whose lineage and truth and trustworthiness we knew. He commanded us to worship God alone and to renounce the stones and idols we used to serve; he enjoined on us prayer, truthfulness, chastity, and kindness to kin.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 古萊什人派遣阿卜杜拉·伊本·阿比·拉比阿與阿慕爾·伊本·阿綏攜帶禮物前往，欲將遷徙者帶回。奈古斯召集了他的主教們；賈法爾說：「國王啊，我們曾是一個崇拜偶像的民族，食腐屍，行醜惡之事，斷絕親屬，作惡多端；後來真主從我們之中派遣了一位先知，我們深知他的血統、他的誠實與他的忠信。他命令我們只崇拜真主，並棄絕我們過去所供奉的石頭與偶像；他囑咐我們禮拜、誠實、貞潔，並善待親屬。」

passages.text: The Negus said, 'Recite to me some of what your companion has brought.' Ja'far recited from the beginning of Surah Maryam. The Negus wept until his beard was wet, and his bishops wept till their books were soaked. Then he said: 'Of a truth this and what Jesus brought have come from the same lamp.' And to the envoys, who demanded the men, he answered: 'These people have sought my protection, and I will not deliver them.' And he returned the gifts they had brought.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 奈古斯說：「把你同伴所帶來的一些念給我聽。」賈法爾誦讀了《麥爾彥章》的開頭。奈古斯哭了，直到他的鬍鬚濕透，他的主教們也哭了，直到他們的經書浸濕。然後他說：「誠然，這與耶穌所帶來之物出自同一盞燈。」而對那些要求交出這些人的使者，他答道：「這些人已尋求我的庇護，我不會交出他們。」於是他退還了他們帶來的禮物。

title.en: The Rejection at Taif
title.zh: 塔伊夫的拒斥

region.en: Taif, vineyards of the Hijaz highlands (literal pin)
region.zh: 漢志高地塔伊夫葡萄園（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: After the death of Khadija and Abu Talib, the Prophet goes to Taif to seek a hearing from the three chiefs of Thaqif. They answer with contempt — one offers the temple-worship of Lat, another marriage, another exile; the rabble is set upon him with stones, and he departs bleeding. In a vineyard he prays a long prayer of complaint; the angel of the mountains asks if he would have the two hills crush the city; the Prophet answers: 'No — I hope that God will bring forth of their seed those who will worship God alone.'
summary.zh: 哈蒂嘉與阿布·塔里卜死後，先知往塔伊夫求見薩吉夫三位首領。他們輕蔑相待——一位獻廟祭拉特，一位提親事，另一位令其離去；暴民以石擊之，他流血而去。於葡萄園作長祈禱；山之天使問是否要兩山壓城；先知答：『不必——我望主將於其後裔中出現敬拜獨一主者。』

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; the prayer at Taif is a locus classicus of Muslim ethics under persecution; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: After the deaths of Khadija and Abu Talib, the Prophet set out for Taif to seek support from the chiefs of Thaqif. He spoke to them privately, but they answered with scorn: one said, 'If God has truly sent you, why does He not protect you?'; another said, 'I will tear down the covering of the Kaaba if God has sent you'; the third said, 'I will not speak to you at all.' The rabble were set upon him, and he was driven out of the town and pelted with stones until his ankles bled.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 海迪徹與阿布·塔利卜去世後，先知啟程前往塔伊夫，向賽基夫的酋長們尋求支持。他私下與他們交談，他們卻以輕蔑之言相答：一人說：「若真主確已派遣你，祂為何不保護你？」另一人說：「若真主派遣了你，我就要拆毀克爾白的覆蓋物。」第三人說：「我根本不會與你說話。」暴民們向他撲來，他被人趕出城鎮，遭人投石，直至腳踝流血。

passages.text: He took refuge in a vineyard outside the town and prayed a long prayer: 'O God, to Thee I complain of my weakness, my few means, and my insignificance among men... If Thou art not angry with me, I care not; Thine approval is my aim.' And as he prayed, the angel of the mountains called to him: 'God has heard the speech of your people to you, and has sent me the angel of the mountains, that I may command them as you wish — shall I bring the two mountains together upon them?' But the Prophet said: 'No; I hope that God will bring forth of their seed those who will worship God alone, and will not associate with Him anything.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他避入城外的一座葡萄園，作了長久的祈禱：「真主啊，我向祢訴說我的軟弱、我微薄的資源，以及我在眾人眼中的卑微……若祢不對我發怒，我便不在意；得祢喜悅才是我的目標。」當他祈禱時，山岳的天使呼喚他：「真主已聽見你的族人對你所說的話，並派我這山岳的天使前來，好讓我按你的意願處置他們——要我將兩座山合攏壓在他們身上嗎？」但先知說：「不；我希望真主從他們的後裔中興起只崇拜真主、不以任何物配祂的人。」

title.en: The Pledges of Aqaba: Twelve and Seventy
title.zh: 阿克巴之誓：十二人與七十人

region.en: Al-Aqaba, mountain pass near Mina (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 米那附近阿克巴山口（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: Men of Yathrib hear the Prophet at the pilgrimage fairs. At Aqaba a first band of twelve gives the pledge of women: 'not to associate anything with God, not to steal, not to commit adultery, not to kill your children, not to utter slander, and not to disobey in what is right.' The next year seventy men and women come by night: they give the pledge of war to defend the Prophet — 'and your women and children are in Paradise' — and choose twelve deputies. The pledge of the second Aqaba opens the way of the Hijra.
summary.zh: 雅茲里布人在朝覲集市聽先知傳道。阿克巴，首批十二人立女式之誓：『不配主、不偷盜、不通姦、不殺子女、不誣蔑、不違正命。』翌年，夜間七十男女而來：立戰式之誓以護先知——『你們的子女與妻子在樂園』——並選十二代表。第二次阿克巴之誓開啟遷徙之途。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; the two Aqaba pledges are the constitutional moment before the Hijra; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: Men of the Khazraj and Aws heard of the Prophet at the pilgrimage fair and carried the news to Yathrib; God opened their hearts to Islam. In the pilgrimage season of the twelfth year of his mission, twelve men met him at Aqaba and gave the pledge known as the pledge of women: 'not to associate anything with God; not to steal; not to commit adultery; not to kill your children; not to utter slander; and not to disobey the Prophet in what is right.' He said: 'If you fulfil this, Paradise is yours.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 海茲拉吉與奧斯族的人們在朝覲集市上聽到了先知的消息，並將這消息帶回葉斯里卜；真主開啟了他們的心扉，使他們接受伊斯蘭。在他傳教的第十二年朝覲季節，十二名男子在阿卡巴與他相會，立下了被稱為「婦女之誓」的誓約：「不以任何物配真主；不偷盜；不通姦；不殺害你們的子女；不散布誹謗；在正當之事上不違抗先知。」他說：「你們若履行此約，樂園便是你們的。」

passages.text: Next year, seventy men and two women came in secret at night to Aqaba, and the Prophet came with his uncle Abbas. The men and women gathered; Abbas spoke first: 'Muhammad is in his clan's keeping; you ask him to join you. If you can keep him from his enemies, promise it.' They asked what would be their reward if they held to it. He said: 'Paradise.' They stretched forth their hands, and said: 'We pledge ourselves to war in defence of you against all men.' And they said: 'O Prophet of God, we have laid a hand upon you; and we swear that we will protect you as we protect our wives and children.' He said: 'Your women and your children are in Paradise.' And twelve deputies were chosen to lead the people of Yathrib.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 次年，七十名男子與兩名女子在夜間秘密來到阿卡巴，先知與他的叔父阿拔斯一同前來。男女眾人聚集；阿拔斯首先發言：「穆罕默德受其宗族的庇護；你們請求他加入你們。你們若能保護他免受敵人侵害，就向他許諾吧。」他們問，若他們堅守此約，將得到什麼報償。他說：「樂園。」他們伸出手來，說道：「我們立誓為保衛你而與所有人作戰。」他們又說：「真主的先知啊，我們已向你伸出手；我們發誓，將如保護我們的妻兒一般保護你。」他說：「你們的妻兒必在樂園中。」並選出十二名代表來領導葉斯里卜的人民。

title.en: The Hijra: Two in the Cave
title.zh: 遷徙：洞穴中的兩人

region.en: Cave of Thawr, south of Mecca (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥加南方紹爾山洞（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: With Abu Bakr the Prophet slips out of Mecca at night and hides in the cave of Thawr. The Quraysh set a price on their heads and searchers come to the very cave mouth. Abu Bakr fears for the Prophet's life; the Prophet says: 'What think you of two, the third of whom is God?' The tradition tells of a dove's nest at the entrance and a spider's web; the pursuers turn back. After three days the two ride north with a guide, and reach Quba outside Yathrib — the first mosque of Islam.
summary.zh: 先知與阿布·伯克爾夜間出麥加，藏於紹爾山洞。古萊氏懸賞捉拿，搜查者至洞口。阿布·伯克爾恐先知有失；先知言：『兩人之中，其三為主，你以為如何？』相傳洞口有鴿巢與蛛網；追者折返。三日後，二人偕嚮導北行，抵雅茲里布郊外的庫巴——伊斯蘭第一座清真寺。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; the Hijra marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: The clans of Quraysh met in council to kill the Prophet, each clan contributing a man so that the blood-money would be spread. God revealed to him their plot; and he went out at night, and took Abu Bakr with him, and they hid in the cave of Thawr. Abu Bakr had given instructions that his two she-camels should be made ready.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 古萊什的各宗族聚會議事，要殺害先知，每一宗族各出一人，以使血債分攤於眾人。真主向他揭示了他們的陰謀；他便在夜間出走，帶著阿布·伯克爾同行，兩人躲藏在騷爾洞中。阿布·伯克爾事先已吩咐將他的兩頭母駝備好。

passages.text: The Quraysh searched every road; a search-party came to the mouth of the cave itself, and Abu Bakr whispered: 'If one of them looks down at his feet he will see us.' The Prophet said: 'What think you, Abu Bakr, of two men the third of whom is God?' And the searchers turned back. The tradition tells that a dove had nested at the entrance and a spider had spun its web across the mouth of the cave. After three days the two rode north with a guide, and reached Quba, where the Prophet stayed and built the first mosque of Islam; then he entered Yathrib — henceforth Medina — and the era of the Hijra began.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 古萊什人搜查了每一條道路；一支搜索隊來到洞口，阿布·伯克爾低聲說：「他們中若有人低頭看腳下，就會看見我們。」先知說：「阿布·伯克爾啊，你以為如何？兩人同行，而真主是第三位。」搜索者們便折返而去。傳說記載，一隻鴿子在洞口築了巢，一隻蜘蛛在洞口結了網。三日之後，兩人由一名嚮導帶領向北騎行，抵達庫巴，先知在此停留，並建造了伊斯蘭的第一座清真寺；隨後他進入葉斯里卜——自此稱為麥地那——遷徙紀元便由此開始。

title.en: The Charter of Medina and the Turning of the Qibla
title.zh: 麥地那盟約與朝向之改

region.en: Medina, market of the city (literal pin)
region.zh: 麥地那城市場（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: The Prophet writes a charter between the Muhajirun of Quraysh and the people of Yathrib: one community (umma) to the exclusion of others; mutual defence; the Jews have their religion and the Muslims theirs; blood-money shared; the Prophet to judge in every dispute; no protection given to Quraysh; the killing of a believer requited. At the same season the qibla is turned from Jerusalem to Mecca, and the fast of Ramadan is instituted in place of the fast of Ashura.
summary.zh: 先知書寫雅茲里布古萊氏遷民與當地人之間的盟約：一體之民（烏瑪）；相互防衛；猶太人有其教，穆斯林有其教；血錢共擔；紛爭由先知裁決；不得庇護古萊氏；殺信士者償血。同一季節，朝向由耶路撒冷改向麥加，萊麥丹月之齋取代阿舒拉齋。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; the Charter of Medina is read in modern scholarship as a constitutional document; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: The Prophet wrote a document between the Muhajirun and the Ansar, joining the Jews with them in one community: 'The Jews shall have their religion, and the Muslims their religion; the Muhajirun of Quraysh shall keep to their custom, and shall pay blood-money among themselves and ransom their prisoners... The believers shall not forsake a destitute believer by giving him abundant help against murder or debt. No believer shall take as ally a client of another believer, or the freedman of another believer... God's protection is one; the least of them may grant protection to a stranger on behalf of all. And wherever there is dispute among the people of this document which may cause trouble, it shall be referred to God and to Muhammad, the Messenger of God.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 先知在遷士與輔士之間寫了一份文書，並使猶太人與他們同為一個社群：「猶太人有其宗教，穆斯林有其宗教；古萊什的遷士當守其習俗，彼此之間交付血金，並贖回其俘虜……信士不可撇下一個貧困的信士，不給他充分的援助以對抗殺害或債務。任何信士不可把另一位信士的附庸，或另一位信士的釋奴，收為盟友……真主的庇護是一體的；他們中最卑微者亦可代表全體給予外人庇護。凡此文書之民中發生可能引起紛爭的爭執，當呈交真主與真主的使者穆罕默德。」

passages.text: In the second year the qibla was turned from Jerusalem towards the Kaaba at Mecca, and the Prophet's face was turned to the sacred mosque; and the month of Ramadan was appointed as the month of fasting in place of the fast of Ashura which had been kept among the Muslims of Medina.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在第二年，朝向由耶路撒冷轉向麥加的克爾白，先知的面容轉向聖寺；並規定齋月為齋戒之月，以取代麥地那穆斯林原先所守的阿舒拉齋戒。

title.en: Umar at His Sister's Door
title.zh: 歐瑪爾在妹妹門前

region.en: Mecca, quarter of Safa (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥加薩法區（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: Umar, the fierce persecutor, resolves to kill Muhammad, and is told by a passer-by that his own sister and her husband have become Muslims. He goes and hears Surah Ta-Ha being read behind a door; when he enters, his sister confesses. The reading continues, and Umar's soul is moved; he goes to the house where the Prophet was, and is met by Hamza: 'What do you want?' — 'I want to believe.' The Prophet praises God; the strongest persecutor has become the mightiest helper.
summary.zh: 兇猛迫害者歐瑪爾決意殺穆罕默德，途中被告知其妹與妹夫已入教。他前去，隔門聽誦《塔哈章》；入門，其妹認罪。誦經續，歐瑪爾心動；至先知所在之宅，遇哈姆扎：『何事？』——『我要歸信。』先知讚美主；最強的迫害者成了最強的助力。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: Umar ibn al-Khattab, one of the strong men of Quraysh, set out one day with his sword to kill the Prophet. He was met by Nu'aym, who said: 'Where are you going?' He said, 'I am going to kill Muhammad.' Nu'aym said, 'Will you not go back to your own house first? Your sister and her husband are Muslims.' Umar went and heard, behind the closed door, a passage of the Quran which had newly been revealed: 'Ta-Ha. We have not sent down the Quran upon thee to be thy distress...' — Surah Ta-Ha.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 歐麥爾·本·哈塔卜是古萊什的強者之一，某日持劍出門，欲殺先知。他途中遇見努阿伊姆，努阿伊姆說：「你往何處去？」他說：「我去殺穆罕默德。」努阿伊姆說：「你何不先回自己家中？你的姊妹和她的丈夫已成了穆斯林。」歐麥爾前去，在閉著的門後聽見一段新近降示的《古蘭經》：「塔哈。我降《古蘭經》給你，不為使你受苦……」——《塔哈章》。

passages.text: He knocked; his sister hid the manuscript, but he had heard some of it. He demanded it; when they said they were Muslims he struck her, and then relented. He said: 'Let me see what you were reading.' His sister said, 'You are unclean, and none but the purified may touch it; wash thyself.' He washed, and read: 'Verily I am God; there is no God but Me: therefore serve Me, and observe prayer in My remembrance.' Umar's soul was moved, and he went to the house where the Prophet was. At the door Hamza met him: 'What do you want, Umar?' He said, 'I want to believe.' And the Prophet cried 'Allahu akbar' with such joy that those in the house came out; and Umar became the mightiest helper of Islam.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他敲門；他的姊妹把經卷藏起，但他已聽見其中一些。他索要經卷；當他們說自己已是穆斯林時，他打了她，隨後又悔悟。他說：「讓我看看你們所讀的。」他的姊妹說：「你不潔淨，唯有潔淨者方可觸摸它；你先洗淨自身。」他洗淨後讀道：「我確是真主，除我外別無神靈：故當事奉我，並為記念我而謹守禮拜。」歐麥爾的心靈為之感動，便前往先知所在之屋。在門口哈姆扎遇見他：「歐麥爾，你要什麼？」他說：「我要信道。」先知高聲念「真主至大」，其歡欣之情使屋內之人皆走出來；歐麥爾遂成為伊斯蘭最強有力的援助者。

title.en: Yao Cedes the Empire to Hsü Yu (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 堯讓天下於許由（莊子）

region.en: Fen-yang, Yao's capital (Linfen, Shanxi, China)
region.zh: 汾陽（堯都，今山西臨汾）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 1, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 1

summary.en: The Golden-Age emperor Yao begs the hermit Hsü Yu to take the throne, comparing himself to a torch lit in sunshine. Hsü Yu refuses: the tit needs only one twig, the tapir only a bellyful of river; reputation is but the shadow of reality, and the empire has no need of him.
summary.zh: 堯讓天下於許由，自比燭火之於日月。許由辭之：鷦鷯巢林不過一枝，偃鼠飲河不過滿腹；名者實之賓，天下於我無所用。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: The Emperor Yao wished to abdicate in favour of Hsü Yu, saying, "If, when the sun and moon are shining, you persist in lighting a torch, is not that a misapplication of fire? If, when the rainy season is at its height, you still continue to water the ground, is not this a waste of labour? Now, sir, do you assume the reins of government, and the empire will be at peace. I am but a dead body, conscious of my own deficiency. I beg you will ascend the throne."
passages.zh: 堯帝欲讓位於許由，說道：「日月既已照耀，而你仍堅持點燃火炬，這豈非徒勞用火？雨季正盛，而你仍繼續澆灌土地，這豈非白費力氣？如今先生若執掌政柄，天下必將安寧。我不過是一具屍骸，自知有所不足。懇請你登臨帝位。」

passages.text: "Ever since you, sire, have directed the administration," replied Hsü Yu, "the empire has enjoyed tranquillity. Supposing, therefore, that I were to take your place now, should I gain any reputation thereby? Besides, reputation is but the shadow of reality; and should I trouble myself about the shadow? The tit, building its nest in the mighty forest, occupies but a single twig. The tapir slakes its thirst from the river, but drinks enough only to fill its belly. To you, sire, belongs the reputation: the empire has no need for me. If a cook is unable to dress his funeral sacrifices, the boy who impersonates the corpse may not step over the wines and meats and do it for him."
passages.zh: 許由回答說：「自君上主持政事以來，天下已享安寧。那麼，假使我如今取代你的位置，我難道能藉此獲得什麼名聲嗎？況且，名聲不過是實質的影子；我又何必為影子而自尋煩惱？鷦鷯在大森林中築巢，所佔不過一根樹枝。犀牛從河中解渴，所飲不過填滿其腹。名聲歸於君上：天下並不需要我。倘若廚師不能料理他的祭祀供品，扮作屍主的孩子也不可越過酒肉而去代他行事。」

title.en: The Divine Man of the Miao-ku-shê Mountain (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 藐姑射山之神人（莊子）

region.en: Miao-ku-shê mountain, a fabulous peak (symbolic pin: Songshan, Henan, China)
region.zh: 藐姑射山（神話之山；象徵定位：河南嵩山）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 1, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 1

summary.en: Chien Wu mocks the madman Chieh Yü's tale of a divine man on the Miao-ku-shê mountain — flesh like ice and snow, living on air and dew, riding clouds with dragons for his team. Lien Shu answers that such blindness is of the mind: the flood and the scorched drought cannot harm him, and out of his dust one might fashion two such men as Yao and Shun.
summary.zh: 肩吾譏接輿之言狂妄無稽；連叔答以心盲——藐姑射神人肌膚若冰雪，不食五穀，吸風飲露，乘雲氣御飛龍；洪水焦金不可害之，其塵垢秕糠猶可陶鑄堯舜。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). The immortal-on-a-sacred-mountain image became a founding vision of Daoist transcendence.

passages.text: "He declared," replied Chien Wu, "that on the Miao-ku-shê mountain there lives a divine man whose flesh is like ice or snow, whose demeanour is that of a virgin, who eats no fruit of the earth, but lives on air and dew, and who, riding on clouds with flying dragons for his team, roams beyond the limits of mortality. This being is absolutely inert. Yet he wards off corruption from all things, and causes the crops to thrive. Now I call that nonsense, and do not believe it."
passages.zh: 肩吾回答說：「他宣稱，在藐姑射山上住著一位神人，肌膚如冰雪般潔白，姿態如處女般柔美，不食五穀，只吸風飲露，乘雲氣、駕飛龍，遨遊於四海之外。這位神人凝神寂靜，使萬物不受病害，使年穀豐熟。我認為這是狂言，不敢相信。」

passages.text: "Well," answered Lien Shu, "you don't ask a blind man's opinion of a picture, nor do you invite a deaf man to a concert. And blindness and deafness are not physical only. There is blindness and deafness of the mind, diseases from which I fear you yourself are suffering. The good influence of that man fills all creation. Yet because a paltry generation cries for reform, you would have him condescend to the details of an empire!
passages.zh: 連叔回答說：「是啊，盲人無法欣賞圖畫之美，聾人無法聆聽鐘鼓之聲。然而，盲與聾豈止是形體上的？心智也有盲與聾，這恐怕正是你所患的病症。那位神人的德行，將廣被萬物。然而你卻因為區區世俗之人祈求治理天下，就想讓神人屈尊去管那些瑣碎的政務嗎？

passages.text: "Objective existences cannot harm him. In a flood which reached to the sky, he would not be drowned. In a drought, though metals ran liquid and mountains were scorched up, he would not be hot. Out of his very dust and siftings you might fashion two such men as Yao and Shun. And you would have him occupy himself with objectives!"
passages.zh: 「外物不能傷害他。洪水滔天，他不會被淹沒；大旱使金石熔化、山岳焦枯，他也不會感到炎熱。從他身上搓下的塵垢糠秕，都足以造就出像堯、舜那樣的聖人。你怎麼會想讓他去操勞那些身外之事呢！」

title.en: The Five-Bushel Gourd and the Salve of Chapped Hands (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 五石之瓠與不龜手之藥（莊子）

region.en: Prince of Wu's court, Suzhou (Jiangsu, China)
region.zh: 吳王之廷（今江蘇蘇州）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 1, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 1

summary.en: Hui Tzü boasts of a gourd too large to be of use, which he smashed. Zhuangzi answers with the Sung silk-washer's secret salve for chapped hands: sold for a hundred ounces of silver, it won the Prince of Wu a naval victory and its seller a fief — the same drug, a different use. Float the gourd as a boat over river and lake.
summary.zh: 惠子謂莊子：魏王貽大瓠之種，樹成五石之實，無所用之而掊之。莊子舉宋人洴澼絖之秘藥：鬻技百金，吳王以之敗越，裂地而封。物之大小，繫於所用。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: Hui Tzŭ said to Chuang Tzŭ, "The Prince of Wei gave me a seed of a large-sized kind of gourd. I planted it, and it bore a fruit as big as a five-bushel measure. Now had I used this for holding liquids, it would have been too heavy to lift; and had I cut it in half for ladles, the ladles would have been ill adapted for such purpose. It was uselessly large, so I broke it up."
passages.zh: 惠子對莊子說：「魏王送我大葫蘆的種子。我把它種下，結出的果實有五石容量那麼大。用來盛水，它太重而舉不起來；剖開做瓢，瓢又太大而無處可容。它大得無用，我就把它砸了。」

passages.text: "Sir," replied Chuang Tzŭ, "it was rather you who did not know how to use large things. There was a man of Sung who had a recipe for salve for chapped hands, his family having been silk-washers for generations. Well, a stranger who had heard of it, came and offered him 100 oz. of silver for this recipe; whereupon he called together his clansmen and said, 'We have never made much money by silk-washing. Now, we can make 100 oz. in a single day. Let the stranger have the recipe.'
passages.zh: 莊子回答說：「先生，這實在是你不知道如何使用大東西啊。宋國有一個人，擅長配製防止手凍裂的藥膏，他家世世代代以漂洗絲絮為業。有個外地人聽說了，便來找他，願出百金買這個藥方。於是那人召集族人商議說：『我們世世代代漂洗絲絮，所得不過很少。如今一旦賣出這個藥方，就能得到百金。就讓他把藥方拿去吧。』

passages.text: "So the stranger got it, and went and informed the Prince of Wu who was just then at war with the Yüeh State. Accordingly, the Prince used it in a naval battle fought at the beginning of winter with the Yüeh State, the result being that the latter was totally defeated. The stranger was rewarded with territory and a title. Thus, while the efficacy of the salve to cure chapped hands was in both cases the same, its application was different. Here, it secured a title; there, a capacity for washing silk."
passages.zh: 「那人得到藥方後，便去遊說吳王。當時吳國正與越國交戰。吳王便用這個藥方，在寒冬之初與越國進行水戰，結果大敗越軍。那人因此被封賞土地、賜予爵位。同樣是防止手凍裂的藥膏，功效相同，但用法不同。一處用它得到了封賞，另一處卻只會用來漂洗絲絮。」

passages.text: "Now as to your five-bushel gourd, why did you not make a boat of it, and float about over river and lake? You could not then have complained of its not holding anything! But I fear you are rather woolly inside."
passages.zh: 「如今你有個能容五石的大葫蘆，為什麼不把它做成腰舟，浮游於江湖之上呢？那樣你就不會抱怨它盛不了什麼東西了！我只怕你心裡還是茅塞不通啊。」

title.en: The Gnarled Tree Too Big for the Axeman (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 樗散之樹（莊子）

region.en: State of Sung (Shangqiu, Henan, China)
region.zh: 宋國（今河南商丘）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 1, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 1

summary.en: Hui Tzü complains that Zhuangzi's words are like his worthless tree — knotted, twisted, ignored by every carpenter. Zhuangzi contrasts the wild cat, clever and doomed to the snare, with the yak too big to catch mice and therefore safe; plant the useless tree in the domain of non-existence and repose beneath its shade, beyond the axe and all injury.
summary.zh: 惠子謂莊子言大而無用。莊子對以狸狌之死於機辟與斄牛之不能執鼠；無用之樹當樹之於無何有之鄉，彷徨乎無為其側，不夭斤斧，物無害者。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: Hui Tzŭ said to Chuang Tzŭ, "Sir, I have a large tree, of a worthless kind. Its trunk is so irregular and knotty that it cannot be measured out for planks; while its branches are so twisted as to admit of no geometrical subdivision whatever. It stands by the roadside, but no carpenter will look at it. And your words, sir, are like that tree;--big and useless, not wanted by anybody."
passages.zh: 惠子對莊子說：「先生，我有一棵大樹，是無用之材。它的樹幹彎曲多結，無法量取來鋸成木板；枝條又扭曲盤結，不合任何規矩方圓。它長在路旁，卻沒有木匠肯看它一眼。而先生您的話，就像這棵樹一樣——大而無用，誰也不需要。」

passages.text: "Sir," rejoined Chuang Tzŭ, "have you never seen a wild cat, crouching down in wait for its prey? Right and left it springs from bough to bough, high and low alike,--until perchance it gets caught in a trap or dies in a snare. On the other hand, there is the yak with its great huge body. It is big enough in all conscience, but it cannot catch mice.
passages.zh: 莊子回答說：「先生，您難道沒見過野貓嗎？牠蹲伏下來等候獵物，忽左忽右地從這枝跳到那枝，無論高低都一樣——直到偶然落入陷阱，或死在網羅之中。另一方面，還有那氂牛，身軀龐大。牠確實夠大了，卻捉不到老鼠。

passages.text: "Now if you have a big tree and are at a loss what to do with it, why not plant it in the domain of non-existence, whither you might betake yourself to inaction by its side, to blissful repose beneath its shade? There it would be safe from the axe and from all other injury; for being of no use to others, itself would be free from harm."
passages.zh: 「如今您有棵大樹，卻不知拿它怎麼辦，為什麼不把它種在無何有之鄉，您可以無所事事地在它旁邊徘徊，在它的蔭下安然休憩呢？在那裡，它可免於斧斤之害和一切損傷；因為它對別人無用，自身便能免於禍害。」

title.en: My Song of the Deep: Psalm 104
title.zh: 深淵之歌：詩篇一〇四篇

region.en: Jerusalem (symbolic pin for the temple singers)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷（聖殿歌手的象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 6th-4th c. BCE; collected in the Psalter (Ezra-Nehemiah era stabilization); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Psalm 104, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The great nature-poem of the Psalter: God wrapped in light 'as with a garment', riding the clouds as a chariot, laying the beams of His chambers on the waters, sending springs for wild asses, grass for cattle, wine 'to gladden the heart of man'. Sinners vanish; 'my song of praise shall be sweet to Him' — creation as ongoing, ordered joy.
summary.zh: 詩篇的自然頌歌：神以光為衣，乘雲如車，在 waters 上立殿宇之棟樑；使泉源流於野驢，草生於牲畜，酒「悅人心」。罪人消沒；「願我的吟頌蒙他喜悅」——創造是持續而有序的喜樂。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Bless the LORD, O my soul; O LORD my God, Thou art very great; Thou art clothed with glory and majesty. Who coverest Thyself with light as with a garment, who stretchest the heavens like a curtain; who layest the beams of Thy chambers in the waters, who makest the clouds Thy chariot, who walkest upon the wings of the wind; who makest Thy angels into winds, and Thy ministers a flaming fire.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Psalm 104:1-4 (public domain).
passages.zh: 我的心哪，你要稱頌耶和華！耶和華我的神啊，你為至大；你以尊榮威嚴為衣。你以光為衣，如披外袍；你鋪張諸天，如展開幔子；你在水中立定樓閣的棟樑，你以雲彩為車輦，行走在風的翅膀上；你以風為使者，以火焰為僕役。

passages.text: The Psalm walks through creation's economy: springs in the valleys 'that the wild asses of the dry places quench their thirst', birds nesting by them, wine 'that gladdeneth the heart of man', oil 'to make the face to shine', bread 'to strengthen the heart'; the sun rises, lions roar, man goes forth to his work until evening. The poet ends: 'I will sing unto the LORD as long as I live... my meditation of Him shall be sweet; I will be glad in the LORD.' Paraphrase of Psalm 104:10-34 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Psalm 104:10-34 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 這篇詩篇遍歷受造的秩序：山谷中的泉源，「使野驢得解其渴」；鳥兒在泉旁築巢；酒「能悅人心」；油「能潤人面」；糧「能扶人心」；日頭升起，獅子吼叫，人出去做工，直到晚上。詩人最後寫道：「我要一生向耶和華唱詩……我默念他的時候，要以為甘甜；我要因耶和華歡喜。」此為詩篇一〇四篇10至34節（JPS 1917年版）的意譯，並非逐字引用。

title.en: What Is Man? Psalm 8
title.zh: 人算什麼？詩篇八篇

region.en: Jerusalem (symbolic pin for the temple singers)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷（聖殿歌手的象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 6th-4th c. BCE; collected in the Psalter; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Psalm 8, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Under the full sky the poet asks the question the eden narrative answers in story: 'When I behold Thy heavens... what is man, that Thou art mindful of him?' The answer: 'Thou hast made him but little lower than the divine, and hast crowned him with glory and honour... to have dominion over the works of Thy hands' — man the ruler of the deep creatures named in the first creation account.
summary.zh: 仰望穹蒼之際，詩人問出伊甸敘事所答之問：「我觀看你指頭所造的天……人算什麼，你竟顧念他？」答案是：「你叫他比天使微小一點，並賜他榮耀尊貴為冠冕……派他管理你手所造的」——人為首章受造深處之物的治理者。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: O LORD, our Lord, How glorious is Thy name in all the earth! Whose majesty is recounted above the heavens... When I behold Thy heavens, the work of Thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which Thou hast established; what is man, that Thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that Thou thinkest of him? Yet Thou hast made him but little lower than the divine, and hast crowned him with glory and honour.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Psalm 8:1-6 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 耶和華我們的主啊，你的名在全地何其榮耀！你的威嚴傳述於諸天之上……我觀看你指頭所造的天，並你所陳設的月亮星宿，便說：人算什麼，你竟顧念他？世人算什麼，你竟眷顧他？你卻使他比神聖者稍為微小，又賜他榮耀尊貴為冠冕。

title.en: Thou Didst Break the Heads of the Sea-Monsters: Psalm 74
title.zh: 你曾打破水中大魚的頭：詩篇七十四篇

region.en: Jerusalem, in ruins (exilic lament)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，廢墟（被擄哀歌）

period: Composed c. 6th-5th c. BCE (community lament); collected in the Psalter; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Psalm 74:12-23, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: In a lament over the burned sanctuary the poet still recalls the old combat myth: 'O God, my King... Thou didst break the heads of the sea-monsters in the waters. Thou brakest the heads of Leviathan... Thou didst set springs and torrents' — creation as defeat of primordial waters, preserved in poetry long after Genesis had excluded the battle from prose.
summary.zh: 聖所被焚的哀歌中仍存古老爭戰神話：「神我的王……你曾打破水中大魚的頭。你曾砸碎利未亞坦的頭……你曾使泉源谿川湧流」——創造即戰勝原初大水，詩體長存，而創世記散文已除其爭戰。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Cross-tradition chaoskampf cluster (Tiamat parallels); tag noted as interpretive.

passages.text: O God, my King, from of old, who wroughtest deliverance in the midst of the earth; Thou didst break the sea by Thy strength; Thou didst break the heads of the sea-monsters in the waters. Thou didst break the heads of Leviathan in pieces, and gavest him to be food to the folk inhabiting the wilderness. Thou didst cleave fountain and brook; Thou driedst up ever-flowing rivers.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Psalm 74:12-15 (public domain).
passages.zh: 神啊，我的王，你自古以來就在地中施行拯救；你曾以能力分開滄海；你曾在水族中打碎海怪的首級。你曾將利維坦的首級打得粉碎，把他給荒野的居民作食物。你曾裂開泉源與溪流；你曾使長流的江河乾涸。

title.en: The LORD Said Unto My Lord: Psalm 2
title.zh: 耶和華對我主說：詩篇二篇

region.en: Zion, city of David (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 錫安，大衛之城（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 10th-6th c. BCE (royal psalm); collected in the Psalter; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Psalm 2, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: A coronation psalm: the nations rage and 'the kings of the earth set themselves... against the LORD, and against His anointed'; from heaven the King laughs. 'I will tell of the decree: the LORD said unto me: Thou art My son... Ask of Me, and I will give the nations for Thine inheritance' — the king installed on Zion, ruling 'with a rod of iron', warned: 'Do homage to the son, lest he be angry.'
summary.zh: 加冕詩：外邦喧嚷，「地上的君王一起起來……敵擋耶和華並他的受膏者」；天上的王發笑。「我必傳聖旨：耶和華曾對我說：你是我的兒子……你求我，我就將列國賜你為基業」——受膏者坐於錫安聖山，以鐵杖轄管，警告：「當親吻其子，恐怕他發怒。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Royal psalms acquired messianic readings; record describes the royal-court setting.

passages.text: I will tell of the decree; the LORD said unto me: 'Thou art My son, this day have I begotten thee. Ask of Me, and I will give the nations for Thine inheritance, and the ends of the earth for Thy possession. Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; Thou shalt dash them to pieces like a potter's vessel.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Psalm 2:7-9 (public domain).
passages.zh: 我要傳述那諭旨；耶和華曾對我說：『你是我的兒子，我今日生了你。你向我求，我就將列國賜你為基業，將地極賜你為產業。你必用鐵杖打破他們；你必將他們如同窯匠的瓦器摔碎。』

title.en: The LORD Is My Shepherd: Psalm 23
title.zh: 耶和華是我的牧者：詩篇二十三篇

region.en: Jerusalem (symbolic pin for the temple singers)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷（聖殿歌手的象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; collected in the Psalter; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Psalm 23, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The most-recited psalm in the world: green pastures, still waters, the valley of the shadow of death walked 'I fear no evil, for Thou art with me', the table in the presence of enemies, anointing, overflowing cup, and the ending — 'I shall dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.'
summary.zh: 世上最常誦讀的詩篇：青草地、安歇水、死蔭的幽谷「我必不遭害，因為你與我同在」，敵人面前的筵席、膏油、滿溢的杯，與結語——「我且要住在耶和華的殿中，直到永遠」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures; He leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul; He guideth me in straight paths for His name's sake. Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for Thou art with me; Thy rod and Thy staff, they comfort me.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Psalm 23:1-4 (public domain).
passages.zh: 耶和華是我的牧者，我必不致缺乏。他使我躺臥在青草地上；他領我在可安歇的水邊。他使我的靈魂甦醒；為自己的名引導我走正直的路。我雖然行過死蔭的幽谷，也不怕遭害，因為你與我同在；你的杖、你的竿，都安慰我。

title.en: A Broken and Contrite Heart: Psalm 51
title.zh: 憂傷痛悔的心：詩篇五十一篇

region.en: Jerusalem (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 6th-4th c. BCE (superscription links to David and Bathsheba); collected in the Psalter; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Psalm 51, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The penitential psalm par excellence, headed 'when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bath-sheba': 'Wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin... Hide Thy face from my sins, and blot out all mine iniquities. Create me a clean heart, O God... restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation'. Sacrifice is redefined: 'the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, Thou wilt not despise.'
summary.zh: 悔罪詩之首，標題「先知拿單來見他之後，他與拔示巴犯了罪之後」：「求你將我的罪孽洗除淨盡，並潔除我的罪……求你掩面不看我的罪，塗抹我一切的罪孽。神啊，求你為我造清潔的心……求你使我仍得救恩之樂」。祭物重釋：「神所要的祭，就是憂傷的靈；憂傷痛悔的心，你必不輕看。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Recited daily in the morning liturgy.

passages.text: Have mercy upon me, O God, according to Thy lovingkindness; according unto the multitude of Thy compassions, blot out my transgressions. Wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin; for I know my transgressions; and my sin is ever before me.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Psalm 51:1-3 (public domain).
passages.zh: 神啊，求你按你的慈愛憐恤我；按你豐盛的慈悲塗抹我的過犯。求你將我的罪孽洗除淨盡，並潔除我的罪；因為我知道我的過犯；我的罪常在我面前。

title.en: By the Rivers of Babylon: Psalm 137
title.zh: 巴比倫河畔：詩篇一三七篇

region.en: Babylon, rivers of exile
region.zh: 巴比倫，被擄之河

period: Composed c. 6th-5th c. BCE (exilic); collected in the Psalter; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Psalm 137, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The exile's psalm: 'By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion. We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that led us captive required of us songs... saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD'S song in a foreign land?' — ending with the darkest imprecation in the Psalter, against Edom and against Babylon's infants, kept as the memory of atrocity.
summary.zh: 被擄之詩：「我們曾在巴比倫的河邊坐下，一追想錫安就哭了。我們把琴掛在那裡的柳樹上。因為在那裡擄掠我們的要我們唱歌……說：給我們唱一篇錫安的歌吧。我們怎能在外邦唱耶和華的歌呢？」——末節咒詛以東與巴比倫的嬰孩，作暴行記憶之最暗遺存。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The closing verses preserve ancient war-curse conventions; record states the text.

passages.text: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion. We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that led us captive required of us songs, and them that tormented us required of us mirth, saying: 'Sing us one of the songs of Zion.' How shall we sing the LORD'S song in a foreign land?
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Psalm 137:1-4 (public domain).
passages.zh: 我們曾在巴比倫的河邊坐下，一想起錫安就哭了。我們把琴掛在那裡的柳樹上。因為在那裡，擄掠我們的要我們唱歌，折磨我們的要我們作樂，說：『給我們唱一首錫安的歌吧。』我們怎能在外邦唱耶和華的歌呢？

title.en: Teach Us to Number Our Days: Psalm 90
title.zh: 求你教我們數算自己的日子：詩篇九十篇

region.en: Wilderness of Sinai (attributed to Moses)
region.zh: 西奈曠野（摩西所作）

period: Composed c. 6th-4th c. BCE (attributed to Moses); collected in the Psalter; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Psalm 90, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The psalm of mortality, titled 'A Prayer of Moses': a thousand years as yesterday; a flood sweeping men asleep; seventy, or eighty by strength, years 'in which we travail'; the request that crowns the prayer — 'Teach us to number our days, that we may get us a heart of wisdom' — and the return: 'satisfy us in the morning with Thy lovingkindness... make us glad according to the days'.
summary.zh: 論必死之詩，題「神人摩西的祈禱」：千年如昨日；如洪水掃人入睡；七十歲，若強壯可到八十，「其中所矜誇的，不過是勞苦愁煩」。禱告的冠冕是：「求你指教我們怎樣數算自己的日子，好叫我們得著智慧的心」——及其回應：「求你使我們早早飽得你的慈愛……照著你使我們受苦的日子，和我們遭難的年歲，叫我們喜樂。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Lord, Thou hast been our dwelling-place in all generations. Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever Thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, Thou art God. ... The days of our years are three-score years and ten, or even by reason of strength fourscore years; yet is their pride but travail and vanity; for it is speedily gone, and we fly away. ... So teach us to number our days, that we may get us a heart of wisdom.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Psalm 90:1, 10, 12 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 主啊，你世世代代作我們的居所。諸山未曾生出，地與世界你未曾造成，從亙古到永遠，你是神。……我們一生的年日是七十歲，若是強壯可到八十歲；但其中所矜誇的不過是勞苦愁煩，轉眼成空，我們便如飛而去。……求你指教我們怎樣數算自己的日子，好叫我們得著智慧的心。

title.en: Praise Ye the LORD: The Great Hallel
title.zh: 你們要讚美耶和華：大哈利路

region.en: Jerusalem, temple courts
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，聖殿院宇

period: Composed c. 6th-4th c. BCE (Egyptian Hallel collected); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Psalm 113-118, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The Hallel — Psalms 113-118 — sung at the Passover Seder and the great festivals: God 'who dwelleth on high... that He may look down low upon heaven and upon the earth', raising the poor from the dust; Israel passing through the sea; 'the stone which the builders refused is become the head-stone'; and the thanksgiving refrain, 'His mercy endureth for ever'.
summary.zh: 哈利路——詩篇一一三至一一八——於逾越節家宴與大節期所唱：神「坐在至高之處，自己謙卑，觀看天上地下的事」，使貧窮人從灰塵裡抬舉；以色列過海；「匠人所棄的石頭，已成了房角的頭塊石頭」；並感謝的副歌：「他的慈愛永遠長存。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Hallel is living liturgy (Pesach, Sukkot, Shavuot, Rosh Chodesh).

passages.text: Praise ye the LORD! Praise, O ye servants of the LORD, praise the name of the LORD; blessed be the name of the LORD from this time forth and for ever. From the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof the LORD'S name is to be praised. The LORD is high above all nations, and His glory above the heavens. ... The stone which the builders refused is become the head-stone of the corner. This is the LORD'S doing; it is marvellous in our eyes.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Psalms 113:1-4; 118:22-23 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 你們要讚美耶和華！耶和華的僕人哪，你們要讚美，讚美耶和華的名！耶和華的名是應當稱頌的，從今時直到永遠。從日出之地到日落之處，耶和華的名是應當讚美的。耶和華超乎萬民之上，他的榮耀高過諸天。……匠人所棄的石頭，已成了房角的頭塊石頭。這是耶和華所做的，在我們眼中看為希奇。

title.en: Wisdom Cries Aloud in the Streets: Proverbs 8
title.zh: 智慧在街市上呼喊：箴言八章

region.en: City gates of Judah (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 猶大城門（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE (Solomonic collections); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Proverbs 8, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Wisdom personified as a woman at the crossways, crying to the simple. Most remarkably, she claims a place at creation: 'The LORD made me at the beginning of His way, before His works of old... When He made a decree for the rain... then I was by Him, as a master-workman; and I was daily all delight, rejoicing always before Him.' Wisdom's antediluvian presence makes her a quasi-divine builder of the world.
summary.zh: 智慧被擬人化為道路口呼喊的女子，向愚蒙人發聲。最顯著處，她自述參與創造：「耶和華在祂道路的起頭，在太古創造我……祂為雨水設定例……那時我在祂那裡為工師，日日為祂所喜愛，常常在祂面前踴躍。」智慧先於世界而在，近乎為世界的營造者。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Personified Wisdom later shaped Sophia traditions; tag interpretive.

passages.text: Doth not wisdom cry, and understanding put forth her voice? On the top of high places by the way, where the paths meet, she standeth; beside the gates, at the entry of the city, at the coming in at the doors, she crieth aloud. Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice is to the sons of men.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Proverbs 8:1-4 (public domain).
passages.zh: 智慧豈不呼叫？聰明豈不發聲？她在道旁高處的頂上，在十字路口站立；在城門旁，在城門口，在城門洞，大聲說：眾人哪，我呼叫你們，我向世人發聲。

passages.text: 'When there were no depths, I was brought forth... Before the mountains were settled, before the hills, was I brought forth... When He gave to the sea His decree, that the waters should not transgress His commandment, when He appointed the foundations of the earth; then I was by Him, as a master-workman; and I was daily all delight, rejoicing always before Him; rejoicing in His habitable earth; and my delights are with the sons of men.' Paraphrase of Proverbs 8:24-31 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Proverbs 8:24-31 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「沒有深淵，沒有大水的泉源，我已生出……大山未曾奠定，小山未有之先，我已生出……他為滄海定出界限，使水不越過他的命令，立定大地的根基；那時，我在他那裡為工師，日日為他所喜愛，常常在他面前踴躍，踴躍在他為人預備可住之地，也喜悅住在世人之間。」（箴言八章24至31節意譯，非逐字引用。）

title.en: Vanity of Vanities: Koheleth under the Sun
title.zh: 虛空的虛空：日光之下的傳道者

region.en: Jerusalem (speaker styled 'son of David, king in Jerusalem')
region.zh: 耶路撒冷（講者自稱「在耶路撒冷作王的大衛的兒子」）

period: Composed c. 3rd c. BCE (Persian-Hellenistic era); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Ecclesiastes 1-3; 12, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The sceptical sage's sermon: 'Vanity of vanities... all is vanity'; a time to be born and a time to die; the race not to the swift; 'the dead know not any thing'; the final frame — 'fear God, and keep His commandments; for this is the whole duty of man' — while the wheel turns: 'the sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he ariseth.'
summary.zh: 懷疑派智者的講道：「虛空的虛空……凡事都是虛空」；生有時死有時；快跑的未必能贏；「死了的人毫無所知」；末段的框架：「敬畏神，謹守他的誡命，這是人所當盡的本分」——而輪迴不止：「日頭出來，日頭落下，急歸所出之地。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Read at Sukkot in the Five Scrolls cycle.

passages.text: Vanity of vanities, saith Koheleth; vanity of vanities, all is vanity. What profit hath man of all his labour wherein he laboureth under the sun? One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh; and the earth abideth for ever. The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he ariseth.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Ecclesiastes 1:2-5 (public domain).
passages.zh: 傳道者說：虛空的虛空，虛空的虛空，凡事都是虛空。人一切的勞碌，就是他在日光之下的勞碌，有什麼益處呢？一代過去，一代又來，地卻永遠長存。日頭出來，日頭落下，急歸所出之地。

title.en: I Am Black but Comely: The Song of Songs
title.zh: 我雖黑卻秀美：雅歌

region.en: Vineyards of Judah and royal palaces (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 猶大葡萄園與王宮（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 5th-3rd c. BCE (lyric collection); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Song of Songs 1-4; 7-8, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The most openly amorous book in scripture, canonized as the love between God and Israel: 'I am black, but comely... Look not upon me, because I am swarthy'; 'Behold, thou art fair, my love'; the garden locked, 'a fountain sealed'; and the ending, 'Set me as a seal upon thy heart... for love is strong as death.' 'Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it.'
summary.zh: 聖經中最直白的情歌，正典化為神與以色列之愛：「我雖黑卻秀美……不要因日頭把我曬黑了就輕看我」；「我的佳偶，你甚美麗」；關鎖的園、「禁閉的井」；結尾：「求你將我印在你心上……因為愛情如死之堅強。」「眾水不能熄滅愛情，洪水也不能淹沒。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Rabbi Akiva: 'the whole world is not worth the day on which the Song of Songs was given'; allegorical reading is the normative Jewish one.

passages.text: The song of songs, which is Solomon's. Oh that he would kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; for thy love is better than wine. I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem... Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon?
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Song of Songs 1:1-7 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 所羅門的歌，是歌中的雅歌。願他用口與我親嘴；因你的愛情比酒更美。耶路撒冷的眾女子啊，我雖然黑，卻是秀美……我心所愛的啊，求你告訴我，你在何處牧羊，晌午在何處使羊歇臥？

passages.text: 'A garden shut is my sister, my bride; a rock-mystic spring, a fountain sealed' — the bride's body is temple-garden language. The book ends with the invitation of love's strength: 'Set me as a seal upon thy heart, as a seal upon thine arm; for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave... Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it.' Paraphrase of Song of Songs 4:12; 8:6-7 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Song of Songs 4:12; 8:6-7 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「我的妹子，我的新婦，你乃是關鎖的園，禁閉的井，封閉的泉源」——新婦的身體是以聖殿與園圃的語言來描寫的。這卷書以愛之力量的邀請作結：「求你將我放在你心上如印記，帶在你臂上如戳記；因為愛情如死之堅強，嫉恨如陰間之殘忍……眾水不能息滅愛情，大水也不能淹沒。」改述《雅歌》4:12；8:6-7（JPS 1917），非逐字引用。

title.en: How Doth the City Sit Solitary: Lamentations
title.zh: 城何以孤坐：哀歌

region.en: Jerusalem, in ruins after 586 BCE
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，公元前586年後的廢墟

period: Composed c. 6th-5th c. BCE (response to the destruction); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Lamentations 1-5, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The five laments of the destroyed city, chanted in acrostic on Tisha B'Av: 'How doth the city sit solitary, that was full of people!' — Judah gone into exile, 'none to comfort her'; children faint for hunger; but chapter 3's centrepiece of hope: 'His compassions fail not. They are new every morning; great is Thy faithfulness. The LORD is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in Him.'
summary.zh: 毀城五首哀歌，按字母離合體於聖殿被毀日吟誦：「先前滿有人民的城，現在何竟孤獨！」——猶大被擄，「無人安慰」；孩童因饑餓昏倒；但三章的核心盼望：「他的憐憫不斷絕，每早晨都是新的；你的信實極其廣大。我心裡說：耶和華是我的分；因此，我要仰望他。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Read on Tisha B'Av to recall the destruction of the Temples.

passages.text: How doth the city sit solitary, that was full of people! How is she become as a widow! She that was great among the nations, and princess among the provinces, how is she become tributary! ... For these things I weep; mine eye, mine eye runneth down with water; because the comforter that should refresh my soul is far from me; my children are desolate, because the enemy prevailed.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Lamentations 1:1; 1:16 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 先前滿有人民的城，現在何竟獨坐！她何竟像寡婦！先前在列國中為大的，在諸省中為王后的，現在竟成為進貢的！……我因這些事哭泣；我眼淚汪汪，因為那當安慰我、救我性命的，離我甚遠；我的兒女孤苦，因為仇敵得了勝。

passages.text: Chapter 3 turns the dirge into hope: 'It is of the LORD'S mercies that we are not consumed... They are new every morning; great is Thy faithfulness. The LORD is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in Him. The LORD is good unto them that wait for Him... It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD.' Paraphrase of Lamentations 3:22-26 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lamentations 3:22-26 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 第三章將哀歌轉為盼望：「我們不致消滅，是出於耶和華諸般的慈愛……每早晨這都是新的；你的誠實極其廣大。我心裏說：耶和華是我的分，因此我要仰望他。耶和華善待等候他的人……人仰望耶和華，靜默等候他的救恩，這原是好的。」改述《耶利米哀歌》3:22-26（JPS 1917），非逐字引用。

title.en: Badr: The Day of the Criterion
title.zh: 白德爾：分明之日

region.en: Wells of Badr, on the Medina-Mecca road (literal pin)
region.zh: 麥地那-麥加道上的白德爾水井（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: A caravan of Quraysh wealth returns from Syria; the Prophet rides out to meet it, and instead a thousand-man army comes under Abu Jahl. The Prophet prays through the night: 'O God, accomplish for me what Thou hast promised — if this band perish today Thou wilt not be worshipped on earth.' Rain falls, angels descend, and on Friday the 17th of Ramadan the outnumbered Muslims break the Meccan line; Abu Jahl is struck down at the water. 'This is the day of the Criterion.'
summary.zh: 古萊氏商隊自敘利亞載財而歸；先知出迎，卻遇千人大軍由阿布·賈希勒率領。先知徹夜祈禱：『主啊，成就你所許我的——若此眾今日滅亡，地上再無人拜你。』雨落，天使下臨；賴麥丹月十七日周五，以少勝多；阿布·賈希勒倒斃水邊。『此乃分明之日。』

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; battle narrative kept as recorded in public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: A rich caravan of Quraysh under Abu Sufyan was returning from Syria, and the Prophet rode out with a band of Muhajirun and Ansar to meet it. But word came that a relief army of a thousand men with six hundred camels and a hundred horses had marched from Mecca under Abu Jahl. The two forces encamped at the wells of Badr, and the Prophet moved his men and took the upper well.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 一支由阿布·蘇富揚率領、滿載貨物的古萊什商隊正從敘利亞歸來，先知便率領一隊遷士與輔士出迎。然而消息傳來：一支千人援軍，帶著六百峰駱駝與一百匹馬，已由阿布·賈赫勒率領自麥加開拔。兩軍在巴德爾的井泉旁紮營，先知調動部眾，佔據了上游的井。

passages.text: That night the Prophet prayed: 'O God, if this band perish today, Thou wilt not be worshipped on earth. O God, accomplish for me what Thou hast promised me.' He slumbered and said: 'Be of good cheer, for God has promised me one of the two parties; by God, I see the enemy slain.' And God sent down a rain, and He sent a thousand angels, and the two armies drew up against one another.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那一夜，先知祈禱說：「真主啊，若這隊人今日覆滅，大地上便無人崇拜你了。真主啊，求你為我成就你所應許我的事。」他小睡片刻，說道：「你們當歡欣，因為真主已應許我兩軍之一；以真主發誓，我彷彿看見敵人已被擊殺。」真主降下雨水，又派遣了千名天使，兩軍便相對列陣。

passages.text: The battle was fought on the morning of Friday, the 17th of Ramadan, in the second year of the Hijra. The Muslims broke the Meccan line; Abu Jahl was struck down at the water where he had sworn to drink, and his dying words were 'What a high place for a man to be slain.' Seventy of the Quraysh were slain and seventy taken, at the loss of fourteen of the believers; the Prophet caused the bodies of the unbelieving leaders to be cast into a pit. 'This is the day of the Criterion', said the Quran.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 這場戰役發生於遷徙紀元第二年齋月十七日星期五的早晨。穆斯林擊破了麥加軍的陣線；阿布·賈赫勒在他曾發誓要飲其水的泉邊被擊倒，他臨終的話是：「一個人被殺於何等崇高的境地。」古萊什一方有七十人被殺、七十人被俘，信士一方則損失十四人；先知命人將不信道首領們的屍體拋入坑中。《古蘭經》說：「這是判別之日。」

title.en: The Ransomed Captives: Teach Ten to Write
title.zh: 被贖俘虜：教十人讀寫

region.en: Medina, after the battle of Badr (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那，白德爾戰後（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: The captives of Badr are divided among the Muslims. Umar urges killing them; Abu Bakr urges ransom, and the Prophet ransoms them. Among them are men of learning: for a captive who could not pay, the Prophet takes as ransom that he teach ten children of Medina to write; it is said that a man ransomed so became one of the first teachers of the written Book.
summary.zh: 白德爾俘虜分於眾穆斯林。歐瑪爾主張處死；阿布·伯克爾主張贖金，先知採納贖金之策。其中有識字者：無力付贖者，以教十名麥地那兒童讀寫為贖；相傳如此得釋者，成為書寫經典的第一批教師。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: When the captives of Badr were divided among the Muslims, Umar said: 'Kill them; for they are the eyes and leaders of unbelief.' Abu Bakr said: 'This is a hard matter; but ransom them, and let their wealth be a help to us against the unbelievers.' The Prophet ransomed them, and it is told that among them were men who could write: for a captive who could not pay his ransom the Prophet took the promise that he should teach ten of the children of Medina to write; and so it was done.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當白德爾的俘虜被分配給穆斯林時，歐麥爾說：「殺了他們吧；因為他們是不信的眼睛和首領。」阿布·伯克爾說：「這是件難事；但讓他們贖身吧，讓他們的財富成為我們對抗不信者的助力。」先知讓他們贖身，據說俘虜中有能書寫的人：對於無力支付贖金的俘虜，先知要他承諾教導麥地那的十個孩子書寫；事情就這樣辦了。

title.en: The Goldsmiths of Qaynuqa Are Expelled
title.zh: 卡努卡金匠被逐

region.en: Qaynuqa market in Medina (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那卡努卡市場（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: After Badr, a quarrel breaks out in the market of the Jewish tribe of Qaynuqa; the word spreads: 'If you meet the army of Muhammad you will learn what men are.' The Prophet beseeches them in the market and they answer with scorn: 'Foolish man, think not your victory over the caravan will strike terror into us.' God commands them to be surrounded; their market is blockaded fifteen days, then the tribe is expelled to Wadi al-Qura.
summary.zh: 白德爾戰後，猶太部族卡努卡的市場起紛爭；一言散播：『若遇穆罕默德之軍，便知何為人。』先知於市場勸誡，眾人譏之：『愚者，勿以商險之勝嚇我。』主命圍之；其市被圍十五日，遂被逐往庫拉谷。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; the expulsion of a Jewish tribe is part of the received narrative and is recorded without embellishment.

passages.text: After Badr a smith and a Muslim quarrelled in the market of Qaynuqa, and a Jew who came to the smith's aid killed the Muslim. The Muslims retaliated. Then word was spread through the tribe: 'If you meet the army of Muhammad you will learn what men are.' The Prophet came to the market and called upon them: 'O assembly of Jews, beware lest God bring upon you the like of what He brought upon the people of Badr — become Muslims, for you know well that you know that this is His religion.' They said: 'O Muhammad, think not that you have struck terror into the men of Quraysh; if you meet us in war you will find us such men as they are not.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 白德爾之後，一名鐵匠和一名穆斯林在蓋努卡族的市場上爭吵，一名前來幫助鐵匠的猶太人殺死了那名穆斯林。穆斯林們進行了報復。隨後，部落中傳開了這樣的話：「如果你們遇上穆罕默德的軍隊，你們就會知道人是什麼樣的。」先知來到市場，向他們呼喚道：「猶太人的會眾啊，當心真主降臨於你們的，如同祂降臨於白德爾之民的那樣——歸信伊斯蘭吧，因為你們很清楚，你們知道這是祂的宗教。」他們說：「穆罕默德啊，不要以為你已使古萊什人膽寒；如果你在戰爭中遇上我們，你會發現我們是他們所不是的那樣的人。」

passages.text: God revealed the command to beset them: 'If you fear betrayal from a people, throw back to them their treaty.' The Prophet besieged them in their quarters for fifteen days; then they surrendered, and were expelled from Medina with their families and tools, going to Wadi al-Qura and then to Syria.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 真主降示了圍困他們的命令：「如果你們害怕一個民族的背叛，就把他們的盟約拋還給他們。」先知在他們的住地圍困了他們十五天；然後他們投降了，帶著家人和工具被逐出麥地那，前往瓦迪·古拉，然後前往敘利亞。

title.en: Hamza's Bow: The Uncle's Conversion
title.zh: 哈姆扎之弓：叔父歸信

region.en: Mecca, hill of Safa (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥加薩法崗（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: Abu Jahl insults the Prophet at Safa; the slave-woman tells Hamza, returning from the hunt with his bow, that his nephew has been reviled. Hamza goes straight to the assembly, lifts his bow, and strikes Abu Jahl on the head: 'Would you insult him, when I follow his religion?' The Prophet thanks God: 'By Him in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, if you are pleased with the religion of Islam, I will pray for you.'
summary.zh: 阿布·賈希勒於薩法辱罵先知；侍女告哈姆扎——正持弓歸獵——其侄受辱。哈姆扎徑赴聚會，舉弓擊阿布·賈希勒頭部：『你辱罵他，而我信奉他的宗教。』先知感謝主：『以穆罕默德性命在其手中的主起誓，若你滿意伊斯蘭之教，我必為你祈禱。』

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib returned one day from hunting with his bow at his shoulder, and a woman of Makhzum told him that Abu Jahl had reviled his nephew and insulted him. Hamza went straight to the Kaaba, where Abu Jahl was sitting among the Quraysh, and stood over him and struck him on the head with his bow: 'Would you insult him, when I follow his religion and believe in what he says? Take vengeance if you can.' Abu Jahl's companions rose to help him; but he said: 'Leave Hamza alone, for I insulted his nephew deeply.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一天，哈姆扎·伊本·阿卜杜勒·穆塔利卜打獵歸來，肩上扛著弓，一位馬赫祖姆族的婦人告訴他，阿布·賈赫勒辱罵了他的侄子並侮辱了他。哈姆扎徑直前往克爾白，阿布·賈赫勒正坐在古萊什人中間，他站到他上方，用弓擊打他的頭：「你侮辱他，而我卻追隨他的宗教、相信他所說的嗎？如果你能，就來報復吧。」阿布·賈赫勒的同伴們起身要幫他；但他說：「別管哈姆扎，因為我深深地侮辱了他的侄子。」

passages.text: And when the Prophet was told, he thanked God that the strongest of the Quraysh had turned; and Hamza came to the Prophet and said: 'By God, if you are pleased with the religion of Islam, I will pray for you.' And Islam grew strong in Mecca.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當先知得知此事，他感謝真主，因為古萊什人中最強壯的人已經歸信了；哈姆扎來到先知面前說：「以真主發誓，如果你對伊斯蘭的宗教感到滿意，我就為你祈禱。」伊斯蘭在麥加日益強大。

title.en: Uhud: The Archers on the Hill
title.zh: 吳候德：山上的弓箭手

region.en: Mount Uhud, north of Medina (literal pin)
region.zh: 麥地那北方的吳候德山（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: Abu Sufyan comes to Medina with three thousand men. The Prophet draws up his men with fifty archers on the hill under Abdullah ibn Jubayr, with orders not to move; the Muslims break the Meccans, but the archers leave their post for the spoils, and Khalid ibn al-Walid wheels around the hill. The Prophet is wounded, Rumah's tooth is broken; Hamza falls, his body mutilated by Hind. 'Return! I am the servant of God.' The Muslims regroup on the mountain, and the Meccans ride home.
summary.zh: 阿布·蘇富揚率三千人至麥地那。先知布陣，五十弓箭手據山，命勿動；穆斯林破古萊氏，弓箭手棄位掠財，哈立德·本·瓦利德繞山回擊。先知負傷，齒被擊斷；哈姆扎陣亡，其屍被欣德毀。『回來！我是主的僕人。』穆斯林重整於山上；古萊氏騎馬而返。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; battle narrative and mutilation of Hamza kept as recorded in public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: In the third year of the Hijra Abu Sufyan came to Medina with three thousand men. The Prophet went out with a thousand, and posted fifty archers on the hill of Aynayn under Abdullah ibn Jubayr: 'Keep the enemy off our backs; if you see us snatching spoil, do not join us; if you see us slain, do not come to help us.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在希吉拉第三年，阿布·蘇富揚率三千人來到麥地那。先知率一千人出城，並在艾奈因山丘上派駐五十名弓箭手，由阿卜杜拉·伊本·朱拜爾率領：「擋住敵人，別讓他們從背後襲擊我們；如果你們看見我們奪取戰利品，不要加入我們；如果你們看見我們被殺，不要來救我們。」

passages.text: The Muslims broke the Meccans and pursued them for spoil; and the archers left their post, all but a dozen. Khalid ibn al-Walid wheeled round the hill and fell on the Muslims from behind; and the Prophet was struck, and his tooth broken, and blood ran down his face. A man cried, 'Muhammad is slain!' and the Muslims wavered; then the Prophet called out: 'Return! I am the servant of God.' And they gathered about him and drew back to the mountainside.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 穆斯林擊潰了麥加人，並追擊他們以奪取戰利品；弓手們離開了他們的崗位，只有十來人留下。哈立德·伊本·瓦利德繞過山丘，從背後襲擊穆斯林；先知受了傷，一顆牙被打斷，鮮血從他臉上流下。有人喊道：『穆罕默德被殺了！』穆斯林於是動搖；接著先知喊道：『回來！我是神的僕人。』他們便聚集到他身邊，退回到山腰。

passages.text: Hamza, the Lion of God, was slain by Wahshi, a javelin-thrower; Hind, wife of Abu Sufyan, mutilated his body and wore his liver as a trophy. Abu Sufyan cried from the hill: 'Glory to Hubal! ... Exalted is our religion.' The Prophet sent back word; and Abu Sufyan turned and rode home to Mecca. The Prophet washed the bodies of the martyrs and buried them; and the Quran reproached the Muslims for the day of Uhud, and then consoled them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「神的雄獅」哈姆扎被投擲標槍的瓦赫希所殺；阿布·蘇富揚之妻辛德殘毀了他的遺體，並把他的肝臟當作戰利品佩戴。阿布·蘇富揚從山上喊道：『榮耀歸於胡巴爾！……我們的宗教是崇高的。』先知傳話回去；阿布·蘇富揚便轉身騎馬返回麥加。先知洗淨了殉道者的遺體並埋葬了他們；《古蘭經》因烏侯德之日責備穆斯林，隨後又安慰了他們。

title.en: The Christians of Najran and the Prayer of Mutual Curse
title.zh: 奈季蘭的基督徒與互相咒詛之禱

region.en: Najran, south Arabian oasis of Christian tribes (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 南阿拉伯奈季蘭綠洲基督教部族（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: A deputation of Christians from Najran visits the Prophet in Medina, debates with him, and disagrees about the nature of Jesus. The Prophet invites them to mubahala — the prayer of mutual imprecation: 'Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, and pray that the curse of God fall on the liars.' They withdraw and agree to pay tribute instead; the Prophet grants them protection of their faith and their churches.
summary.zh: 奈季蘭的基督徒使團至麥地那，與先知辯論，於爾撒之性質上未能一致。先知邀行穆巴哈拉——互相咒詛之禱：『來，我們召集我們的子與你們的子，我們的婦女與你們的婦女，我們自己與你們自己，祈主降咒於說謊者。』他們退而約定繳納貢賦；先知許其信仰與教堂得保護。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; the mubahala episode touches Christian-Muslim relations; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: A deputation of the Christians of Najran, among them their bishop, came to the Prophet at Medina. They entered the mosque in the afternoon, wearing their garments, and debated with him. When they disagreed about Jesus — one saying he is God, another the son of God, a third the third of three — the Prophet said to them: 'Submit, and you will be safe; or pay the jizyah, or come out to a prayer of mutual curse.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 納季蘭的基督徒代表團，其中包括他們的主教，來到麥地那見先知。他們在午後穿著自己的衣服進入清真寺，與他辯論。當他們對耶穌意見不一時——一人說他是神，另一人說他是神之子，第三人說他是三位中的第三位——先知對他們說：『你們歸順，便可平安；或者繳納人丁稅，或者出來與我們一同作互相咒詛的祈禱。』

passages.text: They said, 'Let us consider, and we will answer you.' And when they consulted among themselves, one said: 'You know that he is a prophet sent; and it has reached us that no people who have taken a prayer of mutual curse against a prophet have been spared.' So they said, 'We make peace with you; we will not curse, nor will you curse us.' And the Prophet wrote them a covenant that their faith, their priests, their monks, and their churches should be protected, and that they should pay a tribute in kind.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們說：『讓我們考慮一下，我們會答覆你。』當他們彼此商議時，一人說：『你們知道他是一位被派遣的先知；我們也聽說，凡向先知作互相咒詛之祈禱的民眾，無一得以倖免。』於是他們說：『我們與你們議和；我們不咒詛，你們也不要咒詛我們。』先知便為他們寫下盟約，規定他們的信仰、他們的司祭、他們的修士和他們的教堂應受保護，並規定他們應繳納實物貢賦。

title.en: The Trench: Salman's Ditch and the Wind of God
title.zh: 壕溝之戰：薩勒曼的溝渠與主之風

region.en: Northern Medina, site of the trench (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那北方壕溝戰場（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: Ten thousand of the confederates march on Medina. Salman the Persian advises digging a trench across the open north; the Prophet digs with the men, hauling stones and chanting. The confederates find the city impassable and besiege; Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud, secretly a Muslim, sows distrust between Quraysh and the Jewish allies. Then God sends a wind and a cold: the camp is blown away overnight, and Abu Sufyan breaks up his army.
summary.zh: 聯軍萬人進兵麥地那。波斯人薩勒曼獻策：於北方開闊處掘壕。先知與眾人同掘，搬石而歌。聯軍見城不可入而圍之；秘密歸信的努艾姆·本·麥斯歐德於古萊氏與猶太盟友間播疑。主遣寒風：一夜之間營帳吹散；阿布·蘇富揚撤軍。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: The Quraysh and the Jewish tribes of Nadir gathered a confederacy of ten thousand to crush Medina. The Prophet consulted his Companions, and Salman al-Farisi, the Persian, said: 'In Persia, when we feared horsemen, we dug a trench.' So a trench was dug on the northern side where the city lay open, and the Prophet himself carried the earth and helped the diggers; and as he worked he chanted: 'O God, there is no life but the life of the world to come; so forgive the Ansar and the Muhajirun.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 古萊什人與納迪爾的猶太部落結成萬人聯盟，以粉碎麥地那。先知與他的同伴們商議，波斯人薩爾曼·法里西說：『在波斯，當我們畏懼騎兵時，我們就挖壕溝。』於是他們在城防空虛的北面挖了一條壕溝，先知親自搬土，幫助挖掘的人；他一邊勞作一邊吟唱：『神啊，除了來世的生命，別無生命；所以求你饒恕輔士與遷士。』

passages.text: The confederates found Medina hedged by the trench and laid siege for some days. Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud, who had become a Muslim in secret, went first to Quraysh and then to the Jews, and told each that the other meant to betray them, so that neither dared trust the other. Then God sent against them a wind and armies they could not see: the tent of Abu Sufyan was uprooted, the fires went out, and in the morning the confederates were gone.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 聯盟軍發現麥地那有壕溝為屏障，便圍攻了數日。暗中歸信伊斯蘭的努阿伊姆·伊本·馬斯歐德先到古萊什人那裡，再到猶太人那裡，告訴每一方說另一方打算背叛他們，以致雙方都不敢信任對方。接著神差遣風和他們看不見的軍隊來攻擊他們：阿布·蘇富揚的帳篷被連根拔起，火堆熄滅，到了早晨聯盟軍已經離去。

title.en: The Judgment on Banu Qurayza
title.zh: 古萊扎部族之判

region.en: Banu Qurayza quarter, Medina (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那古萊扎部族居地（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: After the trench, Gabriel in armour orders the Prophet against Banu Qurayza, who had been confederates of the enemy. The tribe shuts itself in its forts for twenty-five days; then it offers to depart leaving its property, and the Prophet refers the case to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, their ally, who judges by the law of their own book: the men to die, the women and children into captivity, the property divided. The judgment is executed; modern historians read the episode as the grim law of tribal siege-war.
summary.zh: 壕溝戰後，吉布里勒披甲諭先知討古萊扎部族——其曾為敵盟。該族閉守堡壘二十五日；後請求棄財而去；先知以其盟友薩德·本·穆阿茲裁決，按其本教之法判：男子處死，婦孺入俘，財產分配。判決執行；現代史家視之為部落圍城戰之嚴法。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; the judgment on Banu Qurayza is among the gravest episodes of the sira; recorded as received, without embellishment, and noted as the tradition's own account.

passages.text: When the confederates had withdrawn, the angel Gabriel came to the Prophet wearing a turban of brocade and riding a mule with a saddle of brocade, and said: 'Have you laid down your arms? The angels have not yet laid down theirs; God commands you to go to Banu Qurayza: I am about to go to shake their fortress.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當同盟軍撤退後，天使加百列來到先知面前，頭戴錦緞頭巾，騎著一頭配著錦緞鞍的騾子，說道：「你已經放下武器了嗎？天使們尚未放下他們的武器；真主命令你前往古萊扎族：我這就要去震動他們的堡壘。」

passages.text: The Prophet besieged their forts for twenty-five days. Then they sent asking that Abu Lubaba be sent to them, and they asked whether they should submit; he pointed to his throat — death. They said: 'We will depart with our families and children and leave our property.' He refused. They said: 'Let judgment be given by Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, our ally.' And Sa'd, wounded from the trench and brought on a donkey, judged according to their Torah: 'The men shall be killed, the property divided, and the women and children taken captive.' The Prophet said: 'You have judged them with the judgment of the King above the kings.' And it was done as Sa'd judged.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 先知圍攻他們的堡壘二十五日。於是他們派人請求派阿布·魯巴巴前來，並詢問他們是否應當投降；他指了指自己的喉嚨——意即死亡。他們說：「我們願帶著家眷和子女離去，留下我們的財產。」他拒絕了。他們說：「那就讓我們的盟友薩阿德·伊本·穆阿茲來裁決吧。」薩阿德在壕溝之戰中負傷，被人用驢子載來，他依照他們的《托拉》裁決道：「男子當殺，財產當分，婦孺當俘。」先知說：「你已用萬王之王之上的君王的裁決裁決了他們。」於是便照薩阿德所裁決的實行了。

title.en: Hudaybiyya: The Pledge of the Tree
title.zh: 侯代比亞：樹下之誓

region.en: Hudaybiyya, on the road to Mecca (literal pin)
region.zh: 麥加道上的侯代比亞（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: The Prophet sets out for the umra with fourteen hundred men, and the Quraysh bar the way at Hudaybiyya. Uthman is sent to treat and is reported slain; the Prophet takes the oath of the tree — the Pledge of Ridwan — and God gives 'a manifest victory' by revelation. The treaty is signed: peace for ten years, return of this year's pilgrims, pilgrimage next year. The Companions are dismayed; Umar protests, and Abu Bakr answers that the Prophet knows; then the sura of the Victory is revealed.
summary.zh: 先知率千四百人往副朝，古萊氏於侯代比亞阻道。遣奧斯曼議和；傳其遇害；先知行樹下之誓——里德萬之誓——主降『明顯的勝利』之啟示。條約成：十年止戈，今年朝者返，明年可朝。聖門弟子惶惑；歐瑪爾抗議，阿布·伯克爾答：先知自知；隨後《勝利章》降示。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: In the sixth year of the Hijra the Prophet set out with fourteen hundred men, dressed as pilgrims, with sacrificial camels, for the umra of Mecca. The Quraysh barred the way at Hudaybiyya. Uthman ibn Affan was sent to negotiate; a rumour came that he had been killed. The Prophet called his men beneath a tree and took from them the pledge of life and death — the Pledge of Ridwan: 'We will not flee.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 遷徙歷第六年，先知率一千四百人出發，身著朝覲者的服裝，帶著獻祭的駱駝，前往麥加行副朝。古萊什族在侯代比亞阻擋了道路。奧斯曼·伊本·阿凡被派去談判；有傳言說他被殺了。先知在一棵樹下召集他的部下，從他們那裡接受了生死之誓——里德萬之誓：「我們絕不逃跑。」

passages.text: Then came Suhayl ibn Amr to treat, and the treaty was written: peace between the parties for ten years; the Muslims to return this year without entering; pilgrimage allowed in the following year, three days only. Umar cried out in dismay: 'Are we not on the truth, and they on error?' Abu Bakr said: 'He is the servant of God, and He will not abandon him.' Then the sura of Victory came down: 'We have given thee a manifest victory, that God may forgive thee... and guide thee on a straight path.' And the Prophet shaved his head and sacrificed, and returned to Medina.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 隨後蘇海勒·伊本·阿姆爾前來議和，和約遂寫成：雙方休戰十年；穆斯林今年返回，不得進入；次年准許朝覲，僅限三日。歐麥爾驚呼道：「我們難道不在真理之上，而他們在迷誤之中嗎？」阿布·伯克爾說：「他是真主的僕人，真主絕不會拋棄他。」隨後《勝利章》降示：「我確已賜你一種明顯的勝利，以便真主赦宥你……並引導你於正路。」先知遂剃頭並獻祭，返回麥地那。

title.en: Khaybar: Ali and the Gate
title.zh: 海白爾：阿里與門扉

region.en: Fortresses of Khaybar, oasis north of Medina (literal pin)
region.zh: 麥地那以北海白爾綠洲要塞（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: The confederacy broken, the Prophet marches against the strongholds of Khaybar. Day after day a different chief leads; every fort falls. 'Tomorrow I shall give the banner to a man whom God and His Messenger love.' Ali ibn Abi Talib, with an inflamed eye, is given the banner; he prays and advances, fights Marhab, and in the tradition lifts the gate of the fortress and fights behind it. The terms of surrender give the Jews their lives, their land and half the year's crop.
summary.zh: 聯軍既破，先知進軍海白爾要塞。日日易帥，堡壘相繼陷落。『明日我將授旗於主與其使者所愛之人。』阿里·本·阿比·塔里卜眼疾發作而受旗；他祈禱進軍，戰馬爾哈布；相傳其獨力舉起要塞之門，門後作戰。降約保其生命、土地與半年收成之半。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; the gate of Khaybar is a famous Shi'i devotion episode; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: After the treaty of Hudaybiyya the Prophet marched on the fortresses of Khaybar, where the Jewish chiefs of the confederacy had taken refuge. He took the forts one after another, the banner passing day by day from chief to chief; and when a fort stood fast he said: 'Tomorrow I shall give the banner to a man whom God and His Messenger love, who will return with victory.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 侯代比亞和約之後，先知進軍海巴爾的堡壘，同盟軍的猶太首領們曾逃往那裡避難。他逐一攻下各堡，旗幟一日一日地從一位首領手中傳到另一位首領手中；當一座堡壘久攻不下時，他說：「明日我將把旗幟交給一個真主及其使者所喜愛的人，他將帶著勝利歸來。」

passages.text: Ali ibn Abi Talib was given the banner though his eyes were inflamed; the Prophet spat upon them and they healed. Ali advanced against Marhab, the master of the fort, and slew him; and in the tradition he wrenched the gate of the fortress from its hinges, and fought with it as a shield. The terms of surrender spared the lives of the defenders: they were left their land and half the crop of each year.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿里·伊本·阿比·塔利卜雖雙眼紅腫，仍被授予旗幟；先知向他的雙眼吐了唾沫，雙眼便痊癒了。阿里向堡壘之主馬爾哈卜進擊，將他殺死；據傳述，他將堡壘的大門從鉸鏈上拔下，以之為盾而戰。投降的條件保全了守衛者的性命：他們保有自己的土地，並每年分得收成的一半。

title.en: Mu'tah: The Three Martyrs of the Standing Ground
title.zh: 穆塔：三位烈士的陣地

region.en: Mu'tah, on the road to Syria (literal pin)
region.zh: 敘利亞道上的穆塔（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: A small expedition of three thousand goes to Syria after the killing of the Prophet's envoy. It meets the army of Heraclius' commanders. Zayd falls; then Ja'far, leaping from his horse and hamstringing it, advances crying 'Paradise, Paradise' until both arms are cut off; then Abdullah ibn Rawaha, weeping, saying he does not fear death. Khalid ibn al-Walid, fourth in command, saves the remnant by his manoeuvres and brings them home — the battle of the standing ground.
summary.zh: 使者被害後，三千人的小隊赴敘利亞。遇希拉克略將領之軍。載德陣亡；繼而加法爾，下馬斷其馬腱，高呼『樂園，樂園』，直至雙臂被斬；再而伊本·勞瓦哈含淚赴死。第四任指揮哈立德·本·瓦利德以機動保全部眾而歸——陣地之戰。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: The Prophet's envoy to the Ghassanid ruler was killed at Mu'tah, and an expedition of three thousand set out under Zayd ibn Haritha; if he fell, Ja'far; if he fell, Abdullah ibn Rawaha; if he fell, let the Muslims choose. They met the army of the Byzantine commanders at Mu'tah.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 先知派往加薩尼王室的使者於穆塔遇害，於是三千人的遠征隊在宰德·伊本·哈里薩率領下出發；若他陣亡，則由賈法爾接任；若他陣亡，則由阿卜杜拉·伊本·拉瓦哈接任；若他陣亡，則讓穆斯林自行推選。他們在穆塔與拜占庭將領的軍隊相遇。

passages.text: Zayd fought on until he was killed; then Ja'far took the banner. He fought until his right hand was cut off, then his left; he leapt from his horse, hamstrung it, and advanced on foot crying: 'Paradise! Paradise!' — and was slain with a sword-stroke. Abdullah ibn Rawaha took the banner weeping — not for death, he said, but because he could not describe what he longed for: 'O soul, go forth; you are being offered no more than death.' He too fell. Khalid ibn al-Walid, last named in command, kept the army from breaking and brought the survivors home.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 宰德奮戰至死；接著賈法爾接過旗幟。他奮戰至右手被砍斷，接著左手也被砍斷；他跳下馬，割斷馬腿，徒步向前，高呼：「樂園！樂園！」——隨後被一刀殺死。阿卜杜拉·伊本·拉瓦哈接過旗幟，哭泣著——他說，不是為死亡而哭，而是因為他無法描述自己所渴望的：「啊，靈魂，前進吧；你所被給予的，不過是死亡。」他也倒下了。哈立德·伊本·瓦利德，最後被任命為統帥，阻止了軍隊潰散，並將生還者帶回家鄉。

title.en: Letters to the Kings: Heraclius, Khosrau, the Negus
title.zh: 致君王之書：希拉克略、霍斯勞與尼格斯

region.en: Medina, dispatch of envoys (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那遣使之時（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: After Hudaybiyya, letters are sent sealed to the rulers of the world: to Heraclius at Constantinople, to Khosrau in Persia, to the Negus of Abyssinia, to Muqawqis in Egypt. Khosrau tears up his letter; the Prophet says: 'May God tear his kingdom.' Heraclius asks after the genealogy and truthfulness of the claimant and weighs the signs. The Negus reads, and weeps; Muqawqis sends gifts, among them two slave-girls, one of whom, Mary, the Prophet takes to wife.
summary.zh: 侯代比亞之後，封印之書致各國之主：君士坦丁堡的希拉克略、波斯的霍斯勞、阿比西尼亞的尼格斯、埃及的穆卡瓦斯。霍斯勞撕裂其書；先知言：『願主撕裂其國。』希拉克略問其譜系與誠實，權衡其兆。尼格斯讀之而泣；穆卡瓦斯饋禮，其中有侍女二人，其一馬麗亞，後為先知之妻。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: The Prophet sent letters to the kings of the earth, sealed and delivered by riders: to Heraclius in Constantinople, to Khosrau the Persian, to the Negus of Abyssinia, to Muqawqis in Egypt, to the Ghassanid and the Himyarite princes.
