To each, the same invitation: 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. From Muhammad, the servant of God and His Messenger, to Heraclius the great of Byzantium: Peace to him who follows the guidance. I invite you with the invitation of Islam... If you turn away, then upon you be the sin of the peasants.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 先知向大地上的君王們派遣書信，加封並由騎手遞送：致君士坦丁堡的希拉克略，致波斯的霍斯勞，致阿比西尼亞的奈古斯，致埃及的穆卡烏基斯，致加薩尼與希木葉爾的親王們。致每一位，都是同樣的邀請：「奉至仁至慈的真主之名。來自真主的僕人及其使者穆罕默德，致拜占庭的偉大者希拉克略：願平安歸於遵循正道者。我以伊斯蘭的邀請邀請你……若你轉身離去，那麼農民的罪責將歸於你。」

passages.text: Khosrau tore the letter and said, 'A slave of my slaves writes to me?' The Prophet was told and said: 'May God tear his kingdom.' Heraclius assembled the patriarchs of his realm and asked of the claimant's lineage, his following, his wars; the traders of Quraysh answered him, and Heraclius weighed the signs. The Negus read the letter and wept, and said: 'Of a truth this is the spirit of truth.' Muqawqis sent gifts, among them two slave-girls, one of whom, Mary, became the wife of the Prophet.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 霍斯勞撕毀了書信，說道：「我奴隸中的一個奴隸寫信給我？」先知得知後說道：「願真主撕裂他的王國。」希拉克略召集其國土的宗主教們，詢問那位自稱者的血統、他的追隨者、他的戰爭；古萊什的商人回答了他，希拉克略權衡了種種跡象。奈古斯讀了書信後哭泣，說道：「誠然，這是真理之靈。」穆卡烏基斯送來禮物，其中有兩名女奴，其中一位名叫瑪利亞，後來成為先知的妻子。

title.en: Tzŭ Ch'i Buries Himself: The Music of Heaven, Earth, and Man (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 南郭子綦隱機而坐：天籟、地籟、人籟（莊子）

region.en: Nan-kuo (southern wall quarter), Ch'i or Song capital (symbolic pin: Shangqiu, Henan, China)
region.zh: 南郭（象徵定位：河南商丘）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 2, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 2

summary.en: Tzŭ Ch'i of Nan-kuo sits at his table like dry wood, and buries himself. From that entranced state he explains the three musics: the wind roaring through every hollow of hill and forest is the music of Earth; pipes and flutes the music of Man; and the music of Heaven is what gives each aperture its individual sound.
summary.zh: 南郭子綦隱機而坐，嗒焉似喪其耦，自謂今者吾喪我；乃論三籟：山林之畏佳大木百圍之竅穴，風之作則萬竅怒呺——此天籟之風、地籟之穴、人籟之比竹。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: Tzŭ Ch'i of Nan-kuo sat leaning on a table. Looking up to heaven, he sighed and became absent, as though soul and body had parted. Yen Ch'êng Tzŭ Yu, who was standing by him, exclaimed, "What are you thinking about that your body should become thus like dry wood, your mind like dead ashes? Surely the man now leaning on the table is not he who was here just now." "My friend," replied Tzŭ Ch'i, "your question is apposite. To-day I have buried myself.... Do you understand?... Ah! perhaps you only know the music of Man, and not that of Earth. Or even if you have heard the music of Earth, you have not heard the music of Heaven."
passages.zh: 南郭的子綦靠著几案坐著。他仰頭望天，嘆了口氣，變得恍恍惚惚，彷彿魂魄與形體已經分離。站在他身旁的顏成子游驚呼道：「您在思索什麼，竟使您的形體變得如此像枯木，您的心靈像死灰？剛才靠著几案的人，肯定已經不是現在這個人了。」「我的朋友，」子綦回答說，「你的問題問得好。今天我把自己丟失了……你明白嗎？……啊！也許你只知道人的音樂，而不知道地的音樂。或者，即使你聽過地的音樂，你也沒有聽過天的音樂。」

passages.text: "The breath of the universe," continued Tzŭ Ch'i, "is called wind. At times, it is inactive. But when active, every aperture resounds to the blast. Have you never listened to its growing roar? Caves and dells of hill and forest, hollows in huge trees of many a span in girth;--these are like nostrils, like mouths, like ears, like beam-sockets, like goblets, like mortars, like ditches, like bogs. And the wind goes rushing through them, sniffing, snoring, singing, soughing, puffing, purling, whistling, whirring, now shrilly treble, now deeply bass, now soft, now loud; until, with a lull, silence reigns supreme. Have you never witnessed among the trees such a disturbance as this?"
passages.zh: 「宇宙的氣息，」子綦繼續說道，「叫做風。有時，它靜止不動。但當它活動時，每一個孔竅都對它的吹拂發出迴響。你難道從未聽過它逐漸增長的呼嘯嗎？山丘與森林的洞穴與谷地，周長數丈的大樹中的空洞；——這些就像鼻孔、像嘴巴、像耳朵、像梁孔、像杯盂、像臼、像溝渠、像沼澤。風衝過它們，嗅著、打鼾、歌唱、颯颯作響、噴氣、潺潺、呼嘯、嗡嗡作響，時而尖細如高音，時而深沉如低音，時而柔和，時而響亮；直到一陣平息，寂靜統治一切。你難道從未在樹林間見過這樣的騷動嗎？」

passages.text: "Well, then," enquired Tzŭ Yu, "since the music of earth consists of nothing more than holes, and the music of man of pipes and flutes,--of what consists the music of Heaven?" "The effect of the wind upon these various apertures," replied Tzŭ Ch'i, "is not uniform. But what is it that gives to each the individuality, to all the potentiality, of sound?"
passages.zh: 「那麼，」子游問道，「既然地籟不過是眾竅穴所發之聲，人籟不過是簫管笛竹所奏之音——那麼天籟又是什麼呢？」「風吹過這些種種孔竅，」子綦回答，「所生的聲響並不齊一。但究竟是什麼，使每一孔竅各得其獨特之聲，使一切孔竅皆具成聲之能呢？」

title.en: Three in the Morning: The Monkey-Keeper's Chestnuts (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 朝三暮四（莊子）

region.en: A monkey-keeper's park (symbolic pin: Song, Henan, China)
region.zh: 狙公之園（象徵定位：宋，今河南）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 2, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 2

summary.en: A monkey-keeper announces a ration of three chestnuts in the morning and four at night; the monkeys rage. Four in the morning and three at night, and they are delighted. The total never changed — only the adaptation to their likes and dislikes, which is how the sage handles contraries.
summary.zh: 狙公賦芧曰朝三而暮四，眾狙皆怒；曰然則朝四而暮三，眾狙皆悅。名實未虧而喜怒為用，聖人和之以是非而休乎天鈞。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: "What is Three in the Morning?" asked Tzŭ Yu. "A keeper of monkeys," replied Tzŭ Ch'i, "said with regard to their rations of chestnuts that each monkey was to have three in the morning and four at night. But at this the monkeys were very angry, so the keeper said they might have four in the morning and three at night, with which arrangement they were all well pleased. The actual number of the chestnuts remained the same, but there was an adaptation to the likes and dislikes of those concerned. Such is the principle of putting oneself into subjective relation with externals."
passages.zh: 「什麼是『朝三』？」子游問道。「有一個養猴的人，」子綦回答，「談到分給猴子橡子的口糧時說，每隻猴子早晨給三顆，晚上給四顆。猴子們聽了非常憤怒，於是養猴人便說，可以早晨給四顆，晚上給三顆，猴子們對這樣的安排都十分滿意。橡子的實際數目仍舊一樣，只是順應了猴子們的喜惡罷了。這就是把自己與外物置於主觀關係之中的道理。」

title.en: Before the Beginning: The Regress of Time (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 有始也者：莊子的時間追溯（莊子）

region.en: The realm of contemplation (symbolic pin: Song, Henan, China)
region.zh: 思辨之境（象徵定位：宋，今河南）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 2, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 2

summary.en: Zhuangzi's cosmogonic regress: if there was a beginning, there was a time before that beginning, and a time before that time; if there is existence, there must have been non-existence, and a time before that when even nothing did not exist — ending in the claim that the universe and I came into being together, and all things are one.
summary.zh: 莊子之宇宙論追溯：有始也者，有未始有始也者，有未始有夫未始有始也者；有有也者，有無也者，有未始有無也者——天地與我並生，而萬物與我為一。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); a priority Creation & Cosmology narrative.

passages.text: "If there was a beginning, then there was a time before that beginning. And a time before the time which was before the time of that beginning. "If there is existence, there must have been non-existence. And if there was a time when nothing existed, then there must have been a time before that--when even nothing did not exist. Suddenly, when nothing came into existence, could one really say whether it belonged to the category of existence or of non-existence? Even the very words I have just now uttered,--I cannot say whether they have really been uttered or not.
passages.zh: 「如果有開始，那麼就有在那開始之前的時間。而且還有在那開始之前的時間之前的時間。如果有存在，就必定曾有不存在。而如果曾有一個什麼都不存在的時候，那麼就必定曾有在那之前的時候——那時甚至連『無』也不存在。忽然之間，當『無』產生出來的時候，人真能說它屬於存在的範疇，還是屬於不存在的範疇嗎？甚至我剛才所說的這些話——我也不能斷定它們究竟是真的被說出來了，還是沒有。」

passages.text: "There is nothing under the canopy of heaven greater than the tip of an autumn spikelet. A vast mountain is a small thing. Neither is there any age greater than that of a child cut off in infancy. P'êng Tsu himself died young. The universe and I came into being together; and I, and everything therein, are ONE."
passages.zh: 「普天之下，沒有比秋毫之末更大的東西。巍峨的大山是渺小的。也沒有比夭折的嬰兒更長壽的。彭祖本人倒是少年早亡。天地與我並生，而萬物與我為一。」

title.en: Wang Ni and the Perfect Man Who Drives Sun and Moon (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 王倪論至人（莊子）

region.en: The dialogue of remote antiquity (symbolic pin: Song, Henan, China)
region.zh: 上古問答（象徵定位：宋，今河南）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 2, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 2

summary.en: Yeh Ch'üeh presses Wang Ni to affirm an absolute standard of good; Wang Ni answers with the eel that likes wet, the monkey that likes trees, and the beauties at whom fish and birds flee. The Perfect Man, though, is a spiritual being: scorched ocean and frozen Milky Way cannot touch him; he mounts the clouds, driving the sun and moon before him, beyond death and life.
summary.zh: 齧缺問王倪四問而四不知；乃言民濕寢則疾、鰍然乎哉，正處正味正色相對而莫定；至人神矣——大澤焚而不能熱，河漢冱而不能寒，乘雲氣，騎日月，而遊乎四海之外，死生無變於己。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: "How can I know?" answered Wang I. "Do you know what you do not know?" "How can I know?" replied Yeh Ch'üeh. "But can then nothing be known?" "How can I know?" said Wang I. "Nevertheless, I will try to tell you. How can it be known that what I call knowing is not really not knowing, and that what I call not knowing is not really knowing? Now I would ask you this. If a man sleeps in a damp place, he gets lumbago and dies. But how about an eel? And living up in a tree is precarious and trying to the nerves;--but how about monkeys? Of the man, the eel, and the monkey, whose habitat is the right one, absolutely? Human beings feed on flesh, deer on grass, centipedes on snakes, owls and crows on mice. Of these four, whose is the right taste, absolutely?
passages.zh: 「我怎麼知道呢？」王倪回答。「你知道你所不知道的嗎？」「我怎麼知道呢？」齧缺回答。「那麼，難道就什麼都不能知道了嗎？」「我怎麼知道呢？」王倪說。「不過，我還是試著告訴你吧。怎麼能知道我所謂的知道，其實並不是不知道；而我所謂的不知道，其實並不是知道呢？現在我來問你這個問題。假如一個人睡在潮濕的地方，他會腰疼乃至死去。可是鰻魚又怎樣呢？住在樹上既危險又使神經緊張——可是猴子又怎樣呢？人、鰻魚和猴子，究竟誰的居處才是絕對正確的呢？人吃禽獸之肉，鹿吃草，蜈蚣吃蛇，貓頭鷹和烏鴉吃老鼠。這四者，究竟誰的口味才是絕對正確的呢？」

passages.text: "Monkey mates with monkey, the buck with the doe; eels consort with fishes, while men admire Mao Ch'iang and Li Chi, at the sight of whom fishes plunge deep down in the water, birds soar high in the air, and deer hurry away. Yet who shall say which is the correct standard of beauty?
passages.zh: 「猿猴與猿猴交配，麋鹿與麋鹿相配；鰻魚與魚類為伴，而人卻愛慕毛嬙與麗姬，魚見了她們便潛入水底，鳥見了她們便高飛入空，鹿見了她們便急忙逃開。然而誰能說哪一種才是正確的美的標準呢？」

passages.text: "The Perfect Man," answered Wang I, "is a spiritual being. Were the ocean itself scorched up, he would not feel hot. Were the Milky Way frozen hard, he would not feel cold. Were the mountains to be riven with thunder, and the great deep to be thrown up by storm, he would not tremble. In such case, he would mount upon the clouds of heaven, and driving the sun and the moon before him, would pass beyond the limits of this external world, where death and life have no more victory over man;--how much less what is bad for him?"
passages.zh: 「至人，」王倪回答，「是神靈般的存在。即使海洋本身被燒乾，他也不會感到炎熱。即使銀河凍結堅硬，他也不會感到寒冷。即使山岳被雷電劈裂，深海被暴風掀起，他也不會顫抖。如此一來，他便會登上天際的雲彩，驅使日月在前，超越這外在世界的界限，在那裡生死再也無法勝過人；——更何況是對他不利的事物呢？」

title.en: Li Chi's Weeping and the Great Awakening (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 麗姬之泣與大覺（莊子）

region.en: The court of Chin (Houma, Shanxi, China)
region.zh: 晉宮（今山西侯馬）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 2, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 2

summary.en: Li Chi, the border chieftain's daughter, wept until her dress was soaked when she was taken to the Duke of Chin — then repented of her tears once she ate rich food in the palace. From this Zhuangzi argues that the dead may repent of clinging to life, and that waking and dreaming, life and death, are one great dream whose Great Awakening lies ten thousand generations away.
summary.zh: 麗姬初聞晉君之聘，泣涕沾襟；及至王所，與王同筐牀，食芻豢，而悔其泣也。莊周因言：死生如夢覺，方其夢也不知其夢——大覺而後知此其大夢也。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); a Taoist death-and-transformation narrative, tagged origin-of-death as a comparative (non-origin-myth) analogue.

passages.text: "The lady Li Chi was the daughter of Ai Fêng. When the Duke of Chin first got her, she wept until the bosom of her dress was drenched with tears. But when she came to the royal residence, and lived with the Duke, and ate rich food, she repented of having wept. How then do I know but that the dead repent of having previously clung to life?
passages.zh: 「麗姬是艾封的女兒。晉獻公初次得到她時，她哭泣不止，直到衣襟被淚水浸透。但當她來到王宮，與獻公同住，吃著豐盛的食物，她便後悔當初的哭泣。那麼，我怎能知道死者不會後悔先前對生命的執著呢？」

passages.text: "Those who dream of the banquet, wake to lamentation and sorrow. Those who dream of lamentation and sorrow wake to join the hunt. While they dream, they do not know that they dream. Some will even interpret the very dream they are dreaming; and only when they awake do they know it was a dream. By and by comes the Great Awakening, and then we find out that this life is really a great dream. Fools think they are awake now, and flatter themselves they know if they are really princes or peasants. Confucius and you are both dreams; and I who say you are dreams,--I am but a dream myself. This is a paradox. Tomorrow a sage may arise to explain it; but that tomorrow will not be until ten thousand generations have gone by."
passages.zh: 「那些夢見宴飲的人，醒來時卻悲嘆哀傷。那些夢見悲嘆哀傷的人，醒來時卻投身狩獵。當他們做夢時，並不知道自己正在做夢。有些人甚至會解讀自己正在做的夢；只有當他們醒來時，才知道那是一場夢。漸漸地，大覺醒來臨，那時我們便會發現，這一生其實是一場大夢。愚人以為自己現在是清醒的，並自誇知道自己是真正的君王還是農夫。孔子和你都是夢；而說你們是夢的我——我自己也不過是一場夢。這是一個悖論。明天或許會有聖人出現來解釋它；但那明天要等到萬代過去之後才會到來。」

title.en: The Penumbra and the Umbra (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 罔兩問景（莊子）

region.en: The dialogue of shadows (symbolic pin: Song, Henan, China)
region.zh: 影之問答（象徵定位：宋，今河南）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 2, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 2

summary.en: The penumbra upbraids the shadow's constant shifting — now moving, now resting, now sitting down. The shadow answers that it depends on something which itself depends on something else, like the snake's scales or the cicada's wings; how can it tell why it does one thing or another?
summary.zh: 罔兩責景之無常；景答：行止坐起皆有所待，而所待者又有所待，如蛇蚹蜩翼，惡識所以然、惡識所以不然？

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: The Penumbra said to the Umbra, "At one moment you move: at another you are at rest. At one moment you sit down: at another you get up. Why this instability of purpose?" "I depend," replied the Umbra, "upon something which causes me to do as I do; and that something depends in turn upon something else which causes it to do as it does. My dependence is like that of a snake's scales or of a cicada's wings. How can I tell why I do one thing, or why I do not do another?"
passages.zh: 半影對影子說：「有時你移動，有時你靜止。有時你坐下，有時你起身。為何這般意志不定？」「我依賴於某物，」影子回答，「是它使我如此行動；而那某物又依賴於另一物，是它使其如此行動。我的依賴就像蛇的鱗片或蟬的翅膀。我怎能知道我為何做一件事，或為何不做另一件事呢？」

title.en: Tobit Buries the Dead in Nineveh and Loses His Sight
title.zh: 多比在尼尼微葬死者而失明

region.en: Nineveh, land of exile
region.zh: 尼尼微，被擄之地

period: Composed c. 3rd-2nd c. BCE (Aramaic/Hebrew original); principal text: Codex Sinaiticus Greek, 4th c. CE

source.work: Tobit 1-2 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: Tobit of the Naphtali exile keeps tithes and alms in Assyria alone among his kinsmen; he carries the dead bodies of murdered Israelites at risk of his life, and his neighbours mock him: 'he is afraid to be killed for the works he does'. Sleeping in his courtyard, sparrow droppings fall in his eyes and he is blind; his wife Anna works for wages, and his rebuke — 'were it not better for us to have alms and righteousness?' — closes the first movement of the book of mercy.
summary.zh: 拿弗他利支派被擄的多比在亞述獨行什一與賙濟；他不顧性命攜葬被殺的以色列人，鄰舍譏笑：「他怕人殺他，但這樣行有何益處？」在院中睡臥，雀糞落入眼中而失明；妻子亞拿做傭工，他的責備——「不如行賙濟行公義」——結束這部憐憫之書的第一幕。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture (scripture for Catholic/Orthodox communities; 'reading' for Jewish tradition); quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha. Found in the Cairo Genizah and Qumran in Aramaic and Hebrew.

passages.text: In the days of Shalmaneser king of the Assyrians, I, Tobit, was carried away captive... And because I was mindful of God with all my heart, all the days of my life did I walk righteously... I carried the dead bodies of them into my house; and at midnight I buried them. ... And because I had kept the commandments of God my father, they murmured against me.
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Tobit 1:3-19 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 在亞述王撒縵以色的日子，我多俾亞被擄去……因為我全心謹記上帝，我一生行走正直……我將他們的屍體搬進我的屋內；並在半夜埋葬他們。……因為我遵守了我父上帝的誡命，他們便向我抱怨。

passages.text: Resting in the courtyard, warm sparrows fell on his open eyes and left white films; 'whereby I was deprived of my sight'. His wife brought wages, and also a kid; Tobit heard it bleat and said: 'Take heed lest it be stolen; carry it back again'. His wife answered: 'Were it not better for us to have alms and righteousness? For I have brought them, and heard the bleating of the goat.' Tobit was grieved and prayed. Paraphrase of Tobit 2:1-14 (KJV Apocrypha); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Tobit 2:1-14 (KJV Apocrypha); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他在庭院中休息時，溫熱的麻雀落在他的眼睛上，留下白色的薄膜；「因此我失去了視力」。他的妻子帶回了工錢，還有一隻小山羊；多俾亞聽見牠的叫聲便說：「小心，免得那是偷來的；把牠送回去。」他的妻子回答：「我們有施捨和公義豈不更好嗎？因為是我帶回來的，而且我聽見了山羊的叫聲。」多俾亞憂傷並祈禱。改述自《多俾亞傳》2:1-14（欽定版次經）；並非逐字照錄。

title.en: Raphael Travels with Tobias: The Demon Asmodeus and the Fish
title.zh: 拉斐爾同行多比雅：惡魔阿斯莫德與魚

region.en: Road to Ecbatana, Media
region.zh: 往瑪代伊克巴他拿之路

period: Composed c. 3rd-2nd c. BCE; principal text: Codex Sinaiticus Greek, 4th c. CE

source.work: Tobit 6-11 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: Sent to Media to reclaim money, young Tobias travels with a 'companion' who is the angel Raphael in disguise. A fish leaps out of the Tigris; the angel orders its heart and liver burned on coals — the smoke drives away the demon Asmodeus, who has killed seven bridegrooms of Sarah; its gall cures Tobit's blind eyes. Raphael reveals himself only at the end: 'I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels', and teaches: 'alms do deliver from death'.
summary.zh: 多比雅受遣往瑪代取銀，得「同伴」同行——實為喬裝的天使拉斐爾。底格里斯河中大魚躍出；天使命以其心肝於炭上焚燒——烟氣驅走阿斯莫德惡魔，它曾連殺撒拉七個丈夫；魚膽醫好多比的眼睛。末了拉斐爾自顯：「我是拉斐爾，七位聖天使之一」，並教導：「賙濟能救人脫離死亡」。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha. Angelology here (seven holy angels) shaped later Jewish and Christian angel-lore.

passages.text: And they went forth, and came to the river Tigris, and lodged together. And when the young man went down to wash himself, a fish leaped out of the river, and would have devoured him. Then the angel said unto him: 'Take the fish.' And the young man laid hold of the fish, and drew it upon land. ... Then the angel said to him: 'Take the heart and the liver of the fish and put them in thy vessel'; ... And the angel said unto him: 'If thou wilt take this... and make smoke thereof before a man or woman afflicted with any evil spirit, it will drive it away.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Tobit 6:1-8 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 他們便出發，來到底格里斯河，一同投宿。少年人下去洗身的時候，有一條魚從河裡跳出來，想要吞了他。天使對他說：「抓住那條魚。」少年人就抓住那條魚，把它拉上岸來。……天使對他說：「取出那魚的心和肝，放在你的器皿裡」；……天使對他說：「你若取這……在受任何惡神折磨的男人或女人面前燻出煙來，就能把那惡神驅走。」

passages.text: Sarah, daughter of Raguel, had been given seven husbands, 'which Asmodeus the evil spirit had killed, before they had lain with her'; the maids blamed her as though she had strangled them. Tobias accepts her in marriage per the law of Moses; the fish-heart and liver are burned on the coals of perfumes, 'the smell thereof put the evil spirit to flight', and the angel pursues him into Egypt and binds him. Tobit's eyes are cured with the gall. Raphael reveals himself: 'I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels... and all the days of my life did walk with the blind'; and the book closes with the teaching 'it is better to have alms with righteousness than goods without righteousness'. Paraphrase of Tobit 7-8; 11; 12-13 (KJV Apocrypha); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Tobit 7-8; 11-13 (KJV Apocrypha); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 拉古珥的女兒撒拉曾被許配給七個丈夫，「那惡神阿斯摩太在他們與她同房之前就把他們殺了」；婢女們卻歸罪於她，彷彿是她把他們勒死的。多俾亞照摩西的律法娶她為妻；魚心和魚肝在香料炭火上焚燒，「其氣味使那惡神逃遁」，天使追趕他進入埃及，將他捆綁。多俾特的眼用魚膽治好。辣法耳顯明自己：「我是辣法耳，是七位聖天使之一……我一生一世與那盲者同行」；全書以這教訓作結：「行施捨而兼有公義，勝於積財而無公義。」（多俾亞傳七至八章、十一章、十二至十三章之釋義，據欽定本旁經；非逐字引錄。）

title.en: Judith Rebukes the Elders of Bethulia
title.zh: 猶滴斥責比突里亞長老

region.en: Bethulia, Judean hill town
region.zh: 比突里亞，猶大山地小城

period: Composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE; principal text: Vulgate/Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: Judith 7-8 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: Holofernes has cut off the city's water; the thirsty people beg Ozias to surrender in five days. Judith — a widow who has lived years in sackcloth and fasting — rebukes him: 'Who are ye, that have tempted God this day?... ye cannot find the depth of the heart of man, neither can ye perceive the things that God will do.' Her five days becomes her own plan: 'what thing soever it be that shall please you, I will do it before the day', and she prays with sackcloth and ashes for strength.
summary.zh: 何樂弗尼截斷城的水源；乾渴的百姓求烏西雅五日內投降。寡婦猶滴——多年披麻禁食——斥責他：「你們今日竟試探神麼？……你們不能參透人心，也不知道神將行何事。」她的五日改為自己的計劃：「你們所喜悅的，我在那日之先必為你們成就」，遂披麻蒙灰祈求力量。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: And she said to Ozias: 'Who art thou, that hast tempted God this day, and hast stood instead of God among the children of men? And now ye try the Lord God of all fathers... And ye cannot find the bottom of the heart of man, neither can ye perceive the things that he hath prepared. ... For they that are most favored by him shall stand instead of him in doing these things.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Judith 8:12-16 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 她對敖齊雅說：「你是誰，竟在今天試探天主，又在世人中間代替天主的位置？如今你們是在試探萬父之主天主……你們既不能測透人心的深處，也不能明白他所預備的事。……因為最蒙他恩寵的人，將代替他成就這些事。」

title.en: Judith in the Tent of Holofernes
title.zh: 猶滴在何樂弗尼的帳中

region.en: Assyrian camp below Bethulia
region.zh: 比突里亞山下亞述營地

period: Composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE; principal text: Vulgate/Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: Judith 10-13 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: Judith takes off her widow's sackcloth, bathes, puts on 'her garment of gladness', and walks out with her maid to the enemy camp, praying: 'O God of my father Simeon... make haste and come to mine help'. Holofernes gives her three days' leave to pray; she eats her own provisions. On the fourth night, alone with the drunken general, she prays 'give me strength this day, O Lord God of Israel', takes the sword at his bed's head and strikes his neck twice, rolls off the canopy, and gives the head to her maid.
summary.zh: 猶滴脫下寡婦麻衣，沐浴，穿上「喜樂的衣服」，攜婢走出至敵營，禱告：「我祖西緬的神啊……求你速速來幫助我」。何樂弗尼許她三日祈禱之假；她自帶食物。第四夜，與醉酒的元帥獨處，她求「耶和華以色列的神啊，今日賜我力量」，取帳柱頭上的刀，兩擊其頸，扯下錦帳，將首級交給婢女。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: And she came to the pillar of the bed, which was at Holofernes' head, and took down the faulchion from it; and approached to his bed, and took hold of the hair of his head; and said: 'Strengthen me, O Lord God of Israel, this day!' And she smote twice upon his neck with all her might, and she took away his head from him. And tumbled down the body from the bed, and pulled down the canopy from the pillars; and anon after she went forth, and gave Holofernes his head to her maid.
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Judith 13:6-10 (public domain).
passages.zh: 她走到床柱旁，那柱正在敖羅斐乃頭邊，就從其上取下他的刀；走近他的床，抓住他頭上的頭髮，說：「以色列的主天主啊，求你今日賜我力量！」她用盡全力在他頸上砍了兩下，就把他的頭從他身上取下來。又把屍身從床上滾落，從柱上扯下帳幕；隨後她立刻出去，把敖羅斐乃的頭交給她的婢女。

title.en: Judith's Song: The Victory of the Lowly
title.zh: 猶滴之歌：卑微者的得勝

region.en: Bethulia and Jerusalem
region.zh: 比突里亞與耶路撒冷

period: Composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE; principal text: Vulgate/Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: Judith 14-16 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: The head hung on the wall; at dawn the Assyrians flee 'in a valley so strait that they could hardly get out'. Judith's victory-song retells Simeon's sword at Shechem and Jael's tent-pin: 'The Lord hath taken counsel by a woman against our enemies... her beauty deceived him'. The people worship in Jerusalem; she lives to a hundred and five, 'and none did molest her'.
summary.zh: 首級懸於城牆；黎明亞述人在「難以脫出的狹谷」潰逃。猶滴的得勝之歌追述西緬在示劍的刀與雅億的帳橛：「耶和華藉一個女人設謀攻擊我們的仇敵……她的美色迷惑了他」。百姓在耶路撒冷敬拜；她活到一百零五歲，「沒有人擾害她」。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: Judith said: 'Begin unto my God with timbrels, sing unto my Lord with cymbals, tune unto him a new psalm: exalt him, and call upon his name. For God breaketh the battles: for among the camps in the midst of the people he hath made me conqueror. For the mighty one of Assyria... came from the mountains of the north... and behold, he is broken by a woman's hand.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Judith 16:1-4 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 友弟德說：「你們當擊鼓向我天主謳歌，敲鐃鈸向我主頌揚，為他譜一首新詩：尊崇他，呼求他的名。因為天主止息爭戰：他在營壘之中、百姓之間使我得勝。因為那亞述的強者……從北方的山嶺而來……看哪，他已被一個婦人的手擊碎。」

title.en: Mattathias at Modin: The Revolt Begins
title.zh: 瑪他提亞在摩丁：起義開始

region.en: Modin, Judean hill town
region.zh: 摩丁，猶大山地

period: Narrative set 167 BCE; composed c. late 2nd-early 1st c. BCE; principal text: Codex Vaticanus Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: 1 Maccabees 2 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: The king's officers demand sacrifice to the idols at Modin. Mattathias, priest of the sons of Joarib, answers before the whole city: 'Though all the nations that are under the king's dominion obey him... yet will I and my sons walk in the covenant of our fathers.' A willing apostate steps to the altar; Mattathias kills him and the king's officer in a fury, then pulls down the altar — and flees to the mountains with his sons, rallying 'every one that is zealous of the law'.
summary.zh: 王的官吏命摩丁眾人向偶像獻祭。約亞里家的祭司瑪他提亞當眾回答：「王的轄下各國雖都聽從他……但我與我兒必照我們列祖的約而行。」一個甘願變節者上前祭壇；瑪他提亞憤而誅之，連同王的官吏一併殺死，拆毀祭壇——攜眾子逃入山地，召集「凡熱心律法者」。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha. Foundational narrative of Hanukkah.

passages.text: Then Mattathias answered and spake with a loud voice: 'Though all the nations that are under the king's dominion obey him, every one having left the religion of his fathers, and given consent to his commandments; yet will I and my sons and my brethren walk in the covenant of our fathers. God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances. We will not hearken to the king's words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand, or the left.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, 1 Maccabees 2:19-22 (public domain).
passages.zh: 瑪他提亞回答，高聲說：「縱然凡在王權之下的萬民都聽從他，各人離棄自己祖宗的宗教，同意他的命令；然而我和我的兒子們、我的弟兄們，仍要遵行我們祖宗的盟約。天主決不容我們離棄律法和典章。我們決不聽從王的話，無論偏右或偏左，去離開我們的宗教。」

title.en: Judas Maccabeus: 'For the Battle Is Not to the Multitude'
title.zh: 猶大馬加比：「爭戰的勝敗不全靠人多」

region.en: Emmaus and Beth-horon passes, Judea
region.zh: 以馬忤斯與伯和崙山道，猶大

period: Narrative set 166-160 BCE; composed c. late 2nd-early 1st c. BCE; principal text: Codex Vaticanus Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: 1 Maccabees 3-4; 7 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: Judas 'surnamed Maccabeus', 'like as a giant', gathers the faithful; his war-speech enters scripture: 'For the battle is not to the multitude, but success is from heaven... we shall fight for our lives and our laws'. Victory at Beth-horon, Emmaus, and over Nicanor — whose head and hand are displayed at Jerusalem; 'the nations should know that there is one that fighteth for Israel'.
summary.zh: 號稱「馬加比」的猶大「如同巨獅」，召集忠民；其戰前宣言成為經文：「爭戰的勝敗不全靠人多，天上來的能力使人得勝……我們要為性命與律法爭戰」。伯和崙、以馬忤斯、尼迦拿之戰連連得勝——其首與手示於耶路撒冷；「萬國當知道，有一位為以色列爭戰者」。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: Then answered Judas and said: 'It is no great matter for many that are forbidden to fight to be overcome of a few; for there is no difference in the saving of many or of a few by heaven: for the victory of battle standeth not by the multitude of an host; but strength is from heaven.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, 1 Maccabees 3:17-19 (public domain).
passages.zh: 猶大回答說：「許多人被少數人所勝，這並非什麼大事；因為蒙上天拯救，多與少並無分別：因為爭戰的勝利不在乎軍隊的眾多，力量乃出於上天。」

title.en: The Abomination upon the Altar: Antiochus's Persecution
title.zh: 祭壇上的可憎之物：安提阿古之迫害

region.en: Jerusalem, Temple Mount
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，聖殿山

period: Narrative set 167 BCE; composed c. late 2nd-early 1st c. BCE; principal text: Codex Vaticanus Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: 1 Maccabees 1 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: Antiochus Epiphanes plunders the Temple and issues the decree 'that all should be one people': circumcision forbidden, sabbaths profaned, books of the law burned with those found keeping them put to death. 'The abomination of desolation' is built upon the altar of burnt-offering; women who circumcise their children are cast from the rocks with their babes. 'And there was exceeding great wrath upon Israel.'
summary.zh: 安提阿古四世洗劫聖殿，頒令「使萬民成為一體」：禁割禮、污穢安息日、燒毀律法書，藏書者與守誡者處死。「那行毀壞可憎的」被立於燔祭壇上；為嬰孩行割禮的婦人連嬰孩一同被推下山岩。「以色列中大發烈怒。」

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: And king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people, and every one should leave his laws. ... And they sacrificed to idols the sacrifices forbidden upon the altars. ... And whosoever was found with any the book of the testament, or if any committed himself to it, if he would it according to the law, the king's commandment was, that they should put him to death.
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, 1 Maccabees 1:41, 54, 57 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 安提阿古王寫信給他的全國，要眾人都成為一個民族，各人都捨棄自己的律法。……他們在祭壇上獻那被禁止的祭物給偶像。……凡被查出藏有約書的，或有人歸附這書的，若他願意照律法而行，王的命令就是要將他處死。

title.en: The Mother and Her Seven Sons
title.zh: 母親與她的七個兒子

region.en: Jerusalem, under the persecution
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，迫害之下

period: Composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE; principal text: Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: 2 Maccabees 7 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: Seven brothers, racked with wheels and scourges, refuse the king's swine's flesh one by one, each answering with resurrection-faith: 'The King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws'. The youngest promises the king: 'We suffer because of our sins... thou shalt find of our nation no more strength'; he is king of the children by outstretched hands. The mother watches all seven die — 'the mother was marvellous above all' — and dies last.
summary.zh: 七兄弟被輪盤拷打，逐一拒食王賜的豬肉，各以復活之信回答：「為他的律法而死的，世界之主要使我們復活」。最小的對王說：「我們受苦是因我們的罪……我民的勇力必不復存」；他向王伸出手臂。母親看著七子逐一死去——「那母親是超乎一切所當讚美的」——最後殉難。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha. Foundational martyrdom narrative read in Jewish as well as Christian tradition (cf. Lamentations Rabbah's Esther-echo).

passages.text: And when he was at the last breath, he said: 'Thou like a fury executors this cruelty without us; but, o thou king, I will not die, for the Lord God raiseth up again his faithful servants unto life again.' ... And after him was the sixth son brought forth, who, when he was a-hanging... said boldly: 'For our own sins, and the sins of our fathers, we receive these things.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, 2 Maccabees 7:9; 7:16 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.
passages.zh: 當他到了最後一息時，他說：「你這狂怒之徒，在我們身上施行這殘酷的事；然而，哦王啊，我必不死，因為主神必使他的忠僕再復活，得著生命。」……在他之後，第六個兒子被帶出來，當他被懸掛……時，他放膽說：「因我們自己的罪，和我們祖先的罪，我們遭受這些事。」

passages.text: The mother encouraged each son 'with the language of their fathers' reason': 'I was a pure maid, and went not astray, nor nourished up... seven sons born of one mother, all seven died the same day'. Her last speech: 'The Creator of the world... will again have mercy upon them, as he did in the beginning; therefore, now, o thou wretched man, when thou hast already judged thyself worthy of so many plagues, let me alone and my seven sons.' Paraphrase of 2 Maccabees 7:23-41 (KJV Apocrypha); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of 2 Maccabees 7:23-41 (KJV Apocrypha); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那母親用「他們祖先的言語」所表達的道理鼓勵每一個兒子：「我本是純潔的少女，未曾走迷，也未曾……同一個母親所生的七個兒子，七個都在同一天死了。」她最後的話說：「世界的創造主……必再憐憫他們，如同起初一樣；所以，如今，你這可憐的人哪，你既已判定自己該受這麼多的災禍，就任憑我和我的七個兒子吧。」此為《瑪加伯下》7:23-41（欽定本旁經）的意譯；並非逐字照錄。

title.en: Heliodorus Cast Down in the Temple
title.zh: 希利多羅被推倒於聖殿

region.en: Temple treasury, Jerusalem
region.zh: 聖殿庫房，耶路撒冷

period: Composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE; principal text: Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: 2 Maccabees 3 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: Seleucus's minister Heliodorus comes to seize the treasury of widows and orphans kept in the Temple 'for the saying of Heliodorus... that whosoever saw would be filled with wonder at the power of God'. The high priest Onias prays: 'Behold... our sanctuary... is coming to destruction'; while Heliodorus is entering, there appears 'a horse with a terrible rider upon him... having garments of gold' who strikes him — and two young men of 'exceeding beauty', scourging him continuously, cast him down senseless. He is restored only through Onias's sacrifice and testifies: 'there is a certain power of God.'
summary.zh: 西流基的宰相希利多羅奉命奪取聖殿中寡婦孤兒的存款，因「他看見的必因神的大能滿心驚訝」之語。大祭司阿尼亞禱告：「看哪……我們的聖所……將被毀壞」；他進入之際，有「一匹可怕的馬，上面有騎者，披著金甲」擊打他——並有「極其俊美的二位少年」不斷鞭打他，使之昏迷倒地。惟藉阿尼亞的祭得以痊癒，且見證：「確有神的權能。」

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: But when they were now at the treasury of the temple, and he that kept the door was come in, there was suddenly... a great horse with a terrible rider upon him, in rich array, and he rushed fiercely, striking Heliodorus with his fore-feet. And he that sat upon him seemed to have armour of gold, and his raiment was like to that of a man running swiftly for a prize.
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, 2 Maccabees 3:25-26 (public domain).
passages.zh: 但當他們現在到了聖殿的庫房，守門的人已經進來，忽然有……一匹駿馬，上面騎著一位可怕的騎士，衣著華麗，他猛烈衝來，用前蹄踢擊赫利奧多羅斯。那騎在馬上的，似乎穿著金甲，他的衣裳好像那奔跑爭獎之人的衣裳。

title.en: Nicanor Falls: The Day Before the Day of Mordecai
title.zh: 尼迦拿傾覆：末底改日的前一日

region.en: Plain of Beth-horon, Judea
region.zh: 伯和崙平原，猶大

period: Narrative set 161 BCE; composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE; principal text: Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: 2 Maccabees 15 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: Before the battle with Nicanor, Judas encourages his men with a dream: the dead high priest Onias and the prophet Jeremiah appear — 'Jeremiah stretched forth his right hand and gave unto Judas a golden sword, saying: Take this holy sword, a gift from God'. Nicanor falls; his head and right hand are cut off and displayed at Jerusalem; the day before Purim is kept as Nicanor's Day.
summary.zh: 與尼迦拿交戰之前，猶大以異夢激勵軍士：亡故的大祭司阿尼亞與先知耶利米顯現——「耶利米伸出右手，賜給猶大一柄金劍，說：拿這聖劍，這是神的恩賜」。尼迦拿倒下；其首與右手被割，示於耶路撒冷；普珥日之前一日定為尼迦拿日。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: Then Onias the high priest lifting up his hands, prayed for the whole body of the Jews, saying in this manner: 'O Lord God... this holy city, and the temple of thine heritage... and Jeremiah the prophet, who is the writer of the resurrection to them that believe, gave his right hand and gave Judas a sword of gold, and said unto him: Take this holy sword, a gift from God, wherewith thou shalt wound the adversaries.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, 2 Maccabees 15:12-16 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 於是，大祭司俄尼亞舉起雙手，為全體猶太人禱告，這樣說：「主神啊……這聖城，和你產業的聖殿……先知耶利米，就是為信的人記載復活之事的那位，伸出右手，把一把金劍交給猶大，對他說：『拿這聖劍，這是神所賜的禮物，你要用它刺傷仇敵。』」

title.en: Let Us Now Praise Famous Men: Ben Sira 44
title.zh: 我們當讚美顯揚之人：便西拉四十四章

region.en: Jerusalem, scribal school (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，文士學堂（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 190-175 BCE (Hebrew original, translated into Greek c. 132 BCE by grandson); principal text: Cairo Genizah Hebrew MS

source.work: Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 44 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: Ben Sira's hymn to the ancestors: 'Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us... such as have left a name behind them'. Abraham 'the great father of a multitude of nations', Moses 'beloved of God and men', and on through the judges and prophets — the memory of the tradition kept alive by the scribe's own office: 'the assembly shall show forth their wisdom'.
summary.zh: 便西拉對先祖的頌歌：「我們當讚美顯揚之人，及生育我們的列祖……這些人留下名聲」。亞伯拉罕「萬國的大父」，摩西「神與世人所愛」，繼而士師與先知——由文士的職分保存記憶：「會眾必述他們的智慧。」

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical wisdom book; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha. Hebrew text recovered from the Cairo Genizah (1896).

passages.text: Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us. The Lord hath wrought great glory by them through his great power from the beginning. Such as did bear rule in their kingdoms, men renowned for their power, giving counsel by their understanding... These were merciful men, whose righteousness hath not been forgotten. With their seed shall continually remain a good inheritance, and their children are within the covenant.
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Ecclesiasticus 44:1-12 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 如今讓我們讚美那些著名的人物，以及生養我們的祖先。上主藉著祂的大能，從起初就在他們身上成就了極大的榮耀。他們中有在國中掌權的，有因權勢而聞名的，有憑聰明獻策的……這些都是仁慈的人，他們的義沒有被遺忘。他們的後裔必永遠存留美好的產業，他們的子孫也在聖約之中。

title.en: Wisdom Praise Her Own Work: Ben Sira 24
title.zh: 智慧頌己工：便西拉二十四章

region.en: Jerusalem, temple precincts (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，聖殿院宇（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 190-175 BCE; principal text: Cairo Genizah Hebrew MS; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 24 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: Ben Sira's Wisdom-hymn, Jewish counterpart to Proverbs 8 and forerunner of John's Logos: 'I came out of the mouth of the Most High... Before the mountains... I was brought forth'. Wisdom seeks a resting place through the whole earth and is commanded: 'Make thy dwelling in Jacob' — she flourishes as the law 'which Moses commanded us', a river of understanding pouring forth teaching like prophecy.
summary.zh: 便西拉的智慧頌，箴言八章的猶太呼應，約翰邏各斯之源：「我出於至高者之口……在山嶺之先，我被生出」。智慧遍尋安身之地，得命：「在雅各中住下」——作為「摩西所吩咐我們的律法」而榮耀，如理解之河，教導湧流如預言。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical wisdom book; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: I came out of the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth as a cloud. I dwelt in high places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar. I alone compassed the circuit of heaven, and walked in the bottom of the deep. ... In every nation and people I was. With all these I sought rest; and in whose inheritance shall I abide? So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said: 'Lodge in Jacob, and in Israel take thine inheritance.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Ecclesiasticus 24:3-8 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 我從至高者的口中而出，如雲彩覆蓋大地。我住在高處，我的寶座在雲柱之中。唯有我環繞諸天，行走於深淵的底處。……我在萬國萬民之中。我在這一切之中尋求安息；我當住在誰的產業中呢？於是萬物的創造者賜我命令，造我的那位使我的帳幕安歇，說：『住在雅各中，在以色列中承受你的產業。』

title.en: Prayer for the Exiles: Baruch's Confession
title.zh: 為被擄者的祈禱：巴錄的認罪

region.en: Babylon, exile community
region.zh: 巴比倫，被擄社群

period: Composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE (attributed to Jeremiah's scribe); principal text: Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: Baruch 1-3 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: Baruch, 'the son of Nerias', reads the words of the book in Babylon, gathering silver for offerings to Jerusalem's sanctuary; the confession follows: 'Unto the Lord our God belongeth righteousness, but unto us confusion of faces'. The famous invitation: 'Learn where is wisdom, where is strength, where is understanding... who hath gone up into heaven, and taken her?... but he that knoweth all things knoweth her; he found her by his own count.'
summary.zh: 尼利亞的兒子巴錄在巴比倫宣讀書中言語，收集銀子為聖殿獻祭；認罪隨後：「公義屬耶和華我們的神，至於我們，當羞愧滿面」。著名的邀請：「智慧在哪裡？能力在哪裡？聰明在哪裡……誰曾上天取下她？……惟知道一切事的神認識她；他以自己的計謀尋見她。」

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: And now, Lord Almighty, God of Israel, the grieving soul in great trouble crieth: 'Hear, O Lord, and have mercy; for we are sinners before thee. Thou art set forth for ever, and we perish for ever.' O Lord Almighty, thou God of Israel, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites, and of their children, which have sinned before thee, and not hearkened unto the voice of thee their God.
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Baruch 3:2-5 (public domain).
passages.zh: 如今，全能的主，以色列的神啊，那在極大困苦中憂傷的靈魂呼求說：『主啊，求你垂聽，施以憐憫；因為我們在你面前是罪人。你永遠長存，我們卻永遠滅亡。』全能的主，以色列的神啊，求你如今垂聽那些已死的以色列人，以及他們子孫的祈禱，他們曾在你面前犯罪，沒有聽從你——他們的神——的聲音。

title.en: Daniel Serves Bel and Slays the Dragon
title.zh: 但以理事奉彼勒並殺龍

region.en: Babylon, temple of Bel
region.zh: 巴比倫，彼勒神廟

period: Composed c. 3rd-2nd c. BCE (Greek addition to Daniel); principal text: LXX/Theodotion; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: Bel and the Dragon (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: The king asks Daniel why he worships not Bel; Daniel answers: 'because I do not worship idols made with hands, but the living God'. A night-watch exposes the seventy priests consuming the offerings secretly; the ashes test proves the fraud, and the priests are cast in. Then the dragon — 'a great dragon, and the Babylonians worshipped him' — is killed by Daniel's recipe of pitch, fat, and hair: 'and they that drank of it died', and the dragon bursts.
summary.zh: 王問但以理為何不拜彼勒；他答：「我不拜手所造的偶像，但拜永活的神」。夜間守候揭露七十祭司暗食祭物；灰燼之試證其詐，祭司被投入。繼而那龍——「巴比倫人所拜的大龍」——被但以理的配方（瀝青、脂、髮）所殺：「喫的都死了」，龍即爆裂。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical (Greek additions to Daniel); quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: Then Daniel took pitch, and fat, and hair, and did seethe them together, and made lumps thereof: this he gave in manner unto the dragon to eat; and the dragon did eat it, and burst in sunder. And he said: 'Lo, these are the gods ye worship, and they that eat of them shall die.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Bel and the Dragon, v. 27 (public domain).
passages.zh: 於是但以理取了瀝青、脂油和毛髮，一同煮熬，做成塊狀；他把這些照樣給那龍吃；龍吃了，就脹裂而亡。他說：『看哪，這就是你們所敬拜的神，凡吃這些的必死。』

title.en: Susanna and the Two Elders
title.zh: 蘇撒拿與二長老

region.en: Garden of Joacim, Babylon
region.zh: 約雅金的花園，巴比倫

period: Composed c. 3rd-2nd c. BCE (Greek addition to Daniel); principal text: LXX/Theodotion; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: Susanna (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: The beautiful wife of Joacim is ambushed by two judges in her husband's garden; refusing them, she is falsely accused of adultery and condemned by her own beauty as evidence. Young Daniel, moved by the Spirit, cross-examines the elders apart from each other — 'under what tree sawest thou them together?' — mallow and evergreen oak; the answers differ, and the judges are executed by the law they misused. 'And there arose such a cry and shout... for Susanna'; 'from that day forth was Daniel had in reputation.'
summary.zh: 約雅金的美好妻子在園中被二審判官伏擊；拒絕後被誣告通姦，其美貌竟成罪證。少年但以理受靈感動，隔開二長老分別訊問——「你們在什麼樹下見他們行淫？」——乳香樹與長青橡樹；答案相異，濫用律法的審判官反被所立之法處死。「全會眾呼喊大聲……為蘇撒拿」；「從那日起，但以理在眾民眼前大得尊榮。」

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical (Greek additions to Daniel); quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha. Read in the Easter Vigil of the Western tradition; noted for its legal drama.

passages.text: Then Daniel stood up in the midst of them, and said: 'Are ye so foolish, O ye sons of Israel, that without examination or knowledge of the truth ye have condemned a daughter of Israel?' ... So he put them asunder one from another, and called one of them, and said unto him: 'O thou that art grown old in evil days, now are thy sins come to purpose, which thou hast committed beforetime... Under what tree sawest thou them companying together?'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Susanna, vv. 48-53 (public domain), condensed.
passages.zh: 於是但以理站在他們中間，說：『以色列的子孫啊，你們竟如此愚昧，未經審查、不識真理，就定了以色列女子的罪嗎？』……於是他把他們彼此分開，叫其中一人來，對他說：『你這在邪惡日子中長老的人啊，如今你素來所犯的罪已到了結局……你見他們二人相聚，是在什麼樹下？』

title.en: The Three Bodyguards and Zerubbabel's Answer
title.zh: 三侍衛與所羅巴伯之答

region.en: Persian court (symbolic pin at Susa)
region.zh: 波斯王庭（以書珊象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE (Greek expansion of Ezra material); principal text: LXX; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: 1 Esdras 3-4 (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: Darius's three bodyguards compete: what is strongest — wine, the king, or women? Zerubbabel's answer wins the prize and the king's promise: 'Truth is the greatest of all... it endureth and shall continue for ever, and liveth and conquereth for evermore'. His reward — the rebuilding of Jerusalem and the return of the sacred vessels — he asks for his father's city.
summary.zh: 大流士的三侍衛比試：何者最強——酒、王、或女人？所羅巴伯之答得賞與王許：「真理最大……它堅立，必永存，並永遠得勝而活」。所求的賞賜——重建耶路撒冷與聖器歸還——他為祖城求之。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: Then answered Zorobabel: 'O king, wine is not the strongest, nor the king; nor are women, though they bear the mastery of men; nor yet are these things that ye have said; but truth passeth all these things, and shall overcome them. For, O king, all things obey truth; and the earth obeyeth truth... Truth endureth, and is always strong; it liveth and conquereth for evermore, without respecting of persons in judging.',
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, 1 Esdras 4:34-38 (public domain).
passages.zh: 於是所羅巴伯回答說：『王啊，酒不是最強的，王也不是；婦女也不是，雖然她們轄管男人；你們所說的這些也不是；惟有真理超過這一切，並且必勝過它們。因為，王啊，萬物都順從真理；大地也順從真理……真理長存，永遠堅強；它活著，永遠得勝，在審判時不偏待人。』

title.en: The Opening of Mecca: Bilal on the Kaaba
title.zh: 麥加之開：比拉勒立於天房

region.en: Mecca, Kaaba courtyard (literal pin)
region.zh: 麥加天房庭院（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: The treaty of Hudaybiyya is broken; the Prophet marches on Mecca with ten thousand and enters without battle. He circles the Kaaba, smashes the idols with the word of God — 'Truth hath come, and falsehood hath passed away' — and proclaims a general amnesty: 'Go, for ye are free.' Bilal ascends the Kaaba roof and gives the adhan over the city of his former bondage.
summary.zh: 侯代比亞之約被毀；先知率萬人進軍麥加，不戰而入。他繞行天房，以真主之言擊碎偶像——『真理已至，虛妄已逝』——並宣佈大赦：『去吧，你們自由了。』比拉勒登上天房之頂，在其昔日為奴之城喚禮。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: The Quraysh broke the treaty of Hudaybiyya by helping a tribe to attack an ally of the Prophet. He marched from Medina in Ramadan of the eighth year with ten thousand men, and entered Mecca almost without battle. He made his tawaf around the Kaaba and pointed with his staff at the idols around it — three hundred and sixty — and each fell as he recited: 'Truth hath come, and falsehood hath passed away; falsehood is ever doomed to vanish.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 古萊什人違背了侯代比亞條約，協助一個部落攻擊先知的盟友。他在第八年的齋月率一萬人從麥地那出發，幾乎未經戰鬥便進入麥加。他繞行克爾白完成環遊禮，並以手杖指向環繞四周的偶像——共三百六十尊——當他誦念：「真理已來臨，虛妄已消逝；虛妄終將消亡。」每一尊偶像便應聲倒下。

passages.text: He gathered the Meccans at Safa and said: 'O Quraysh, what do you expect me to do to you?' They said, 'Good — a noble brother, son of a noble brother.' He said: 'Go, for ye are free.' And they entered the faith in crowds. He ordered Bilal to ascend the roof of the Kaaba and give the call to prayer, and the adhan of the freed slave of Abyssinia sounded over the city of his former masters.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他將麥加人聚集在薩法丘上，說道：「古萊什人啊，你們料想我會如何處置你們？」他們說：「善待——你是高貴的兄弟，高貴兄弟之子。」他說：「去吧，你們已獲自由。」於是他們成群結隊地皈依了信仰。他命比拉勒登上克爾白的屋頂宣禮，於是這位阿比西尼亞獲釋奴隸的宣禮聲，響徹他昔日主人們的城邑。

title.en: Hunayn and the Distribution of Spoils
title.zh: 侯奈因與戰利品分配

region.en: Valley of Hunayn, near Taif (literal pin)
region.zh: 塔伊夫附近侯奈因谷（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: The tribes of Hawazin ambush the Muslims in the narrow valley of Hunayn; the army wavers, and the Prophet mounts a white mule, crying: 'I am the Prophet, no liar; I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib!' Abbas shouts the call, and the Muslims turn. The captives and herds of Hawazin are taken; when the tribes come pleading for their women and children, the Prophet gives back his own fifth and calls on the men of Muhajirun to do the same. To the new converts of the Delegation he gives camels by the hundred, and the old guard murmurs.
summary.zh: 哈瓦津部族於侯奈因狹谷伏擊；穆斯林陣亂，先知乘白騾，呼喊：『我是先知，非謊者；我是阿布杜·穆塔利卜之子！』阿巴斯高聲召喚，穆斯林轉身。哈瓦津之俘與牛群盡取；部族前來求還婦孺；先知讓出其五分之一，並號召眾人同讓。對代歸信者賞以百駝；老兵低語。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: The tribes of Hawazin and Thaqif gathered to attack the Muslims on their way from the conquest of Mecca, and lay in ambush in the valley of Hunayn. In the dawn the Muslims were struck from the heights; the army wavered and fell back. The Prophet mounted a white mule and rode into the press of the enemy, crying: 'I am the Prophet, no liar; I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib!' Abbas called out: 'O Companions of the acacia!' — and the Muslims turned and fought.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 海瓦津與薩基夫諸部落聚集起來，欲在穆斯林從征服麥加歸途中襲擊他們，並埋伏於侯奈因山谷。黎明時分，穆斯林從高處遭到突襲；軍隊動搖，節節後退。先知騎上一頭白色騾子，衝入敵陣之中，高呼：「我是先知，絕非謊言之人；我是阿卜杜勒·穆塔里布之子！」阿巴斯高喊：「金合歡樹下的同伴們啊！」——穆斯林於是轉身奮戰。

passages.text: The captives of Hawazin were gathered, twenty-four thousand camels and six thousand women and children. The chiefs of Hawazin came pleading, saying, 'We are a people of kinship and of stock.' The Prophet said: 'Which is better, your women and children or your wealth?' They said, 'Our women and children.' He gave back his own fifth and called on the Muslims to do the same; and they gave up their portions. And to the new converts of the Delegation he gave each a hundred camels; and the men of the Muhajirun murmured, saying, 'We were in hunger and need.' He said: 'I have given to them to draw their hearts near; and you, return with the Prophet of God.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 海瓦津的俘虜被集中起來，計有兩萬四千峰駱駝與六千名婦孺。海瓦津的酋長們前來懇求，說道：「我們是血親相連、同宗同源之民。」先知說：「你們的婦孺與你們的財富，何者更為可貴？」他們說：「我們的婦孺。」他歸還了自己應得的五分之一，並號召穆斯林同樣歸還；他們便放棄了各自所得的份額。他又給新皈依的使團成員每人一百峰駱駝；遷士們便低聲抱怨，說道：「我們曾身處飢餓與困乏之中。」他說：「我給他們，是為了撫慰他們的心；而你們，當與真主的先知一同歸返。」

title.en: Tabuk: The Three Who Stayed Behind
title.zh: 塔布克：缺席的三人

region.en: Tabuk oasis, north Arabian marches (literal pin)
region.zh: 北阿拉伯塔布克綠洲（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: The Prophet marches to the Byzantine frontier in the heat of summer; three Muslims stay behind without excuse — Murara, Ka'b ibn Malik and Hilal. The army finds no enemy and returns. Ka'b buys two rides for himself and fails to set out; then he is shunned by the whole town for fifty days until the earth — even his own — is estranged from him. God accepts the repentance of the three, and the earth grows kindly again around Ka'b.
summary.zh: 先知冒暑進軍拜占庭邊境；三名穆斯林無故缺席——穆拉拉、卡布·本·馬利克與希拉勒。軍中不見敵而返。卡布購二乘卻未出發；此後全城與之絕交五十日，直至大地——連他腳下的大地——也與他疏遠。主接受三人懺悔；大地又對卡布和善。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: The Prophet marched to Tabuk, on the borders of the Byzantine lands, in the heat of the summer, and all who were able rode out. Three stayed behind without excuse: Murara ibn al-Rabi, Ka'b ibn Malik and Hilal ibn Umayya. The army met no enemy; the Byzantines had withdrawn. The Prophet returned to Medina in the month of Ramadan.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 先知在盛夏酷暑中進軍塔布克，該地位於拜占庭領地的邊界，凡有能力者皆隨軍出征。有三人未經任何藉口而留守：穆拉拉·伊本·拉比、凱厄卜·伊本·馬利克與希拉勒·伊本·烏麥耶。軍隊未遇任何敵人；拜占庭人已然撤退。先知於齋月返回麥地那。

passages.text: Ka'b told his own story: 'I had two rides ready, and yet I did not set out; and when the Prophet returned I came to him and spoke; and he was silent. Then he proclaimed that no one should speak to the three of us; and the town turned its face from us, and the earth itself, though vast, grew narrow for us. After fifty days God sent down our repentance: He has turned to the three of them. And the earth grew kindly again around me, and my friend wept.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 凱厄卜講述了自己的經歷：「我已備好兩匹坐騎，卻終究沒有出發；當先知歸來時，我前去向他陳述；他卻默然不語。隨後他宣告眾人不得與我們三人交談；於是全城都對我們轉過臉去，而大地雖廣闊，對我們卻變得狹窄。五十天之後，真主降下了我們悔罪的啟示：祂已寬恕了他們三人。於是我周圍的大地又變得親切起來，我的朋友也哭了。」

title.en: Muadh Sent to Yemen: A Guide for a Guide
title.zh: 穆阿茲赴也門：引路者之引

region.en: Yemen, Sanaa (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 也門薩那（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: The Prophet sends Muadh ibn Jabal to Yemen as teacher and governor. 'How will you judge when a matter comes to you?' — 'By the Book of God.' 'And if it is not found there?' — 'By the sunnah of the Messenger of God.' 'And if it is not found there?' — 'Then I shall judge by my own opinion, and not be remiss.' The Prophet strikes his hand upon Muadh's breast: 'Praise be to God who has made the messenger of the Messenger of God succeed.'
summary.zh: 先知遣穆阿茲·本·賈巴勒赴也門為師與長。『遇事如何斷？』——『憑主之經典。』『經中無者呢？』——『憑使者之聖行。』『聖行中亦無者呢？』——『我以己意而斷，不致怠惰。』先知手按穆阿茲之胸：『讚美主，使主使者的使者成功。』

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: The Prophet sent Muadh ibn Jabal to Yemen as teacher and governor, and said to him: 'How will you judge when a matter comes to you?' He said, 'By the Book of God.' He said, 'And if you do not find it there?' He said, 'By the sunnah of the Messenger of God.' He said, 'And if you do not find it there?' He said, 'Then I shall judge by my own opinion, and not be remiss.' The Prophet struck his hand upon Muadh's breast and said: 'Praise be to God who has made the messenger of the Messenger of God succeed in what pleases the Messenger of God.' He gave him a last instruction: 'Make things easy and not difficult; give good tidings and do not repel; and call to the worship of God alone.' And Muadh rode out to the tribes of Yemen.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 先知派遣穆阿茲·伊本·賈巴勒前往葉門，擔任教師與總督，並對他說：「當一件事來到你面前時，你將如何判決？」他說：「依真主的經典。」先知說：「若你在其中找不到呢？」他說：「依真主使者的聖行。」先知說：「若你在其中也找不到呢？」他說：「那我就以自己的判斷來判決，絕不疏忽懈怠。」先知把手拍在穆阿茲的胸前，說道：「讚美真主，祂使真主使者的使者，在真主使者所喜悅的事上得以成功。」他給他最後的囑咐：「當使人容易，不要使人困難；當報喜訊，不要使人退避；當召人只崇拜真主。」於是穆阿茲騎行前往葉門的各部落。

title.en: The Farewell Pilgrimage: 'I Leave Among You Two Things'
title.zh: 辭朝：「我留下兩件事物」

region.en: Arafat plain, near Mecca (literal pin)
region.zh: 麥加附近阿拉法特平原（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: In the tenth year the Prophet performs the pilgrimage of farewell with a hundred thousand. From the back of his camel at Arafat he preaches: blood and property are sacred; usury is forbidden; women have rights over their husbands; 'I leave among you two things — the Book of God and my sunnah; hold fast to them and you will not go astray.' Then from the valley he proclaims: 'This day I have perfected for you your religion.' And the pilgrims cry: 'We have heard and obeyed.'
summary.zh: 第十年，先知與十萬人同行辭朝。於阿拉法特乘駝講道：血與財神聖；禁利；婦女於丈夫有權；『我留下兩件事物——主之經典與我的聖行；緊握之，必不迷失。』於谷中宣告：『今日我已為你們成全你們的宗教。』朝覲者呼：『我們聽從並順服。』

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; the Farewell Sermon is read as a constitutional text within the tradition; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: In the tenth year of the Hijra the Prophet performed the pilgrimage of farewell, and the tribes came out to him from every road: it was said they were a hundred thousand. He rode to Arafat, and from the back of his she-camel, al-Qaswa, he preached: 'O people, your blood and your property are sacred to one another... Every usury is abolished; and fear God concerning women, for you have taken them under the protection of God: they have a right against you and you have a right against them.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在希吉拉第十年，先知行了辭別朝覲，各部落從四面八方前來見他：據說有十萬人。他騎行至阿拉法特，從他的母駝「卡斯瓦」背上宣講：「眾人啊，你們的血與你們的財產，彼此都是神聖的……一切高利貸都已廢除；你們當敬畏真主，善待婦女，因為你們是憑真主的庇護而娶了她們：她們對你們有權利，你們對她們也有權利。」

passages.text: He said: 'O people, I leave among you two things: the Book of God, and my sunnah; if you hold fast to them you will not go astray. And know that every Muslim is the brother of every Muslim, and that the Muslims are one brotherhood.' Then from the valley he proclaimed: 'This day I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favour upon you, and have chosen for you Islam as your religion.' And the pilgrims cried out: 'We have heard, and we obey.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他說：「眾人啊，我在你們中間留下了兩樣東西：真主的經典與我的聖行；你們若緊守它們，就不會迷誤。你們當知道，每一個穆斯林都是每一個穆斯林的兄弟，穆斯林是一個兄弟整體。」隨後他從山谷中宣告：「今日我為你們成全了你們的宗教，我對你們完成了我的恩惠，我為你們選擇了伊斯蘭作為你們的宗教。」朝覲者們高聲喊道：「我們聽見了，我們服從。」

title.en: The Death of the Prophet
title.zh: 先知之死

region.en: Medina, Aisha's apartment (literal pin)
region.zh: 麥地那阿伊莎居室（實際定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: After the farewell pilgrimage the Prophet falls ill of fever; he is carried to Aisha's chamber. Abu Bakr is called to lead the prayer; the Prophet is laid to rest. 'There is no prophet after me.' He speaks of prayer and the servants, of the oath of Ghadir; and in the last words Aisha hears: 'Rather the Highest Companion, Paradise.' He is buried beneath her apartment; Umar weeps at his own days of ignorance, and Abu Bakr says to the crowd: 'Whoso worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad is dead; whoso worshipped God, God is living and does not die.'
summary.zh: 辭朝後，先知染熱病；移居阿伊莎居室。請阿布·伯克爾領禮；先知安臥。『我之後再無先知。』他囑禮拜與僕人之事，及蓋迪爾之誓；臨終阿伊莎聞其言：『寧取至高之伴侶，樂園。』葬於其居室之下；歐瑪爾為其蒙昧時代之回憶而泣；阿布·伯克爾對眾言：『拜穆罕默德者，穆罕默德已死；拜真主者，真主永活不死。』

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; the death of the Prophet is treated with the same paraphrase discipline as other episodes.

passages.text: After the pilgrimage of farewell the Prophet fell ill of a fever. He was carried to the chamber of Aisha. He called for water for ablution, and led the prayer while sitting; then Abu Bakr was bidden to lead the prayers in his place, and the Muslims understood. The Prophet said: 'There is no prophet after me; and whoever of my people, after me, claims prophethood is a liar.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 辭別朝覲之後，先知患熱病而病倒。他被抬到阿伊莎的房間。他叫人取水作小淨，並坐著領拜；隨後阿布·伯克爾奉命代替他領拜，穆斯林們便明白了。先知說：「我之後再無先知；我這教民中若有人在我之後自稱先知，便是說謊者。」

passages.text: His last words were heard by Aisha: 'God on high, the Highest Companion' — and she knew that he had chosen the higher of the two abodes. He was buried where he died, beneath her apartment. Umar refused to believe and drew his sword, till Abu Bakr came to the crowd and said: 'Whoso worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad is dead; whoso worshipped God, God is living and does not die.' And he recited the verse: 'Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿伊莎聽見了他最後的話：「至高真主，至高的伴侶」——她便知道，他選擇了兩處居所中較高的一處。他被葬於他逝世之處，即她的居室之下。歐麥爾不肯相信，拔出劍來，直到阿布·伯克爾來到人群前說道：「誰崇拜穆罕默德，穆罕默德已死；誰崇拜真主，真主是永生的，不會死去。」他誦讀經文：「穆罕默德只是一位使者；在他之前已有許多使者逝去了。」

title.en: Salman the Persian: Four Masters in Search of Truth
title.zh: 波斯人薩勒曼：尋求真理的四位導師

region.en: Isfahan to Medina, road of seekers (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伊斯法罕至麥地那的求道之路（象徵性定位）

period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: Salman al-Farisi, a Persian of Isfahan, turns from fire-worship to Christianity and travels church by church, seeking the truest servant of God. The last master tells him of a prophet about to appear in the land of the Arabs — his signs: he accepts gifts and not alms; the seal of prophethood between his shoulders; he does not eat of charity. Salman is sold into slavery and passes through Medina; the test is made — the Prophet accepts the gift of dates and declines the charity — and Salman falls at his feet and confesses Islam.
summary.zh: 伊斯法罕的波斯人薩勒曼，由拜火轉向基督教，逐一訪求最真誠的主僕。末位導師告訴他：阿拉伯之地將出先知——其兆：受饋贈而不受施捨；肩胛間有聖印；不吃施捨之物。薩勒曼被賣為奴，途經麥地那；試之——先知收椰棗禮而拒施捨——薩勒曼伏其足前而宣示歸信。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; the Salman conversion legend is beloved of Persian Sufism; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: Salman was a Persian of Isfahan, the son of the chief of his village, who served the fire. Passing a church of the Christians he entered, and found their prayer fair; and he said, 'This religion is better than ours.' He told his father, who put him in chains; he escaped, and went from church to church, and from master to master, seeking the best of them. The last of the masters told him: 'A prophet is about to arise in the land of the Arabs, who accepts gifts and not alms, and between whose shoulders is the seal of prophethood.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 薩爾曼是伊斯法罕的波斯人，是他村莊首領之子，曾侍奉聖火。他路過一座基督徒的教堂，便走了進去，覺得他們的祈禱很美好；他說：「這個宗教比我們的更好。」他告訴了父親，父親便給他戴上鎖鏈；他逃了出來，從一座教堂到另一座教堂，從一位主人到另一位主人，尋求他們中最好的。最後一位主人對他說：「一位先知即將在阿拉伯人的土地上興起，他接受贈禮而不接受施捨，他的兩肩之間有先知職分的印記。」

passages.text: Salman was treacherously sold to a Jew of Medina, and dug his ditch in the ditch of the Confederates. He saw the Prophet and tested him: he brought dates as charity and the Prophet did not eat; he brought them as a gift and the Prophet ate, and said to his Companions: 'Take and eat, but not from charity.' Salman fell at his feet and kissed them, and said: 'This is the master of whom my last master told me.' And the Prophet ordered his ransom and his freedom.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 薩爾曼遭人背信出賣，被賣給麥地那的一名猶太人，並在聯軍之役中為他挖掘壕溝。他見到了先知，並加以試探：他帶來棗子作為施捨，先知沒有吃；他帶來棗子作為餽贈，先知便吃了，並對他的同伴們說：「拿去吃吧，但不要吃施捨之物。」薩爾曼撲倒在他腳前親吻，說道：「這就是我上一位主人所告訴我的那位主人。」先知便下令為他贖身，使他得自由。

title.en: Cook Ting Cuts Up an Ox (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 庖丁解牛（莊子）

region.en: Prince Hui's court of Liang (Kaifeng, Henan, China)
region.zh: 梁惠王之廷（今河南開封）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 3, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 3

summary.en: A cook carves an ox to the rhythm of ancient dances. He has followed the Tao for nineteen years: he sees the animal only in its natural seams, inserts a blade without thickness into the interstices, and his chopper is still fresh from the whetstone after thousands of bullocks. From his words, the Prince says, he has learned how to nourish his life.
summary.zh: 庖丁為文惠君解牛，進乎技者道也；依乎天理，因其固然，以無厚入有間，十九年而刀刃若新發於硎。文惠君曰：得養生焉。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the charter story of wu-wei skill. Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: Prince Hui's cook was cutting up a bullock. Every blow of his hand, every heave of his shoulders, every tread of his foot, every thrust of his knee, every whshh of rent flesh, every chhk of the chopper, was in perfect harmony,--rhythmical like the dance of the Mulberry Grove, simultaneous like the chords of the Ching Shou. "Well done!" cried the Prince. "Yours is skill indeed." "Sire," replied the cook; "I have always devoted myself to TAO. It is better than skill. When I first began to cut up bullocks, I saw before me simply whole bullocks. After three years' practice, I saw no more whole animals. And now I work with my mind and not with my eye.
passages.zh: 惠王的廚子正在宰切一頭牛。他手的每一次拍擊、肩膀的每一次聳動、腳的每一次踩踏、膝的每一次頂撞、皮肉撕裂的每一聲唰、刀斧砍落的每一聲嚓，都完全和諧——有節奏，如同桑林之舞；合拍，如同經首之樂的旋律。「好啊！」惠王驚嘆道，「你的技藝真是高超。」「大王，」廚子回答，「我一向專心致力於道。道勝過技藝。我最初開始宰牛時，眼前所見只是一頭整牛。經過三年練習之後，我便不再看見整頭的牛了。如今我是用心神來運作，而不是用眼睛。

passages.text: "A good cook changes his chopper once a year,--because he cuts. An ordinary cook, once a month,--because he hacks. But I have had this chopper nineteen years, and although I have cut up many thousand bullocks, its edge is as if fresh from the whetstone. For at the joints there are always interstices, and the edge of a chopper being without thickness, it remains only to insert that which is without thickness into such an interstice. By these means the interstice will be enlarged, and the blade will find plenty of room.
passages.zh: 「好的廚子一年換一次刀——因為他是在切割。普通的廚子一個月換一次刀——因為他是在砍剁。但我這把刀已經用了十九年，雖然宰切過數千頭牛，它的刀刃卻仍像剛從磨刀石上磨出來一般。因為關節之處總有空隙，而刀刃本身沒有厚度，只需把那沒有厚度的刀刃插入這樣的空隙之中。如此一來，空隙便會被撐大，刀刃也就有充分的餘地了。

passages.text: "Nevertheless, when I come upon a hard part where the blade meets with a difficulty, I am all caution. I fix my eye on it. I stay my hand, and gently apply my blade, until with a hwah the part yields like earth crumbling to the ground. Then I take out my chopper, and stand up, and look around, and pause, until with an air of triumph I wipe my chopper and put it carefully away." "Bravo!" cried the Prince. "From the words of this cook I have learnt how to take care of my life."
passages.zh: 「然而，當我遇到刀刃受阻的堅硬部位時，我便格外謹慎。我凝神注視，停下手中的動作，輕輕地運刀，直到嘩的一聲，那部位便如泥土崩落於地般分解開來。然後我抽出刀，站起身來，環顧四周，從容佇立，最後帶著得意的神情把刀擦拭乾淨，小心地收好。」「妙極了！」惠王驚嘆道，「我從這位廚子的話中，學到了如何保養自己的生命。」

title.en: When Lao Tzŭ Died: Ch'in Shih's Three Yells (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 老聃死，秦失弔之（莊子）

region.en: The funeral of Lao Tzŭ (symbolic pin: Ku county, Bozhou, Anhui, China)
region.zh: 老子之喪（象徵定位：安徽亳州苦縣）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 3, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 3

summary.en: When Lao Tzŭ died, his friend Ch'in Shih mourned with three yells and left. The Master came because it was his time to be born and went because it was his time to die; the ancients spoke of death as God cutting down a man suspended in the air. The fuel is consumed, but the fire may be transmitted — and we know not that it comes to an end.
summary.zh: 老聃死，秦失弔之，三號而出：適來，夫子時也；適去，夫子順也。安時而處順，哀樂不能入也。古者謂是帝之縣解。指窮於為薪，火傳也，不知其盡也。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the 'fire transmitted' image is the classic Taoist death-and-continuity narrative, tagged origin-of-death and resurrection as comparative (non-origin-myth) analogues.

passages.text: When Lao Tzŭ died, Ch'in Shih went to mourn. He uttered three yells and departed. A disciple asked him saying, "Were you not our Master's friend?" "I was," replied Ch'in Shih. "And if so, do you consider that a sufficient expression of grief at his loss?" added the disciple. "I do," said Ch'in Shih. "I had believed him to be the man of all men, but now I know that he was not. When I went in to mourn, I found old persons weeping as if for their children, young ones wailing as if for their mothers. And for him to have gained the attachment of those people in this way, he too must have uttered words which should not have been spoken, and dropped tears which should not have been shed, thus violating eternal principles, increasing the sum of human emotion, and forgetting the source from which his own life was received.
passages.zh: 老子去世時，秦失前去弔唁。他號哭了三聲便離開了。有弟子問他說：「您不是我們老師的朋友嗎？」「我是。」秦失回答。弟子又問：「既然如此，您認為這樣足以表達對他的哀悼之情嗎？」「足夠了。」秦失說。「我原以為他是人中之人，如今才知道他並非如此。我進去弔唁時，看見老人哭得像為自己的孩子哭一般，年輕人哀號得像為自己的母親哭一般。他能如此得到那些人的愛戴，必定也曾說過不該說的話，流過不該流的淚，因而違背了永恆的法則，增添了人間情感的總量，忘卻了自己生命所從受的本源。

passages.text: "The ancients called such emotions the trammels of mortality. The Master came, because it was his time to be born; he went, because it was his time to die. For those who accept the phenomenon of birth and death in this sense, lamentation and sorrow have no place. The ancients spoke of death as of God cutting down a man suspended in the air. The fuel is consumed, but the fire may be transmitted, and we know not that it comes to an end."
passages.zh: 「古人稱這樣的情感為人生的枷鎖。老師來，是因為他該出生了；他去，是因為他該死亡了。對於以這種眼光看待生死現象的人，哀傷與悲愁便無所容身。古人談到死亡，就像談到上帝砍斷一個懸在空中的人。柴薪燒盡了，但火卻可以傳續下去，而我們並不知道它會終結。」

title.en: The Fasting of the Heart (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 心齋（莊子）

region.en: The court of Lu (Qufu, Shandong, China)
region.zh: 魯國曲阜

period: Zhuangzi ch. 4, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 4

summary.en: Yen Hui sets out to reform a murderous ruler of Wei, and Confucius teaches him the fasting of the heart: hear not with the ears but with the mind, not with the mind but with the soul, until the mind stops and the soul stands passively responsive — the empty room through which light enters. It is easy to stop walking; the trouble is to walk without touching the ground.
summary.zh: 顏回將之衛，夫子告以心齋：無聽之以耳而聽之以心，無聽之以心而聽之以氣；虛室生白，吉祥止止。人莫鑒於流水而鑒於止水。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the fast of the heart became the classic interior-ritual term of later Daoist meditation. Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: Confucius said, "FAST.... Let me explain. You have a method, but it is difficult to practise. Those which are easy are not from God." "Well," replied Yen Hui, "my family is poor, and for many months we have tasted neither wine nor flesh. Is not that fasting?" "The fasting of religious observance it is," answered Confucius, "but not the fasting of the heart." "And may I ask," said Yen Hui, "in what consists the fasting of the heart?" "Cultivate unity," replied Confucius.
passages.zh: 孔子說：「齋戒吧……讓我解釋一下。你有方法，但難以實行。那些容易的，並非出自神。」「是這樣，」顏回回答說，「我家貧窮，好幾個月沒嚐過酒和肉了。這不就是齋戒嗎？」「那是宗教儀式的齋戒，」孔子回答說，「但不是心的齋戒。」「請問，」顏回說，「心的齋戒究竟是什麼？」「修養專一，」孔子回答說。

passages.text: "You hear not with the ears, but with the mind; not with the mind, but with your soul. But let hearing stop with the ears. Let the working of the mind stop with itself. Then the soul will be a negative existence, passively responsive to externals. In such a negative existence, only TAO can abide. And that negative state is the fasting of the heart."
passages.zh: 「你不是用耳朵聽，而是用心聽；不是用心聽，而是用你的靈魂聽。但要讓聽覺止於耳朵。讓心的作用止於自身。這樣，靈魂便成為一種虛空的存有，被動地回應外物。在這樣一種虛空的存有中，唯有道能安住。而那虛空的狀態，就是心的齋戒。」

passages.text: "Look at that window. Through it an empty room becomes bright with scenery; but the landscape stops outside. Were this not so, we should have an exemplification of sitting still and running away at one and the same time. In this sense, you may use your ears and eyes to communicate within, but shut out all wisdom from the mind. And there where the supernatural can find shelter, shall not man find shelter too? This is the method for regenerating all creation. It was the instrument which Yü and Shun employed. It was the secret of the success of Fu Hsi and Chi Chü."
passages.zh: 「看那扇窗。透過它，一間空屋因景物而明亮；但景色止於窗外。若不是這樣，我們便會有一個同時靜坐不動又逃之夭夭的例子了。在這個意義上，你可以用耳朵和眼睛向內溝通，但要把一切智慧關在心的外面。而在那超自然之物能尋得庇護的地方，人豈不也能尋得庇護嗎？這是使萬物重生的方法。這是禹和舜所運用的工具。這是伏羲和几蘧成功的祕訣。」

title.en: The Sacred Tree That Dreamed of Uselessness (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 櫟社樹之夢（莊子）

region.en: Ch'ü-yüan, en route to Ch'i (symbolic pin: Linzi, Shandong, China)
region.zh: 曲轅（往齊途中；象徵定位：山東臨淄）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 4, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 4

summary.en: An artisan passing the giant sacred li-tree refuses to stop: boat it and it sinks, coffin it and it rots. That night the tree appears in his dream and rebukes him — the fruit-bearers are stripped and snapped for their own value, while the tree has aimed at uselessness through long perils and so attained its venerable size; his sacredness is only the last of its tricks of escape.
summary.zh: 匠石之齊，見櫟社樹，不視而行。木夢而責之：果屬以其能苦其生，不終其天年；而予求無所可用久矣，幾死，乃今得之。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); tree-oracle dream narrative. 'dream-vision' is an interpretive tag pending a dedicated motif. Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: A certain artisan was travelling to the Ch'i State. On reaching Ch'ü-yüan, he saw a sacred li tree, large enough to hide an ox behind it, a hundred spans in girth, towering up ten cubits over the hill top, and carrying behind it branches, many tens of the smallest of which were of a size for boats. Crowds stood gazing at it, but our artisan took no notice, and went on his way without even casting a look behind. His apprentice however gazed his fill, and when he caught up his master, said, "Ever since I have handled an adze in your service, I have never seen such a splendid piece of timber as that. How was it that you, sir, did not care to stop and look at it?"
passages.zh: 有一位匠人前往齊國。到了曲轅，他看見一棵神聖的櫟樹，大得足以在它後面藏一頭牛，樹幹周長百尺，高出山頂十仞，它後面伸展出的枝條，其中許多最小的都大得足以造船。成群的人站著觀望它，但我們的匠人卻毫不理會，逕自前行，甚至連回頭看一眼都沒有。然而他的徒弟卻看個夠，當他趕上師父時，說道：「自從我在您手下拿起斧頭以來，從未見過這樣一棵壯麗的木材。先生您怎麼竟不願停下來看一看它呢？」

passages.text: "It's not worth talking about," replied his master. "It's good for nothing. Make a boat of it,--'twould sink. A coffin,--'twould rot. Furniture,--'twould soon break down. A door,--'twould sweat. A pillar,--'twould be worm-eaten. It is wood of no quality, and of no use. That is why it has attained its present age."
passages.zh: 「不值一提，」他的師父回答說。「它一無用處。拿它造船——會沉。做棺材——會爛。做家具——很快就會壞。做門——會滲水。做柱子——會被蟲蛀。這是沒有品質、沒有用處的木頭。正因如此，它才活到了現在這個年歲。」

passages.text: When the artisan reached home, he dreamt that the tree appeared to him in a dream and spoke as follows:--"What is it that you compare me with? Is it with the more elegant trees?--The cherry-apple, the pear, the orange, the pumelo, and other fruit-bearers, as soon as their fruit ripens are stripped and treated with indignity. The great boughs are snapped off, the small ones scattered abroad. Thus do these trees by their own value injure their own lives. They cannot fulfil their allotted span of years, but perish prematurely in mid-career from their entanglement with the world around them. Thus it is with all things. For a long period my aim was to be useless. Many times I was in danger, but at length I succeeded, and so became useful as I am to-day."
passages.zh: 匠人回到家後，夢見那棵樹在夢中向他顯現，說道：「你拿我比作什麼？是比作那些更雅致的樹嗎？——櫻桃、蘋果、梨、橘、柚，以及其他結果的樹，一旦果實成熟，就被剝奪、被粗暴對待。大枝被折斷，小枝被散落四方。這些樹就這樣以自己的價值傷害了自己的生命。它們不能享盡天年，而是在中途因與周圍世界的糾纏而夭折。萬物皆是如此。長久以來，我的目標就是成為無用。許多次我身陷險境，但終於成功了，於是才有了今日這般的有用。」

title.en: The Hunchback Whom the Conscription Passed By (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 支離疏（莊子）

region.en: The conscription muster (symbolic pin: Song, Henan, China)
region.zh: 徵兵之會（象徵定位：宋，今河南）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 4, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 4

summary.en: The hunchback Su — jaws touching navel, shoulders above head, viscera upside down — earns his living at work that stoops, and is spared by conscription and public works while drawing grain and firewood rations. If bodily deformity preserves the body to its allotted end, how much more will moral and mental deformity avail.
summary.zh: 支離疏者，頤隱於臍，肩高於頂，會撮指天，五管在上，兩髀為脅；挫針治繲足以餬口，鼓筴播精足以食十人。上徵武士，則支離攘臂而遊於其間。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: There was a hunchback named Su. His jaws touched his navel. His shoulders were higher than his head. His hair knot looked up to the sky. His viscera were upside down. His buttocks were where his ribs should have been. By tailoring, or washing, he was easily able to earn his living. By sifting rice he could make enough to support a family of ten.
passages.zh: 有一個名叫蘇的駝背人。他的下巴貼到肚臍。他的肩膀高過頭頂。他的髮髻朝天。他的五臟顛倒。他的臀部長在肋骨該在的地方。靠著裁衣或洗衣，他輕易就能謀生。靠著篩米，他賺得的足以養活十口之家。

passages.text: When orders came down for a conscription, the hunchback stood unconcerned among the crowd. And similarly, in matters of public works, his deformity shielded him from being employed. On the other hand, when it came to donations of grain, the hunchback received as much as three chung, and of firewood, ten faggots. And if physical deformity was thus enough to preserve his body until its allotted end, how much more would not moral and mental deformity avail!
passages.zh: 當徵兵的號令下達時，那駝背人毫不在意地站在人群之中。同樣地，在公共工程的事上，他的殘疾使他免於被徵用。另一方面，到了捐獻穀物時，那駝背人領到多達三鍾，柴薪則領到十束。形體上的殘疾尚且足以保全他的身體直到天年終盡，那麼道德與心智上的殘疾又將有多大用處呢！

title.en: O Phœnix, O Phœnix: Chieh Yü's Mad Song at Confucius' Door (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 鳳兮鳳兮：接輿之狂歌（莊子）

region.en: The court of Ch'u (Jingzhou, Hubei, China)
region.zh: 楚廷（今湖北荊州）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 4, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 4

summary.en: In the Ch'u State the feigned madman Chieh Yü passes Confucius' door singing: O phœnix, how has thy virtue fallen! The honours of this world are light as feathers, yet none value them; its misfortunes are weighty as earth, yet none escape them. Hills suffer from the trees they produce; the cinnamon tree furnishes food and is cut down — all men know the use of useful things, but they do not know the use of useless things.
summary.zh: 孔子適楚，楚狂接輿遊其門而歌：鳳兮鳳兮，何如德之衰也；來世不可待，往世不可追也。人皆知有用之用，而莫知無用之用也。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the Confucius-and-the-mad-song episode is retold from the Lun-yü by Zhuangzi. Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: When Confucius was in the Ch'u State, the eccentric Chieh Yü passed his door, saying, "O phœnix, O phœnix, how has thy virtue fallen!-- unable to wait for the coming years or to go back into the past. If TAO prevails on earth, prophets will fulfil their mission. If TAO does not prevail, they will but preserve themselves. At the present day they will but just escape.
