passages.zh: 孔子在楚國時，怪人接輿經過他的門前，說道：「鳳凰啊，鳳凰啊，你的德性怎麼衰落了！——既不能等待來年，又不能回到過去。如果道行於世，聖人就會成就他們的使命。如果道不行於世，他們就只能保全自身。當今之世，他們也只能勉強免於禍患。」

passages.text: "The honours of this world are light as feathers, yet none estimate them at their true value. The misfortunes of this life are weighty as the earth itself, yet none can keep out of their reach. No more, no more, seek to influence by virtue. Beware, beware, move cautiously on! O ferns, O ferns, wound not my steps! Through my tortuous journey wound not my feet! Hills suffer from the trees they produce. Fat burns by its own combustibility. Cinnamon trees furnish food: therefore they are cut down. The lacquer tree is felled for use. All men know the use of useful things; but they do not know the use of useless things."
passages.zh: 「世上的榮華輕如羽毛，卻沒有人估量它們的真正價值。此生的禍患重如大地本身，卻沒有人能避開它們。罷了，罷了，不要再想以德行去感化人。當心，當心，謹慎前行！蕨草啊，蕨草啊，不要纏住我的腳步！在我曲折的旅途中，不要纏住我的雙腳！山丘因所生的樹木而受害。油脂因自身的可燃而耗盡。桂樹供人食用：因此被砍伐。漆樹為了取用而被伐倒。人人都知道有用之物的用處；卻不知道無用之物的大用。」

title.en: Adam and Eve Meet at Arafat
title.zh: 阿丹與哈娃於阿拉法特重逢

region.en: Mount Arafat, near Mecca (traditional site of the reunion; literal pin)
region.zh: 麥加附近阿拉法特山（傳統重逢地；實際定位）

period: Qisas al-Anbiya tradition (Arabic, c. 8th-11th centuries CE); paraphrase from Arabic

source.archive: Wikisource (Arabic; al-Kisa’i, Qisas al-Anbiya, Leiden ed. 1922)
source.work: Muhammad al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Tales of the Prophets), Arabic c. 1100; cf. Thackston 1978 translation (cited for reference; passages paraphrased from Arabic)

license: Arabic original public domain; paraphrase original

summary.en: After the expulsion from Eden, Adam descends, the legend says, in India or Serendib and Eve on the Arabian shore; for two hundred years they wander the earth seeking one another. Where their paths finally cross, a mountain called Arafat — 'he knew' — rises; God accepts the prayer of the pair, ordains the pilgrimage round the House, and teaches Adam the rites of the hajj, which are performed on this ground to this day.
summary.zh: 相傳出園之後，阿丹降於印度或楞伽島，哈娃降於阿拉伯海岸；二人尋覓相望二百年。其行跡交會之山名為阿拉法特——『他知道了』——主應允二人之祈，命環繞天房之朝，並教阿丹朝覲之儀——即今日此地所行者。

sensitivity.note: Qisas legend of a living tradition; such tales are regarded within Islam as edifying but not authoritative; paraphrased from the Arabic original.

passages.text: When the two were sent down from the Garden, they were separated: Adam, it is said, came down on a mountain of Ceylon, and Eve on the shore of Arabia. Each wandered over the earth asking after the other, weeping and repenting, until at last they met in a valley of the mountains of Arabia; and the place was called Arafat, 'the place of knowing,' because there each one knew the other again.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當二人被逐出樂園時，他們被分開了：據說亞當降落在錫蘭的一座山上，夏娃則落在阿拉伯的海岸。二人各自在大地上遊蕩，彼此打聽對方的下落，哭泣悔罪，直到最後在阿拉伯群山中的一座山谷裡重逢；那地方被稱為阿拉法特，意即「相認之地」，因為二人就在那裡彼此重新相認。

passages.text: God forgave them there and commanded Adam to build the House. He taught him the rites of the pilgrimage — the tawaf around the Kaaba, the run between the two hills, the stand at Arafat — and appointed the seasons of the sacred months. And the pilgrims stand at Arafat every year on the ninth of Dhu'l-Hijja, on the ground where the first human pair were rejoined.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 神在那裡赦免了他們，並命令亞當建造那殿。祂教他朝覲的儀式——繞行克爾白、在兩山之間奔走、在阿拉法特駐立——並規定了神聖月份的時節。而朝覲者每年都在都爾希哲月的第九日駐立於阿拉法特，就在那第一對人類重逢之地。

title.en: Seth Receives the Succession
title.zh: 塞特承其統緒

region.en: Land of Adam's children (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿丹子孫之地（象徵性定位）

period: Qisas al-Anbiya tradition (Arabic, c. 8th-11th centuries CE); paraphrase from Arabic

source.archive: Wikisource (Arabic; al-Kisa’i, Qisas al-Anbiya, Leiden ed. 1922)
source.work: Muhammad al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic c. 1100); passages paraphrased from Arabic

license: Arabic original public domain; paraphrase original

summary.en: After Adam's death the succession passes to Seth, the pure son, whom God had set in his father's place: to him are given fifty books of wisdom, and he teaches his people the worship of God, the reckoning of the sun and the moon, and the craft of prophecy — until his line is corrupted in the days before the Flood.
summary.zh: 阿丹歿後，其統緒傳於純潔之子塞特——主立之於其父之位：賜其五十卷智慧之書；他教人民敬拜主、推算日月、承先知之藝——直至洪水前其世系墮落。

sensitivity.note: Qisas legend of a living tradition; paraphrased from the Arabic original.

passages.text: When Adam died, God set Seth in his place as a prophet over his children, and gave him fifty books, in which were written the wisdom of the ages, the reckoning of the sun and the moon and the stars, and the signs of the times. Seth taught his people to worship God and to shun the works of Cain's line, which had begun to build cities and to make instruments of iron and song.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 亞當死後，神立塞特代替他，作他子孫的先知，並賜給他五十部書，書中記載了歷代的智慧、日、月與星辰的運行，以及時代的徵兆。塞特教導他的族人敬拜神，並遠離該隱一族的作為——該隱的後裔已開始建造城邑，製作鐵器與樂器。

passages.text: Seth prophesied of the Flood and of the coming of the messengers, and taught his sons the names of the prophets to come, from Noah to the Seal. And when he died he was gathered to his father's grave in the mountain; and his people kept the faith for a season, until the sons of men took the daughters of the descendants of Cain, and the worship of God grew cold before the Flood.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 塞特預言了大洪水與眾使者的來臨，並將此後要來的眾先知之名教給他的兒子們，從挪亞直到封印者。他死後，被歸葬於山間他父親的墳墓；他的族人守持信仰一時，直到人的兒子們娶了該隱後裔的女子，在大洪水之前，對神的敬拜便漸漸冷淡了。

title.en: The Donkey, the Name of God, and the Stowaway of the Ark
title.zh: 驢、主之名與方舟偷渡者

region.en: Mount Judi, landing of the Ark (traditional site; literal pin)
region.zh: 朱迪山——方舟停靠地（傳統地點；實際定位）

period: Qisas al-Anbiya tradition (Arabic, c. 8th-11th centuries CE); paraphrase from Arabic

source.archive: Wikisource (Arabic; al-Kisa’i, Qisas al-Anbiya, Leiden ed. 1922)
source.work: Muhammad al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic c. 1100); passages paraphrased from Arabic

license: Arabic original public domain; paraphrase original

summary.en: The beasts are gathered two by two; but one creature will not board — a donkey in whom the Evil One is hidden. Noah cries 'In the name of God, get in!', and the demon is driven out — and in shame of his flight, Satan clutches the donkey's tail, which stands up on end from that day. Of the two ravens and the dove; of the dog that guarded the ark; and of the hog that Noah formed of the elephant's — these are the legendary deck-mates of the Flood.
summary.zh: 獸類成雙登舟；惟一獸不願登——驢，魔匿於其中。努哈呼『奉主之名，進來！』——魔被驅出；魔羞而攫驢之尾，故驢尾自是翹起。二鴉與鴿；守舟之犬；以及由象所造之豬——此皆洪水的傳奇艙友。

sensitivity.note: Qisas legend of a living tradition; the Satan-in-the-donkey tale is classic popular qisas; paraphrased from the Arabic original.

passages.text: When the creatures were gathered into the ark, one would not go in: a donkey at whom Satan had hidden. Noah dragged it, and it brayed and hung back; then Noah said, 'In the name of God, get in!' and the demon fled from the donkey. But as he fled, Satan clutched the donkey's tail with his hand, and it stood on end from that day — and this is why men say the braying of the ass is the voice of the Evil One.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當眾生被聚集進方舟時，有一隻不肯進去：那是一頭驢，撒但藏在牠身上。挪亞拉牠，牠便鳴叫著往後退；於是挪亞說：「奉神的名，進去！」那惡魔便從驢身上逃走了。但當他逃走時，撒但用手抓住了驢的尾巴，從那日起驢尾便豎立起來——這就是為何人們說驢的鳴叫是那惡者的聲音。

passages.text: Noah sent out two ravens to seek the dry land, and a dove; and the dove returned with a green leaf in its beak. And among the creatures of the ark was a dog that is said to have guarded the door, and the pair of swine; and the legend tells that the hog was formed of the elephant and called swine, that its flesh might be a medicine against the serpent's venom. When the water sank the ark came to rest on Mount Judi, and Noah and his household came forth upon the earth.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 挪亞放出兩隻烏鴉去尋找乾地，又放出一隻鴿子；那鴿子銜著一片綠葉回來。方舟的眾生之中，據說還有一隻守門的狗，以及一對豬；傳說那豬是由象造成的，稱為豬，為要使牠的肉成為解蛇毒之藥。水退之後，方舟停在朱迪山上，挪亞和他的家眷便出來，踏上大地。

title.en: Azazil: Iblis Among the Angels of the First Heaven
title.zh: 阿扎齊勒：初天的天使易卜劣廝

region.en: Lower heaven of the angels (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 天使的低層天（象徵性定位）

period: Qisas al-Anbiya tradition (Arabic, c. 8th-11th centuries CE); paraphrase from Arabic

source.archive: Wikisource (Arabic; al-Kisa’i, Qisas al-Anbiya, Leiden ed. 1922)
source.work: Muhammad al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic c. 1100); passages paraphrased from Arabic

license: Arabic original public domain; paraphrase original

summary.en: Before Adam there were jinn, made of smokeless fire, who wasted the earth with blood; God sent an army of angels against them, and among the captives was a youth named Azazil, who worshipped God with such devotion that he was raised into the lower heaven and taught the angels. When Adam was created, God said 'Bow down'; and Azazil — the proudest of the worshippers — could not bow to a thing of clay: 'I am better than he; Thou hast created me of fire and him of clay.' And pride was the first sin.
summary.zh: 阿丹之前有精靈，由無煙之火所造，以血染地；主遣天使軍征之，俘中有名阿扎齊勒之青年，拜主至誠，被擢於低層天，教授天使。阿丹受造，主命俯首；阿扎齊勒——最傲的敬拜者——不能向黏土之身俯首：『我比他尊貴；你以火造我，以土造他。』傲慢乃第一罪。

sensitivity.note: Qisas legend of a living tradition; the name Azazil and the jinn backstory come from tafsir/qisas lore; paraphrased from the Arabic original.

passages.text: Before the children of Adam the jinn walked the earth, made of the smokeless fire, and they shed blood and corrupted it. God sent down an army of angels, and they fought them and took captives; and among the captives was a youth of wonderful beauty, called Azazil. He was raised to the lower heaven and taught the angels, and worshipped God with the angels; and there was none among them more devout than he.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在亞當的子孫之前，精靈曾行走於大地，他們由無煙之火造成，流人血、敗壞大地。神差遣一隊天使降下，他們與精靈爭戰，擄獲了俘虜；俘虜之中有一個容貌極美的少年，名叫阿撒瀉勒。他被提升到最低一層天，教導眾天使，並與天使一同敬拜神；他們之中沒有一個比他更虔誠的。

passages.text: When God created Adam from clay and breathed into him of His spirit, He said to the angels, 'Bow down'; and they bowed, all of them, but Azazil refused and was too proud, and said, 'I am better than he: Thou hast created me of fire, and him of clay.' Then God said, 'Get thee down from it, for thou art not to glorify Me here'; and the worshipper of many years became the Accursed, and the first sin in heaven was pride.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當神用泥土創造亞當，並將祂的靈吹入他裡面時，祂對眾天使說：「你們當叩拜」；他們全都叩拜了，唯有阿撒瀉勒拒絕，過於驕傲，說：「我比他更好：你以火造我，卻以泥土造他。」於是神說：「你從這裡下去吧，因為你不可在此榮耀我」；那敬拜多年者成了被詛咒者，而天上第一樁罪便是驕傲。

title.en: Harut and Marut: The Two Angels of Babylon
title.zh: 哈魯特與馬魯特：巴比倫的兩位天使

region.en: Babylon, between heaven and earth (literal pin)
region.zh: 巴比倫，天地之間（實際定位）

period: Qur'an 2:102 with Qisas/tafsir expansions (Arabic); paraphrase from Arabic

source.archive: Wikisource (Arabic; al-Kisa’i, Qisas al-Anbiya, Leiden ed. 1922)
source.work: Qur'an 2:102 with Qisas al-Anbiya / tafsir legends (al-Kisa'i; al-Tha'alabi); passages paraphrased from Arabic

license: Arabic original public domain; paraphrase original

summary.en: The angels marvel that men sin so; God names two of them to be sent down and given the desires of men. Harut and Marut descend to Babylon in the form of men, and are undone by a woman — one named Zuhra, who demands wine, idolatry and murder of them before she will hear the greatest name of God. They fall; the Name escapes them; and they hang head-down between heaven and earth until the Day of Resurrection, where they teach magic to whoever comes to them in Babylon — warning all who learn: 'We are a trial; do not disbelieve.'
summary.zh: 天使訝異人類之罪；主遣二天使下降，賦以人之欲。哈魯特與馬魯特化身為人降至巴比倫，毀於一女子——名祖赫拉者，她要先得酒、偶像與殺人，方肯聽主至大之名。二人墮落；名逃逸；二人倒懸於天地之間直至復活日，於巴比倫教人魔術——並警誡學者：『我們是考驗，你們不要悖信。』

sensitivity.note: Qisas legend built on Qur'an 2:102; presented as the tradition's own account; paraphrased from the Arabic original.

passages.text: In the Qur'an it is said: Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching men sorcery; and in Babylon the two angels Harut and Marut; and they did not teach anyone until they had said, 'We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.' The legend tells how the angels, seeing the wickedness of men, said in praise of their own obedience; and God said, 'Choose two of yourselves, and I will send you down and give you the desires of men.' Harut and Marut were chosen.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 2:102 and al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 《古蘭經》中說：素萊曼未曾不信道，乃是眾惡魔不信道，教人魔術；又在巴比倫有兩位天使哈魯特與馬魯特；他們未教任何人，直到先說：『我們只是一種考驗，故你們不要不信道。』傳說講述：眾天使見人類的罪惡，便誇讚自己的順從；真主說：『你們從自己當中選出兩位，我要把你們降下，並賜予你們人類的慾望。』哈魯特與馬魯特於是被選中。

passages.text: They descended in the shape of handsome men to the gates of Babylon, and a woman named Zuhra came to them and was smitten with love; and when they turned from her she called for wine, and for idolatry, and lastly for the killing of a traveller, before she would listen to the greatest Name of God which they knew. They fell; and the Name flew up to heaven. In some tellings they hang head downward between heaven and earth, suffering until the Day of Resurrection; in Babylon they sit at a well and teach magic to all who come — but they say first, 'We are a trial; do not disbelieve.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i / al-Tha'alabi, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們以俊美男子的形貌降臨巴比倫城門，一位名叫祖赫拉（金星）的女子來到他們面前，為愛所困；當他們轉身離她而去時，她先以酒相求，再以偶像崇拜相求，最後以殺害一名旅人相求，才肯聽他們所知的最大的真主之名。他們墮落了；那名字便飛升上天。在某些傳說中，他們頭朝下懸掛於天地之間，受苦直到復活日；在巴比倫，他們坐在一口井旁，向所有前來的人傳授魔法——但他們必先說：『我們是一種考驗；不要不信道。』

title.en: The Peacock and Iblis at the Gate of the Garden
title.zh: 孔雀與易卜劣廝於樂園門前

region.en: Gate of the Garden of Eden (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伊甸園門前（象徵性定位）

period: Qisas al-Anbiya tradition (Arabic, c. 8th-11th centuries CE); paraphrase from Arabic

source.archive: Wikisource (Arabic; al-Kisa’i, Qisas al-Anbiya, Leiden ed. 1922)
source.work: Muhammad al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic c. 1100); passages paraphrased from Arabic

license: Arabic original public domain; paraphrase original

summary.en: Cast down, Iblis sits outside the Garden for a thousand years, unable to enter. A peacock of paradise asks him what he wants. 'I want to get in.' 'But the gate has been shut against you.' 'Tell me one thing: will the peacock's house endure for ever?' — 'No; everything but God will perish.' Iblis takes his chance: 'Show me a way in — under your foot, in your beak, in your body — and I will teach you the grain that makes death not return.' The peacock repeats it to the serpent; the serpent carries Iblis in; and paradise is opened to sorrow.
summary.zh: 易卜劣廝被逐後，於樂園外坐一千年，不得入。樂園孔雀問其所求。『我要進去。』『門已向你關閉。』『告我一事：孔雀之居將永存嗎？』——『不會；除主外萬物皆滅。』易卜劣廝乘機：『示我一入之法——足下、喙中、身內——我教你一粒穀，使死不復返。』孔雀轉告蛇；蛇攜其入；樂園自此有憂。

sensitivity.note: Qisas legend of a living tradition; the peacock-serpent-Iblis dialogue is a classic of al-Kisa'i; paraphrased from the Arabic original.

passages.text: When Iblis was cast out of the Garden he sat weeping at its gate for a thousand years. A peacock, one of the birds of Paradise, came and asked him why he wept. He said, 'I have been shut out of my house.' The peacock said, 'But why should you weep? The gate is shut against you.' Iblis said: 'Answer me one question: will your dwelling in the Garden endure for ever, and will you never die?' The peacock said, 'No; everything will perish except the face of God.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當易卜劣廝被逐出樂園時，他坐在園門口哭泣了一千年。一隻孔雀——樂園的鳥兒之一——前來問他為何哭泣。他說：『我被逐出了我的家。』孔雀說：『可你為何要哭呢？門已對你關閉了。』易卜劣廝說：『回答我一個問題：你在樂園中的居所會永存嗎？你永遠不會死嗎？』孔雀說：『不會；萬物皆將毀滅，唯有真主的面容長存。』

passages.text: Then Iblis said, 'Show me a way into the Garden — under your foot, or in your beak, or within your body — and I will teach you a word by which you will never die, nor your children after you.' The peacock went to the serpent, who was the most beautiful of the animals, and told him; and the serpent said, 'I will carry him in within me.' So Iblis entered the Garden on the serpent's back, and whispered to Adam by the tree of eternity; and that is how death came into the world, if the legend is believed.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是易卜劣廝說：『給我指一條進入樂園的路——在你的腳下，或你的喙中，或你的體內——我便教你一句話，憑它你永遠不死，你的子孫後代也永遠不死。』孔雀去找蛇——牠是動物中最美的——告訴了牠；蛇說：『我把他藏在我體內帶進去。』於是易卜劣廝騎在蛇背上進入了樂園，在永恆之樹旁向阿丹低語；若相信這傳說，死亡便是這樣進入世界的。

title.en: The Tower of Babel in the Muslim Telling
title.zh: 穆斯林講述中的巴別塔

region.en: Babel, on the Euphrates (literal pin)
region.zh: 幼發拉底河畔的巴別（實際定位）

period: Qisas al-Anbiya tradition (Arabic, c. 8th-11th centuries CE); paraphrase from Arabic

source.archive: Wikisource (Arabic; al-Kisa’i, Qisas al-Anbiya, Leiden ed. 1922)
source.work: Qisas al-Anbiya / tafsir legends (al-Tabari, Tarikh; al-Tha'alabi); passages paraphrased from Arabic

license: Arabic original public domain; paraphrase original

summary.en: After the Flood the children of Noah multiply in one tongue and one speech, and in the land of Babel they say: 'Let us build a tower to the sky, and fight the God of heaven.' Nimrod (in the Muslim legend, Nemrud) leads the work; fire is taken up to the top and set as a sun. God confounds their one language into seventy-two tongues; the builders can no longer understand one another, and the tower is left standing half-built as a wonder of the ancients.
summary.zh: 洪水之後，努哈子孫同語同音，於巴別之地言：『我們建塔通天，與天主作戰。』尼姆魯德（傳說中的奈姆魯德）領工；火被運至頂端，立如日。主將一語化為七十二種方言；工匠彼此不復能解，塔半成而廢，為古人奇觀。

sensitivity.note: Qisas legend; the Nimrod tower narrative is an Islamic reworking of Genesis 11; paraphrased from the Arabic original.

passages.text: The children of Noah multiplied after the Flood and spoke one language; and in the land of Babel they said one to another: 'Let us build a tower whose top will reach to heaven, that we may climb to it and wage war upon the God of the heaven.' And Nimrod said, 'Build'; and they built year upon year, carrying fire to the summit and setting it there as a sun, that their work might be seen from afar.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Tabari, Tarikh (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 洪水之後，努哈的子孫繁衍增多，說同一種語言；在巴別之地，他們彼此說：『讓我們建一座塔，塔頂通天，好讓我們爬上去，向天上的神發動戰爭。』寧錄說：『建吧』；他們便年復一年地建造，把火運到塔頂，置於其上如太陽一般，好讓他們的工程從遠處可見。

passages.text: God confounded their tongue so that one understood not the speech of another: seventy-two languages, it is said, came out of the one. The builders fell to quarrelling, and the work stopped where it stood; and the tower was left half-built as a wonder of the ancients. Some say the place of the confusion was made a city, and the city was called Babel — Bab-Il, the gate of God — because there the tongues of men were divided.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Tabari, Tarikh (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 真主混亂了他們的語言，以致一人聽不懂另一人的話：據說，從那一種語言中分出了七十二種語言。建造者們爭吵起來，工程便停在原處；那塔半途而廢，成了古人的奇觀。有人說，混亂語言之地被建成了一座城，那城名叫巴別——Bab-Il，即神之門——因為人類的語言是在那裡被分開的。

title.en: Wadd and Suwa: Idols Made From the Memory of the Righteous
title.zh: 瓦德與素瓦：由義人記憶所造的偶像

region.en: Arabia between the Flood and Ibrahim (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 洪水與易卜拉欣之間的阿拉伯（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an 71:23 with Qisas/tafsir expansions (Arabic); paraphrase from Arabic

source.archive: Wikisource (Arabic; al-Kisa’i, Qisas al-Anbiya, Leiden ed. 1922)
source.work: Qur'an 71:23; Qisas al-Anbiya / tafsir legends (al-Tabari); passages paraphrased from Arabic

license: Arabic original public domain; paraphrase original

summary.en: Noah's people worship Wadd, Suwa, Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr; the legend says these were the names of righteous men of the generations between Adam and the Flood. When they died, Satan came to their kinsmen in the likeness of a weeping comforter and said: 'Set up a statue in the place where he used to sit, and remember him.' The images were at first honored in memory; then the next generation said: 'Our fathers worshipped them; we will worship them too.' And idols began on earth.
summary.zh: 努哈之民拜瓦德、素瓦、葉巫斯、葉歐克與奈斯爾；傳說此乃阿丹至洪水之間義人之名。其人死後，魔以哭慰者之形臨其親族：『在其常坐之處立像以為記念。』起初因記念而尊崇；下一代則言：『祖輩曾拜之，我輩亦將拜之。』偶像自此始於大地。

sensitivity.note: Qisas legend built on Qur'an 71:23; paraphrased from the Arabic original.

passages.text: Noah called his people night and day, and they put their fingers in their ears; and their chiefs said, 'Do not forsake your gods, and do not forsake Wadd, nor Suwa, nor Yaghuth, nor Ya'uq, nor Nasr.' The legend tells that these were the names of righteous men who had lived between Adam and the Flood, whose death their people mourned.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 71:23 and al-Tabari, Tarikh (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 努哈晝夜呼喚他的族人，他們卻把手指塞進耳中；他們的首領說：『不要捨棄你們的神明，不要捨棄旺德，也不要捨棄蘇瓦、葉巫斯、葉歐格和奈斯爾。』傳說這些是生活在阿丹與大洪水之間的義人之名，他們的族人為他們的死而哀悼。

passages.text: When one of them died, Satan came in the form of a weeping comforter and said: 'Set up a figure of him in the place where he used to sit, and set your children to play around it, that his memory may not leave you.' And they set up the images. The first generation honoured them in remembrance; but when that generation died, the next said, 'Our fathers worshipped these images; we will worship them'; and they worshipped, and made them gods. Thus idolatry began on the earth, if the legend is believed.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Tabari, Tarikh (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他們中有一人死去，撒旦便化作一名哭泣的安慰者前來，說道：『在他從前常坐之處立起他的雕像，並讓你們的孩子在它周圍玩耍，好讓他的記憶不離開你們。』於是他們立起了那些偶像。第一代人為紀念而尊崇它們；但當那一代人死去，下一代人便說：『我們的祖先崇拜這些偶像；我們也要崇拜它們』；於是他們崇拜了，並把它們當作神明。倘若這傳說可信，偶像崇拜便如此在大地上開始了。

title.en: Sarah in the House of the King
title.zh: 撒拉於王宮之中

region.en: Egypt, house of the king (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 埃及王宮（象徵性定位）

period: Qisas al-Anbiya / Isra'iliyat tradition (Arabic); paraphrase from Arabic

source.archive: Wikisource (Arabic; al-Kisa’i, Qisas al-Anbiya, Leiden ed. 1922)
source.work: Qisas al-Anbiya / Isra'iliyat legends (al-Tabari, Tarikh; cf. G. Weil, The Bible, the Koran and the Talmud, 1846); passages paraphrased from Arabic

license: Arabic original public domain; paraphrase original

summary.en: A famine drives Ibrahim into Egypt with Sarah, whose beauty he fears will be taken: 'Say thou art my sister.' The king's men seize her; Ibrahim prays. The king reaches out his hand, and it withers; he is told to release the woman, and is healed only after he swears. He gives her a slave-girl, Hagar, in recompense; and of Hagar comes Ismail.
summary.zh: 饑荒使易卜拉欣攜撒拉入埃及；他恐其美貌被奪：『你說是我的妹妹。』王的人捉她；易卜拉欣祈禱。王伸手，手即枯萎；被告知放人，誓後方得醫。王以婢女夏甲作償；夏甲生易司馬儀。

sensitivity.note: Qisas/Isra'iliyat legend; parallel to Genesis 12; paraphrased from the Arabic original.

passages.text: When famine drove Ibrahim and Sarah into Egypt, he said to her: 'You are the fairest of women; say that you are my sister, for I fear the people of this land.' The men of the king saw her and praised her to him, and she was taken into the king's house. And Ibrahim stood in prayer; and when the king reached out his hand to her, his hand was withered as a plank.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Tabari, Tarikh (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當饑荒迫使易卜拉欣和撒拉進入埃及時，他對她說：『你是最美丽的女子；就說你是我的妹妹吧，因為我畏懼這地方的人。』國王的人看見了她，便向國王誇讚她，於是她被帶進國王的宮中。易卜拉欣站立祈禱；當國王向她伸出手時，他的手便如木板般枯萎了。

passages.text: The king cried out, 'Pray for me, and I will not touch her.' He was healed; and he swore by God, and gave her a slave-girl named Hagar, saying: 'Take her, for I would not have aught of her.' And Sarah returned to Ibrahim; and of Hagar, who became the mother of Ismail, the lineage of the Arabs of the Hijaz descends — if the legend is believed.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Tabari, Tarikh (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 國王喊道：『為我祈禱吧，我絕不碰她。』他痊癒了；他指真主發誓，並給了她一名名叫哈哲爾的女奴，說道：『帶她走吧，我不願從她那裡得到任何東西。』撒拉回到了易卜拉欣身邊；而由哈哲爾——她後來成了易司馬儀的母親——希賈茲阿拉伯人的世系便由此而來——倘若這傳說可信的話。

title.en: Hagar, the Baby Ismail and the Water of Zamzam
title.zh: 夏甲、嬰兒易司馬儀與滲滲泉之水

region.en: Mecca, valley of Bakka (literal pin)
region.zh: 麥加巴克谷（實際定位）

period: Qisas al-Anbiya / sira tradition (Arabic); paraphrase from Arabic

source.archive: Wikisource (Arabic; al-Kisa’i, Qisas al-Anbiya, Leiden ed. 1922)
source.work: Qisas al-Anbiya / al-Tabari, Tarikh (Arabic); cf. Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira; passages paraphrased from Arabic

license: Arabic original public domain; paraphrase original

summary.en: Ibrahim sets Hagar and the child Ismail by the House in a waterless valley and leaves; she runs twice between the hills of Safa and Marwa crying 'Water! Water!' — the origin of the sa'y rite. An angel strikes the ground and Zamzam bursts forth; she walls it with sand. The caravan of Jurhum passes, sees the bird that hangs over water, and asks leave to settle: 'Yes, so long as you do not claim the water.' Their children intermarry with Ismail's, and Mecca is founded.
summary.zh: 易卜拉欣置夏甲與幼兒易司馬儀於天房旁無水之谷而去；她於薩法與瑪爾瓦兩山間往返奔走七次，呼『水！水！』——此即賽艾之儀之源。天使擊地，滲滲泉湧出；她以沙圍之。主爾胡姆商隊見盤旋之鳥知有水，求許定居：『可以，惟不可佔水。』其子孫與易司馬儀通婚，麥加由是建立。

sensitivity.note: Qisas/sira legend of a living tradition; foundational for the Meccan sanctuary and the hajj rites; paraphrased from the Arabic original.

passages.text: Ibrahim brought Hagar and her son Ismail and set them by the House, in a valley without sown land or water, and said: 'God has commanded me.' She asked, 'Then who will look after us?' He said, 'Your Lord.' And he went away; and she ran between the two hills, Safa and Marwa, seven times, seeking water for the child — and this, the legend says, is the rite of sa'y performed by every pilgrim since.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Tabari, Tarikh (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 易卜拉欣帶著哈哲爾和她的兒子易司馬儀，把他們安置在天房旁，一個沒有耕地也沒有水的山谷中，說道：『真主已命令我。』她問：『那麼誰來照顧我們呢？』他說：『你的主。』他便離去了；她在賽法和麥爾臥兩座山丘之間奔跑了七趟，為孩子尋水——傳說說，這便是此後每位朝覲者所行的賽儀之禮的由來。

passages.text: An angel struck the ground beside the child, and water burst up. Hagar scooped earth and dammed it, saying 'Zam, zam' — stay, stay; and the well of Zamzam was made. A caravan of Jurhum coming up the road saw a bird circling that never left the place — a sign of water — and asked Hagar leave to settle by the spring. She said, 'Yes, so long as you claim no right over the water.' They settled, and their children intermarried with Ismail's; and thus Mecca was founded, if the legend is believed.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Tabari, Tarikh (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 一位天使擊打孩子身旁的地面，水便湧了出來。哈哲爾捧起泥土把它堵住，說道『滲、滲』——停下、停下；滲滲泉便由此而成。一隊上路的朱爾胡姆人看見一隻鳥在此盤旋，從不離開此地——這是水的徵兆——便請求哈哲爾允許他們在泉邊定居。她說：『可以，只要你們不主張對水有任何權利。』他們便定居下來，他們的子女與易司馬儀的子女通婚；倘若這傳說可信，麥加便如此建立起來了。

title.en: The Martyrdom of Yahya
title.zh: 葉海雅之殉道

region.en: Jordan, Herod's court (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 約旦希律宮廷（象徵性定位）

period: Qisas al-Anbiya tradition (Arabic, al-Kisa'i); paraphrase from Arabic

source.archive: Wikisource (Arabic; al-Kisa’i, Qisas al-Anbiya, Leiden ed. 1922)
source.work: Muhammad al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic c. 1100); passages paraphrased from Arabic

license: Arabic original public domain; paraphrase original

summary.en: Herod the tetrarch loves a woman forbidden to him by the Torah, his brother's wife. Yahya preaches against it; the woman's daughter dances before the king, and the king promises her whatever she asks; she asks for the head of Yahya on a charger. The head is brought; it speaks no more, but the tradition says the blood cried out, and the ground where it fell still bubbles, if the legend is believed.
summary.zh: 分封王希律戀慕律法所禁之女子——其兄弟之妻。葉海雅講道反對；女子之女於王前起舞，王許諾無論何求；她求葉海雅之首於盤中。首級被呈；頭不再言語，但相傳其血鳴於地，血落之處至今汩汩，如傳說所信。

sensitivity.note: Qisas legend of a living tradition; the Yahya martyrdom is shared with Christian tradition; paraphrased from the Arabic original.

passages.text: Herod the tetrarch desired a woman whom the Torah forbade him, the wife of his brother; and Yahya, the son of Zakariyya, preached against it. The woman contrived that her daughter should dance before the king on his feast day, and the king swore before his guests to give her whatever she asked; and she asked for the head of Yahya on a charger.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 分封的王希律貪戀一個女子，就是托拉所禁止他的、他兄弟的妻子；而宰凱里雅的兒子葉哈雅曾就此宣講斥責。那女子設計讓自己的女兒在王設宴之日於王前跳舞，王便當著賓客起誓，凡她所求的都賜給她；她便求以盤盛上葉哈雅的頭。

passages.text: The head was brought in, and the king and his guests saw that it did not speak again; and the legend says that the blood cried out from the ground where it was spilled, and that the earth there bubbled up and has bubbled ever since, so that it was called the boiling ground. And God raised the soul of Yahya, and the prophets wept for him: 'There was not born among the children of Adam one more lawful in what he ate and more chaste than Yahya.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那頭被端了進來，王與賓客見它不再言語；傳說又說，那血從灑落之地呼喊起來，那地方的土地因而翻湧冒泡，自此一直冒泡不息，因此被稱為沸騰之地。真主升起了葉哈雅的靈魂，眾先知為他哀哭：『在阿丹的子孫中，未曾生出一個在飲食上比他更合律法、比他更貞潔的人。』

title.en: Dhul-Qarnayn and the Well of the Water of Life
title.zh: 左勒蓋爾奈英與生命之水井

region.en: Land of darkness, beyond the sunrise (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 日出之外的黑暗之地（象徵性定位）

period: Qisas al-Anbiya tradition (Arabic, al-Kisa'i); paraphrase from Arabic

source.archive: Wikisource (Arabic; al-Kisa’i, Qisas al-Anbiya, Leiden ed. 1922)
source.work: Muhammad al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic c. 1100); passages paraphrased from Arabic

license: Arabic original public domain; paraphrase original

summary.en: In the legend, Dhul-Qarnayn the two-horned comes at last to the land of darkness, where a well holds the water of life: whoever drinks shall not die. He enters with his cooks, each carrying a fish; the fish in one man's hand jumps into the water, and the man washes — and is granted age without end. Dhul-Qarnayn himself is not permitted: the voice tells him that death is written for him as for all. He builds his wall against Gog and Magog, and returns to his kingdom to wait for the appointed day — the Islamic cousin of Gilgamesh's plant, the quest of immortality that must fail.
summary.zh: 傳說中，雙角的左勒蓋爾奈英終至黑暗之地，其井中有生命之水：飲者不死。他攜廚師入內，各持一魚；一人手中之魚躍入水中，其人洗手——遂得不死之壽。左勒蓋爾奈英本人未蒙准許：有聲告知其死期已定，如眾人一樣。他築牆防雅朱者與馬朱者，返國等候注定之日——此即吉爾伽美什仙草的伊斯蘭親緣，注定失敗的求不死之旅。

sensitivity.note: Qisas legend; the water-of-life episode parallels the Gilgamesh quest-immortality cluster; paraphrased from the Arabic original; motif tagging cross-traditional and interpretive.

passages.text: Dhul-Qarnayn travelled until he came to the land of darkness, where it is said there is a well of the water of life: whoever drinks of it does not die. He entered it with his servants, each carrying a fish; and the fish in one man's hand leapt from it into the water, and the man washed his hand — and he was granted life that does not end.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 雙角王一路行去，直到來到黑暗之地，據說那裡有一口生命之水井：凡飲此水者不死。他與僕從進入其中，各人帶著一條魚；其中一人手中的魚躍入水中，那人便洗了手——於是他被賜予了無盡的生命。

passages.text: Dhul-Qarnayn himself was not permitted to drink: a voice said to him that death is written upon every son of Adam, and that his term was with his Lord. So he went out of the darkness and turned to the work God gave him — the wall of iron and copper between the peoples and Gog and Magog — and returned to his kingdom to await the appointed day. The legend makes him the seeker of the water of life who must fail, as the poets of Mesopotamia made Gilgamesh before him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 雙角王本人卻未蒙允許飲水：有聲音對他說，死亡寫在每一個阿丹子孫的身上，他的壽限在於他的主。於是他走出黑暗，轉而從事真主交託他的工作——在諸民族與雅朱者、馬朱者之間築起鐵與銅的牆——然後回到他的國度，等候那指定的日子。傳說使他成為尋求生命之水而必定失敗的人，正如美索不達米亞的詩人在他之前使吉爾伽美什如此。

title.en: The Staff of Musa: Cut From the Tree of Life
title.zh: 穆薩之杖：取自生命之樹

region.en: Garden of Eden and Tuwa (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伊甸園與圖窪（象徵性定位）

period: Qisas al-Anbiya tradition (Arabic, al-Kisa'i); paraphrase from Arabic

source.archive: Wikisource (Arabic; al-Kisa’i, Qisas al-Anbiya, Leiden ed. 1922)
source.work: Muhammad al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic c. 1100); passages paraphrased from Arabic

license: Arabic original public domain; paraphrase original

summary.en: The staff in Moses' hand, the legend says, is one of the trees of the Garden of Eden, brought down by Adam; the wood passed from prophet to prophet until God gave it to Musa, and with it the sign: cast it down and it becomes a serpent; strike the rock and twelve springs flow; part the sea with it. The staff passes out of the world when its work is done — the relic that binds Eden, Sinai and the Exodus in a single object.
summary.zh: 相傳穆薩手中之杖乃伊甸園諸樹之一，由阿丹帶下；此木自先知傳至先知，直至主賜穆薩；並賜其兆：擲之則化蛇；擊石則湧十二泉；持之分海。其功既成，杖遂離世——此一聖物將伊甸、西奈與出埃及繫於一物。

sensitivity.note: Qisas legend of a living tradition; the staff's Edenic origin is popular lore; paraphrased from the Arabic original.

passages.text: The staff that Musa carried, the legend says, was cut from one of the trees of the Garden of Eden, and brought down by Adam when he was expelled; and the wood was handed down from prophet to prophet, from Adam to Idris to Nuh, until God gave it to Musa in the valley of Tuwa.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 據傳說，穆薩所持的手杖取自伊甸園中的一棵樹，是阿丹被逐出時帶下來的；那木頭由先知代代相傳，從阿丹傳到易德里斯，再傳到努哈，直到真主在圖瓦山谷把它賜給穆薩。

passages.text: With it God gave him his signs: cast it down before Pharaoh and it becomes a serpent that swallows the serpents of the magicians; strike the rock with it and twelve springs gush out, one for each tribe; stretch it over the sea and the waters stand like walls. And when the work of Musa was finished the staff went out of the world, and is not found — for it was, the legend says, the last relic of the Garden among men.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Kisa'i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 真主藉它賜給他種種蹟象：把它丟在法老面前，它就變成一條蛇，吞下術士們的蛇；用它擊打磐石，便有十二道泉水湧出，每一支族一道；把它伸在海面上，海水便如牆壁般立起。及至穆薩的事工完成，那手杖便離開了世間，再也尋不見——因為據傳說，它是園中留在人間的最後一件遺物。

title.en: Wang T'ai the Toeless Teacher (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 兀者王駘（莊子）

region.en: The State of Lu (Qufu, Shandong, China)
region.zh: 魯國（今山東曲阜）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 5, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 5

summary.en: In Lu lives Wang T'ai, a mutilated man with as many disciples as Confucius himself, who neither preaches nor discusses yet sends those who come empty away full. Confucius calls him a prophet: from the point of view of sameness all things are one, and the discrepancy of his toes is to him as the loss of so much mud — for a man does not seek to see himself in running water, but in still water.
summary.zh: 魯有兀者王駘，從之遊者與仲尼相若；立不教，坐不議，虛而往實而歸。夫子曰：自其同者視之，萬物皆一也；人莫鑒於流水，而鑒於止水。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: In the State of Lu there was a man, named Wang T'ai, who had had his toes cut off. His disciples were as numerous as those of Confucius. Ch'ang Chi asked Confucius, saying, "This Wang T'ai has been mutilated, yet he divides with you, Sir, the teaching of the Lu State. He neither preaches nor discusses; yet those who go to him empty, depart full. He must teach the doctrine which does not find expression in words; and although his shape is imperfect, his mind is perhaps complete. What manner of man is this?"
passages.zh: 魯國有一個人，名叫王駘，被砍去了腳趾。他的門徒人數與孔子的門徒一樣多。常季問孔子說：「這個王駘是個受過刑戮的人，可是他在魯國與先生您分庭抗禮，傳授學問。他既不講說也不議論；然而那些空手前去的人，卻滿載而歸。他必定是傳授那不藉言語表達的道理；雖然他的形體殘缺，他的心性或許是完備的。這是怎樣的一個人呢？」

passages.text: "He is a prophet," replied Confucius, "whose instruction I have been late in seeking. I will go and learn from him. And if I,--why not those who are not equal to me? And I will take with me, not the State of Lu only, but the whole world." "The fellow has been mutilated," said Ch'ang Chi, "and yet people call him Master. He must be very different from the ordinary run. But how does he use his mind in this sense?"
passages.zh: 孔子回答說：「他是一位先知，我尋訪他的教誨已經太遲了。我要前去向他學習。而且連我尚且如此——何況那些不如我的人呢？我要帶著的不只是魯國，而是整個天下。」常季說：「這人受過刑戮，可是人們卻稱他為夫子。他必定與常人極為不同。但他究竟是怎樣運用他的心的呢？」

passages.text: "From the point of view of difference," replied Confucius, "we distinguish between the liver and the gall, between the Ch'u State and the Yüeh State. From the point of view of sameness, all things are ONE. Such is the position of Wang T'ai. He does not trouble about what reaches him through the senses of hearing and sight, but directs his whole mind towards the very climax of virtue. He beholds all things as though ONE, without observing their discrepancies. And thus the discrepancy of his toes is to him as would be the loss of so much mud."
passages.zh: 孔子回答說：「從相異的觀點來看，我們分辨肝與膽，分辨楚國與越國。從相同的觀點來看，萬物都是一體的。這就是王駘的立場。他不理會那些經由耳聞目見而來到他身上的事物，而是把整個心靈導向德性的極致。他把萬物都看作一體，而不去計較它們之間的差異。因此，他腳趾的殘缺，對他來說就如同失去了一些泥土一般。」

passages.text: "A man," replied Confucius, "does not seek to see himself in running water, but in still water. For only what is itself still can instil stillness into others. ... Besides, he awaits his appointed hour, and men flock to him of their own accord. He makes no effort to attract them."
passages.zh: 孔子回答說：「人不會在流動的水中照見自己，而是在靜止的水中照見自己。因為只有本身靜止的，才能把靜止傳授給他人。……此外，他等待著他命定的時刻，人們便自動聚集到他身邊。他並不費力去吸引他們。」

title.en: No-toes Defends the Fetters of the Sage (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 兀者叔山無趾（莊子）

region.en: The State of Lu (Qufu, Shandong, China)
region.zh: 魯國（今山東曲阜）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 5, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 5

summary.en: The mutilated Shu Shan No-toes comes walking on his heels to Confucius, who rebukes him for his past carelessness; he answers that he comes with something more precious than toes. Later he tells Lao Tzŭ that Confucius aims at dialectical reputation — the fetters of a criminal — and Lao Tzŭ bids him meet the Sage with the continuity of life and death; No-toes answers that God has already punished him and it would be impossible to release him.
summary.zh: 叔山無趾踵見仲尼；曰：猶有尊足者存。見老聃曰：孔子之於德，未至者也；名聞，桎梏也。老聃曰：胡不使死生為一條，以是為一貫，解其桎梏？

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: There was a man of the Lu State who had been mutilated,--Shu Shan No-toes. He came walking on his heels to see Confucius; but Confucius said, "You did not take care, and so brought this misfortune upon yourself. What is the use of coming to me now?" "In my ignorance," replied No-toes, "I made free with my body and lost my toes. But I come with something more precious than toes which I now seek to keep. There is no man, but Heaven covers him: there is no man, but Earth supports him;--and I thought that you, sir, would be as Heaven and Earth. I little expected to hear these words from you."
passages.zh: 魯國有一個受過刑戮的人——叔山無趾。他用腳跟走著路來見孔子；可是孔子說：「你不謹慎自愛，才招來這般不幸。如今來見我又有什麼用呢？」無趾回答說：「我因無知，輕率地對待自己的身體，因而失去了腳趾。但我帶著比腳趾更為珍貴的東西而來，如今我想要保全它。沒有哪一個人，不是天所覆蓋的；沒有哪一個人，不是地所承載的——我以為先生您會像天地一樣。我實在沒料到會從您口中聽到這樣的話。」

passages.text: No-toes went off to Lao Tzŭ and said, "Is Confucius a sage, or is he not? How is it he has so many disciples? He aims at being a subtle dialectician, not knowing that such a reputation is regarded by real sages as the fetters of a criminal." "Why do you not meet him with the continuity of life and death, the identity of can and can not," answered Lao Tzŭ, "and so release him from these fetters?" "He has been thus punished by God," replied No-toes. "It would be impossible to release him."
passages.zh: 無趾去見老子，說：「孔子是聖人，還是不是？他怎麼會有這麼多門徒？他致力於成為一個精微的辯者，卻不知道這樣的聲名被真正的聖人看作是罪犯的枷鎖。」老子回答說：「你為什麼不以生死的一貫、可與不可的同一來與他相見，從而使他從這些枷鎖中解脫出來呢？」無趾回答說：「他是被上天這樣懲罰的。要使他解脫，是不可能的。」

title.en: Ai T'ai T'o the Leper and the Litter of Pigs (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 哀駘它與彘子食於其死母（莊子）

region.en: The Wei court (Anyang region, Henan, China)
region.zh: 衛宮（今河南安陽一帶）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 5, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 5

summary.en: Duke Ai of Lu marvels at the loathsome leper Ai T'ai T'o whom women and men alike crowd around. Confucius tells him of the litter of pigs that left their dead mother's body when she no longer looked at them: what they loved was not the body but that which made the body what it was. Talent perfect and virtue without outward form is a water-level — water at perfect repose.
summary.zh: 衛有惡人哀駘它；夫子言：丘也嘗遊於楚，見豚子之食於其死母者，皆棄之而走——所愛其母者，非愛其形也，愛使其形者也。德不形者，物不能離也。平者，水停之盛也。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the dead-mother piglets episode is a classic Taoist meditation on form and animating spirit, tagged resurrection as a comparative (non-narrative) analogue. Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: Duke Ai of the Lu State said to Confucius, "In the Wei State there is a leper, named Ai T'ai T'o. The men who live with him like him and make no effort to get rid of him. Of the women who have seen him, many have said to their parents, Rather than be another man's wife, I would be his concubine. He never preaches at people, but puts himself into sympathy with them. He wields no power by which he may protect men's bodies. He has at his disposal no appointments by which to gratify their hearts. He is loathsome to a degree. He sympathises, but does not instruct. His knowledge is limited to his own State. Yet males and females alike all congregate around him.
passages.zh: 魯國哀公對孔子說：「衛國有一個駝背畸形的人，名叫哀駘它。與他相處的男子都喜歡他，捨不得離開他。見過他的女子，許多都對父母說：『與其做別人的妻子，我寧願做他的妾。』他從不向人說教，只是與人相感相通。他沒有權勢可以保護人的身體，也沒有俸祿官位可以滿足人的心意。他的形貌醜陋至極。他與人相感，卻不教導人。他的見識只限於本國。然而男男女女都聚集在他身邊。」

passages.text: "When I was on a mission to the Ch'u State," replied Confucius, "I saw a litter of young pigs sucking their dead mother. After a while they looked at her, and then they all left the body and went off. For their mother did not look at them any more, nor did she any more seem to be of their kind. What they loved was their mother; not the body which contained her, but that which made the body what it was.
passages.zh: 孔子回答說：「我出使楚國時，看見一窩小豬在吮吸死去的母豬。過了一會兒，牠們看了看母豬，便都離開屍體走開了。因為牠們的母親不再看牠們，也不再像是牠們的同類了。牠們所愛的是牠們的母親；不是那承載母親的形體，而是那使形體成為形體的東西。」

passages.text: "Life and Death," replied Confucius, "existence and non-existence, success and non-success, poverty and wealth, virtue and vice, good and evil report, hunger and thirst, warmth and cold,--these all revolve upon the changing wheel of Destiny. Day and night they follow one upon the other, and no man can say where each one begins. ... In a water-level," said Confucius, "the water is in a most perfect state of repose. Let that be your model. The water remains quietly within, and does not overflow. It is from the cultivation of such harmony that virtue results. And if virtue takes no outward form, man will not be able to keep aloof from it."
passages.zh: 孔子回答說：「生與死、存在與不存在、成功與不成功、貧窮與富有、德行與過失、善與惡的名聲、飢與渴、暖與寒——這些都在命運變化的輪子上旋轉。日夜相繼，沒有人能說出每一項從何處開始。……孔子說：『在水準之中，水處於最完美的靜止狀態。讓那成為你的榜樣。水靜靜地留在裡面，不會溢出。正是從培養這樣的和諧中產生德行。而如果德行不顯露於外，人便無法與它疏遠。』」

title.en: Shên T'u Chia and the Minister's Slippers (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 申徒嘉與子產（莊子）

region.en: The Chêng court (Zhengzhou, Henan, China)
region.zh: 鄭廷（今河南鄭州）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 5, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 5

summary.en: The Minister Tzŭ Ch'an will not walk out of class with his mutilated fellow-student Shên T'u Chia and demands precedence. The toeless man answers that a bright mirror gathers no dust; that he who studies under the Master nineteen years has ceased to feel the loss of his toes; and that he who would stand before the bull's-eye while Hou I shoots would be hit — and if not hit, it would be destiny. Tzŭ Ch'an changes countenance and begs him to say no more.
summary.zh: 申徒嘉，兀者也，與子產同師於伯昏無人。子產讓其先出；嘉曰：鑒明則塵垢不止。自狀其過以不當亡者眾；不狀其過以不當存者寡。遊於羿之彀中，中央者，中地也；然而不中者，命也。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); tagged oracle-divination for the Hou-I bull's-eye destiny figure (interpretive). Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: "Dear me!" replied Shên T'u Chia, "I didn't know we had a Minister of State in the class. Perhaps you think that because you are one you should take precedence over the rest. Now I have heard that if a mirror is perfectly bright, dust and dirt will not collect on it. That if they do, it is because the mirror was not bright. He who associates for long with the wise will be without fault. Now you have been improving yourself at the feet of our Master, yet you can utter words like these. Is not the fault in you?"
passages.zh: 申徒嘉回答說：「哎呀！我不知道我們這一班裡還有個執政大臣。也許你以為因為你是執政大臣，就該排在別人前面。我聽說，鏡子如果完全明亮，灰塵污垢就不會積在上面。如果積在上面，那是因為鏡子不明亮。與賢人長久相處的人，不會有過失。如今你在我們老師門下修養自己，卻能說出這樣的話。這過失不就在你身上嗎？」

passages.text: "To recognise the inevitable and to quietly acquiesce in Destiny, is the achievement of the virtuous man alone. He who should put himself in front of the bull's-eye when Hou I was shooting, would be hit. If he was not hit, it would be destiny. Those with toes who laugh at me for having no toes are many. This used to make me angry. But since I have studied under our Master, I have ceased to trouble about it. It may be that our Master has so far succeeded in purifying me. At any rate I have been with him nineteen years without being aware of the loss of my toes." At this Tzŭ Ch'an began to fidget, and changing countenance, begged Shên T'u Chia to say no more.
passages.zh: 「認清不可避免的事，並安然順從命運，這只有有德之人才能做到。若有人站在后羿射箭的靶心之前，就會被射中。如果沒有被射中，那就是命運。腳趾齊全的人譏笑我沒有腳趾的很多。這過去常使我發怒。但自從我在我們老師門下學習以來，我已不再為此煩擾。也許我們老師已經在某種程度上使我純淨了。無論如何，我跟隨他十九年，卻不曾察覺自己失去了腳趾。」聽到這裡，子產開始坐立不安，改變了臉色，請求申徒嘉不要再說下去。

title.en: The Six Days and the Seven Heavens (Qur'an)
title.zh: 六日與七重天（古蘭經）

region.en: Mecca / Medina recitation contexts (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥加／麥地那誦經語境（象徵性定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; canonical rasm fixed under Uthman c. 650 CE; tafsir tradition from al-Tabari (d. 923 CE)

source.work: Qur'an 41:9-12; 7:54; 50:38; 25:59 (Arabic text; English: J. M. Rodwell, The Koran, 1861)

license: Arabic text public domain; Rodwell 1861 translation public domain

summary.en: The Lord who created the heavens and the earth in six days — 'and His throne was upon the water' — made the heavens as seven stories and adorned the lowest with lamps. The earth was spread like a carpet, the mountains cast down as weights, and every goodly thing appointed in pairs. He rose over the throne: 'Say: ask Him who created the heavens and the earth — is He not better than that which they worship?'
summary.zh: 主於六日中造天地——『其寶座原在水上』——造七層天，以燈飾最近之天。地如毯鋪展，山為重錘鎮壓，美善之物皆成雙配對。他升於寶座之上：『你說：造天地者——豈非勝過你們所拜者？』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; translations are interpretations, and only public-domain translations are quoted with the Arabic as primary. 'Six days' in the Qur'an (41:9-12) is compared by exegetes with the Biblical week; the Qur'an does not say God rested.

narrative.en:
The Qur'an speaks of creation not as a story told once but as a set of sayings scattered through the revelation, each answering a different need. To the Meccans who worshipped many gods it says: ask yourselves who made the heavens and the earth in six days — 'Ask them: is it they who created the heavens and the earth, or are they stronger in creation?' (52:35-36). The earliest account runs: 'Your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and then mounted the throne; He makes the night enfold the day, pursuing it ceaselessly; the sun and the moon and the stars are made subject to His command' (7:54). A second passage gives the order: 'Say: do you disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and set up equals to Him? He made therein firm mountains and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, alike for those who ask. Then He mounted to the heaven, while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: come ye, willingly or unwillingly. They said: we come willingly. And He completed them seven heavens in two days, and revealed in every heaven its command; and We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps, and made it a guard' (41:9-12).

The keynote of the account is measure: the earth is a carpet spread out, the mountains are pegs driven in to keep it from shifting under the inhabitants; the heaven is raised without pillars that you can see, and the water cycle is the mercy by which the dead land is revived. The spirit is breathed into man of God's own breath; the angels are made of light, and jinn of smokeless fire; and the first man is taught the names of all things. Creation is an act of command — 'Be' — not of labour: when the unbelievers taunt God with weariness after creating the heavens and the earth, the answer is that a day with the Lord is as a thousand years of your reckoning, and that weariness does not touch Him; the Qur'an says expressly that He created in six days and 'did not feel wearied' (50:38).

In the exegetical tradition the days are variously reckoned; al-Tabari reports that they are days of the unseen order, not the days of this earth; al-Biruni, the eleventh-century astronomer, discusses the question in his Chronology and notes that the six days of the Qur'an are not six solar days but six periods, so that the age of the world is a matter of the divine command rather than of the sun's circuit. The throne upon the water is a proof-text for the theologians of the divine superiority: the water existed first, beneath the throne, and the heavens and the earth were brought forth from it in the appointed measure. The seven heavens are the storeys of a tower of command, each with its own law; the lowest is adorned with lamps — the stars — and guarded against the satans who seek to listen. In the popular qisas the whole of creation is gathered into a single week of wonders, the week ending with the creation of Adam on Friday, the day of the great assembly; the theologians hold instead that the days are six periods and that their order is a mystery of the command.

Culturally, the creation sayings of the Qur'an function as the ground of worship: the daily prayers turn to the East because the sun and the moon are made subject to command; the fast of Ramadan is timed by the moon because the moon is one of the measured things; and the sabbath-like rest is absent precisely because God does not rest — the world runs on His command without weariness, and the Muslim's week has no day of divine repose.
narrative.zh: 古蘭經以散見各章的言述講創造：『你們的主是造天地於六日的主，然後升於寶座；夜追逐晝，絡繹不絕；日月星辰皆受其命』。地如毯鋪展，山為釘鎮，天無柱而升；『主造之而毫無倦意』。七重天各有其律；最近之天飾以燈。『其寶座原在水上』。經注家解六日為主之時期，非地上之日。

functions: Grounds the five daily prayers in the cosmic order (sun and moon subject to command)
Provides the doctrine of divine measure (qadar): creation in appointed proportions, not chance
Serves as the principal argument against idolatry: none of the gods can create
Frames the Islamic week: no day of divine rest, since God does not weary

variants.name: Tabari's tafsir on 41:9-12
variants.summary: The days are 'days of the unseen order'; the throne on the water precedes the earth; the heavens are completed in two days after four.

variants.name: Al-Biruni, Chronology of Ancient Nations (Sachau 1879)
variants.summary: The six days are six periods, not solar days; Biruni reconciles the Qur'anic week with the astrological week of the Persians and Greeks.

variants.name: Popular qisas week
variants.summary: Creation retold as a week of wonders with Adam made on Friday, the day of assembly.

canonical_translation: J. M. Rodwell, The Koran (1861); E. H. Palmer, The Qur'an (Sacred Books of the East, 1880)

primary_sources.citation: Surahs 41:9-12, 7:54, 50:38, 25:59, 52:35-36 (Arabic rasm, c. 650 CE; English: Rodwell 1861)

primary_sources.work: al-Biruni, Al-Athar al-Baqiya (Chronology of Ancient Nations)
primary_sources.citation: ed. & trans. C. E. Sachau, London 1879, sections on the creation days

secondary_sources.work: al-Tabari, Jami' al-Bayan (Tafsir)
secondary_sources.citation: al-Tabari (d. 923), commentary on 41:9-12 and 7:54; Arabic, Bulaq ed.

Al-Kisa’i, Qisas al-Anbiya (Arabic text, Wikisource; Leiden ed. 1922, public domain)

sensitivity_guidance: The Qur'an is the literal word of God within Islam; all English renderings are interpretations. Records present the text in public-domain translation with the Arabic as primary and avoid doctrinal commentary.

passages.text: Your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and then mounted the throne; He makes the night enfold the day, pursuing it ceaselessly; and the sun and the moon and the stars are made subject to His command. ... It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a reflected light.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:54; 10:5 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim; ellipsis marks omitted clause.
passages.zh: 你們的主是真主，他在六日內創造了天地，然後升上寶座；他使黑夜籠罩白晝，黑夜不停地追隨白晝；太陽、月亮和星辰都服從他的命令。……是他使太陽成為發光的光體，使月亮成為反射的光。

passages.text: Say: do you disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and set up equals to Him? He made therein firm mountains and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, alike for those who ask. Then He mounted to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: Come, willingly or unwillingly! They said: We come willingly. And He made seven heavens in two days, and revealed in every heaven its command; and We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps for watchfulness. Such is the ordaining of the Mighty, the Knowing.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 41:9-12 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你說：你們不信那在兩日內創造大地、並為祂設立同等者之主嗎？祂在其中安置穩固的山岳，並賜福於它，又在四日內量定其中的給養，對於詢問者皆然。然後祂升臨於天，那時天還是煙霧，祂對天與地說：你們順從或違逆，都要來！它們說：我們情願順從而來。祂在兩日內造化了七重天，並在每一重天中啟示其命令；我們以燈盞裝飾最低的天，作為守望之用。這是那萬能者、全知者的安排。

passages.text: And He created the heavens and the earth in six days — and His throne was upon the water — that He might try which of you is the best in deeds; ... We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no weariness touched Us; and the angels celebrate the praise of their Lord.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 11:7; 50:38 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 祂在六日內創造了諸天與大地——那時祂的寶座在水上——以便考驗你們之中誰的行為最善；……我們在六日內創造了諸天、大地以及它們之間的一切，疲倦未曾觸及我們；眾天使讚頌他們的主。

title.en: Nuh and the Flood: The Ark, the Son, and the Wave
title.zh: 努哈與洪水：方舟、其子與巨浪

region.en: Mesopotamian plain and Mount Judi (traditional landing; literal pin)
region.zh: 美索不達米亞平原與朱迪山（傳統停靠地；實際定位）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs Hud 11:25-49, Nuh 71, al-Qamar 54:9-17; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Suras 11:25-49 and 71

license: Arabic text public domain; Rodwell 1861 translation public domain

summary.en: Noah is sent to his people who serve five idols; he builds the Ark while they mock, and boards it with the believers and a pair of every species. His own son refuses the call — 'I will take refuge in a mountain that will save me from the water' — and the wave passes between father and son. The fountains of the great deep are burst, the earth's valleys stream; the Ark is said to have rested on Judi, and the last word: 'Peace on Nuh among all creatures.'
summary.zh: 努哈被遣至拜五偶像之民；他造方舟而受嘲，攜信士及各類成雙之獸登舟。其親子拒召——『我將避於能救我的山』——巨浪從父子之間經過。大淵的泉源盡裂，山谷奔流；相傳方舟停於朱迪山。末語：『願平安歸於努哈，在眾世界之間。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the flood of Nuh is a cardinal narrative shared with the Biblical deluge; presented in public-domain translation.

narrative.en:
Noah is the first of the great warners of the Qur'an. He is sent to his people, who worship the idols Wadd, Suwa, Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr; he calls them night and day, and they put their fingers in their ears. He says: 'I am to you a plain warner: serve God and fear Him and obey me; He will forgive you your sins and respite you to an appointed term; but the term of God when it comes is not deferred — did you but know it.' The chiefs answer: 'You are no more than a man like us; you wish to turn us from what our fathers worshipped; bring the punishment you promise if you speak truth.'

Then comes the command of God: 'Build the Ark under Our eyes and Our revelation, and do not speak to Me for the wrongdoers; they shall be drowned.' Noah builds in the open, and the people laugh as they pass: 'What do you build?' — 'An ark; you will know.' The waters come. 'Load into it of every species two by two, and your family, except those against whom the word has gone before; and do not speak to Me for those who have done wrong.' The fountains of the great deep are burst open and the windows of heaven opened, and the earth's valleys stream together. Noah calls to his son, who had kept apart: 'Embark with us, my son, and be not with the unbelievers.' The son answers: 'I will take refuge on a mountain that will save me from the water.' 'There is no safety this day from the command of God, except for him on whom He has mercy' — and the wave passes between the two, and the son is among the drowned.

The Ark runs with them between waves like mountains. Noah calls to his son who is riding apart: 'Embark with us.' 'I will take refuge in a mountain.' 'There is no refuge today from the command of God except for him on whom He has mercy.' And the wave comes between them. When the command comes and the oven — the tannur — boils over, the sign of the end, the earth's valleys stream together: 'We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring down, and made the earth to gush forth with fountains, and the waters met, as was the matter decreed. And We bore him on a vessel of planks and nails, which ran under Our eyes — a reward for him who had been disbelieved. And We left it a sign: is there then any that will be mindful?'

The flood rises and covers all, and the Ark is carried until it rests, the tradition says, on Judi — the mountain of the north Mesopotamian border. Noah calls to his Lord: 'My Lord, my son is of my family, and Thy promise is true.' The answer is the severest lesson of the story: 'He is not of thy family; he hath wrought a work that is not right. Ask Me not for what thou knowest not; I admonish thee lest thou become one of the ignorant.' 'My Lord, I take refuge with Thee, lest I ask Thee that whereof I have no knowledge.' Then comes the end: 'Depart in peace, Nuh, and blessings on thee and on the nations that spring from those with thee; and blessings on some of them, but the rest shall be suffered to go astray.' The story closes with the formula of peace: 'Peace on Nuh among all creatures' — and with the promise that this is a warning to the world: the flood is both judgement and renewal, the washing of the earth for a new people.

Culturally the story stands behind the Qur'anic doctrine of the messengers: every prophet tells his people the same three things — worship God alone, fear the Day, follow the guide — and every people answers with the same refusal. The flood of Nuh is the archetype of the destroyed generations (Aad, Thamud, Lut's people, the people of Shu'ayb), and its remembrance is built into the calendar of Muslim practice: the fast of Ashura, the tenth of Muharram, is kept in the tradition in memory of the day the Ark came to rest.
narrative.zh: 努哈是古蘭經第一位大警誡者。其民拜瓦德、素瓦、葉巫斯、葉歐克與奈斯爾；他日夜呼喚，他們以指塞耳。主諭：『造舟於我鑒與我啟示之下；勿為不義者代求，他們必被淹死。』眾人譏笑；舟成，『各類成雙而載，你的家眷——惟此前已被判決者除外』。大淵泉源裂，天門開，山谷奔流。其子拒登：『我將避於一山』——『今日主之命令，非蒙慈者無人可避』——巨浪經於父子之間。舟載於波峰如山之間，停於朱迪山。努哈求其子；主諭：『他非你的家眷；勿問你不知道的事。』結語：『平安歸於努哈，在眾世界之間。』阿舒拉日之齋，相傳紀念方舟靠岸之日。

functions: Archetype of the destroyed generations: grounds the Qur'anic pattern of messenger, refusal, judgement
Establishes the doctrine that kinship is not salvation: 'he is not of thy family'
Remembrance in the fast of Ashura, kept in memory of the Ark's resting
Underlies the ethic of da'wa (calling) under mockery: build, and wait

passages.text: Build the Ark under Our eyes and Our revelation, and do not speak to Me for the wrongdoers; they shall be drowned. ... Load into it of every species two by two, and your family, except those against whom the word has gone before; and do not speak to Me for those who have done wrong.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 11:37, 40 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim; ellipsis marks omitted verse.
passages.zh: 你要在我們的看顧與啟示之下建造方舟，不要為不義者向我求情；他們必將被淹沒。……你要將每種生物各一對載入舟中，並載上你的家屬，除了那已先有判詞臨及者；不要為那些行惡的人向我求情。

passages.text: Noah called to his son, who had kept apart: Embark with us, and be not with the unbelievers! He said: I will betake me to a mountain that shall secure me from the water. He said: There is no security today from the decree of God, except for him on whom He shall have mercy; and a wave passed between them, and he was among the drowned. And it was said: O Earth, swallow up thy water; and, O heaven, withhold thy rain. And the waters abated, and the decree was fulfilled, and the Ark rested upon Al-Judi.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 11:42-44 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 努哈呼喚他那獨自離去的兒子：與我們一同登舟吧，不要與不信道者同伍！他說：我將登上山去，那山能使我免於水患。他說：今日除了蒙祂憐憫者外，無人能免於真主的判決；一個波浪在他們之間經過，他便成了被淹沒者之一。於是有人說：大地啊，吞下你的水吧；天啊，收起你的雨吧。水便退去，判決得以完成，方舟停泊在朱迪山上。

passages.text: It was said: O Noah, disembark in peace from Us, and blessings on you and on the peoples with you; but there shall be people whom we will suffer to enjoy a brief respite. This is a history of the cities which We narrate to you; some are standing, and others have been cut off. Noah cried: My Lord, leave not one family of the unbelievers on the earth! For if Thou leave them, they will seduce Thy servants and will beget none but ungrateful sinners.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 11:48-49; 71:26-27 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有人說：努哈啊，你平安地從我們這裡下舟吧，願福澤降於你和你同行的各民族；但也有一些民族，我們將讓他們短暫享受，然後加以懲罰。這是那些城鎮的消息，我們向你敘述；有些仍然存在，有些已被割除。努哈呼喊說：我的主啊，求你不要在大地上留下一個不信道的家庭！因為你若留下他們，他們必將誘惑你的僕人，只會生出忘恩負義的罪人。

title.en: The Night Journey and Ascension (Isra and Mi'raj)
title.zh: 夜行與登霄（伊斯拉與米爾拉吉）

region.en: Mecca to Jerusalem to the seven heavens (route pin at Jerusalem)
region.zh: 自麥加至耶路撒冷至七重天（路線定位於耶路撒冷）

period: Event placed c. 619-621 CE; recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab as-Salat, no. 349); hadith narrative tradition

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab as-Salat, no. 349 — the Hadith of the Night Journey, narrated by Anas ibn Malik; Qur'an 17:1

license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Carried by Buraq from the Kaaba to 'the farthest mosque' of Jerusalem, Muhammad leads the prophets in prayer; then from the Rock he is taken up through the heavens: he meets Adam, Yahya and Isa, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa and Ibrahim; sees Paradise and Hell; receives the command of fifty prayers, negotiated down to five. In the morning he tells his story in Mecca; Abu Bakr believes him at once, and the mosque of Jerusalem and the five prayers are the legacy of the night.
summary.zh: 乘布拉克由天房至耶路撒冷『遠寺』；先知率眾先知禮拜；後自磐石登七重天：遇阿丹、葉海雅與爾撒、優素福、易德里斯、哈倫、穆薩與易卜拉欣；見樂園與火獄；受五十拜之命，經折衷定為五拜。晨返麥加述其事；阿布·伯克爾即刻相信；耶路撒冷之寺與五番拜乃那一夜之遺產。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; the Night Journey is a cardinal miracle. Presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; no doctrinal commentary.

narrative.en:
In the year of sorrows, after the deaths of Khadija and Abu Talib, the Prophet was taken by night from the Sacred Mosque of Mecca to 'the farthest mosque' — al-Aqsa, in Jerusalem — on a white steed, Buraq, 'long as a mule and higher than a donkey, whose stride reached as far as the eye could see.' At Jerusalem he tethered Buraq at the Rock, and led the prophets of God in prayer: the meeting of the envoys of the old covenant with the Seal.

Then he was taken up. From the first heaven, guarded by an angel, he met Adam; in the second, Yahya and Isa, cousins and relatives of the Word; in the third, Yusuf, given half of beauty; in the fourth, Idris; in the fifth, Harun with his white beard; in the sixth, Musa, weeping — because, he said, a young man will enter Paradise after me, and more of his people than of mine; in the seventh, Ibrahim, sitting with his back against the Bait al-Ma'mur, the House of the Frequented, where seventy thousand angels pray every day and do not return. And above the seventh heaven he saw Sidrat al-Muntaha, the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, whose fruits are like great jars and its leaves like elephants' ears; and beyond it the divine majesty: 'And I was given three things: the five prayers, the last verses of Surah al-Baqarah, and the pardon of my people who die not joining aught with God.'

The command that came down was fifty prayers a day. On the way back Musa stopped him: 'Your people will not bear it; go back and ask for less.' Between the Throne and the Prophet the toll went down to five, and Musa still said, 'Go back'; but the Prophet said: 'I am ashamed before God; I will not go back again.' Then a voice said: 'Five prayers, and they are as fifty: the word is not changed before Me.'

In the morning he told the story in Mecca, and the Quraysh mocked: a caravan returns from Syria in ten days, and Muhammad says he went to Jerusalem by night and back before dawn. Abu Bakr answered at once: 'If he says so, it is true' — and was called al-Siddiq, the Verifier. The tradition adds the answer of the Prophet: as he rode, caravans passed him; he told the Quraysh where they were, and the news, checked, confirmed him. The legacy of the night is twofold: the five daily prayers, whose number was settled in the ascent, and the sanctity of Jerusalem, whose farthest mosque is the qibla of the first years and the third sanctuary of Islam.

The Isra and Mi'raj stand in the cross-tradition company of the seer's ascensions — Ezekiel's chariot-throne, Arda Viraf's tour of heaven and hell, Er's vision at the end of Plato's Republic — but with its own centre: the Prophet does not see his own soul's fate; he intercedes, and the number of prayers is the outcome. In Sufism the Mi'raj becomes the model of the mystic's own ascent; in popular devotion the 27th of Rajab is kept as the Night of the Ascension; and in the Qur'an the night is covered by a single verse — 'Glory to Him who carried His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose precincts We have blessed, to show him of Our signs' (17:1) — with the ascent alluded to in the Sura of the Star: 'He saw him in another descent, at the Lote-Tree of the Boundary, near which is the Garden of Refuge.'
narrative.zh: 憂傷之年，先知夜間乘白騸布拉克——『其奔馳及目力所及』——自麥加禁寺至耶路撒冷遠寺。繫驂於磐石，率眾先知禮拜。隨後登霄：第一天遇阿丹；第二天遇葉海雅與爾撒；第三天遇優素福；第四天遇易德里斯；第五天遇哈倫；第六天遇穆薩——因見其後進樂園者更多而泣；第七天遇易卜拉欣，倚於日日有七萬天使禮拜的『常訪之殿』。其上見極境之酸棗樹，果如大甕、葉如象耳；受賜三事：五番拜、黃牛章末數節、及不以物配主而亡者的赦宥。降命五十拜；穆薩屢勸求減，至五拜而先知言：『我於主前羞愧，不復往矣。』有聲曰：『五拜同於五十拜，主前之言不變。』晨返麥加述之，古萊氏譏之；阿布·伯克爾即信，被稱為『誠信者』。那一夜的遺產：五番拜與耶路撒冷的聖所地位。

functions: Establishes the five daily prayers, whose number was fixed during the ascent
Consecrates Jerusalem as the third sanctuary of Islam and first qibla
Model of the Sufi ascent: the mystic's journey follows the Prophet's Mi'raj
Kept in popular devotion as Laylat al-Mi'raj, the 27th of Rajab

Rodwell's Koran (1861), for Qur'an 17:1 and 53

passages.text: Glory be to Him who carried His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose precincts We have blessed, that We might show him of Our signs; He it is who hears and sees. The Prophet is mounted on Buraq, the steed with the face of a woman and the body of a horse, guided by Gabriel; he leads the prophets in prayer at Jerusalem — Abraham, Moses, Jesus — then is raised through the seven heavens, where he meets the fathers of the faith at each gate, until above the Lote-tree of the boundary he draws near 'as two bow-shots or nearer', and the prayer is enjoined upon the believers, fifty bowed down to five by the intercession of Moses.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 17:1 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of the Isra and Mi'raj hadith tradition; not verbatim; composite of Bukhari/Muslim narratives as summarized.
passages.zh: 讚頌那在夜間帶著祂的僕人從禁寺行至遠寺的主，我們已賜福其四周，以便我們向他顯示我們的跡象；祂確是聽聞的、明察的。先知騎著布拉克，那是有著女子面容、馬匹身軀的坐騎，由吉卜利勒引導；他在耶路撒冷率領眾先知禮拜——易卜拉欣、穆薩、爾撒——然後被升上七重天，在每一道門處與信仰的先祖相會，直到在極界的酸棗樹之上，他接近「如兩弓之距或更近」，於是禮拜被規定於信士，由穆薩的求情，從五十番減為五番。

passages.text: Muhammad said: While I was at the House in a state between sleep and wakefulness, an angel came to me and split open my breast, and washed it with the water of Zamzam in a basin of gold; then a white animal was brought, between a mule and an ass, and I was set upon it, and Gabriel went with me to the Farthest Mosque, and thence upward; and I saw paradise and the fire.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Mi'raj hadith tradition; not verbatim; paraphrased from the classical accounts.
passages.zh: 穆罕默德說：當我在天房之中，處於半睡半醒之間，一位天使來到我面前，剖開我的胸膛，用金盆中的滲滲泉水洗滌它；隨後牽來一頭白色的牲畜，介於騾與驢之間，我被扶上牠，加百列與我同行，前往遠寺，再從那裡升上；我看見了樂園與火獄。

title.en: The Day of Judgment: The Trumpet, the Scales, the Bridge
title.zh: 審判日：號角、天秤與橋樑

region.en: Plain of Resurrection (symbolic pin at Medina)
region.zh: 復活的平原（象徵性定位於麥地那）

period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE (Surahs 75, 81, 82, 99); hadith tradition compiled 9th century CE

source.work: Qur'an 75:1-19; 81:1-14; 99:1-8 (English: Rodwell 1861); with Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq (eschatological traditions)

license: Arabic text public domain; Rodwell 1861 translation public domain

summary.en: When the sun is folded up and the stars fall, when the trumpet is blown and all who are in the heavens and the earth swoon save whom God wills, the dead are raised: 'I swear by the Day of Resurrection, and by the self-accusing soul.' The books are opened — 'whoever's book is in his right hand, an easy reckoning; whoever's in his left, would that he had not received a book' — the scales are set, and the Sirat is stretched over Hell thinner than a hair. The sun draws near; the earth tells its tidings; and judgment is God's alone.
summary.zh: 日月纏裹、星辰殞落、號角吹響，天地間萬物昏厥——惟主所欲者除外。死者被復起：『我以復活日盟誓，以自責的靈魂盟誓。』功過簿展開——右手得簿者，易於清算；左手得簿者，恨不得未曾得簿——天秤已設，火獄之上的橋比髮絲還細。日臨近；大地報其消息；清算惟屬主。

sensitivity.note: Sacred eschatology of a living tradition; presented in public-domain translation with the Arabic as primary.

narrative.en:
The Qur'an speaks of the Last Day in a vocabulary of catastrophe and courtroom. The signs are drawn in the earliest Meccan suras: 'When the sun shall be folded up, and the stars shall fall, and when the mountains shall be made to pass away... when the seas shall suffer ebullition, and when souls shall be paired' (81:1-2). The earth is shaken with its earthquake and brings forth its burdens: 'On that day she shall tell her tidings' (99:1-4). The trumpet — sur — is blown by the angel Israfil, and all that are in the heavens and the earth swoon away, save him whom God pleases; then it is blown again, and they rise and look on.

The dead come forth from their graves 'as if they were locusts spread abroad'; the sky is opened and becomes as gates; the mountains are driven forth and become as mirage. Every soul is brought with its driver and witness: the earth is ordered to bring out its record — 'this day it shall tell its tidings, for thy Lord hath inspired it.' The books are opened: whoever's book is given into his right hand shall be reckoned with an easy reckoning and return rejoicing to his people; but whoever's book is in his left hand, or behind his back, 'would that he had not received a book, and had not known his reckoning' (69:19-25). The scales (mizan) are set: those whose good deeds are heavy are the prosperous; those whose good deeds are light — their books are empty — are those who have undone themselves, in Hell to abide. Even the deeds that seemed small are weighed: 'an atom's weight of good shall see it, and an atom's weight of evil shall see it' (99:7-8).

The bridge — Sirat — is stretched over the Fire, finer than a hair and sharper than a sword: the believers cross it with the speed of lightning, and the feet of the wicked slip. Under the bridge is Hell, whose fuel is men and stones, whose keepers are stern angels; above is Paradise, 'as broad as the heavens and the earth,' with rivers of water that does not corrupt and milk whose taste changes not, and the shade where there is no oppressive heat. Between the scales and the abodes stand the account and the intercession: the Prophet's intercession is asked, the believers are brought to the Pool of Kawthar, and the last word belongs to God: 'To whom belongeth the kingdom this day? To God, the One, the Almighty' (40:16).

In the hadith the scene is filled out with the interrogation in the grave by Munkar and Nakir, the blowing of Israfil, the standing of mankind for 'a day whose measure is fifty thousand years', and the arrival of the Judgement throne borne by the eight angels. The Prophet is told that the first suit between God's creatures will be about blood wrongly shed; that the feet of a man will not move before he is asked of four things — his life, his youth, his wealth, and his knowledge. The tradition also holds out the mercy: whoever has an atom of faith will be brought out of the Fire at last; the last of the people of Hell is the last to enter Paradise; and God laughs at the man who asks for less than is prepared for him. The Last Day is thus at once terror and arithmetic: the scales, the books, the bridge — and, at the end of it, the Presence.
narrative.zh: 古蘭經以災變與法庭的語彙講末日：日月纏裹、星辰殞落、群山流逝、海洋鼎沸（81:1-2）；大地震動並吐其重負，『是日它將報告其消息』（99:1-4）。號角吹響，天地萬物昏厥；再吹則復起。死者如蝗蟲四散而出；功過簿展開——右手得簿者易算而歸於家人喜悅；左手得簿者恨不得未曾得簿（69:19-25）。天秤設立；善行重者為成功者；『一微塵之善必見之，一微塵之惡必見之』。火獄之上的橋比髮絲細、比劍利；信者如電掠過，惡者足滑。聖訓補足：墓中之審問（蒙卡爾與納基爾）、伊斯拉菲勒吹號、五萬年之久的一日、以及最終的憐憫——『凡有一微塵信仰者，終將自火中得出』。

functions: Grounds Islamic ethics in final accountability: the scales and the books
Centres the daily prayers and the creed in eschatological hope and fear
Provides the imagery of the sermon and the mosque: the Trumpet, the Bridge, the Pool
Supports the doctrine of intercession and the mercy at the end of the Fire

passages.text: When the earth shall be shaken with a terrible shaking, and the mountains shall crumble and pass away, and become as scattered dust; and the ranks of men shall be ranged — and the day of the rising blast, the day on which a man shall fly from his brother, his mother, his father, his wife and his sons, on that day every man shall have business enough to occupy him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 80:33-37 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim; opening scene of the Great Awakening.
passages.zh: 當大地被猛烈地震撼，群山崩裂消逝，化為四散的塵土；眾人的行列被排定——在那復活之日的號角吹響之日，在那人將逃離其兄弟、其母親、其父親、其妻子與其兒女之日，在那日，每個人都有足夠的事務使他自顧不暇。

passages.text: The trumpet is sounded — and, lo, from the graves they hasten forth to their Lord. We will call up the registers, and the wicked book of the sinners is set out. Weigh with exact weights on that day; they whose balances are heavy are the prosperous; but they whose balances are light have ruined themselves. And there shall be a cry: O people of the Book, why did ye disbelieve the signs of God? And a bridge is set over hell, thinner than a hair, sharper than a sword, over which all must pass; the righteous cross as lightning, the wicked fall.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 7:8-9; 36:51; 19:68-69; and eschatological hadith tradition (Rodwell 1861 + hadith summaries); not verbatim; composite.
passages.zh: 號角吹響——看哪，他們從墳墓中急忙奔向他們的主。我們將召來功過簿，罪人的惡簿被展開。那日要以精確的天秤稱量；天秤重的人便是成功者；天秤輕的人則已自毀。並有呼聲說：有經的人啊，你們為何不信真主的跡象？一座橋被架在火獄之上，細於毛髮，利於刀劍，所有人都必須經過；義人如閃電般通過，惡人則墜落。

passages.text: The day whereon neither wealth nor sons shall avail, except him who bringeth to God a sound heart; and the day the heaven shall be cloven asunder, and the earth stretched forth, and hell made to gape, and the gardens brought near; then shall he know what he hath brought forward and what he hath left behind.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 26:88-89; 81:10-13; 100:9-10 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在那日，財富與子嗣皆無濟於事，唯有那帶著純潔之心來到真主面前的人除外；在那日，天將裂開，地將鋪展，火獄張開大口，樂園被拉近；那時他將知道自己所預先送出的與所遺留在後的。

title.en: The Pure Men of Old (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 古之真人（莊子）

region.en: The age of the ancients (symbolic pin: Song, Henan, China)
region.zh: 古之世（象徵定位：宋，今河南）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 6, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 6

summary.en: Zhuangzi's portrait of the pure men of old: they acted without calculation, could scale heights without fear, enter water without becoming wet, fire without feeling hot; they slept without dreams, breathed from their uttermost depths, and did not love life nor hate death — quickly come, quickly go — playing their allotted parts and waiting patiently for the end.
summary.zh: 古之真人：不逆寡，不雄成，不謨士；登高不慄，入水不濡，入火不熱；其寢不夢，其覺無憂，其息深深；不知說生，不知惡死——翛然而往，翛然而來而已矣。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the archetypal zhenren portrait that later Daoist hagiography made concrete. Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: But what is a pure man?--The pure men of old acted without calculation, not seeking to secure results. They laid no plans. Therefore, failing, they had no cause for regret; succeeding, no cause for congratulation. And thus they could scale heights without fear; enter water without becoming wet; fire, without feeling hot. So far had their wisdom advanced towards TAO.
passages.zh: 但什麼是真人呢？——古時的真人行事不經算計，不求確保結果。他們不預先謀劃。因此，失敗時，他們沒有悔恨的理由；成功時，也沒有慶賀的理由。於是他們能攀登高處而不懼；入水而不濕；入火而不覺熱。他們的智慧已如此接近道。

passages.text: The pure men of old slept without dreams, and waked without anxiety. They ate without discrimination, breathing deep breaths. For pure men draw breath from their uttermost depths; the vulgar only from their throats. The pure men of old did not know what it was to love life or to hate death. They did not rejoice in birth, nor strive to put off dissolution. Quickly come, and quickly go;--no more. They did not forget whence it was they had sprung, neither did they seek to hasten their return thither. Cheerfully they played their allotted parts, waiting patiently for the end.
passages.zh: 古時的真人睡覺不做夢，醒來不憂慮。他們飲食不挑剔，呼吸深沉。因為真人從其最深處呼吸；凡人只從喉嚨呼吸。古時的真人不知道什麼是貪生或惡死。他們不為出生而歡喜，也不力求延緩消亡。來得迅速，去得迅速——如此而已。他們不忘記自己從何而來，也不尋求加速返回那裡。他們欣然扮演所分配的角色，耐心等待終結。

title.en: Before Heaven and Earth: The Transmission of the Tao (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 夫道，有情有信，無為無形（莊子）

region.en: Mount T'ai and the cosmic stations (symbolic pin: Mount T'ai, Shandong, China)
region.zh: 泰山與諸天寰宇（象徵定位：山東泰山）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 6, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 6

summary.en: The genealogy of the Tao itself: before heaven and earth were, TAO was; the Great Bear obtained it and never erred from its course; K'an P'i established the K'un-lun mountains; the Yellow Emperor soared on the clouds to heaven; Yü Ch'iang fixed himself at the North Pole; Hsi Wang Mu settled at Shao Kuang; P'êng Tsu lived from Shun to the Five Princes; and Fu Yüeh, charioted upon one constellation, was enrolled among the stars.
summary.zh: 夫道，有情有信，無為無形；可得而不可見；自本自根，未有天地，自古以固存。狶韋氏得之以挈天地；堪坏得之以襲崑崙；馮夷得之以遊大川；肩吾得之以處太山；黃帝得之以登雲天；西王母得之坐乎少廣；彭祖得之，上及有虞，下及五伯；傅說得之，乘東維騎箕尾而比於列星。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); a priority Creation & Cosmology narrative — the scriptural charter for Taoist cosmogony and for the deification of sages.

passages.text: TAO has its laws, and its evidences. It is devoid both of action and of form. It may be transmitted, but cannot be received. It may be obtained, but cannot be seen. Before heaven and earth were, TAO was. It has existed without change from all time. Spiritual beings drew their spirituality therefrom, while the universe became what we can see it now. To TAO, the zenith is not high, nor the nadir low; no point in time is long ago, nor by lapse of ages has it grown old.
