passages.zh: 莊子與惠子一同在濠水的橋上遊玩，莊子說：「你看那些小魚游得多麼從容自在！這就是魚的快樂。」惠子說：「你不是魚，怎麼知道魚的快樂是什麼？」莊子回答說：「你不是我，怎麼知道我不知道魚的快樂？」

passages.text: "If I, not being you, cannot know what you know," urged Hui Tzŭ, "it follows that you, not being a fish, cannot know in what consists the pleasure of fishes." "Let us go back," said Chuang Tzŭ, "to your original question. You asked me how I knew in what consists the pleasure of fishes. Your very question shows that you knew I knew. I knew it from my own feelings on this bridge."
passages.zh: 惠子追問說：「我不是你，固然不能知道你所知道的；那麼你不是魚，也就不能知道魚的快樂是什麼了。」莊子說：「讓我們回到你最初的問題。你問我怎麼知道魚的快樂，你這樣問，就表明你已經知道我知道了。我是在這橋上憑自己的感受而知道的。」

title.en: Drumming on a Bowl at His Wife's Death (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 莊子妻死，鼓盆而歌（莊子）

region.en: Chuang Tzŭ's home in Sung (Shangqiu, Henan, China)
region.zh: 莊子之居，宋國（今河南商丘）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 18, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 18

summary.en: When Chuang Tzŭ's wife died, Hui Tzŭ found the widower singing with his legs spread out, beating time on a bowl. Chuang Tzŭ explains that she existed before birth without form or substance, then gained substance, form, and birth; now, passing from one phase to another like spring, summer, autumn, and winter, she lies asleep in Eternity — to go about weeping would be to proclaim myself ignorant of these natural laws.
summary.zh: 莊子妻死，惠子弔之；莊子則方箕踞鼓盆而歌。莊子曰：察其始而本無生；非徒無生也，而本無形——人且偃然寢於巨室，而我噭噭然隨而哭之，自以為不通乎命，故止也。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the most-cited Taoist mourning scene, retold in the drum-on-basin opera tradition. Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: When Chuang Tzŭ's wife died, Hui Tzŭ went to condole. He found the widower sitting on the ground, singing, with his legs spread out at a right angle, and beating time on a bowl. "To live with your wife," exclaimed Hui Tzŭ, "and see your eldest son grow up to be a man, and then not to shed a tear over her corpse,--this would be bad enough. But to drum on a bowl, and sing; surely this is going too far."
passages.zh: 莊子的妻子死了，惠子前去弔唁。他看見莊子坐在地上，岔開兩腿，一邊敲著瓦盆一邊唱歌。惠子說：「與妻子共同生活，看著長子長大成人，如今她死了，不哭也就罷了，竟然還敲著瓦盆唱歌，這未免太過分了。」

passages.text: "Not at all," replied Chuang Tzŭ. "When she died, I could not help being affected by her death. Soon, however, I remembered that she had already existed in a previous state before birth, without form, or even substance; that while in that unconditioned condition, substance was added to spirit; that this substance then assumed form; and that the next stage was birth. And now, by virtue of a further change, she is dead, passing from one phase to another like the sequence of spring, summer, autumn, and winter. And while she is thus lying asleep in Eternity, for me to go about weeping and wailing would be to proclaim myself ignorant of these natural laws. Therefore I refrain."
passages.zh: 莊子回答說：「並非如此。她剛死的時候，我怎能不為之悲傷呢。可是不久我便想到，她本來就未曾出生，不僅未曾出生，而且本來沒有形體；不僅沒有形體，而且本來沒有氣息。在恍恍惚惚之間，氣息變化而有了形體，形體變化而有了生命，如今又變化而死去。這就像春夏秋冬四季運行一樣。她如今安然睡在天地這大屋之中，而我卻在旁邊嚎啕大哭，這就說明我不通曉天命，所以我才不哭。」

title.en: The Skull Under His Head as a Pillow (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 莊子之楚，見髑髏（莊子）

region.en: En route to Ch'u (symbolic pin: Jingzhou, Hubei, China)
region.zh: 適楚道中（象徵定位：湖北荊州）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 18, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 18

summary.en: Chuang Tzŭ interrogates a bleached empty skull — ambitious citizen, ruined statesman, shamed wretch, starving beggar, or natural old age? — then sleeps with it as a pillow. In the night the skull explains that in death there is no sovereign above and no subject below, and when offered restoration to life and kin, opens its eyes wide and knits its brows: how should I cast aside happiness greater than that of a king?
summary.zh: 莊子之楚，見空髑髏，髏然有形；撽以馬捶而問之。夜半，髑髏見夢曰：死，無君於上，無臣於下；亦無四時之事，從然以天地為春秋，雖南面王樂，不能過也。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the skull-dream is Zhuangzi's Hamletian counter-meditation on death, tagged dream-vision pending a dedicated motif. Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: Chuang Tzŭ one day saw an empty skull, bleached, but still preserving its shape. Striking it with his riding whip, he said, "Wert thou once some ambitious citizen whose inordinate yearnings brought him to this pass?--some statesman who plunged his country in ruin and perished in the fray?--some wretch who left behind him a legacy of shame?--some beggar who died in the pangs of hunger and cold? Or didst thou reach this state by the natural course of old age?"
passages.zh: 莊子有一天看見一個空骷髏，枯骨裸露，卻還保持著原來的形狀。他用馬鞭敲了敲它，問道：「你是因為貪生縱欲、違背常理而落到這步田地的嗎？還是因為國家敗亡、遭到刀斧誅戮而這樣的呢？還是因為行為不善、怕給父母妻兒留下恥辱而自殺的呢？還是因為受凍挨餓而死的呢？還是因為享盡天年而死的呢？」

passages.text: When he had finished speaking, he took the skull, and placing it under his head as a pillow, went to sleep. In the night, he dreamt that the skull appeared to him and said, "You speak well, Sir; but all you say has reference to the life of mortals, and to mortal troubles. In death there are none of these. Would you like to hear about death?" Chuang Tzŭ having replied in the affirmative, the skull began:--"In death, there is no sovereign above, and no subject below. The workings of the four seasons are unknown. Our existences are bounded only by eternity. The happiness of a king among men cannot exceed that which we enjoy."
passages.zh: 說完，他拿起那具骷髏，枕在頭下便睡著了。夜裡，他夢見骷髏顯現於他面前，說道：「你談得很好，先生；但你所說的都關乎生人的生命，以及生人的種種憂患。死後這些一概沒有。你可願意聽聽死的情形嗎？」莊子回答願意，骷髏便開始說道：「死後，上沒有君王，下沒有臣民。四時的運行也無從知曉。我們的存在只以永恆為限。人間君王的快樂，也比不上我們所享受的。」

passages.text: Chuang Tzŭ, however, was not convinced, and said, "Were I to prevail upon God to allow your body to be born again, and your bones and flesh to be renewed, so that you could return to your parents, to your wife, and to the friends of your youth,--would you be willing?" At this, the skull opened its eyes wide and knitted its brows and said, "How should I cast aside happiness greater than that of a king, and mingle once again in the toils and troubles of mortality?"
passages.zh: 然而莊子並不相信，說道：「倘若我能說動造物者，讓你的身體重新降生，使你的骨肉得以更新，好讓你回到父母身邊、回到妻子身邊、回到你少年時的朋友身邊——你願意嗎？」骷髏聽了，睜大眼睛、皺起眉頭說道：「我怎能捨棄這勝過君王的快樂，再一次混入生人的勞苦與憂患之中呢？」

title.en: Life Is a Loan: The Hunchback and the One-Legged Man at K'un-lun (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 右師與介者觀於昆侖（莊子）

region.en: The tombs of departed heroes on the K'un-lun mountains (mythic; symbolic pin: Kunlun, Xinjiang, China)
region.zh: 崑崙黃帝之陵（神話之地；象徵定位：新疆崑崙）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 18, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 18

summary.en: A hunchback and a one-legged man gaze at the tombs of departed heroes on the K'un-lun mountains where the Yellow Emperor rests, when ulcers break out upon their left elbows. Do you loathe this? asks the hunchback. Not I, replies the other — life is a loan with which the borrower does but add more dust and dirt; life and death are as day and night.
summary.zh: 支離叔與滑介叔觀於冥伯之丘，昆侖之虛，黃帝之所休；俄而柳生其左肘。滑介叔曰：亡，予何惡？生者，假借也——死生為晝夜。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: A hunchback and a one-legged man were looking at the tombs of departed heroes, on the K'un-lun Mountains, where the Yellow Emperor rests. Suddenly, ulcers broke out upon their left elbows, of a very loathsome description. "Do you loathe this?" asked the hunchback. "Not I," replied the other, "why should I? Life is a loan with which the borrower does but add more dust and dirt to the sum total of existence. Life and death are as day and night; and while you and I stand gazing at the evidences of mortality around us, if the same mortality overtakes me, why should I loathe it?"
passages.zh: 一個駝背的人和一個獨腳的人，在崑崙山上黃帝安息之處，觀看已逝英雄們的墳墓。忽然，他們的左肘上長出了十分可憎的毒瘡。「你厭惡這個嗎？」駝背的人問道。「我不厭惡，」另一個回答，「我為什麼要厭惡呢？生命不過是一筆借貸，借貸者只是在這存在的總數上再添些塵土與污穢罷了。生與死如同晝與夜；你我正站在這裡，望著四周種種死亡的跡象，倘若這同樣的死亡臨到我身上，我為什麼要厭惡它呢？」

title.en: The Sea-Bird in the Temple of Lu (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 昔者海鳥止於魯郊（莊子）

region.en: The capital of Lu (Qufu, Shandong, China)
region.zh: 魯郊（今山東曲阜）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 18, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 18

summary.en: When a sea-bird alighted outside the capital of Lu, the prince received it with wine in the temple, the Chiu Shao music, and a slaughtered bullock. The bird, dazed and too timid to eat or drink, died in three days — treated like a man, not as a bird would treat a bird. Water, which is life to fishes, is death to man.
summary.zh: 昔者海鳥止於魯郊，魯侯御而觴之於廟，奏九韶以為樂，具太牢以為膳。鳥乃眩視憂悲，不敢食一膾，不敢飲一杯，三日而死。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: "Besides, have you not heard that of old when a sea-bird alighted outside the capital of Lu, the prince went out to receive it, and gave it wine in the temple, and had the Chiu Shao played to amuse it, and a bullock slaughtered to feed it? But the bird was dazed and too timid to eat or drink anything; and in three days it was dead. This was treating the bird like oneself, and not as a bird would treat a bird. Had he treated it as a bird would have treated a bird, he would have put it to roost in a deep forest, to wander over a plain, to swim in a river or lake, to feed upon fish, to fly in order, and to settle leisurely.
passages.zh: 「況且，你難道沒有聽說過，古時候有一隻海鳥飛落在魯國都城之外，國君親自出城迎接，在宗廟裡以酒款待牠，命人演奏九韶之樂來取悅牠，又宰殺一頭牛來餵養牠？可是那鳥卻頭昏眼花，過於驚懼，什麼也不敢吃、不敢喝；三天之後便死了。這是把鳥當作自己來對待，而不是以對待鳥的方式來對待鳥。倘若他以對待鳥的方式來對待鳥，就該讓牠棲息在深林之中，漫步於原野之上，游泳於江河湖泊之間，捕食魚類，成群飛翔，從容棲息。」

passages.text: "When the bird was already terrified at human voices, fancy adding music! Play the Hsien Ch'ih or the Chiu Shao in the wilds of Tung-t'ing, and birds will fly away, beasts will take themselves off, and fishes will dive down below. But men will collect to hear. "Water, which is life to fishes, is death to man. Being differently constituted, their likes and dislikes are different."
passages.zh: 「那鳥本已被人聲嚇得驚恐萬分，還妄想再添上音樂！在洞庭的荒野上演奏咸池或九韶之樂，鳥兒會飛走，野獸會逃散，魚兒會潛入水底。可是人卻會聚集起來聆聽。「水對魚是生命，對人卻是死亡。由於稟性不同，他們的所好與所惡也就不同。」

title.en: The Chain of Metamorphoses: From Germ to Man (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 種有幾：萬化一樞（莊子）

region.en: The roadside (symbolic pin: Song, Henan, China)
region.zh: 道旁（象徵定位：宋，今河南）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 18, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 18

summary.en: Lieh Tzŭ, eating by the roadside, points a blade of grass at an old skull: only you and I know that there is no such thing as life and no such thing as death. Then follows Zhuangzi's great chain of metamorphoses — germs become duckweed, lichen, the dog-tooth violet, grubs and butterflies, the Kan-yü-ku bird, the wine fly — ending in the leopard that produces the horse, which produces man, who goes back into the great Scheme from which all things come.
summary.zh: 種有幾：得水則為繼，得水土之際則為蛙蠙之衣，生於陵屯則為陵舄——久竹生青寧，青寧生程，程生馬，馬生人。人又反入於機。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the zhong-you-ji passage is Zhuangzi's spontaneous-generation cosmogony. Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: Lieh Tzŭ, being on a journey, was eating by the roadside, when he saw an old skull. Plucking a blade of grass, he pointed at it and said, "Only you and I know that there is no such thing as life and no such thing as death. Are you really at peace? Or am I really happy?
passages.zh: 列子出行途中，在路旁進食，看見一具舊骷髏。他拔起一根草，指著它說道：「只有你和我才知道，無所謂生，也無所謂死。你果真安寧嗎？還是果真快樂呢？」

passages.text: "Certain germs, falling upon water, become duckweed. When they reach the junction of the land and the water, they become lichen. Spreading up the bank, they become the dog-tooth violet. Reaching rich soil, they become wu-tsu, the root of which becomes grubs, while the leaves comes from butterflies, or hsü. These are changed into insects, born in the chimney corner, which look like skeletons. Their name is ch'ü-to. After a thousand days, the ch'ü-to becomes a bird, called Kan-yü-ku, the spittle of which becomes the ssŭ-mi. The ssŭ-mi becomes a wine fly, and that comes from an i-lu. The huang-k'uang produces the chiu-yu and the mou-jui produces the glow-worm. The yang-ch'i grafted to an old bamboo which has for a long time put forth no shoots, produces the ch'ing-ning, which produces the leopard, which produces the horse, which produces man. "Then man goes back into the great Scheme, from which all things come and to which all things return."
passages.zh: 「有些微生物落在水上，便化為浮萍。當它們到達水陸交界之處，便化為地衣。蔓延上河岸，便化為犬齒紫堇。抵達肥沃的土壤，便化為烏足，其根化為蠐螬，而其葉則出自蝴蝶，即蠨。這些化為昆蟲，生於煙囪角落，形似枯骨。它們的名字叫蛣蜣。經過一千日，蛣蜣化為鳥，名叫乾餘骨，其唾液化為斯彌。斯彌化為酒蠅，而酒蠅出自頤輅。黃軏生出九猷，瞀芮生出螢火蟲。羊奚嫁接於久不抽芽的老竹，生出青寧，青寧生出豹，豹生出馬，馬生出人。」「然後人又歸返於那偉大的造化之中，萬物皆由之而出，萬物皆歸之而去。」

title.en: Kuan Yin on the Perfect Man Who Walks Through Walls (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 列子問關尹：至人潛行不窒（莊子）

region.en: Kuan Yin's retreat at the western pass (symbolic pin: Hangu Pass, Lingbao, Henan, China)
region.zh: 關尹之居（象徵定位：河南靈寶函谷關）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 19, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 19

summary.en: Lieh Tzŭ asks Kuan Yin how the perfect man can walk through solid bodies unobstructed, pass through fire unburnt, and scale the highest heights without fear. Kuan Yin answers that he is in a condition of absolute purity — man can attain to formlessness and vanquish death — and tells the parable of the drunken man who falls out of a cart and does not die, for his spirit is in a condition of security; and if such security is to be got from wine, how much more from God.
summary.zh: 列子問關尹曰：至人潛行不窒，蹈火不熱，行乎萬物之上而不慄——是純氣之守也，非知巧果敢之列。醉者之墜車，雖疾不死；骨節與人同，而犯害與人異，其神全也。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the invulnerability passage is the charter of later Daoist immortality-arts claims. Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: Lieh Tzŭ asked Kuan Yin, saying, "The perfect man can walk through solid bodies without obstruction. He can pass through fire without being burnt. He can scale the highest heights without fear. How does he bring himself to this?" "It is because he is in a condition of absolute purity," replied Kuan Yin. "It is not cunning which enables him to dare such feats. Be seated, and I will tell you.
passages.zh: 列子問關尹說：「至人能穿行於堅實之物而無所阻礙。他能穿越烈火而不被燒傷。他能攀登至高的高處而無所畏懼。他如何使自己達到這般境地？」關尹回答說：「因為他處於絕對純淨的狀態。使他敢於行此等奇事的，並非機巧。請坐下，我來告訴你。

passages.text: "All that has form, sound, and colour, may be classed under the head thing. Man differs so much from the rest, and stands at the head of all things, simply because the latter are but what they appear and nothing more. But man can attain to formlessness and vanquish death. And with that which is in possession of the eternal, how can mere things compare?
passages.zh: 「凡有形、有聲、有色者，皆可歸入物之類。人與其餘萬物差異如此之大，而居於萬物之首，只因後者不過是其表象而已，別無其他。但人能夠達到無形，並戰勝死亡。而對於那擁有永恆者，區區萬物又怎能與之相比？

passages.text: "A drunken man who falls out of a cart, though he may suffer, does not die. His bones are the same as other people's; but he meets his accident in a different way. His spirit is in a condition of security. He is not conscious of riding in the cart; neither is he conscious of falling out of it. Ideas of life, death, fear, etc., cannot penetrate his breast; and so he does not suffer from contact with objective existences. And if such security is to be got from wine, how much more is it to be got from God. It is in God that the Sage seeks his refuge, and so he is free from harm."
passages.zh: 「一個醉漢從車上摔下，雖可能受傷，卻不會死。他的骨骼與他人相同；但他遭遇意外的方式卻不同。他的精神處於安穩的狀態。他不知道自己坐在車上；也不知道自己從車上摔下。生、死、恐懼等念頭無法侵入他的胸懷；因此他不因與客觀存在之物接觸而受害。而若這樣的安穩能從酒中得到，那麼從神那裡得到的又該多多少呢。聖人正是在神那裡尋求庇護，因此他免於傷害。」

title.en: The Hunchback Who Caught Cicadas as Though With His Hand (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 痀僂丈人承蜩（莊子）

region.en: The forest en route to Ch'u (symbolic pin: Jingzhou, Hubei, China)
region.zh: 適楚林中（象徵定位：湖北荊州）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 19, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 19

summary.en: In a forest on the way to Ch'u, Confucius sees a hunchback catching cicadas as though with his hand. The hunchback explains his training in balancing balls atop his pole, until heaven and earth and all creation may be around him, but he is conscious only of his cicada's wings. Singleness of purpose induces concentration of the faculties, says Confucius.
summary.zh: 仲尼適楚，出於林中，見痀僂者承蜩，猶掇之也。用志不分，乃凝於神——天地之大，萬物之多，而唯蜩翼之知。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: When Confucius was on his way to the Ch'u State, he came to a forest where he saw a hunchback catching cicadas as though with his hand. "How clever you are!" cried Confucius. "Have you any way of doing this?" "I have a way," replied the hunchback. "In the fifth and sixth moons I practise balancing two balls one on top of the other. If they do not fall, I do not miss many cicadas. When I can balance three balls, I only miss one in ten; and when five, then it is as though I caught the cicadas with my hand. My body is as motionless as the stump of a tree; my arms like dead branches. Heaven and earth and all creation may be around me, but I am conscious only of my cicada's wings. How should I not succeed?" Confucius looked round at his disciples and said, "Singleness of purpose induces concentration of the faculties. Of such is the success of this hunchback."
passages.zh: 孔子前往楚國途中，來到一片樹林，看見一個駝背的人在捕蟬，彷彿用手拾取一般。「你多麼靈巧啊！」孔子驚嘆道。「你有什麼方法能做到這樣嗎？」「我有方法，」駝背人回答說。「在第五、第六個月，我練習把兩顆彈丸疊在一顆之上。如果它們不掉落，我就很少漏掉蟬。當我能疊三顆彈丸時，我只漏掉十分之一；而當能疊五顆時，那就像用手拾取蟬一樣了。我的身體靜止如樹樁；我的手臂如枯枝。天地與萬物或許環繞著我，但我只意識到蟬的翅膀。我怎麼會不成功呢？」孔子環顧弟子說：「專一其志便能凝聚諸般能力。這個駝背人的成功正是如此。」

title.en: The Boatman of the Shang-shên Rapid and the Gambler's Stake (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 津人操舟若神，以瓦注者巧（莊子）

region.en: The Shang-shên rapid (symbolic pin: Lüliang gorge of the Yellow River, Shanxi, China)
region.zh: 商深之淵（象徵定位：山西呂梁黃河石門）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 19, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 19

summary.en: Crossing the Shang-shên rapid, Yen Yüan sees a boatman manage his craft with marvellous skill — they row as if the boat wasn't there. Confucius explains: such a man is oblivious of the water around him, and tells of the gambler who plays well for counters but, staking yellow gold, loses his wits; every one who attaches importance to the external becomes internally without resource.
summary.zh: 顏淵問仲尼：津人操舟若神。仲尼曰：善遊者數能，忘水也；以瓦注者巧，以鉤注者憚，以黃金注者殙——外重者內拙。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: Yen Yüan said to Confucius, "When I crossed over the Shang-shên rapid, the boatman managed his craft with marvellous skill. I asked him if handling a boat could be learnt. 'It can,' replied he. 'The way of those who know how to keep you afloat is more like sinking you. They row as if the boat wasn't there.' I enquired what this meant, but he would not tell me. May I ask its signification?" "It means," answered Confucius, "that such a man is oblivious of the water around him. He regards the rapid as though dry land. He looks upon an upset as an ordinary cart accident. And if a man can but be impervious to capsizings and accidents in general, whither should he not be able comfortably to go?"
passages.zh: 顏淵對孔子說：「當我渡過商深急流時，船夫操縱他的船技藝神妙。我問他駕船是否可以學會。『可以，』他回答說。『那些懂得如何讓你浮著的人，其方法更像是讓你沉下去。他們划船，彷彿船不存在一般。』我請教這是什麼意思，但他不肯告訴我。我可以問問它的含義嗎？」「它的意思是，」孔子回答說，「這樣的人忘卻了周圍的水。他把急流看作乾地。他把翻船看作普通的車禍。而一個人若能對翻船與種種意外都無動於衷，那麼他還有什麼地方不能安然前往呢？」

passages.text: "A man who plays for counters will play well. If he stakes his girdle, he will be nervous; if yellow gold, he will lose his wits. His skill is the same in each case, but he is distracted by the value of his stake. And every one who attaches importance to the external, becomes internally without resource."
passages.zh: 「以瓦片為注者，心思靈巧；以腰帶為注者，心生畏懼；以黃金為注者，則心神昏亂。其技藝本無不同，卻因所注之物的貴重而分心。凡是看重外物的人，內心便無所憑藉。」

title.en: The Grand Augur Addresses the Pigs (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 祝宗人玄端以臨牢柙（莊子）

region.en: The shambles beside the temple (symbolic pin: Song, Henan, China)
region.zh: 牢柙之前（象徵定位：宋，今河南）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 19, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 19

summary.en: The Grand Augur, in ceremonial robes, offers the pigs three months' fattening and a carved sacrificial dish — then, speaking from their point of view, admits it is better perhaps to live on bran and escape the shambles; yet from his own point of view, to enjoy honour when alive one would readily die on a war-shield. So he rejected the pigs' point of view — in what sense then was he different from the pigs?
summary.zh: 祝宗人玄端以臨牢柙，說彘曰：汝奚惡死？吾將三月豢汝，七日戒，三日齋——吾自取之，則異於彘。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the shambles-scene is Zhuangzi's great parable on sacrificial honour. Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: The Grand Augur, in his ceremonial robes, approached the shambles and thus addressed the pigs: "How can you object to die? I shall fatten you for three months. I shall discipline myself for ten days and fast for three. I shall strew fine grass, and place you bodily upon a carved sacrificial dish. Does not this satisfy you?"
passages.zh: 太祝身著禮服，走近屠宰場，對豬說道：「你們何必怕死呢？我將餵養你們三個月，自己齋戒十天、禁食三天，鋪上潔淨的茅草，把你們整隻放在雕花的祭器上。這樣難道還不能令你們滿意嗎？」

passages.text: Then speaking from the pigs' point of view, he continued, "It is better perhaps after all to live on bran and escape the shambles...." "But then," added he, speaking from his own point of view, "to enjoy honour when alive one would readily die on a war-shield or in the headsman's basket." So he rejected the pigs' point of view and adopted his own point of view. In what sense then was he different from the pigs?
passages.zh: 接著，他從豬的立場說道：「說到底，或許還是吃糠糟、免於屠宰更好些……」但隨後他又從自己的立場補充道：「然而，若能在生前享盡榮華，人便甘願死於戰盾之上或劊子手的刑筐之中。」於是，他捨棄了豬的立場，採納了自己的立場。那麼，他與豬又有何分別呢？

title.en: Duke Huan Sees the Wei-i Bogy by the Marsh (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 齊桓公見鬼於澤（莊子）

region.en: The marshes of Ch'i (Linzi, Shandong, China)
region.zh: 齊國之澤（今山東臨淄）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 19, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 19

summary.en: Out hunting with Kuan Chung as charioteer, Duke Huan sees a bogy and falls delirious. The sage Huang Tzŭ Kao Ngao catalogues the spirits — the mud spirit Li, the fire spirit Kao, the K'uei of the mountain, the Wei-i of the marsh, as broad as a cart-wheel, in purple clothes and a red cap, who stands up respectfully when it hears thunder — and those who see it are like to be chieftains among men. Ere the day had closed, without knowing it, the Duke's sickness had left him.
summary.zh: 齊桓公田於澤，見鬼焉。皇子告敖曰：鬼者——水有罔象，丘有宰，山有夔，野有彷徨，澤有委蛇；其大如轂，其長如轅，紫衣而朱冠；惡者殆於霸。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the spirit-catalog is a landmark of early Chinese demonology. Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: When Duke Huan was out hunting, with Kuan Chung as his charioteer, he saw a bogy. Catching hold of Kuan Chung's hand, he asked him, saying, "What do you see?" "I see nothing," replied Kuan Chung. But when the Duke got home he became delirious, and for many days was unable to go out. There came a certain Huang Tzŭ Kao Ngao of the Ch'i State and said, "Your Highness is self-injured. How could a bogy injure you? When the vital strength is dissipated in anger, and is not renewed, there is a deficiency. When its tendency is in one direction upwards, the result is to incline men to wrath. When its tendency is in one direction downwards, the result is loss of memory. When it remains stagnant, in the middle of the body, the result is disease."
passages.zh: 齊桓公出獵，管仲為他駕車，桓公看見了一個鬼怪。他抓住管仲的手，問道：「你看見什麼了？」管仲回答說：「我什麼也沒看見。」但桓公回到宮中後便神志昏亂，許多天都無法外出。齊國有位名叫皇子告敖的人前來說道：「君上這是自己傷害了自己。鬼怪怎能傷害您呢？當精氣因憤怒而消散，且得不到補充，便會出現虧虛。精氣若一味向上，結果便使人易怒；若一味向下，結果便使人健忘；若滯留於身體中部，結果便會生病。」

passages.text: "There are," replied Huang, "such things as bogies. There is the mud spirit Li; the fire spirit Kao; Lei T'ing, the spirit of the dust-bin; P'ei O and Wa Lung, sprites of the north-east; Yi Yang of the north-west; Wang Hsiang of the water; the Hsin of the hills; the K'uei of the mountain; the P'ang Huang of the moor; the Wei I of the marsh." "And what may the Wei I be like?" asked the Duke. "The Wei I," replied Huang, "is as broad as a cart-wheel and as long as the shaft. It wears purple clothes and a red cap. It is a sentient being, and whenever it hears the rumble of thunder, it stands up in a respectful attitude. Those who see this bogy are like to be chieftains among men." The Duke laughed exultingly and said, "The very one I saw!" Thereupon he dressed himself and sat up; and ere the day had closed, without knowing it, his sickness had left him.
passages.zh: 告敖回答說：「鬼怪這種東西是有的。有泥中的精怪履；有火中的精怪高；有糞堆的精怪雷霆；有東北方的精怪倍阿與鮭蠪；有西北方的精怪泆陽；有水中的精怪罔象；有山丘的精怪莘；有山中的精怪夔；有曠野的精怪彷徨；有沼澤的精怪委蛇。」桓公問道：「那委蛇是什麼樣子呢？」告敖回答說：「委蛇，粗如車輪，長如車轅。身穿紫衣，頭戴紅冠。它是個有知覺的生靈，每當聽到雷聲隆隆，便恭敬地立起身來。凡是見到這種鬼怪的人，將要成為人間的霸主。」桓公聽罷，高興地大笑說：「我見到的正是它啊！」於是便整衣端坐起來；不到一天，他的病竟在不知不覺中痊癒了。

title.en: Chi Hsing Tzŭ Trains Game-Cocks (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 紀渻子為王養鬥雞（莊子）

region.en: The prince's cock-pit (symbolic pin: Linzi, Shandong, China)
region.zh: 王之鬥場（象徵定位：山東臨淄）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 19, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 19

summary.en: Chi Hsing Tzŭ trains fighting cocks for the prince in ten-day stages: still seeking fiercely for a foe; still excited by sounds and shadows; still roused to rage at the sight of an enemy — until they stand as though of wood, virtue complete, at which strange cocks will not dare meet them but will run.
summary.zh: 紀渻子為王養鬥雞。十日而問：雞已乎？曰：未也，方虛驕而恃氣——望之似木雞矣，其德全矣；異雞無敢應者，反走矣。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the 'wooden cock' is a proverbial image of internal concentration. Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: Chi Hsing Tzŭ was training fighting cocks for the prince. At the end of ten days the latter asked if they were ready. "Not yet," replied Chi; "they are in the stage of seeking fiercely for a foe." Again ten days elapsed, and the prince made a further enquiry. "Not yet," replied Chi; "they are still excited by the sounds and shadows of other cocks." Ten days more, and the prince asked again. "Not yet," answered Chi; "the sight of an enemy is still enough to excite them to rage."
passages.zh: 紀渻子為君王馴養鬥雞。過了十天，君王問他雞是否已馴養好了。紀渻子回答說：「還沒有；它們正處於兇猛尋敵的階段。」又過了十天，君王再次詢問。紀渻子回答說：「還沒有；它們仍會被其他雞的聲音和身影所激奮。」再過十天，君王又問。紀渻子回答說：「還沒有；一見到敵手，仍足以激起它們的怒氣。」

passages.text: But after another ten days, when the prince again enquired, Chi said, "They will do. Other cocks may crow, but they will take no notice. To look at them one might say they were of wood. Their virtue is complete. Strange cocks will not dare meet them, but will run."
passages.zh: 但又過了十天，當王子再次詢問時，紀說：「可以了。別的公雞或許會啼叫，但牠們不會理會。看牠們的樣子，可以說像木頭一般。牠們的德性已完備。別的公雞不敢與牠們對峙，只會逃跑。」

title.en: The Old Man Who Swam the Lü-liang Cataract (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 呂梁丈夫蹈水（莊子）

region.en: The Lü-liang falls of the Yellow River (Shanxi, China)
region.zh: 呂梁瀑布（今山西呂梁）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 19, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 19

summary.en: At the Lü-liang cataract, whose foam reaches forty li away, Confucius sees an old man plunge in as though to drown himself — and emerge a hundred paces off, carolling along the bank. No way, says the old man: there was my original condition to begin with, then habit growing into nature, and lastly acquiescence in destiny. Plunging in with the whirl, I come out with the swirl.
summary.zh: 孔子觀於呂梁，縣水三十仞，流沫四十里，黿鼉魚鱉之所不能遊也。見一丈夫遊之，數百步而出，被髮行歌而遊於塘下。吾始乎故，長乎性，成乎命。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: Confucius was looking at the cataract at Lü-liang. It fell from a height of thirty jen, and its foam reached forty li away. No scaly, finny creature could enter therein. Yet Confucius saw an old man go in, and thinking that he was suffering from some trouble and desirous of ending his life, bade a disciple run along the side to try and save him. The old man emerged about a hundred paces off, and with flowing hair went carolling along the bank. Confucius followed him and said, "I had thought, Sir, you were a spirit, but now I see you are a man. Kindly tell me, is there any way to deal thus with water?"
passages.zh: 孔子在呂梁觀看瀑布。瀑布從三十仞的高處落下，水沫濺到四十里之外。任何有鱗有鰭的生物都無法進入其中。然而孔子看見一位老人走了進去，以為他遭遇某種困擾而想結束自己的性命，便命一名弟子沿著岸邊跑去設法救他。那老人卻在約百步之外浮出水面，披散著頭髮，沿著岸邊歌唱而行。孔子跟隨他，說道：「我原以為先生是鬼神，如今才知您是凡人。請您告訴我，可有什麼方法能這樣對付水？」

passages.text: "No," replied the old man; "I have no way. There was my original condition to begin with; then habit growing into nature; and lastly acquiescence in destiny. Plunging in with the whirl, I come out with the swirl. I accommodate myself to the water, not the water to me. And so I am able to deal with it after this fashion." "What do you mean," enquired Confucius, "by your original condition to begin with, habit growing into nature, and acquiescence in destiny?" "I was born," replied the old man, "upon dry land, and accommodated myself to dry land. That was my original condition. Growing up on the water, I accommodated myself to the water. That was what I meant by nature. And doing as I did without being conscious of any effort so to do, that was what I meant by destiny."
passages.zh: 「沒有，」老人回答，「我沒有什麼方法。起初是我的本然狀態；其次是習慣成長為天性；最後是順應命運。隨著漩渦潛入，又隨著迴流浮出。我順應水，而不是水順應我。因此我能夠這樣對付水。」孔子問道：「您所說的起初的本然狀態、習慣成長為天性、順應命運，是什麼意思？」老人回答：「我生於乾燥的陸地，便順應乾燥的陸地。那是我的本然狀態。成長於水中，便順應水。那就是我所說的天性。而做這些事時並不自覺有任何努力，那就是我所說的命運。」

title.en: The Chief Carpenter's Seven Days of Quiescence (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 梓慶削木為鐻（莊子）

region.en: The workshop of Lu (Qufu, Shandong, China)
region.zh: 魯之梓匠（今山東曲阜）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 19, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 19

summary.en: The chief carpenter Ch'ing carves a stand for musical instruments so fine that its work seems supernatural. His secret: three days of quiescence until he forgets reward, five days until he forgets fame, seven days until unconscious of his four limbs and physical frame — then into the mountain forest to find the tree that already contains the form required, bringing his own natural capacity into relation with that of the wood.
summary.zh: 梓慶削木為鐻，見者驚猶鬼神。臣將為鐻，未嘗敢以耗氣也——必齊以靜心：齊三日，而不敢懷慶賞爵祿；齊五日，不敢懷非譽巧拙；齊七日，輒然忘吾有四枝形體也。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: Ch'ing, the chief carpenter, was carving wood into a stand for hanging musical instruments. When finished, the work appeared to those who saw it as though of supernatural execution. And the prince of Lu asked him, saying, "What mystery is there in your art?" "No mystery, your Highness," replied Ch'ing; "and yet there is something.
passages.zh: 木匠首領慶正在雕刻木頭，製作懸掛樂器的架子。完成之後，作品在見到的人看來彷彿是神靈所造。魯國國君問他說：「你的技藝中有什麼奧秘？」「沒有奧秘，君上，」慶回答，「然而確有某種東西。

passages.text: "When I am about to make such a stand, I guard against any diminution of my vital power. I first reduce my mind to absolute quiescence. Three days in this condition, and I become oblivious of any reward to be gained. Five days, and I become oblivious of any fame to be acquired. Seven days, and I become unconscious of my four limbs and my physical frame. Then, with no thought of the Court present to my mind, my skill becomes concentrated, and all disturbing elements from without are gone. I enter some mountain forest. I search for a suitable tree. It contains the form required, which is afterwards elaborated. I see the stand in my mind's eye, and then set to work. Otherwise, there is nothing. I bring my own natural capacity into relation with that of the wood."
passages.zh: 「當我將要製作這樣的架子時，我先防止自己生命力的任何減損。我首先使自己的心靈歸於絕對的寂靜。如此狀態三天，我便忘卻任何可得的獎賞。五天，我便忘卻任何可獲的名聲。七天，我便忘卻我的四肢與形體。然後，心中不再有朝廷的念頭，我的技藝便凝聚起來，一切外來的干擾因素都消失了。我進入某處山林。我尋找合適的樹木。它含有我所需要的形態，之後再加以精細加工。我在心中看見那架子，然後才動手。否則，便什麼也沒有。我將自己天生的能力與木材的天性相結合。」

title.en: Shan Pao the Mountain-Drinker and the Hungry Tiger (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 單豹張毅：鞭其後者也（莊子）

region.en: The mountains of Lu (Mengshan, Shandong, China)
region.zh: 魯山之阿（象徵定位：山東蒙山）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 19, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 19

summary.en: Duke Wei asks T'ien K'ai Chih what his master Chu Hsien teaches about the art of life. Keeping life is like keeping a flock of sheep — you look out for the laggards: Shan Pao drank mountain water and at seventy had a child's complexion, until a hungry tiger ate him; Chang I frequented rich and poor alike and died at forty of internal disease. Each failed to whip up the laggards.
summary.zh: 魯有單豹者，巖居而水飲，不與民共利，行年七十而猶有嬰兒之色；不幸遇餓虎，虎殺而食之。有張毅者，高門縣薄，無不趨也；行年四十而有內熱之病以死。豹養其內而虎食其外。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: "Well," replied T'ien, "I have heard my master say that keeping life is like keeping a flock of sheep. You look out for the laggards, and whip them up. "In the State of Lu," said T'ien, "there was a man named Shan Pao. He lived on the mountains and drank water. All worldly interests he had put aside. And at the age of seventy, his complexion was like that of a child. Unluckily, he one day fell in with a hungry tiger who killed and ate him.
passages.zh: 「嗯，」田回答，「我聽我的老師說過，養生就像放牧一群羊。你要留意那些落後的，用鞭子趕上牠們。」田說：「在魯國，有一個名叫單豹的人。他住在山上，喝水。一切世俗的利益他都擱置一旁。到了七十歲，他的面色還像孩童一般。不幸的是，他有一天遇到一隻飢餓的老虎，被牠咬死吃掉了。」

passages.text: "There was also a man named Chang I, who frequented the houses of rich and poor alike. At the age of forty he was attacked by some internal disease and died. "Shan Pao took care of his inner self, and a tiger ate his external man. Chang I took care of himself externally, but disease attacked him internally. These two individuals both omitted to whip up the laggards."
passages.zh: 「又有一人名叫張毅，他出入富貴與貧賤之家。到了四十歲，為內疾所侵而亡。」單豹善養其內在之身，卻有老虎吃掉他外在的形軀。張毅善養其外在之身，卻有疾病侵襲他的內在。這兩個人，都是疏於鞭策那些落後懈怠之處。

title.en: The Tree That Was No Use and the Goose That Didn't Cackle (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 山木不材，雁以不鳴（莊子）

region.en: The mountain-path and the old friend's house (symbolic pin: Song, Henan, China)
region.zh: 山行與故人之家（象徵定位：宋，今河南）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 20, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 20

summary.en: On a mountain, the useless tree completes its allotted span; at the old friend's house, the goose that doesn't cackle is killed for dinner. Asked which horn of the dilemma he rests on, Chuang Tzŭ smiles that he rests halfway between — or better, charioted upon TAO, floating far above mortality, changing with the change of time, swaying all things and swayed by none.
summary.zh: 莊子行於山中，見大木枝葉盛茂，伐木者止其旁而不取——此木以不材得終其天年。明日弟子問：昨日山中之木以不材得終其天年；今主人之雁以不材死——先生將何處？

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: Chuang Tzŭ was travelling over a mountain when he saw a huge tree well covered with foliage. A woodsman had stopped near by, not caring to take it; and on Chuang Tzŭ enquiring the reason, he was told that it was of no use. "This tree," cried Chuang Tzŭ, "by virtue of being good for nothing succeeds in completing its allotted span." When Chuang Tzŭ left the mountain, he put up at the house of an old friend. The latter was delighted, and ordered a servant to kill a goose and cook it. "Which shall I kill?" enquired the servant; "the one that cackles or the one that doesn't?"
passages.zh: 莊子行於山中，看見一棵大樹，枝葉十分茂盛。一位伐木的人停在旁邊，卻無意取用；莊子問其緣故，那人回答說這樹沒有用處。莊子嘆道：「這棵樹正因為不成材，才能夠享盡它天賦的壽命。」莊子離開山之後，投宿在一位老友家中。老友十分高興，吩咐僕人殺一隻鵝來烹煮。「我該殺哪一隻？」僕人問道，「是會叫的那隻，還是不會叫的那隻？」

passages.text: His master told him to kill the one which did not cackle. And accordingly, the next day, a disciple asked Chuang Tzŭ, saying, "Yesterday, that tree on the mountain, because good for nothing, was to succeed in completing its allotted span. But now, our host's goose, which is good for nothing, has to die. Upon which horn of the dilemma will you rest?" "I rest," replied Chuang Tzŭ with a smile, "halfway between the two. In that position, appearing to be what I am not, it is impossible to avoid the troubles of mortality; though, if charioted upon TAO and floating far above mortality, this would not be so. No praise, no blame; both great and small; changing with the change of time, but ever without special effort; both above and below; making for harmony with surroundings; reaching creation's First Cause; swaying all things and swayed by none;--how then shall such troubles come? This was the method of Shên Nung and Huang Ti."
passages.zh: 主人叫他殺那隻不會叫的。於是，第二天，有位弟子問莊子說：「昨天，山中的那棵樹，因為不成材，才能夠享盡它天賦的壽命。如今，主人家的鵝，因為不成材，卻得死。您將立於這進退兩難的哪一端呢？」莊子笑著回答：「我立於兩者之間。處於那樣的位置，看似是我而非我，便無法避免有生之患；然而，若能乘道而浮遊於生死之外，就不會如此了。無譽無毀；或大或小；隨時間而變化，卻始終不刻意造作；或上或下；與周遭相和諧；達於造化之第一因；主宰萬物而不為萬物所主宰——如此，那些禍患又從何而來呢？這正是神農與黃帝的方法。」

title.en: The Fox's Skin, Established-Virtue, and the Empty Boat (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 魯君之皮，建德之國，虛舟（莊子）

region.en: The prince's court at Lu and Nan-yüeh (symbolic pin: Qufu, Shandong, China)
region.zh: 魯廷與南越建德之國（象徵定位：山東曲阜）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 20, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 20

summary.en: The philosopher of Shih-nan tells the melancholy prince of Lu that the fox and the leopard die for their skins — is not the State of Lu your skin? — and sends him towards the district of Established-Virtue. And the empty boat: if an empty boat is about to collide with yours, even an irritable man does not lose his temper; but if some one is in it, bad language inevitably follows — if a man could only roam empty through life, who would be able to injure him?
summary.zh: 市南宜僚見魯侯；虎豹以皮為災。南越有邑焉名為建德之國。方舟而濟於河，有虛船來觸舟——人能虛己以遊世，其孰能害之！

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the empty-boat parable is a classic of Taoist self-effacement. Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: "Your Highness' method of avoiding misfortune," said the philosopher of Shih-nan, "is but a shallow one. A handsome fox or a striped leopard will live in a mountain forest, hiding beneath some precipitous cliff. This is their repose. They come out at night and keep in by day. This is their caution. Though under the stress of hunger and thirst, they lie hidden, hardly venturing to slink secretly to the river bank in search of food. This is their resoluteness. Nevertheless, they do not escape the misfortune of the net and the trap. But what crime have they committed? 'Tis their skin which is the cause of their trouble; and is not the State of Lu your Highness' skin?
passages.zh: 「君上避禍的方法，」市南先生說，「實在淺薄。一隻俊美的狐狸或一隻斑紋的豹子，會棲居於山林之中，藏身於陡峭的崖壁之下。這是牠們的安息。牠們夜間出來，白天隱伏。這是牠們的謹慎。縱然在飢渴的逼迫之下，牠們仍潛伏不動，幾乎不敢偷偷溜到河岸去覓食。這是牠們的堅定。然而，牠們仍逃不過羅網與陷阱之禍。可是牠們犯了什麼罪呢？正是牠們的皮毛招來禍患；而魯國，不正是君上的皮毛嗎？」

passages.text: "In Nan-yüeh there is a district, called Established-Virtue. Its people are simple and honest, unselfish, and without passions. They can make, but cannot keep. They give, but look for no return. They are not conscious of fulfilling obligations. They are not conscious of subservience to etiquette. Their actions are altogether uncontrolled, yet they tread in the way of the wise. Life is for enjoyment; death, for burial. And thither I would have your Highness proceed, power discarded and the world left behind, only putting trust in TAO."
passages.zh: 「在南越有一個地方，名叫建德。那裡的百姓純樸誠實，無私無欲。他們能製造，卻不能積藏。他們施予，卻不求回報。他們不自覺在履行義務。他們不自覺在屈從禮節。他們的行動全然不受拘束，卻行走在智者的道路上。生是為了享樂；死是為了安葬。我願君上前往那裡，捨棄權力，拋下天下，只信託於道。」

passages.text: "Suppose a boat is crossing a river, and another empty boat is about to collide with it. Even an irritable man would not lose his temper. But supposing there was some one in the second boat. Then the occupant of the first would shout to him to keep clear. And if the other did not hear the first time, nor even when called to three times, bad language would inevitably follow. In the first case there was no anger, in the second there was; because in the first case the boat was empty, and in the second it was occupied. And so it is with man. If he could only roam empty through life, who would be able to injure him?"
passages.zh: 「假設有一隻船正渡河，而另一隻空船將要撞上它。即使是一個暴躁的人，也不會發脾氣。但假設第二隻船上有人。那麼第一隻船上的人就會向他呼喊，要他避開。如果對方第一次沒聽見，甚至呼喊三次仍沒聽見，惡言惡語便不可避免地隨之而來。頭一種情形沒有怒氣，第二種卻有；因為頭一種情形船是空的，第二種情形船是有人 的。人也是如此。倘若他能空空洞洞地浮遊於世，誰又能傷害他呢？」

title.en: Collecting Subscriptions Without Injury (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 北宮奢為衛靈公賦斂以為鐘（莊子）

region.en: The city gate of Wei (Puyang, Henan, China)
region.zh: 衛城門外之壇（今河南濮陽）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 20, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 20

summary.en: Pei Kung Shê levies contributions at an altar outside the Wei city gate for making bells, and in three months the chime is hung. Asked how he managed it, he answers: in the domain of ONE there may not be managing — he made allowances for ignorance and suspicion, forbade not those who came nor detained those who went, showed no resentment to the unwilling nor gratitude to the givers; every one subscribed what he liked.
summary.zh: 北宮奢為衛靈公賦斂以為鐘，為之壇乎郭門之外；三月而成上下之縣。奢曰：一之間，無敢設也——因以為弟子，順其自然而己矣。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: Pei Kung Shê, minister to Duke Ling of Wei, levied contributions for making bells. An altar was built outside the city gate; and in three months the bells, upper and lower, were all hung. When Wang Tzŭ Ch'ing Chi saw them, he asked, saying, "How, Sir, did you manage this?" "In the domain of ONE," replied Shê, "there may not be managing. I have heard say that which is carved and polished reverts nevertheless to its natural condition. And so I made allowances for ignorance and for suspicion. I betrayed no feeling when welcomed or dismissed. I forbade not those who came, nor detained those who went away. I showed no resentment towards the unwilling, nor gratitude towards those who gave. Every one subscribed what he liked; and thus in my daily collection of subscriptions, no injury was done.--How much more then those who have the great WAY?"
passages.zh: 衛靈公之臣北宮奢為靈公徵收鑄鐘之資。於城門外築壇；三月而成，上下之鐘皆懸。王子慶忌見之，問曰：「子何以能如此？」奢答曰：「在『一』之域中，或無所謂經營。吾聞雕琢琢磨者，終歸於自然之狀。故吾於無知與疑貳者，皆有所寬容。迎之送之，吾不露其情。來者不禁，去者不留。不願者不怨，施與者不謝。各隨其所樂而輸；故吾日日徵集，而無所傷也。——況乎擁有大道者乎？」

title.en: The I-êrh Birds of the Eastern Sea (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 意怠之鳥（莊子）

region.en: Between Ch'ên and Ts'ai, where Confucius starved (Zhoukou, Henan, China)
region.zh: 陳蔡之間（今河南周口一帶）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 20, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 20

summary.en: Hemmed in between Ch'ên and Ts'ai for seven days without food, Confucius is told by the minister Jen the way not to die: the i-êrh birds of the eastern sea fly simultaneously and roost in a body, none striving to be first, eating only the leavings of others — and so the outside world cannot harm them. Straight trees are the first felled; sweet wells are soonest exhausted.
summary.zh: 孔子圍於陳蔡之間，七日不火食。大公任往弔之——東海有意怠之鳥：其為鳥也，翪翪爾而飛，進不敢為前，退不敢為後；食不敢先嘗，取其餘——是以不入於俗而外乎世也。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: When Confucius was hemmed in between Ch'ên and Ts'ai, he passed seven days without food. The minister Jen went to condole with him, and said, "You were near, Sir, to death." "I was indeed," replied Confucius. "Do you fear death, Sir?" enquired Jen. "I do," said Confucius. "Then I will try to teach you," said Jen, "the way not to die.
passages.zh: 孔子被困於陳、蔡之間，七日不食。大臣任往弔之，曰：「夫子幾乎死矣。」孔子曰：「然。」任問曰：「夫子懼死乎？」孔子曰：「然。」任曰：「然則吾試教夫子不死之道。」

passages.text: "In the eastern sea there are certain birds, called the i-êrh. They behave themselves in a modest and unassuming manner, as though unpossessed of ability. They fly simultaneously: they roost in a body. In advancing, none strives to be first; in retreating, none ventures to be last. In eating, none will be the first to begin; it is considered proper to take the leavings of others. Therefore, in their own ranks they are at peace, and the outside world is unable to harm them. And thus they escape trouble. "Straight trees are the first felled. Sweet wells are soonest exhausted. And you, you make a show of your knowledge in order to startle fools. You cultivate yourself in contrast to the degradation of others. And you blaze along as though the sun and moon were under your arms; consequently, you cannot avoid trouble."
passages.zh: 「東海有鳥焉，名曰意怠。其為人也，謙卑而不自矜，若無能然。其飛也同飛，其棲也同棲。進則無敢為先，退則無敢為後。食則無敢先嘗，取人之餘以為常。故其黨內和，而外物不能害之。是以免於患。「直木先伐。甘井先竭。而夫子飾知以驚愚，修身以明汙，昭昭乎若揭日月而行，故不免於患。」

passages.text: "Good indeed!" replied Confucius; and forthwith he took leave of his friends and dismissed his disciples and retired to the wilds, where he dressed himself in skins and serge and fed on acorns and chestnuts. He passed among the beasts and birds and they took no heed of him. And if so, how much more among men?
passages.zh: 孔子曰：「善哉！」於是辭其友，遣其弟子，退居於野，衣裘褐，食橡栗。行於禽獸之間，禽獸不顧；況於人乎？

title.en: Lin Hui Casts Aside the Regalia and Carries Off the Child (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 林回棄千金之璧，負赤子而趨（莊子）

region.en: The flight from the fall of Kuo (symbolic pin: Sanmenxia, Henan, China)
region.zh: 國亡奔逃之路（象徵定位：河南三門峽）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 20, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 20

summary.en: When the men of Kuo fled, Lin Hui cast aside most valuable regalia and carried away his child upon his back. The regalia involved a mere question of money, he said; the child was from God. The friendship of the superior man is negative like water; the friendship of the mean man is full-flavoured like wine — the one passes from the negative to the affectionate, the other from the full-flavoured to nothing.
summary.zh: 林回曰：彼以利合，此以天屬也。夫以利合者，迫窮禍患害相棄也；以天屬者，迫窮禍患害相收也——君子之交淡若水，小人之交甘若醴。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: Confucius asked Tzŭ Sang Hu, saying, "I have been twice expelled from Lu. My tree was cut down in Sung. I have been tabooed in Wei. I am a failure in Shang and Chou. I was surrounded between Ch'ên and Ts'ai. And in addition to all these troubles, my friends have separated from me and my disciples are gone. How is this?" "Have you not heard," replied Sang Hu, "how when the men of Kuo fled, one of them, named Lin Hui, cast aside most valuable regalia and carried away his child upon his back?
passages.zh: 孔子問子桑雽曰：「吾再逐於魯，伐樹於宋，削跡於衛，窮於商、周，圍於陳、蔡。加以此數患，親戚益疏，徒友益散，何也？」桑雽曰：「子獨不聞假人之亡與？林回棄千金之璧，負赤子而趨。

passages.text: Lin Hui himself said, 'The regalia involved a mere question of money. The child was from God.' "And so it is that in trouble and calamity mere money questions are neglected, while we ever cling nearer to that which is from God. ... "The friendship of the superior man is negative like water. The friendship of the mean man is full-flavoured like wine. That of the superior man passes from the negative to the affectionate. That of the mean man passes from the full-flavoured to nothing." "I hear and obey," replied Confucius; and forthwith he went quietly home, put an end to his studies and cast aside his books. His disciples no longer saluted him as teacher; but his love for them deepened every day.
passages.zh: 林回自曰：『彼以利合，此以天屬也。』「故夫患難之中，利合者相棄，天屬者相收。……「君子之交淡若水，小人之交甘若醴。君子淡以親，小人甘以絕。」孔子曰：「敬聞命矣。」於是辭歸，絕學捐書。弟子無挹於前，其愛益加進。

title.en: The Climbing Ape, the Bramble Bush, and the Prince of Wei (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 莊子衣大布而補之，猿楠之喻（莊子）

region.en: The Wei court (Anyang region, Henan, China)
region.zh: 魏廷（今河南安陽一帶）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 20, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 20

summary.en: Chuang Tzŭ, in patched cotton clothes, visits the prince of Wei, who cries that he looks miserable. It is poverty, not misery: give a climbing ape a large tree and it twirls as monarch of all it surveys; put it in a bramble bush and it trembles with fear — living under foolish sovereigns and wicked ministers, how should any one help being miserable? It was under such circumstances that Pi Kan was disembowelled.
summary.zh: 莊子衣大布而補之，正緳繫履而過魏王。王曰：何先生之憊邪？莊子曰：貧也，非憊也——處勢不便，未足以逞其能也。今處昏上亂相之間，而欲無憊，奚可得邪？

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: Chuang Tzŭ put on cotton clothes with patches in them, and arranging his girdle and tieing on his shoes, went to see the prince of Wei. "How miserable you look, Sir!" cried the prince. "It is poverty, not misery," replied Chuang Tzŭ. "A man who has TAO cannot be miserable. Ragged clothes and old boots make poverty, not misery. Mine is what is called being out of harmony with one's age.
passages.zh: 莊子穿著打補丁的粗布衣裳，整理好腰帶、繫好鞋子，前去謁見魏王。「先生怎麼這般潦倒啊！」魏王驚呼。莊子回答：「這是貧窮，不是潦倒。懷有道的人不會潦倒。破衣舊鞋只算貧窮，不算潦倒。我這情形，叫做生不逢時。

passages.text: "Has your Highness never seen a climbing ape? Give it some large tree, and it will twist and twirl among the branches as though monarch of all it surveys. Yi and Fêng Mêng can never catch a glimpse of it. But put it in a bramble bush, and it will move cautiously with sidelong glances, trembling all over with fear. Not that its muscles relax in the face of difficulty, but because it is at a disadvantage as regards position, and is unable to make use of its skill. And how should any one, living under foolish sovereigns and wicked ministers, help being miserable, even though he might wish not to be so? It was under such circumstances that Pi Kan was disembowelled."
passages.zh: 「大王難道沒見過攀援的猿猴嗎？給牠一棵大樹，牠便在枝葉間盤旋騰躍，彷彿睥睨一切、唯我獨尊。后羿與逢蒙也休想瞥見牠一眼。可是把牠放在荊棘叢中，牠便側目而視、小心翼翼，渾身顫抖，滿心恐懼。這並非牠的筋骨在困難面前鬆懈了，而是所處的位置對牠不利，無法施展牠的本領。再說，一個人生活在昏君與奸臣之下，縱然不想潦倒，又怎能不潦倒呢？比干就是在那樣的情形下被剖心的。」

title.en: The Mantis, the Cicada, and the Strange Bird of Tiao-ling Park (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 螳螂捕蟬，異鵲在後（莊子）

region.en: The park at Tiao-ling (symbolic pin: Xiangyang, Hubei, China)
region.zh: 彫陵之樊（象徵定位：湖北襄陽）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 20, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 20

summary.en: In the park at Tiao-ling Chuang Tzŭ sees a strange bird with wings seven feet across fly past his head into a chestnut grove. Stalking it with his cross-bow, he finds a cicada enjoying the shade, a mantis springing upon it — forgetting its own body, which the bird pounces on, forgetting its own nature. Loss follows the pursuit of gain, cries Chuang Tzŭ, and is driven from the park as a thief; for three months he does not leave the house.
summary.zh: 莊周遊於彫陵，睹一異鵲自南方來者；翼廣七尺，目大運寸，感周之顙——見得而忘其形，異鵲從而利之，見利而忘其真。物固相累，二類相召也。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing); the mantis-stalks-the-cicada scene is one of the most widely popularised images in Chinese art. Included as a comparative text.

passages.text: When Chuang Tzŭ was wandering in the park at Tiao-ling, he saw a strange bird which came from the south. Its wings were seven feet across. Its eyes were an inch in circumference. And it flew close past Chuang Tzŭ's head to alight in a chestnut grove. "What manner of bird is this?" cried Chuang Tzŭ. "With strong wings it does not fly away. With large eyes it does not see." So he picked up his skirts and strode towards it with his cross-bow, anxious to get a shot. Just then he saw a cicada enjoying itself in the shade, forgetful of all else. And he saw a mantis spring and seize it, forgetting in the act its own body, which the strange bird immediately pounced upon and made its prey. And this it was which had caused the bird to forget its own nature.
passages.zh: 莊子在雕陵的園圃中遊逛時，看見一隻從南方飛來的怪鳥。牠的翅膀寬達七尺，眼睛圓有一寸。牠貼著莊子的頭頂飛過，停落在栗樹林中。「這是什麼鳥啊？」莊子驚呼，「翅膀強健卻不飛走，眼睛很大卻看不見。」於是他提起衣襟，拿著彈弓快步走向牠，急著想射一箭。就在這時，他看見一隻蟬在樹蔭下自得其樂，忘了一切。又看見一隻螳螂躍起抓住了牠，在這一刻卻忘了自己的身體，而那隻怪鳥立刻撲上去，把螳螂當作了獵物。正是這一切，使那隻鳥忘了自己的本性。

passages.text: "Alas!" cried Chuang Tzŭ with a sigh, "how creatures injure one another. Loss follows the pursuit of gain." So he laid aside his bow and went home, driven away by the park-keeper who wanted to know what business he had there. For three months after this, Chuang Tzŭ did not leave the house; and at length Lin Chü asked him, saying, "Master, how is it that you have not been out for so long?" "While keeping my physical frame," replied Chuang Tzŭ, "I lost sight of my real self. Gazing at muddy water, I lost sight of the clear abyss. ... Now when I strolled into the park at Tiao-ling, I forgot my real self. That strange bird which flew close past me to the chestnut grove, forgot its nature. The keeper of the chestnut grove took me for a thief. Consequently I have not been out."
passages.zh: 「唉！」莊子長嘆一聲，「萬物互相傷害，得失總是緊隨追逐利益而來。」於是他放下彈弓回家，卻被園圃的守園人趕了出來，那人想知道他到這裡來做什麼。此後三個月，莊子沒有出門；最後藺且問他道：「先生，怎麼這麼久都不出門呢？」莊子回答：「我顧惜自己的形骸，卻迷失了真正的自我。望著渾濁的水，便看不見清澈的深淵。……先前我漫步走進雕陵的園圃，忘掉了真正的自我。那隻貼著我飛過、停落栗林的怪鳥，忘掉了自己的本性。栗林的守園人把我當成了小偷。因此我才不出門。」

title.en: The Innkeeper's Beautiful and Ugly Concubines (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 陽子之宋，逆旅人有妾二人（莊子）

region.en: An inn in the Sung State (Shangqiu, Henan, China)
region.zh: 宋國逆旅（今河南商丘）

period: Zhuangzi ch. 20, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, ch. 20

summary.en: Passing a night at a Sung inn, Yang Tzŭ finds the innkeeper loves his ugly concubine and hates the beautiful one. The beautiful one is so conscious of her beauty that one does not think her beautiful; the ugly one so conscious of her ugliness that one does not think her ugly. Note this, my disciples: be virtuous, but without being consciously so, and wherever you go, you will be beloved.
summary.zh: 陽子之宋，宿於逆旅。逆旅人有妾二人，其一人美，其一人惡；惡者貴而美者賤。美者自美，吾不知其美也；惡者自惡，吾不知其惡也。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: When Yang Tzŭ went to the Sung State, he passed a night at an inn. The innkeeper had two concubines, one beautiful, the other ugly. The latter he loved; the former, he hated. Yang Tzŭ asked how this was; whereupon one of the inn servants said, "The beautiful one is so conscious of her beauty that one does not think her beautiful. The ugly one is so conscious of her ugliness that one does not think her ugly." "Note this, my disciples!" cried Yang Tzŭ. "Be virtuous, but without being consciously so; and wherever you go, you will be beloved."
passages.zh: 楊子前往宋國時，在一家旅店過夜。店主有兩個妾，一個美麗，一個醜陋。他寵愛醜的，厭惡美的。楊子問這是什麼緣故；於是店中的一名僕役說道：「那美的自覺其美，所以人們不覺得她美。那醜的自覺其醜，所以人們不覺得她醜。」「弟子們記住這一點！」楊子高聲說道，「行善而不自覺其在行善，那麼無論你到哪裡，都會受人喜愛。」

title.en: Joachim and Anna: The Childless Offering
title.zh: 約雅敬與亞拿：無子者的奉獻

region.en: Jerusalem temple and shepherd pastures
region.zh: 耶路撒冷聖殿與牧人草場

period: Gospel of the Birth of Mary, c. 150 CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: The Gospel of the Birth of Mary, chaps. 1-2 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: The pious couple Joachim and Anna, childless for twenty years, vow any child to the Lord; the high priest Issachar publicly rejects Joachim's offerings — 'cursed is every one who shall not beget a male in Israel.' Shamed, Joachim retires to the shepherds, where an angel of the Lord appears 'with a prodigious light', recalling Sarah and Rachel: 'when he shuts the womb of any person, he does it for this reason, that he may in a more wonderful manner again open it' — and promises a daughter to be called Mary.
summary.zh: 敬虔的約雅敬與亞拿無子二十年，起誓將孩子獻與主；大祭司以薩迦當眾拒其奉獻——「凡在以色列中不生男丁的，都是被咒詛的」。約雅敬羞愧退到牧人中間，主的使者帶著大光顯現，引撒拉與拉結為例：「神封閉人的胎，是為要以更奇妙的方式再開啟——使所生的不是情慾之果，而是神的恩賜」——並應許生女取名馬利亞。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal infancy-cycle text, formative for the Marian traditions (Nativity of Mary feast). Presented as legendary narrative, distinct from canonical scripture.

passages.text: Their lives were plain and right in the sight of the Lord, pious and faultless before men; for they divided all their substance into three parts; one of which they devoted to the temple and officers of the temple; another they distributed among strangers, and persons in poor circumstances; and the third they reserved for themselves and the uses of their own family. In this manner they lived for about twenty years chastely, in the favour of God, and the esteem of men, without any children.
passages.zh: 他們的生活在主眼中樸素而正直，在人面前虔誠而無可指摘；因為他們把所有財物分成三份：一份奉獻給聖殿和聖殿的職司人員；一份分給異鄉人和貧困之人；第三份留給自己和自己家庭之用。他們就這樣貞潔地生活了大約二十年，蒙神恩寵，受世人敬重，卻沒有子女。

passages.text: Who, when he saw Joachim along with the rest of his neighbours, bringing his offerings, despised both him and his offerings, and asked him, Why he, who had no children, would presume to appear among those who had? Adding, that his offerings could never be acceptable to God; the Scripture having said, Cursed is every one who shall not beget a male in Israel. But Joachim being much confounded with the shame of such reproach, retired to the shepherds who were with the cattle in their pastures.
passages.zh: 他看見約阿希姆與其餘鄰人一同帶著祭品前來，便輕視他和他所獻的祭品，問他說：你這沒有子嗣的人，為何竟敢出現在有子嗣的人中間？又說，他的祭品絕不可能蒙神悅納；因為經上說：凡在以色列中不生育男子的人，都是受咒詛的。約阿希姆因這羞辱的責備而大為惶恐，便退到與牲畜同在牧場的牧人那裏去了。

passages.text: On a certain day when he was alone, the angel of the Lord stood by him with a prodigious light. And the angel who had appeared to him, endeavouring to compose him, said: Be not afraid, Joachim, nor troubled at the sight of me, for I am an angel of the Lord sent by him to you, that I might inform you that your prayers are heard, and your alms ascended in the sight of God. For God is the avenger of sin, and not of nature; and so when he shuts the womb of any person, he does it for this reason, that he may in a more wonderful manner again open it, and that which is born appear to be not the product of lust, but the gift of God.
passages.zh: 某一天，他獨自一人時，主的使者帶著奇異的光芒站在他身旁。那向他顯現的使者設法安撫他，說：約阿希姆，不要害怕，也不要因見到我而驚惶，因為我是主的天使，是他差遣我到你們這裏來，為要告訴你，你的祈禱已蒙垂聽，你的施捨已上達神面前。因為神是罪的報應者，而非本性的報應者；所以當他關閉任何人的母腹時，他這樣做是為要再以更奇妙的方式開啟它，使所生下的顯明不是情慾的產物，而是神的恩賜。

title.en: Mary Danced on the Altar Steps
title.zh: 馬利亞在祭壇臺階上跳躍

region.en: Temple of the Lord, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，主的聖殿

period: Protevangelion of James, c. 150 CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: The Protevangelion, chaps. 7-8 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: At three years old Mary is led to the temple by virgins bearing lamps 'that the child may not turn back again', received by the high priest — 'Mary, the Lord God hath magnified thy name to all generations' — placed on the third step of the altar, and there 'the Lord gave unto her grace, and she danced with her feet, and all the house of Israel loved her.' She is kept in the temple 'as a dove educated there', fed by the hand of an angel — the founding legend of the Presentation of Mary.
summary.zh: 三歲的馬利亞由持燈的童女引領入殿——「免得孩子回頭，心裏不願往主的殿去」——大祭司接納她並祝福：「馬利亞，主神已使你的名在萬代中得尊崇。」把她安置在祭壇第三級臺階上，「主賜她恩典，她便以足跳舞，以色列全家都愛她」。她如鴿子般住在殿中，「從天使手中得食」——馬利亞進殿節的傳說本源。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal; formative for the Presentation of Mary feast. Legendary narrative, distinct from canonical scripture.

passages.text: But the girl grew, and when she was two years old, Joachim said to Anna, Let us lead her to the temple of the Lord, that we may perform our vow. And Anna said, Let us wait the third year, lest she should be at a loss to know her father. And when the child was three years old, Joachim said, Let us invite the daughters of the Hebrews, who are undefiled, and let them take each a lamp, and let them be lighted, that the child may not turn back again, and her mind be set against the temple of the Lord. And they did thus till they ascended into the temple of the Lord.
passages.zh: 但這女孩漸漸長大，當她兩歲時，約阿希姆對安娜說：讓我們領她上主的殿去，好履行我們的誓願。安娜說：讓我們等到第三年，免得她還不認得父親。當孩子三歲時，約阿希姆說：讓我們邀請希伯來人中潔淨無瑕的女兒們來，讓她們各拿一盞燈，並點亮它們，使這孩子不致回頭，心意也不致背向上主的殿。他們就這樣行，直到登上主的殿。

passages.text: And the high-priest received her, and blessed her, and said, Mary, the Lord God hath magnified thy name to all generations, and to the very end of time by thee will the Lord shew his redemption to the children of Israel. And he placed her upon the third step of the altar, and the Lord gave unto her grace, and she danced with her feet, and all the house of Israel loved her. And her parents went away filled with wonder, and praising God, because the girl did not return back to them.
passages.zh: 大祭司接待了她，為她祝福，說：馬利亞，主神已使你的名在萬代中為大，直到時間的終結，主也要藉著你向以色列的子孫顯明他的救贖。他又把她安置在祭壇的第三級上，主賜恩典給她，她便用腳跳舞，以色列全家都喜愛她。她的父母滿懷驚奇地離去，讚美神，因為這女孩沒有回到他們那裏。

passages.text: But Mary continued in the temple as a dove educated there, and received her food from the hand of an angel. And when she was twelve years of age, the priests met in a council, and said, Behold, Mary is twelve years of age, what shall we do with her, for fear lest the holy place of the Lord our God should be defiled?
passages.zh: 但馬利亞留在殿中，如同在那裏受教養的鴿子，從天使手中得食物。當她十二歲時，祭司們聚集商議，說：看哪，馬利亞已十二歲了，我們該怎樣處置她，免得主我們神的聖所被玷污？

title.en: The Rods of the Widowers and Joseph's Dove
title.zh: 鰥夫之杖與約瑟杖上的鴿子

region.en: Temple of the Lord, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，主的聖殿

period: Protevangelion of James, c. 150 CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: The Protevangelion, chap. 8 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: To keep the temple undefiled, the angel tells Zacharias to summon all the widowers of Judaea, 'every one of them bring his rod, and he by whom the Lord shall shew a sign shall be the husband of Mary.' The trumpet sounds, all assemble, and as the high priest prays over the rods, a dove comes forth from Joseph's rod and alights on his head. The old carpenter protests he has children and wants no wife; he is compelled, takes Mary home, and returns to his trade.
summary.zh: 為免聖所玷污，天使命撒迦利亞召集猶太全境的鰥夫，「各人拿自己的杖來，主藉誰顯出記號，誰就是馬利亞的丈夫」。吹角聚集後，大祭司拿杖禱告——「約瑟杖中飛出一隻鴿子，落在約瑟頭上」。老木匠連連推辭——「我有兒女，已經年老，再娶妻子豈合宜」——終被勸服，攜馬利亞回家，隨即重操建築舊業。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal betrothal legend; the sign-by-rod is a divination type noted as such.

passages.text: And behold the angel of the Lord came to him, and said, Zacharias, Zacharias, Go forth and call together all the widowers among the people, and let every one of them bring his rod, and he by whom the Lord shall shew a sign shall be the husband of Mary. And the criers went out through all Judaea, and the trumpet of the Lord sounded, and all the people ran and met together. And Joseph also throwing away his hatchet, went out to meet them; and when they were met, they went to the high-priest; taking every man his rod.
passages.zh: 看哪，主的使者來到他那裏，說：撒迦利亞，撒迦利亞，出去召集百姓中所有的鰥夫，讓他們各人帶來自己的杖，主向他顯出記號的那人，就是馬利亞的丈夫。於是傳令的人走遍全猶太地，主的號角吹響，眾百姓都跑來聚集。約瑟也丟下他的斧頭，出去與他們相會；他們聚集之後，各人拿著自己的杖，一同去見大祭司。

passages.text: After the high-priest had received their rods, he went into the temple to pray; and when he had finished his prayer, he took the rods, and went forth and distributed them; and there was no miracle attending the last rod which Joseph took. But Joseph took the rod first of all the people... for a dove came out of the rod, and alighted upon his head.
passages.zh: 大祭司收下他們的杖之後，就進殿祈禱；祈禱完畢，他拿起那些杖，出去分發給眾人；約瑟最後取的那根杖並沒有伴隨任何神蹟。但約瑟是在眾人之前最先取杖的……因為有一隻鴿子從杖中出來，落在他的頭上。

title.en: Joseph's Dream and the Water of Ordeal
title.zh: 約瑟的夢與苦水試驗

region.en: Jerusalem, temple and courts
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，聖殿與院中

period: Protevangelion of James, c. 150 CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: The Protevangelion, chaps. 10-11 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: Returning from building houses, Joseph finds his espoused wife grown big, and grieves in Adam's words — 'the serpent came and found Eve alone.' Mary answers with tears, 'I am innocent, and have known no man'; an angel settles the matter in a dream. Yet the scribe Annas drags both before the priest, and they drink the water of the Lord's ordeal, like the Sotah of Numbers — 'if any secret sin be in you, it will appear in your eyes' — and both go home unharmed, glorifying God.
summary.zh: 建屋歸來，約瑟見訂婚的妻已懷身孕，便照亞當的話哀哭——「蛇來時，夏娃獨自一人」。馬利亞流淚答「我是清白的，我從未認識男人」；天使在夢中化解此事。文士亞拿斯卻把二人拖到祭司面前，叫他們喝主的水行 ordeal（如民數記疑妻法）——「你們若隱瞞罪惡，必在你們眼中顯明」——二人毫無損傷回家，榮耀歸神。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal; the ordeal mirrors Numbers 5's Sotah rite; presented as legend.

passages.text: AND when her sixth month was come, Joseph returned from his building houses abroad, which was his trade, and entering into the house, found the Virgin grown big: then smiting upon his face, he said, With what face can I look up to the Lord my God? For I received her a Virgin out of the temple of the Lord my God, and have not preserved her such! Is not the history of Adam exactly accomplished in me? For in the very instant of his glory, the serpent came and found Eve alone, and seduced her. Just after the same manner it has happened to me.
passages.zh: 到了她懷孕的第六個月，約瑟從他出外建造房屋的地方回來——那是他的本行——進了家，發現那童女已經大腹便便；他便捶打自己的臉，說：我還有什麼臉面仰望主我的神呢？因為我是從主我神的殿中把她作為童女領回來的，卻沒有使她保持如此！亞當的事蹟豈不正在我身上絲毫不差地重演了嗎？因為就在他榮耀的那一刻，蛇前來，見夏娃獨自一人，就誘惑了她。同樣的事也發生在我身上。

passages.text: But she, with a flood of tears, replied, I am innocent, and have known no man. Then said Joseph, How comes it to pass you are with child? Mary answered, As the Lord my God liveth, I know not by what means. Then Joseph was exceedingly afraid, and went away from her, considering what he should do with her; If I conceal her crime, I shall be found guilty by the law of the Lord; and if I discover her to the children of Israel, I fear, lest she being with child by an angel, I shall be found to betray the life of an innocent person. What therefore shall I do? I will privately dismiss her. Then the night was come upon him, when behold an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, and said, Be not afraid to take that young woman, for that which is within her is of the Holy Ghost.
passages.zh: 但她淚如泉湧，回答說：我是清白的，未曾認識任何男子。約瑟便說：你怎麼會有孕呢？馬利亞回答說：我指著主我的神起誓，我也不知道是怎麼回事。約瑟於是極其害怕，就離開她，思量該怎樣處置她；我若隱瞞她的罪，在主律法上就要被定為有罪；我若把她的事告訴以色列的子民，我又怕她若是因天使而懷孕，我就成了出賣無辜者性命的。那我該怎麼辦呢？我要私下打發她走。到了夜間，看哪，主的一位天使在夢中向他顯現，說：不要怕，只管娶過這年輕女子，因為她裡面所懷的是出於聖靈。

passages.text: And the priest said, Joseph, do that miracle which is required of you... And he took of the water of the ordeals and poured it upon the head of Joseph, and drank into his nostrils; and then he sent him out to walk about in a circuit... and returned without any harm, and glorified the God of Israel. And they did the same to Mary; and they both returned home without any harm, glorifying, and praising, and admiring the God of Israel.
passages.zh: 祭司便說：約瑟，行那向你要求的神蹟吧……他就取了那試驗用的水，倒在約瑟頭上，又灌入他的鼻孔；然後打發他出去繞行一圈……他回來時毫髮無傷，就歸榮耀給以色列的神。他們也照樣對馬利亞行了；兩人回家時都毫髮無傷，歸榮耀、讚美並驚嘆以色列的神。

title.en: The Cave Full of Lights
title.zh: 充滿大光的洞穴

region.en: Cave near Bethlehem
region.zh: 伯利恆近郊洞穴

period: First Gospel of the Infancy of Jesus Christ, c. 6th-7th century CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: First Gospel of the Infancy of Jesus Christ, chap. 1 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: Framed as reports 'found in the book of Joseph the high-priest, called by some Caiphas', the infancy gospel opens with the infant Jesus speaking from the cradle and with the nativity moved to a cave: at sunset the midwife and Joseph enter, 'and behold, it was all filled with lights, greater than the light of lamps and candles, and greater than the light of the sun itself.' The old woman touches the infant at Mary's word and is healed of her infirmity; the cave 'seemed like a glorious temple' while angels and shepherds sing together.
summary.zh: 此福音託名「約瑟（該亞法）大祭司的書」：襁褓中的耶穌竟能說話。降生被置於洞穴：日落時分，接生婆與約瑟入洞——「看哪，洞裏充滿大光，勝過燈燭之光，也勝過太陽之光」。老婦照馬利亞的話伸手摸嬰孩，痼疾立愈；牧人歌唱之際，「那洞便如同榮耀的聖殿，天使與人的聲音一同讚美神」。

sensitivity.note: Late apocryphal infancy legend; basis of the cave-nativity tradition behind the Church of the Nativity's grotto.

passages.text: THE following accounts we found in the book of Joseph the high-priest, called by some Caiphas: He relates, that Jesus spake even when he was in the cradle, and said to his mother: Mary, I am Jesus the Son of God, that word, which thou didst bring forth according to the declaration of the angel Gabriel to thee, and my father hath sent me for the salvation of the world.
passages.zh: 以下記載見於大祭司約瑟的書中，有人稱他為該亞法：他記述說，耶穌甚至在搖籃中就已說話，對他母親說：馬利亞，我是神的兒子耶穌，就是那照天使加百列向你宣告的話、由你所生出的道，我父差遣我來為要拯救世人。

passages.text: And when they came by the cave, Mary confessed to Joseph that her time of bringing forth was come, and she could not go on to the city, and said, Let us go into this cave. At that time the sun was very near going down. But Joseph hastened away, that he might fetch her a midwife. It was after sunset, when the old woman and Joseph with her reached the cave, and they both went into it. And behold, it was all filled with lights, greater than the light of lamps and candles, and greater than the light of the sun itself.
passages.zh: 當他們來到那洞穴旁時，馬利亞向約瑟承認她生產的時候到了，無法再繼續前往城裡，就說：我們進這洞穴去吧。那時太陽快要下山了。約瑟卻急忙離去，要去為她請一位接生婆。日落之後，那老婦人和與她同去的約瑟才到了洞穴，兩人一同進去。看哪，洞中充滿了光，比燈和燭的光更亮，也比太陽本身的光更亮。

passages.text: And as she was going forth, she said, From henceforth, all the days of my life, I will attend upon and be a servant of this infant. After this, when the shepherds came, and had made a fire, and they were exceedingly rejoicing, the heavenly host appeared to them, praising and adoring the supreme God. And as the shepherds were engaged in the same employment, the cave at that time seemed like a glorious temple, because both the tongues of angels and men united to adore and magnify God, on account of the birth of the Lord Christ.
passages.zh: 她正要離去時說：「從今以後，我一生所有的日子，都要照料並服事這嬰孩。」此後，牧羊人來了，生了火，他們極其歡喜，天軍向他們顯現，讚美並敬拜至高上帝。當牧羊人正做同樣的事時，那洞穴當時彷彿成了榮耀的聖殿，因為天使與人的舌頭因主基督的降生而聯合起來敬拜並頌揚上帝。

title.en: Clay Birds That Fly and Cloths Dyed in the Furnace
title.zh: 會飛的泥雀與爐中染布

region.en: Streets of the childhood city
region.zh: 孩童居城的街巷

period: First Gospel of the Infancy of Jesus Christ, c. 6th-7th century CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: First Gospel of the Infancy of Jesus Christ, chap. 15 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: At seven years old Jesus plays with boys his age, who make clay figures of asses, oxen, and birds; Jesus commands his figures to walk and his sparrows to fly — and they obey, even eating and drinking at his word. The alarmed fathers warn their children, 'he is a sorcerer; shun and avoid him.' Thence the dyer's shop of Salem: Jesus throws every cloth into the furnace, and draws them out dyed each to the colour its owner desired — 'and then he presently began to take the cloths out of the furnace.'
summary.zh: 七歲的耶穌與同齡孩童嬉戲，眾人以泥作驢、牛、雀鳥之形比賽；耶穌命己所造者行走、飛翔——皆聽命而行，甚至遵言而食。驚懼的父輩告誡孩子「他是行邪術的，務要遠避他」。他又入染匠沙倫的店中，把各家要染的布全數投入火爐——再取出時，每匹布都染上了各自想要的顏色。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal; the clay-birds episode has a parallel in the Quranic Infancy story (Surah 3:49) — noted as a shared motif.

passages.text: AND when the Lord Jesus was seven years of age, he was on a certain day with other boys his companions about the same age; who, when they were at play, made clay into several shapes, namely--asses, oxen, birds, and other figures; each boasting of his work, and endeavouring to exceed the rest. Then the Lord Jesus said to the boys, I will command these figures which I have made to walk. And immediately they moved, and when he commanded them to return, they returned. He had also made the figures of birds and sparrows, which, when he commanded to fly, did fly, and when he commanded to stand still, did stand still; and if he gave them meat and drink, they did eat and drink.
passages.zh: 主耶穌七歲的時候，有一天與其他同齡的男孩同伴在一起；他們玩耍時，把泥土捏成各種形狀，就是驢、牛、鳥和其他形象；各人誇耀自己的作品，竭力要勝過其餘的人。那時主耶穌對男孩們說：「我要吩咐我所造的這些形象行走。」它們立刻就走動了；當他吩咐它們回來時，它們就回來。他也造了鳥和麻雀的形象，當他吩咐它們飛時，它們就飛；當他吩咐它們站住不動時，它們就站住不動；他若給它們肉吃、水喝，它們就吃就喝。

passages.text: When at length the boys went away, and related these things to their parents, their fathers said to them, Take heed, children, for the future of his company, for he is a sorcerer; shun and avoid him, and from henceforth never play with him. On a certain day also, when the Lord Jesus was playing with the boys, he passed by a dyer's shop, whose name was Salem. And there were in his shop many pieces of cloth belonging to the people of that city, which they designed to dye of several colours. Then the Lord Jesus going into the dyer's shop, took all the cloths, and threw them into the furnace. And then he presently began to take the cloths out of the furnace, and they were all dyed of those same colours which the dyer desired.
passages.zh: 後來男孩們終於離去，把這些事告訴了父母，他們的父親對他們說：「孩子們，今後要提防與他來往，因為他是個行邪術的；要躲避他、遠離他，從今以後絕不要再與他玩耍。」又有一天，主耶穌正與男孩們玩耍時，經過一家染坊，坊主名叫撒冷。他坊中有許多屬於那城百姓的布匹，他們打算把它們染成各種顏色。那時主耶穌走進染坊，把所有的布都拿起來，扔進爐中。隨後他立刻開始從爐中取出布匹，它們全都染成了染匠所想要的那些顏色。

title.en: Thecla at the Window of Iconium
title.zh: 以哥念窗邊的特格拉

region.en: Iconium, house of Onesiphorus
region.zh: 以哥念，奧尼色弗家中

period: Acts of Paul and Thecla, c. 180 CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: Acts of Paul and Thecla, chaps. 9-10 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: The betrothed virgin Thecla sits at her window 'like a spider's web fastened to the window', three days without food, 'captivated by the discourses of Paul' in the house of Onesiphorus across the way — preaching one God and chastity. Her mother and her bridegroom Thamyris weep and plead in vain; the whole city is stirred, and Thamyris drags Paul before the governor, while Thecla's mother demands, 'Burn the lawless one! Burn her that are unwilling to marry, in the midst of the theatre, that all the women who have been taught by this man may also be afraid.'
summary.zh: 已許配人的處女特格拉在窗邊「如蛛網黏在窗上」，三日不食不飲，只為隔壁奧尼色弗家中保羅的講道著迷——宣講獨一真神與貞潔之道。母親與未婚夫他米利哀哭勸說皆無效，全城為之震動；他米利將保羅拖到方伯面前，其母則喊道：「燒死那不法者！把那不肯嫁人的燒死在戲院當中，好叫所有受這人教導的女人都懼怕。」

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal; the Thecla cycle was among the most beloved legends of the early church and remains part of Eastern Orthodox tradition.

passages.text: WHILE Paul was preaching this sermon in the church which was in the house of Onesiphorus, a certain virgin named Thecla (whose mother's name was Theoclia, and who was betrothed to a man named Thamyris) sat at a certain window in her house. From whence, by the advantage of a window in the house where Paul was, she both night and day heard Paul's sermons concerning God, concerning charity, concerning faith in Christ, and concerning prayer; nor would she depart from the window, till with exceeding joy she was subdued to the doctrines of faith.
passages.zh: 保羅在阿尼西弗家中教會裡宣講這篇道時，有一個名叫特克拉的童女（她母親名叫提阿革利亞，她已許配給一個名叫塔米里斯的人）坐在她家中某個窗戶旁。她從那裡，藉著保羅所在房屋窗戶的便利，晝夜聽保羅講論上帝、講論愛心、講論對基督的信仰、講論祈禱；她不肯離開窗戶，直到她以極大的喜樂被信心的教導所折服。

passages.text: But when she would not be prevailed upon to depart from the window, her mother sent to Thamyris, who came with the greatest pleasure, as hoping now, to marry her. Theoclia replied, Thamyris, I have something very strange to tell you; for Thecla, for the space of three days, will not move from the window, not so much as to eat or drink, but is so intent in hearing the artful and delusive discourses of a certain foreigner. For that man has disturbed the whole city of Iconium, and even your Thecla, among others. All the women and young men flock to him to receive his doctrine; who, besides all the rest, tells them that there is but one God, who alone is to be worshipped, and that we ought to live in chastity. Notwithstanding this, my daughter Thecla, like a spider's web fastened to the window, is captivated, by the discourses of Paul, and attends upon them with prodigious eagerness, and vast delight.
passages.zh: 但她既不肯被勸離窗戶，她母親就打發人去見塔米里斯，他極其歡喜地來了，因為他盼望如今能娶她。提阿革利亞回答說：「塔米里斯，我有非常奇怪的事要告訴你；因為特克拉一連三天不肯離開窗戶，甚至不吃不喝，卻如此專注地聽某個外鄉人巧妙而虛妄的言論。因為那人攪擾了整個以哥念城，甚至也攪擾了你的特克拉，與其他人一樣。所有的婦女和青年都湧向他領受他的教導；他除了其餘一切之外，還告訴他們只有一位上帝，唯獨他當受敬拜，並且我們應當守貞潔。儘管如此，我的女兒特克拉卻像黏在窗戶上的蜘蛛網一般，被保羅的言論所擄獲，以驚人的熱切和極大的喜樂專注於這些言論。

title.en: Thecla Among the Beasts: A Cloud of Fire
title.zh: 特格拉與猛獸：火雲護身

region.en: Theatre of Antioch
region.zh: 安提阿劇場

period: Acts of Paul and Thecla, c. 180 CE (Wake trans., Hone, 1820)

source.work: The Forbidden Gospels and Epistles: Acts of Paul and Thecla, chaps. 21-22 (trans. Wake, in Hone, 1820)

license: Public domain (Wake translation, 18th c., ed. Hone 1820)

summary.en: Condemned to the beasts in the theatre of Antioch, Thecla sees the pit of water and declares, 'Now it is a proper time for me to be baptized... In thy name, O my Lord Jesus Christ, I am this last day baptized' — and leaps in before the horrified crowd. Lightning and fire kill the seals; 'a cloud of fire surrounded Thecla; so that as the beasts could not come near her, so the people could not see her nakedness'; the women scatter perfumes till the beasts lie as if asleep, and the bulls' cords are burnt away as she stands 'as unconcerned as if she had not been bound.'
summary.zh: 特格拉被判喂獸，見場中有水坑便說：「現在正是我受洗的時候……主耶穌基督啊，我在你名裏今天受洗」——當眾縱身入水。閃電與火擊斃海豹；「火雲圍繞特格拉，猛獸不能近她，眾人也不能看見她的身體」；婦女們遍撒香膏使群獸如睡，綁牛的繩索被火燒斷——她「安然立於場中，若無其事」。

sensitivity.note: Apocryphal; the self-baptism in the arena is the legend's signature scene and a famous image of women's apostolic authority.

passages.text: Then a she-bear ran fiercely towards her, but the she lion met the bear, and tore it in pieces. Again a he-lion, who had been wont to devour men, and which belonged to Alexander, ran towards her; but the she-lion encountered the he-lion, and they killed each other. Then the women were under a greater concern, because the she-lion, which had helped Thecla, was dead. Afterwards they brought out many other wild beasts; but Thecla stood with her hands stretched towards heaven, and prayed; and when she had done praying, she turned about, and saw a pit of water, and said, Now it is a proper time for me to be baptized. Accordingly she threw herself into the water, and said, In thy name, O my Lord Jesus Christ, I am this last day baptized.
passages.zh: 於是一頭母熊兇猛地朝她奔來，但那頭母獅迎上母熊，把它撕成碎片。又有一頭慣於吞吃人的公獅，是屬於亞歷山大的，朝她奔來；但那母獅迎上公獅，它們彼此相殺而死。於是婦女們更加憂慮，因為那幫助過特克拉的母獅死了。之後他們又牽出許多別的野獸；但特克拉站著，雙手向天伸展祈禱；她祈禱完畢，轉過身來，看見一個水池，就說：「如今正是我受洗的適當時機。」於是她投身入水，說：「奉你的名，哦我的主耶穌基督，我在這最後一日受洗。」
